body.text:
śrī-siṃha-bhūpāla-viracito
rasārṇava-sudhākaraḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s>, composed by Śrī <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s>

body.text:
(1)
prathamo vilāsaḥ
body.translated_text: (1) First <s>Vilāsa</s> (Chapter)

body.text: rañjakollāsaḥ
body.translated_text: The Delight of <s>Rasa</s> (Aesthetic Relish)

children.translated_text: The affection between <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) and <s>Vīra</s> (heroic sentiment), the fragrance of artlessness and coquetry,
the grace of <s>Lāsya</s> (gentle dance) and <s>Tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous dance) — we worship that conjugal pair. ||1.1||
I always bow to <s>Vāṇī</s> (Sarasvatī), who holds a <s>vīṇā</s> in her hand, who is doe-eyed,
who is the ever-blissful goddess, the beloved of the lotus-seated one (<s>Brahmā</s>). ||1.2||
There exists a certain supreme being, the source of supreme bliss,
whose chest is curious about the firmness of <s>Kamalā</s>'s (Lakṣmī's) bosom. ||1.3||
From the lotus of His feet was born a syllable free from impurity,
with which the fruit of <s>Bhagīratha</s>'s austerity attained co-natality. ||1.4||
In that [lineage], like the moon of the autumn full-moon night upon the ocean of the <s>Reca</s> dynasty,
was the treasure-house of arts, of generous glory, the lord of the <s>Dācaya</s> clan. ||1.5||
By the path of whose sword-edge — though it be a difficult passage — on the battlefield,
the goddess of victory came from the elephant-armies of the <s>Pāṇḍya</s> king. ||1.6||
In whom, <s>Aṅga-Nārāyaṇa</s>, glory abides most firmly,
the earth became a tamed she-elephant, for he was the goad upon the wicked king-elephants. ||1.7||

children.text: tasya bhāryā mahābhāgyā viṣṇoḥ śrīr iva viśrutā |
children.translated_text: His wife, of great fortune, renowned like <s>Śrī</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
<s>Pocamāmbā</s>, generous in virtues, was born of the <s>Tāmarasa</s> lineage. ||1.8||
Of those two were born, like wish-fulfilling trees of the earth,
three sons, who terrified the heroes among enemies:
<s>Siṃha-prabhu</s> and <s>Venna-manāyaka</s>,
and the foremost of heroes, <s>Reca</s>, the lord of the earth. ||1.9||

children.text: kalāv eka-pado dharmo yair ebhiś caraṇair iva |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, having only one foot in the <s>Kali</s> age, through these [sons] as its [four] feet,
having attained completeness of feet, does not long for the <s>Kṛta</s> age. ||1.10||
Among them, while <s>Siṃha-mahīpāla</s> rules the entire earth,

children.text: namatām unnatiś citraṃ rājñām anamatāṃ natiḥ ||SRs_1.11||
children.translated_text: the exaltation of those who bow, and the humbling of kings who do not bow — a marvel! ||1.11||
In the presence of <s>Kṛṣṇaileśvara</s>, at <s>Meleśvara</s> where great offerings were made,
by that lord who performed the installation of <s>Brahman</s> free from destruction on numerous occasions,

children.text: ānṛṇya samapādi yena vibhunā tat-tad-guṇair ātmano
children.translated_text: freedom from debt was attained by that powerful one through his own various virtues,
even as <s>Brahmā</s> was engrossed in the weight of the effort of the excellence of creation. ||1.12||
Seeing his curved sword, like the tongue of the god of death,
the enemies who tremble,
find the arising of perspiration extending the pacification
of the heat of pride accumulated in their hearts. ||1.13||
The illustrious <s>Reca-mahīpati</s>, of noble conduct, whose younger brother he clearly is,
having attained the far-flung fame of a hero's preceptor, the seal of a hero,
having obtained the title <s>Kaṭhāri-rāya</s>, marked with the <s>Rāhuttarāya</s> [title],
[begot] a son, <s>Nāga-yanāyaka</s>, the sole crest-jewel of heroes on earth. ||1.14||

children.text: so' yaṃ siṃha-mahīpālo vasudeva iti sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: This <s>Siṃha-mahīpāla</s> is clearly <s>Vasudeva</s> [himself],
whose two sons, <s>Ananta</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, are protectors of the world. ||1.15||
Among them, the younger, the lord <s>Mādhava-nāyaka</s>,
whose valor is renowned in all the quarters,
whose descendants — kings who are propagators of the dynasty —
are foremost like <s>Veda-giri</s> (the mountain of the Vedas). ||1.16||
His elder brother, on account of his connection with royal virtues on earth
being unbroken — that is, free from fault — bore the name <s>Anapota</s>,
which became literally true,
as well as the title <s>Ananta</s> and the quality of being a support of the earth. ||1.17||

children.text: sodaryo balabhadra-mūrtir aniśaṃ devī priyā rukmiṇī
children.translated_text: His brother is the embodiment of <s>Balabhadra</s>, his beloved queen is eternally <s>Rukmiṇī</s>,
his son is <s>Pradyumna</s>, and his host of grandsons begins with <s>Aniruddha</s>.

children.text: so' yaṃ śrīpatir annapota-nṛpatiḥ kiṃ cānanāmbhoruhe
children.translated_text: This lord of <s>Śrī</s>, King <s>Annapota</s> — and moreover upon his lotus-face
he bears the beauty of the lovely <s>Sudarśana</s> (discus) upon the lotus of his goodness-filled hand. ||1.18||
Where he protects the earthly world, having made it abound in sons of <s>Soma</s>,
<s>Hari</s> is embarrassed, protecting the heavenly world with but one son of <s>Soma</s>. ||1.19||
In the <s>Soma</s>-dynasty, like <s>Paraśurāma</s>,
terrible in the strength of arms, like <s>Gobāla</s> to the enemy-herds,
where he is awake and ruling,
eternal auspiciousness awakes for the worlds. ||1.20||
By the gifts of golden mountains, placing into the hands of Brahmins
a golden mountain,
he who made <s>Śrī-parvata</s> (the sacred mountain) accessible to all people's feet
through a beautiful stairway path. ||1.21||
He who, though uprooting many heroes, is yet innumerable,
though beyond counting, has an unbroken course of conduct,
though born without mixture of castes — a wonder! —
bears the mark of the <s>Soma</s>-dynasty and the <s>Bhārgava</s> lineage. ||1.22||
The enemy kings, struck back from the battlefield, fleeing and fleeing,

children.text: khaḍge khaḍge phalita-vapuṣaṃ yaṃ purastād vilokya |
children.translated_text: seeing before them him whose body bore the fruit of every sword,

children.text: pratyāvṛttā api tata ito vīkṣamāṇā yadīyaṃ
children.translated_text: even when turned back, looking at his [mark] from this side,
clearly confirm as true his title '<s>Khaḍga-Nārāyaṇa</s>' (the <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> of the sword). ||1.23||
The queen of that lord of the earth, renowned as <s>Annamāmbā</s>,
like <s>Śivā</s> (Pārvatī) to <s>Śiva</s>, was most resplendent among the crown of kings. ||1.24||
As <s>Śrutakīrti</s> delights <s>Śatrughna</s>, and <s>Subhadrā</s> [delights] <s>Arjuna</s> with glory,
the dark-complexioned <s>Śyāmā</s> delights her illustrious royal husband. ||1.25||

children.text: tayor abhūtāṃ putrau dvāv ādyo veda-girīśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Of those two were born two sons: the elder was <s>Veda-girīśvara</s>,

children.text: dvitīyas tv advitīyo' sau yaśasā siṃha-bhūpatiḥ ||SRs_1.26||
children.translated_text: and the second, unrivaled in fame, was <s>Siṃha-bhūpati</s>. ||1.26||
Now, the illustrious <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s>, long-lived, this earth
he places firmly and genuinely upon the seat of his own shoulders. ||1.27||
Unfailing is the bowstring's binding, splendid with gold is the supreme bow,

children.text: bali-dhvaṃsī bāṇaḥ para-puram anekaṃ ca viṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: the arrow destroys enemies, and many a fortress is his domain.
Thus, on account of his preparation for battle being almost supernatural,

children.text: maheśo' yaṃ siṃha-kṣitipa iti yaṃ jalpati janaḥ ||SRs_1.28||
children.translated_text: people say of him: 'This King <s>Siṃha</s> is <s>Maheśvara</s> (Śiva) himself.' ||1.28||
When he prepares for battle,
for his opponents, departing from their own city is but grass-walking,
wandering in the forest, or attending to his feet,
is the [only] refuge of his adversaries. ||1.29||
Bringing delight to the good, effecting the blossoming of lotuses,

children.text: kalāḥ kāntāḥ puṣṇan dadhad api ca jaivātṛka-kathām |
children.translated_text: nourishing the lovely arts, and bearing the narrative of a life-giver,

children.text: nitāntaṃ yo rājā prakaṭayati mitrodayam aho
children.translated_text: this king exceedingly manifests the rise of a friend — ah! —
and also the joy of the discus-bearer and the splendid delight of the lotus. ||1.30||

children.text: tal-labdhāni ghanāghanair atitarāṃ vārāṃ pṛṣanty ambudhau
children.translated_text: What is obtained from dense rain clouds — drops of water greatly enter the ocean,

children.text: svātyām eva hi śuktikāsu dadhate muktāni muktātmatām |
children.translated_text: and in the <s>Svāti</s> constellation, in oyster shells, they become pearls, attaining the nature of the liberated.

children.text: yad dānodaka-vipruṣas tu sudhiyāṃ haste patantyo' bhavan
children.translated_text: But the drops of the water of his gifts, falling into the hands of the wise, become

children.text: māṇikyāni mahāmbarāṇi bahuśo dhāmāni hemāni ca ||SRs_1.31||
children.translated_text: rubies, great garments, many abodes, and gold. ||1.31||
His eye [sees] virtue, [and what is] without virtue
as positioned and unpositioned — understanding their own [nature], the enemy kings
of him who is skilled in the virtues of statecraft
bow down to the foot of his lotus-throne. ||1.32||

children.text: prāṇānāṃ parirakṣaṇāya bahuśo vṛttiṃ madīyāṃ gatās
children.translated_text: 'For the protection of our lives, your feudatory kings have gone to your service repeatedly;
they are to be protected by you out of compassion' —
to whisper this in his ear, I think, of those most intimate friends,

children.text: manye yasya dṛg-antayoḥ parisaraṃ sā kāma-dhenuḥ śritā ||SRs_1.33||
children.translated_text: that wish-fulfilling cow has taken refuge in the precincts of his two eyes resting at the ear-tips. ||1.33||
'How did you protect your lives in the terrible face-to-face battle?' —

children.text: ity antaḥ-pura-pṛcchayā yad ariṣu prāpteṣu lajjā-vaśam |
children.translated_text: by this questioning of the inner chambers, when the enemies are overcome with shame,
announce [their defeat] those who have reached the far shore of the activity of honoring the response,
[their blush visible in] the sprouts of color from the emerald and ruby ear-ornaments swinging on their cheeks. ||1.34||
[Named after] <s>Mandāra</s>, <s>Pārijātaka</s>,
<s>Candana</s>, <s>Santāna</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>-tree, and <s>Maṇi</s>,
<s>Anapota</s>, <s>Dāca</s>, <s>Vallabha</s>,
<s>Veda-giri</s>, <s>Svāmi</s>, <s>Māda</s>, and <s>Dāmaya</s> by name — ||1.35||
with sons born of himself, of great magnificence,
delighting in gifts not easily accessible to other people, he on earth
shines like an ocean of jewels,
adorned with the splendid delight of lotuses fashioned by royal artisans. ||1.36||
Whose eldest, the foremost prince, the illustrious <s>Annapota</s>, in virtues
is the foremost of one [brother] in his own form and prowess, the foremost of two in archery,
mounting to the foremost of three in irresistible might of arms, triumphant,

children.text: satyoktau caturagrajaṃ vitaraṇe kiṃ cāpi pañcāgrajam ||SRs_1.37||
children.translated_text: the foremost of four in truthful speech, and indeed the foremost of five in generosity. ||1.37||
In battle, of that prince <s>Dācaya</s>, the powerful one, in the water of the stream from his sword's edge,
the opposing kings, scorched by the heat of valor, are submerged.
A wonder — their women, with tilaka-marks effaced, with dark locks disheveled,
with saffron falling from their bosoms, with collyrium streaming from the corners of their eyes. ||1.38||
While his jewel-like son is being nourished,
the beloved <s>Vallabha-rāya</s>, a full moon,
the remnant of the glory of the good arises —
and the growth of lotuses indeed is a wonder. ||1.39||

children.text: etair anyaiś ca tanayaiḥ so' yaṃ siṃha-mahīpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: With these and other sons, this <s>Siṃha-mahīpati</s>
attains stability through six [sons], like a lord through well-coordinated limbs. ||1.40||
That king occupied the capital named <s>Rājācala</s> (the Royal Mountain),
which had been the ancestral seat of the dynasty,

children.text: satāṃ ca rakṣām asatāṃ ca śikṣāṃ
children.translated_text: administering protection of the good and correction of the wicked
in accordance with justice. ||1.41||
Ruling the region between the <s>Vindhya</s> and the <s>Śrī-śaila</s> mountains through his sons,
the propagators of the dynasty, he enjoys wealth, an <s>Indra</s> of enjoyments. ||1.42||
While that <s>Siṃha-bhūmi-ramaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Annapota</s>, rules the earth,
firmness resides in the bosom-globes, tremulousness at the eye-corners, of beautiful-browed women,
unevenness in the three folds [of the belly], slowness of step in their graceful, languid gait,

children.text: kauṭilyaṃ cikureṣu kiṃ ca kṛśatā madhye paraṃ badhyate ||SRs_1.43||
children.translated_text: curvedness in their tresses, and moreover slenderness in their waists is especially bound. ||1.43||
I, of auspicious form, the sole cause of the excellence of aesthetic expression,
for the purpose of gratifying the learned, shall describe the characteristics of <s>Nāṭya</s> (dramatic art). ||1.44||
Of old, <s>Purandara</s> (Indra) and the other gods, having bowed to the four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>),
standing with palms joined, asked the all-knowing one: ||1.45||

children.text: bhagavan śrotum icchāmaḥ śrāvyaṃ dṛśyaṃ manoharam |
children.translated_text: 'O Lord, we wish to hear that which is pleasant to hear, delightful to see, captivating to the mind,
conducive to <s>Dharma</s>, fame, and wealth, and which demonstrates all the arts. ||1.46||
A supreme fifth <s>Āmnāya</s> (Veda), accessible to all <s>varṇas</s> (classes).'

children.text: iti pṛṣṭaḥ sa tair brahmā sarva-vedān anusmaran ||SRs_1.47||
children.translated_text: Thus asked by them, <s>Brahmā</s>, recalling all the <s>Vedas</s>, ||1.47||

children.text: tebhyaś ca sāram ādāya nāṭya-vedam athāsṛjat |
children.translated_text: extracted the essence from them and then created the <s>Nāṭya-veda</s> (the Veda of Drama).
Having taught it to the preceptor <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) spoke: ||1.48||

children.text: saha putrair imaṃ vedaṃ prayogeṇa prakāśaya |
children.translated_text: 'Together with your sons, bring this <s>Veda</s> to light through practice.'

children.text: iti tena niyuktas tu bharataḥ saha sūnubhiḥ ||SRs_1.49||
children.translated_text: Thus commissioned by him, <s>Bharata</s>, together with his sons, ||1.49||
presented it in <s>Sudharmā</s> (Indra's assembly hall) before <s>Indra</s>, with the hosts of <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs),
and for the benefit of all the worlds, he composed the <s>Nāṭya-śāstra</s> (Treatise on Drama). ||1.50||

children.text: tathā tad-anusāreṇa śāṇḍilyaḥ kohalo' pi ca |
children.translated_text: Then, following that, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> and <s>Kohala</s> also

children.text: dattilaś ca mataṅgaś ca ye cānye tat-tanūdbhavāḥ ||SRs_1.51||
children.translated_text: <s>Dattila</s> and <s>Mataṅga</s>, and others born from his body, ||1.51||

children.text: granthān nānā-vidhāṃś cakruḥ prakhyātās te mahītale |
children.translated_text: composed treatises of various kinds and became renowned on the earth.
Due to the extreme profundity of those [works], and the scattering of [their] systematic order, ||1.52||
due to the interruption of the tradition, and the rarity of those who know it,
the path of <s>Nāṭya</s> (drama) has become mostly obscure, with few who traverse it. ||1.53||
Therefore, this effort of ours, aimed at illuminating that [art],
delights the minds of the wise, who grasp the essence of things. ||1.54||
Would not a lamp of the present day uproot the mass of darkness?
Would not the moonlight, adorning the time, serve to delight the <s>Cakora</s> bird?

children.text: bālaḥ kiṃ kamalākarān dina-maṇir nollāsayed añjasā
children.translated_text: Would not the sun easily cause lotus-pools to bloom?

children.text: tat sampraty api mādṛśām api vacaḥ syād eva samprītaye ||SRs_1.55||
children.translated_text: Therefore, even now, the words of even one such as myself may indeed bring delight. ||1.55||
Pure and sweet in its essence (<s>rasa</s>), captivating with the reflections of its subject matter,
the path of <s>Nāṭya</s> (drama), together with the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>), should be enjoyed like a treasure of gold. ||1.56||
Since through <s>sāttvika</s> and other modes of <s>abhinaya</s> (histrionic representation), in the spectators there arises
the conviction of identity between the actor and the hero — that is called <s>Nāṭya</s> (drama). ||1.57||

children.text: rasotkarṣo hi nāṭyasya prāṇās tat sa nirūpyate |
children.translated_text: The excellence of <s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) is the very life of <s>Nāṭya</s>; that is now elucidated.
Through <s>Vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>Anubhāvas</s> (consequents), <s>Sāttvika</s> (involuntary reactions), and <s>Vyabhicāri</s> (transitory emotions), ||1.58||

body.text: ānīyamānaḥ svādutvaṃ sthāyī bhāvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ |
body.translated_text: the <s>Sthāyī-bhāva</s> (permanent emotion), being brought to a state of relish, is called <s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment).

body.text: atha vibhāvāḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Vibhāvas</s> (determinants) —

body.text: tatra jñeyo vibhāvas tu rasa-jñāpana-kāraṇam ||SRs_1.59||
body.translated_text: There, <s>Vibhāva</s> should be understood as the cause of making <s>Rasa</s> known. ||1.59||

children.text: budhair jñeyo' yam ālamba uddīpana iti dvidhā |
children.translated_text: The learned should know it as twofold: <s>Ālambana</s> (foundational) and <s>Uddīpana</s> (excitant).
By virtue of being the substrate and the object, both the hero (<s>Nāyaka</s>) and the heroine (<s>Nāyikā</s>) [serve as <s>Ālambana-vibhāva</s>]. ||1.60||
There, the hero (<s>Nāyaka</s>) —

children.text: ālambanaṃ mataṃ tatra nāyako guṇavān pumān |
children.translated_text: The <s>Ālambana</s> (foundational determinant) there is considered to be the hero, a man endowed with virtues.
His qualities are: great fortune (<s>mahā-bhāgya</s>), magnanimity (<s>audārya</s>), steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>), and dexterity (<s>dakṣatā</s>), ||1.61||

children.text: aujjvalyaṃ dhārmikatvaṃ ca kulīnatvaṃ ca vāgmitā |
children.translated_text: radiance (<s>aujjvalya</s>), righteousness (<s>dhārmikatva</s>), noble birth (<s>kulīnatva</s>), and eloquence (<s>vāgmitā</s>),
gratitude (<s>kṛtajñatva</s>), political wisdom (<s>nayajñatva</s>), purity (<s>śucitā</s>), and self-respect (<s>māna-śālitā</s>), ||1.62||
spiritedness (<s>tejasvitā</s>), mastery of arts (<s>kalāvattva</s>), and the ability to delight subjects (<s>prajā-rañjakatā</s>), and so forth.

children.text: ete sādhāraṇāḥ proktāḥ nāyakasya guṇā budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.63||
children.translated_text: These have been declared by the wise as the general qualities of the hero (<s>Nāyaka</s>). ||1.63||

body.text:
tatra mahābhāgyam-
sarvātiśāyi-rājyatvaṃ mahābhāgyam udāhṛtam ||SRs_1.64|| 64ab
body.translated_text: There, great fortune (<s>mahābhāgya</s>) — Sovereignty surpassing all is called <s>mahābhāgya</s> (great fortune). ||1.64||

body.text:
yathā-
pautraḥ kuśasyāpi kuśeśayākṣaḥ
sasāgarāṃ sāgara-dhīra-cetāḥ |
ekātapatrāṃ bhuvam eka-vīraḥ
purārgalādīrgha-bhujo bubhoja ||SRs_1.65|| (ra.vaṃ. 18.4)
body.translated_text: For example — The grandson of <s>Kuśa</s>, the lotus-eyed one, of ocean-like steadfast mind, the sole hero, enjoyed the earth up to the oceans, under a single royal umbrella, with his long arms [that had removed] the bar of the enemy's fortress. ||1.65|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 18.4)

body.text:
atha audāryam-
yad-viśrāṇana-śīlatvaṃ tad audāryaṃ budhā viduḥ ||SRs_1.66|| 64cd
body.translated_text: Now, magnanimity (<s>audārya</s>) — That which is the disposition of generous giving, the wise know as <s>audārya</s> (magnanimity). ||1.66||

body.text:
yathā-
janasya sāketa-nivāsinas tau
dvāv apy abhūtām abhinandya-sattvau |
guru-pradeyādhika-niḥspṛho' rthī
nṛpo' rthi-kāmād adhika-pradaś ca ||SRs_1.67|| (ra.vaṃ. 5.37)
body.translated_text: For example — Both of those two inhabitants of <s>Sāketa</s> (Ayodhyā) were beings worthy of praise: the supplicant was free from desire for more than what the elders [deemed] worthy of giving, and the king gave more than what the supplicant desired. ||1.67|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 5.37)

body.text:
atha sthairyam-
vyāpāraṃ phala-paryantaṃ sthairym āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||SRs_1.68|| 65ab
body.translated_text: Now, steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>) — The wise call it the carrying through of an undertaking to its fruition. ||1.68||

body.text:
yathā-
na navaḥ prabhur āphalodayāt
sthira-karmā virarāma karmaṇaḥ |
na ca yoga-vidher navetaraḥ
sthira-dhīrā paramātma-darśanāt ||SRs_1.69|| (ra.vaṃ. 8.22)
body.translated_text: For example — The young king did not desist from action until the fruit had appeared, steadfast in his undertakings; nor did any other than the one versed in the discipline of <s>Yoga</s>, steadfast in resolve, [desist] from the vision of the Supreme Self. ||1.69|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 8.22)

body.text:
atha dakṣatā-
duṣkare kṣipra-kāritvaṃ dakṣatāṃ paricakṣate ||SRs_1.70|| 65cd
body.translated_text: Now, dexterity (<s>dakṣatā</s>) — Swift execution of difficult tasks is called <s>dakṣatā</s> (dexterity). ||1.70||

body.text:
yathā-
vāladhiṃ trātum āvṛtya camareṇārpite gale |
patantam iṣum anyena sa kṛpālur akhaṇḍayat ||SRs_1.71|| [*1]
[*1] Some MSS. have the following example: sa dakṣiṇaṃ tūṇa-mukhena vāmaṃ | vyāpārayan hastam alakṣyatājau | ākarṇa-kṛṣṭā sakṛd asya yoddhum | aurvīva bāṇān suṣuve ripu-ghnān ||(ra.vaṃ. 7.57)
body.translated_text: For example — When the <s>cāmara</s> (yak-tail fan) was placed around the neck to protect the tail-hair, he, compassionate, shattered the falling arrow with another [arrow]. ||1.71|| [Some manuscripts have the following example: He was seen in battle, engaging his left hand with the right through the quiver's mouth; his bowstring, drawn to the ear, once released, gave birth to enemy-slaying arrows. (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.57)]

body.text:
atha aujjvalyam-
aujjvalyaṃ nayanānanda-kāritvaṃ kathyate budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.72|| 66ab
body.translated_text: Now, radiance (<s>aujjvalya</s>) — <s>Aujjvalya</s> (radiance) is described by the wise as the quality of causing delight to the eyes. ||1.72||

body.text:
yathā-
tā rāghavaṃ cakṣurbhir āpibantyo
nāryo na jagmur viṣayāntarāṇi |
tathā hi śeṣendriya-vṛttir āsāṃ
sarvātmanā cakṣur iva praviṣṭā ||SRs_1.73|| (ra.vaṃ. 7.12)
body.translated_text: For example — Those women, drinking in <s>Rāghava</s> with their eyes, did not let their senses wander to other objects; for the activity of their remaining senses had entered entirely into their eyes, as it were. ||1.73|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.12)

body.text:
atha dharmikatvam-
dharma-pravaṇa-cittatvaṃ dhārmikatvam itīryate ||SRs_1.74|| 66cd
body.translated_text: Now, righteousness (<s>dhārmikatva</s>) — The inclination of the mind toward <s>Dharma</s> is called <s>dhārmikatva</s> (righteousness). ||1.74||

body.text:
yathā-
sthityai daṇḍayato daṇḍyān pariṇetuḥ prasūtaye |
apy artha-kāmau tasyāstāṃ dharma eva manīṣiṇaḥ ||SRs_1.75|| (ra.vaṃ. 7.25)
body.translated_text: For example — Though he punished the punishable for the sake of order, and married for the sake of progeny, even his <s>Artha</s> (wealth) and <s>Kāma</s> (pleasure) were rooted in <s>Dharma</s> alone, [say] the wise. ||1.75|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.25)

body.text:
atha kulīnatvam-
kule mahati sambhūtiḥ kulīnatvam udāhṛtam ||SRs_1.76|| 67ab
body.translated_text: Now, noble birth (<s>kulīnatva</s>) — Birth in a great family is called <s>kulīnatva</s> (noble lineage). ||1.76||

body.text:
yathā-
sūryācandramasau yasya mātāmaha-pitāmahau |
svayaṃ vṛtaḥ patir dvābhyāṃ urvaśyā ca bhuvā ca yaḥ ||SRs_1.77|| (vi.u. 4.19)
body.translated_text: For example — He whose maternal grandfather and paternal grandfather were the Sun and the Moon, who was himself chosen as husband by both <s>Urvaśī</s> and the Earth. ||1.77|| (<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.19)

body.text:
atha vāgmitā-
vāgmitā tu budhair uktā samayocita-bhāṣitā ||SRs_1.78|| 67cd
body.translated_text: Now, eloquence (<s>vāgmitā</s>) — <s>Vāgmitā</s> (eloquence) is described by the wise as speech appropriate to the occasion. ||1.78||

body.text:
yathā-
nanu vajriṇa eva vīryam etad
vijayante dviṣato yad asya pakṣyāḥ |
vasudhādhara-kandarād visarpī
pratiśabdo' pi harer bhinatti nāgān ||SRs_1.79|| (vi.u. 1.18)
body.translated_text: For example — Is not this indeed the might of <s>Vajrin</s> (Indra), since his allies are victorious over enemies? Even the echo of <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), issuing from mountain caves, shatters the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpents/elephants). ||1.79|| (<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 1.18)

body.text:
atha kṛtajñatvam-
kṛtānām upakārāṇām abhjñatvaṃ kṛtajñatā ||SRs_1.80|| 68ab
body.translated_text: Now, gratitude (<s>kṛtajñatva</s>) — Awareness of favors received is called <s>kṛtajñatā</s> (gratitude). ||1.80||

body.text:
yathā-
ekasyaivopakārasya prāṇān dāsyāmi te kape |
pratyahaṃ kriyamāṇasya śeṣasya ṛṇino vayam ||SRs_1.81|| (ha.nā. 13.35)
body.translated_text: For example — 'For even one act of kindness, O monkey, I would give my life to you; for the favors being rendered day after day, I remain ever indebted.' ||1.81|| (<s>Hanūmannāṭaka</s> 13.35)

body.text:
atha nayajñatvam-
sāmādy-upāya-cāturyaṃ nayajñatvam udāhṛtam ||SRs_1.82|| 68cd
body.translated_text: Now, political wisdom (<s>nayajñatva</s>) — Skill in the means [of statecraft] beginning with conciliation (<s>sāma</s>) is called <s>nayajñatva</s> (political wisdom). ||1.82||

body.text:
yathā-
anārataṃ tena padeṣu lambhitā
vibhajya samyag viniyoga-sat-kriyāḥ |
phalanty upāyāḥ paribṛṃhitāyatīr
upetya saṅgharṣam ivārtha-sampadaḥ ||SRs_1.83|| (ki.ā. 1.15)
body.translated_text: For example — By him, the means [of statecraft], constantly employed in [proper] sequence, properly distributed and applied with due ceremony, bear fruit, their scope expanded, as if wealth-accumulations came together in mutual competition. ||1.83|| (<s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 1.15)

body.text:
atha śucitā-
antaḥ-karaṇa-śuddhir yā śucitā sā prakīrtitā ||SRs_1.84|| 69ab
body.translated_text: Now, purity (<s>śucitā</s>) — Purity of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is declared as <s>śucitā</s> (purity). ||1.84||

body.text:
yathā-
kā tvaṃ śubhe kasya parigraho vā
kiṃ vā mad-abhyāgama-kāraṇaṃ te |
ācakṣva matvā vaśināṃ raghūṇāṃ
manaḥ para-strī-vimukha-pravṛtti ||SRs_1.85|| (ra.vaṃ. 16.8)
body.translated_text: For example — 'Who are you, O fair one? Whose wife are you? And what is the reason for your coming to me? Speak, knowing that the minds of the self-controlled <s>Raghus</s> are turned away from another's wife.' ||1.85|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 16.8)

body.text:
atha mānitā-
akārpaṇya-sahiṣṇutvaṃ kathitā māna-śālitā ||SRs_1.86|| 69cd
body.translated_text: Now, self-respect (<s>mānitā</s>) — The inability to endure servility is called <s>māna-śālitā</s> (self-respect). ||1.86||

body.text: yathā-

children.text: santuṣṭe tisṛṇām purām api ripau kaṇḍūla-dor-maṇḍalī-
children.translated_text: When even the enemy of the three cities (<s>Śiva</s>) was satisfied, the itching circle of arms
of that hero, desirous [of battle], whose severed heads grew back again in sport — to him, splendor is fitting.

children.text: yācñā-dainya-parāñci yaysa kalahāyante mithyas tvaṃ vṛṇu
children.translated_text: The faces that turn away from the abasement of supplication, that quarrel falsely [saying] 'you choose!' —

children.text: tvaṃ vṛṇv ity abhito mukhāni sa daśagrīvaḥ kathaṃ varṇyatām ||SRs_1.87||
children.translated_text: That ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), 'you choose, you choose!' [they cry] on all sides — how can he be described? ||1.87||

body.translated_text: For example —
(<s>Anargharāghava</s> 3.41)

body.text:
atha tejasvitā-
tejasvitvam avajñāder asahiṣṇutvam ucyate ||SRs_1.88|| 70ab
body.translated_text: Now, spiritedness (<s>tejasvitā</s>) — <s>Tejasvitva</s> (spiritedness) is said to be the inability to endure contempt. ||1.88||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: He who thrice seven times completely uprooted the lineage of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,
the hero who pierced <s>Krauñca</s> [mountain], who performed an unprecedented swan-descent upon the earth's surface,
the conqueror of <s>Tārakāri</s> (<s>Kārttikeya</s>'s enemy), along with the armies led by <s>Heramba</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) and <s>Bhṛṅgī</s> —

children.text: tvāṃ pṛcchan jāmadagnyaḥ sva-guru-hara-dhanur bhaṅga-roṣād upaiti ||SRs_1.89||
children.translated_text: that <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) approaches you, enraged at the breaking of his guru <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) bow. ||1.89||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (ma.vī.ca. 2.17)
body.translated_text: (<s>Mahāvīracarita</s> 2.17)

body.text:
atha kalāvattvam-
kalāvattvaṃ nigaditaṃ sarva-vidyāsu kauśalam ||SRs_1.90|| 70cd
body.translated_text: Now, mastery of arts (<s>kalāvattva</s>) — <s>Kalāvattva</s> (mastery of arts) is declared as skill in all branches of knowledge. ||1.90||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: In assemblies, of the body of arts accumulated among the learned,
he, free from pride, [discerned] the relative hierarchy
as if he were the touchstone of gold,
the boundary of discrimination. ||1.91||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha prajā-rañjakatvam-
rañjakatvaṃ tu sakala-cittāhlādana-kāritā ||SRs_1.92|| 71ab
body.translated_text: Now, the ability to delight subjects (<s>prajā-rañjakatva</s>) — <s>Rañjakatva</s> (the ability to delight) is the capacity to gladden the hearts of all. ||1.92||

children.translated_text: For example —

children.text: aham eva mato mahīpater iti sarvaḥ prakṛtiṣv acintayat |
children.translated_text: 'I alone am esteemed by the king' — thus everyone among the subjects thought.

children.text: udadher iva nimnagāśateṣv abhavan nāsya vimānanā kvacit ||SRs_1.93||
children.translated_text: Like an ocean toward hundreds of rivers, there was never any disregard [shown] by him toward anyone. ||1.93||

body.text: uktair guṇaiś ca sakalair yuktaḥ syād uttamo netā | 71cd
body.translated_text: One endowed with all the aforementioned qualities is the supreme hero (<s>Uttama Netā</s>);

body.text: madhyaḥ katipaya-hīno bahu-guṇa-hīno' dhamo nāma ||SRs_1.94||
body.translated_text: one lacking a few is the middling (<s>Madhyama</s>); one lacking many qualities is called the inferior (<s>Adhama</s>). ||1.94||

body.text: netā caturvidho' sau dhīrodāttaś ca dhīra-lalitaś ca | 72
body.translated_text: The hero (<s>Netā</s>) is of four kinds: <s>Dhīrodātta</s> (the exalted-steadfast), <s>Dhīra-lalita</s> (the graceful-steadfast),

body.text: dhīra-praśānta-nāmā tataś ca dhīroddhataḥ khyātaḥ ||SRs_1.95||
body.translated_text: the one called <s>Dhīra-praśānta</s> (the calm-steadfast), and then <s>Dhīroddhata</s> (the impetuous-steadfast). ||1.95||

body.text: tatra dhīrodāttaḥ-

children.translated_text: Compassionate, profoundly grave, modest, possessed of essential goodness,

children.text:
dṛḍha-vratas titikṣāvān ātmaślāghāparāṅmukhaḥ |
nigūḍhāhaṅkṛtir dhīrair dhīrodātta udāhṛtaḥ ||SRs_1.96|| 74
children.translated_text: firm in vows, forbearing, averse to self-praise, with concealed pride — such is described by the wise as <s>Dhīrodātta</s>. ||1.96||

body.translated_text: There, the <s>Dhīrodātta</s> (exalted-steadfast hero) —

body.text:
tatra dayāvattvam-
dayātiśaya-śālitvaṃ dayāvattvam udāhṛtam ||SRs_1.97|| 75ab
body.translated_text: There, compassion (<s>dayāvattva</s>) — Exceeding abundance of compassion is called <s>dayāvattva</s>. ||1.97||

body.text:
yathā-
sa-śoṇitais tena śilīmukhāgrair
nikṣepitāḥ ketuṣu pārthivānām |
yaśo hṛtaṃ samprati rāghaveṇa
na jīvitaṃ vaḥ kṛpayeti varṇāḥ ||SRs_1.98|| (ra.vaṃ. 7.65)
body.translated_text: For example — By his blood-stained arrow-tips lodged in the banners of the kings, [he announced:] 'Your fame has now been taken by <s>Rāghava</s>, not your lives — out of compassion' — such were the letters. ||1.98|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.65)

body.text:
atigambhīratā-
gāmbhīryam avikāraḥ syāt saty api kṣobha-kāraṇe ||SRs_1.99|| 75cd
body.translated_text: Profound gravity (<s>atigambhīratā</s>) — <s>Gāmbhīrya</s> (gravity) is the absence of agitation even when a cause for disturbance exists. ||1.99||

body.text:
yathā-
dadhato maṅgala-kṣaume vasānasya ca balkale |
dadṛśur vismitās tasya mukha-rāgaṃ samaṃ janāḥ ||SRs_1.100|| [raghu. 12.8]
body.translated_text: For example — Whether wearing auspicious silk garments or clad in bark, the people saw with astonishment that his facial complexion remained the same. ||1.100|| [<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 12.8]

body.text:
vinītatvaṃ-
avaloka eva nṛpateḥ sma dūrato
rabhasād rathād avatarītum icchataḥ |
avatīrṇavān prathamam ātmanā harir
vinayaṃ viśeṣayati sambhrameṇa saḥ ||SRs_1.101|| (māgha. 13.7)
body.translated_text: Modesty (<s>vinītatva</s>) — When the king wished to descend impetuously from his chariot from afar upon merely seeing [him], <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>/<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), having descended first by himself, enhanced his modesty by that eagerness. ||1.101|| (<s>Māgha</s>/<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 13.7)

body.text:
sattva-sāratvam, yathā-
utsmāyitvā mahābāhuḥ prekṣya cāsthi mahābalaḥ |
pādāṅguṣṭhena cikṣepa sampūrṇaṃ daśa-yojanam ||SRs_1.102|| (rāmā. 1.1.65)
body.translated_text: Essential goodness (<s>sattva-sāratva</s>), for example — The mighty-armed one, of great strength, having smiled and looked at the bone, flung it with his big toe a full ten <s>yojanas</s>. ||1.102|| (<s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> 1.1.65)

body.text:
dṛḍha-vratatvaṃ, yathā-
tam aśakyam apākraṣṭuṃ nideśāt svargiṇaḥ pituḥ |
yayāce pāduke paścāt kartuṃ rājyādhidevate ||SRs_1.103|| (ra.vaṃ. 12.17)
body.translated_text: Firmness of vows (<s>dṛḍha-vratatva</s>), for example — Unable to draw him away from the command of his father who had gone to heaven, [<s>Bharata</s>] then asked for [<s>Rāma</s>'s] sandals to serve as the presiding deities of the kingdom. ||1.103|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 12.17)

body.text:
titikṣāvattvaṃ, yathā-
prativācam adatta keśavaḥ
śapamānāya na cedi-bhūbhuje |
anuhuṅkurute ghana-dhvaniṃ
na hi gomāyu-rutāni kesarī ||SRs_1.104|| (māgha. 16.25)
body.translated_text: Forbearance (<s>titikṣāvattva</s>), for example — <s>Keśava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) gave no reply to the king of <s>Cedi</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) who was cursing him; for a lion does not respond to the howling of jackals when the thunder rumbles. ||1.104|| (<s>Māgha</s>/<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 16.25)

body.text:
ātma-ślāthāparāṅmukhatvaṃ, yathā-
tasya saṃstūyamānasya caritārthais tapasvibhiḥ |
śuśubhe vikramodagraṃ vrīḍayāvanataṃ śiraḥ ||SRs_1.105|| (ra.vaṃ. 15.27)
body.translated_text: Aversion to self-praise (<s>ātma-ślāghāparāṅmukhatva</s>), for example — When he was being praised by the sages whose purposes had been fulfilled, his head, upright with valor, shone beautifully, bowed down with modesty. ||1.105|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 15.27)

body.text: nigūḍhāhaṅkāratvaṃ, yathā-

children.text: bhūmātraṃ kiyad etad arṇavmitaṃ tat sādhitaṃ hāryate
children.translated_text: 'What is this mere earth? That ocean-bounded [realm] — let that be conquered and taken away,

children.text: yad vīreṇa bhavādṛśena vadatā triḥ sapta-kṛtvo jayam |
children.translated_text: which is spoken of as a thrice-seven-times victory by a hero such as you.',

children.text: ḍimbho' haṃ nava-bāhur īdṛ;cam idaṃ ghoraṃ ca vīra-vrataṃ
children.translated_text: 'I am but a child with nine arms; this fierce vow of heroism is such [a trifle] —

children.text: tat krodhād virama prasīda bhagavan jātyaiva pūjyo' si naḥ ||SRs_1.106||
children.translated_text: therefore, cease from anger, be gracious, O blessed one — you are venerable to us by birth itself.' ||1.106||

body.translated_text: Concealed pride (<s>nigūḍhāhaṅkāratva</s>), for example —

body.text: (anargha. 4.35)
body.translated_text: (<s>Anargharāghava</s> 4.35)

body.text:
atha dhīra-lalitaḥ-
niścinto dhīra-lalitas taruṇo vanitā-vaśaḥ ||SRs_1.107|| 76ab
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Dhīra-lalita</s> (graceful-steadfast hero) — The <s>Dhīra-lalita</s> is carefree, youthful, and devoted to women. ||1.107||

body.text:
yathā-
so' dhikāram abhikaḥ kulocitaṃ
kāścana svayam avartayat samāḥ |
saṃniveśya saciveṣv ataḥparaṃ
strī-vidheya-nava-yauvano' bhavat ||SRs_1.108|| (ra.vaṃ. 19.4)
body.translated_text: For example — Having himself attended to certain royal duties befitting his lineage for some years, and thereafter entrusting them to his ministers, he, in the bloom of new youth, became subject to women. ||1.108|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 19.4)

body.text: atha dhīra-śāntaḥ -

children.translated_text: One whose nature is tranquility, who is forbearing of suffering, and who is discriminating,

children.text:
lalitādi-guṇopeto vipro vā sacivo vaṇik |
dhīra-śāntaś cārudatta-mādhavādir udāhṛtaḥ ||SRs_1.109|| 77
children.translated_text: endowed with grace (<s>lalita</s>) and other qualities — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or a minister, or a merchant; the <s>Dhīra-śānta</s> is exemplified by <s>Cārudatta</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, and others. ||1.109||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Dhīra-śānta</s> (calm-steadfast hero) —

body.text:
yathā-
kuvalaya-dala-śyāmo' py aṅgaṃ dadhat paridhūsaraṃ
lalita-vikaṭa-nyāsaḥ śrīmān mṛgāṅka-nibhānanaḥ |
harati vinayaṃ vāmo yasya prakāśita-sāhasaḥ
pravigalad-asṛk-paṅkaḥ pāṇir lalan nara-jāṅgalaḥ ||SRs_1.110|| (mālatīmādhavam 5.5)
atha dhīroddhataḥ-
mātsaryavān ahaṅkārī māyāvī roṣaṇaś calaḥ |
vikatthano bhārgavādir dhīroddhata udāhṛtaḥ ||SRs_1.111|| 78
body.translated_text: For example — Though dark as a blue lotus petal, bearing a body covered in dust, with graceful yet fierce movements, handsome, moon-faced, whose audacious left hand, dripping with blood and flesh, playing [with severed limbs], steals away [one's] composure — [such is the description of <s>Mādhava</s> in] a wilderness of men. ||1.110|| (<s>Mālatīmādhava</s> 5.5) Now, the <s>Dhīroddhata</s> (impetuous-steadfast hero) — Envious, proud, deceitful, irascible, fickle, and boastful — the <s>Dhīroddhata</s> is exemplified by <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) and others. ||1.111||

body.text:
yathā-
na trastaṃ yadi nāma bhūta-karuṇā-santāna-śāntātmanas
tena vyārujatā dhanur bhagavato devād bhavānī-pateḥ | tat-putras tu madāndha-tāraka-vadhād viśvasya dattotsavaḥ

children.text: skandaḥ skanda iva priyo' ham athavā śiṣyaḥ kathaṃ vismṛtaḥ ||SRs_1.112||
children.translated_text: Skanda — am I dear like Skanda [to him], or rather, how has a disciple been forgotten? ||1.112||

body.translated_text:
For example —
If indeed he was not frightened, being one whose nature is tranquil through the continuity of compassion for beings,
then by him who bent the bow of the blessed Lord, the god Bhavānī's consort — his son, who gave joy to the world by slaying the pride-blinded Tāraka,

body.text: (mahāvīra 2.28)
body.translated_text: (Mahāvīra 2.28)

body.text:
ete ca nāyakāḥ sarva-rasa-sādhāraṇāḥ smṛtāḥ |
śṛṅgārāpekṣayā teṣāṃ traividhyaṃ kathyate budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.113|| 79
patiś copapatiś caiva vaiśikaś ceti bhedataḥ |
patis tu vidhinā pāṇigrāhakaḥ kathyate budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.114|| 80
body.translated_text:
These heroes are considered common to all <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments).
With respect to <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), their threefold classification is stated by the learned: ||1.113||
By distinction, [they are] the husband (<s>pati</s>), the paramour (<s>upapati</s>), and the libertine (<s>vaiśika</s>).
The husband is said by the learned to be one who takes the hand [in marriage] according to prescribed rites. ||1.114||

body.text:
yathā-
sa mānasīṃ meru-sakhaḥ pitṝṇāṃ
kanyāṃ kulasya sthitaye sthitijñaḥ |
menāṃ munīnām api mānanīyām
ātmānurūpāṃ vidhinopayeme ||SRs_1.115|| (ku.saṃ. 1.18)
body.translated_text:
For example —
That friend of <s>Meru</s>, knower of propriety, for the continuity of the lineage of the ancestors,
married according to prescribed rites <s>Menā</s>, the mental daughter of the <s>Pitṛs</s>,
who was worthy of honor even among sages, and suited to himself. ||1.115|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 1.18)

body.text:
caturdhā so' pi kathito vṛttyā kāvya-vicakṣaṇaiḥ |
anukūlaḥ śaṭho dhṛṣṭo dakṣiṇaś ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_1.116|| 81
body.translated_text:
He [the husband] too is described as fourfold by conduct, by those skilled in poetry:
the faithful (<s>anukūla</s>), the deceitful (<s>śaṭha</s>), the bold (<s>dhṛṣṭa</s>), and the gallant (<s>dakṣiṇa</s>) — by distinction. ||1.116||

body.text:
tatra-
anukūlas tv eka-jāniḥ ||SRs_1.117|| 82a
body.translated_text:
Among these —
The faithful one (<s>anukūla</s>) has but one wife. ||1.117||

body.text:
tatra dhīrodāttānukūlo, yathā-
sītāṃ hitvā daśamukha-ripur nopayeme yad anyāṃ
tasyā eva pratikṛti-sakho yat kratūnājahāra |
vṛttāntena śravaṇa-viṣaya-prāpiṇā tena bhartuḥ
sā durvāraṃ katham api parityāga-duḥkhaṃ viṣehe ||SRs_1.118|| (ra.vaṃ. 14.87)
body.translated_text:
Among these, the <s>dhīrodātta-anukūla</s> (noble-spirited faithful hero), for example —
Since the enemy of the ten-headed one (<s>Rāma</s>) did not marry another after abandoning <s>Sītā</s>,
and since he performed the sacrifices with a likeness of her as companion,
by that account of her lord, which reached the range of her hearing,
she somehow endured the irresistible grief of separation. ||1.118|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 14.87)

body.text:
dhīra-lalitānukūlo, yathā-
sa kadācid avekṣita-prajaḥ
saha devyā vijahāra suprajāḥ |
nagaropavane śacī-sakho
marutāṃ pālayiteva nandane ||SRs_1.119|| (ra.vaṃ. 8.32)
body.translated_text:
The <s>dhīra-lalita-anukūla</s> (gentle-spirited faithful hero), for example —
He, of excellent progeny, having looked after his subjects,
sported with the queen at one time
in the royal garden, like the companion of <s>Śacī</s>,
the protector of the <s>Maruts</s>, in <s>Nandana</s> [garden]. ||1.119|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 8.32)

body.text:
dhīraśāntānukūlo, yathā-
priya-mādhave kim asi mayy avatsalā
nanu so' ham eva yam anandayat purā |
svayam āgṛhīta-kamanīya-kaṅkaṇas
tava mūrtimān iva mahotsavaḥ karaḥ ||SRs_1.120|| (mālatī-mādhave 9.9)
body.translated_text:
The <s>dhīra-śānta-anukūla</s> (serene-spirited faithful hero), for example —
O dear <s>Mādhava</s>, are you without affection for me?
Am I not the very same who delighted you before?
Your hand, which itself grasped the beautiful bracelet,
is like an embodied festival for you. ||1.120|| (<s>Mālatī-Mādhava</s> 9.9)

body.text:
dhīroddhatānukūlo, yathā-
kiṃ kaṇṭhe śithilīkṛto bhuja-latā-pāśaḥ pramādān mayā
nidrāccheda-vivartaneṣv abhimukhaṃ nādyāsi sambhāvitā |
anya-strī-jana-saṅkathā-laghur ahaṃ svapne' pi nālakṣito
doṣaṃ paśyasi kaṃ priye parijanopālambha-yogye mayi ||SRs_1.121|| (veṇī 2.9)
body.translated_text:
The <s>dhīroddhata-anukūla</s> (vehement-spirited faithful hero), for example —
Has the noose of the vine-like arm been loosened from the neck through my negligence?
Have I not greeted you face-to-face when turning during interruptions of sleep?
Have I not been detected even in dreams speaking lightly of other women?
What fault do you see, O beloved, in me who is worthy of being reproached by attendants? ||1.121|| (<s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 2.9)

body.text:
atha śaṭhaḥ-
śaṭho gūḍhāparādha-kṛt ||SRs_1.122|| 82b
body.translated_text:
Now the deceitful one (<s>śaṭha</s>) —
The deceitful one commits offenses secretly. ||1.122||

body.text:
yathā-
svapna-kīrtita-vipakṣam aṅganāḥ
pratyabhaitsur avadanty eva tam |
pracchadānta-galitāśru-bindubhiḥ
krodha-bhinna-valayir vivartanaiḥ ||SRs_1.123|| (ra.vaṃ. 19.22)
body.translated_text:
For example —
The women rebuked him who was named [by them] as the rival [spoken of] in sleep,
even as they spoke [his name];
with tear-drops secretly fallen,
with bangles broken in anger, with turnings away. ||1.123|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 19.22)

body.text:
atha dhṛṣṭaḥ-
dhṛṣṭo vyaktānya-yuvatī-bhoga-lakṣmāpi nirbhayaḥ ||SRs_1.124|| 82cd
body.translated_text:
Now the bold one (<s>dhṛṣṭa</s>) —
The bold one is fearless even when the marks of enjoyment with other women are visible. ||1.124||

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.text: ko doṣo maṇi-mālikā yadi bhavet kaṇṭhe na kiṃ śaṅkaro
children.translated_text: What fault if a gem-necklace be on the neck? Does not <s>Śaṅkara</s>

children.text: dhatte bhūṣaṇam ardha-candram amalaṃ candre na kiṃ kālimā |
children.translated_text: wear a spotless half-moon as ornament? And is there not darkness in the moon?

children.text: tat sādhv eva kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaṇitibhir naivāparāddhaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: Therefore, well done indeed — enough of these words — you have committed no offense;

children.text: bhāgyaṃ draṣṭum anīśayaiva bhavataḥ kāntāparāddhaṃ mayā ||SRs_1.125||
children.translated_text: it is I who have offended, my beloved, by being unable to see your fortune. ||1.125||

body.translated_text: For example, by me myself —

body.text:
atha dakṣiṇaḥ-
nāyikāsv apy anekāsu tulyo dakṣiṇa ucyate ||SRs_1.126|| 83ab
body.translated_text:
Now the gallant one (<s>dakṣiṇa</s>) —
Among many heroines, the gallant one is said to be equal [in affection to all]. ||1.126||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'The daughter of the lord of <s>Kuntala</s> stands freshly bathed; it is the turn of the sister of the king of <s>Aṅga</s>;

children.text: dyūte rātrir iyaṃ jitā kamalayā devī prasādyādya ca |
children.translated_text: this night has been won at dice by <s>Kamalā</s>; and the queen must be propitiated today' —

children.text: ity antaḥ-pura-sundarīḥ prati mayā vijñāya vijñāpite
children.translated_text: thus when I informed [the king] regarding the beauties of the inner chambers after ascertaining [the situation],
the king, his mind bewildered by indecision, stood still for two or three <s>nāḍikās</s> (time-units). ||1.127||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atha upapatiḥ-

children.text: laṅghitācārayā yas tu vināpi vidhinā striyā | 83cd
children.translated_text: He with whom a woman of transgressed conduct, even without prescribed rites,

children.text: saṅketaṃ nīyate prokto budhair upapatis tu saḥ ||SRs_1.128|| 84ab
children.translated_text: is brought to a rendezvous, is declared by the learned to be the paramour (<s>upapati</s>). ||1.128||

body.translated_text: Now the paramour (<s>upapati</s>) —

body.text: yathā-

children.text: bhartā niḥśvasite' py asūyati mano-jighraḥ sapatnī-janaḥ
children.translated_text: The husband is jealous even of a sigh; the co-wives, smelling the mind [for secrets];
the mother-in-law is a deity of gestures; the sisters-in-law are inquisitors of guesses.

children.text: tad dūrād ayam añjaliḥ kim amunā dṛghaṅgi-pātena te
children.translated_text: Therefore from afar, this salutation — what use is this furtive side-glance of yours,
O connoisseur of the artifice of love's elaborate designs — this effort here is in vain. ||1.129||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: dākṣiṇyam ānukūlyaṃ ca dhārṣṭyaṃ cāniyatatvataḥ | 84cd
body.translated_text: Gallantry, faithfulness, and boldness — because of the absence of fixed attachment —

body.text: nocitānyasya śāṭhyaṃ syād anya-cittatva-sambhavāt ||SRs_1.130|| 85ab
body.translated_text: are not appropriate for his deceitfulness, [which] arises from his mind being fixed on another. ||1.130||

body.text: śaṭhopapatir, yathā-
body.translated_text: The deceitful paramour (<s>śaṭha-upapati</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: At midday, when the place is empty of people, when the lotuses have been eaten by the she-elephant,

children.text: avisesaṇṇa kahaṃ bia gado si saṇa-bāḍḍiaṃ daṭṭhuṃ ||SRs_1.131||
children.translated_text: O undiscriminating one, how indeed have you gone to see the hemp garden? ||1.131||
[At midday, when the place is empty of people, when the lotuses have been eaten by the she-elephant,

children.text: aviśeṣajña katham iva gato' si śaṇa-vāṭikāṃ draṣṭum ||]
children.translated_text: O undiscriminating one, how indeed have you gone to see the hemp garden?]

body.text: atra kayācit svairiṇyāṃ mayi saṅketaṃ gatāyāṃ tvaṃ tu śāṇa-vāṭikāyāṃ kathāpi rantuṃ gato' sīti vyaṅgyārthenānyāsaṅga-sūcanād ayaṃ śaṭhopapatiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, when a certain free-willed woman had gone to a rendezvous with me, 'but you have gone to the hemp garden to sport with some [other woman]' — by this implied meaning suggesting attachment to another, this is the deceitful paramour (<s>śaṭha-upapati</s>).

body.text: atha vaiśikaḥ-

children.translated_text: Handsome, endowed with good character, learned in the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures), pleasing to behold,
of noble family, intelligent, valiant, a youth of charming attire, ||1.132||

body.translated_text: Now the libertine (<s>vaiśika</s>) —

body.text: adīnaḥ surabhis tyāgī sahanaḥ priya-bhāṣaṇaḥ | 86
body.translated_text: not despondent, fragrant, generous, patient, sweet-spoken,

body.text: śaṅka-vihīno mānī ca deśa-kāla-vibhāga-vit ||SRs_1.133||
body.translated_text: free from suspicion, proud, and a knower of the distinctions of place and time, ||1.133||

body.text: dākṣya-cāturya-mādhurya-saubhāgyādibhir anvitaḥ | 87
body.translated_text: endowed with skill, cleverness, sweetness, good fortune, and other qualities,

body.text: veśyopabhoga-rasiko yo bhavet sa tu vaiśikaḥ ||SRs_1.134||
body.translated_text: one who delights in the enjoyment of courtesans — he is the libertine (<s>vaiśika</s>). ||1.134||

body.text: kalakaṇṭhādiko lakṣyo bhāṇādāv eva vaiśikaḥ | 88
body.translated_text: <s>Kalakaṇṭha</s> and others should be observed as libertines in <s>Bhāṇa</s> (monologue drama) and such [genres].

body.text: sa tridhā kathyate jyeṣṭha-madhya-nīca-vibhedataḥ ||SRs_1.135|| 89ab
body.translated_text: He is described as threefold by the distinction of superior, middling, and inferior. ||1.135||

body.text: teṣāṃ lakṣaṇāni bhāva-prakāśikāyām uktāni | yathā-
body.translated_text: Their characteristics are stated in the <s>Bhāva-prakāśikā</s>. For example —

children.text: asaṅgo' pi svabhāvena saktavac ceṣṭate muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Though unattached by nature, he acts as if attached repeatedly;
generous, sweet by nature, equal in sorrow and joy, and pure. ||1.136||
Skilled in the arts of love, expert in conciliating the angered;
he becomes disaffected if there is even a slight quiver on the beloved's lip. ||1.137||

children.text: upacāra-paro hy eṣa uttamaḥ kathyate budhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: One devoted to courteous behavior — he is declared by the learned to be the superior type.

children.text: vyalīka-mātre dṛṣṭe' syā na kupyati na rajyati ||SRs_1.138||
children.translated_text: On seeing even a trifle of deception in her, he neither becomes angry nor attached. ||1.138||

children.text: dadāti kāle kāle ca bhāvaṃ gṛhṇāti bhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: He gives at the proper time and apprehends her feelings through genuine emotion;

children.text: sarvārthair api madhya-sthas tām evopacaret punaḥ ||SRs_1.139||
children.translated_text: neutral in all matters, he would attend to her again. ||1.139||

children.text: dṛṣṭe doṣe virajyeta sa bhaven madhyamaḥ pumān |
children.translated_text: On seeing a fault, he would become detached — such a man is the middling type.
Shameless in the arts of love, harsh in amorous play, ||1.140||
ignorant of fear and indignation, of deluded intellect regarding what should and should not be done,

children.text: mūrkhaḥ prasakta-bhāvaś ca viraktāyām api striyām ||SRs_1.141||
children.translated_text: foolish, of persistent attachment even to a woman who is disaffected, ||1.141||

body.text:
mitrair nivāryamāṇo' pi pāruṣyaṃ prāpito' pi ca |
anya-sneha-parāvṛttāṃ saṃkrānta-ramaṇām api |
striyaṃ kāmayate yas tu so' dhamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||SRs_1.142|| [bhā.pra. 5.37-44] iti |
body.translated_text:
even when restrained by friends, even when brought to harshness,
even a woman whose affection has turned elsewhere and whose lover has moved on —
he who desires such a woman is declared the lowest type. ||1.142|| [<s>Bhāva-prakāśikā</s> 5.37-44] Thus.

body.text: atha śṛṅgāra-netṝṇāṃ sāhāyya-karaṇocitāḥ | 89cd
body.translated_text: Now, those suited to rendering assistance to the heroes of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment)

body.text: nirūpyante pīṭhamarda-viṭa-ceṭa-vidūṣakāḥ ||SRs_1.143||
body.translated_text: are described: the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>, the <s>viṭa</s>, the <s>ceṭa</s>, and the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester). ||1.143||

body.text: tatha pīṭhamardaḥ-

children.text: nāyakānucaro bhaktaḥ kiñcid ūnaś ca tad-guṇaiḥ | 90
children.translated_text: A devoted follower of the hero, slightly inferior to him in qualities,
known as the <s>pīṭhamarda</s>, skilled in propitiating angry women. ||1.144||

body.translated_text: Then, the <s>pīṭhamarda</s> —

body.text: kāma-tantra-kalā-vedī viṭa ity abhidhīyate | 91
body.translated_text: One versed in the arts of love-science is called the <s>viṭa</s> (gallant companion).

body.text:
sandhāna-kuśalaś ceṭaḥ kalahaṃsādiko mataḥ |
vikṛtāṅga-vaco-veṣair hāsya-kārī vidūṣakaḥ ||SRs_1.145|| 92
body.translated_text:
The <s>ceṭa</s> (servant), like <s>Kalahaṃsa</s> and others, is skilled in mediation.
The <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester) produces laughter through distorted body, speech, and attire. ||1.145||

body.text:
atha sahāya-guṇāḥ-
deśa-kālajñatā bhāṣā-mādhuryaṃ ca vidagdhatā |

children.translated_text: skill in encouragement, and speaking as directed,
secrecy of counsel — these and others are considered the qualities of companions. ||1.146||

body.translated_text:
Now, the qualities of the companions —
Knowledge of place and time, sweetness of speech, and wit,

body.text: iti nāyaka-prakaraṇam
body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the hero (<s>nāyaka-prakaraṇa</s>).

body.text: atha nāyikā nirūpyante-
body.translated_text: Now the heroines (<s>nāyikās</s>) are described —

body.text: netṛ-sādhāraṇa-guṇair upetā nāyikā matā | 94
body.translated_text: One endowed with qualities common to the heroes is considered a heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>).

body.text: svakīyā parakīyā ca sāmānyā ceti sā tridhā ||SRs_1.147||
body.translated_text: She is threefold: one's own (<s>svakīyā</s>), another's (<s>parakīyā</s>), and common (<s>sāmānyā</s>). ||1.147||

body.text: tatra svakīyā-

children.text: sampat-kāle vipat-kāle yā na muñcati vallabham | 95
children.translated_text: She who does not abandon her beloved in times of prosperity or adversity,
endowed with the virtues of modesty and sincerity — she is called <s>svakīyā</s> by the learned. ||1.148||

body.translated_text: Among these, the one's own (<s>svakīyā</s>) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: What use to me is a father whose foot-tips are licked by the crests of kings?
What use to me is a father-in-law who sits upon the great throne of <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>)?

children.text: te desā giriṇo a de vaṇamahī saccea me vallahā
children.translated_text: Those lands, those mountains, and those forest-lands are dear to me in truth,

children.text: kosallātaṇaassa jattha calaṇe vandāmi ṇandāmi a ||SRs_1.149||
children.translated_text: where I bow to the feet of the son of <s>Kausalyā</s> and rejoice. ||1.149||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (bāla-rāmāyaṇa 6.79)
body.translated_text: (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 6.79)

children.translated_text: [What use to me is a father whose foot-tips are licked by the crests of kings?
What use to me is a father-in-law who sits upon the great throne of <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>)?

children.text: te deśā girayaś ca te vana-mahī sā caiva me vallabhāḥ
children.translated_text: Those lands, those mountains, and those forest-lands are truly dear to me,

children.text: kausalyā-tanayasya yatra caraṇau vande ca nandāmi ca ||]
children.translated_text: where I bow to and rejoice in the feet of the son of <s>Kausalyā</s>.]

body.text: sā ca svīyā tridhā mugdhā madhyā prauḍheti kathyate ||SRs_1.150|| 96
body.translated_text: And that own wife (<s>svīyā</s>) is described as threefold: the naive (<s>mugdhā</s>), the moderate (<s>madhyā</s>), and the mature (<s>prauḍhā</s>). ||1.150||

body.text:
tatra mugdhā-
mugdhā nava-vayaḥ-kāmā ratau vāmā mṛduḥ krudhi |
yatate rata-ceṣṭāyāṃ gūḍhaṃ lajjā-manoharam ||SRs_1.151|| 97
kṛtāparādhe dayite vīkṣate rudatī satī |
apriyaṃ vā priyaṃ vāpi na kiñcid api bhāṣate ||SRs_1.152|| 98
vayasā mugdhā, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: When the moon rose, the dense darkness was stirred,
the pair of arrows of the formidable accomplisher [Kāmadeva] were readied,
a pair of golden buds emerged,
and a slender wave-like line was made to appear in the sky. ||1.153||

body.translated_text: Naive by age, for example, by me myself —

body.text: nava-kāmā, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: The young girl fixes her mind on the rites of adornment,
gives attention to the wedding of gem-dolls,
becomes bashful at the soft laughter of her own companions —
herein is observed the fresh descent of love's emotion. ||1.154||

body.translated_text: Newly amorous (<s>nava-kāmā</s>), for example, by me myself —

body.text: ratau vāmatvaṃ, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: Seeing her own beloved reflected in the gems of her necklace,
suddenly turning around thinking 'he is embracing [me],'
grasped by the hand and trembling,
she in her confusion clung to her companion. ||1.155||

body.translated_text: Contrariness in love-making (<s>ratau vāmatva</s>), for example, by me myself —

body.text: mṛdu-kopatvaṃ, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: Even in the effort to turn away and walk off, the feet advance toward him;

children.text: bhrūbhedo' pi tad īkṣaṇa-vyasaninā vyasmāri me cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: even the knitting of the brow was remembered by my eye, addicted to gazing at him;

children.text: cāṭūktāni karoti dagdha-rasanā rukṣākṣre' py udyatā
children.translated_text: even when resolved upon harsh syllables, my burnt tongue utters sweet words —

children.text: sakhyaḥ kiṃ karavāṇi māna-samaye saṅghāta-bhedo mama ||SRs_1.156||
children.translated_text: O friends, what shall I do? In the time of love-quarrel, my firmness falls apart! ||1.156||

body.translated_text: Gentleness of anger (<s>mṛdu-kopatva</s>), for example, by me myself —

body.text:
sa-vrīḍa-surata-prayatanaṃ, yathā-
autsukyena kṛtatvarā sahabhuvā vyāvartamānā hriyā
tais tair bandhu-vadhū-janasya vacanair nītābhimukhyaṃ punaḥ |
dṛṣṭvāgre varam ātta-sādhvasa-rasā gaurī nave saṅgame
saṃrohat-pulakā hareṇa hasatā śliṣṭā śivāyāstu vaḥ ||SRs_1.157|| (ratnāvalī 1.2)
body.translated_text:
The effort of love-making accompanied by modesty, for example —
Hurried by eagerness, held back by modesty at every turn,
brought face to face again by those various words of the kinswomen,
seeing the bridegroom before her and overcome by the sentiment of alarm, <s>Gaurī</s> in the new union,
with rising goosebumps, was embraced by the laughing <s>Hara</s> — may it be for your welfare! ||1.157|| (<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 1.2)

body.text: krodhād abhāṣaṇā rudatī, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: When her beloved, having committed an offense, turned about before her,
a sudden friendship arose between the lotus and the moon [her face and tears].
As the beautiful-eyed one was unable to utter a word of anger,
the pair of blue lotuses [her eyes] received a stream of frost [tears]. ||1.158||

body.translated_text: Not speaking and weeping due to anger, for example, by me myself —

body.text:
atha madhyā-
samāna-lajjā-madanā prodyat-tāruṇya-śālinī |
madhyā kāmayate kāntaṃ mohānta-surata-kṣamā ||SRs_1.159|| 99
body.translated_text:
Now the moderate (<s>madhyā</s>) —
She in whom modesty and love are equal, graced with dawning youth,
the moderate one desires her beloved, capable of love-making to the point of ecstasy. ||1.159||

body.text: atha tulya-lajjā-smaratvaṃ, yathā mamaiva-

children.text: kānte paśyati sānurāgam abalā sācīkaroty ānanaṃ
children.translated_text: When her beloved gazes with passion, the tender woman turns her face aside;
when he, skilled in the full array of love's arts, turns his face away,
looking at him repeatedly with eyes swaying, her inner desire churning,
poised between modesty and love, she was indeed most pleasing to him. ||1.160||

body.translated_text: Now, equal modesty and desire (<s>tulya-lajjā-smaratva</s>), for example, by me myself —

body.text: prodyat-tāruṇya-śālitvaṃ, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: Her glance, graceful with the corner of the eye and turned with charm,
the hip makes friendship with the sandbank;
the breast-buds resemble a pair of wheels, and the eternal
splendor of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) shines forth exceedingly. ||SRs_1.161||

body.translated_text: Graced with dawning youth (<s>prodyat-tāruṇya-śālitva</s>), for example, by me myself —

body.text: mohānta-surata-kṣamatvaṃ, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: With perspiration scattered over the body, with disheveled locks of hair,
with both eyes half-closed, yielding to helpless abandon,
blossoming with bliss, all other states having ceased —
we long for some indescribable activity of the large-eyed one. ||SRs_1.162||

body.translated_text: Capacity for love-making that ends in swoon, as [composed] by me —

body.text: madhyā tridhā māna-vṛtter dhīrādhīrobhayātmikā ||SRs_1.163||
body.translated_text: The <s>Madhyā</s> (middle heroine), by her conduct in <s>Māna</s> (love-sulk), is of three kinds: <s>Dhīrā</s> (steadfast), <s>Adhīrā</s> (unsteadfast), and of both natures combined. ||SRs_1.163||

body.text:
tatra dhīrā-
dhīrā tu vakti vakroktyā sotprāsaṃ sāgasaṃ priyam ||SRs_1.164|| 100
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Dhīrā</s> (steadfast one) addresses her beloved through indirect speech (<s>vakrokti</s>), with ridicule and with reproach. ||SRs_1.164||

body.text:
yathā mamaiva-
ko doṣo maṇi-mālikā yadi bhavet kaṇṭhe na kiṃ śaṅkaro
dhatte bhūṣaṇam ardha-candram amalaṃ candre na kiṃ kālimā |
tat sādhv eva kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaṇitibhir naivāparāddhaṃ tvayā
bhāgyaṃ draṣṭum anīśayaiva bhavataḥ kāntāparāddhaṃ mayā ||SRs_1.165|| [*2]
[*2] Also appears as 1.125.
body.translated_text: As [composed] by me — 'What fault is it if there be a jeweled necklace on the neck? Does not <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) wear as ornament the spotless half-moon? And is there not a dark spot on the moon? Therefore, well done indeed, well done! No offense has been committed by you through [such] words — it is by me, unable to behold your fortune, that the offense against a wife has been committed.' ||SRs_1.165|| [Also appears as 1.125.]

body.text:
atha adhīrā-
adhīrā paruṣair vākyaiḥ khedayed vallabhaṃ ruṣā ||SRs_1.166|| 101ab
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Adhīrā</s> (unsteadfast one) — the <s>Adhīrā</s> distresses her beloved with harsh words, in anger. ||SRs_1.166||

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: Seeing the offender come without any hesitation,
a certain woman, extremely harsh, with face turned away,

children.text: kiṃ prārthanābhir adhikaṃ sukham edhi yāhi
children.translated_text: 'What use are entreaties? Be happy! Go!
Go!' — saying this repeatedly, she made him miserable. ||SRs_1.167||

body.translated_text: As [composed] by me —

body.text:
atha dhīrādhīrā-
dhīrādhīra tu vakroktyā sa-bāṣpaṃ vadati priyam ||SRs_1.168|| 101cd
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Dhīrādhīrā</s> (steadfast-unsteadfast one) — the <s>Dhīrādhīrā</s> speaks to her beloved through indirect speech, with tears. ||SRs_1.168||

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: 'She too, your beloved, was made tender by you through an embrace that revealed your heart's desire, was kissed by you,
was entertained [by you] eager to hear witty sayings — in her [company] the night passed thus.

children.text: tad yuktaṃ divasāgame' tra jaḍatā kārśyaṃ kalā-hīnatā
children.translated_text: Therefore it is fitting that at daybreak here there is stupor, emaciation, and lack of skill.'

children.text: rājann ity uditāśru-gadgada-padaṃ kācid bravīti priyam ||SRs_1.169||
children.translated_text: Thus a certain woman speaks to her beloved, her words choked with tears and a faltering voice, saying 'O King...' ||SRs_1.169||

body.translated_text: As [composed] by me —

body.text:
atha pragalbhā-
sampūrṇa-yauvanonmattā pragalbhā rūḍha-manmathā |

children.translated_text: as if merged into the body of her beloved, she exerts herself in love-sports.
Even at the very commencement of love-making, she reaches a swoon of ecstasy. ||SRs_1.170||

body.translated_text: Now the <s>Pragalbhā</s> (bold heroine) — intoxicated by the fullness of youth, the <s>Pragalbhā</s> is one in whom <s>Manmatha</s> (love) is deep-rooted;

children.translated_text: Fullness of youth, as [illustrated] —
Her breast-globes are lofty, her pair of thighs resembles the trunk of a plantain tree,

children.text: tarale dṛśau ca tasyāḥ sṛjatā dhātrā kim āhitaṃ sukṛtam ||SRs_1.171||
children.translated_text: and her eyes are restless — what merit had the Creator (<s>Dhātṛ</s>) accumulated when fashioning her? ||SRs_1.171||

body.text: rūḍha-manmathā, yāthā mamaiva-
body.translated_text: One in whom <s>Manmatha</s> (love) is deep-rooted, as [composed] by me —

body.text:
niḥśvāsollasad-unnata-stana-taṭaṃ nirdaṣṭa-bimbādharaṃ
nirmṛṣṭāṅga-vilepanaiś ca karaṇaiś citre pravṛtte rate | kāñcī-dāma vibhinnam aṅgada-yugaṃ bhagnaṃ tathāpi priyaṃ

children.text: samprotsāhayati sma sā vidadhatī hastaṃ kvaṇat-kaṅkaṇam ||SRs_1.172||
children.translated_text: she continued to encourage him, placing her hand with its jingling bracelets [upon him]. ||SRs_1.172||

body.translated_text: With the surface of her upraised breasts heaving with sighs, her <s>bimba</s>-red lower lip bitten, her body-unguents smeared away by the movements — though in the midst of passionate lovemaking, the girdle-string broken, the pair of armlets shattered, still [urging on] her beloved,

body.text: māna-vṛtteḥ pragalbhāpi tridhā dhīrādi-bhedataḥ ||SRs_1.173|| 103cd
body.translated_text: The <s>Pragalbhā</s> too, by her conduct in <s>Māna</s> (love-sulk), is of three kinds, distinguished as <s>Dhīrā</s> and so forth. ||SRs_1.173||

body.text:
tatra dhīra-pragalbhā-
udāste surate dhīrā sāvahitthā ca sādarā ||SRs_1.174|| 104ab
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Dhīra-pragalbhā</s> (steadfast bold one) — the steadfast one remains indifferent during love-making, with dissimulation (<s>avahitthā</s>) and with reserve. ||SRs_1.174||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: She does not rise to greet him, using the pretext of adjusting her girdle-string and such;
she does not accept the fresh cluster of blossoms offered [by him], using the excuse of fear of bees;

children.text: datte darpaṇam ādareṇa na giraṃ rūkṣākṣaraṃ māninī
children.translated_text: she accepts the mirror reverently but speaks not a word, [her expression] with stern syllables — the sulking heroine (<s>Māninī</s>)

children.text: cāturyād vidadhāti mānam athavā vyaktīkaroti priyā ||SRs_1.175||
children.translated_text: either enacts her <s>Māna</s> (love-sulk) through cleverness, or else the beloved reveals [her true feelings]. ||SRs_1.175||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text:
atha adhīra-pragalbhā-
santarjya niṣṭhuraṃ roṣād adhīrā tāḍayet priyam ||SRs_1.176|| 104cd
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Adhīra-pragalbhā</s> (unsteadfast bold one) — the unsteadfast one, threatening harshly in anger, strikes her beloved. ||SRs_1.176||

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.text: kānte sāgasi kācid antika-gate nirbhartsya roṣāruṇair
children.translated_text: When the guilty beloved comes near, a certain woman, rebuking him with anger-reddened,
crooked brow-furrowed sidelong glances, looking [at him] again and again,
with the girdle of the bride, [seeing] the forehead marked with the lac from the lotus-feet of the rival woman,
strikes his forehead with a playful blue lotus — overcome with rage. ||SRs_1.177||

body.translated_text: As [composed] by me —

body.text:
atha dhīrādhīra-pragalbhā-
dhīrādhīra-guṇopetā dhīrādhīreti kathyate ||SRs_1.178|| 105ab
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Dhīrādhīra-pragalbhā</s> (steadfast-unsteadfast bold one) — she who possesses the qualities of both <s>Dhīrā</s> and <s>Adhīrā</s> is called <s>Dhīrādhīrā</s>. ||SRs_1.178||

body.text: yathā, mamaiva-

children.text: pratyāsīdati sāgasi priyatame sā sambhramād utthitā
children.translated_text: When the guilty beloved approaches, she rises with agitation,

children.text: vaiyātyāt purataḥ sthite sati punar mānāvadhūtāśayā |
children.translated_text: but when he stands before her, out of impudence, her mind is shaken off by <s>Māna</s> (pride);

children.text: rātrau kvāsi na cet kvacin māṇimayī mālā kutas te vadety
children.translated_text: 'Where were you at night? If nowhere — then whence this jeweled garland on you?' — saying thus,

children.text: uktvā mekhalayā hatena sahasāśliṣṭā sa-bāṣpaṃ sthitā ||SRs_1.179||
children.translated_text: having struck [him] with her girdle, she suddenly embraced him and stood there weeping. ||SRs_1.179||

body.translated_text: As [composed] by me —

body.text: dvedhā jyeṣṭhā kaniṣṭheti madhyā prauḍhāpi tādṛśī ||SRs_1.180|| 105cd
body.translated_text: The <s>Madhyā</s> (middle heroine) is of two kinds: <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (senior wife) and <s>Kaniṣṭhā</s> (junior wife); and the <s>Prauḍhā</s> (mature heroine) is also likewise. ||SRs_1.180||

body.text:
ubhe api, yathā-
ekatrāsana-saṅgate priyatame paścād upetyādarād
ekasyā nayane nimīlya vihita-krīḍānubandha-cchalaḥ |
īṣad-vakrima-kandharaḥ sa-pulakaḥ premollasan-mānasām
antar-hāsa-lasat-kapola-phalakāṃ dhūrto' parāṃ cumbati ||SRs_1.181|| [amaru 19]
body.translated_text: Both [illustrated], as — 'When the beloved is seated beside one [wife], the rogue approaches from behind and, under the pretext of initiating a game, closes the eyes of one [wife]; then, with neck slightly turned, hair standing on end, he kisses the other, whose cheek-surface gleams with suppressed laughter, and whose mind is thrilling with love.' ||SRs_1.181|| [<s>Amaru</s> 19]

body.text: atretarasyāṃ paśyantyām api sambhāvanārhatayā pihita-locanāyā jyeṣṭhatvam | tatra samakṣaṃ sambhāvanānarhatvāt cumbitāyāḥ kanīyastvam | evam itarad-udāhāryam |
body.translated_text: Here, the one whose eyes are covered, though the other is watching, is the <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (senior wife), since she is worthy of such regard; and the one who is kissed, being unworthy of such regard in plain sight, is the <s>Kaniṣṭhā</s> (junior wife). Other examples may be similarly derived.

body.text: dhīrādhīrādi-bhedena madhyā-prauḍhe tridhā tridhā |

children.translated_text: by the distinction of <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> (senior) and <s>Kaniṣṭhā</s> (junior), each of those is again of two kinds.

children.text: mugdhā tv eka-vidhā caivaṃ sā trayodaśadhoditā ||SRs_1.182|| 107ab
children.translated_text: The <s>Mugdhā</s> (naïve heroine), however, is of one kind only — thus she is described as of thirteen types in all. ||SRs_1.182||

body.translated_text: By the distinction of <s>Dhīrā</s>, <s>Adhīrā</s>, etc., the <s>Madhyā</s> and <s>Prauḍhā</s> are each of three kinds;

body.text:
atha parakīyā-
anyāpi dvividhā kanyā paroḍhā ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_1.183|| 107cd
tatra kanyā tv anūḍhā syāt sa-lajjā pitṛ-pālitā |
sakhī-keliṣu visrabdhā prāyo mugdhā-guṇānvitā ||SRs_1.184|| 108
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Parakīyā</s> (another's woman) — she too is of two kinds: <s>Kanyā</s> (unmarried maiden) and <s>Paroḍhā</s> (married to another), by distinction. ||SRs_1.183|| Among these, the <s>Kanyā</s> is unmarried, modest, under her father's guardianship, confident in the sports of her companions, and generally possessing the qualities of the <s>Mugdhā</s> (naïve heroine). ||SRs_1.184||

body.text:
yathā-
tāṃ nāradaḥ kāma-caraḥ kadācit
kanyāṃ kila prekṣya pituḥ samīpe |
samādideśaika-vadhūṃ bhavitrīṃ
premṇā śarīrārdha-harāṃ harasya ||SRs_1.185|| [ku.saṃ. 1.50]
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — '<s>Nārada</s>, the wanderer of desires, once beholding that maiden near her father, declared her to be the sole wife destined to be the one who steals half the body of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), with love.' ||SRs_1.185|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 1.50]

body.text:
pradhānam apradhānaṃ vā nāṭakādāv iyaṃ bhavet |
mālatī-mādhave lakṣye mālatī-madayantike ||SRs_1.186|| 109
 atha paroḍhā-
paroḍhā tu pareṇoḍhāpy anya-sambhoga-lālasā |
lakṣyā kṣudra-prabandhe sā sapta-śatyādike budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.187|| 110
body.translated_text: She may be either the principal or secondary [character] in a <s>Nāṭaka</s> (drama) and other [forms] — as <s>Mālatī</s> is to be recognized in <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s>, and <s>Madayantikā</s> [as secondary]. ||SRs_1.186|| Now the <s>Paroḍhā</s> (married to another) — the <s>Paroḍhā</s>, though married to another, is eager for union with a different man. She is to be depicted by the wise in minor literary compositions such as <s>Saptaśatī</s> and the like. ||SRs_1.187||

body.text:
yathā vā-
bhartā niśvasite' py asūyati mano-jighraḥ sapatnī-janaḥ
śvaśrūr iṅgita-daivataṃ nayanayor īhāliho yātaraḥ |
tad dūrād ayam aṅjaliḥ kim amunā dṛbhaṅga-pātena te
vaidagdhī-racanā-prapañca-rasika vyartho' yam atra śramaḥ ||SRs_1.188|| [*3]
[*3] This verse is not found in all editions. Venkatachari has not included it in his edition.
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] alternatively — 'The husband is suspicious even at a sigh, the co-wife, keen-scented, is a soul-searcher, the mother-in-law's divinity is gesture-reading, the sisters-in-law are eager to lick up [any signs of] desire. Therefore from afar, this salutation — what use is this sidelong glance of yours? O connoisseur of the artful display of cleverness, this effort here is in vain.' ||SRs_1.188|| [This verse is not found in all editions.]

body.text:
atha sāmānyā-
sādhāraṇa-strī gaṇikā kalā-prāgalbhya-dhārṣṭya-yuk ||SRs_1.189|| 111ab
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Sāmānyā</s> (courtesan) — the common woman, the <s>Gaṇikā</s> (courtesan), is endowed with skill in arts, boldness, and audacity. ||SRs_1.189||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: With the surface of her breasts pressed in tight embrace, her cheek-surface perspiring,
with lip bitten and hissing sounds released, with eyebrows wildly dancing and hands gesticulating,
marked by various flattering words and utterances and by amorous cries,

children.text: veśyānāṃ dhṛti-dhāma puṣpa-dhanuṣaḥ prāpnoti dhanyo ratam ||SRs_1.190||
children.translated_text: the blessed one attains the lovemaking of courtesans — the abode of fortitude of the flower-bowed [god of love]. ||SRs_1.190||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text: (śṛṅgāra-tilake 1.127)
body.translated_text: (<s>Śṛṅgāra-tilaka</s> 1.127)

body.text:
eṣā syād dvividhā raktā viraktā ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_1.191|| 111cd
tatra raktā tu varṇyā syād aprādhānyena nāṭake |
agnimitrasya vijñeyā yathā rājña irāvatī ||SRs_1.192|| 112
pradhānam apradhānaṃ vā nāṭaketara-rūpake |
sā ced divyā nāṭake tu prādhānyenaiva varṇyate ||SRs_1.193|| 113
body.translated_text: She is of two kinds: <s>Raktā</s> (attached) and <s>Viraktā</s> (detached), by distinction. ||SRs_1.191|| Among these, the <s>Raktā</s> is to be described in a secondary role in a <s>Nāṭaka</s> (drama). As, for example, <s>Irāvatī</s> is to be recognized as [the <s>Raktā</s>] of King <s>Agnimitra</s>. ||SRs_1.192|| She may be principal or secondary in a <s>Rūpaka</s> (dramatic form) other than a <s>Nāṭaka</s>; if she be divine, then in a <s>Nāṭaka</s> she is described as principal only. ||SRs_1.193||

body.text:
yathā-
ā darśanāt praviṣṭā sā me sura-loka-sundarī hṛdayam |
bāṇena makara-ketoḥ kṛta-mārgam abandhya-pātena ||SRs_1.194|| (vikramo. 2.2)
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'From the moment of seeing her, that celestial beauty entered my heart, through the path made by the arrow of the <s>Makara</s>-bannered one (the god of love), with an unerring shot.' ||SRs_1.194|| (<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 2.2)

body.text:
viraktā tu prahasana-prabhṛtiṣv eva varṇyate |
tasyā dhaurya-prabhṛtayo guāṣ tad-upayoginaḥ ||SRs_1.195|| 114
channa-kāmān ratārthājñān bāla-pāṣaṇḍa-ṣaṇḍakān |
rakteva rañjayed ibhyān niḥsvān mātrā vivāsayet ||SRs_1.196|| 115
body.translated_text: The <s>Viraktā</s> (detached one) is to be described only in <s>Prahasana</s> (farce) and similar [forms]. Her qualities — impudence and the like — serve that [genre]. ||SRs_1.195|| She entices, as if attached, those with secret desires, those seeking pleasure, the ignorant, the young, heretics, and eunuchs — [all of them] the wealthy; but expels the destitute through deception. ||SRs_1.196||

body.text: channa-kāmāḥ śrotriyādayaḥ | ratārthā rati-sukha-prayojanāḥ | ajñā mūḍhāḥ | śeṣāḥ prasiddhāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Those with secret desires' means <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic scholars) and such. 'Those seeking pleasure' means those whose purpose is the joy of lovemaking. 'The ignorant' means the deluded. The rest are well known.

children.translated_text: Here some say —
A <s>Gaṇikā</s> (courtesan) has no real attachment even to a virtuous hero;
and in describing an unattached one, a semblance of <s>Rasa</s> (<s>Rasābhāsa</s>) would arise. ||SRs_1.197||

body.text: ataś ca nāṭakādau tu varṇyā sā na bhaved iti ||SRs_1.198|| 116ab
body.translated_text: And therefore she should not be described [as a heroine] in a <s>Nāṭaka</s> and the like. ||SRs_1.198||

body.text: tathā cāhuḥ [śṛ.ti. 1.62,64}-

children.text: sāmānyā vanitā veśyā sā dravyaṃ param icchatā ||SRs_1.199||
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāmānyā</s> (common woman), the courtesan — she desires wealth above all. ||SRs_1.199||

body.translated_text: And thus they say [<s>Śṛṅgāra-tilaka</s> 1.62, 64] —

body.text:
guṇa-hīne ca na dveṣo nānurāgo guṇiny api |
śṛṅgārābhāsa etāsu na śṛṅgāraḥ kadācana ||SRs_1.200|| iti |
body.translated_text: She has neither hatred for the unvirtuous nor attachment to the virtuous. In these [courtesans] there is only a semblance of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), never true <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>. ||SRs_1.200|| Thus [they say].

body.text: tan-mataṃ nānumanute dhīmān śrī-siṃha-bhūpatiḥ | 116
body.translated_text: The wise <s>Śrī Siṃha-bhūpati</s> does not approve of that view.

body.text: bhāvānubandhābhāve ca nāyikātva-parāhateḥ ||SRs_1.201||
body.translated_text: Because, even in the absence of an emotional bond (<s>bhāvānubandha</s>), her status as <s>Nāyikā</s> (heroine) is not negated; ||SRs_1.201||

body.text: tasyāḥ prakaraṇādau ca nāyikātva-vidhānataḥ |117
body.translated_text: because her status as <s>Nāyikā</s> is prescribed in <s>Prakaraṇa</s> (social drama) and the like;

body.text: anāyikā-varṇane tu rasābhāsa-prasaṅgataḥ ||SRs_1.202||
body.translated_text: and because in describing a non-heroine, the fault of <s>Rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>Rasa</s>) would arise; ||SRs_1.202||

body.text: tathā prakaraṇādīnām arasāśrayatāgateḥ |118
body.translated_text: and because <s>Prakaraṇa</s> and other [forms] would then become devoid of <s>Rasa</s>;

body.text: rasāśrayaṃ tu daśadhety ādi-śāstra-virodhataḥ ||SRs_1.203||
body.translated_text: and because it would contradict the original treatise which states that the receptacle of <s>Rasa</s> is tenfold. ||SRs_1.203||

body.text: tasmāt sādhāraṇa-strīṇāṃ guṇa-śālini nāyake | 119
body.translated_text: Therefore, in common women, when the hero is endowed with virtues,

body.text: bhāvānubandhaḥ syād eva rudraṭasyāpi bhāṣaṇāt ||SRs_1.204|| 120ab
body.translated_text: an emotional bond (<s>bhāvānubandha</s>) certainly exists — this being the statement of <s>Rudraṭa</s> as well. ||SRs_1.204||

body.text:
tatrāha rudraṭaḥ-(śṛ.ti. 1.69)
īrṣyā kula-strīṣu na nāyakasya
niḥśaṅka-kelir na parāṅganāsu |
veśyāsu caitad dvitayaṃ prarūḍhaṃ
sarvasvam etās tad aho smarasya ||SRs_1.205|| iti |
