body.translated_text: There <s>Rudraṭa</s> says (<s>Śṛṅgāra-tilaka</s> 1.69) — 'The hero has no jealousy toward women of noble family, nor uninhibited sport with other men's wives. In courtesans, both these [jealousy and uninhibited sport] are full-grown — they are the very essence; ah, [they are the all] of the god of love!' ||SRs_1.205|| Thus.

body.text: udāttādi-bhidāṃ kecit sarvāsām api manvate | 120cd
body.translated_text: Some consider the distinctions of <s>Udāttā</s> (exalted) and so forth to apply to all [heroines].

body.text: tās tu prāyeṇa dṛśyante sarvatra vyavahārataḥ ||SRs_1.206||
body.translated_text: But these are generally observed everywhere in practical usage. ||SRs_1.206||

body.text: prathamaṃ proṣita-patikā vāska-sajjā tataś ca virahotkā | 121
body.translated_text: First, the <s>Proṣita-patikā</s> (one whose husband is away), then the <s>Vāsaka-sajjā</s> (one dressed for her lover's arrival), and next the <s>Virahotkā</s> (one suffering from separation);

body.text: atha khaṇḍitā matā syāt kalahāntaritābhisārikā caiva ||SRs_1.207||
body.translated_text: then the <s>Khaṇḍitā</s> (one deceived by her lover) is considered, and also the <s>Kalahāntaritā</s> (one estranged by quarrel) and the <s>Abhisārikā</s> (one who goes to meet her lover). ||SRs_1.207||

body.text: kathitā ca vipralabdhā svādhīna-patis tathā cānyā | 122
body.translated_text: And the <s>Vipralabdhā</s> (one deceived) is described, and the <s>Svādhīna-pati</s> (one whose husband is under her control) likewise, and yet another.

body.text: śṛṅgāra-kṛtāvasthābhedāt tāś cāṣṭadhā bhinnāḥ ||SRs_1.208||
body.translated_text: By the distinction of states produced by <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), these are divided into eight. ||SRs_1.208||

body.text: tatra proṣita-patikā-

children.translated_text: When the beloved has gone to a distant land, she becomes the <s>Proṣita-bhartṛkā</s> (one whose husband has departed).
Her [characteristic signs are]: wakefulness, emaciation, observation of omens and such, ||SRs_1.209||

body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Proṣita-patikā</s> (one whose husband is away) —

body.text: mālinyam anavasthānaṃ prāyaḥ śayyā-niveṣaṇam | 124
body.translated_text: pallor, restlessness, mostly remaining in bed,

body.text: jāḍya-cintā-prabhṛtayo vikriyāḥ kathitā budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.210|| 125ab
body.translated_text: torpor, anxiety, and similar disturbances are described by the learned. ||SRs_1.210||

body.text: yathā mama-

children.text: dūre tiṣṭhati so' dhunā priyatamaḥ prāpto vasantodayaḥ
children.translated_text: 'He, my most beloved, now stands far away, and the rise of spring has arrived;
alas, the cuckoo's cooings have suddenly burst forth, [bringing] thunderbolts of pain!

children.text: aṅgāny apy avaśāni yānti tanutāṃ yātīva me cetanā
children.translated_text: My limbs too, helplessly, grow thin; my consciousness seems to depart.

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ mama duṣkṛtasya mahimā candro' pi caṇḍāyate ||SRs_1.211||
children.translated_text: Ah, woe! Such is the greatness of my ill-fortune — even the moon becomes cruel!' ||SRs_1.211||

body.translated_text: As [composed] by me —

body.text: atha vāsaka-sajjikā-

children.text: bharatādayair abhidadhe strīṇām vāras tu vāsakaḥ | 125cd
children.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> and others have stated that <s>Vāsaka</s> means the 'turn' of women [i.e., the appointed night].
When the beloved is to come to the inner chamber by virtue of her appointed turn, ||SRs_1.212||

body.translated_text: Now the <s>Vāsaka-sajjikā</s> (one adorned for her lover's arrival) —

body.text: sajjī-karoti cātmānaṃ yā sā vāsaka-sajjikā | 126
body.translated_text: she who adorns herself [in preparation] is the <s>Vāsaka-sajjikā</s>.

body.text: asyās tu ceṣṭāḥ samparka-manoratha-vicintanam ||SRs_1.213||
body.translated_text: Her characteristic behaviors are: fantasizing about union, ||SRs_1.213||

body.text: sakhī-vinodo hṛl-lekho muhur dūti-nirīkṣaṇam | 127
body.translated_text: amusement with her companion, writing love-letters, repeatedly glancing toward the messenger,

body.text: priyābhigamana-mārgābhivīkṣaṇa-pramukhā matāḥ ||SRs_1.214|| 128ab
body.translated_text: and looking toward the path of her beloved's approach — these and similar [signs] are recognized. ||SRs_1.214||

body.text: yatha mamaiva-

children.translated_text: 'Having sent the bed to the pleasure-chamber, having adorned her own body,
gazing again and again with reverence upon the path of her beloved,
imagining in her mind the various love-sports to come,
the doe-eyed one sits sighing with the humming of battle-sounds. ||1.215||

body.translated_text: As [composed] by me —

body.text: atha virahotkaṇṭhitā-

children.text: anāgasi priyatame cirayaty utsukā tu yā | 128
children.translated_text: She who is anxious when her beloved, though guiltless, delays — 128
she is called <s>Virahotkaṇṭhitā</s> by those who know the <s>bhāvas</s> (emotional states). ||1.216||

body.translated_text: Now, the Virahotkaṇṭhitā (one distressed by separation) —

body.text: asyās tu ceṣṭā hṛt-tāpo vepathuś cāṅga-sādanam | 129
body.translated_text: Her actions are: burning of the heart, trembling, and bodily weakness, 129

body.text: aratir bāṣpa-mokṣaś ca svāvasthā-kathanādayaḥ ||SRs_1.217|| 130ab
body.translated_text: listlessness, shedding of tears, narrating one's own condition, and so forth. ||1.217|| 130ab

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: When the heart's beloved delays, the beloved woman, though he is guiltless, grows anxious;

children.text: madhu malayajaṃ mākandaṃ vā nirīkṣitum akṣamā |
children.translated_text: she is unable to look upon honey, sandalwood paste, or <s>mākanda</s> (mango);

children.text: galita-palitaṃ no jānīte karād api kaṅkaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: she does not even notice the bracelet slipping from her loosened, pallid hand;
hearing the call of the <s>parabhṛta</s> (cuckoo), she sheds tears and trembles. ||1.218||

body.translated_text: As in my own [verse] —

body.text: atha khaṇḍitā-

children.translated_text: She whose lover, having transgressed the agreement, bearing marks of enjoyment with another, 130cd

children.text: bhoga-lakṣmāñcitaḥ prātar āgacchet sā hi khaṇḍitā ||SRs_1.219||
children.translated_text: returns in the morning adorned with signs of pleasure — she is the <s>Khaṇḍitā</s>. ||1.219||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Khaṇḍitā</s> (one whose trust is broken) —

body.text: asyās tu cintā niḥśvāsas tūṣṇīṃ-bhāvo' śru-mocanam | 131
body.translated_text: Her [reactions] are: brooding, sighing, silence, shedding tears, 131

body.text: kheda-bhrānty-asphuṭālāpā ity ādyā vikriyā matāḥ ||SRs_1.220||
body.translated_text: weariness, confusion, and indistinct speech — these and others are considered her transformations. ||1.220||

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: At dawn, seeing her lord with body imprinted with fresh marks of <s>Madana</s> (Love),

children.text: vadhūr dṛṣṭvā roṣāt kim api kuṭilaṃ jalpati muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: the young bride, out of anger, utters something crooked repeatedly;

children.text: muhur dhatte cintāṃ muhur api paribhrāmyati muhur
children.translated_text: now she falls into brooding, now she wanders about, now

children.text: vidhatte niḥśvāsaṃ muhur api ca bāṣpaṃ visṛjati ||SRs_1.221||
children.translated_text: she heaves sighs, and now again she sheds tears. ||1.221||

body.translated_text: As in my own [verse] —

body.text: atha kalahāntaritā-

children.text: yā sakhīnāṃ puraḥ pāda-patitaṃ vallabhaṃ ruṣā | 132
children.translated_text: She who, in the presence of her friends, angrily rejects her beloved fallen at her feet, 132

children.text: nirasya paścāt tapati kalahāntaritā hi sā ||SRs_1.222||
children.translated_text: and afterwards repents — she is the <s>Kalahāntaritā</s>. ||1.222||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Kalahāntaritā</s> (one separated by a quarrel) —

body.text: asyās tu bhrānti-saṃlāpau moho niḥśvasitaṃ jvaraḥ | 133
body.translated_text: Her [reactions] are: confusion, talking [to herself], delusion, sighing, fever, 133

body.text: muhuḥ pralāpa ity ādyā iṣṭāś ceṣṭā manīṣibhiḥ ||SRs_1.223||
body.translated_text: and repeated lamentation — these and others are considered the desired behaviors by the wise. ||1.223||

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.text: niḥśaṅkā nitarāṃ nirasya dayitaṃ pādānataṃ preyasī
children.translated_text: Having fearlessly and emphatically rejected her beloved who had fallen at her feet, the sweetheart

children.text: kopenādya kṛtaṃ mayā kim idam ity ārtā sakhīṃ jalpati |
children.translated_text: speaks to her friend in distress, 'What have I done today in anger!';

children.text: sodvegaṃ bhramati kṣipaty anudiśaṃ dṛṣṭiṃ vilolākulāṃ
children.translated_text: she wanders about in agitation, casting her restless, troubled gaze in every direction,

children.text: ramyaṃ dveṣṭi muhur muhuḥ pralapati śvāsādhikaṃ mūrcchati ||SRs_1.224||
children.translated_text: detests pleasant things, repeatedly laments, sighs excessively, and faints. ||1.224||

body.translated_text: As in my own [verse] —

body.text: atha abhisārikā (svīyā)-

children.translated_text: She who, scorched by the fire of <s>Madana</s> (Love), sends for her beloved, 134
[going forth] in moonlight or darkness, wearing garments and ornaments suitable for the journey. ||1.225||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Abhisārikā</s> (the one who goes to a tryst) (<s>Svīyā</s>, one's own wife) —

body.text: svayaṃ vābhisared yā tu sā bhaved abhisārikā | 135
body.translated_text: Or she who herself goes to the tryst — she is the <s>Abhisārikā</s>. 135

body.text: asyāḥ santāpa-cintādyā vikriyās tu yathocitam ||SRs_1.226||
body.translated_text: Her transformations are burning desire, anxiety, and so forth, as appropriate. ||1.226||

body.text: kāntābhisaraṇae svīyā lajjānāśādi-śaṅkayā | 136
body.translated_text: The <s>Svīyā</s> (one's own wife), when going to meet her lover, fearing loss of modesty and the like, 136

body.text: vyāghra-huṅkāra-santrasta-mṛga-śāva-vilocanā ||SRs_1.227||
body.translated_text: has eyes like those of a fawn startled by the roar of a tiger. ||1.227||

body.text: nīlyādi-rakta-vasana-racitāṅgāvaguṇṭhanā | 137
body.translated_text: She veils her limbs with garments made of dark blue or red cloth, 137

body.text: svāṅge vilīnāvayavā niḥśabdaṃ pāda-cāriṇī ||SRs_1.228||
body.translated_text: her body contracted into itself, walking silently on foot. ||1.228||

body.text: susnigdhaika-sakhī-mātra-yuktā yāti samutsukā | 138
body.translated_text: She goes forth eagerly, accompanied only by one very affectionate friend, 138

body.text: mṛṣā priye tu nidrāṇe pārśve tiṣṭhati niścalā ||SRs_1.229||
body.translated_text: and if her beloved happens to be asleep, she stands motionless at his side. ||1.229||

body.text: garvātireka-nibhṛtā śītaiḥ srag-dāma-candanaiḥ | 139
body.translated_text: Restrained by excess of pride, with cool garlands, wreaths, and sandalwood, 139

body.text: bhāvajñā bodhayaty enaṃ tad-bhāvāvekṣaṇotsukā ||SRs_1.230||
body.translated_text: the one who knows his moods awakens him, eager to observe his feelings. ||1.230||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: She put on ornaments the color of darkness,
she removed her anklet for the fault of its jingling;
the <s>abhisārikā</s>, out of fear of the bright moonlight, did not wish
to wait, [and so] she sent a messenger-woman. ||1.231||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text:
yathā vā-
mallikā-māla-bhāriṇyaḥ
sarvāṅgīṇārdra-candanāḥ |
kṣaumavatyo na lakṣyante
jyotsnāyām abhisārikā ||SRs_1.232|| (kāvyādarśa 2.213)
body.translated_text: Or as — Bearing garlands of <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), with moist sandalwood paste on every limb, wearing fine linen, the <s>abhisārikās</s> are not visible in the moonlight. ||1.232|| (from <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> 2.213)

body.text:
(anyāṅganābhisārikā-kanyakā)
svīyāvat kanyakā jñeyā kāntābhisaraṇa-krame ||SRs_1.233|| 140
body.translated_text: (The <s>Abhisārikā</s> who is another man's woman — the maiden) The maiden should be understood as like the <s>Svīyā</s> in the manner of going to meet a lover. ||1.233|| 140

body.text:
(veśyābhisārikā)
veśyābhisārikā tv eti hṛṣṭā vaiśika-nāyakam |
āvirbhūta-smita-mukhī mada-ghūrṇita-locanā ||SRs_1.234|| 141
anuliptākhilāṅgī ca vicitrābharaṇānvitā |
snehāṅkurita-romāñca-sphuṭībhūta-manobhavā ||SRs_1.235|| 142
saṃveṣṭitā parijanair bhogopakaraṇānvitaiḥ |
raśanārāva-mādhurya-dīpitānaṅga-vaibhavā ||SRs_1.236|| 143
caraṇāmbuja-saṃlagna-maṇi-mañjīra-mañjulā |

children.translated_text: And she, with soft touches such as scratching the hair and the like, 144
awakens him, and when he wakes, she looks at him with eyes feigning loving anger. ||1.237||

body.translated_text: (The courtesan as <s>Abhisārikā</s>) The courtesan-<s>abhisārikā</s> goes joyfully to the <s>Vaiśika</s> hero, with a smile on her face, eyes rolling with intoxication, ||1.234|| 141 her entire body anointed, adorned with varied ornaments, with horripilation sprouting from affection, desire openly manifest, ||1.235|| 142 surrounded by attendants bearing articles of enjoyment, the splendor of love kindled by the sweet tinkling of her girdle, ||1.236|| 143 beautiful with jeweled anklets clinging to her lotus-feet.

children.translated_text: As in my own [verse] —
In the month of <s>Madhu</s> (spring), on a night white with moonbeams, amid the chatter of her companions,

children.text: madanāturābhisarati praṇayavatī yaṃ sa eva khalu dhanyaḥ ||SRs_1.238||
children.translated_text: she who is devoted goes forth to meet him, afflicted by desire — he alone is truly fortunate. ||1.238||

body.text: atha preṣyābhisārikā-

children.translated_text: With <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) blossoms loosened and falling from her disheveled hair-braid tossed by arm-gestures, 145
with graceful, coquettish glances accompanied by movements of her eyebrows and the like, ||1.239||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Preṣyābhisārikā</s> (the one who goes to a tryst with attendants) —

body.text: maireyāviratāsvāda-mada-skhalita-jalpitā | 146
body.translated_text: her speech faltering with the intoxication from incessant drinking of <s>maireya</s> (wine), 146

body.text: preṣyābhiyāti dayitaṃ ceṭībhiḥ saha garvitā ||SRs_1.240||
body.translated_text: the <s>Preṣyā</s> goes to her beloved with her maidservants, full of pride. ||1.240||

body.text: priyaṃ kaṅkaṇa-nikvāṇa-mañju-vyajana-vījanaiḥ | 147
body.translated_text: With the sweet fanning of her fan accompanied by the tinkling of bracelets, 147

body.text: vibodhya nirbhartsayati nāsābhaṅga-puraḥsaram ||SRs_1.241||
body.translated_text: she awakens her beloved and then rebukes him, led by a wrinkle of the nose. ||1.241||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: With garlands and hair-braid fallen loose, with graceful arching brows licking [her forehead] with intoxication,
her speech indistinct, at every step flinging her vine-like arms here and there,
having gone eagerly to her sleeping beloved and awakened him with the clinking

children.text: kvāṇena pratibodhya bhartsayati yaṃ dhanyaḥ sa ekaḥ pumān ||SRs_1.242||
children.translated_text: of her jingling bracelets, she rebukes him — fortunate indeed is that sole man. ||1.242||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text: atha vipralabdhā-

children.text: kṛtvā saṅketam aprāpte daivād vyathitā tu yā | 148
children.translated_text: She who, having made a tryst, is distressed when [her lover] fails to arrive due to fate — 148

children.text:
vipralabdheti sā proktā budhair asyās tu vikriyā |
nirveda-cintā-khedāśru-mūrcchā-niḥśvasanādayaḥ ||SRs_1.243|| 149
children.translated_text: she is called <s>Vipralabdhā</s> by the wise. Her transformations are: despondency, brooding, weariness, tears, fainting, sighing, and so forth. ||1.243|| 149

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one) —

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: The moon-orb has risen over the eastern mountain —
see, friend, by it we have been deceived!
What now? Take me to my own house —

children.text: tatra vā kim iti vivyathe vadhūḥ ||SRs_1.244||
children.translated_text: or what is to be done there? — thus the young bride was tormented. ||1.244||

body.translated_text: As in my own [verse] —

body.text:
atha svādhīna-bhartṛkā-
svāyattāsanna-patikā hṛṣṭā svādhīna-vallabhā |

children.translated_text: Her actions are described as: the great festival of worship of <s>Smara</s> (Love), 150
forest sports, water games, gathering of flowers, and the like. ||1.245||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Svādhīna-bhartṛkā</s> (one whose husband is under her control) — She whose husband is near and devoted, who is joyful — she is the <s>Svādhīna-vallabhā</s>.

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: Playfully placing in her hair-braid an arrangement of gently smiling white lotuses,
on her cheek a trembling leaf-mark made of musk,
on the expanse of her bosom an elegant <s>makarī</s> (crocodile design) made of saffron —

children.text: yuvā dhanyaḥ so' yaṃ madayati ca nityaṃ priyatamām ||SRs_1.246||
children.translated_text: fortunate is that young man who thus constantly delights his beloved. ||1.246||

body.translated_text: As in my own [verse] —

body.text: uttamā madhyamā nīcety evaṃ sarvāḥ striyas tridhā ||SRs_1.247|| 151
body.translated_text: Thus all women are of three kinds: <s>Uttamā</s> (superior), <s>Madhyamā</s> (middling), and <s>Nīcā</s> (inferior). ||1.247|| 151

body.text:
tatrottamā-
abhijātair bhoga-tṛptair guṇibhir yā ca kāmyate |
gṛhṇāti kāraṇe kopam anunītā prasīdati ||SRs_1.248|| 152
vidadhaty apriyaṃ patyau svayam ācarati priyam |
vallabhe sāparādhe' pi tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhati sottamā ||SRs_1.249|| 153
body.translated_text: Of these, the <s>Uttamā</s> — She who is desired by the well-born, those satiated with pleasures, and the virtuous; who takes offense only with cause and is appeased when conciliated; ||1.248|| 152 who does what is pleasing to her husband even when he does what is displeasing to her; who remains silent even when her beloved is at fault — she is the <s>Uttamā</s>. ||1.249|| 153

body.text:
atha madhyamā-
puṃsaḥ svayaṃ kāmayate kāmyate yā ca tair vadhūḥ |
sakrodhe krudhyati muhuḥ sānṛte' nṛta-vādinī ||SRs_1.250|| 154
sāpakāre' pakartrī syāt snigdhe snihyati vallabhe |
evam ādi-guṇopetā madhyamā sā prakīrtitā ||SRs_1.251|| 155
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Madhyamā</s> — The woman who herself desires men and is desired by them; who is angry when [her husband] is angry, repeatedly speaks untruth when he is untruthful; ||1.250|| 154 who retaliates when wronged, and is affectionate to her beloved when he is affectionate — she who is endowed with such qualities is called the <s>Madhyamā</s>. ||1.251|| 155

body.text:
atha nīcā-
akasmāt kupyati ruṣaṃ prārthitāpi na muñcati |
surūpaṃ vā kurūpaṃ vā guṇavantam athāguṇam ||SRs_1.252|| 156
sthaviraṃ taruṇaṃ vāpi yā vā kāmayate muhuḥ |
īrṣyā-kopa-vivādeṣu niyatā sādhamā smṛtā ||SRs_1.253|| 157
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Nīcā</s> — She who gets angry without reason, and even when entreated does not release her anger; who desires repeatedly whether handsome or ugly, virtuous or without virtue, ||1.252|| 156 old or young — she who is fixed in jealousy, anger, and quarrels is considered the lowest. ||1.253|| 157

body.text: āsām udāharaṇāni lokata evāvagantavyāni |
body.translated_text: Examples of these should be understood from worldly observation itself.

body.text:
svīyā trayodaśa-vidhā vividhā ca varāṅganā |
vaiśikaivaṃ ṣoḍaśadhā tāś cāvasthābhir aṣṭabhiḥ ||SRs_1.254|| 158
ekaikam aṣṭadhā tāsām uttamādi-prabhedataḥ |
traividhyam evaṃ sa-caturaśītis triśatī bhavet ||SRs_1.255|| 159

children.translated_text: Some say that for another man's wife there are only three states. ||1.256||

body.translated_text: The <s>Svīyā</s> is of thirteen varieties, and the <s>Varāṅganā</s> (excellent woman) is of various kinds; the <s>Vaiśikā</s> (courtesan) is likewise of sixteen types, and these with eight states ||1.254|| 158 — each being eightfold by the division into <s>Uttamā</s> and the rest, being threefold — thus the total becomes three hundred and eighty-four. ||1.255|| 159

children.translated_text: As follows —
Another man's wife has only three states: first, she is distracted by the longing of separation;
then, having become an <s>Abhisārikā</s>, she herself goes forth to the tryst. ||1.257||

body.text:
saṅketāc cet paribhraṣṭā vipralabdhā bhavet punaḥ |
parādhīna-patitvena nānyāvasthātra saṅgatā ||SRs_1.258|| iti | (bhāva-prakāśa)
body.translated_text: If disappointed at the rendezvous, she becomes a <s>Vipralabdhā</s> again. Because her husband belongs to another [woman], no other state applies here. ||1.258|| Thus. (from <s>Bhāva-prakāśa</s>)

body.text: atha nāyikā-sahāyāḥ-

children.text: āsāṃ dūtyaḥ sakhī ceṭī liṅginī prativeśinī | 160
children.translated_text: Their messengers are: a female friend, a maidservant, a woman in religious guise, a neighbor, 160

children.text:
dhātreyī śilpakārī ca kumārī kathinī tathā |
kārur vipraśnikā ceti netṛ-mitra-guṇānvitāḥ ||SRs_1.259|| 161
children.translated_text: a foster-sister, a craftswoman, a maiden, a <s>Kathinī</s>, a female artisan, and a female fortune-teller — endowed with the qualities of a leader and friend. ||1.259|| 161

body.translated_text: Now, the companions of the <s>Nāyikā</s> —

body.text: liṅginī paṇḍita-kauśikyādiḥ | prativeśinī samīpa-gṛha-vartinī | śilpa-kārī vīṇā-vādanādi-nipuṇā | kārū rajakyādiḥ | vipraśnikā daivajñā | śeṣāḥ prasiddhāḥ | itara-rasālambanānām anati-nirūpaṇīyatayā pṛthak-prakaraṇārambhasyānupayogāt tat-tad-rasa-prasaṅga eva nirūpaṇaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Liṅginī</s> is a learned woman such as a female <s>Kauśikī</s> ascetic. <s>Prativeśinī</s> is one dwelling in a nearby house. <s>Śilpa-kārī</s> is one skilled in playing the <s>vīṇā</s> and the like. <s>Kārū</s> is a washerwoman and the like. <s>Vipraśnikā</s> is a female astrologer. The rest are well known. Since the <s>ālambanās</s> (substrata) of other <s>rasas</s> need not be elaborated at great length, and since beginning a separate section would be unprofitable, we shall describe them in connection with each respective <s>rasa</s>.

body.text: iti nāyikā-prakaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on <s>Nāyikās</s> (heroines). ||

body.text: atha śṛṅgārasyoddīpana-vibhāvaḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Uddīpana-vibhāva</s> (excitant determinant) of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) —

body.text:
uddīpanaṃ caturdhā syād ālambana-samāśrayam |
guṇa-ceṣṭālaṅkṛtayas taṭasthāś ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_1.260|| 162
body.translated_text: The excitant is fourfold, depending on the <s>ālambana</s> (substrate): qualities, actions, adornments, and extrinsic factors — such is the division. ||1.260|| 162

body.text:
tatra guṇāḥ-
yauvanaṃ rūpa-lāvaṇye saundaryam abhirūpatā |
mārdavaṃ saukumāryaṃ cety ālambana-gatā guṇāḥ ||SRs_1.261|| 163
body.translated_text: Of these, the qualities — Youth, beauty, charm, comeliness, gracefulness, softness, and delicacy — these are the qualities residing in the <s>ālambana</s>. ||1.261|| 163

body.text:
tatra yauvanam-
sarvāsām api nārīṇāṃ yauvanaṃ tu caturvidham |
pratiyauvanam etāsāṃ ceṣṭitāni pṛthak pṛthak ||SRs_1.262|| 164
body.translated_text: Of these, youth — The youth of all women is of four kinds. The behaviors of each <s>Prati-yauvana</s> (stage of youth) are distinct. ||1.262|| 164

body.text:
tatra prathama-yauvanam-
īṣac-capala-netrāntaṃ smara-smera-mukhāmbujam |
sa-garva-jarajogaṇḍam asamagrāruṇādharam ||SRs_1.263|| 165
lāvaṇyodbheda-ramyāṅgaṃ vilasad-bhāva-saurabham |
unmīlitāṅkura-kucam asphuṭāṅgaka-sandhikam ||SRs_1.264|| 166
prathamaṃ yauvanaṃ tatra vartamānā mṛgekṣaṇā |
apekṣate mṛdu-sparśaṃ sahate noddhatāṃ ratim ||SRs_1.265|| 167
sakhī-keli-ratā svāṅga-saṃskāra-kalitādarā |

children.translated_text: she does not experience anger or joy at the sight of a rival wife and the like; 168

children.text: nātirajyati kāntasya saṅgame kiṃ tu lajjate ||SRs_1.266||
children.translated_text: she does not greatly delight in union with her lover, but rather feels bashful. ||1.266||

body.translated_text: Of these, the first youth — With slightly restless eye-corners, a lotus-face smiling with the hints of love, cheeks endowed with a proud, faint down, lips not fully reddened, ||1.263|| 165 limbs lovely with the budding of charm, radiant with the fragrance of emerging emotion, breasts like sprouting buds, joints of the body not yet fully defined, ||1.264|| 166 — the doe-eyed woman in that first youth desires gentle touch but cannot endure vigorous love-play; ||1.265|| 167 she delights in sports with her friends and takes care in adorning her own limbs,

body.text: yathā-

children.text: vistārī stana-bhāra eṣa gamito na svocitām unnatiṃ
children.translated_text: This increasing weight of the breasts has not yet reached its proper fullness,

children.text: rekhodbhāsi tathā vali-trayam idaṃ na spaṣṭa-nimnottam |
children.translated_text: likewise the three folds appearing as lines are not clearly concave and convex;
at her waist, a straight, long, half-tawny line of hair is seen —
a charming age is passing, mixed with the interplay of youth and childhood. ||1.267||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text: (daśarūpakāvaloke' pi uddhṛtam idam)
body.translated_text: (This verse is also cited in the <s>Daśarūpakāvaloka</s>.)

body.text: asyāś ceṣṭā, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: The tremors of first-sight shyness,
the dismissive attention to the chatter of her companions,
the sweetness of pretended anger — of the daughter of the mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>),
may those gestures at the new meeting protect you! ||1.268||

body.translated_text: Her behavior, as in my own [verse] —

body.text: atha dvitīya-yauvanam-

children.text: stanau pīnau tanur madhyaḥ pāṇipādasya raktimā | 169
children.translated_text: The breasts are full, the waist is slender, the hands and feet have redness; 169

children.text:
ūrū karikarākārāv aṅgaṃ vyaktāṅga-sandhikam |
nitambo vipulo nābhir gabhīrā jaghanaṃ ghanam ||SRs_1.269|| 170
vyaktā romāvalī snaigdhyam aṅga-keśaradākṣiṣu |
dvitīya-yauvane tena kalitā vāma-locanā ||SRs_1.270|| 171
sakhīṣu svāśayajñāsu snigdhā prāyeṇa māninī |
na prasīdaty anunaye sapatnīṣv abhyasūyinī ||SRs_1.271|| 172
nāparādhān viṣahate praṇayerṣyākaṣāyitā |
rati-keliṣv anibhṛtā ceṣṭate garvitā rahaḥ ||SRs_1.272|| 173
children.translated_text: The thighs are shaped like elephant trunks, the body has well-defined joints, the hips are broad, the navel deep, and the pelvis is full. ||SRs_1.269|| The line of hair on the abdomen is visible, and there is glossiness in the body-hair and complexion. In the second youth (dvitīya-yauvana), by this she is reckoned a <s>vāma-locanā</s> (one with sidelong glances). ||SRs_1.270|| She is affectionate toward companions who know her inner feelings, mostly proud (<s>māninī</s>), does not relent to entreaties, and is jealous toward co-wives. ||SRs_1.271|| She does not tolerate offenses, is embittered by the jealousy of love (<s>praṇaya-īrṣyā</s>), is uninhibited in love-play, and behaves haughtily in private. ||SRs_1.272||

body.translated_text: Now, the second youth —

body.text:
yathā-
tanvī śyāmā śikharī-daśanā pakva-bimbādharauṣṭhī
madhye kṣāmā cakita-hariṇī-prekṣaṇā nimna-nābhiḥ |
śroṇī-bhārād alasa-gamanā stoka-namrā stanābhyāṃ
yā tatra syād yuvatī-viṣaye sṛṣṭir ādyaiva dhātuḥ ||SRs_1.273|| [me.dū. 2.22]
body.translated_text: For example — Slender, dark-complexioned, with teeth like mountain peaks, with lips like ripe <s>bimba</s> fruits, narrow at the waist, with glances like those of a startled doe, with a deep navel, slow-gaited from the weight of her hips, slightly bowed by her breasts — whatever maiden there might be of such description, she would be the very first creation of the Creator in the domain of young women. ||SRs_1.273|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 2.22]

body.text:
atha tṛtīya-yauvanam-
asnigdhatā nayanayor gaṇḍayor mlāna-kāntitā |
vicchāyatā khara-sparśo' py aṅgānāṃ ślathatā manāk ||SRs_1.274|| 174
adhare masṛṇo rāgas tṛtīye yauvane bhavet |
tatra strīṇām iyaṃ ceṣṭā rati-tantra-vidagdhatā ||SRs_1.275|| 175
vallabhasyāparityāgas tadākarṣaṇa-kauśalam |
anādaro' parādheṣu sapatnīṣv apy amatsaraḥ ||SRs_1.276|| 176
body.translated_text: Now, the third youth (<s>tṛtīya-yauvana</s>) — There is a lack of luster in the eyes, faded radiance of the cheeks, loss of complexion, rough texture, and slight looseness of the limbs. ||SRs_1.274|| The color of the lips becomes smooth [i.e., faded] in the third youth. The conduct of women in this stage is expertise in the arts of love (<s>rati-tantra-vidagdhatā</s>). ||SRs_1.275|| She does not abandon her beloved, possesses skill in attracting him, disregards offenses, and is free from jealousy even toward co-wives. ||SRs_1.276||

body.text: yathā ānanda-kośa-prahasane-

children.translated_text: With faces blooming only through effort, and cheeks that are wrinkled,
with waists that have become fleshier, and breasts that have become slack,
even on the path of <s>Ratipati</s>'s (the God of Love's) bell [i.e., in the arena of love], these women surely
mock flowers that have loosened from their stalks. ||SRs_1.277||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Ānanda-kośa</s> farce (<s>prahasana</s>) —

body.text:
atha caturtha-yauvanam-
jarjaratvaṃ stana-śroṇi-gaṇḍoru-jaghanādiṣu |
nirmāṃsatā ca bhavati caturthe yauvane striyāḥ ||SRs_1.278|| 177
tatra ceṣṭā rati-vidhāv anutsāho' samarthatā |
sapatnīṣv ānukūlyaṃ ca kāntenāviraha-sthitiḥ ||SRs_1.279|| 178
body.translated_text: Now, the fourth youth (<s>caturtha-yauvana</s>) — There is flabbiness in the breasts, hips, cheeks, thighs, pelvis, and other parts, and the woman's body becomes emaciated in the fourth youth. ||SRs_1.278|| The conduct in this stage is lack of enthusiasm and incapacity in love-making, agreeableness toward co-wives, and maintaining a state of non-separation from the husband. ||SRs_1.279||

body.text: yathā ānanda-kośa-prahasane-

children.text: kṣāmaiś ca gaṇḍa-phalakair viralaiś ca dantair
children.translated_text: With emaciated cheekbones and sparse teeth,
with drooping breasts and conversations full of stories of the past,
with limbs slack without effort, never to be approached [for love],
they desire their husband's wagers — alas, these women with languid limbs! ||SRs_1.280||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Ānanda-kośa</s> farce (<s>prahasana</s>) —

body.text:
tatra śṛṅgāra-yogyatvaṃ sarasāhlāda-kāraṇam |
ādya-dvitīyayor eva na tṛtīya-caturthayoḥ ||SRs_1.281|| 179
body.translated_text: Of these, suitability for the erotic sentiment (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) and the capacity to produce heartfelt delight belong only to the first and second [stages of youth], not to the third and fourth. ||SRs_1.281||

body.text:
atha rūpam-
aṅgāny abhūṣitāny eva prakṣepādyair vibhūṣaṇaiḥ |
yena bhūṣitavad bhāti tad rūpam iti kathyate ||SRs_1.282|| 180
body.translated_text: Now, beauty (<s>rūpa</s>) — That by which the limbs, even without being adorned by ornaments such as decorative marks and the like, shine as if adorned — that is called <s>rūpa</s> (beauty). ||SRs_1.282||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: A certain woman of surpassing beauty (<s>udāra-rūpā</s>), having removed her ornaments,
unable to bear adorning her body again
with garlands and other adornments, went outside,
and seeing her, those who were adorned felt ashamed. ||SRs_1.283||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha lāvaṇyam-
muktāphaleṣu chāyāyās taralatvam ivāntarā |
pratibhāti yad aṅgeṣu lāvaṇyaṃ tad ihocyate ||SRs_1.284|| 181
body.translated_text: Now, charm (<s>lāvaṇya</s>) — That which shines forth in the limbs like an inner shimmering of luster within pearls — that is called <s>lāvaṇya</s> (charm). ||SRs_1.284||

children.translated_text: For example —
In limbs as beautiful as crystal mirrors, there radiates
a pure, soft radiance, as if moonlight were reflected therein. ||SRs_1.285||

body.text:
atha saundaryam-
aṅga-pratyāngakānāṃ yaḥ sanniveśo yathocitam |
susliṣṭa-sandhi-bandhaḥ syāt tat saundaryam itīryate ||SRs_1.286|| 182
body.translated_text: Now, handsomeness (<s>saundarya</s>) — That arrangement of major and minor limbs in due proportion, with well-knit joints and connections — that is called <s>saundarya</s> (handsomeness). ||SRs_1.286||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: With long eyes, a face of autumnal moon's radiance, arms reaching down to the shoulders,

children.text: saṅkṣiptaṃ niviḍonnata-stanam uraḥ pārśve pramṛṣṭe iva |
children.translated_text: a compact chest with firm, upraised breasts, sides as if smoothly polished,

children.text: madhyaḥ pāṇim ito nitambi jaghanaṃ pādāvarālaṅgulī
children.translated_text: a waist [fitting] a hand, broad-hipped, with well-shaped toes on the feet —

children.text: chando nartayitur yathaiva manasi śliṣṭaṃ tathāsyā vapuḥ ||SRs_1.287||
children.translated_text: just as the meter [resides] in the mind of the dancer, so is her body perfectly composed. ||SRs_1.287||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (mālavikāgni-mitram 2.3)
body.translated_text: (<s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 2.3)

body.text:
atha abhirūpatā-
yadātmīya-guṇotkarṣair vastv anyan nikaṭa-sthitam |
sārūpyaṃ nayati prājñair ābhirūpyaṃ tad ucyate ||SRs_1.288|| 183
body.translated_text: Now, comeliness (<s>ābhirūpya</s>) — When something, through the excellence of its own qualities, brings a nearby object to a state of resemblance [with itself], that is called <s>ābhirūpya</s> (comeliness) by the wise. ||SRs_1.288||

body.text:
yathā-
eko' pi traya iva bhāti kanduko' yaṃ
kāntāyāḥ karatala-rāga-rakta-raktaḥ |
bhūmau tac-caraṇa-nakhāṃśu-gaura-gauraḥ
khasthaḥ san nayana-marīci-nīla-nīlaḥ ||SRs_1.289|| (bhoja-caritre 298)
body.translated_text: For example — Even though this ball is one, it appears as if three: red-red from the redness of the beloved's palm, white-white from the rays of her toenails when on the ground, and blue-blue from the glances of her eyes when in the sky. ||SRs_1.289|| (In <s>Bhoja-caritra</s> 298)

body.text:
atha mārdavam-
spṛṣṭaṃ yatrāṅgam aspṛṣṭam iva syān mārdavaṃ hi tat ||SRs_1.290|| 184ab
body.translated_text: Now, softness (<s>mārdava</s>) — That by which a limb, when touched, seems as if untouched — that indeed is <s>mārdava</s> (softness). ||SRs_1.290||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: From those [thighs], glimpsed through the intervening silk garment,
the gaze slips away due to their quality of smoothness.
Therefore, even at the time of creation, the Creator's hands
had the apprehension of [daring to] touch those thighs. ||SRs_1.291||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra amūrtāpi dṛṣṭir visraṃsate | mūrtau karau kim uteti ślakṣṇatvātiśaya-kathanān mārdavam |
body.translated_text: Here, even the immaterial gaze slips away — how much more so the material hands! This describes <s>mārdava</s> (softness) through the declaration of an extreme degree of smoothness.

body.text: atha saukumāryam-

children.translated_text: That inability of the limbs to bear the touch even of a soft object —
that is <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy), which is threefold: superior, middling, and inferior. ||SRs_1.292||

body.translated_text: Now, delicacy (<s>saukumārya</s>) —

body.text:
atha uttama-saukumāryam-
aṅgaṃ puṣpādi-saṃsparśāsahaṃ yena tad uttamam ||SRs_1.293|| 185
body.translated_text: Now, superior delicacy (<s>uttama-saukumārya</s>) — That by which a limb cannot bear the touch even of flowers and the like — that is the superior [degree]. ||SRs_1.293||

body.text:
yathā-
mahārha-śayyā-parivartana-cyutaiḥ
svakeśa-puṣpair api yā sma dūyate |
aśeta sā bāhu-latopadhāyinī
niṣeduṣī sthaṇḍila eva kevale ||SRs_1.294|| [ku.saṃ. 5.12]
body.translated_text: For example — She who used to suffer even from the flowers fallen from her own hair on a luxurious bed as she tossed, she, using [his] arm-creeper as a pillow, slept on the bare ground itself. ||SRs_1.294|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 5.12]

body.text: atra yadyapy uttarārdhe sthaṇḍila-sparśa-sahatvam uktam | tathāpi sthirāgrahasyaiva manasaḥ kleśa-sahiṣṇutvaṃ pratīyate na punaḥ śarīrasyety atrottama-saukumāryam upapadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, although in the latter half tolerance of contact with the bare ground is stated, what is understood is the endurance of hardship by a mind firm in resolve, not by the body — thus superior delicacy (<s>uttama-saukumārya</s>) is established here.

body.text:
atha madhyama-saukumāryam-
na saheta kara-sparśaṃ yenāṅgaṃ madhyamaṃ hi tat ||SRs_1.295|| 186ab
body.translated_text: Now, middling delicacy (<s>madhyama-saukumārya</s>) — That by which a limb cannot bear even the touch of a hand — that is the middling [degree]. ||SRs_1.295||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: No sooner was the forefoot of a certain woman barely touched
by the hand of her friend, soft as a young lotus,
for the purpose of applying lac-dye, than it turned red,

children.text: lākṣā-rasaḥ punar abhūn na tu bhūṣaṇāya ||SRs_1.296||
children.translated_text: but the lac-dye itself was of no use as ornament [since her foot was already naturally red]. ||SRs_1.296||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (utprekṣā-vallabhasyeti sūkti-muktāvaliḥ)
body.translated_text: (From the <s>Sūkti-muktāvali</s> of <s>Utprekṣā-vallabha</s>)

body.text:
atha adhama-saukumāryam-
yenāṅgamātapādīnām asahaṃ tad ihādhamam ||SRs_1.297|| 186
body.translated_text: Now, inferior delicacy (<s>adhama-saukumārya</s>) — That by which a limb cannot bear sunlight and the like — that is called the inferior [degree] here. ||SRs_1.297||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Bearing fragrance and giving delight,
with bees nestled like dark curls upon it,
the lotus-face of <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) in an instant became
copper-hued even by the soft radiance of the sun. ||SRs_1.298||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: tac-ceṣṭā līlā-vilāsādayaḥ | te' py anubhāva-prakaraṇe vakṣyante |
body.translated_text: Her behavior [includes] <s>līlā</s> (grace), <s>vilāsa</s> (coquetry), and so forth. These too will be discussed in the section on <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions).

body.text:
atha alaṅkṛtiḥ-
caturdhālaṅkṛtir vāso-bhūṣā-mālyānulepanaiḥ ||SRs_1.299|| 187ab
body.translated_text: Now, adornment (<s>alaṅkṛti</s>) — Adornment is fourfold: by garments, ornaments, garlands, and unguents. ||SRs_1.299||

body.text: tatra vastrālaṅkāro, yathā-
body.translated_text: Of these, adornment by garments, for example —

body.text:
kṣīroda-veleva saphena-puñjā
paryāpta-candreva śarat-triyāmā |
navaṃ nava-kṣauma-nivāsinī sā
bhūyo babhau darpaṇam ādadhānā ||SRs_1.300|| [ku.saṃ. 7.26]
body.translated_text: Like the shore of the Milk Ocean with its heaps of foam, like an autumnal night fully endowed with moonlight, she, clad in a new linen garment, shone even more, holding a mirror. ||SRs_1.300|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 7.26]

body.text: bhūṣālaṅkāro, yathā-
body.translated_text: Adornment by ornaments, for example —

body.text:
sā sambhavadbhiḥ kusumair lateva
jyotirbhir udyadbhir iva triyāmā | sarid vihaṅgair iva līyamānair
āmucyamānābharaṇā cakāśe ||SRs_1.301|| [ku.saṃ. 7.27]
body.translated_text: She shone like a creeper with its flowers blossoming forth, like the night with its luminaries rising, like a river with birds alighting — as her ornaments were being put on. ||SRs_1.301|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 7.27]

body.text: mālyānulepanālaṅkāro, yathā-
body.translated_text: Adornment by garlands and unguents, for example —

children.translated_text: The wearing of garlands in her hair is inferred by the restless bees,

children.text: kāntiḥ kāpi kapolayoḥ prathayate tāmbūlam antargatam |
children.translated_text: a certain radiance on her cheeks reveals the betel within,
the process of anointing her limbs is perceived through their fragrance —

children.text: veṣaḥ ko' pi vidagdha eṣa sudṛśaḥ sūte sukhaṃ cakṣuṣoḥ ||SRs_1.302||
children.translated_text: some indescribable, refined attire of the beautiful-eyed woman produces delight to the eyes. ||SRs_1.302||

body.text: atha taṭasthāḥ-

children.translated_text: The external [stimulants] are moonlight, shower-pavilion, and moonrise,

children.text:
kokilālāpam ākanda-manda-māruta-ṣaṭ-padāḥ |
latā-maṇḍapa-bhūgeha-dīrghikā-jala-dāravāḥ ||SRs_1.303|| 188
prāsāda-garbha-saṅgīta-krīḍādri-sarid-ādayaḥ |
evam ūhyā yathā kālam upabhogopayoginaḥ ||SRs_1.304|| 189
children.translated_text: the song of the cuckoo, the mango tree, the gentle breeze, bees, the bower of creepers, the underground chamber, the water-channel, and rain; palace chambers, music, pleasure-hills, rivers, and so forth. Thus [other stimulants] should be inferred as appropriate to the season and conducive to enjoyment. ||SRs_1.303-304||

body.translated_text: Now, the external stimulants (<s>taṭastha</s>) —

body.text: tatra candrikāya uddīpanatvam, yathā-

children.translated_text: When moonlight made [the outdoors] inaccessible, the graceful one was hidden
by her group of companions in a bower of creepers.
But seeing from somewhere a drop of moonlight fallen from a <s>cakora</s> bird's beak,

children.text: kuto' pi dṛṣṭvā bhajati sma mūrcchanām ||SRs_1.305||
children.translated_text: she fell into a swoon. ||SRs_1.305||

body.translated_text: Of these, the stimulating power of moonlight (<s>candrikā</s>), for example —

body.text: dhārā-gṛhasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: She, unable to remain even on the moonstone terrace
beloved of the moon,
having reached the shower-pavilion, regarded even that
as a house of the terrible sword-edges of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless God of Love). ||SRs_1.306||

body.translated_text: Of the shower-pavilion (<s>dhārā-gṛha</s>), for example —

body.text: candrodayasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: The disc of the moon has arrived at the eastern mountain —
look, friend, by it we have been deceived!
Shall you take me to my own house here,

children.text: tatra vā kim iti vivyathe vadhūḥ ||SRs_1.307||
children.translated_text: or what [shall we do] there? — thus the young bride was distressed. ||SRs_1.307||

body.translated_text: Of moonrise (<s>candrodaya</s>), for example —

body.text:
kokilālāpasya, yathā-
cūtāṅkurāsvāda-kaṣāya-kaṇṭhaḥ
puṃskokilo yan madhuraṃ cukūja |
manasvinī-māna-vighāta-dakṣaṃ
tad eva jātaṃ vacanaṃ smarasya ||SRs_1.308|| [ku.saṃ. 3.32]
body.translated_text: Of the song of the cuckoo (<s>kokilālāpa</s>), for example — The male cuckoo, whose throat is bitter from tasting mango sprouts, sang sweetly; that very [song] became a speech of <s>Smara</s> (the God of Love), capable of destroying the pride of proud women. ||SRs_1.308|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.32]

body.text: mākandasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: This young mango tree, long nurtured
by waterings from pots poured by one's own hands,
now produces the arrows of the Flower-weaponed one (<s>Kusumāyudha</s>, <s>Kāmadeva</s>) —
thus indeed with milk one nourishes a serpent. ||SRs_1.309||

body.translated_text: Of the mango tree (<s>mākanda</s>), for example —

body.text: mākanda ity aśokādīnām upalakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: <s>Mākanda</s> (mango) is used here as a representative term for the <s>aśoka</s> and other trees as well.

body.text: manda-mārutasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: Having been deeply inhaled by the serpent-women
and exhaled together with their venom,

children.text: tad anyathā cet katham akṣiṇot tām
children.translated_text: for how else could it have harmed her? —
the ungracious southern wind (<s>dakṣiṇa-mātariśvan</s>). ||SRs_1.310||

body.translated_text: Of the gentle breeze (<s>manda-māruta</s>), for example —

body.text: ṣaṭpada-svanasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: With their sweet humming, like unprecedented <s>mantras</s>,
the bees, languid with intoxication,
of the beauty of spring (<s>madhu-śrī</s>),
perform the exorcism of the pride-spirit from proud women. ||SRs_1.311||

body.translated_text: Of the sound of bees (<s>ṣaṭpada-svana</s>), for example —

body.text: latā-maṇḍapasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: Here is an areca grove with flowers in full bloom, with mango trees all around,
in its midst also a lake with a gentle breeze carrying the bliss of love-play's conclusion,
on its bank a plantain-bower, beautifully adorned, and within it

children.text: vallī-maṇḍapam atra sā sunayanā tvan-mārgam avekṣate ||SRs_1.312||
children.translated_text: a pavilion of <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) creepers — there the beautiful-eyed one awaits your path. ||SRs_1.312||

body.translated_text: Of the bower of creepers (<s>latā-maṇḍapa</s>), for example —

body.text: bhūgehasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: In the underground chambers, fragrant with the sweet scent
of black <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) smoke and perfumed with incense,
men sheltered in the warmth of dark-complexioned women's bosoms
did not tremble before the winter winds. ||SRs_1.313||

body.translated_text: Of the underground chamber (<s>bhū-geha</s>), for example —

body.text:
dīrghikāyā, yathā-
etasmin mada-kala-mallikākṣa-pakṣa-
vyādhūta-sphurad-uru-daṇḍa-puṇḍarīkāḥ |
bāṣpāmbhaḥ paripatanodgamāntarāle
dṛśantām avirahita-śriyo vibhāgāḥ ||SRs_1.314|| (mālatī-mādhava 9.14)
body.translated_text: Of the water-channel (<s>dīrghikā</s>), for example — In this [canal], the lotuses with great shaking stalks, their petals tossed by intoxicated bees with <s>mallikā</s>-flower eyes, appear in the intervals of falling and rising tear-drops — let these splendid portions be beheld, never bereft of beauty. ||SRs_1.314|| (<s>Mālatī-Mādhava</s> 9.14)

body.text: jaladāravasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: The pride even of the minds of proud women
was so removed by the thundering of the clouds
that, though embracing those of known offenses,
the clever women appeared angry only for a moment. ||SRs_1.315||

body.translated_text: Of the sound of rain (<s>jaladārava</s>), for example —

body.text: atra jaladārava-grahaṇaṃ vidyud-ādīnām apy upalakṣaṇam | vidyuto, yathā-
body.translated_text: Here, the mention of the sound of rain (<s>jaladārava</s>) serves as a representative term for lightning and the like as well. Of lightning (<s>vidyut</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: In those rains, illuminated for an instant,
a cowherd woman embraced <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
and the lightning, seeing the beauty of his limbs,
as if ashamed, quickly entered the cloud. ||SRs_1.316||

body.text: prāsāda-garbhasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: In those palace chambers where peacocks perched on the rafters
and pigeons rested on the pigeon-ledges,
inaccessible to the rain-bearing winds,
he sported, with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic pleasure) as his second [companion]. ||SRs_1.317||

body.translated_text: Of the palace chamber (<s>prāsāda-garbha</s>), for example —

body.text: saṅgītasya, yathā-

children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), in the bower of sweet <s>mādhavī</s> creepers,
amid the loudly buzzing bees,
sang with his flute, sweet to the ears,
which was [like] a fish-hook for the pride of the <s>gopikās</s> (cowherd women). ||SRs_1.318||

body.translated_text: Of music (<s>saṅgīta</s>), for example —

body.text:
krīḍādrer, yathā-
nīcair ākhyaṃ girim adhivases tatra viśrāma-hetos
tvat-samparkāt pulakitam iva prauḍha-puṣpaiḥ kadambaiḥ |
yaḥ puṇya-strī-rati-parimalodgāribhir nāgarāṇām
uddāmāni prathayati śilā-veśmabhir yauvanāni ||SRs_1.319|| [me.dū. 1.26]
body.translated_text: Of the pleasure-mountain, as for example — 'You dwell on a low-named mountain for the sake of rest, where, as if thrilling from your contact, the <s>kadamba</s> trees bear full blossoms; which, with its stone pavilions emitting the fragrance of the lovemaking of virtuous women, displays the unbridled passions of the townsfolk.' ||1.319|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 1.26]

body.text:
sarito, yathā-
athormi-mālonmada-rāja-haṃse
rodho-latā-puṣpa-vahe sarayvāḥ |
vihartum icchā vanitā-sakhasya
tasyāmbhasi grīṣma-sukhe babhūva ||SRs_1.320|| (ra.vaṃ. 16.54)
body.translated_text: Of rivers, as for example — 'Then, in the waters of the <s>Sarayū</s>, bearing the flowers of creepers on its banks, with royal swans maddened by garlands of waves, the desire to sport arose in the friend of women, [the waters being] pleasant in summer.' ||1.320|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 16.54)

body.text: ity ādy anyad apy udāhāryam |
body.translated_text: And so forth — other examples may also be cited.

body.text: athānubhāvāḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions) —

body.text:
ālambana-gatāś ceṣṭā anubhāvā vivakṣitāḥ |
bhāvaṃ manogataṃ sākṣāt sva-hetuṃ vyañjayanti ye |
te' nubhāvā iti khyātā bhrū-kṣepa-smitādayaḥ ||SRs_1.321|| 190
te caturdhā citta-gātra-vāg-buddhyārambha-sambhavāḥ |
tatra ca bhāvo hāvo helā śobhā kānti-dīptī ca ||SRs_1.322|| 191
prāgalbhyaṃ mādhuryaṃ dhairyaudāryaṃ ca cittajā bhāvāḥ |
nirvikārasya cittasya bhāvaḥ syād ādi-vikriyā ||SRs_1.323|| 192
body.translated_text: The actions residing in the <s>ālambana</s> (substrate) are called <s>Anubhāvas</s>. Those that directly manifest the mental state, their own cause, are known as <s>Anubhāvas</s> — such as raising of the eyebrows, smiling, and the like. ||1.321|| 190 They are of four kinds, arising from mind, body, speech, and intellectual effort. Of these, the mental ones are: <s>Bhāva</s> (nascent emotion), <s>Hāva</s> (coquetry), <s>Helā</s> (playful display), <s>Śobhā</s> (radiance), <s>Kānti</s> (loveliness), <s>Dīpti</s> (brilliance), ||1.322|| 191 <s>Prāgalbhya</s> (boldness), <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>Dhairya</s> (fortitude), and <s>Audārya</s> (magnanimity) — these are the <s>bhāvas</s> born of the mind. <s>Bhāva</s> is the initial transformation of a mind that was previously undisturbed. ||1.323|| 192

body.text: tatra bhāvaḥ, tathoktaṃ hi prāktanair api-
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>Bhāva</s> — as stated also by earlier authorities:

body.text:
cittasyāvikṛtiḥ sattvaṃ vikṛteḥ kāraṇe sati |
tatrādyā vikriyā bhāvo bījasyādi-vikāravat ||SRs_1.324|| iti |
(from Śāradatanaya's Bhāva-prakāśa)
body.translated_text: 'The natural state of the mind is <s>sattva</s> (purity); when a cause of transformation arises, the first transformation thereof is <s>bhāva</s>, like the initial sprouting of a seed.' ||1.324|| Thus. (from <s>Śāradatanaya</s>'s <s>Bhāva-prakāśa</s>)

body.text:
bhāvo, yathā mamaiva-
bālā prasādhana-vidhau nidadhāti cittaṃ
dattādarā pariṇaye maṇi-putrikāṇām |
sā śaṅkate nija-sakhī-jana-manda-hāsair
ālakṣyate tad iha bhāvanavāvatāraḥ ||SRs_1.325|| (above 1.154)
body.translated_text: <s>Bhāva</s>, as in my own [verse] — 'A young girl fixes her mind on the ritual of adornment, bestowing care on the wedding of her gem-dolls; she becomes apprehensive at the gentle laughter of her own companions — here is observed the first descent of <s>Bhāva</s> (nascent love).' ||1.325|| (same as 1.154 above)

body.text: atra pūrvaṃ śaiśavena rasānabhijñasya cittasya prasādhana-vidhitsā-pāñcālikā-pariṇayādara-sakhī-jana-hāsa-śaṅkādīnāṃ tat-prathamam eva sambhūtatvād bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the mind, previously innocent through childhood and unacquainted with <s>rasa</s>, experiences for the very first time the desire for self-adornment, the care for the wedding of dolls, the apprehension at the laughter of friends, and so forth — this is <s>Bhāva</s>.

body.text:
atha hāvaḥ-
grīvā-recaka-saṃyukto bhrū-netrādi-vilāsa-kṛt |
bhāva īṣat-prakāśo yaḥ sa hāva iti kathyate ||SRs_1.326|| 193
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Hāva</s> (coquetry) — That <s>Bhāva</s> which, accompanied by movements of the neck, produces play of the eyebrows, eyes, and the like, and which is slightly manifest, is called <s>Hāva</s>. ||1.326|| 193

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: By the words of her nurse, whose sounds carried hidden meanings,
for a moment she felt shame mixed with an angry smile;
she joined together a pair of dolls
as bride and groom from among her own companions. ||1.327||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text: atra citta-vikārāṇāṃ roṣa-harṣa-lajjādīnāṃ kuṭilekṣaṇa-smita-natānanatvādibhir īṣat-prakāśanād ayaṃ hāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the mental transformations — anger, joy, shame, and the like — are only slightly manifested through sidelong glances, smiles, bowing of the face, and so forth, this is <s>Hāva</s>.

body.text:
atha helā-
nānā-vikāraiḥ suvyaktaḥ śṛṅgārākṛti-sūcakaiḥ |
hāva eva bhaved dhelā lalitābhinayātmikā ||SRs_1.328|| 194
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Helā</s> (playful display) — <s>Hāva</s> itself, when clearly expressed through various transformations indicative of the erotic mood, and consisting of graceful acting, becomes <s>Helā</s>. ||1.328|| 194

body.text:
yathā-
vivṛṇvatī śaila-sutā bhāvam aṅgaiḥ
sphurad bāla-kadamba-kalpaiḥ |
sācīkṛtā cārutareṇa tasthau
mukhena paryasta-vilocanena ||SRs_1.329|| [ku.saṃ. 3.68]
body.translated_text: As for example — 'The daughter of the mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>), revealing her emotion through limbs resembling budding young <s>kadamba</s> blossoms, stood with her face averted most charmingly, with eyes turned aside.' ||1.329|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.68]

body.text: atra romāñca-mukha-sācīkaraṇa-paryasta-vilocanatvādi-vikāraiś citta-vyāpārasyātiprakāśatvena helā |
body.translated_text: Here, because the mental activity is excessively manifest through transformations such as horripilation, averting the face, turning the eyes aside, and so forth, this is <s>Helā</s>.

body.text:
tatra śobhā--
sā śobhā rūpa-bhogādyair yat syād aṅga-vibhūṣaṇam ||SRs_1.330|| 195ab
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>Śobhā</s> (radiance) — <s>Śobhā</s> is the adornment of the body through beauty of form, enjoyment, and the like. ||1.330|| 195ab

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: With body-paint half remaining from a tight embrace,
hair-braid fallen on the shoulder from the unceasing vigor of lovemaking,
rising from the bedchamber at dawn, stumbling,
holding her waist-garment with her palm, with timid eyes — may we worship her! ||1.331||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text:
atha kāntiḥ--
śobhaiva kāntir ākhyātā manmathāpyāyanojjvalā ||SRs_1.332|| 195cd
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Kānti</s> (loveliness) — <s>Śobhā</s> itself, when brilliant with the gratification of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), is called <s>Kānti</s>. ||1.332|| 195cd

body.text: yathā-

children.text: uttiṣṭhantyā ratānte bharam uragapatau pāṇinaikena kṛtvā
children.translated_text: As she rises at the end of lovemaking, placing on the lord of serpents (<s>Śeṣa</s>) the weight with one hand,

children.text: dhṛtvā cānyena vāsaḥ śithilita-kavarī-bhāram aṃse vahantyāḥ |
children.translated_text: holding her garment with the other, bearing on her shoulder the weight of her loosened braid,
may the body of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, languid with beautifully drooping arms, embraced back to the bed

children.text: śayyām āliṅgya nītaṃ vapur alasa-lasad-bāhu lakṣmyāḥ punātu ||SRs_1.333||
children.translated_text: by <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), whose delight in lovemaking was doubled by her beauty at that moment, purify you! ||1.333||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text: (veṇī-saṃhāra 1.3)
body.translated_text: (from <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 1.3)

body.text: atra pūrva-ratānta-janitāyā vapuḥ-kānter uttara-ratārambha-hetutvān manmathāpyāyakatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, because the bodily loveliness born of the preceding lovemaking becomes the cause of renewed lovemaking, it has the quality of gratifying <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) — hence <s>Kānti</s>.

body.text:
atha dīptiḥ--
kāntir eva vayo-bhoga-deśa-kāla-guṇādibhiḥ |
uddīpitātivistāraṃ yātā ced dīptir ucyate ||SRs_1.334|| 196
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Dīpti</s> (brilliance) — If <s>Kānti</s> itself, stimulated by age, enjoyment, place, time, qualities, and the like, expands to a great extent, it is called <s>Dīpti</s>. ||1.334|| 196

body.text:
yathā-
yatra strīṇāṃ priyatama-bhujocchvāsitāliṅgitānām
aṅga-glāniṃ surata-janitāṃ tantu-jālāvalambāḥ |
tvat-saṃrodhāpagama-viśadaś candra-pādair niśīthe
vyālumpanti sphuṭa-jala-lava-syandinaś candra-kāntāḥ ||SRs_1.335|| [meghadūta 2.9]
body.translated_text: As for example — 'Where the moonstone columns, dripping with clear water drops, made transparent by the cessation of your obstruction, with moonbeams at midnight, wipe away the fatigue born of lovemaking from the limbs of women who are embraced, lifted by the arms of their most beloved, supported by nets of threads.' ||1.335|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 2.9]

body.text: atra priyatamāliṅgana-saudha-jyotsnādi-guṇaiḥ surata-glāni-vyālopanād uttara-suratotsāha-rūpā dīptiḥ pratīyate |
body.translated_text: Here, through qualities such as the beloved's embrace, the palace, the moonlight, and so forth, the wiping away of the fatigue of lovemaking produces <s>Dīpti</s>, which has the form of renewed enthusiasm for further lovemaking.

body.text:
atha prāgalbhyam--
niḥśaṅkatvaṃ prayogeṣu prāgalbhyaṃ parikīrtyate ||SRs_1.336|| 197ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Prāgalbhya</s> (boldness) — Fearlessness in practice is called <s>Prāgalbhya</s>. ||1.336|| 197ab

body.text:
śiṣyatāṃ nidhuvanopadeśinaḥ
śaṅkarasya rahasi prapannayā |
śikṣitaṃ yuvati-naipuṇaṃ tayā
yat tad eva guru-dakṣiṇī-kṛtam ||SRs_1.337|| [ku.saṃ. 8.17]
body.translated_text: 'Having become his pupil in private, the instructor of <s>Nidhuvana</s> (the art of love) being <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) himself, that skill in womanly arts which she was taught — that itself became her preceptor's fee.' ||1.337|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.17]

body.text: atra guru-dakṣiṇī-kṛtam ity anena pratikaraṇa-rūpaṃ prāgalbhyaṃ pratīyate |
body.translated_text: Here, by the phrase 'became the preceptor's fee,' <s>Prāgalbhya</s> in the form of reciprocation is perceived.

body.text:
atha mādhuryam--
mādhuryaṃ nāma ceṣṭānāṃ sarvāvasthāsu mārdavam ||SRs_1.338|| 197cd
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness) — <s>Mādhurya</s> is the softness of actions in all states. ||1.338|| 197cd

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Placing her left hand on her hip, with bangles stilled at the joint,
extending the other [arm] like a dark creeper-branch, relaxed and free,
her gaze cast down to the pavement where flowers are disturbed by her toe —

children.text: nṛttād asyāḥ sthitam atitarāṃ kāntam ṛjvāyatārdham ||SRs_1.339||
children.translated_text: her stance after the dance, erect and half-extended, is exceedingly lovely. ||1.339||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text: (mālavikāgni-mitram 2.6)
body.translated_text: (from <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 2.6)

body.text:
atra pādāṅguṣṭhena kusuma-lolanādi-kriyāṇāṃ nṛttānta-pariśrāntāv api cārutvān[*4] mādhuryam |
[*4] Note that cārutā, as found in Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi, is the word used here in the place of mārdava.
body.translated_text: Here, because actions such as disturbing flowers with the toe possess charm even in the fatigue after dance — this is <s>Mādhurya</s>. [Note: <s>cārutā</s>, as found in <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>, is the word used here in place of <s>mārdava</s>.]

body.text:
atha dhairyam-
sthirā cittonnatir yā tu tad dhairyam iti saṃjñitam ||SRs_1.340|| 198ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Dhairya</s> (fortitude) — The steady elevation of the mind is called <s>Dhairya</s>. ||1.340|| 198ab

body.text:
yathā-
atha viśvātmane gaurī sandideśa mithaḥ sakhīm |
dātā me bhūtbhṛtāṃ nāthaḥ pramāṇīkriyatām iti ||SRs_1.341|| [ku.sam. 6.1]
body.translated_text: As for example — 'Then <s>Gaurī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) secretly conveyed a message to the lord of all beings through her friend: "Let my father, the lord of mountains, be made the authority [to give me away]."' ||1.341|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 6.1]

body.text:
atha audāryam-
audāryaṃ vinayaṃ prāhuḥ sarvāvasthānugaṃ budhāḥ ||SRs_1.342|| 198cd
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Audārya</s> (magnanimity) — The wise call <s>Audārya</s> that modesty which accompanies all states. ||1.342|| 198cd

body.text:
yathā-
kalyāṇa-buddher athavā tavāyaṃ
na kāma-cāro mayi śaṅkanīyaḥ |
mamaiva janmāntara-pātakānāṃ
vipāka-visphūrjathur aprasahyaḥ ||SRs_1.343|| (ra.vaṃ. 14.62)
body.translated_text: As for example — 'Or perhaps, for one of your noble disposition, this willful conduct toward me should not be suspected; it is the ripening of my own sins from a previous birth — an irresistible thunderclap.' ||1.343|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 14.62)

body.text: atrānaparādhe' pi niṣkāsayato rāmasyānupālambhāt sītāyā audāryaṃ pratīyate | sarvāvasthā-samatvāviditeṅgitākāratva-rūpayor lakṣaṇayoś citta-dhairya evāntarbhūtatvāt bhoja-rāja-lakṣitau sthairya-gāmbhīrya-rūpāv anyau dvau cittārambhau cāsmad-ukte dhairya evāntarbhūtāv iti daśaiva cittārambhāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because <s>Sītā</s> does not reproach <s>Rāma</s> even though he banishes her without fault, <s>Audārya</s> is perceived. Since the two qualities of equanimity in all states and imperceptibility of gestures and expressions are already included within mental fortitude (<s>Dhairya</s>), the two further mental dispositions of steadiness and depth as identified by <s>Bhoja-rāja</s> are also subsumed under our definition of <s>Dhairya</s> — thus there are only ten mental dispositions.

body.text:
atha gātrārambhāḥ-
līlā vilāso vicchittir vibhramaḥ kilakiñcitam |

children.translated_text: <s>Moṭṭāyita</s> (manifestation of desire), <s>Kuṭṭamita</s> (feigned anger), <s>Bibboka</s> (studied indifference), <s>Lalita</s> (graceful movement), and likewise 199

children.text: vihṛtaṃ ceti vijñeyā yoṣitāṃ daśa gātrajāḥ ||SRs_1.344||
children.translated_text: <s>Vihṛta</s> (playful diversion) — these ten are known to arise from the body of women. ||1.344||

body.translated_text: Now, the physical expressions (<s>Gātrārambhāḥ</s>) — <s>Līlā</s> (sportive imitation), <s>Vilāsa</s> (coquettish display), <s>Vicchitti</s> (effortless elegance), <s>Vibhrama</s> (confused disarray),  <s>Kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotions),

body.text: tatra līlā-

children.translated_text: That which consists of imitating the beloved with sweet speech, 200

children.text: ceṣṭitair gatibhir vā syāt sā līleti nigadyate ||SRs_1.345||
children.translated_text: gestures, and gaits is called <s>Līlā</s>. ||1.345||

body.translated_text: Of these, <s>Līlā</s> (sportive imitation) —

body.text:
yathā-
duṣṭa-kāliya tiṣṭhādya kṛṣṇo' ham iti cāparā |
bāhum āsphoṭya kṛṣṇasya līlā-sarvasvam ādade ||SRs_1.346|| [vi.pu. 5.13.27]
body.translated_text: As for example — 'Another [<s>gopī</s>], slapping her own arm and saying "O wicked <s>Kāliya</s>, stand still, I am <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!" took on the full essence of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>Līlā</s>.' ||1.346|| [<s>Viṣṇu-purāṇa</s> 5.13.27]

body.text: atha vilāsaḥ-

children.translated_text: At the time of meeting with the beloved, the special transformation 201

children.text: tātkāliko viśeṣo yaḥ sa vilāsa itīritaḥ ||SRs_1.347||
children.translated_text: of eyebrows, eyes, and face that occurs at that moment is called <s>Vilāsa</s>. ||1.347||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vilāsa</s> (coquettish display) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: The young maiden, half-hidden behind the creeper-like body of her friend,
gazing upon you with innocent, sweet, languid sidelong glances,
O husband of <s>Siṃha-kṣamā</s>, [struck] by the bewildering weapons of the mind-born [Love] —
she remains long like <s>Lakṣmī</s> painted on a wall. ||1.348||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text:
atha vicchittiḥ-
ākalpa-kalpanālpāpi vicchittir atikānti-kṛt ||SRs_1.349|| 202
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vicchitti</s> (effortless elegance) — Even a minimal effort in arranging adornments, when it produces extraordinary beauty, is <s>Vicchitti</s>. ||1.349|| 202

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: The presence of a garland in her hair is detected by the restless bees,

children.text: kāntiḥ kāpi kapolayoḥ prathayate tāmbūlam antargatam |
children.translated_text: some indefinable radiance on her cheeks betrays the betel within,
the application of unguents to her limbs is inferred from their fragrance —

children.text: veṣaḥ ko' pi vidagdha eṣa sudṛśaḥ sūte sukhaṃ cakṣuṣoḥ ||SRs_1.350||
children.translated_text: some indescribable, artful attire of the beautiful-eyed one gives delight to the eyes. ||1.350||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text:
atha vibhramaḥ-
priyā-gamana-velāyāṃ madanāveśa-sambhramāt |
vibhramo' ṅgada-hārādi-bhūṣā-sthāna-viparyayaḥ ||SRs_1.351|| 203
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vibhrama</s> (confused disarray) — At the time of the beloved's arrival, due to the agitation of the onset of <s>Madana</s> (Love), <s>Vibhrama</s> is the misplacement of ornaments such as armlets, necklaces, and the like. ||1.351|| 203

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: One woman placed her girdle-band on the pair of her breast-globes
smeared with white sandalwood paste;
another, her gaze sent toward her beloved,
tied her necklace upon the orb of her hip. ||1.352||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text:
atha kilakiñcitam-
śoka-roṣāśru-harṣādeḥ saṅkaraḥ kila-kiñcitam ||SRs_1.353|| 204ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotions) — <s>Kilakiñcita</s> is the mingling of grief, anger, tears, joy, and the like. ||1.353|| 204ab

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: When the wager made at dice with her friends was given
and [the lover] was about to speak, she, with eyebrows furrowed,
clasping his neck with both hands,
covered his mouth with her cheek. ||1.354||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text: yathā vā-

children.translated_text: In the game of love-play, having somehow obtained the forfeit,
when I [seized] her lower lip with its sweet, melodious voice —
with furrowed brows, she displayed a face [expressing] half-embarrassment, half-weeping,

children.text: smita-krodhodbhrāntaṃ punar api vidadhyān mayi mukham ||SRs_1.355||
children.translated_text: smiling, anger, and bewilderment, turned again toward me. ||1.355||

body.translated_text: Or as —

body.text: (dhanikasya avalokaḥ to da.rū. 2.39)
body.translated_text: (from <s>Dhanika</s>'s <s>Avaloka</s> on <s>Daśarūpaka</s> 2.39)

body.text:
atha moṭṭāyitam-
svābhilāṣa-prakaṭam moṭṭāyitam itīritam ||SRs_1.356|| 204
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Moṭṭāyita</s> (manifestation of desire) — The open manifestation of one's own desire is called <s>Moṭṭāyita</s>. ||1.356|| 204

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: Hearing the words of her beloved, a sole elixir for the pair of ears,
spoken in conversations among friends,
with a charming jingling of swaying bracelets,
the slender woman's creeper-like arm bends with graceful bodily movement. ||1.357||

body.translated_text: As in my own [verse] —

body.text:
atha kuṭṭamitam-
keśādharādi-grahaṇe modamāne' pi mānase |
duḥkhiteva bahiḥ kupyed yatra kuṭṭamitaṃ hi tat ||SRs_1.358|| 205
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Kuṭṭamita</s> (feigned anger) — Where, even though the mind delights in the seizing of hair, lips, and the like, one outwardly appears as if distressed and shows anger — that is <s>Kuṭṭamita</s>. ||1.358|| 205

body.text:
yathā--
pāṇi-pallava-vidhūnanam antaḥ-
śītkṛtāni nayanārdha-nimeṣāḥ |
yoṣitāṃ rahasi gadgada-vācām
astratām upayayur madanasya ||SRs_1.359|| [kirāṭa 9.50]
body.translated_text: As for example — 'The fluttering of the petal-soft palm, the hissing through the teeth, the half-closing of the eyes — these became weapons of <s>Madana</s> for the women speaking with faltering voices in private.' ||1.359|| [<s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 9.50]

body.text: atra rahasīti sāmānya-sūcitānāṃ keśādhara-grahaṇādīnāṃ kārya-bhūtaiḥ pāṇi-pallava-vidhūnana-sītkṛtādibhir bahir eva kopasya pratīyamānatvāt kuṭṭamitam |
body.translated_text: Here, since the word 'in private' generally implies the seizing of hair, lips, and the like, and since anger is perceived outwardly through the effects — the fluttering of the palm, the hissing, and so forth — this is <s>Kuṭṭamita</s>.

body.text:
atha bibbokaḥ-
iṣṭe' py anādaro garvān mānād bibboka īritaḥ ||SRs_1.360|| 206ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Bibboka</s> (studied indifference) — Disregard toward the beloved even though desired, arising from pride or wounded dignity, is called <s>Bibboka</s>. ||1.360|| 206ab

body.text: garvād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Though conciliated by men with a hundred <s>Sāma-Veda</s> hymns of praise,
one woman, out of pride, remained as if indifferent;
wayward women treat even things
not desired by themselves as if they were meant for others. ||1.361||

body.translated_text: From pride, as for example —

body.text:
mānād, yathā-
nirvibhujya daśana-cchadaṃ tato
vāci bhartur avadhīraṇā-parā |
śaila-rāja-tanayā samīpagām
ālalāpi vijayām ahetukam ||SRs_1.362|| [ku.saṃ. 8.49]
body.translated_text: From wounded dignity (<s>māna</s>), as for example — 'Then, biting her lip, the daughter of the king of mountains (<s>Pārvatī</s>), intent on reproaching her husband's words, spoke causeless [angry words] to <s>Vijayā</s> who was nearby.' ||1.362|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.49]

body.text: atra sandhyā-nimittaṃ mānād anādareṇa bibbokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Bibboka</s> arises through disregard born of wounded dignity occasioned by the evening [prayers].

body.text: atha lalitam-

children.translated_text: Where the postures, movements, and play of the limbs are enchanting with the coquetry of the eyebrows, 206
and delicate — that is called <s>Lalita</s>. ||1.363||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Lalita</s> (graceful movement) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Adorning the threshold with the radiance of her lotus-feet,
shaking the golden door-panel with her hand,
filling the gateway with her blue-lotus-like eyes,
this beautiful-bodied one sits like the <s>Lakṣmī</s> (goddess of fortune) of the palace itself. ||1.364||

body.translated_text: As for example —

body.text: atha vihṛtam-

children.text: īrṣyayā māna-lajjābhyāṃ na dattaṃ yogyam uttaram | 207
children.translated_text: Where the appropriate reply, withheld due to jealousy, pride, or modesty,

children.text: kriyayā vyajyate yatra vihṛtaṃ tad udīritam ||SRs_1.365||
children.translated_text: is expressed through action — that is called <s>Vihṛta</s> (enacted response). ||1.365||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vihṛta</s> (enacted response) —

body.text: īrṣyayā, yathā-

children.translated_text: When her friend arrived, the staff-bearing [attendant]
addressed her friend playfully in jest:
'Noble lady, let us go elsewhere'; and then
the bride cast a sidelong glance, curved with jealousy, at her. ||1.366||

body.translated_text: Due to jealousy, for example —

body.text: atra na vrajāva ity uttaram adattvā kuṭila-darśanenaiva vyañjanād vihṛtam |
body.translated_text: Here, without giving the reply 'let us not go,' the <s>Vihṛta</s> is conveyed through suggestion by the curved glance alone.

body.text: mānena, yathā-

children.translated_text: Even now it revolves in my mind —
that night, when I sneezed, the princess,
suppressing from anger the auspicious word 'live!',
without speaking, placed a gold leaf upon my ear. ||1.367||

body.translated_text: Due to pride (<s>māna</s>), for example —

body.text: caura-pañcāśikā 11
body.translated_text: <s>Caura-pañcāśikā</s> 11

body.text:
lajjayā, yathā-
apy avastuni kathā-pravṛttaye
praśna-tatparam anaṅga-śāsanam |
vīkṣitena parigṛhya pārvatī
mūrdha-kampamayam uttaraṃ dadau ||SRs_1.368|| [ku.saṃ. 8.6]
body.translated_text: Due to modesty (<s>lajjā</s>), for example — When the command of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless God of Love), eager for questions to initiate conversation, was presented even on a trivial subject, <s>Pārvatī</s>, receiving it with a glance, gave an answer consisting of a nod of the head. ||1.368|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.6]

body.text: itthaṃ śrī-siṃha-bhūpena sattvālaṅkāra-śālinā | 208
body.translated_text: Thus, by the illustrious <s>Siṃha-bhūpa</s>, adorned with the ornament of inner character (<s>sattva</s>),

body.text: kathitāḥ sattvajāḥ strīṇām alaṅkārās tu viṃśatiḥ ||SRs_1.369||
body.translated_text: have been described twenty ornaments of women born of <s>sattva</s> (inner nature). ||1.369||

body.text: sattvād daśaiva bhāvādyā jātā līlādayas tu na | 209
body.translated_text: Only ten, beginning with <s>bhāva</s>, are born of <s>sattva</s>; those beginning with <s>līlā</s> are not.

body.text: ato hi viṃśatir bhāvāḥ sāttvikā iti nocitam ||SRs_1.370||
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is not proper to say that there are twenty <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> (involuntary emotions). ||1.370||

body.text: yujyate sāttvikatvaṃ ca bhāvādi-sahacāriṇaḥ | 210
body.translated_text: The <s>sāttvika</s> nature is also fitting for the group of ten beginning with <s>līlā</s>,

body.text: līlādi-daśakasyāpi chatri-nyāya-balāt sphuṭam ||SRs_1.371||
body.translated_text: which accompanies those beginning with <s>bhāva</s>, clearly by the force of the 'umbrella principle' (<s>chatrī-nyāya</s>). ||1.371||

body.text: bhojena krīḍitaṃ kelir ity anyau gātrajau smṛtau | 211
body.translated_text: <s>Bhoja</s> has stated that <s>Krīḍita</s> (play) and <s>Keli</s> (sport) are two others born of the body.

body.text: ato viṃśatir ity atra saṅkhyeyaṃ nopapadyate ||SRs_1.372||
body.translated_text: Therefore, the count of twenty is not justified here. ||1.372||

body.text:
tathā hi lakṣitam anenaiva ca-
krīḍitaṃ kelir ity anyau gātrārambhāv udāhṛtau |
bālya-yauvana-kaumāra-sādhāraṇa-vihāra-bhāk |
viśeṣaḥ krīḍitaṃ kelis tad eva dayitāśrayam ||SRs_1.373|| iti |
body.translated_text: For indeed, this very [author] has defined — '<s>Krīḍita</s> (play) and <s>Keli</s> (sport) are stated as two other bodily activities; <s>Krīḍita</s> is play common to childhood, youth, and adolescence; <s>Keli</s> is that same [activity] when it is centered on the beloved.' ||1.373||

body.text:
udāhṛtaṃ ca | krīḍitaṃ, yathā-
mandākinī-saikata-vedikābhiḥ
sā kandukaiḥ kṛtrima-putrakaiś ca |
reme muhur madhya-gatā sakhīnāṃ
krīḍā-rasaṃ nirviśatīva bālye ||SRs_1.374|| [ku.saṃ. 7.29]
body.translated_text: And the examples are given — <s>Krīḍita</s> (play), for example — She sported amid her companions on the sandy banks of the <s>Mandākinī</s>, with balls and toy dolls, as if savoring the essence of play in her childhood. ||1.374|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 7.29]

body.text:
kelir, yathā-
vyapohituṃ locanato mukhānilair
apārayantaṃ kila puṣpajaṃ rajaḥ |
payodhareṇorasi kācid unmanāḥ
priyaṃ jaghānonnata-pīvara-stanī ||SRs_1.375|| [kirāṭa 8.19] iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Keli</s> (sport), for example — Unable to brush away the pollen of flowers from her eyes with the breeze of her face, a certain woman with uplifted, full breasts, lost in rapture, struck her beloved on the chest with her bosom. ||1.375|| [<s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 8.19]

body.text: atrocyate bhāva-tattva-vedinā siṃha-bhūbhujā | 212
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Siṃha-bhūbhuj</s> (King <s>Siṃha</s>), the knower of the essence of <s>bhāva</s>, states:

body.text: ādyaḥ prāg eva bhāvādi-samutpatteś ca śaiśave ||SRs_1.376||
body.translated_text: The first [<s>Krīḍita</s>] occurs even before the arising of <s>bhāva</s> and others, in early childhood.

body.text: kanyā-vinoda-mātratvād anubhāveṣu neṣyate | 213
body.translated_text: Being merely a maiden's diversion, it is not admitted among the <s>Anubhāvas</s> (consequents).

body.text:
prema-visrambha-mātratvān nānyasyāpy anubhāvatā |
ato viṃśatir ity eṣā saṅkhyā saṅkhyāvatāṃ matā ||SRs_1.377|| 214
body.translated_text: The other [<s>Keli</s>] also is not [considered] an <s>Anubhāva</s> because it is merely an expression of love and trust. Therefore, the count of twenty is the view accepted by those skilled in enumeration. ||1.377||

body.text:
atha pauruṣa-sāttvikāḥ-
śobhā vilāso mādhuryaṃ dhairyaṃ gāmbhīryam eva ca |
lalitaudārya-tejāṃsi sattva-bhedās tu pauruṣāḥ ||SRs_1.378|| 215
body.translated_text: Now, the masculine <s>sāttvika</s> [ornaments] — <s>Śobhā</s> (splendor), <s>Vilāsa</s> (grace), <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>Dhairya</s> (composure), <s>Gāmbhīrya</s> (gravity), <s>Lalita</s> (elegance), <s>Audārya</s> (magnanimity), and <s>Tejas</s> (luster) — these are the masculine varieties of <s>sattva</s>. ||1.378||

body.text:
tatra śobhā-
nīce dayādhike spardhā śauryotsāhau ca dakṣatā |
yatra prakaṭatāṃ yānti sā śobheti prakīrtitā ||SRs_1.379|| 216
body.translated_text: There, <s>Śobhā</s> (splendor) — Where compassion toward the lowly, superabundant rivalry, valor, enthusiasm, and dexterity become manifest — that is proclaimed as <s>Śobhā</s> (splendor). ||1.379||

body.text: nīce dayādhike spardhā, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Petty ones! Let these monkeys abandon their fear — having split the frontal globes of <s>Indra</s>'s elephant,

children.text: yuṣmad-gātreṣu lajjāṃ dadhati paramam amī sāyakāḥ sampatantaḥ |
children.translated_text: these arrows raining down bring supreme shame upon your bodies.

children.text: saumitre tiṣṭha pātraṃ tvam api na hi ruṣāṃ nanv ahaṃ meghanādaḥ
children.translated_text: O son of <s>Sumitrā</s>, stand aside — you too are no worthy target for my anger. I am <s>Meghānāda</s> (<s>Indrajit</s>) indeed!
I seek <s>Rāma</s>, who restrains the ocean with a mere play of his eyebrows.' ||1.380||

body.translated_text: Compassion toward the lowly and superabundant rivalry, for example —

body.text: (hanuman-nāṭake 12.2)
body.translated_text: (<s>Hanūmannāṭaka</s> 12.2)

body.text: atra prathamārdhe kṣudra-kapi-viṣaye dayā, uttarārdhe rāma-viṣayā spardhā cendrajitaḥ pratīyate | śaurye sattva-sāraḥ | utsāhaḥ sthairyam | dakṣatā kṣipra-kāritvam | eṣāṃ nāyaka-guṇa-nirūpaṇāvasara evodāharaṇāni darśitāni |
body.translated_text: Here, in the first half, compassion toward the lowly monkeys is perceived; in the latter half, <s>Indrajit</s>'s rivalry toward <s>Rāma</s>. Valor implies essential strength (<s>sattva-sāra</s>); enthusiasm implies steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>); dexterity means swift execution. Examples for these have already been shown during the exposition of the hero's qualities.

body.text:
atha vilāsaḥ-
vṛṣabhasyeva gambhīrā gatir dhīraṃ ca darśanam |
sasmitaṃ ca vaco yatra sa vilāsa itīritaḥ ||SRs_1.381|| 217
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vilāsa</s> (grace) — Where there is a majestic gait like that of a bull, a steady gaze, and speech accompanied by a smile — that is called <s>Vilāsa</s> (grace). ||1.381||

body.text:
gambhīra-gamanaṃ, yathā-
tān arghyān arghyam ādāya dūraṃ pratyudyayau giriḥ |
namayan sāra-gurubhiḥ pāda-nyāsair vasundharām ||SRs_1.382|| [ku.saṃ. 6.50]
body.translated_text: Majestic gait, for example — Taking the <s>arghya</s> (offering) for those worthy of <s>arghya</s>, the Mountain (<s>Himālaya</s>) came forward a great distance to welcome them, making the earth bow down with his footsteps, heavy with substance. ||1.382|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 6.50]

body.text: dhīra-dṛṣṭir, yathā-

children.translated_text: With that profound,
averted gaze, beautiful as a morning lotus,
the Self-born of Spring (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, son of <s>Madhu</s>) looked [at him],
and he (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) addressed the messenger of the <s>Daityas</s> (demons). ||1.383||

body.translated_text: Steady gaze, for example —

body.text:
sasmitaṃ vaco, yathā-
dyotitāntaḥ-sabhaiḥ kunda-kuḍmalāgra-dataḥ smitaiḥ |
snapitevābhavat tasya śuddha-varṇā sarasvatī ||SRs_1.384|| (māgha. 2.7)
