body.translated_text: Speech with a smile, for example — Illuminated from within by smiles [gleaming] from the tips of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds that were his teeth, his <s>Sarasvatī</s> (speech) appeared as if bathed in pure syllables. ||1.384|| (<s>Māgha</s>/<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 2.7)

body.text:
atha mādhuryam-
tan mādhuryaṃ yatra ceṣṭā-dṛṣṭy-ādeḥ spṛhaṇīyatā ||SRs_1.385|| 218ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness) — That <s>Mādhurya</s> is where the gestures, glances, and other [expressions] become worthy of desire. ||1.385||

body.text: ||SRs_1.386|| MISSING

yathā-
ṛjutāṃ nayataḥ smarāmi te
śaram utsaṅga-niṣaṇṇa-dhanvanaḥ |
madhunā saha sasmitāṃ kathāṃ
nayanopānta-vilokitaṃ ca yat ||SRs_1.387|| [ku.saṃ. 4.23]
body.translated_text: For example — 'I remember you straightening the arrow while the bow rested on your lap, your sweet conversation with <s>Madhu</s> (Spring/Honey) accompanied by smiles, and your sidelong glance from the corner of your eye.' ||1.387|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 4.23]

body.text: dhairya-gāmbhīrye tu nāyaka-guṇa-varṇanāvasara evokte |
body.translated_text: <s>Dhairya</s> (composure) and <s>Gāmbhīrya</s> (gravity) have already been described during the exposition of the hero's qualities.

body.text:
atha lalitam-
śṛṅgāra-pracurā ceṣṭā yatra tal lalitaṃ bhavet ||SRs_1.388|| 218cd
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Lalita</s> (elegance) — Where the gestures abound in <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) — that is <s>Lalita</s> (elegance). ||1.388||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: On the cheek of <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>), which robbed the luster of the elephant's temple-globe,
his lotus-face, with the horripilation of his cheeks' tumescence, smiling with love's smile,
gazing again and again, hearing the tumult of the army of the night-wanderers (<s>Rākṣasas</s>),
the chief of the <s>Raghus</s> tightens the knot of his matted locks. ||1.389||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (hanuman-nāṭake 1.19)
body.translated_text: (<s>Hanūmannāṭaka</s> 1.19)

body.text: audārya-tejasor api nāyaka-prasaṅga eva lakṣaṇodāharaṇe prokte |
body.translated_text: The definitions and examples of <s>Audārya</s> (magnanimity) and <s>Tejas</s> (luster) have already been stated in the context of the hero.

body.text:
atra gāmbhīrya-dhairye dve cittaje gātrajāḥ pare |
eke sādhāraṇān etān menire citta-gātrayoḥ ||SRs_1.390|| 219
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Gāmbhīrya</s> (gravity) and <s>Dhairya</s> (composure) are two that are mind-born; the rest are body-born. Some have considered these to be common to both mind and body. ||1.390||

body.text:
atha vāg-ārambhāḥ-
ālāpaś ca vilāpaś ca saṃlāpaś ca pralāpakaḥ |
anulāpāpalāpau ca sandeśaś cātideśakaḥ ||SRs_1.391|| 220
nirdeśaś copadeśaś cāpadeśo vyapadeśakaḥ |
evaṃ dvādaśadhā proktā kīrtitā vāg-ārambhā vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||SRs_1.392|| 221
body.translated_text: Now, the speech-modes (<s>Vāg-ārambhas</s>) — <s>Ālāpa</s> (endearing speech), <s>Vilāpa</s> (lamentation), <s>Saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue), <s>Pralāpa</s> (raving), <s>Anulāpa</s> (repetition), <s>Apalāpa</s> (dissimulation), <s>Sandeśa</s> (message), <s>Atideśa</s> (extended application), <s>Nirdeśa</s> (self-declaration), <s>Upadeśa</s> (instruction), <s>Apadeśa</s> (indirect expression), and <s>Vyapadeśa</s> (pretextual expression) — thus the speech-modes have been declared by the discerning to be of twelve kinds. ||1.391-392||

body.text:
tatra ālāpaḥ-
tatrālāpaḥ priyoktiḥ syāt ||SRs_1.393|| 222a
body.translated_text: There, <s>Ālāpa</s> (endearing speech) — <s>Ālāpa</s> is speech that is pleasant and affectionate. ||1.393||

children.translated_text: For example, by me [the author] —

children.text: kas te vākyāmṛtaṃ tyaktvā śṛṇoty anya-giraṃ budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Who, being wise, would abandon the nectar of your words and listen to another's speech?

children.text: sahakāra-rasaṃ tyaktvā nimbaṃ cumbati kiṃ śukaḥ ||SRs_1.394||
children.translated_text: Would a parrot, forsaking the sap of the mango, kiss the neem tree?' ||1.394||

body.text: yathā vā-

children.text: dhatse dhātur madhupa kamale saukhyam adhyāsikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'O bee, at the lotus you partake of the sweetness of the Creator's [handiwork],
you bear a resemblance to the tresses of doe-eyed women with [your] honey,

children.text: cāpe kiṃ ca vrajasi guṇatāṃ śambarāreḥ kim anyat
children.translated_text: on the bow [of <s>Kāma</s>] you attain the status of a bowstring — what else?
The worship-flowers that are offered to the gods become your leftovers!' ||1.395||

body.translated_text: Or for example —

body.text:
atha vilāpaḥ-
vilāpo duḥkhajaṃ vacaḥ ||SRs_1.396|| 222b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vilāpa</s> (lamentation) — <s>Vilāpa</s> is speech born of sorrow. ||1.396||

body.text:
yathā-
sītāṃ sva-hastena vane vimoktuṃ
śrotuṃ ca tasyāḥ paridevitāni |
sukhena laṅkā-samare mṛtaṃ mām
ajīvayan mārutir ātta-vairaḥ ||SRs_1.397|| [ha.nā. 14.91]
body.translated_text: For example — 'To release <s>Sītā</s> with his own hand in the forest and to hear her lamentations — better that I had died happily in the battle of <s>Laṅkā</s>! The son of the Wind (<s>Māruti</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>), having taken up enmity [on my behalf], kept me alive [for this].' ||1.397|| [<s>Hanūmannāṭaka</s> 14.91]

body.text:
atha saṃlāpaḥ-
ukti-pratyuktimad-vākyaṃ saṃlāpa iti kīrtitam ||SRs_1.398|| 222cd
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue) — Speech consisting of statement and reply is called <s>Saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue). ||1.398||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Give alms, O beautiful lotus-petal-eyed one!
I, who am worshipped by gods and demons, am indeed in bloom.'

children.text: bāle tathā yadi phalaṃ tvayi vidyate me
children.translated_text: 'O child, if thus you have fruit in you [to offer] me —'

children.text: vākyair alaṃ phala-bhug īśa paro' sti yāhi ||SRs_1.399||
children.translated_text: 'Enough of words! The enjoyer of fruit is another, the Lord — go!' ||1.399||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha pralāpaḥ--
vyarthālāpaḥ pralāpaḥ syāt ||SRs_1.400|| 223a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Pralāpa</s> (raving) — <s>Pralāpa</s> is meaningless or incoherent speech. ||1.400||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Her face is like the moon, the moon, the moon,

children.text: stanau ca pīnau kaṭhinau ṭhinau ṭhinau |
children.translated_text: her breasts are full and firm, so firm, so firm,
her hips are broad, with passion, passion, passion —
oh, how wonderful is this young woman, woman, woman!' ||1.401||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha anulāpaḥ-
anulāpo muhur vacaḥ ||401|| 223b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Anulāpa</s> (repetition) — <s>Anulāpa</s> is repeated speech. ||1.402||

body.text: yathā-

children.text: tamas tamo nahi nahi mecakāḥ kacāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Darkness! Darkness! No, no — her locks are dark-hued.

children.text: śaśī śaśī nahi nahi dṛk-sukhaṃ mukham |
children.translated_text: The moon! The moon! No, no — her face is a delight to the eyes.

children.text: late late nahi nahi sundarau karau
children.translated_text: Creepers! Creepers! No, no — her arms are beautiful.

children.text: nabho nabho nahi nahi cāru madhyamam ||SRs_1.402||
children.translated_text: The sky! The sky! No, no — her waist is lovely.' ||1.402||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
athāpalāpaḥ-
apalāpas tu pūrvoktasyānyathā yojanaṃ bhavet ||SRs_1.403|| 223cd
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Apalāpa</s> (dissimulation) — <s>Apalāpa</s> is the reinterpretation of something previously said in a different sense. ||1.403||

body.text:
yathā-
tvam rukmiṇī tvaṃ khalu satyabhāmā
kim atra gotra-skhalanaṃ mameti | prasādayan vyāja-padena rādhāṃ

children.translated_text: may Lord <s>Puruṣottama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>/<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) purify you all. ||1.404||

body.translated_text: 'You are <s>Rukmiṇī</s>! You are indeed <s>Satyabhāmā</s>! Why this stumbling over names on my part?' — thus placating <s>Rādhā</s> with a feigned word,

body.text: atra nāyikā-vācakayoḥ rukmiṇī-satyabhāmā-padayoḥ pūrvoktayoḥ suvarṇavattva-satya-kopatva-lakṣaṇenārthena yojanād apalāpaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Apalāpa</s> consists in the reinterpretation of the previously uttered words '<s>Rukmiṇī</s>' and '<s>Satyabhāmā</s>' — which are names of the hero's other consorts — in the sense of 'golden-complexioned' and 'truly angry' respectively, as spoken to the heroine.

body.text:
atha sandeśaḥ-
sandeśas tu proṣitasya sva-vārtā-preṣaṇaṃ bhavet ||SRs_1.405|| 224ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Sandeśa</s> (message) — <s>Sandeśa</s> is the sending of one's own tidings when one is away. ||1.405||

body.text:
yathā-
etasmān māṃ kuśalinam abhijñāna-dānād viditvā
mā kaulīnād asita-nayane mayy aviśvāsinī bhūḥ |
snehān āhuḥ kim api virahe dhvaṃsinas te tv abhogād
iṣṭe vastuny upacita-rasāḥ prema-rāśī-bhavanti ||SRs_1.406|| [me.dū. 2.52]
body.translated_text: For example — 'Having learned from this token of recognition that I am well, O dark-eyed one, do not be distrustful of me from noble propriety. They say that love diminishes somewhat in separation; but when centered on a desired object, the accumulated sentiments become a flood of love.' ||1.406|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 2.52]

body.text:
atha atideśaḥ-
so' tideśo mad-uktāni tad-uktānīti yad vacaḥ ||SRs_1.407|| 224cd
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Atideśa</s> (extended application) — <s>Atideśa</s> is speech where 'what I said' is [represented as] 'what he/she said.' ||1.407||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: '<s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the Self of the universe, <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Being) himself,
asks for your daughter.
Understand our speech as resembling
an echo from a mountain cave, O Ocean!' ||1.408||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha nirdeśaḥ-
nirdeśas tu bhavet so' yam aham ity ādi-bhāṣaṇam ||SRs_1.409|| 225ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Nirdeśa</s> (self-declaration) — <s>Nirdeśa</s> is speech beginning with 'this is I,' 'these are [mine],' etc. ||1.409||

body.text:
yathā-
ete vayam amī dārāḥ kanyeyaṃ kula-jīvitam |
brūta yenātra vaḥ kāryam anāsthā bāhya-vastuṣu ||SRs_1.410|| [ku.saṃ. 6.63]
body.translated_text: For example — 'These are we; these are our wives; this daughter is the life of our family. Speak — whatever you need here — [for] we have no attachment to external possessions.' ||1.410|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 6.63]

body.text:
atha upadeśaḥ-
yatra śikṣārtha-vacanam upadeśaḥ sa ucyate ||SRs_1.411|| 225
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Upadeśa</s> (instruction) — Where the speech serves the purpose of teaching — that is called <s>Upadeśa</s> (instruction). ||1.411||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Enjoy the wealth that has been given;
honor the honorable; serve the virtuous.
[For] like a lamp-flame tossed by
exceedingly harsh winds, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) is fickle.' ||1.412||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha apadeśaḥ-
anyārtha-kathanaṃ yatra so' padeśa itīritaḥ ||SRs_1.413|| 226ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Apadeśa</s> (indirect expression) — Where another's matter is spoken [to convey one's own meaning] — that is called <s>Apadeśa</s> (indirect expression). ||1.413||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'This lotus-pool bears a pair of seed-pods pecked by geese;
this mango creeper bears a new sprout tasted by the male cuckoo.'

children.text: ity ākarṇya mithaḥ sakhī-jana-vacaḥ sā dīrghikāyās taṭe
children.translated_text: Hearing these mutual words of her friends at the bank of the pool,
she concealed her breast-region with the edge of her garment and her lower lip with her hand. ||1.414||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha vyapadeśaḥ-
vyājenātmābhilāṣoktir yatrāyaṃ vyapadeśakaḥ ||SRs_1.415|| 226cd
yathā-
ahiṇa-vamahulolubo tumaṃ
taha paricuṃbia cūda-mañjariṃ |
kamala-basai-metta-ṇibbudo
mahara bihmarido' si ṇaṃ kahaṃ ||SRs_1.416|| [saku. 5.1]
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vyapadeśa</s> (pretextual expression) — Where one's own desire is expressed under a pretext — that is <s>Vyapadeśa</s> (pretextual expression). ||1.415|| For example — 'O you who are greedy for fresh honey, having thus kissed the mango blossom, content with merely residing in the lotus — O bee, how have you forgotten her?' ||1.416|| [<s>Śākuntala</s> 5.1]

body.text: [asya chāyā-

children.translated_text: 'You who are greedy for fresh honey,
having thus kissed the mango blossom,
content with merely dwelling in the lotus —
O bee, how have you forgotten her?']

body.translated_text: [The Sanskrit rendering (chāyā) of the above Prakrit verse —

body.text: atha buddhy-ārambhāḥ-

children.translated_text: <s>Buddhy-ārambhas</s> (intellectual modes) are thus declared to be <s>Rīti</s> (style), <s>Vṛtti</s> (mode), and <s>Pravṛtti</s> (regional practice). ||1.417||

body.translated_text: Now, the intellectual modes (<s>Buddhy-ārambhas</s>) —

body.text: tatra rītiḥ |

children.text: rītiḥ syāt pada-vinyāsa-bhaṅgī sā tu tridhā matā | 227
children.translated_text: <s>Rīti</s> (style) is the manner of word-arrangement; it is considered to be threefold:

children.text: komalā kaṭhinā miśrā ceti syāt tatra komalā ||SRs_1.418||
children.translated_text: <s>Komalā</s> (soft), <s>Kaṭhinā</s> (harsh), and <s>Miśrā</s> (mixed) — of these, the soft (<s>Komalā</s>) — ||1.418||

body.translated_text: There, <s>Rīti</s> (style) —

body.text: dvitīya-turya-varṇair yā svalpair vargeṣu nirmitā | 228
body.translated_text: That [style] which is constructed in the letter-groups with few second and fourth consonants,

body.text: alpa-prāṇākṣara-prāyā daśa-prāṇa-samanvitā ||SRs_1.419||
body.translated_text: predominantly composed of unaspirated letters (<s>alpa-prāṇa</s>), and endowed with ten vital qualities (<s>daśa-prāṇa</s>), ||SRs_1.419||

body.text: samāsa-rahitā svalpaiḥ samāsair vā vibhūṣitā | 229
body.translated_text: free from compounds or adorned with only few compounds,

body.text: vidarbha-jana-hṛdyatvāt sā vaidarbhīti kathyate ||SRs_1.420||
body.translated_text: is called <s>Vaidarbhī</s> because it is pleasing to the people of <s>Vidarbha</s>. ||SRs_1.420||

body.text: mahā-praṇavārṇālpatvam alpa-prāṇākṣara-prāyatvaṃ ca, yathā mamaiva-
body.translated_text: The paucity of aspirated consonants (<s>mahā-praṇa</s>) and the predominance of unaspirated letters (<s>alpa-prāṇākṣara</s>) — for example, from my own [work] —

body.text:
utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam udgata-manda-hāsam
udvela-rāgam urarīkṛta-kāma-tantram |
hastena hastam avalambya kadā nu seve
saṃlāpa-rūpam amṛtaṃ sarasīruhākṣyāḥ ||SRs_1.421|| [ku. 3.4]
body.translated_text: When shall I enjoy the nectar in the form of conversation with the lotus-eyed one, with her cheeks in full bloom, with a gently risen smile, with overflowing passion, having mastered the art of love, holding hand in hand? ||SRs_1.421|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4]

body.text:
samāsa-rāhityaṃ, yathā-
atha yantāram ādiśya dhuryān viśrāmayeti saḥ |
tām avāropayat patnīṃ rathād avatatāra ca ||SRs_1.422|| [raghu. 1.54]
body.translated_text: The absence of compounds, for example — Then, having directed the charioteer to rest the draft-horses, he helped his wife descend from the chariot and dismounted himself. ||SRs_1.422|| [<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 1.54]

body.text: daśa-prāṇās tu-

children.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion), <s>prasāda</s> (clarity), <s>samatā</s> (evenness), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy),

children.text:
artha-vyaktir udāratvam ojaḥ kānti-samādhayaḥ |
ete vaidarbha-mārgasya prāṇā daśa guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ ||SRs_1.423|| 231
children.translated_text: <s>artha-vyakti</s> (lucidity of meaning), <s>udāratva</s> (nobility), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), <s>kānti</s> (charm), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — these ten qualities are considered the vital breaths of the <s>Vaidarbha</s> style. ||SRs_1.423||

body.translated_text: Now the ten vital qualities (<s>daśa-prāṇa</s>) are —

body.text:
tatra śleṣaḥ-
kevalālpa-prāṇa-varṇa-pada-sandarbha-lakṣaṇam |
śaithilyaṃ yatra na spṛṣṭaṃ sa śleṣaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ ||SRs_1.424|| 232
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion) — That characterized by a composition of words made exclusively of unaspirated consonants, in which there is no looseness of contact [between sounds] — that is called <s>śleṣa</s>. ||SRs_1.424||

body.text:
yathā mamaiva utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4][*5] ity ādau śliṣṭa-varṇa-miśrita-bandhatvāt śleṣaḥ |
[*5] Quoted just above.
body.translated_text: For example, from my own [verse] beginning 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — because the composition is interwoven with cohesive consonants, there is <s>śleṣa</s>.

body.text:
atha prasādaḥ-
prasiddhārtha-padatvaṃ yat sa prasādo nigadyate ||SRs_1.425|| 233ab
body.translated_text: Now <s>prasāda</s> (clarity) — That which consists of words with well-known meanings — that is called <s>prasāda</s>. ||SRs_1.425||

body.text: yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] ity atra padānām akleśenaivārtha-bodhana-sāmarthyāt prasādaḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — because the words have the capacity to convey meaning without difficulty, there is <s>prasāda</s>.

body.text: atha samatā-

children.translated_text: Evenness is the absence of unevenness in composition, in the arrangement of words.

children.text: bandho mṛduḥ sphuṭo miśra iti tredhā sa nigadyate ||SRs_1.426|| 234ab
children.translated_text: That composition is said to be threefold: soft (<s>mṛdu</s>), clear (<s>sphuṭa</s>), and mixed (<s>miśra</s>). ||SRs_1.426||

body.translated_text: Now <s>samatā</s> (evenness) —

body.text: tatra mṛdu-varṇa-bandhasya samatā, yathā-
body.translated_text: Of these, evenness of soft consonant-composition, for example —

children.translated_text: Adorning the threshold with the radiance of her lotus-feet,
shaking the golden door-panels with her hand,
filling the archway with her lotus-like eyes —
this beautiful-bodied one stands like the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the mansion itself. ||SRs_1.427||

body.text: atra mṛdu-varṇa-prāya-bandhasya nirvyūḍhatvān mṛdu-bandha-samatā |
body.translated_text: Here, because the composition predominantly of soft consonants is carried through smoothly, there is evenness of soft composition.

body.text:
sphuṭa-bandha-samatā, yathā-
madhurayā madhu-bodhita-mādhavī-
madhu-samṛddhi-samedhita-medhayā |
madhukarāṅganayā muhur unmada-
dhvani-bhṛtānibhṛtākṣaram ujjage ||SRs_1.428|| [māghe 6.20]
body.translated_text: Evenness of clear composition, for example — With the sweetness of a bee-maiden whose intellect is enriched by the abundance of honey awakened by the <s>mādhavī</s> creeper's nectar in spring, she sang repeatedly with intoxicated, unrestrained syllables of buzzing sound. ||SRs_1.428|| [<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 6.20]

body.text: atra sphuṭa-varṇa-prāya-bandhasya nirvyūḍhatvāt sphuṭa-bandha-samatā |
body.translated_text: Here, because the composition predominantly of clear [hard] consonants is carried through smoothly, there is evenness of clear composition.

body.text: miśra-bandha-samatā, yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] ity ādau | atra miśrī-bhūta-mṛdu-sphuṭa-varṇa-bandhasya nirvāhād miśra-bandha-samatā |
body.translated_text: Evenness of mixed composition, for example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] and so forth. Here, because the composition of intermingled soft and clear consonants is sustained throughout, there is evenness of mixed composition.

body.text:
atha mādhuryam-
tan mādhuryaṃ bhaved yatra śabde' rthe ca sphuṭo rasaḥ ||SRs_1.429|| 234cd
body.translated_text: Now <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) — That is <s>mādhurya</s> where <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) is manifest in both sound and meaning. ||SRs_1.429||

body.text: yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] ity atra śabdārthayoḥ śṛṅgāra-parivāhitvena mādhuryam |
body.translated_text: For example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — because both sound and meaning overflow with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment), there is <s>mādhurya</s>.

body.text:
atha sukumāratā-
yad aniṣṭhura-varṇatvaṃ saukumāryaṃ tad ucyate ||SRs_1.430|| 235ab
body.translated_text: Now <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy) — That which consists of non-harsh consonants — that is called <s>saukumārya</s>. ||SRs_1.430||

body.text: yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] udgata-manda-hāsam ity atra saṃyuktākṣara-sadbhāve' py aniṣṭhuratvāt saukumāryam |
body.translated_text: For example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom, with a gently risen smile' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — even though conjunct consonants are present, because there is no harshness, there is <s>saukumārya</s>.

body.text: atha artha-vyaktiḥ-

children.translated_text: That quality of a sentence being heard whereby the meaning is comprehended
without the desire for any additional word — that is considered <s>artha-vyakti</s> (lucidity of meaning). ||SRs_1.431||

body.translated_text: Now <s>artha-vyakti</s> (lucidity of meaning) —

body.text: yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] ity atra sarveṣāṃ padānām adhyāhāraya-pada-nirākāṅkṣatayā artha-vyaktiḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — because all words are independent of any word needing to be supplied, there is <s>artha-vyakti</s>.

body.text:
atha udāratvam-
ukte vākye guṇotkarṣa-pratibhānam udāratā ||SRs_1.432|| 236cd
body.translated_text: Now <s>udāratva</s> (nobility) — The apprehension of excellence of qualities in a spoken sentence — that is <s>udāratā</s> (nobility). ||SRs_1.432||

body.text: yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] ity atrānyonyānurāgotkarṣa-pratibhānād udāratvam |
body.translated_text: For example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — because there is the apprehension of the excellence of mutual passion, there is <s>udāratva</s>.

body.text:
atha ojaḥ-
samāsa-bahulatvaṃ yat tad ojaḥ iti gīyate ||SRs_1.433|| 237ab
yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] ity atra yathocita-samāsa-bāhulyād ojaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now <s>ojas</s> (vigor) — That which is the abundance of compounds — that is celebrated as <s>ojas</s>. ||SRs_1.433|| For example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — because of the appropriate abundance of compounds, there is <s>ojas</s>.

body.text: atha kāntiḥ-

children.translated_text: The conveyance of pleasing meaning without transgressing worldly convention —

children.text: kāntiḥ syād dvividhā khyātā vārtāyāṃ varṇanāsu ca ||SRs_1.434|| 238ab
children.translated_text: that is <s>kānti</s>, which is said to be twofold: in conversation and in description. ||SRs_1.434||

body.translated_text: Now <s>kānti</s> (charm) —

body.text: vārtā nāma kuśala-praśna-pūrvikā saṅkathā | tatra yathā-

children.translated_text: By the water that has washed your feet, cool as the rays of the new moon,
the submarine fire (<s>aurva-pāvaka</s>) that continually pierces my vitals has been extinguished, as it were. ||SRs_1.435||

body.translated_text: <s>Vārtā</s> (conversation) means discourse preceded by inquiry about well-being. An example of that —

body.text: atra brāhmaṇa-pādodakasya santāpa-śamana-rūpāṃ laukikīṃ sthitim anullaṅghyaiva samudreṇa munīnāṃ purataḥ saṅkathanāt kāntiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the ocean converses before the sages without transgressing the worldly convention that the water washing a Brahmin's feet has the property of quelling torment, there is <s>kānti</s>.

children.translated_text: In description, for example from my own [work] —
Her upraised breast-pitchers, her thigh-pair like pillars of a pavilion,

children.text: tarale dṛśau ca tasyāḥ sṛjatā dhātrā kim āhitaṃ sukṛtam ||SRs_1.436||
children.translated_text: and her tremulous eyes — what merit was deposited by the Creator in creating her? ||SRs_1.436||

body.text: atra viśiṣṭa-vastu-nirmāṇam apuṇya-kṛtāṃ na bhavatīti loka-sthity-anurodhenaiva varṇanāt kāntiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the description accords with the worldly convention that the creation of an extraordinary object does not occur without merit, there is <s>kānti</s>.

body.text:
atha samādhiḥ-
samādhiḥ so' nya-dharmāṇāṃ yad anyatrādhiropaṇam ||SRs_1.437|| 238
body.translated_text: Now <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — <s>Samādhi</s> is the superimposition of the properties of one thing upon another. ||SRs_1.437||

body.text: yathā utphulla-gaṇḍa-yugam [ku. 3.4] ity atrotphullodgatodvelatva-rūpāṇāṃ puṣpa-prāṇi-samudra-dharmāṇaṃ gaṇḍa-sthala-manda-hāsa-rāgeṣu samāropitatvāt samādhiḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in 'with cheeks in full bloom' [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.4] — because the properties of flowers, living beings, and the ocean — namely blooming, rising, and overflowing — are superimposed upon the cheeks, the gentle smile, and passion respectively, there is <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text:
atha kaṭhina-rītiḥ-
atidīrgha-samāsa-yutā bahulair varṇair yutā mahā-prāṇaiḥ |
kaṭhinā sā gauḍīyety uktā tad-deśa-budha-manojñatvāt ||SRs_1.438|| 239
body.translated_text: Now the hard style (<s>kaṭhina-rīti</s>) — That which is joined with excessively long compounds, furnished with many aspirated consonants, and is hard — that is called <s>Gauḍīyā</s>, because it pleases the learned of that region. ||SRs_1.438||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: With cheek-boulders smeared with heavy red chalk, with a disposition of irresistible pride arising from the prosperity of arms eager to harass
the brides of the celestial city blinded by the nectar sport of the mountains,
<s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), the chariot-warrior with divine weapons,

children.text: bāṇair dāśarathī rathī ratha-gataṃ vivyādha divyāyudhaḥ ||SRs_1.439||
children.translated_text: pierced <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the terror of mortals and immortals, seated in his chariot, with arrows seized by force. ||SRs_1.439||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra dīrgha-samsatvaṃ mahā-prāṇākṣara-prāyatvaṃ ca spaṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Here the predominance of long compounds and of aspirated consonants is evident.

body.text:
atha miśra-rītiḥ-
yatrobhaya-guṇa-grāma-saṃniveśas tulādhṛtaḥ |
sā miśrā saiva pāñcālīty uktā tad-deśaja-priyā ||SRs_1.440|| 240
body.translated_text: Now the mixed style (<s>miśra-rīti</s>) — Where the assemblage of qualities of both [styles] is held in balance, that is the mixed [style], and it is also called <s>Pāñcālī</s>, being dear to those born in that region. ||SRs_1.440||

body.text:
yathā-
parimlānaṃ pīna-stana-jaghana-saṅgād ubhayatas
tanor madhyasyāntaḥ parimilanam aprāpya haritam |
idaṃ vyasta-nyāsaṃ praśithila-bhujākṣepa-valanaiḥ
kṛśāṅgyāḥ santāpaṃ vadati visinī-patra-śayanam ||SRs_1.441|| [ratnāvalī 2.12]
body.translated_text: For example — The lotus-leaf bed, with its petals disarranged by the tossing of limp arms, its green inner center unreached by contact because of the pressing of her full breasts and hips on both sides, declares the torment of the slender-limbed woman. ||SRs_1.441|| [<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.12]

body.text: atrālpa-samāsatva-dīrgha-samāsatva-rūpayoḥ prasāda-sphuṭa-bandhatva-rūpayor aniṣṭhurākṣara-prāyatva-rūpayoḥ pṛthak-padatva-granthilatvayoś ca ubhaya-rīti-dharmayos tulādhṛtayor iva saṃniveśān miśreyaṃ rītiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the characteristics of both styles — shortness and length of compounds, clarity and tightness of composition, predominance of non-harsh syllables, independence of words and knottiness — are arranged as if held in balance, this is the mixed style.

body.text:
āndhrī lāṭī ca saurāṣṭrīty ādayo miśra-rītayaḥ |
santi tat-tad-deśa-vidvat-priya-miśraṇa-bhedataḥ ||SRs_1.442|| 241
ta eva pada-saṅghātās tā evārtha-vibhūtayaḥ |
tathāpi navyaṃ bhavati kāvyaṃ grathana-kauśalāt ||SRs_1.443|| 242
tāsāṃ grantha-gaḍutvena lakṣaṇaṃ nocyate mayā |
bhojādi-grantha-bandheṣu tad-ākāṅkṣibhir īkṣyatām ||SRs_1.444|| 243
body.translated_text: <s>Āndhrī</s>, <s>Lāṭī</s>, <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s>, and so forth are [also] mixed styles, differing by the type of mixture pleasing to the learned of each respective region. ||SRs_1.442|| The very same groups of words, the very same abundances of meaning — yet poetry becomes novel through skill in composition. ||SRs_1.443|| I do not state the characteristics of these [subsidiary styles] in full, as they would be a tumor on the work; let those who desire them look in the compositions of <s>Bhoja</s> and others. ||SRs_1.444||

body.text:
atha vṛttayaḥ-
bhāratī sātvatī caiva kaiśiky ārabhaṭīti ca |
catasro vṛttayas tāsām utpattir vakṣyate sphuṭam ||SRs_1.445|| 244
jagaty ekārṇave jāte bhagavān avyayaḥ pumān |
bhogi-bhogam adhiṣṭhāya yoga-nidrā-paro' bhavat ||SRs_1.446|| 245
tadā vīrya-madonmattau daityendrau madhu-kaiṭabhau |
tarasā devadeveśam āgatau raṇa-kāṅkṣiṇau ||SRs_1.447|| 246
vividhaiḥ paruṣair vākyair adhikṣepa-vidhāyinau |
muṣṭi-jānu-prahāraiś ca yodhayāmāsatur harim ||SRs_1.448|| 247
tan-nābhi-kamalotpannaḥ prajāpatir abhāṣata |
kim etad bhāratī-vṛttir adhunāpi pravartate ||SRs_1.449|| 248
tad imau naya durdharṣau nidhanaṃ tvarayā vibho |
iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā nijagāda janārdanaḥ ||SRs_1.450|| 249
idaṃ kāvya-kriyā-hetor bhāratī nirmitā dhruvam |
bhāṣaṇād vākya-bāhulyād bhāratīyaṃ bhaviṣyati ||SRs_1.451|| 250
adhunaiva nihanmy etāv ity ābhāṣya vaco hariḥ |
nirmalair nirvikāraiś ca sāṅga-hārair manoharaiḥ ||SRs_1.452|| 251
aṅgais tau yodhayāmāsa daityendrau yuddha-śālinau |
bhūmi-sthānaka-saṃyogaiḥ pada-kṣepais tathā hareḥ ||SRs_1.453|| 252
bhūmes tadābhavad bhāras tad-vaśād api bhāratī |
valgitaiḥ śārṅgiṇas tatra dīptaiḥ sambhrama-varjitaiḥ ||SRs_1.454|| 253
sattvādhikair bāhu-daṇḍaiḥ sātvatvī vṛttir udgatā |
vicitrair aṅga-hāraiś ca helayā sa tadā hariḥ ||SRs_1.455|| 254
yat tau babandha keśeṣu jātā sā kaiśikī tataḥ |
sa-saṃrambhaiḥ savegaiś ca citra-cārī-samutthitaiḥ ||SRs_1.456|| 255
niyuddha-karaṇair jātā citrair ārabhaṭī tataḥ |
yasmāc citrair aṅgahāraiḥ kṛtaṃ dānava-mardanam ||SRs_1.457|| 256
tasmād abja-bhuvā loke niyuddha-samayaḥ kṛtaḥ |
yaḥ śastrāstrādi-mokṣeṣu nyāyaḥ sa pāribhāṣitaḥ ||SRs_1.458|| 257
nāṭya-kāvya-kriyā-yoge rasa-bhāva-samāśritaḥ |
sa eva samayo dhātrā vṛttir ity eva saṃjñitaḥ ||SRs_1.459|| 258
hariṇā tena yad vastu valigitair yādṛśaṃ kṛtam |
tadvad eva kṛtā vṛttir dhātrā tasyāṅga-sambhavā ||SRs_1.460|| 259
ṛgvedāc ca yajurvedāt sāmavedād atharvaṇaḥ |
bhāraty-ādyā kramāj jātā ity anye tu pracakṣate ||SRs_1.461|| 260
body.translated_text: Now the dramatic modes (<s>vṛtti</s>) — <s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Sātvatī</s>, <s>Kaiśikī</s>, and <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> — these are the four <s>vṛttis</s>; their origin will now be clearly stated. ||SRs_1.445|| When the world had become a single ocean, the imperishable Supreme Person (<s>Bhagavān</s>), reclining upon the coils of the Serpent, was absorbed in the sleep of <s>Yoga</s> (<s>yoga-nidrā</s>). ||SRs_1.446|| Then, intoxicated with the pride of their power, the two demon-lords <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, eager for battle, swiftly approached the Lord of the gods of gods. ||SRs_1.447|| Hurling various harsh words of abuse, and striking with fist-blows and knee-blows, they fought <s>Hari</s>. ||SRs_1.448|| Then <s>Prajāpati</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), born from His navel-lotus, spoke: 'What is this? The <s>Bhāratī</s> mode is being enacted even now! ||SRs_1.449|| Bring these two invincible ones to their destruction swiftly, O Lord!' Hearing his words, <s>Janārdana</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) replied: ||SRs_1.450|| 'This <s>Bhāratī</s> has surely been fashioned for the purpose of poetic composition; from speech and abundance of words, it shall be known as <s>Bhāratī</s>. ||SRs_1.451|| I shall slay these two right now!' — having spoken thus, <s>Hari</s>, with limbs that were pure, unperturbed, and charming with complete <s>aṅgahāras</s> (choreographic movements), ||SRs_1.452|| fought the two demon-lords, who were skilled in battle. Through <s>Hari</s>'s footwork and earth-stances, ||SRs_1.453|| the earth bore weight — from that also arose <s>Bhāratī</s>. From <s>Hari</s>'s leaps, which were radiant and unhurried, ||SRs_1.454|| charged with <s>sattva</s> (heroic energy), [performed] with his staff-like arms, the <s>Sātvatī</s> mode arose. And with various graceful <s>aṅgahāras</s>, when he playfully ||SRs_1.455|| seized those two by their hair — from that arose <s>Kaiśikī</s>. With movements that were forceful and swift, arising from elaborate combat-techniques, ||SRs_1.456|| with extraordinary wrestling maneuvers, <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> arose. Because the crushing of the demons was accomplished through extraordinary <s>aṅgahāras</s>, ||SRs_1.457|| <s>Brahmā</s> (the Lotus-born) established in the world the convention of wrestling. The principle governing the discharge of weapons and missiles is the rule established [thereby]. ||SRs_1.458|| In the practice of dramatic and poetic composition, that same convention, grounded in <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>, was named <s>vṛtti</s> (dramatic mode) by the Creator. ||SRs_1.459|| Whatever substance was produced by <s>Hari</s> through those leaps and such [movements] — in exactly that manner the <s>vṛtti</s>, born of his limbs, was fashioned by the Creator. ||SRs_1.460|| Others, however, state that <s>Bhāratī</s> and the rest arose in order from the <s>Ṛg-veda</s>, <s>Yajur-veda</s>, <s>Sāma-veda</s>, and <s>Atharva-veda</s>. ||SRs_1.461||

body.text:
tatra bhāratī -
prayuktatvena bharatair bhāratīti nigadyate |
prastāvanopayogitvāt sāṅgaṃ tatraiva lakṣyate ||SRs_1.462|| 261
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>Bhāratī</s> — Because it is employed by actors (<s>Bharatas</s>), it is called <s>Bhāratī</s>. Because it serves the introduction (<s>prastāvanā</s>), its full [definition] is observed therein. ||SRs_1.462||

body.text:
atha sātvatī -
sāttvikena guṇenātityāga-śauryādinā yutā |
harṣa-pradhānā santyakta-śoka-bhāvā ca yā bhavet ||SRs_1.463|| 262
sātvatī nāma sā vṛttiḥ proktā lakṣaṇa-kovidaiḥ |

children.text: aṅgāny asyās tu catvāri saṃlāpottāpakāv api | 263
children.translated_text: that is called the <s>Sātvatī</s> mode by those learned in definitions. Its four constituents are <s>saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue) and <s>uttāpaka</s> (exciter),

children.text: saṅghātyaḥ parivartaś cety eṣāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate ||SRs_1.464||
children.translated_text: <s>saṅghātya</s> (combination) and <s>parivarta</s> (reversal) — the definitions of these are now stated. ||SRs_1.464||

body.translated_text: Now <s>Sātvatī</s> — That which is endowed with the <s>sāttvika</s> quality characterized by sacrifice, valor, and the like, which is dominated by joy, and in which the sentiment of sorrow is abandoned — ||SRs_1.463||

body.text: īrṣyā-krodhādibhir bhāvai rasair vīrādbhutādibhiḥ | 264
body.translated_text: Through <s>bhāvas</s> such as jealousy and anger, and <s>rasas</s> such as the heroic and the marvelous,

body.text: parasparaṃ gabhīroktiḥ saṃlāpa iti śabdyate ||SRs_1.465|| 265ab
body.translated_text: that which is a profound mutual utterance — that is called <s>saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue). ||SRs_1.465||

body.text:
yathānargha-rāghave, rāmaḥ-
bandīkṛtya jagad-vijitvara-bhuja-stambhaugha-duḥsañcaraṃ
rakṣo-rājam api tvayā vidadhatā sandhyā-samādhi-vratam |
pratyakṣīkṛta-kārtavīrya-caritām unmucya revāṃ samaṃ
sarvābhir mahiṣībhir ambu-nidhayo viśve' pi vismāpitāḥ ||SRs_1.466|| (5.44)
body.translated_text: As in <s>Anargha-rāghava</s>, <s>Rāma</s> [says] — 'Having imprisoned the king of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, whose arms, pillars of world-conquest, made passage difficult, and having observed the twilight meditation-vow by you, [you] who manifested the exploits of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, having released the <s>Revā</s> (Narmadā) river together with all his queens — even the oceans were astonished.' ||SRs_1.466|| (5.44)

body.text:
bālī (vihasya):
cirāya rātriṃcara-vīra-cakra-
mārāṅka-vaijñānika payśatas tvām |
sudhāsadharmāṇam imāṃ ca vācaṃ
na śṛṇvatas tṛpyati mānasaṃ me ||SRs_1.467|| (5.45)
body.translated_text: <s>Bālī</s> (laughing): 'For a long time, seeing you — the moon-mark on the forehead of the circle of night-wandering heroes, an expert — my mind is not satisfied hearing this speech of yours, which is akin to nectar.' ||SRs_1.467|| (5.45)

body.text: atra dhīrodātta-dhīroddhatayoḥ rāma-bālinoḥ parasparaṃ yuddha-cikīrṣābhiprāya-yogād anyonya-parākramotkarṣa-varṇanāt saṃlāpaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the dialogue (<s>saṃlāpa</s>) arises between <s>Rāma</s>, the <s>Dhīrodātta</s> (steadfast-exalted hero), and <s>Bālī</s>, the <s>Dhīroddhata</s> (steadfast-haughty hero), through their mutual intent to fight and through the description of each other's supreme valor.

body.text:
atha utthāpakaḥ -
preraṇaṃ yat parasyādau yuddhāyotthāpakas tu saḥ ||SRs_1.468|| 265
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Utthāpaka</s> (provocator) — that which is the initial instigation of another to battle is called <s>Utthāpaka</s>. ||SRs_1.468||

body.text:
yathānargha-rāghave, yathā-
nṛpān apratyakṣān kim apavadase nanv ayam ahaṃ
śiśu-krīḍā-bhagna-tripura-hara-dhanvā tava puraḥ |
ahaṅkāra-krūrārjuna-bhuja-vana-vraścana-kalā-
nisṛṣṭārtho bāhuḥ kathaya kataras te paraharatu ||SRs_1.469|| (4.56)
body.translated_text: As in <s>Anargha-rāghava</s>, for example — 'Why do you disparage kings who are absent? Here I am before you, who broke the bow of the Destroyer of the Three Cities (<s>Tripura-hara</s>, <s>Śiva</s>) as a child's game. This arm, whose purpose was discharged in the art of felling the forest of the arms of the arrogance-cruel <s>Arjuna</s> (<s>Kārtavīrya</s>) — tell me, which [arm] of yours shall strike me?' ||SRs_1.469|| (4.56)

body.text: atra rāmabhadreṇa prāk prahārāya jāmadagnyaḥ prerita ity utthāpakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) was first provoked to strike by <s>Rāmabhadra</s> — hence this is an <s>Utthāpaka</s>.

body.text:
atha saṅghātyaḥ -
mantra-śaktyārtha-śaktyā vā daiva-śaktyātha pauruṣāt |
saṅghasya bhedanaṃ yat tu saṅghātyaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ ||SRs_1.470|| 266
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Saṅghātya</s> (alliance-breaker) — the breaking of an alliance through the power of counsel (<s>mantra-śakti</s>), the power of wealth (<s>artha-śakti</s>), the power of destiny (<s>daiva-śakti</s>), or through prowess — that is called <s>Saṅghātya</s>. ||SRs_1.470||

body.text: mantro naya-prayogaḥ | tasya śaktyā yathā mudrā-rākṣase cāṇakyena śatru-sahāyānāṃ bhedanāt saṅghātyaḥ | artha-śaktyā yathā mahābhārate ādiparvaṇi devais tilottamālakṣaṇenārthena sundopasundayor atisnigdhayor bhedanāt saṅghātyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Mantra</s> means the application of statecraft. Through its power, as in <s>Mudrā-rākṣasa</s>, <s>Cāṇakya</s> broke apart the allies of the enemy — hence <s>Saṅghātya</s>. Through the power of wealth, as in the <s>Ādiparvan</s> of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, the gods caused a rift between <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, who were deeply attached to each other, through the device of <s>Tilottamā</s> — hence <s>Saṅghātya</s>.

body.text: daiva-śaktyā, yathā mahāvīra-carite mālyavān-
body.translated_text: Through the power of destiny, as in <s>Mahāvīra-carita</s>, <s>Mālyavān</s> [says] —

body.text:
hā vatsāḥ khara-dūṣaṇa-prabhṛtayo vadhyāḥ stha pāpasya me
hā hā vatsa vibhīṣaṇa tvam api me kāryeṇa heyaḥ sthitaḥ |
hā mad-vatsala vatsa rāvaṇa mahat paśyāmi te saṅkaṭaṃ
vatse kekasi hā hatāsmi na cirāt trīn putrakān paśyasi ||SRs_1.471|| (ma.vī.ca. 4.11)
body.translated_text: 'Alas, dear ones — <s>Khara</s>, <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, and the others — you are destined to be slain because of my sin! Alas, alas, dear <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, you too must be abandoned by me through necessity! Alas, my dear devoted <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, I foresee great danger for you! Dear <s>Kekasī</s>, alas, I am destroyed — ere long you shall [lose] three sons!' ||SRs_1.471|| (<s>Mahāvīra-carita</s> 4.11)

body.text: atra rāghavānukūla-daiva-mohitena mālyavatā khara-dūṣaṇa-triśirasāṃ bhedaḥ saṃvihita iti saṅghātyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the rift among <s>Khara</s>, <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Triśiras</s> was brought about by <s>Mālyavān</s>, who was deluded by destiny favorable to <s>Rāghava</s> — hence <s>Saṅghātya</s>.

body.text:
atha parivartakaḥ -
pūrvodyuktasya kāryasya parityāgena yad bhavet |
kāryāntara-svīkaraṇaṃ jñeyaḥ sa parivartakaḥ ||SRs_1.472|| 267
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Parivartaka</s> (reversal) — the abandoning of a previously undertaken action and the adoption of a different course of action — that is known as <s>Parivartaka</s>. ||SRs_1.472||

body.text: yathottara-rāma-carite pañcamāṅke kumārau (anyonyaṃ prati)-aho priya-darśanaḥ kumāraḥ | (snehānurāgaṃ vivarṇya)
body.translated_text: As in the fifth act of <s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s>, the two princes (to each other) — 'Ah, what a delightful-looking prince!' (describing their mutual affection) —

body.text:
yadṛcchā-saṃvādaḥ kim u guṇa-gaṇānām atiśayaḥ
purāṇo vā janmāntara-niviḍa-baddhaḥ paricayaḥ |
nijo vā sambandhaḥ kim u vidhivaśāt ko' py avidito
mamaitasmin dṛṣṭe hṛdayam avadhānaṃ racayati ||SRs_1.473|| (u.rā.ca. 5.16)
body.translated_text: 'Is this chance conversation, or a surpassing excellence of virtues, or an acquaintance firmly bound from a previous birth, or an innate kinship, or some unknown [bond] brought about by fate? Upon seeing this one, my heart fashions attentiveness.' ||SRs_1.473|| (<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 5.16)

body.text: atra lavasya candraketoś ca parasparākāra-viśeṣa-sandarśanena raṇa-saṃrambhauddhatya-parihāreṇa vinayārjava-svīkāra-kathanāt parivartakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, when <s>Lava</s> and <s>Candraketu</s>, upon seeing each other's distinctive appearance, abandoned the impetuosity of battle-fury and adopted modesty and sincerity — this constitutes <s>Parivartaka</s>.

body.text:
atha kaiśikī -
nṛtya-gīta-vilāsādi-mṛdu-śṛṅgāra-ceṣṭitaiḥ |
samanvitā bhaved vṛttiḥ kaiśikī ślakṣṇa-bhūṣaṇā ||SRs_1.474|| 268
aṅgāny asyās tu catvāri narma tat-pūrvakā ime |
sphañja-sphoṭau ca garbhaś ca teṣāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate ||SRs_1.475|| 269
body.translated_text: Now the <s>Kaiśikī</s> [style] — the <s>Vṛtti</s> (style) that is accompanied by dance, song, graceful gestures, and other soft, erotic activities, adorned with delicate ornamentation, is <s>Kaiśikī</s>. ||SRs_1.474|| Its limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>) are four: <s>Narma</s> (jest), and those preceded by it [i.e., <s>Narma-sphañja</s>, <s>Narma-sphoṭa</s>, and <s>Narma-garbha</s>] — their definitions are now stated. ||SRs_1.475||

body.text:
tatra narma -
śṛṅgāra-rasa-bhūyiṣṭhaḥ priya-cittānurañjakaḥ |
agrāmyaḥ parihāsas tu narma syāt tat tridhā matam ||SRs_1.476|| 270
śṛṅgāra-hāsyajaṃ śuddha-hāsyajaṃ bhaya-hāsyajam |
śṛṅgāra-hāsyajaṃ narma trividhaṃ parikīrtitam ||SRs_1.477|| 271
sambhogecchā-prakaṭanād anurāga-niveśanāt |

children.translated_text: and likewise from the exposing of the beloved's offense.
The revelation of desire for union is of three kinds: through speech, through dress, and through gesture. ||SRs_1.478||

body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Narma</s> (jest) — a non-vulgar pleasantry, predominantly of the erotic sentiment (<s>Śṛṅgāra-rasa</s>), which delights the beloved's heart, is <s>Narma</s>; it is considered to be of three kinds. ||SRs_1.476|| Born of erotic humor, born of pure humor, and born of fear-humor. The <s>Narma</s> born of erotic humor is declared to be of three sub-types: ||SRs_1.477|| from the revelation of desire for union, from the disclosure of love,

body.text: tatra vācā sambhogecchā-prakaṭanād, yathā-
body.translated_text: Among these, revelation of desire for union through speech, for example —

children.text: gacchāmy acyuta darśanena bhavataḥ kiṃ tṛptir utpadyate
children.translated_text: 'I am leaving, <s>Acyuta</s> — what satisfaction arises from seeing you?

children.text: kiṃ tv evaṃ vijanasthayor hata-janaḥ sambhāvayaty anyathā |
children.translated_text: But when we two are thus alone, the wretched world imagines otherwise.'
Having said this — [<s>Hari</s>] embracing the <s>Gopī</s>, languid with the distress of futile lingering hinted at by her words fashioned as farewell,

children.text: āśliṣyan pulakotkarāñcita-tanur gopīṃ hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||SRs_1.479||
children.translated_text: his body bristling with thrills of joy — may <s>Hari</s> protect you! ||SRs_1.479||

body.text: (kāvya-prakāśādiṣv apy uddhṛtam)
body.translated_text: (This is also quoted in <s>Kāvya-prakāśa</s> and other works.)

body.text: atra nijāvasthāna-vilambanasya vyarthatvaṃ dhīratvādi-sūcakair acyutādi-padair vadantyā tayāpi gopikayā vācā sambhogecchā prakaṭiteti narma |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Gopikā</s>, through her speech using words like '<s>Acyuta</s>' and others that hint at steadfastness, declares the futility of her lingering — thereby revealing her desire for union through speech. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text: veśena sambhogecchā-prakaṭanād, yathā-
body.translated_text: Revelation of desire for union through dress, for example —

children.translated_text: When the lovely and charming moon has risen, the messenger,
with eyes whose minds are pervaded by passion,
the women, their ornaments put on in reverse order, [begin] the elaborate process of adornment,
[thereby] causing laughter among their companions. ||SRs_1.480||

body.text: atra viparīta-nyasta-bhūṣaṇa-lakṣaṇena veṣeṇa janitaiḥ sakhī-jana-hāsaiḥ kāminīnāṃ sambhogecchā prakaṭiteti narma ||
body.translated_text: Here, through the dress characterized by ornaments placed in reverse, laughter is produced among the companions — thus revealing the women's desire for union. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text: ceṣṭayā sambhogecchā-prakaṭanād, yathā-
body.translated_text: Revelation of desire for union through gesture, for example —

body.text:
sāloe cia sūre ghariṇī ghara-sāmiassa ghettūṇa |
ṇecchaṃ tassa bi pāe dhubai hasaṃtī hasaṃtassa ||SRs_1.481|| (gā.sa. 2.30)
body.translated_text: While the sun is still visible, the wife, taking hold of the master of the house,

children.translated_text: [Chāyā translation:] While the sun is still visible, the wife, taking hold of the master of the house,

children.text: necchato' pi pādau dhāvati hasantī hasataḥ ||]
children.translated_text: washes his feet even though he does not wish it, laughing as he laughs. ||SRs_1.481|| (<s>Gāthā-saptaśatī</s> 2.30)

body.text: atra sūryāstamayāt prāg eva caraṇa-prakṣālana-lakṣaṇayā kriyayā niṣkramaṇa-nivāraṇa-janitena hāsena sambhogecchā-prakaṭanān narma |
body.translated_text: Here, through the action of washing the feet even before sunset — through the laughter produced by preventing his departure — the desire for union is revealed. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text: anurāga-prakāśo' pi bhogecchā-narmavat tridhā ||SRs_1.482|| 273cd
body.translated_text: The disclosure of love (<s>anurāga-prakāśa</s>) is also, like the jest of desire for union, of three kinds. ||SRs_1.482||

body.text: vācānurāga-nivedanāt, yathā-
body.translated_text: Disclosure of love through speech, for example —

body.text:
vayaṃ tathā nāma yathāttha kiṃ vadāmy
ayaṃ tv akasmād vikalaḥ kathāntare |
kadamba-golākṛtim āśritaḥ kathaṃ
viśuddha-mugdhaḥ kula-kanyakā-janaḥ ||SRs_1.483|| (mālatī-mādhava 7.1)
body.translated_text: 'We are indeed as you say — what shall I say? But this one, for no reason, is bewildered in the midst of conversation. How can the pure, innocent young maiden have assumed the shape of a <s>kadamba</s> ball?' ||SRs_1.483|| (<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 7.1)

body.text: atra lavaṅgikayā viśuddha-mugdhaḥ kula-kanyakā-jana iti parihāsena madayantikānurāga-nivedanān narma |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Lavaṅgikā</s>, through the jest of saying 'the pure, innocent young maiden,' discloses <s>Madayantikā</s>'s love. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text:
veṣeṇānurāga-nivedanāt, yathā-
autsukyena kṛtatvarā sahabhuvā vyāvartamānā hriyā
tais tair bandhu-vadhū-janasya vacanair nītābhimukhyaṃ punaḥ |
dṛṣṭvāgre varam ātta-sādhvasa-rasā gaurī nave saṅgame
saṃrohat-pulakā hareṇa hasatā śliṣṭā śivāyāstu vaḥ ||SRs_1.484|| (ratnāvalī 1.2)[*6]
[*6] Quoted above at 1.157.
body.translated_text: Disclosure of love through dress, for example — 'Hurrying with eagerness but turning back with modesty as companion, then again brought face to face by the words of kinswomen and attendants — <s>Gaurī</s>, upon seeing the bridegroom before her, seized by the sentiment of trepidation at the new union, her body bristling with thrills, was embraced by the laughing <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) — may it be for your welfare!' ||SRs_1.484|| (<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 1.2) [Quoted above at 1.157.]

body.text: atra pulaka-saṃroha-lakṣaṇa-veṣa-janitena śivasya hasanena gaurī-hṛdayānurāgasya prakāśanān narma |
body.translated_text: Here, through <s>Śiva</s>'s laughter produced by the dress characterized by the bristling of <s>Gaurī</s>'s hair, the love in <s>Gaurī</s>'s heart is disclosed. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text: ceṣṭayānurāga-nivedanāt, yathā-
body.translated_text: Disclosure of love through gesture, for example —

body.text:
kaitavena śayite kutūhalāt
pārvatī pratimukhaṃ nipātitam |
cakṣur unmiṣati sasmitaṃ
priye vidyud āhatam iva ||SRs_1.485|| [ku.saṃ. 8.3]
body.translated_text: '<s>Pārvatī</s>, who had lain down in pretended [sleep], out of curiosity, opened her eye directed toward her husband's face; with a smile, [Śiva saw it] — like lightning striking the beloved.' ||SRs_1.485|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.3]

body.text: atra pati-mukha-darśana-kriyā-janitena śivasya hāsena gaurī-hṛdayānurāga-nivedanān narma |
body.translated_text: Here, through <s>Śiva</s>'s laughter produced by the gesture of looking at her husband's face, the love in <s>Gaurī</s>'s heart is disclosed. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text: priyāparādha-nirbhedo' py uktas tredhā tathā budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.486|| 274ab
body.translated_text: The exposing of the beloved's offense is also stated by the learned to be of three kinds likewise. ||SRs_1.486||

body.text: vācā priyāparādha-nirbhedād, yathā mālavikāgnimitre prathamāṅke' nte devī-
body.translated_text: Exposing the beloved's offense through speech, as at the end of Act One of <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s>, the Queen [says] —

body.text: jai rāa-kajjesu īrisī ṇiuṇadā ayya-uttassa tadā sohaṇaṃ habe | (yadi rāja-kāryeṣu īdṛśī nipuṇatā ārya-putrasya, tadā śobhanaṃ bhavet |) ||SRs_1.487||
body.translated_text: 'If my lord has such skill in royal affairs, then it would be splendid!' ||SRs_1.487||

body.text: atra īdṛśī nipuṇatā yadīti caturokti-parihāsena tvayaiva mālavikā-darśanena nāṭyācaryayor vivādaḥ saṃvihita iti priyāparādhoghāṭanān narma |
body.translated_text: Here, through the witty jest 'if such skill' — [implying that] 'you yourself arranged the dispute between the two dance-masters as a pretext for seeing <s>Mālavikā</s>' — the beloved's offense is exposed. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text: veṣeṇa priyāparādha-nirbhedād, yathā-

children.text: ālepaḥ kriyatām ayaṃ druta-gati-svedair ivārdraṃ vapus
children.translated_text: 'Let this unguent be applied — your body seems moist as if from the sweat of hasty walking;
let that garland be removed — it seems crushed as if by the touch of the sun's rays.'
Thus spoken by the supremely steadfast beloved, with her lotus-face gently smiling —

children.text: cāṭūktāni bhavanti hanta kṛtināṃ modāya bhogād api ||SRs_1.488||
children.translated_text: alas, such witty words bring delight to the fortunate even more than love-making itself! ||SRs_1.488||

body.translated_text: Exposing the beloved's offense through dress, for example —

body.text: atra svedodgama-mālya-mlānatvayor druta-gamana-ravi-kara-sparśa-rūpa-kāraṇāsatyatva-kathana-rūpeṇa parihasanena sapatnī-sambhoga-rūpa-priyāparādha-nirbhedanān narma |
body.translated_text: Here, through the jest of stating false causes — hasty walking and sun's rays — for the perspiration and the wilted garland, the beloved's offense of union with a rival wife is exposed. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text: ceṣṭayā priyāparādha-nirbhedād, yathā-
body.translated_text: Exposing the beloved's offense through gesture, for example —

body.text:
lolad-bhrū-latayā vipakṣa-dig-upanyāse' vadhūtaṃ śiras
tad-vṛttānta-nirīkṣaṇe kṛta-namaskāro vilakṣaḥ sthitaḥ |
kopāt tāmra-kapola-bhittini mukhe dṛṣṭyā gataḥ pādayor
utsṛṣṭo guru-sannidhāv api vidhir dvābhyāṃ na kālocitaḥ ||SRs_1.489|| (amaru 79)
body.translated_text: 'When [the husband] indicated the direction of the rival, she shook her head with a swaying brow-creeper; when he looked for that story [in her face], he stood abashed having bowed; from anger, her cheek-wall reddened, his gaze fell to her feet — [but] released [even from there] in the presence of elders — the conduct of these two was not appropriate to the occasion.' ||SRs_1.489|| (<s>Amaru</s> 79)

body.text: atha vilakṣa-sthiti-śirodhūnana-ceṣṭayā priyāparādha-nirbhedanān narma |
body.translated_text: Here, through the gesture of the abashed stance and the head-shaking, the beloved's offense is exposed. This constitutes <s>Narma</s>.

body.text:
atha śuddha-hāsyajam -
śuddha-hāsyajam apy uktaṃ tadvad eva tridhā budhaiḥ ||SRs_1.490|| 274cd
body.translated_text: Now <s>Narma</s> born of pure humor — that born of pure humor is also stated by the learned to be of three kinds, in the same manner. ||SRs_1.490||

body.text: tatra vācā śuddha-hāsyajaṃ, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Prying open the luminous caverns of the mouth of <s>Vāsuki</s>, from the corners,
touching with the forefinger the venom-mottled tooth-buds, counting them —

children.text: ekaṃ trīṇi navāṣṭa sapta ṣaḍ iti vyastāsta-saṃkhyā-kramā
children.translated_text: "One, three, nine, eight, seven, six" — in disordered and confused sequence of numbers —

children.text: vācaḥ śakti-dharasya śaiśava-kalāḥ kurvantu vo maṅgalam ||SRs_1.491||
children.translated_text: may the childhood sports of the Spear-bearer (<s>Kārttikeya</s>) bring you auspiciousness!' ||SRs_1.491||

body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Narma</s> born of pure humor through speech, for example —

body.text: (daśarūpāvaloke' py uddhṛtam idam | bāṇasyeti sūkti-muktāvalau)
body.translated_text: (This is also quoted in <s>Daśarūpāvaloka</s>. 'Of <s>Bāṇa</s>' — in <s>Sūkti-muktāvalī</s>.)

body.text: veṣeṇa śuddha-hāsyajaṃ, yathā-
body.translated_text: <s>Narma</s> born of pure humor through dress, for example —

body.text:
snāyu-nyāsa-nibaddha-kīka-satanuṃ nṛtyantam ālokya māṃ
cāmuṇḍā-karatāla-kuṭṭita-layaṃ vṛtte vivāhotsave |
hrī-mudrām apanudya yad vihasitaṃ devyā samaṃ śambhunā
tenādyāpi mayi prabhuḥ sa jagatām āste prasādonmukhaḥ ||SRs_1.492|| (bā.rā. 2.1)
body.translated_text: 'Seeing me dance at the wedding celebration, [my body] slender with sinews bound to bones, keeping time to the beat of <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>'s hand-clapping — the laughter that <s>Devī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) shared with <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), casting aside the seal of modesty — by virtue of that, even today the Lord of the worlds remains disposed to grace toward me.' ||SRs_1.492|| (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 2.1)

body.text: atra bhṛṅgi-riṭi-veṣeṇa śivayor hasitāvirbhāvāc chuddha-hāsyajam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the appearance of <s>Bhṛṅgi-riṭi</s>'s dress, laughter arose in <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Pārvatī</s> — this is <s>Narma</s> born of pure humor.

body.text: ceṣṭayā śuddha-hāsyajaṃ, yathā-
body.translated_text: <s>Narma</s> born of pure humor through gesture, for example —

children.translated_text: '<s>Devī</s> (Pārvatī), displaying a graceful dance (<s>lāsya</s>), sweet with playful words,

children.text: yaḥ śṛṅgāro rahasi purataḥ patyur āviṣkṛto' bhūt |
children.translated_text: revealed before her husband in private the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment);
may the humor born of that protect you — [<s>Gaṇeśa</s>], the imitator of his mother,
manifesting it through playful dance-steps of grotesque gait, the Elephant-faced one.' ||SRs_1.493||

body.text:
atha bhaya-hāsyajam -
hāsyād bhayena janitāj janitaṃ bhaya-hāsyajam |
tad dvidhā mukham aṅgaṃ tu tad dvayaṃ pūrvavat tridhā ||SRs_1.494|| 275
body.translated_text: Now <s>Narma</s> born of fear-humor — that which is produced from humor arising from fear is called <s>Narma</s> born of fear-humor. It is of two kinds: primary (<s>mukhya</s>) and subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>); and each of those two is of three kinds, as before. ||SRs_1.494||

body.text: mukhyaṃ bhaya-hāsyajaṃ, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'When chased with terrible howling by a new dog belonging to the lord of the field, hostile to his grotesque form,

children.text: ghorārāvam abhidrutasya vikaṭaiḥ paścāt padair gacchataḥ |
children.translated_text: [<s>Bhṛṅgi-riṭi</s>] running behind with ungainly steps,

children.text: pā pā pāhi phahīti satvarataraṃ vyastākṣaraṃ jalpato
children.translated_text: crying out rapidly with jumbled syllables "Pā! Pā! Pāhi! Phahī!" —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā bhṛṅgiriṭer daśāṃ paśupatiḥ smerānanaḥ pātu vaḥ ||SRs_1.495||
children.translated_text: seeing the plight of <s>Bhṛṅgi-riṭi</s>, may <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva), with a smiling face, protect you!' ||SRs_1.495||

body.translated_text: Primary <s>Narma</s> born of fear-humor, for example —

body.text: atra bhṛṅgiriṭer vikṛtākāreṇa vikaṭa-paścād-gamanena pāhi pāhi pāhīty atra varṇa-vyatyāsa-bhāṣaṇena janitasya paśupati-hāsasyānya-rasānaṅgatayā mukhyaṃ bhaya-hāsyajam |
body.translated_text: Here, through <s>Bhṛṅgi-riṭi</s>'s grotesque form, his ungainly running from behind, and his speaking 'Pāhi pāhi pāhī' with transposed syllables, the laughter of <s>Paśupati</s> is produced — and since it is unconnected with any other <s>Rasa</s>, this is primary <s>Narma</s> born of fear-humor.

body.text: vācā anya-rasāṅgaṃ bhaya-hāsyajaṃ, yathā ratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: <s>Narma</s> born of fear-humor as a subsidiary of another <s>Rasa</s>, through speech, as in <s>Ratnāvalī</s> —

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-kahaṃṇa kido pasādo devīe ja ajjaṃ biakkhada-sarīrā ciṭṭhahma | (kathaṃ na kṛtaḥ prasādo devyā yad adyāpy akṣata-śarīrās tiṣṭhāmaḥ |)
body.translated_text: <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (Jester) — How has the queen not shown favor, since even today we stand with our bodies unscathed? (How has the queen not shown favor, since even today we stand with our bodies unscathed?)

body.text: rājā (sa-smitam)-dhiṅ mūrkha ! kim evam upahasasi ? tvat-kṛta evāyam āpatito' smākam anartha-kramaḥ | (3.14ad) ||SRs_1.496||
body.translated_text: The King (with a smile) — Shame on you, fool! Why do you mock thus? It is because of you that this sequence of misfortune has befallen us! (3.14ad) ||1.496||

body.text: veṣeṇa, yathā-

children.translated_text: May it be auspicious for you — at the marriage ceremony with the trident-bearer (<s>Pināka-pāṇi</s>, <s>Śiva</s>),
of her who was frightened by the serpent-bracelets,
with a startled glance suddenly [uttering] 'Namaḥ Śivāya' —
the face of <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), bowed with a smile at the half-utterance. ||1.497||

body.translated_text: By attire (<s>veṣa</s>), for example —

body.text: (rasa-kalikāyām apy uddhṛtam idam, 23 puṭe)
body.translated_text: (This is also quoted in the <s>Rasa-kalikā</s>, folio 23.)

body.text: atra bhujaga-kaṅkaṇa-lakṣaṇena veṣeṇa janitasya pārvatī-bhaya-hāsyāsya śṛṅgārāṅgatayā kathanāt tad idam aṅgaṃ bhaya-hāsyajam |
body.translated_text: Here, since the humor arising from <s>Pārvatī</s>'s fear — caused by the attire characterized by serpent-bracelets — is described as a subsidiary of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, this is a subsidiary born of fear-humor.

body.text:
ceṣṭayā, yathā-
prahlāda-vatsala vayaṃ bibhimo vihārād
asmād iti dhvanita-narmasu gopikāsu | līlā-mṛdu stana-taṭeṣu nakhāṅkurāṇi

children.translated_text: may the peacock-feather-crowned one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) protect you! ||1.498||

body.translated_text:
By gesture (<s>ceṣṭā</s>), for example —
O <s>Prahlāda</s>-lover, 'we are afraid of this sport,' said the <s>gopikās</s> in playful jest. Applying the tips of his nails gently on their breast-slopes,

body.text: atra nakhāṅkura-vyāpāreṇa janitasya gopikā-hasitasya prahlāda-vatsaleti caturokti-rūpasya śṛṅgārāṅgatayā tad idam aṅgaṃ bhaya-hāsyajam |
body.translated_text: Here, since the laughter of the <s>gopikās</s> produced by the act of nail-play, which is in the form of witty repartee [expressed as] 'O <s>Prahlāda</s>-lover,' is described as a subsidiary of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, this is a subsidiary born of fear-humor.

body.text:
agrāmya-narma-nirmāṇa-vedinā siṃha-bhūbhujā |
narmāṣṭādaśadhā bhinnam eva sphuṭam udāhṛtam ||SRs_1.499|| 276
body.translated_text:
By <s>Siṃha-bhūbhuja</s> (King <s>Siṃhabhūpāla</s>), who knows the creation of refined wit,
wit (<s>narma</s>) has been clearly illustrated in its eighteen varieties. ||1.499||

body.text:
atha narma-sphañjaḥ -
narma-sphañjaḥ sukhodyogo bhayānto nava-saṅgame ||SRs_1.500|| 277ab
body.translated_text:
Now, <s>narma-sphañja</s> (abortive union) —
<s>Narma-sphañja</s> is a joyful endeavor ending in fear during a new union. ||1.500||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: With conversation ceased, with various arts of love-play abandoned,
with the garment's edge loosened by the commencement of hand-contact, lying down,

children.text: muhur baddhotkampaṃ diśi diśi muhuḥ prerita-dṛśor
children.translated_text: repeatedly trembling, repeatedly casting glances in every direction —

children.text: ahalyā-sutrāmṇoḥ kṣaṇikam iva tat saṅgatam abhūt ||SRs_1.501||
children.translated_text: the union of <s>Ahalyā</s> and <s>Sutrāman</s> (<s>Indra</s>) was but momentary. ||1.501||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇe' py uddhṛtam idam)
body.translated_text: (This is also quoted in the <s>Sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇa</s>.)

body.text: atha narma-sphoṭaḥ -

children.text: narma-sphoṭas tu bhāvāṃśaiḥ sūcito' lpa-raso bhavet | 277cd
children.translated_text: <s>Narma-sphoṭa</s> is that which, indicated by traces of emotion (<s>bhāva</s>), is of slight <s>rasa</s>;

children.text: anyais tv akāṇḍe sambhoga-viccheda iti gīyate ||SRs_1.502|| 278ab
children.translated_text: by others [it is defined as] an untimely interruption of union — so it is sung. ||1.502||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>narma-sphoṭa</s> (disclosure of love) —

body.text: ādyo yathā-

children.text: snigdhaṃ vīkṣitam anyato' pi nayane yat prerayantyā tayā
children.translated_text: That tender glance she cast elsewhere [while] directing her eyes [toward him],

children.text: yātaṃ yac ca nitambayor gurutayā mandaṃ vilāsād iva |
children.translated_text: and that she walked slowly with the heaviness of her hips, as if in coquetry,

children.text: mā gā ity uparuddhayā yad api sā sāsūyam uktā sakhī
children.translated_text: and that her friend, who detained her saying 'don't go,' was told with jealousy —

children.text: sarvaṃ tat kila mat-parāyaṇam aho kāmī svatāṃ paśyatī ||SRs_1.503||
children.translated_text: all that, apparently, was directed toward me — ah, a lover sees everything as his own! ||1.503||

body.translated_text: The first type, for example —

body.text: atra sarvaṃ tat kilety aniścayenānurāgasya svalpa-mātra-sūcanayā narma-sphoṭatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, with the expression 'all that, apparently' — by the mere hint of love through uncertainty — it is a <s>narma-sphoṭa</s>.

body.text:
dvitīyo, yathā-
prāptā katham api daivāt kaṇṭham anītaiva sā prakaṭa-rāgā |
ratnāvalīva kāntā mama hastād bhraṃśitā bhavatā ||SRs_1.504|| (ratnāvalī 2.18)
body.translated_text:
The second type, for example —
Having somehow been obtained by fate and brought to [my] neck, she, her passion manifest,
like a garland of jewels (<s>Ratnāvalī</s>), my beloved, was made to slip from my hand by you! ||1.504|| (<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.18)

body.text: atra vidūṣaka-vākya sūcita-devī-śaṅkā-visṛṣṭa-sāgarikā-hastena rājñā akāṇḍe tvayā sambhoga-bhaṅgaḥ kṛta ity uktatvāt narma-sphoṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since the king — whose hand released <s>Sāgarikā</s> out of suspicion of the queen aroused by the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>'s words — says 'you have untimely broken the union,' it is a <s>narma-sphoṭa</s>.

body.text: atha narma-garbhaḥ-

children.text: netur vā nāyikāyā vā vyāpāraḥ svārtha-siddhaye | 278cd
children.translated_text: An activity of either the hero or the heroine for the accomplishment of one's own purpose,

children.text: pracchādana-paro yas tu narma-garbhaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ ||SRs_1.505|| 279ab
children.translated_text: which is intent on concealment — that is proclaimed as <s>narma-garbha</s>. ||1.505||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>narma-garbha</s> (concealed purpose) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Arising suddenly from the circle of smiling-faced friends
where <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) had secretly taken shelter amid the deliberations of remorse for [her] wounded pride,

children.text: samaneṣye dhūrtaṃ tam aham iti jalpan nata-mukhīṃ
children.translated_text: [saying] 'I shall bring that rogue here,' and embracing

children.text: priyāntām āliṅgan harir arati-khedaṃ haratu vaḥ ||SRs_1.506||
children.translated_text: the bowed-faced beloved — may <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) remove the pain of your displeasure! ||1.506||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra kupitāyāḥ śriyaḥ prasādanārthaṃ puruṣottamena pracchanna-sthityādi-rūpo vyāpāraḥ kṛta ity ayaṃ narma-garbhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since <s>Puruṣottama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) performed an activity in the form of concealed positioning and the like, for the purpose of propitiating the angry <s>Śrī</s>, this is a <s>narma-garbha</s>.

body.text: pūrva-sthito vipadyeta nāyako yatra cāparas tiṣṭhet | 279cd
body.translated_text: Where a previous hero falls [from fortune] and another stands [in his place] —

body.text: tam apīha narma-garbhaṃ pravadati bharato hi nāṭya-veda-guruḥ ||SRs_1.507|| 280ab
body.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s>, the teacher of the <s>Nāṭya-veda</s>, declares that too to be a <s>narma-garbha</s>. ||1.507||

children.translated_text: For example —

children.text: mayena nirmitāṃ laṅkāṃ labdhvā mandodarīm api |
children.translated_text: Having obtained <s>Laṅkā</s> constructed by <s>Maya</s>, and also <s>Mandodarī</s>,
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> enjoyed them as if they were the embodied fortune of the ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>). ||1.508||

body.text: (sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇe' py uddhṛtam idam)
body.translated_text: (This is also quoted in the <s>Sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇa</s>.)

body.text: atra rāvaṇe vipanne tat-padābhiṣiktena vibhīṣaṇena mandodaryādiṣu tad ucitaṃ karma nirmitam ity ayaṃ narma-garbhaḥ | kecit tv etad ārabhaṭī-bhedaṃ saṅkṣiptim āhuḥ | tatra mūlaṃ na jānīmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, when <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had fallen, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, consecrated to his position, performed what was appropriate regarding <s>Mandodarī</s> and others — thus this is a <s>narma-garbha</s>. Some, however, call this an <s>ārabhaṭī</s>-subtype, <s>saṅkṣipti</s>. We do not know the basis for that.

body.text: athārabhaṭī -

children.translated_text: Abounding in magic and <s>Indra</s>'s illusions, consisting of wondrous battle-deeds,

children.text: chedyair bhedyaiḥ plutair yuktāṃ vṛttim ārabhaṭīṃ viduḥ ||SRs_1.509||
children.translated_text: combined with cutting, piercing, and leaping — this mode is known as <s>Ārabhaṭī</s>. ||1.509||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> (violent/supernatural dramatic mode) —

body.text: aṅgāny asyās tu catvāri saṅkṣiptir avapātanam | 281
body.translated_text: Its limbs are four: <s>saṅkṣipti</s> (condensation), <s>avapātana</s> (attack),

body.text: vastūtthāpana-sampheṭāv iti pūrve babhāṣire ||SRs_1.510||
body.translated_text: <s>vastūtthāpana</s> (creating illusory objects), and <s>sampheṭa</s> (clash) — so the ancients declared. ||1.510||

body.text: tatra saṅkṣiptiḥ -

children.translated_text: That which has condensed subject-matter and is fashioned through magical artifice

children.text: sā saṅkṣiptir iti proktā bharatena mahātmanā ||SRs_1.511|| 283ab
children.translated_text: is called <s>saṅkṣipti</s> by the great-souled <s>Bharata</s>. ||1.511||

body.translated_text: Among these, <s>saṅkṣipti</s> (condensation) —

body.text:
yathā anargha-rāghave-
nīto dūraṃ kanaka-hariṇa-cchadmanā rāmabhadraḥ
paścād enaṃ drutam anusaraty eṣa vatsaḥ kaniṣṭhaḥ |
bibhyad bibhyat praviśati tataḥ parṇaśālāṃ ca bhikṣur
dhig dhik kaṣṭaṃ prathayati nnijām ākṛtiṃ rāvaṇo' yam ||SRs_1.512|| (5.7)
atra bahu-vidhāno māyānāṃ saṅkṣepeṇa kathanāt saṅkṣiptiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since the manifold illusions are told in condensed form, it is <s>saṅkṣipti</s>.

body.text: vadanty anye tu tāṃ netur avasthāntara-saṅgatim ||SRs_1.513|| 283cd
body.translated_text: Others, however, say that [<s>saṅkṣipti</s>] is the hero's transition to another state. ||1.513||

body.text:
yathā-
yad-artham asmābhir asi prakoptais
tad adya dṛṣṭvā tava dhāma vaiṣṇavam |
viśīrṇa-garvāmayam asmad-āntaraṃ
cirasya kañcil laghimānam aśnute ||SRs_1.514|| (a.rā. 4.59)
body.translated_text:
For example —
Having seen today your <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> splendor,
for which purpose we, enraged, [came],
our inner disease of pride is shattered,
and after a long time [our heart] attains some lightness. ||1.514|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 4.59)

body.text: atra rāmabhadra-sahavāsena parihṛta-dhīroddhata-vikārasya jāmadagnyasya dhīra-śāntāvasthā-parigrahāt saṅkṣiptir iti |
body.translated_text: Here, since <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), whose <s>dhīroddhata</s> (vehement-spirited) nature was removed through association with <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, adopted the state of <s>dhīra-śānta</s> (serene-spirited), it is <s>saṅkṣipti</s>.

body.text: parivartaka-bhedatvāt tad upekṣāmahe vayam ||SRs_1.515|| 284ab
body.translated_text: Since that is a subtype of <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal), we set it aside. ||1.515||

body.text:
athāvapātanam -
vibhrāntir avapātaḥ syāt praveśa-drava-vidravaiḥ ||SRs_1.516|| 284cd
body.translated_text:
Now, <s>avapātana</s> (attack) —
Confusion and assault through entries, flights, and routs constitute <s>avapāta</s>. ||1.516||

body.text: yathā -

children.text: hṛtvā śantanu-nandanasya turagān sūtaṃ kurūṇāṃ guroś
children.translated_text: Having seized the horses of <s>Śantanu</s>'s son (<s>Bhīṣma</s>), the charioteer of the <s>Kuru</s> preceptor (<s>Droṇa</s>),

children.text: chittvā droṇa-sutasya kārmuka-latāṃ kṛtvā visaṃjñaṃ kṛpam |
children.translated_text: having cut the bow-creeper of <s>Droṇa</s>'s son (<s>Aśvatthāman</s>), having rendered <s>Kṛpa</s> unconscious,

children.text: karṇasyāpi rathaṃ vidārya kaṇaśo vidrāvya cānyad balaṃ
children.translated_text: having shattered even <s>Karṇa</s>'s chariot to pieces, and having routed the rest of the army,
your son (<s>Abhimanyu</s>) pursues the path of the <s>Kuru</s> king (<s>Duryodhana</s>) who flees in terror! ||1.517||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (dhanañjaya-vijaya 67)
body.translated_text: (<s>Dhanañjaya-vijaya</s> 67)

body.text:
atha vastūtthāpanam -
tad-vastūtthāpanaṃ yat tu vastu māyopakalpitam ||SRs_1.518|| 285ab
yathā-

children.translated_text: Then <s>Indrajit</s>, skilled in illusion, on the battlefield, [creating] an illusory <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>),

children.text: saumitre drutam āryaputra cakitāṃ māṃ pāhi pāhīti ca |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>)! O noble lord, quickly protect me, protect me!' she cried in terror —

children.text: krośantīṃ vyathitāśayāṃ hanumatā mā meti santarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: the distressed one calling out, was threatened by <s>Hanumat</s> saying 'don't [do this]!' —
[but <s>Indrajit</s>], angry-minded and vile-hearted, cut the throat of the illusory <s>Maithilī</s> with his sword. ||1.519||

body.translated_text:
Now, <s>vastūtthāpana</s> (creating illusory objects) —
<s>Vastūtthāpana</s> is that in which the object is fashioned through illusion. ||1.518||
For example —

body.text: atra nikumbhilāyām abhicāraṃ cikīrṣuṇā indrajitā rāghavādi-buddhi-pramoṣaṇārthaṃ māyā-kalpita-maithilī-kaṇṭha-khaṇḍanaṃ kṛtam iti vastūtthāpanam |
body.translated_text: Here, since <s>Indrajit</s>, wishing to perform sorcery at <s>Nikumbhilā</s>, created and beheaded an illusory <s>Maithilī</s> for the purpose of deluding the minds of <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) and others, it is <s>vastūtthāpana</s>.

body.text:
atha sampheṭaḥ -
sampheṭas tu samāghātaḥ kruddha-saṃrabdhayor dvayoḥ ||SRs_1.520|| 285cd
body.translated_text:
Now, <s>sampheṭa</s> (clash) —
<s>Sampheṭa</s> is the mutual clash of two who are enraged and furious. ||1.520||

body.text:
yathā -
anyonya-sūtonmathanād abhūtāṃ
tāv eva sūtau rathinau ca kaucit |
vyaśvau gadā-vyāyata-samprahārau
bhagnāyudhau bāhu-vimarda-niṣṭhau ||SRs_1.521|| (ra.vaṃ. 7.52)
body.translated_text:
For example —
Through the mutual destruction of each other's charioteers, they became
at one point their own charioteers and chariot-warriors;
without horses, exchanging blows with extended maces,
with weapons broken, they ended in hand-to-hand combat. ||1.521|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.52)

body.text:
āsāṃ ca madhye vṛttīnāṃ śabda-vṛttis tu bhāratī |
tisro' rtha-vṛttayaḥ śeṣās tac-catasro hi vṛttayaḥ ||SRs_1.522|| 286
anye tu miśraṇād āsāṃ miśrāṃ vṛttiṃ ca pañcamīm |
aśeṣa-rasa-sāmānyāṃ manyante lakṣayanti ca ||SRs_1.523|| 287
body.translated_text:
Among these dramatic modes (<s>vṛttis</s>), the speech-mode is <s>Bhāratī</s>;
the remaining three are content-modes — thus there are four modes in all. ||1.522||
Others, however, by mixing these, consider and designate
a fifth mode, the mixed (<s>Miśrā</s>), as common to all <s>rasas</s>. ||1.523||

body.text:
yathā-
yatrārabhaṭy-ādi-gaṇāḥ samantā
miśratvam āśritya mithaḥ prathante |
miśreti tāṃ vṛttim uśanti dhīrāḥ
sādhāraṇīm artha-catuṣṭayasya ||SRs_1.524|| (śṛ.pra. 12) iti |
body.translated_text:
For example —
Where the groups of <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> and others, having assumed mixture,
spread among one another on all sides —
that mode the wise call <s>Miśrā</s> (mixed),
common to the four categories of content. ||1.524|| (<s>Śṛṅgāra-prakāśa</s> 12) Thus.

body.text: tan vicāra-saham | kutaḥ ? tat kiṃ vṛtti-dharmāṇāṃ miśraṇam aikya-rūpeṇa nyūnādhika-bhāvena vā | na prathamaḥ avaiṣamyeṇa miśraṇābhāvāt | tathā miśraṇe tu miśra-vṛtti-vyaṅgyo raso' pi miśro nyūnādhikaḥ prasajyeta | vṛttīnāṃca rasa-viśeṣa-niyamasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt | nanu miśrā vṛttiḥ sarva-rasa-sādhāraṇīti cet, na | bhāratyā vṛttyā apahṛta-viṣayatvāt | mūla-pramāṇābhāvena svokti-mātratvāc ca | nāpi dvitīyaḥ | vaiṣamyeṇa vṛtti-guṇānāṃ miśraṇe yatra yad-vṛtti-pratyabhijñā-hetu-bhūtā bahavo guṇā lakṣyante tatra saiva vṛttir iti niścayāt | nanu, tatra prakaraṇādi-vaśena rasa-viśeṣa-vyaktir iti cet tarhi prastuta-rasānurodhenaiva vṛtti-viśeṣa-nirdhāraṇam apy aṅgīkartavyam eva | tathā ca bharataḥ-
body.translated_text: That is open to examination. Why? Is this mixing of the properties of the modes in the form of unity or in the form of relative preponderance? Not the first, because mixing without inequality is impossible. Moreover, in such mixing, the <s>rasa</s> suggested by the mixed mode would also be mixed and of relative preponderance — which would follow absurdly. And because the restriction of modes to specific <s>rasas</s> will be stated [below]. If one objects that the mixed mode is common to all <s>rasas</s> — no, because the <s>Bhāratī</s> mode already covers that domain. Also because, lacking authoritative textual basis, it is merely [the author's] own statement. Nor the second; because when the properties of modes are mixed with inequality, wherever many properties that are the cause of recognizing a particular mode are observed, precisely that mode is determined. If one objects that in such cases, a specific <s>rasa</s> manifests according to the context and the like — then one must accept that the determination of the specific mode also follows the predominant <s>rasa</s>. And thus <s>Bharata</s> [states] —

body.text:
bhāvo vāpi raso vāpi pravṛttir vṛttir eva vā |
sarveṣāṃ samavetānāṃ rūpaṃ yasya bhaved bahu |
sa mantavyo rasaḥ sthāyī śeṣāḥ sañcāriṇo matāḥ ||SRs_1.525|| (nā.śā. 7.119-120) iti |
body.translated_text:
Whether <s>bhāva</s> or <s>rasa</s> or <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity) or <s>vṛtti</s> (mode) —
among all that are combined, that which predominates
should be considered the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion); the rest are considered <s>sañcārins</s> (transitory emotions). ||1.525|| (<s>Nāṭya-śāstra</s> 7.119-120) Thus.

body.text:
athaitāsāṃ rasa-niyamaḥ-
kaiśikī syāt tu śṛṅgāre rase vīre tu sātvatī |

children.translated_text: the <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> mode is assigned to <s>Raudra</s> (furious) and <s>Bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) [<s>rasas</s>];
and <s>Bhāratī</s> is desirable in all <s>rasas</s> beginning with <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>. ||1.526||

body.translated_text:
Now, the restriction of modes to <s>rasas</s> —
<s>Kaiśikī</s> [mode] applies to the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) <s>rasa</s>, and <s>Sāttvatī</s> to the <s>Vīra</s> (heroic);

body.text: etac ca śṛṅgārādi-grahaṇaṃ taj-janyānāṃ hāsyādīnām apy upalakṣaṇam | ataś ca śṛṅgāra-hāsyayoḥ kaiśikī | vīrādbhutayoḥ sāttvatī | raudra-karuṇayor bībhatsa-bhayānakayoś ca ārabhaṭīti niyamaḥ pratīyate | tathā ca bharataḥ-
body.translated_text: And this expression 'beginning with <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>' is an indication for the [<s>rasas</s>] born of them such as <s>Hāsya</s> (humor) and others as well. Thus the restriction is understood: <s>Kaiśikī</s> for <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>Hāsya</s>; <s>Sāttvatī</s> for <s>Vīra</s> and <s>Adbhuta</s> (wondrous); and <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> for <s>Raudra</s> and <s>Karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>Bībhatsa</s> and <s>Bhayānaka</s> (fearsome). And thus <s>Bharata</s> [states] —

children.text: śṛṅgāraṃ caiva hāsyaṃ ca vṛttiḥ syāt kaiśikī śritā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Kaiśikī</s> mode should be resorted to for <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>Hāsya</s>;
<s>Sāttvatī</s> should be known as the support of <s>Raudra</s>, <s>Vīra</s>, and <s>Adbhuta</s>. ||1.527||

body.text:
bhayānake ca bībhatse raudre cārabhaṭī bhavet |
bhāratī cāpi vijñeyā karuṇābhuta-saṃśrayā ||SRs_1.528|| (nā.śā. 20.73-74)[*7]
[*7] Variant found in K.L.Joshi edition: hāsya-śṛṅgāra-bahulā kaiśikī paricakṣitā | sātvatī cāpi vijñeyā vīrādbhuta-śamāśrayā | raudre bhayānake caiva vijñeyārabhaṭī budhaiḥ | bībhatse karuṇe caiva bhāratī samprakīrtitā ||
body.translated_text:
<s>Ārabhaṭī</s> applies to <s>Bhayānaka</s>, <s>Bībhatsa</s>, and <s>Raudra</s>;
and <s>Bhāratī</s> should be known as the support of <s>Karuṇa</s> and <s>Adbhuta</s>. ||1.528|| (<s>Nāṭya-śāstra</s> 20.73-74)
Variant found in K.L. Joshi edition: <s>Kaiśikī</s> is declared to be rich in <s>Hāsya</s> and <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>; and <s>Sāttvatī</s> should be known as the support of <s>Vīra</s>, <s>Adbhuta</s>, and <s>Śama</s>; <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> is known by the wise for <s>Raudra</s> and <s>Bhayānaka</s>; and <s>Bhāratī</s> is proclaimed for <s>Bībhatsa</s> and <s>Karuṇa</s>.

body.text: atra sātvatyā raudrānupraveśa-kathanaṃ raudra-pratibhaṭasya yuddha-vīrasyaiva saṃlāpādibhiḥ sātvatī-bhedaiḥ paripoṣaṇaṃ na tu dāna-vīra-dayā-vīrayor iti jñāpanārtham | tasmān na niyama-virodhaḥ | bhāratyāś ca karuṇādbhuta-viṣayatva-kathanaṃ tayoḥ prāyeṇa vāg-ārambha-mukhena paripoṣa iti jñāpanārtham | tena bhāratyāḥ sarva-rasa-sādhāraṇayam upapannam eva |
body.translated_text: Here, the statement that <s>Sāttvatī</s> enters the domain of <s>Raudra</s> is for the purpose of indicating that only the battle-hero (<s>yuddha-vīra</s>), who is the adversary of <s>Raudra</s>, is nourished through dialogue and other <s>Sāttvatī</s> subdivisions — not the hero of generosity (<s>dāna-vīra</s>) or the hero of compassion (<s>dayā-vīra</s>). Therefore there is no contradiction of the restriction. And the statement that <s>Bhāratī</s> pertains to <s>Karuṇa</s> and <s>Adbhuta</s> is for indicating that those [<s>rasas</s>] are generally nourished through the medium of verbal expression.
