Hence the universality of <s>Bhāratī</s> across all <s>rasas</s> is well-established.

body.text: kecit tu tam imaṃ ślokaṃ bhāratīyaṃ niyāmakam | 289
body.translated_text: Some, however, regarding this verse as authoritative for <s>Bhāratī</s>,

body.text:
prāyikābhiprāyatayā vyācakṣāṇā vicakṣaṇāḥ |
āsāṃ raseṣu vṛttīnāṃ niyamaṃ nānumanvate ||SRs_1.529|| 290
body.translated_text:
explaining it with the intent that it is [merely] general,
the discerning ones do not accept the restriction of modes to <s>rasas</s>. ||1.529||

body.text: tathā ca kaiśikīty anuvṛttau rudraṭaḥ-
body.translated_text: And thus, in the continuation of [the discussion on] <s>Kaiśikī</s>, <s>Rudraṭa</s> [says] —

body.text:
śṛṅgāra-hāsya-karuṇa-rasātiśaya-siddhaye |
eṣā vṛttiḥ prayatnena prayojyā rasa-kovidaiḥ ||SRs_1.530|| [śṛ.ti. 3.39|| iti |[*8]
[*8] Śṛṅgāra-tilaka reading: śṛṅgāra-hāsya-karuṇa-rasānāṃ parivṛddhaye | eṣā vṛttiḥ paryoktavyā prayatnena budhair yathā ||
body.translated_text: For the enhancement of the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>Hāsya</s> (comic), and <s>Karuṇa</s> (pathetic) sentiments, this mode (<s>vṛtti</s>) should be carefully employed by those expert in <s>rasa</s>. ||1.530|| [<s>Śṛṅgāra-tilaka</s> 3.39] [Note: <s>Śṛṅgāra-tilaka</s> reading: 'For the cultivation of the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, <s>Hāsya</s>, and <s>Karuṇa</s> sentiments, this mode should be carefully employed by the wise.']

body.text:
vicāra-sundaro naiṣa mārgaḥ syād ity udāsmahe |
kaiśikī-vṛtti-bhedānāṃ narmādīnāṃ prakalpanam ||SRs_1.531|| 291
yatra karuṇam āśritya rasābhāsatva-kāraṇam |
rasābhāsa-prakaraṇe vakṣyate tad idaṃ sphuṭam ||SRs_1.532|| 292
tat-tan-nyāya-pravīṇena nyāya-mārgānuvartinā |
darśitaṃ siṃha-bhūpena spaṣṭaṃ vṛtti-catuṣṭayam ||SRs_1.533|| 293
body.translated_text: This path would not be beautiful upon examination — so we set it aside. The classification of subdivisions of the <s>Kaiśikī</s> mode, such as <s>Narma</s> and the rest, ||1.531|| 291 where <s>Karuṇa</s> is made dependent [on <s>Kaiśikī</s>] — the reason for its being a <s>rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) will be clearly stated in the section on <s>rasābhāsa</s>. ||1.532|| 292 The fourfold system of <s>vṛttis</s> has been clearly demonstrated by <s>Siṃha-bhūpa</s>, who is skilled in the principles of each [topic] and follows the path of correct reasoning. ||1.533|| 293

body.text:
atha pravṛttayaḥ-
tat-tad-deśocitā bhāṣā kriyā veṣā pravṛttayaḥ |
tatra bhāṣā dvidhā bhāṣā vibhāṣā ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_1.534|| 294
tatra bhāṣā sapta-vidhā prācyāvantyā ca māgadhī |
bāhlīkā dākṣiṇātyā ca śaurasenī ca mālavī ||SRs_1.535|| 295
saptadhā syād vibhāṣādi śabara-dramilāndhrajāḥ |
śakārābhīra-caṇḍāla-vanecara-bhavā iti ||SRs_1.536|| 296
bhāṣā-vibhāṣāḥ santy anyās tat-tad-deśa-janocitāḥ |

children.translated_text: but since they are not useful [here], their characteristics are not stated. 297
The costumes and actions appropriate to each region are clearly distinct from one another. ||1.537||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Pravṛttis</s> (regional usages) — The speech, actions, and costumes appropriate to each respective region are called <s>Pravṛttis</s>. Of these, speech is twofold: <s>Bhāṣā</s> (standard language) and <s>Vibhāṣā</s> (dialect). ||1.534|| 294 Of these, <s>Bhāṣā</s> is sevenfold: <s>Prācyā</s> (Eastern), <s>Āvantyā</s>, <s>Māgadhī</s>, <s>Bāhlīkā</s>, <s>Dākṣiṇātyā</s> (Southern), <s>Śaurasenī</s>, and <s>Mālavī</s>. ||1.535|| 295 <s>Vibhāṣā</s> and the rest are likewise sevenfold: those of the <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Draviḍas</s>, <s>Andhras</s>, <s>Śakas</s>, <s>Ābhīras</s>, <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, and forest-dwellers. ||1.536|| 296 There are other languages and dialects suited to the people of their respective regions,

body.text: atha sāttvikāḥ-

children.translated_text: The mind of actors (<s>bhāvakas</s>), which engages with empathy 298
in the states of pleasure, pain, and the like of others, ||1.538||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Sāttvikāḥ</s> (involuntary psycho-physical responses) —

body.text: sattvaṃ tad iti vijñeyaṃ prājñaiḥ sattvodbhavān imān | 299
body.translated_text: that is to be understood as <s>Sattva</s> by the wise; the great sages 299

body.text: sāttvikā iti jānanti bharatādi-maharṣayaḥ ||SRs_1.539||
body.translated_text: <s>Bharata</s> and others know these, born from <s>sattva</s>, as <s>sāttvika</s>. ||1.539||

body.text: sarveṣām api bhāvānāṃ yaiḥ sva-sattvaṃ hi bhāvyate | 300
body.translated_text: Those by which the essential nature (<s>sattva</s>) of all <s>bhāvas</s> is realized — 300

body.text: te bhāvā bhāva-tattva-jñaiḥ sāttvikā samudīritāḥ ||SRs_1.540||
body.translated_text: those <s>bhāvas</s> are called <s>sāttvika</s> by those who know the truth of emotions. ||1.540||

body.text: te stambha-sveda-romāñcāḥ svara-bhedaś ca vepathuḥ | 301
body.translated_text: They are: <s>stambha</s> (stupefaction), <s>sveda</s> (perspiration), <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation), <s>svara-bheda</s> (voice-breaking), <s>vepathu</s> (trembling), 301

body.text: vaivarṇyam aśru-pralayāv ity aṣṭau parikīrtitāḥ ||SRs_1.541||
body.translated_text: <s>vaivarṇya</s> (change of color), <s>aśru</s> (tears), and <s>pralaya</s> (fainting) — thus eight are declared. ||1.541||

body.text: tatra stambhaḥ-

children.translated_text: <s>Stambha</s> arises from joy, fear, anger, despondency, and wonder. 302

children.text:
anubhāvā bhavanty ete stambhasya muni-saṃmatāḥ |
saṃjñā-virahitatvaṃ ca śūnyatā niṣprakampatā ||SRs_1.542|| 303
children.translated_text: The <s>anubhāvas</s> of <s>stambha</s>, as approved by the sages, are: loss of awareness, blankness, and motionlessness. ||1.542|| 303

body.translated_text: Of these, <s>Stambha</s> (stupefaction) —

body.text:
atha svedaḥ -
nidāgha-harṣa-vyāyāma-śrama-krodha-bhayādibhiḥ |

children.text: svedaḥ sañjāyate tatra tv anubhāvā bhavanty amī | 304
children.translated_text: <s>sveda</s> arises. The <s>anubhāvas</s> therein are: 304
wiping away perspiration, desire for wind, grasping a fan, and the like. ||1.543||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Sveda</s> (perspiration) — From heat, joy, exercise, fatigue, anger, fear, and the like,

body.text: nidāghād, yathā-

children.translated_text: The sun, taking from the lotuses whose fully-opened bellies were his own,
[drops that resembled] his own,
sprinkled upon her lotus-face
drops of nectar under the pretext of perspiration. ||1.544||

body.translated_text: From heat, as for example —

body.text: harṣād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Coming from behind, with permission given by a friend,
loosening his beloved's hairpins with his fingernails,
a certain man, though he cooled [her] even with the breeze of his mouth,
only made the perspiration within increase further. ||1.545||

body.translated_text: From joy, as for example —

body.text: atrobhayor anyonya-sparśa-harṣeṇa svedaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the perspiration of both [lovers] is from the joy of mutual touch.

body.text:
vyāyāmād, yathā-
gatvodrekaṃ jaghana-puline ruddha-madhya-pradeśaḥ
krāmann ūru-druma-bhuja-latāḥ pūrṇa-nābhi-hradāntaḥ |
ullaṅghyoccaiḥ kuca-taṭa-bhuvaṃ plāvayan roma-kūpān
svedāpūro yuvati-saritāṃ prāpa gaṇḍa-sthalāni ||SRs_1.546|| [māgha. 7.74]
body.translated_text: From exercise, as for example — 'Having swelled over the sand-bank of her hips, obstructed in the middle region, crawling along the tree-trunk-thighs as branch-creepers, past the full lake-navel within, leaping high over the terrain of the breast-slopes, flooding the pores of the skin — the flood of perspiration of the river-like young women reached the plains of their cheeks.' ||1.546|| [<s>Māgha</s> 7.74]

body.text: atra kusumāpacaya-paryaṭanena vyāyāmena svedaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the perspiration is from exercise in wandering about gathering flowers.

body.text: śramo raty-ādi-pariśrāntiḥ, tasmād yathā-

children.translated_text: Of the lotus-eyed women, disturbed by the five arrows [of <s>Kāma</s>],
who had resorted to windows for breeze,
their sweating, weary faces revealed
lovemaking [just concluded]. ||1.547||

body.translated_text: <s>Śrama</s> means the fatigue from lovemaking and the like; from that, as for example —

body.text: ādi-śabdād gīta-nṛtya-śrānty-ādayaḥ |
body.translated_text: The word 'and so forth' includes fatigue from singing, dancing, and the like.

body.text:
gīta-śrāntyā, yathā-
gītāntareṣu śrama-vāri-leśaiḥ
kiṃcit samucchvāsita-patra-lekham |
puṣpāsavāghūrṇita-netra-śobhi
priyā-mukhaṃ kiṃpuruṣaś cucumbe ||SRs_1.548|| [ku.saṃ. 3.38]
body.translated_text: From fatigue of singing, as for example — '<s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> kissed the face of his beloved — adorned with eyes beautiful from their intoxicated rolling by the flower-wine, with its leaf-ornament slightly displaced by drops of perspiration from the intervals between songs.' ||1.548|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.38]

body.text:
nṛtya-śrāntyā, yathā-
cāru-nṛtya-vigame ca tan-mukhaṃ
sveda-bhinna-tilakaṃ pariśramāt |
prema-datta-vadanānilaṃ pibann
atyajīvad amarālakeśvarau ||SRs_1.549|| [raghu. 19.15]
body.translated_text: From fatigue of dancing, as for example — 'At the end of the beautiful dance, her face with its tilaka-mark marred by perspiration from exertion — drinking the breeze of her face given in love, [<s>Aja</s>] outlived even the two lords of the gods.' ||1.549|| [<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 19.15]

body.text:
krodhād, yathā-
dadhat sandhyāruṇa-vyoma-sphurat-tārānukāriṇīḥ |
dviṣad-dveṣoparaktāṅga-saṅginīḥ sveda-vipruṣaḥ ||SRs_1.550|| [māghe 2.18]
body.translated_text: From anger, as for example — 'Bearing drops of perspiration clinging to limbs suffused with hatred for the enemy, resembling the twinkling stars in the twilight-red sky.' ||1.550|| [<s>Māgha</s> 2.18]

body.text:
bhayād, yathā-
kṛtānta-jihvā-kuṭilāṃ kṛpāṇīṃ
dṛṣṭvā yadīyāṃ trasatām arīṇām |
svedodayaś cetasi saṃcitānāṃ
mānoṣmaṇām ātanute praśāntim ||SRs_1.551|| [atraiva 1.13]
body.translated_text: From fear, as for example — 'Seeing his sword, crooked as the tongue of Death, the rising of perspiration in the terrified enemies brought about the cooling of the heat of pride accumulated in their minds.' ||1.551|| [from this very work, 1.13]

body.text: romāñco vismayotsāha-harṣādyais tatra vikriyāḥ | 305
body.translated_text: <s>Romāñca</s> (horripilation) [arises] from wonder, enthusiasm, joy, and the like. Its transformations are: 305

body.text: romodgamolluka-sanagātra-saṃsparśanādayaḥ ||SRs_1.552||
body.translated_text: rising of the body-hair, bristling, and touching of the limbs, and the like. ||1.552||

body.text: vismayena, yathā-

children.translated_text: Having heard of <s>Rāghava</s>'s (<s>Rāma</s>'s) arm-strength,
weighty in substance and formidable in its breaking of the <s>Ājagava</s> bow,
in the midst of the assembly,
the bearer of the trident (<s>Śiva</s>) experienced horripilation. ||1.553||

body.translated_text: From wonder, as for example —

body.text: utsāhena, yathā-

children.translated_text: Binding his own entrails to his foot at the moment of reprieve from unconsciousness,
armoring with horripilation the wound-openings in his limbs over which he has control,
rallying his broken [allies], threatening the enemy soldiers fiercely —
the fortunate one, in the broad pillar of battle, becomes a banner of unbridled victory-splendor. ||1.554||

body.translated_text: From enthusiasm, as for example —

body.text: atrotsāhena romāñcaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the horripilation is from enthusiasm.

body.text:
harṣeṇa, yathā-
romāṇi sarvāṇy api bāla-bhāvād
vara-śriyaṃ vīkṣitum utsukāni |
tasyās tadā korakitāṅga-yaṣṭer
udgrīvikādānam ivān bhūvan ||SRs_1.555|| (naiṣadha 14.53)
body.translated_text: From joy, as for example — 'All her body-hairs, eager in their childlike nature to behold the splendor of the bridegroom, seemed at that time to become upward-stretchings of her body-staff, which had burst into buds.' ||1.555|| (from <s>Naiṣadha</s> 14.53)

body.text:
atha svara-bhedaḥ-
vaisvaryaṃ sukha-duḥkhādyais tatra syur gadgadādayaḥ ||SRs_1.556|| 306
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Svara-bheda</s> (voice-breaking) — Voice-alteration [arises] from pleasure, pain, and the like; its [manifestations] are stammering and the like. ||1.556|| 306

body.text: sukhena, yathā-

children.translated_text: She rebuked her friend who was saying
'May we see him again';
but the voice-alterations that had reached
[her] ears as delighting in love did not recur again. ||1.557||

body.translated_text: From pleasure, as for example —

body.text: atra priya-saṃsmaraṇa-janitena harṣeṇa bhūyo vaisvaryam |
body.translated_text: Here, the repeated voice-alteration is from joy born of remembering the beloved.

body.text:
duḥkhena, yathā-
vilalāpa sa bāṣpa-gadgadaṃ
sahajām apy apahāya dhīratām |
abhitapta-mayo' pi mārdavaṃ
bhajate kaiva kathā śarīriṣu ||SRs_1.558|| (ra.vaṃ. 8.43)
body.translated_text: From pain, as for example — 'He lamented with tears and stammering, abandoning even his innate composure; for even heated iron takes on softness — what then of embodied beings?' ||1.558|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 8.43)

body.text:
atha vepathuḥ-
vepathur harṣa-santrāsa-jarā-krodhādibhir bhavet |
tatrānubhāvāḥ sphuraṇa-gātra-kampādayo matāḥ ||SRs_1.559|| 307
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vepathu</s> (trembling) — Trembling arises from joy, terror, old age, anger, and the like. Its <s>anubhāvas</s> are considered to be: quivering, shaking of limbs, and the like. ||1.559|| 307

body.text: harṣeṇa trāsena ca, yathā-

children.translated_text: The father touched that body, bearing arrow-wounds,
with an arm numb from joy;
and the mother, sighing deeply again and again,
[touched it] with hands trembling from fear. ||1.560||

body.translated_text: From joy and terror, as for example —

body.text:
jarayā, yathā-
rundhānayā bahu-mukhīṃ gatim indriyāṇāṃ
vadhveva gāḍham anayā jarayopagūḍhaḥ |
aṅgena vepathu-matā jaḍatāyujāhaṃ
gantuṃ padād api padaṃ gadituṃ ca nālam ||SRs_1.561|| (kuvalayāvalī, 3.1)
body.translated_text: From old age, as for example — 'Closely embraced by this old age — like a new bride — which blocks the manifold movement of the senses, with a trembling body joined to sluggishness, I am unable to go even a step from [my] step, or to utter [a word].' ||1.561|| (from <s>Kuvalayāvalī</s> 3.1)

body.text: krodhena, yathā-

children.translated_text: Swollen lofty as a lion-lord by rage,
not only his body trembled,
but also the earth with its oceans and mountains, and the sky,
and the heavens with its stars and falling meteors. ||1.562||

body.translated_text: From anger, as for example —

body.text:
atha vaivarṇyam-
viṣādātaparoṣādyair vaivarṇyam upajāyate |
mukha-varṇa-parāvṛtti-kārśyādyās tatra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_1.563|| 308
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vaivarṇya</s> (change of color) — Discoloration arises from despondency, heat, anger, and the like. Its transformations are: alteration of facial color, emaciation, and the like. ||1.563|| 308

body.text:
viṣādena, yathā-
śara-kāṇḍa-pāṇḍu-gaṇḍa-sthalīyam ābhāti parimitābharaṇā |
mādhava-pariṇata-patrā katipaya-kusumeva kundalatā ||SRs_1.564|| (mā.a.mi. 3.8)
body.translated_text: From despondency, as for example — 'She appears with cheek-surfaces pale as a reed-stalk, wearing few ornaments — like a <s>kundalatā</s> (jasmine creeper) that has shed its leaves in late spring, bearing only a few blossoms.' ||1.564|| (from <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 3.8)

body.text: atra viraha-janitena viṣādena pāṇḍutvam |
body.translated_text: Here, the pallor is from despondency born of separation.

body.text:
ātapena, yathā-
dhūtānām abhimukha-pātibhiḥ samīrair
āyāsād aviśad alocanotpalānām |
āninye mada-janitāṃ śriyaṃ vadhūnām
uṣṇāṃśu-dyuti-janitaḥ kapola-rāgaḥ ||SRs_1.565|| (kirātārjunīya 7.3)
body.translated_text: From heat, as for example — 'The flush on the cheeks of the young women — produced by the radiance of the hot sun — which entered [their faces] from the fatigue of winds blowing against them as they shook, from [among] the eye-lotuses, assumed the beauty born of intoxication.' ||1.565|| (from <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 7.3)

body.text:
roṣeṇa, yathā-
kadā mukhaṃ vara-tanu kāraṇād ṛte tavāgataṃ kṣaṇam ayi kopa-pātratām |
aparvaṇi graha-kaluṣendu-maṇḍalā vibhāvarī kathaya kathaṃ bhaviṣyati ||SRs_1.566|| (mālavikāgni-mitra 4.16)
body.translated_text: From anger, as for example — 'When, O beautiful one, has your face, without any cause, even for a moment attained the state of being an object of anger? Tell me, how will the night be, with its moon-disc clouded by an untimely planet?' ||1.566|| (from <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 4.16)

body.text:
athāśru-
viṣāda-roṣa-santoṣā-dhūmādyair aśru tat-kriyāḥ |
bāṣpa-bindu-parikṣepa-netra-saṃmārjanādayaḥ ||SRs_1.567|| 309
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Aśru</s> (tears) — Tears [arise] from despondency, anger, joy, smoke, and the like. Their actions are: scattering of tear-drops, wiping of the eyes, and the like. ||1.567|| 309

body.text:
viṣādena, yathā-
tvām ālikhya praṇaya-kupitāṃ dhātu-rāgaiḥ śilāyām
ātmānaṃ te caraṇa-patitaṃ yāvad icchāmi kartum |
asrais tāvan muhur upacitair dṛṣṭir ālupyate me
krūras tasminn api na sahate saṅgamaṃ nau kṛtāntaḥ ||SRs_1.568|| [me.dū. 2.45]
body.translated_text: From despondency, as for example — 'While drawing you on the rock in mineral colors, angry with love, and wishing to portray myself fallen at your feet — meanwhile, my sight is blurred by tears repeatedly welling up; cruel Fate does not permit even this meeting of ours.' ||1.568|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 2.45]

body.text: roṣeṇa ca, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: When her sinful beloved was standing before her,
a friendship suddenly arose between the lotus and the moon;
as the beautiful-eyed one was unable to utter words of anger,
the pair of blue lotuses [her eyes] received a stream of dew [tears]. ||1.569||

body.translated_text: From anger as well, as in my own [verse] —

body.text: atra sāparādha-priya-darśana-janitena roṣeṇa mugdhāyā bāṣpodgamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the welling of tears is from the anger of the innocent maiden, born of seeing the guilty beloved.

body.text:
santoṣeṇa, yathā-
ānandajaḥ śokajam aśru bāṣpas
tayor aśītaṃ śiśiro bibheda |
gaṅgā-sarayvor jalam uṣṇa-taptaṃ
himādri-niṣyanda ivāvatīrṇaḥ ||SRs_1.570|| (ra.vaṃ. 14.53)
body.translated_text: From joy, as for example — 'The tears born of joy and those born of sorrow — the cold [tear] of those two, the warm, was distinguished. Like the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Sarayū</s>, heated by warmth, as if a stream from the snowy mountain had descended.' ||1.570|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 14.53)

body.text: atra cira-proṣita-pratyāgata-rāma-lakṣmaṇa-darśanānandena kausalyā-sumitrayor bāṣpaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the tears of <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Sumitrā</s> are from the joy of seeing <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, who had returned after long absence.

body.text: dhūmena, yathā-

children.translated_text: At that moment, not perceiving her beloved, she [wept]
with trace of tears welling up, blurred by smoke,
with sidelong glances moist like the inner petals of lotuses,
[serving] as natural ear-ornaments. ||1.571||

body.translated_text: From smoke, as for example —

body.text: atra vivāha-dhūmena lakṣmyā bāṣpodgamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the welling of tears of <s>Lakṣmī</s> is from the smoke of the wedding [fire].

body.text:
atha pralayaḥ-
pralayo duḥkha-dhātādyaiś ceṣṭā tatra visaṃjñatā ||SRs_1.572|| 310ab
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Pralaya</s> (fainting) — Fainting [arises] from pain, a blow, and the like. Its [manifestation] is loss of consciousness. ||1.572|| 310ab

body.text:
duḥkhena, yathā-
vapuṣā karaṇojjhitena sā
nipatantī patim apy apātayan |
nanu taila-niṣeka-bindunā
saha dīpārcir upaiti medinīm ||SRs_1.573|| (ra.vaṃ. 8.38)
body.translated_text: From pain, as for example — 'With her body abandoned by the senses, falling, she brought down her husband too; indeed, together with the drop of sesame-oil, the lamp-flame meets the ground.' ||1.573|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 8.38)

body.text: atrendumatī-vipatti-janitena duḥkhenājasya pralayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the fainting of <s>Aja</s> is from the grief born of the calamity that befell <s>Indumatī</s>.

body.text:
ghātena, yathā-
pūrvaṃ prahartā na jaghāna bhūyaḥ
pratiprahārākṣamam aśvasādī |
turaṅgam askandha-niṣaṇṇa-dehaṃ
pratyāśvasantaṃ ripum ācakāṅkṣa ||SRs_1.574|| (ra.vaṃ. 7.47)
body.translated_text: From a blow, as for example — 'The first striker did not strike again; the horse-rider, unable to bear the counter-blow, [slumped] with his body seated on the horse without its saddle-arch; [the first striker] waited for the enemy to regain consciousness.' ||1.574|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.47)

body.text: atra pratibhaṭa-prahāreṇāśvasādino mūrcchā |
body.translated_text: Here, the fainting of the horse-rider is from the blow of the adversary.

body.text: sarve' pi sattva-mūlatvād bhāvā yadyapi sāttvikāḥ | 310cd
body.translated_text: Although all <s>bhāvas</s> are <s>sāttvika</s> because they are rooted in <s>sattva</s>, 310cd

body.text: tathāpy amīṣāṃ sattvaika-mūlatvāt sāttvika-prathā ||SRs_1.575||
body.translated_text: nevertheless, because these [eight] are exclusively rooted in <s>sattva</s> alone, they have the designation <s>sāttvika</s>. ||1.575||

body.text: anubhāvāś ca kathyante bhāva-saṃsūcanād amī | 311
body.translated_text: They are also called <s>anubhāvas</s> because they indicate the <s>bhāvas</s>. 311

body.text: evaṃ dvairūpyam eteṣāṃ kathitaṃ bhāva-kovidaiḥ ||SRs_1.576||
body.translated_text: Thus, the dual nature of these has been stated by those expert in <s>bhāvas</s>. ||1.576||

body.text:
anubhāvaika-nidhinā sukhānubhava-śālinā |
śrī-siṃha-bhūbhujā sāṅgam anubhāvā nirūpitāḥ ||SRs_1.577|| 312
body.translated_text: By the illustrious <s>Siṃha-bhūpa</s>, the sole treasury of <s>anubhāva</s>, endowed with felicity of experience, the <s>anubhāvas</s> have been described in full. ||1.577|| 312

body.text:
asmat-kalpa-latā-dalāni gilati tvat-kāma-gaurvāryatāṃ
mac-cintāmaṇi-vedibhiḥ pariṇamed dūrān nayoccair gajam |
ity ārūḍha-vitardikāḥ pratipathaṃ jalpanti bhūdevatāḥ
siṃha-kṣmābhuji kalpa-vṛkṣa-surabhī-hasty-ādi-dānodyate ||SRs_1.578|| 313
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahmins</s> standing on raised platforms cry out in every direction as <s>Siṃha-kṣmābhuj</s> (King Siṃha) prepares to distribute wish-fulfilling trees, divine cows, elephants, and other gifts — 'Our wish-fulfilling creeper swallows mere leaves! May your generosity toward wish-fulfilling jewels bear fruit! Keep the tall elephant far away from my wish-fulfilling jewel-platforms!' ||SRs_1.578||

body.text:
rakṣāyāṃ rākṣasāriṃ prabala-vimata-vidrāvaṇe vīrabhadraṃ
kāruṇye rāmabhadraṃ bhuja-bala-vibhavārohaṇe rauhiṇeyam |
pāñcālaṃ cañcalākṣī-paricaraṇa-vidhau pūrṇa-candraṃ prasāde
kandarpa-rūpa-darpe tulayati nitarāṃ siṃha-bhūpāla-candraḥ ||SRs_1.579|| 314
body.translated_text: The moon-like King <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s> compares in every way with <s>Rāma</s>'s enemy (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) in protection, with <s>Vīrabhadra</s> in routing mighty opponents, with <s>Rāmabhadra</s> in compassion, with <s>Rauhiṇeya</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) in the mounting prowess of arm-strength, with <s>Pāñcāla</s> in the attendance of restless-eyed women, and with the full moon in graciousness and with <s>Kandarpa</s> (the God of Love) in the pride of beauty. ||SRs_1.579||

body.text:
iti śrīmad-āndhra-maṇḍalādhīśvara-pratigaṇḍa-bhairava-śrīmad-anapota-narendra-nandana-bhuja-bala-bhīma-śrī-siṃha-bhūpāla-viracite rasārṇava-sudhākara-nāmni nāṭyālaṅkāra-śāstre rañjakollāso nāma
prathamo vilāsaḥ
||1||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter (<s>vilāsa</s>), named <s>Rañjakollāsa</s> (The Delight of Charming), in the treatise on dramatic ornament (<s>nāṭyālaṅkāra-śāstra</s>) called <s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s>, mighty of arm like <s>Bhīma</s>, son of the illustrious emperor <s>Anapota-narendra</s>, <s>Pratigaṇḍa-bhairava</s>, sovereign of the <s>Āndhra</s> realm. ||1||

body.text:
(2)
dvitīyo vilāsaḥ
body.translated_text: (2) Second Chapter (<s>vilāsa</s>)

body.text: rasikollāsaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Rasikollāsa</s> (The Delight of the Connoisseur)

body.text:
kalyāṇa-dāyi bhavatāṃ bhaved bhavya-guṇākaram |
kamalākucakāleya-vyañjitoraḥ-sthalaṃ mahaḥ ||SRs_2.1|| 1
cid-acit-kṣema-kāriṇyai namaḥ śrī-parṇajādibhiḥ |
vandyāyai vārdhi-nandinyai karāgrastha-payoruhe ||SRs_2.2|| 2
body.translated_text: May the radiance whose chest-mark is revealed by the saffron from the breasts of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the mine of auspicious qualities, be the bestower of welfare for you! ||SRs_2.1|| Salutations to the daughter of the ocean (<s>Vārdhi-nandinī</s>), who holds a lotus in the tip of her hand, who is worshipped by <s>Parṇaja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others, and who brings welfare to sentient and insentient beings. ||SRs_2.2||

body.text: atha vyabhicāri-bhāvāḥ-
body.translated_text: Now the transitory states (<s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s>) —

body.text:
vy-abhī ity upasargau dvau viśeṣābhimukhatvayoḥ |
viśeṣeṇābhimukhyena caranti sthāyinaṃ prati ||SRs_2.3|| 3
vāg-aṅga-sattva-sūcyā jñeyās te vyabhicāriṇaḥ |
taṃ cārayanti bhāvasya gatiṃ sañcāriṇo' pi ||SRs_2.4|| 4
unmajjanto nimajjantaḥ sthāyiny amṛta-vāridhau |
ūrmivad vardhayanty enaṃ yānti tad-rūpatāṃ ca te ||SRs_2.5|| 5
nirvedo' tha viṣādo dainyaṃ glāni-śramau ca mada-garvau |
śaṅkā-trāsāvegā unmādāpasmṛtī tathā vyādhiḥ ||SRs_2.6|| 6
moho mṛtir ālasyaṃ jāḍyaṃ vrīḍāvahitthā ca |
smṛtir atha vitarka-cintā-mati-dhṛtayo harṣa utsukatvaṃ ca ||SRs_2.7|| 7
augryam arṣāsūyāś cāpalyaṃ caiva nidrā ca |
suptir bodha itīme bhāvā vyabhicāriṇaḥ samākhyātāḥ ||SRs_2.8|| 8
body.translated_text: The two prefixes <s>vi</s> and <s>abhi</s> denote 'distinctness' and 'directedness.' They move toward the permanent state (<s>sthāyin</s>) with distinctness and directedness, ||SRs_2.3|| and they should be known as <s>vyabhicārins</s>, indicated through speech, gesture, and <s>sāttvika</s> expression. They also cause the movement of the <s>bhāva</s>; hence they are also called <s>sañcārins</s> (accompanying states). ||SRs_2.4|| Rising and sinking in the ocean of nectar that is the permanent state, like waves they augment it and assume its very nature. ||SRs_2.5|| <s>Nirveda</s> (self-deprecation), <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness), <s>glāni</s> (debility), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>garva</s> (pride), ||SRs_2.6|| <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>trāsa</s> (terror), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>unmāda</s> (delirium), <s>apasmṛti</s> (loss of memory), and <s>vyādhi</s> (sickness), ||SRs_2.7|| <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mṛti</s> (death), <s>ālasya</s> (sloth), <s>jāḍya</s> (stupor), <s>vrīḍā</s> (shame), <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>mati</s> (resolve), <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>harṣa</s> (joy), <s>utsukatva</s> (eagerness), ||SRs_2.7|| <s>augrya</s> (ferocity), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>cāpalya</s> (fickleness), and <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>supti</s> (slumber), <s>bodha</s> (awakening) — these are the <s>bhāvas</s> called <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory states). ||SRs_2.8||

body.text:
tatra (1) nirvedaḥ-
tattva-jñānāc ca daurgatyāv āpado viprayogataḥ |
īrṣyāder api saṃjātaṃ nirvedaḥ svāvamānanam ||SRs_2.9|| [*9] 9
[*9] Another reading in some manuscripts: anubhāvas tu naiṣphalya-matir nirveda ucyate | atra cintāśru-niḥśvasa-vaivarṇyocchvāsa-dīnatā ||
body.translated_text: Of these, (1) <s>Nirveda</s> (self-deprecation) — That self-disparagement which arises from knowledge of truth (<s>tattva-jñāna</s>), from misfortune (<s>daurgatya</s>), from calamity (<s>āpad</s>), from separation (<s>viprayoga</s>), or even from jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>) and the like — that is <s>nirveda</s>. ||SRs_2.9||

body.text:
tattva-jñānād, yathā-
prāptāḥ śriyaḥ sakala-kāma-dughās tataḥ kiṃ
nyastaṃ padaṃ śirasi vidviṣatāṃ tataḥ kim |
saṃmānitāḥ praṇayino vibhavais tataḥ kiṃ
kalpaṃ sthitaṃ tanu-bhṛtāṃ tanubhis tataḥ kim ||SRs_2.10|| (vairāgya-śataka 67)
body.translated_text: From knowledge of truth, for example — Wealth that fulfills all desires has been obtained — so what? The foot has been placed on the heads of enemies — so what? Loved ones have been honored with riches — so what? The body of embodied beings has endured for an aeon — so what? ||SRs_2.10|| (<s>Vairāgya-śataka</s> 67)

children.text: kiṃ vidyāsu viśāradair api sutaiḥ prāptādhika-praśrayaiḥ
children.translated_text: What use are sons learned in all sciences, who have attained great humility?
What use is a wife of beautiful form and character, favorable to oneself?
What use is a long life free from the course of diseases?

children.text: dāridryopahataṃ yad etad akhilaṃ duḥkhāya me kevalam ||SRs_2.11||
children.translated_text: All this, afflicted by poverty, is nothing but suffering to me. ||SRs_2.11||

body.text:
āpado, yathā-
surata-śrama-sambhṛto mukhe
dhriyate sveda-lavodgamo' pi te |
atha cāstamitā tvam ātmanā
dhig imāṃ deha-bhṛtām asāratām ||SRs_2.12|| (raghu. 8.57)
body.translated_text: From calamity, for example — Even the perspiration born of love-exertion is still held upon your face; and yet you have set [like the sun] — fie upon this worthlessness of embodied beings! ||SRs_2.12|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 8.57)

body.text:
viprayogād, yathā-
yaysāṃ te divasāstayā saha mayā nītā yathā sve gṛhe
yat-sambandhi-kathābhir eva satataṃ dīrghābhir asthīyate |
ekaḥ samprati nāśita-priyatamas tām eva rāmaḥ kathaṃ
pāpaḥ pañcavaṭīṃ vilokayatu vā gacchatv asambhāvya vā ||SRs_2.13|| (u.rā.ca. 2.29)
body.translated_text: From separation, for example — The days that were spent with you as in my own home, when constantly and at length I would dwell on stories related to you — now alone, the dearest one destroyed, how shall the sinful <s>Rāma</s> look upon this very <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, or shall he go elsewhere, unable to contemplate it? ||SRs_2.13|| (<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 2.29)

body.text: atra sītā-viprayuktasya rāmasya vāg-ārambha-sūcitenātmāvamānanena nirvedaḥ pratīyate |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>nirveda</s> is perceived in <s>Rāma</s>, separated from <s>Sītā</s>, through the self-disparagement indicated by the opening words [calling himself 'sinful'].

body.text: īrṣyayā, yathā-

children.text: kuryuḥ śastra-kathām amī yadi manor vaṃśe manuṣyāṅkurāḥ
children.translated_text: 'If these scions of <s>Manu</s>'s lineage were to speak of the science of weapons,

children.text: syāc ced brahma-gaṇo' yam ākṛti-gaṇas tatreṣyate ced bhavān |
children.translated_text: if this assembly of <s>Brahmins</s> were to count mere forms, and if you were to be envied there —

children.text: samrājāṃ samidhāṃ ca sādhakatamaṃ dhatte chidākāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: the greatest instrument of cutting for both kings and sacrificial kindling —
fie upon this hand of mine, knotted with callosities from drawing bowstrings and <s>kuśa</s> grass! ||SRs_2.14||

body.translated_text: From jealousy, for example —

body.text: (anargha. 4.44)
body.translated_text: (<s>Anargharāghava</s> 4.44)

body.text: atra rāmacandra-śatānanda-viṣayerṣyā-janitena dhig iti vāg-ārambha-sūcitena svātmāvamānanena jāmadagnyasya nirvedaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>nirveda</s> of <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) arises from jealousy concerning <s>Rāmacandra</s> and <s>Śatānanda</s>, through the self-disparagement indicated by the opening word 'fie!'

body.text:
atha (2) viṣādaḥ-
prārabdha-kāryānirvāhād iṣṭānavāpter vipattitaḥ |
aparādha-parijñānād anutāpas tu yo bhavet ||SRs_2.15|| 10
viṣādaḥ sa tridhā jyeṣṭha-madhyamādhama-saṃśrayāt |
sahāyānveṣaṇopāya-cintādyā uttame matāḥ ||SRs_2.16|| 11
anutsāhaś ca vaicittyam ity ādyā madhyame matāḥ |

children.translated_text: The consequent expressions of the inferior are bewilderment and looking about,
weeping, sighing, meditation, drying of the face, and so forth. ||SRs_2.17||

body.translated_text: Now (2) <s>Viṣāda</s> (despondency) — The remorse that arises from failure to accomplish an undertaken task, from non-attainment of the desired, from calamity, or from recognition of one's own offense — ||SRs_2.15|| that is <s>viṣāda</s>. It is threefold according to its association with superior, middling, and inferior [characters]. In the superior, the consequent expressions are said to be searching for allies and deliberation on stratagems. ||SRs_2.16|| In the middling, lack of enthusiasm and bewilderment and so forth are recognized.

body.text:
prārabdha-kāryānirvāhād, yathā-
vāraṃ vāraṃ tirayati dṛśāv udgato bāṣpa-pūras
tat-saṅkalpopahita-jaḍima stambham abhyeti gātram |
sadyaḥ svidyann nayam aviratotkampa-lolāṅgulīkaḥ
pāṇir lekhāvidhiṣu nitarāṃ vartate kiṃ karomi ||SRs_2.18|| (mālatīmādhava 1.38)
body.translated_text: From failure to accomplish an undertaken task, for example — The flood of tears that has risen again and again blurs both my eyes; my body, with the numbness produced by the resolve [to paint her], becomes rigid; my hand, now instantly perspiring, with fingers trembling with incessant quivering — it does not function at all in the task of drawing lines — what shall I do? ||SRs_2.18|| (<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 1.38)

body.text: atra prastuta-citra-nirmāṇānirvāhān mādhavasya kiṃ karomīti vāg-ārambha-sūcitayā tad-darśanopāya-cintayā viṣādo vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>viṣāda</s> of <s>Mādhava</s> is manifested through the deliberation on a stratagem [to see her], indicated by the opening words 'what shall I do?' — arising from his inability to accomplish the painting at hand.

body.text:
tatra iṣṭānavāpter, yathā-
sañcāriṇī dīpa-śikheva rātrau
yaṃ yaṃ vyatīyāya patiṃvarā sā |
narendram ārgāṭṭa iva prapede
vivarṇa-bhāvaṃ sa sa bhūmi-pālaḥ ||SRs_2.19|| (ra.vaṃ. 6.67)
body.translated_text: Of these, from non-attainment of the desired, for example — As the maiden choosing a husband passed by each one, like a moving lamp-flame in the night, each king she passed was reduced to paleness, like a waterwheel [left behind]. ||SRs_2.19|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 6.67)

body.text: atrendumatīm ākāṅkṣatāṃ bhūmipatīnāṃ tad-anavāptyā mukha-vaivarṇyena viṣādo vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>viṣāda</s> of the kings who desired <s>Indumatī</s> is manifested through the facial pallor caused by their failure to attain her.

body.text:
vipattitaḥ, yathā-
hā hā dhik para-gṛha-vāsa-dūṣaṇaṃ yad
vaidehyāḥ praśamitam adbhutair upāyaiḥ |
etat tat punar api daiva-durvipākād
ālarkaṃ viṣam iva sarvataḥ prasṛptam ||SRs_2.20|| (u.rā.ca. 1.40)
body.translated_text: From calamity, for example — Alas, alas, fie! The stain of dwelling in another's house that was removed for <s>Vaidehī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) through marvelous means — that very [stain], due to the cruel turn of fate, has spread everywhere again like the venom of a mad dog! ||SRs_2.20|| (<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 1.40)

body.text: atra sītāpavāda-rūpāyā vipatter hā hā dhig iti vāg-ārambheṇa rāmasya viṣādo gamyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>viṣāda</s> of <s>Rāma</s> is understood through the opening exclamation 'Alas, alas, fie!' — arising from the calamity of the slander of <s>Sītā</s>.

body.text:
yathā vā-
sā durnimittopagatād viṣādāt
sadyaḥ parimlāna-mukhāravindā |
rājñaḥ śivaṃ sāvarajasya bhūyād
ity āśaśaṃśe karaṇair bāhyaiḥ ||SRs_2.21|| (raghu. 14.50)
body.translated_text: Or for example — She, her lotus-face suddenly withered from the despondency caused by the evil omens, wished for the welfare of the king along with his younger brothers, through external organs [of prayer]. ||SRs_2.21|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 14.50)

body.text: atra durnimittānumitāyā vipatter mukha-śoṣaṇenānubhāvena vaidehyā viṣādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>viṣāda</s> of <s>Vaidehī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) is [manifested] through the consequent expression of the withering of the face, arising from the calamity inferred from the evil omens.

body.text:
aparādha-parijñānāt, yathā-
hā tāteti kranditam ākarṇya viṣaṇṇas
tasyānviṣyan vetasa-gūḍhaṃ prabhavaṃ saḥ |
śalya-protaṃ prekṣya sakumbhaṃ muni-putraṃ
tāpād antaḥ-śalya ivāsīt kṣitipo' pi ||SRs_2.22|| (raghu. 9.75)
body.translated_text: From recognition of one's own offense, for example — Hearing the cry 'O father!', distressed, he searched for its source hidden in the reeds; seeing the sage's son pierced by an arrow, dying, the king himself became as if pierced by an internal arrow from remorse. ||SRs_2.22|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 9.75)

body.text: atha (3) dainyam-

children.translated_text: The lack of boldness arising from torment of heart, misfortune, and the like — that is <s>dīnatā</s> (wretchedness).
Its consequent expressions are deemed to be dejection, bodily rigidity, and so forth. ||SRs_2.23||

body.translated_text: Now (3) <s>Dainya</s> (wretchedness) —

body.text:
hṛt-tāpāt, yathā-
etat kṛtvā priyam anucita-prārthanā-vartamno me
sauhārdād vā vidhura iti vā mayy anukrośa-buddhyā |
iṣṭān deśān jalada vihara prāvṛṣā sambhṛta-śrīr
mābhūd evaṃ kṣaṇam api ca te vidyutā viprayogaḥ ||SRs_2.24|| (me.dū. 2.55)
body.translated_text: From torment of heart, for example — Having done this favor for me who make an unseemly request, whether out of friendship, or thinking 'he is afflicted,' or out of compassion toward me — O cloud, wander through the beloved lands, enriched with the splendor of the rainy season; may there never be even a moment's separation from your lightning! ||SRs_2.24|| (<s>Meghadūta</s> 2.55)

body.text: daurgandhyād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Wretched, with wretched-faced children of her own pulling at her worn garment,

children.text: krośadbhiḥ kṣudhitari nirannapiṭharā nekṣyeta ced gehinī |
children.translated_text: crying from hunger, the grain-pot empty — if one should not see the housewife [in such a state] —
from the fear of the wretchedness of begging, with voice faltering, dropping, breaking, and dissolving syllables —

children.text: ko dehīti vadet sva-dagdha-jaṭharasyārthe manasvī pumān ||SRs_2.25||
children.translated_text: what self-respecting man would say 'Give!' for the sake of his own burning belly? ||SRs_2.25||

body.translated_text: From misfortune, for example —

body.text: atha (4) glāniḥ-

children.translated_text: From mental anguish, bodily disease, old age, thirst, exercise, love-making, and the like,

the state of lifelessness is <s>glāni</s> (debility); its [consequent expressions] include emaciated limbs, feeble speech and actions, trembling, lack of enthusiasm, pallor, rolling of the eyes, and so forth. ||SRs_2.26||

body.translated_text: Now (4) <s>Glāni</s> (debility) —

body.text:
ādhinā, yathā-
kisalayam iva mugdhaṃ bandhanād vipralūnaṃ
hṛdaya-kusuma-śoṣī dāruṇo dīrgha-śokaḥ |
glapayati paripāṇḍu kṣāmam asyāḥ śarīraṃ
śaradija iva gharmaḥ ketakī-patra-garbham ||SRs_2.27|| (uttara-rāma-carita 3.5)
body.translated_text: From mental anguish (<s>ādhi</s>), for example — Like a tender bud severed from its stem, the cruel, prolonged grief that withers the flower of her heart makes her body pale, emaciated, and feeble — as the autumnal heat [withers] the inner pith of a <s>ketakī</s> leaf. ||SRs_2.27|| (<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 3.5)

body.text:
vyādhinā, yathā-
tasya pāṇḍu-vadanālpa-bhūṣaṇā
sāvalamba-gamanā mṛdu-svanā |
rāja-yakṣma-parihāṇir āyayau
kāma-yāna-samavasthayā tulām ||SRs_2.28|| (raghu. 19.50)
body.translated_text: From disease (<s>vyādhi</s>), for example — Pale-faced, with few ornaments, walking with support, speaking softly — his decline from royal consumption (<s>rāja-yakṣma</s>) came to equal the condition of one on the vehicle of <s>Kāma</s> (the God of Love) [i.e., approaching death through love]. ||SRs_2.28|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 19.50)

body.text:
jarayā, yathā-
vivṛddhiṃ kampasya prathayatitarāṃ sādhvasa-vaśād
avispaṣṭāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ tirayatitarāṃ bāṣpa-salilaiḥ |
skhalad-varṇāṃ vāṇīṃ janayatitarāṃ gadgadatayā
jarāyāḥ sāhāyyaṃ mama hi paritoṣo' dya kurute ||SRs_2.29|| (ratnāvalī 4.13)
body.translated_text: From old age (<s>jarā</s>), for example — 'The trembling increases greatly from timidity; the dim eyesight is further blurred by tears; the stammering speech is made even more halting by choking emotion — the assistance of old age today gives me complete satisfaction!' ||SRs_2.29|| (<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 4.13)

body.text: atra harṣasya jarā-sahakāritva-kathanād ubhayānubhāvair api kampādibhir jarā-glāner eva prādhānyaṃ gamyate |
body.translated_text: Here, since old age is stated to be a co-factor of joy, the consequent expressions — trembling and the rest — indicate the predominance of debility due to old age through the expressions of both [joy and age].

body.text:
tṛṣṇayā, yathā-
vindhyā-dhvānau virala-salilās tarṣiṇī tatra sītā
yāvan mūrchāṃ kalayati kila vyākule rāmabhadre |
drāk saumitriḥ puṭaka-kalaśīṃ māludhānīdalānāṃ
tāvat prāpto dadhad atibhṛtāṃ vāriṇā nairjhareṇa ||SRs_2.30|| (bāla-rāmāyaṇa 6.50)
body.translated_text: From thirst (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), for example — In the <s>Vindhya</s> wilderness, where water was scarce, the thirsty <s>Sītā</s> was falling into a swoon, while <s>Rāmabhadra</s> was distraught; then <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) arrived at once, carrying a cup-vessel of <s>māludhānī</s> leaves filled to the brim with stream-water. ||SRs_2.30|| (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 6.50)

body.text:
vyāyāmena, yathā-
atanu-kuca-bharānatena bhūyaḥ
śrama-janitānatinā śarīrakeṇa |
anucita-gati-sāda-niḥsahatvaṃ
kala-bhara-karorubhir ūrubhir dadhānaiḥ ||SRs_2.31|| (śi.va. 7.66)
body.translated_text: From exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>), for example — With a body bent further by the weight of her ample breasts, and bent again by fatigue, her broad thighs, heavy with their burden, bearing the inability to endure the unaccustomed faltering of gait. ||SRs_2.31|| (<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 7.66)

body.text: suratena, yathā-

children.translated_text: Languishing from the exertions of love's conclusion,
she was lifted onto the bed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with great effort;
grasping his hand with her hand,
she reached the balcony made joyful by moonlight. ||SRs_2.32||

body.translated_text: From love-making (<s>surata</s>), for example —

body.text:
atha (5) śramaḥ-
śramo mānasa-khedaḥ syād adhva-nṛtya-ratādobhiḥ |
aṅga-mardana-niḥśvāsau pāda-saṃvāhanaṃ tathā ||SRs_2.33|| 16
jṛmbhaṇaṃ mandayānaṃ ca mukhanetra-vighūrṇanam |
sītkṛtiś ceti vijñeyā anubhāvāḥ śramodbhavāḥ ||SRs_2.34|| 17
body.translated_text: Now (5) <s>Śrama</s> (fatigue) — <s>Śrama</s> is mental exhaustion arising from walking, dancing, love-making, and so forth. Its consequent expressions are body-kneading, sighing, foot-massaging, ||SRs_2.33|| yawning, slow gait, rolling of the face and eyes, hissing [through the teeth], and so forth — these should be known as arising from fatigue. ||SRs_2.34||

body.text:
adhvanā, yathā-
sadyaḥ purī-parisare' pi śirīṣa-mṛdvī
sītā javāt tricaturāṇi padāni gatvā |
gantavyam adya kiyad ity asakṛd bruvāṇā
rāmāśuṇaḥ kṛtavatī prathamāvatāram ||SRs_2.35|| (bāla-rāmāyaṇa 6.34)
body.translated_text: From walking (<s>adhvan</s>), for example — <s>Sītā</s>, delicate as a <s>śirīṣa</s> flower, even while still in the precincts of the city, having walked quickly just three or four steps, repeatedly asking 'How far must we walk today?' — she made the first halt for <s>Rāma</s>'s pleasure. ||SRs_2.35|| (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 6.34)

body.text: nṛtyena, yathā-

children.translated_text: Making her arm-creeper, its bangles moistened with sweat, rest on the <s>mṛdaṅga</s> drum,
one foot placed on the hand of a maidservant for the fastening of her anklet,
she, releasing sighs whose velocity was indicated by the trembling of her breasts,
stood at the conclusion of the rhythmic beat, having transformed the performance-arena into one consecrated by <s>Anaṅga</s> (the God of Love). ||SRs_2.36||

body.translated_text: From dancing (<s>nṛtya</s>), for example —

children.translated_text: From love-making (<s>rati</s>), for example, from my own [work] —
Utterly wearied from love-making, fanning herself with the edge of her garment,
I envision my beloved, with languid eye-corners, sweetly speaking. ||SRs_2.37||

body.text:
atha (6) madaḥ-
madas tv ānanda-saṃmoha-sambhedo madirākṛtaḥ |
sa tridhā taruṇo madhyo' pakṛṣṭaś ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_2.38|| 18
dṛṣṭiḥ smerā mukhe rāgaḥ sasmitākulitaṃ vacaḥ |
lalitāviddha-gaty-ādyāś ceṣṭāḥ syus taruṇe made ||SRs_2.39|| 19
body.translated_text: Now, (6) Intoxication (<s>Mada</s>) — <s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is a mixture of joy and delusion, caused by wine. It is threefold: youthful (<s>taruṇa</s>), middling (<s>madhya</s>), and lowest (<s>apakṛṣṭa</s>). In youthful intoxication, the gestures include: smiling glances, flush on the face, speech that is smiling yet agitated, and graceful, swaying gait, etc. ||2.38-39||

body.text:
yathā-
bhāva-hāri hasitaṃ vacanānāṃ
kauśalaṃ dṛśi vikāra-viśeṣāḥ |
cakrire bhṛśam ṛjor api vadhvāḥ
kāmineva taruṇena madena ||SRs_2.40|| (śi.va. 10.13)
body.translated_text: For example — Captivating laughter, skill in words, special changes in the glance — the youthful intoxication made even the straightforward bride behave as if she were a coquette. ||2.40|| (<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 10.13)

body.text:
atha madhyamaḥ-
madhyame tu made vāci skhalanaṃ ghūrṇanaṃ dṛśoḥ |
gamane vaktratā bāhvor vikṣepa-srastatādayaḥ ||SRs_2.41|| 20
body.translated_text: Now, the middling [intoxication] — In middling intoxication, there is stumbling in speech, rolling of the eyes, crookedness in gait, flinging and drooping of the arms, and the like. ||2.41||

body.text:
yathā-
rundhatī nayana-vākya-vikāsaṃ
sāditobhaya-karā parirambhe |
vrīḍitasya lalitaṃ yuvatīnāṃ
kṣībatā bahu-guṇair anujahre ||SRs_2.42|| (bhāraveḥ 9.67)
body.translated_text: For example — <s>Arundhati</s> [i.e. modesty], whose blossoming of eye and word was subdued, whose both hands were engaged in embrace — the intoxication of the young women, with its many virtues, stole away the graceful [modesty] of the bashful one. ||2.42|| (of <s>Bhāravi</s>, [<s>Kirātārjunīya</s>] 9.67)

body.text:
atha nīcaḥ-
apakṛṣṭe tu ceṣṭāḥ syur gati-bhaṅgo visaṃjñatā |
niṣṭhīvanaṃ muhuḥ śvāso hikkā chardyādayo matāḥ ||SRs_2.43|| 21
body.translated_text: Now, the lowest [intoxication] — In the lowest intoxication, the gestures include: stumbling gait, loss of consciousness, spitting, frequent sighing, hiccups, vomiting, and the like. ||2.43||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Spitting, with mouths noisy from the heaviness of their necks,
uttering half-words, trembling and faltering from hiccups,
neither caring about their slipping garments nor disregarding [the situation],
drinking one after another various kinds of wine in a single row — [thus were] the maidens. ||2.44||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
taruṇas tūttamādīnāṃ madhyamo madhya-nīcayoḥ |
apakṛṣṭas tu nīcānāṃ tat-tan-mada-vivardhane ||SRs_2.45|| 22
uttama-prakṛtiḥ śete madhyo hasati gāyati |
adhama-prakṛtir grāmyaṃ paruṣaṃ vakti roditi ||SRs_2.46|| 23
body.translated_text: Youthful intoxication belongs to the superior and other [types of characters]; middling to the middling and low; the lowest to the low alone — each in the enhancement of their respective intoxication. ||2.45|| One of superior nature sleeps; one of middling nature laughs and sings; one of inferior nature speaks coarsely, harshly, and weeps. ||2.46||

body.text: uttama-prakṛter mada-vṛddhir, yathā-
body.translated_text: Enhancement of intoxication in one of superior nature, for example —

body.text:
tat-kṣaṇaṃ viparivartita-hriyor
neṣyatoḥ śayanam iddha-rāgayoḥ |
sā babhūva vaśa-vartinī tayoḥ
preyasaḥ suvadanā madasya ca ||SRs_2.47|| (ku.saṃ. 8.79)
body.translated_text: At that moment, when both had overcome their modesty and were inflamed with passion, ready to lead [her] to bed — that beautiful-faced woman became subject to both: to her beloved and to intoxication. ||2.47|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.79)

body.text: madhyamasya mada-vṛddhir, yathā-

children.translated_text: He laughed wildly without any reason,
he stumbled at every step on a level road,
whirling about from the excess of intoxication,
he grasped at the sky as his support. ||2.48||

body.translated_text: Enhancement of intoxication in the middling, for example —

body.text: adhamasya mada-vṛddhir, yathā-

children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] In such and such manner, the village housewife,
overcome by intoxication, utters this and that;
as the well-born women
hearing [this], flee covering their ears. ||2.49||

body.translated_text: Enhancement of intoxication in the lowest, for example —

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] In such and such manner, the village housewife,

children.text: mada-vivaśā kim api kim api vyāharati |
children.translated_text: overcome by intoxication, utters this and that;
as the well-born women
hearing [this], flee covering their ears.

body.text:
aiśvaryādi-kṛtaḥ kaiścit māno mada itīritaḥ |
vakṣyamāṇasya garvasya bheda evety udāsmahe ||SRs_2.50|| 24
body.translated_text: Some have declared that pride arising from sovereignty, etc. is [called] <s>Mada</s> (intoxication); we set this aside as merely a subdivision of <s>Garva</s> (pride), which is to be described [next]. ||2.50||

body.text:
atha (7) garvaḥ-
aiśvarya-rūpa-tāruṇya-kula-vidyā-balair api |
iṣṭa-lābhādinānyeṣām avajñā garva īritaḥ ||SRs_2.51|| 25
anubhāvā bhavanty atra gurv-ājñādy-ājñā-vyatikramaḥ |
anuttara-praadānaṃ ca vaimukhyaṃ bhāṣaṇe' pi ca ||SRs_2.52|| 26
vibhramāpahnutī vākya-pāruṣyam anavekṣaṇam |
avekṣaṇaṃ nijāṅgānām aṅga-bhaṅgādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.53|| 27
body.translated_text: Now, (7) Pride (<s>Garva</s>) — Contempt of others through the power of sovereignty, beauty, youth, lineage, learning, or strength, or through the attainment of a desired object — that is called <s>Garva</s> (pride). ||2.51|| Its <s>Anubhāvas</s> (consequents) are: transgression of the commands of elders, failure to give replies, aversion even to conversation, ||2.52|| affectation, dissimulation, harshness of speech, inattention, admiration of one's own limbs, gestures of the body, and the like. ||2.53||

body.text: aiśvaryam ājñā-siddhiḥ | tena yathā-
body.translated_text: Sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) means the fulfillment of one's commands. From that, for example —

children.text: rāho tarjaya bhāskaraṃ varuṇa he nirvāpyatāṃ pāvakaḥ
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rāhu</s>, threaten the Sun! O <s>Varuṇa</s>, extinguish the Fire!

children.text: sarve vārimucaḥ sametya kuruta grīṣmasya darpa-cchidām |
children.translated_text: All you rain-clouds, assemble and destroy the arrogance of Summer!
O Snow Mountain, O Moon, O Milk-Ocean, O Winter, O <s>Mandākinī</s> —

children.text: drāg devasya gṛhānupeta bhavatāṃ sevā-kṣaṇo vartate ||SRs_2.54||
children.translated_text: come quickly to the Lord's house — the moment for your service has arrived!' ||2.54||

body.text: (bāla-rāmāyaṇa 5.22)
body.translated_text: (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 5.22)

body.text: yathā vā-

children.text: vahne nihnotum arciḥ paricinu purataḥ siñcato vārivāhān
children.translated_text: 'O Fire, suppress your flames! Gather rain-clouds before you who sprinkle!

children.text: hemantasyāntike syāḥ prathayati davathuṃ yena te grīṣma noṣmā |
children.translated_text: Stay near Winter — for it is not your heat, O Summer, that causes my shivering!
O Suns of fierce heat, for the remedy of calming that heat, take a water-soaked tube!
The Lord, the illustrious Ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), conqueror of the three worlds, does not tolerate the prowess of another!' ||2.55||

body.translated_text: Or for example —

body.text: (bāla-rāmāyaṇa 1.31)
body.translated_text: (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 1.31)

body.text: rūpa-tāruṇyābhyāṃ, yathā-

children.translated_text: Wandering through garden after garden of beautiful women,
the youth, exceedingly proud of his handsomeness,
regarded even the flower-bow [of <s>Kāma</s>] as a blade of grass,
playfully holding a lotus in his hand. ||2.56||

body.translated_text: From beauty and youth, for example —

body.text: kulena, yathā-

children.text: gauḍaṃ rāṣṭram anuttamaṃ nirupamā tatrāpi rāḍhāpurī
children.translated_text: 'The land of <s>Gauḍa</s> is the most supreme; in it, the city of <s>Rāḍhā</s> is without comparison;

children.text: bhūri-śreṣṭhika-nāma dhāma paramaṃ tatrottamo naḥ pitā |
children.translated_text: the most excellent abode there is famed as "of great merchants"; in it, our father is the best.

children.text: tat-putrāś ca mahākulā na viditāḥ kasyātra teṣām api
children.translated_text: And his sons, of great lineage — are they not known to anyone here?
Even among them, I am the best in wisdom, virtue, discernment, composure, modesty, and conduct!' ||2.57||

body.translated_text: From lineage, for example —

body.text: (prabodha-candrodayaḥ, 2.7)
body.translated_text: (<s>Prabodhacandrodaya</s> 2.7)

body.text: vidyayā, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Those whose foremost path ripples with a pair of dots, who make the head-dot,

children.text: karmeti krama-śikṣitānvaya-kalā ye ke' pi tebhyo namaḥ |
children.translated_text: whose sequentially learned syllable-art [amounts to] "this is an action" — to those, whoever they may be, obeisance!
But those who compose poetry by scratching away blemishes from speech upon the whetstone of a thousand texts —

children.text: ullekhaiḥ kavayanti bilhaṇa-kavis teṣv eva saṃnahyati ||SRs_2.58||
children.translated_text: the poet <s>Bilhaṇa</s> girds up his loins against them alone.' ||2.58||

body.translated_text: From learning, for example —

body.text: (karṇa-sundarī)
body.translated_text: (<s>Karṇa-sundarī</s>)

body.text: balena, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'The uprooting of <s>Rudra</s>'s mountain, the clearing of the forest on his own neck, the housing of <s>Hari</s>
in a prison, the seizure of the <s>Puṣpaka</s> [chariot] — these are the mighty sports of him

children.text: so' yaṃ durmada-bāhu-daṇḍa-sacivo laṅkeśvaras tasya me
children.translated_text: whose arm-staff is his counselor in haughty pride, this Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>!

children.text: kā ślāghā guṇa-jarjareṇa dhanuṣākṛṣṭena bhagnena vā ||SRs_2.59||
children.translated_text: What glory is there for me in a bow that was already weakened by its qualities, whether pulled or broken?' ||2.59||

body.translated_text: From strength, for example —

body.text: (bāla-rāmāyaṇa, 1.51)
body.translated_text: (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 1.51)

body.text: iṣṭa-prāptyā, yathā-

children.text: āstāṃ tāvad anaṅga-cāpa-vibhavaḥ kā nāma sā kaumudī
children.translated_text: 'Let alone the power of the flower-bow [of <s>Kāma</s>]; what indeed is that moonlight?
Let the intoxicated cuckoo's song stay far away; let the gentle breezes fan [as they will]!
With playfully restless glances from the corners of her eyes, rippling with waves of laughter's delight,
this young woman herself, with meaningful intent, accepts [my] offering of salutation.' ||2.60||

body.translated_text: From the attainment of a desired object, for example —

body.text:
atha (8) śaṅkā-
śaṅkā cauryāparādhādyaiḥ svāniṣṭotprekṣaṇaṃ matam |
tatra ceṣṭāmuhuḥ pārśva-darśanaṃ mukha-śoṣaṇam ||SRs_2.61|| 28
avakuṇṭhana-vaivarṇya-kaṇṭha-sādādayo' pi ca |
śaṅkā dvidyeyam ātmotthā parotthā ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_2.62|| 29
svākārya-janitā svotthā prāyo vyaṅgyeyam iṅgitaiḥ |
iṅgitāni tu pakṣma-bhrū-tārakā-dṛṣṭi-vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.63|| 30
body.translated_text: Now, (8) Apprehension (<s>Śaṅkā</s>) — <s>Śaṅkā</s> (apprehension) is considered to be the imagining of personal misfortune arising from theft, offenses, and the like. The gestures therein include: frequently looking to the sides, dryness of the mouth, ||2.61|| covering [the face], pallor, weakening of the throat, and the like. <s>Śaṅkā</s> is twofold: self-generated (<s>ātmotthā</s>) and other-generated (<s>parotthā</s>). ||2.62|| Self-generated [apprehension] is born from one's own misdeed; it is usually conveyed through hints (<s>iṅgitas</s>). And the hints are: changes in the eyelashes, brows, pupils, and glances. ||2.63||

body.text: aparādhāt svotthā, yathā-

children.text: tat-sakhyā marutātha vā pracalitā vallīti muhyad-dhiyo
children.translated_text: 'Is that her friend, or a creeper stirred by the wind?' — thus his mind confused,
seeing [her], he speaks with agitated pupils, with false composure on his face.
As <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the new companion of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, enters the inner chambers,

children.text: nūtnā saiva daśā svayaṃ piśunatāṃ devī-sakhīnāṃ gatā ||SRs_2.64||
children.translated_text: the very same [Gaṅgā] now assumes a new role — that of informer among the <s>Devī</s>'s companions. ||2.64||

body.translated_text: Self-generated from an offense, for example —

body.text: saiva cauryeṇa, yathā-

children.translated_text: Rubbing his smooth, fragrant lips with his palms [to remove traces] of the theft of milk and such,
sniffing his hand again and again, quickly roughening [it] against the girdle of tinkling bells,

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ viśāle diśi diśi vikiran locane lolatāre
children.translated_text: repeatedly casting wide glances with restless pupils in every direction —

children.text: mandaṃ mandaṃ jananyāḥ parisaram ayate kūṭa-gopāla-bālaḥ ||SRs_2.65||
children.translated_text: slowly, slowly, the deceitful cowherd child (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) approaches the vicinity of his mother. ||2.65||

body.translated_text: The same [self-generated apprehension] from theft, for example —

body.text: parotthā tu nijasyaiva parasyākāryato bhavet |

children.translated_text: One should convey this mostly through appearance (<s>ākāra</s>) and gesture (<s>ceṣṭā</s>).

children.text: ākāraḥ sāttvikaś ceṣṭā tv aṅga-pratyaṅgajāḥ kriyāḥ ||SRs_2.66|| 32ab
children.translated_text: Appearance is <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary); gesture consists of actions born of the major and minor limbs. ||2.66||

body.translated_text: Other-generated [apprehension], however, arises from one's own [inference of] another's misdeed.

body.text:
parotthā, yathā-
prīte vidhātari purā paribhūya martyān
vavre' nyato yad abhayaṃ sa bhavān ahaṃyuḥ |
tan-marmaṇi spṛśati mām atimātram adya
hā vatsa śāntam athavā daśakandharo' si ||SRs_2.67|| (anargha-rāghava 4.9)
body.translated_text: Other-generated, for example — 'When, having formerly spurned mortals before the pleased Creator, he chose fearlessness from others — that same one, O sir, are you! Today that [fact] touches me to the quick most excessively. Alas, child! Peace — or rather, you are the Ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>)!' ||2.67|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 4.9)

body.text: atra garvita-rāvaṇa-kṛtena martyetarābhaya-varaṇena jātā mālyavataḥ śaṅkā marmaṇi spṛśatītyādinā vāg-ārambheṇa pratīyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the apprehension of <s>Mālyavān</s>, arising from the proud <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s boon of fearlessness from non-mortals, is conveyed through the speech-mode 'it touches me to the quick,' etc.

body.text: atha (9) trāsaḥ-

children.translated_text: <s>Trāsa</s> (terror) is agitation of the mind caused by lightning, predatory beasts, thundering,
as well as ghosts, serpents, and the like. The reactions therein should be known: ||2.68||

body.translated_text: Now, (9) Terror (<s>Trāsa</s>) —

body.text: utkampa-gātra-saṅkoca-romāñca-stambha-gadgadāḥ | 33
body.translated_text: Trembling, contraction of the body, horripilation, paralysis, choking of voice,

body.text: muhur nimeṣa-vibhrānti-pārśvasthālambanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.69||
body.translated_text: frequent blinking, bewilderment, clinging to those nearby, and the like. ||2.69||

body.text: vidyuto, yathā-

children.translated_text: In those rains, frightened by a flash of momentary light,
<s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) embraced the Bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>);
and that lightning, seeing the beauty of his limbs,
as if ashamed, quickly entered the cloud. ||2.70||

body.translated_text: From lightning, for example —

body.text: kravyādo hiṃsra-sattvam | tasmād, yathā-
body.translated_text: '<s>Kravyāda</s>' means a predatory animal. From that, for example —

children.translated_text: In that place where, from the alarm displayed in their own agitation,
the beloved women clung to the necks
of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> (celestial beings) — through a pack of bears,
an unprovoked friendship was formed [between them]. ||2.71||

body.text:
garjitena, yathā-
praṇaya-kopa-bhūto' pi parāṅmukhāḥ
sapadi vāridharārava-bhīravaḥ |
praṇayinaḥ parirabdhum anantaraṃ
vavalire bali-recita-madhyamāḥ ||SRs_2.72|| (śi.va., 6.38)
body.translated_text: From thundering, for example — Though facing away [from their lovers] from love-quarrel, those slender-waisted beloved women, timid at the roar of the rain-clouds, immediately turned around to embrace their lovers closely. ||2.72|| (<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 6.38)

body.text: garjitaṃ mahāravopalakṣaṇam | tena bheryādi-dhvanir api bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Thundering' (<s>garjita</s>) is an illustrative term for great sounds; hence the sound of war-drums and the like is also [included].

body.text: bherī-dhvaninā, yathā-

children.translated_text: The king was delighted even by the departure-drum-sounds that disturbed the pleasure of sleep,
[while] <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) was pressed by the pair of breasts of <s>Padmajā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),
the lotus-born one, whose [breasts] swayed with unexpected alarm
[at the drum sounds]. ||2.73||

body.translated_text: From the sound of war-drums, for example —

children.translated_text: From seeing a ghost, for example —

children.text: sā patyuḥ parivāreṇa piśācair api veṣṭitā |
children.translated_text: She, surrounded by her husband's retinue of <s>Piśācas</s> (ghosts) as well,
with trembling heart, was consoled by her friends. ||2.74||

body.text: bhujaṅgamād, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'May the wedding with the Bearer of <s>Pināka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) be auspicious for you! —
at the terror of the serpent-bangles [on his wrist],
with bewildered glance, [she uttered] suddenly "<s>Namaḥ Śivāya</s>!" —
the half-spoken word, the face bowed with a smile — [such was] <s>Ambikā</s>'s (<s>Pārvatī</s>'s) [reaction].' ||2.75||

body.translated_text: From a serpent, for example —

body.text: (rasa-kalikāyām apy ullikhitam idam, 23 puṭe)
body.translated_text: (This is also cited in <s>Rasa-kalikā</s>, page 23.)

body.text:
atha (10) āvegaḥ-
cittasya sambhramo yaḥ syād āvego' yaṃ sa cāṣṭadhā | 34 utpāta-vāta-varṣāgni-matta-kuñjara-darśanāt ||SRs_2.76||
body.translated_text: Now, (10) Agitation (<s>Āvega</s>) — The flurry of the mind is <s>Āvega</s> (agitation), and it is eightfold: from portents, wind, rain, fire, a maddened elephant, ||2.76||

body.text: priyāpriya-śruteś cāpi śatrava-vyasanād api | 35
body.translated_text: hearing of something dear or hateful, and from an enemy's calamity. ||2.77||

body.text: tatrautpātas tu śailādi-kampa-ketūdayādayaḥ ||SRs_2.77||
body.translated_text: Among these, portents (<s>utpāta</s>) include: trembling of mountains, rising of [inauspicious] banners, and the like.

body.text: taj-jāḥ sarvāṅga-visraṃso vaimukhyam apasarpaṇam | 36
body.translated_text: The reactions born therefrom are: loosening of all limbs, turning away, retreating,

body.text: viṣāda-mukha-vaivarṇya-vismayādyās tu vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.78||
body.translated_text: despondency, pallor of face, astonishment, and the like. ||2.78||

body.text: śaila-prakampanād, yathā-

children.translated_text: When <s>Kailāsa</s> shook, while the <s>Gaṇas</s> (Śiva's attendants), stirred up, displayed their curiosity,

children.text: kroḍaṃ mātuḥ kumāre viśati viṣamuciprekṣamāṇe saroṣam |
children.translated_text: as <s>Kumāra</s> (<s>Kārttikeya</s>) entered the bosom of his mother, looking wrathfully at the poison-spewer (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
as the Ten-faced one's (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s) body sank from the pressure of [<s>Śiva</s>'s] foot-plant, going down to the netherworld's base —

children.text: kruddho' py āśliṣṭa-mūrtir ghanataram umayā pātu hṛṣṭaḥ śivo vaḥ ||SRs_2.79||
children.translated_text: may <s>Śiva</s>, though angered, yet embraced more tightly by <s>Umā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), joyful, protect you! ||2.79||

body.translated_text: From the trembling of a mountain, for example —

body.text: atra kailāsa-kampa-janita-pramatha-gaṇa-vismaya-kārtikeyāpasarpaṇa-kātyāyanī-sādhvasādibhir anubhāvais tat-tad-gata-sambhramātiśaya-rūpa āvego vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the agitation — characterized by the excess of flurry in each [character] — is conveyed through the <s>Anubhāvas</s>: the astonishment of the <s>Pramatha-gaṇas</s>, the retreating of <s>Kārttikeya</s>, the alarm of <s>Kātyāyanī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), etc., all born from the trembling of <s>Kailāsa</s>.

body.text: ketūdayād, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Alas! Seeing the comet in the quarter of the sky, the householders,
their limbs trembling with alarm, hastily gathering at each other's houses, immersed in anxiety,
repeatedly ordering their wives to economize on grains,
meditate, sigh, and sit in groups at the mouths of streets.' ||2.80||

body.translated_text: From the rising of [inauspicious] banners, for example —

body.text: atha vātāvegaḥ-

children.translated_text: Coming in haste, seizing one's garment, and covering oneself,
wiping the eyes, and the like — these are the actions produced by the agitation of wind. ||2.81||

body.translated_text: Now, agitation from wind (<s>vātāvega</s>) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Sweeping away the bases of trees in every direction, raising a dust-column studded with straw into the sky,

children.text: jhāṅkārī śarkarālaḥ pathiṣu viṭapināṃ skandha-kāṣaiḥ sadhūmaḥ |
children.translated_text: buzzing with gravel, smoky with the bark-friction of tree-trunks along the roads —
in the bowers of palaces, the wind blows round about, steady and deep like the outpouring of fresh clouds,

children.text: caṇḍārambhaḥ samīro vahati paridiśaṃ bhīru kiṃ sambhrameṇa ||SRs_2.82||
children.translated_text: impetuous in onset — O timid one, why such alarm? ||SRs_2.82||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (veṇī-saṃhāra 2.19)
body.translated_text: (<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 2.19)

body.text: atra vāta-kṛta-saṃrambho vāg-ārambheṇa pratipādyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the agitation caused by the wind is conveyed through the verbal expression.

body.text: atha varṣāvegaḥ-

children.translated_text: Holding an umbrella, contracting the body, running with arms crossed,
and seeking warm shelter — these and similar are the actions born of agitation from rain. ||SRs_2.83||

body.translated_text: Now the agitation caused by rain (<s>varṣāvega</s>) —

body.text:
yathā-
āmekhalaṃ cañcaratā ghanānāṃ
chāyām adhaḥ sānugatāṃ niṣevya |
udvejitā vṛṣṭibhir āśrayante
śṛṅgāṇi yasyātapavanti siddhāḥ ||SRs_2.84|| [ku.saṃ. 7.5]
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'Taking shelter below the shadow of the clouds that moved down the slopes along the girdle [of the mountain], the <s>Siddhas</s>, disturbed by the showers, resort to the peaks where the sun shines.' ||SRs_2.84|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 7.5]

body.text: atra siddhānām agra-śikhara-dhāvanena sūcitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, it is indicated by the <s>Siddhas</s>' running to the topmost peaks.

body.text: atha agny-āvegaḥ-

children.translated_text: The actions born of fire-agitation are: fanning, shaking the body,
crossing and throwing the legs, shutting the eyes, and the like. ||SRs_2.85||

body.translated_text: Now the agitation caused by fire (<s>agny-āvega</s>) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Striking with flame-pillars the birds wheeling in the sky, which are driven far away,
the fire-charioteer (<s>Bradhna-sūta</s>, the Sun) is agitated anew by the restraint of circling horses falling away —
the mighty fire (<s>Hutāśa</s>) licks the pathway of the sky, as if doubting the appointed time of dissolution,
born from the power of the celebrated fire-weapon discharged by the son of <s>Gaṅgā</s> (<s>Skanda</s>). ||SRs_2.86||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text: (dhanañjaya-vijaya 67)
body.translated_text: (<s>Dhanañjaya-vijaya</s> 67)

body.text: atha kuñjarāvegaḥ-

children.translated_text: In agitation produced by an elephant: swift retreating,
repeatedly looking behind, trembling from fear, and the like are recognized. ||SRs_2.87||

body.translated_text: Now the agitation caused by an elephant (<s>kuñjarāvega</s>) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Even when the path was being cleared without obstruction
far ahead by the crowd of living beings,
with elephants of great splendor, like lamps in darkness,
the way became uncrowded. ||SRs_2.88||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text: aśvena, yathā-

children.translated_text: Having uprooted the stake together with the rope, in a fit of pride,
impossible to catch even with utmost effort,
a horse quickly caused confusion in the camp;
[people] shouting 'A horse! A horse!' ran after another horse that had bolted. ||SRs_2.89||

body.translated_text: By a horse, for example —

body.text: priya-śravaṇād, yathā-

children.translated_text: In this [agitation] born of hearing pleasant news: rising up, embracing,

children.text: prīti-dānaṃ priyaṃ vākyaṃ romaharṣādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.90||
children.translated_text: giving gifts, speaking kind words, horripilation, and the like. ||SRs_2.90||

body.translated_text: From hearing pleasant news, for example —

body.text:
yathā-
janāya śuddhānta-carāya śaṃsate
kumāra-janmāmṛta-saṃmitākṣaram |
adeyam āsīt trayam eva bhūpateḥ
śaśiprabhaṃ chatram ubhe ca cāmare ||SRs_2.91|| (ra.vaṃ. 3.16)
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'To the inner-chamber attendant announcing the news of the prince's birth, with words [sweet] as nectar, there were only three things the king could not give: the moon-bright umbrella and the two fly-whisks.' ||SRs_2.91|| (<s>Raghu-vaṃśa</s> 3.16)

body.text: apriya-śruter, yathā-

children.translated_text: In this [agitation] born of hearing unpleasant news: lamentation, tossing about,
wailing, falling down, wandering around, and the like. ||SRs_2.92||

body.translated_text: From hearing unpleasant news, for example —

body.text: śātravād, yathā-

children.translated_text: The actions in agitation from an enemy are: taking up armor and weapons,
hastily mounting chariots, horses, and elephants, and the like. ||SRs_2.93||

body.translated_text: From an enemy, for example —

body.text: yathā-

children.text: rāmo nāma babhūva huṃ tad abalā sīteti huṃ tāṃ pitur
children.translated_text: 'There was [a king] named <s>Rāma</s> — humph! And a weak woman named <s>Sītā</s> — humph! While he dwelt
in the <s>Pañcavaṭī</s> forest at his father's command, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> abducted her.'
Hearing this ancient story of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s [previous incarnation] narrated by his mother,

children.text: saumitre kva dhanur dhanur dhanur iti vyagrā giraḥ pāntu vaḥ ||SRs_2.94||
children.translated_text: [the child <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> cried out:] '<s>Saumitra</s>, where is the bow? The bow! The bow!' — may these agitated words protect you! ||SRs_2.94||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text: kṛ.ka.2.72
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta</s> 2.72

body.text: ete syur uttamādīnām anubhāvā yathocitam ||SRs_2.95|| 44
body.translated_text: These should be the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) of the superior and other [character types], as appropriate. ||SRs_2.95||

body.text:
atha unmādaḥ-
unmādaś citta-vibhrāntir viyogād iṣṭa-nāśataḥ |
viyogaje tu ceṣṭāḥ syur dhāvanaṃ paridevanam ||SRs_2.96|| 45
asambaddha-pralapanaṃ śayaṇaṃ sahasotthitiḥ |
acetanaiḥ sahālāpo nirnimitta-smitādayaḥ ||SRs_2.97|| 46
body.translated_text: Now <s>Unmāda</s> (madness) — <s>Unmāda</s> is the derangement of the mind, arising from separation or the loss of a loved one. In [madness] born of separation, the actions are: running about, lamenting, ||SRs_2.96|| incoherent babbling, lying down, suddenly rising up, conversing with inanimate objects, causeless smiling, and the like. ||SRs_2.97||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Sudden rising, counting animate and inanimate things alike,
intense hot sighing, tears flowing repeatedly,

children.text: nirlakṣyā vāg gatir aviṣayā nirnimittaṃ smitaṃ ca
children.translated_text: aimless speech, purposeless movement, causeless smiling —
these mostly reveal her state that induces bewilderment. ||SRs_2.98||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text:
iṣṭa-nāśād, yathā-
iṣṭa-nāśa-kṛte tv asmin bhasmādi-parilepanam |

children.translated_text: composing dances and songs, wearing grass and discarded garlands,
wrapping oneself in rags, and the previously mentioned disturbances as well.

body.translated_text: From the loss of a loved one, for example — In this [madness] caused by the loss of a loved one: smearing oneself with ashes and such, ||SRs_2.99||

body.text: yathā-

children.text: kīnāśo' pi bibheti yādava-kulād vṛddhasya kā me gatir
children.translated_text: 'Even Death is afraid of the <s>Yādava</s> clan — what refuge is there for me, an old man?

children.text: bhedaḥ syāt svajaneṣu kiṃ nu śatadhā sīdanti gātrāṇi me |
children.translated_text: Could there be division among my own people? Why do my limbs sink a hundredfold?

children.text: so' yaṃ buddhi-viparyayo mama samaṃ sarve hatā bāndhavā
children.translated_text: This must be a delusion of my intellect — all my kinsmen are slain together!

children.text: na śraddeyam idaṃ hi vākyam ahahā muhyanti marmāṇi me ||SRs_2.100||
children.translated_text: This speech is not to be believed — alas, my vital spots are bewildered!' ||SRs_2.100||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text: atha (12) apasmṛtiḥ-

children.translated_text: The mental disturbance caused by imbalance of humors, spirit-possession, and the like

children.text: citta-kṣobhas tv apasmāras tatra ceṣṭāḥ prakampanam ||SRs_2.101||
children.translated_text: is called <s>Apasmāra</s> (epilepsy). The actions therein are: trembling, ||SRs_2.101||

body.translated_text: Now (12) <s>Apasmṛti</s> (epilepsy/seizure) —

body.text: dhāvanaṃ patanaṃ stambho bhramaṇaṃ netra-vikriyāḥ | 49
body.translated_text: running, falling, rigidity, whirling, distortion of the eyes,

body.text: svoṣṭha-daṃśa-bhujāsphoṭa-lālā-phenādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.102||
body.translated_text: biting one's own lip, slapping the arms, drooling and foaming, and the like. ||SRs_2.102||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: With the corners of his lips bent and moistened by an overflow of drooling foam,
singing and singing, his voice mixed with weeping, bowing down and falling,
eyes rigid, upturned, and agitated, whirling in circles —

children.text: bhūtāviṣṭaṃ kam api puruṣaṃ tatra vīthyām apaśyam ||SRs_2.103||
children.translated_text: I saw on that street a certain man possessed by a spirit. ||SRs_2.103||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text: doṣa-vaiṣamyajas tv eṣa vyādhir evety udāsmahe ||103|| 50
body.translated_text: This, however, being a disease caused by humoral imbalance, we set it aside. ||

body.text:
atha (13) vyādhiḥ-
doṣodreka-viyogādyair syād vyādhir atra tu |
gātra-stambhaḥ ślathāṅgatvaṃ kūjanaṃ mukha-kūṇanam ||SRs_2.104|| 51
srastāṅgatākṣi-vikṣepa-niḥśvāsādyās tu vikriyāḥ |
saśīto dāha-yuktaḥ sa dvividhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||SRs_2.105|| 52[*10]
hanu-sañcālanaṃ bāṣpaḥ sarvāṅgotkampa-kūjane |
jānu-kuñcana-romāñca-mukha-śoṣādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.106|| 53
[*10] The following half karika is found in only one edition: (śīta-jvare tu ceṣṭāḥ syuḥ santāpaś cāṅga-sādanam | This does not appear to be serious. (See karika 54)
body.translated_text: Now (13) <s>Vyādhi</s> (disease) — disease arises from excess of humors, separation, and the like. Herein [the symptoms are]: rigidity of the body, limpness of limbs, moaning, contortion of the face, ||SRs_2.104|| drooping of the body, rolling of the eyes, sighing, and such disturbances. It is declared to be of two kinds: accompanied by cold (<s>śīta</s>) and accompanied by burning (<s>dāha</s>). ||SRs_2.105|| Chattering of the jaw, tears, trembling of the whole body, moaning, bending of the knees, horripilation, dryness of the mouth, and the like. ||SRs_2.106||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: It produces horripilation abundantly
through the contact pervading all the limbs —
for women whose breasts are clasped by their crossed arms,
cold fever is like a lover. ||SRs_2.107||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text:
dāha-jvare tu ceṣṭāḥ syuḥ śīta-mālyādi-kāṅkṣaṇam |
pāṇi-pāda-parikṣepa-mukha-śoṣādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.108|| 54
body.translated_text: In burning fever, the actions are: craving for cool garlands and such, flinging of hands and feet, dryness of the mouth, and the like. ||SRs_2.108||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'The flower-bed turns to dust from the contact of her body;
the lotus-leaf fans at her side wilt from the heat of her body;

children.text: nyastaṃ ca stana-maṇḍale malayajaṃ śīrṇāntaraṃ dṛśyate
children.translated_text: the sandalwood paste placed on the surface of her breasts is seen to have crumbled within;
the lotus-stalk ornaments quickly become foam-mouthed from the heat.' ||SRs_2.109||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text:
atha (14) mohaḥ-
āpad-bhīti-viyogādyair mohaś cittasya mūḍhatā |

children.text: vikriyās tatra vijñeyā indriyāṇāṃ ca śūnyatā | 55
children.translated_text: The disturbances therein should be known as: vacancy of the senses,
motionlessness, whirling of the body, falling, reeling, and the like. ||SRs_2.110||

body.translated_text: Now (14) <s>Moha</s> (stupor/delusion) — <s>Moha</s> is the bewilderment of the mind arising from calamity, fear, separation, and the like.

body.text:
āpado, yathā-
tato' bhiṣaṅgānila-vipraviddhā
prabhraśyamānābharaṇa-prasūtā |
sva-mūrti-lābha-prakṛtiṃ dharitrīṃ
lateva sītā sahasā jagāma ||SRs_2.111|| (ra.vaṃ. 14.54)
body.translated_text: From calamity, for example — 'Then, struck by the wind of the curse, her ornaments falling away, <s>Sītā</s> suddenly fell to the earth — which had resumed its natural form of receiving her — like a creeper.' ||SRs_2.111|| (<s>Raghu-vaṃśa</s> 14.54)

body.text:
bhīter, yathā-
smaras tathābhūtam ayugma-netraṃ
paśyann adūrān manasāpy adhṛṣyam |
nālakṣayat sādhvasa-sanna-hastaḥ
srastaṃ śaraṃ cāpam api sva-hastāt ||SRs_2.112|| [ku.saṃ. 3.51]
body.translated_text: From fear, for example — '<s>Smara</s> (the God of Love), seeing the Odd-eyed one (<s>Śiva</s>) in such a state nearby, unapproachable even by the mind, did not notice — his hand drooping with terror — the arrow and the bow slipping from his own hand.' ||SRs_2.112|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.51]

body.text:
viyogād, yathā-
tad-vaktraṃ nayena ca te smita-sudhā-mugdhaṃ ca tad vācikaṃ
sā veṇī sa bhuja-kramo' tisaralo līlālasā sā gatiḥ |
tanvī seti ca seti seti satataṃ tad-dhyāna-baddhātmano
nidrā no na ratir na cāpi viratiḥ śūnyaṃ mano vartate ||SRs_2.113|| (rasa-kalikā, 32)
body.translated_text: From separation, for example — 'That face of hers, and the speech charming with the nectar of her smile, that braid, that sequence of arms so very graceful, that gait languid with playfulness — she is slender, and she is [gone], and she, and she — constantly absorbed in meditation on her, there is for me neither sleep, nor pleasure, nor cessation — my mind moves in emptiness.' ||SRs_2.113|| (<s>Rasa-kalikā</s> 32)

body.text: atha (15) mṛtiḥ-

children.translated_text: The separation from the self of the vital air called <s>Dhanañjaya</s>,
which is coextensive with the body — that is called death. ||SRs_2.114||

body.translated_text: Now (15) <s>Mṛti</s> (death) —

body.text: etac ca dvividhaṃ proktaṃ vyādhijaṃ cābhighātajam | 57
body.translated_text: And this is declared to be of two kinds: arising from disease and arising from violence.
