body.text: ādyaṃ tv asādhya-hṛc-chūla-viṣūcy-ādi-samudbhavam ||SRs_2.115||
body.translated_text: The first arises from incurable heart-disease, cholera, and the like. ||SRs_2.115||

body.text: amī tatrānubhāvāḥ syur avyaktākṣara-bhāṣaṇam | 58
body.translated_text: The <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions) therein are: speaking indistinct syllables,

body.text:
vivarṇa-gātratā manda-śvāsādi stambha-mīlane |
hikkā parijanāpekṣā-niśceṣṭendriyatādayaḥ ||SRs_2.116|| 59
body.translated_text: pallor of the body, faint breathing, rigidity, closing of the eyes, hiccups, looking toward one's attendants, motionlessness of the senses, and the like. ||SRs_2.116||

body.text: yathā-

children.text: kāye sīdati kaṇṭha-rodhini kaphe kuṇṭhe ca vāṇī-pathe
children.translated_text: 'When the body is sinking, when phlegm obstructs the throat, when the pathway of speech is blunted,

children.text: jihmāyāṃ dṛśi jīvite jigamiṣau śvāse śanaiḥ śāmyati |
children.translated_text: when the eye is askew, when the life-force desires to depart, when the breath gradually subsides —

children.text: āgatya svayam eva naḥ karuṇayā kātyāyanī-vallabhaḥ
children.translated_text: may the beloved of <s>Kātyāyanī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) himself come of his own accord, out of compassion,
and describe in my ear the saving <s>Tāraka</s> [mantra], [delivering me] from the fear of the ocean of existence.' ||SRs_2.117||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text:
dvitīyaṃ ghāta-patana-dohodbandha-viṣādijam |
tatra ghātādije bhūmi-patana-krandanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.118|| 60
body.translated_text: The second kind arises from striking, falling, strangling, hanging, or poison. In that arising from striking and the like: falling to the ground, crying out, and the like. ||SRs_2.118||

children.translated_text: As in <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s> —
'From the wound of the noble one's arrow-fall, muddied with frothy, bubbling tears,

children.text: apatan na calati kiṃcid vikṛtākṛtir adya vajra-nihateva ||SRs_2.119||
children.translated_text: she fell, not moving at all, her form distorted, as if struck by a thunderbolt.' ||SRs_2.119||

body.text: viṣaṃ tu vatsanābhādyam aṣṭau vegās tad-udbhavāḥ |

children.text: kārṣṇyaṃ kampo dāho hikkā phenaś ca kandhara-bhaṅgaḥ | 61
children.translated_text: blackening, trembling, burning, hiccups, foaming, bending of the neck,

children.text: jaḍatā mṛtir iti kathitā kramaśaḥ prathamādyā vegajāś ceṣṭāḥ ||SRs_2.120||
children.translated_text: torpor, and death — thus are stated the actions born of the successive stages, beginning with the first. ||SRs_2.120||

body.translated_text: Poison means <s>vatsanābha</s> (aconite) and the like. The eight stages arising from it are:

body.text: yatha priya-darśikāyāṃ (4.9)-

children.text: eṣā mlīayatīdam akṣi-yugalaṃ jātā mamāndhā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: 'She grows faint — this pair of eyes — the directions have become blind to me;

children.text: kaṇṭho' syā uparudhyate mama giro niryānti kṛcchrād imāḥ |
children.translated_text: her throat is obstructed — these words of mine issue forth with difficulty;

children.text: etasyāḥ śvasitaṃ hṛtaṃ mama tanur niśceṣṭatām āgatā
children.translated_text: her breath is stolen — my body has become motionless;

children.text: manye' syāḥ viṣa-vega eva hi paraṃ sarvaṃ tu duḥkhaṃ mayi ||SRs_2.121||
children.translated_text: I think indeed it is the effect of poison on her — yet all the suffering is mine.' ||SRs_2.121||

body.translated_text: As in <s>Priya-darśikā</s> (4.9) —

body.text: atrākṣi-nimīlana-kaṇṭha-rodhana-niḥśvāsāyāsādibhir āraṇyikāyā viṣa-vega-janitā mṛtir avagamyate |
body.translated_text: Here, through the closing of the eyes, obstruction of the throat, labored breathing, and similar [symptoms], the death of <s>Āraṇyikā</s> caused by the effects of poison is understood.

body.text: atha (16) ālasyam-

children.translated_text: Caused by natural disposition, fatigue, satiation, fullness of pregnancy, and the like —

children.text: kṛcchrāt kriyonmukhatvaṃ yat tad ālasyam iha kriyāḥ ||SRs_2.122||
children.translated_text: the reluctant inclination toward action is <s>Ālasya</s> (languor). The actions herein are: ||SRs_2.122||

body.translated_text: Now (16) <s>Ālasya</s> (languor) —

body.text: aṅga-bhaṅgaḥ kriyā-dveṣo jṛmbhaṇākṣi-vimardane | 63
body.translated_text: bending of the body, aversion to activity, yawning, rubbing the eyes,

body.text: śayyāsanaika-priyatā tandrī-nidrādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.123||
body.translated_text: fondness solely for bed and seat, drowsiness, sleep, and the like. ||SRs_2.123||

body.text:
svabhāva-śramābhyāṃ, yathā-
muhur iti vana-vibhramābhiṣaṅgād
atami tadā nitarāṃ nitambinībhiḥ |
mṛdutara-tanavo' lasāḥ prakṛtyā
ciram api tāḥ kim uta prayāsa-bhājaḥ ||SRs_2.124|| (śi.va. 7.68)
body.translated_text: From natural disposition and fatigue, for example — 'How much more then these women, slender-bodied and languid by nature, who had long been devoted to exertion, wandering through the forest — they were greatly exhausted at that time.' ||SRs_2.124|| (<s>Śiśupāla-vadha</s> 7.68)

body.text:
sauhityaṃ bhojanādi-tṛptiḥ, tena yathā-
trailokyābhaya-lagnakena bhavatā vīreṇa vismāritas
taj-jīmūta-muhūrta-maṇḍana-dhanuḥ-pāṇḍityam ākhaṇḍalaḥ |
kiṃ cājasra-makhārpitena haviṣā samphulla-māṃsollasat
sarvāṅgīṇa-balī-vilupta-nayana-vyūhaḥ kathaṃ vartate ||SRs_2.125|| (a.rā. 1.28)
atra mando-vṛddhyā śakrasya sauhityam | tat-kṛtam ālasyaṃ kathaṃ vartate ity anena vāg-ārambheṇa vyajyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Sauhitya</s> means satisfaction from eating and such. From that, for example — 'By you, O hero, who cling to the fearlessness of the three worlds, <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> (<s>Indra</s>), who wielded the bow that adorned him momentarily like <s>Jīmūta</s> (a cloud), has been made to forget [his prowess]. Moreover, from the oblations constantly offered in sacrifices, his corpulent, blooming body, swelling in all parts — how does he fare with his array of eyes overwhelmed by the <s>balī</s> offerings?' ||SRs_2.125|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.28) Here, through the growth of fat, the satiation of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) is [indicated]. The languor caused by it is expressed through the verbal expression 'how does he fare.'

children.translated_text: From the fullness of pregnancy, for example —
'For her, fond only of sitting, leaning on the body of her companion,
the bearing of her own body became a burden, due to the languor of pregnancy.' ||SRs_2.126||

body.text: atha (17) jāḍyam-

children.translated_text: <s>Jāḍya</s> is the inability to respond upon hearing something desired or undesired,

children.text:
dṛṣṭer vā virahādeś ca kriyās tatrānimeṣatā |
aśrutiḥ pāravaśyaṃ ca tūṣṇīm-bhāvādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.127|| 65
children.translated_text: or from seeing [something], or from separation and the like. The actions therein are: unblinking stare, not hearing, helplessness, silence, and the like. ||SRs_2.127||

body.translated_text: Now (17) <s>Jāḍya</s> (stupefaction) —

body.text:
iṣṭa-śruter, yathā-
priye' parā yacchati vācam unmukhī
nibaddha-dṛṣṭiḥ śithilākuloccayā |
samādadhe nāṃśukam āhitaṃ vṛthā
na veda puṣpeṣu ca pāṇi-pallavam ||SRs_2.128|| (kirātārjunīye 8.15)
body.translated_text:
From hearing something desired, for example —
As the beloved speaks, the other [woman], face upturned,
with gaze fixed, her disheveled tresses loosely gathered,
took up the garment placed in vain,
and did not notice the flower-blossom in her palm. ||2.128|| (<s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 8.15)

body.text: atra priya-vākya-śravaṇa-janita-jāḍyam animeṣatvādinā vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the stupor (<s>jāḍya</s>) produced by hearing the beloved's words is expressed through the unblinking gaze and other [signs].

body.text:
priya-darśanād, yathā-
ehai so bi pauttho ahaṃ a kuppejja so bi aṇuṇejja |
ia ciṃteṃtī bahuā daṭṭhūṇa piaṃ ṇa kiṃ pi sammarai ||SRs_2.129|| [*11]
[*11] pūrvārdha-mātraṃ gāthā-saptaśatyāṃ dṛśyate 1.17.
body.translated_text:
From seeing the beloved, for example —
'He too, the departed one, will come; and I shall be angry; he too will conciliate me' —
thus thinking, the young bride, upon seeing her beloved, remembers nothing at all. ||2.129||

children.text: (eṣyati so' pi proṣitaḥ ahaṃ ca kupyeyaṃ so' py anuneṣyati |
children.translated_text: ('He too, the departed one, will come; and I shall be angry; he too will conciliate me' —

children.text: iti cintayantī vadhūr dṛṣṭvā priyaṃ na kim api saṃsmarati ||)
children.translated_text: thus thinking, the young bride, upon seeing her beloved, remembers nothing at all.)

body.text: atra priya-darśana-janitaṃ jāḍyaṃ pūrva-cintita-kriyā-vismaraṇena vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the stupor produced by seeing the beloved is expressed through the forgetting of previously planned actions.

children.translated_text: From hearing something unpleasant, for example —

children.text: āpucchantasya bahū gamiduṃ daiassa suṇia addhottim |
children.translated_text: The young bride, hearing the half-spoken farewell of her beloved who is asking leave to depart,

children.text: aṇumaṃṇiduṃ na jāṇai ṇa nivāreduṃ paravasā ubaha ||SRs_2.130||
children.translated_text: knows not how to consent nor how to prevent him — helpless, behold! ||2.130||
(The young bride, hearing the half-spoken farewell of her beloved who is asking leave to depart,

children.text: anumantuṃ na jānāti na nivārayituṃ para-vaśā paśyata ||)
children.translated_text: knows not how to consent nor how to prevent him — helpless, behold!)
From seeing something undesired, for example —
When the father-in-law is being cremated, near the house, upon the heap of funeral pyre-wood,

children.text: ṇa suṇai suṇhā suṇṇā bahuso kahidaṃ bi sasurāe ||SRs_2.131||
children.translated_text: the daughter-in-law, vacant-minded, does not hear even though told many times by her mother-in-law. ||2.131||
(When the father-in-law is being cremated, near the house, upon the heap of funeral pyre-wood,

children.text: na śṛṇoti snuṣā śūnyā bahuśaḥ kathitam api śvaśrvā ||)
children.translated_text: the daughter-in-law, vacant-minded, does not hear even though told many times by her mother-in-law.)

body.text: viyogād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Though asked, he questioned again, his throat choked with sobs;

children.text: śuśrāva noktam api śūnya-manāḥ sa kiñcit |
children.translated_text: though told, he heard nothing, his mind empty;

children.text: sasmāra na smṛtam api kṣaṇam ātma-kṛtyaṃ
children.translated_text: though reminded, he did not remember his own duty for even a moment;

children.text: śrutvāham ity upagato' pi na saṃviveda ||SRs_2.132||
children.translated_text: though he arrived hearing 'I am [here],' he did not recognize [anyone]. ||2.132||

body.translated_text: From separation (<s>viyoga</s>), for example —

body.text: (abhinandasya rāma-carite 19.61)
body.translated_text: (<s>Abhinanda</s>'s <s>Rāma-carita</s> 19.61)

body.text: atra sītā-viraha-janitaṃ rāvaṇasya jāḍyaṃ punaḥ-praśna-śruty-ādibhir avagamyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the stupor of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> produced by separation from <s>Sītā</s> is understood through re-questioning, [not] hearing, and the like.

body.text:
atha (18) vrīḍā-
akārya-karaṇāvajñā-stuti-nūtana-saṅgamaiḥ |
pratīkārākriyādyaiś ca vrīḍatvanatidhṛṣṭatā ||SRs_2.133|| 66
tatra ceṣṭā nigūḍhoktir ādhomukhya-vicintane |

children.translated_text: not going out anywhere, veiling oneself from afar,
biting the nails, drawing lines on the ground, and similar actions. ||2.134||

body.translated_text:
Now, (18) <s>Vrīḍā</s> (Shame) —
Shame, which is the state of not being bold, [arises] from doing what ought not to be done, from contempt, from praise, and from a new union;
from failure to retaliate, and the like. ||2.133||
Its gestures are: concealed speech, downcast face and reflection,

body.text:
akārya-karaṇād, yathā-
gurv-ādeśād eva nirmīyamāṇo
nādharmāya strī-vadho' pi sthito' yam |
adya sthitvā śvo gamiṣyadbhir alpair
lajjāsmābhir mīlitākṣair jitaiva ||SRs_2.135|| (a.rā. 2.59)
body.translated_text:
From doing what ought not to be done, for example —
This very slaying of a woman, undertaken by the command of the preceptor himself,
stands fixed as not being against <s>dharma</s>.
[Yet] today, we who are ashamed, with eyes closed, standing here
and departing tomorrow — we are but few [who feel thus], and she is already conquered. ||2.135|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 2.59)

children.translated_text: From contempt, for example —
Shaken off by enemies, reduced to the status of deer,
we are ashamed even before one another — how much more before companions! ||2.136||

body.text: (kirātārjunīya 11.58)
body.translated_text: (<s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 11.58)

body.text:
stutyā, yathā-
tasya saṃstūyamānasya caritārthais tapasvibhiḥ |
śuśubhe vikramodagraṃ vrīḍayāvanataṃ śiraḥ ||SRs_2.137|| (ra.vaṃ. 15.27)
body.translated_text:
From praise, for example —
As he was praised by sages whose purposes had been fulfilled,
his head, lifted high in valor,
shone, bowed down by modesty. ||2.137|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 15.27)

body.text:
nava-saṅgamena, yathā-
paṭā-lagne patyau namayati mukhaṃ jāta-vinayā
haṭhāśleṣaṃ vāñchaty apaharati gātrāṇi nibhṛtam |
na śaknoty ākhyātuṃ smita-mukha-sakhī-datta-nayanā
hriyā tāmyaty antaḥ prathama-parihāse nava-vadhūḥ ||SRs_2.138|| (amaru. 37)
pratīkārākaraṇād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Of <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), whose fierce anger arose from the death of <s>Abhimanyu</s> wrought by the risen enemies,
who had not yet wreaked vengeance on the foes, fainting inwardly with grief —

children.text: kīrṇā bāṣpa-kaṇaiḥ patanti dhanuṣi vrīḍā-jaḍā dṛṣṭayo
children.translated_text: his gazes, numb with shame, fall upon his bow, scattered with tear-drops;

children.text: hā vatseti giraḥ sphuranti na punar niryānti kaṇṭhād bahiḥ ||SRs_2.139||
children.translated_text: 'Alas, my child!' — the words form but do not come forth from his throat. ||2.139||

body.translated_text: From failure to retaliate, for example —

body.text: (nārāyaṇasyeti śārṅgadhara-paddhatiḥ)
body.translated_text: (By <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — so the <s>Śārṅgadhara-paddhati</s>.)

body.text: atha (19) avahitthā-

children.translated_text: <s>Avahitthā</s> is the concealment of one's true state, arising from crookedness, majesty, policy,
shame, alarm, gallantry, boldness, defeat, and the like. ||2.140||

body.translated_text: Now, (19) <s>Avahitthā</s> (Dissimulation) —

body.text: anyathā-kathanaṃ mithyā-dhairyam anyatra vīkṣaṇam | 69
body.translated_text: Speaking otherwise, feigned composure, looking elsewhere,

body.text: kathā-bhaṅgādayo' py asyām anubhāvā bhavanty amī ||SRs_2.141||
body.translated_text: breaking off a conversation — these and others are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions) in this [state]. ||2.141||

body.text:
jaihmyād, yathā-
liṅgair mudaḥ saṃvṛta-vikriyās te
hradāḥ prasannā iva gūḍha-nakrāḥ |
vaidarbham āmantrya yayus tadīyāṃ
pratyarpya pūjām upadācchalena ||SRs_2.142|| (ra.vaṃ 7.30)
body.translated_text:
From crookedness (<s>jaihmya</s>), for example —
They, whose emotions were concealed, with signs of joy hidden,
like clear lakes with crocodiles lurking within,
took leave of the <s>Vaidarbha</s> (king) and departed, returning his honors
under the pretext [of reciprocation]. ||2.142|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.30)

body.text:
prābhavād, yathā-
anirbhinno gabhīratvād antargūḍha-ghana-vyathaḥ |
puṭa-pāka-pratīkāśo rāmasya karuṇo rasaḥ ||SRs_2.143|| (u.rā.ca. 3.1)
body.translated_text:
From majesty (<s>prābhava</s>), for example —
Unbroken due to his depth, with intense pain concealed within,
like the heating of ore in a crucible,
was the <s>Karuṇa</s> (pathetic) <s>rasa</s> of <s>Rāma</s>. ||2.143|| (<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 3.1)

body.text: nītyā, yathā-

children.translated_text: Outwardly conducting himself charmingly, inclined to all appearances,
he conceals even the most minute points of the adversary's strategy.

children.text: janaṃ vidvān ekaḥ sakalam atisandhāya kapaṭais
children.translated_text: One wise man, having deceived all people through stratagems,

children.text: taṭasthaḥ svān arthān ghaṭayati ca maunaṃ ca bhajate ||SRs_2.144||
children.translated_text: standing aloof, accomplishes his own purposes and observes silence. ||2.144||

body.translated_text: From policy (<s>nīti</s>), for example —

body.text: (mālatī-mādhave 1.17)
body.translated_text: (<s>Mālatī-Mādhava</s> 1.17)

body.text:
lajjayā, yathā-
cikṣep lakṣmīr niṭilān nakhāgraiḥ
prasveda-vāryātapam ākṣipantī |
jugopa devo' pi sa romaharṣaṃ
jaḍābdhi-vātāhati-kaitavena ||SRs_2.145|| (kandarpa-sambhava)
body.translated_text:
From shame (<s>lajjā</s>), for example —
<s>Lakṣmī</s> scratched her forehead with her nail-tips,
wiping away the perspiration [pretending it was] the sun's heat;
and the Lord too concealed his goosebumps
under the pretense of being struck by a cold ocean breeze. ||2.145|| (<s>Kandarpa-sambhava</s>)

body.text:
sādhvasena, yathā-
śrutvā duḥśravam adbhutaṃ ca mithilā-vṛttāntam antaḥ-patac-
cintāpahnava-sāvahittha-vadana-tvag-viprakīrṇa-smitaḥ |
helākṛṣṭa-surāvarodha-ramaṇī-sīmanta-santānaka-
srag-vāsojjvala-pāṇir apy avati māṃ vatso na laṅkeśvaraḥ ||SRs_2.146|| (a.rā. 4.8)
body.translated_text:
From alarm (<s>sādhvasa</s>), for example —
Upon hearing the wondrous and terrible news of <s>Mithilā</s>, with a smile
scattered over the face's skin as a concealment of inner anxiety by dissimulation,
with a hand resplendent with the <s>santānaka</s> flower-garland from the parting of <s>Surāvarodha</s> (celestial) women's hair, playfully drawn — may my child, the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), protect me! ||2.146|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 4.8)

body.text:
dākṣiṇyād, yathā-
tvayy ardhāsana-bhāji kiṃ nara-gaṇodgītair bhavad-vikramair
antaḥ-sambhṛta-matsaro' pi bhagavān ākāra-guptau kṛtī |
unmīlad-bhavadīya-dakṣiṇa-bhujā-romāñca-viddhoccarad-
bāṣpair eva vilocanair abhinayaty ānandam ākhaṇḍalaḥ ||SRs_2.147|| (a.rā. 1.29)
body.translated_text:
From gallantry (<s>dākṣiṇya</s>), for example —
When you share half his throne, what [need is there] of the songs of men praising your valor?
Even the blessed one (<s>Indra</s>), though inwardly nursing jealousy, is skilled in concealing his demeanor;
only with his eyes, from which tears rise, stirred by the goosebumps on your mighty right arm as they unfold,
does <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> (<s>Indra</s>) express his delight. ||2.147|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.29)

body.text:
prāgalbhyena, yathā-
ekatrāsana-saṅgatiḥ parihṛtā pratyudgamād dūratas
tāmbūlānayana-cchalena rabhasāśleṣo' pi saṃvighnitaḥ |
ālāpo' pi na miśritaḥ parijanaṃ vyāpārayanty āntike- kāntaṃ pratyupacārataś caturayā kopaḥ kṛtārthīkṛtaḥ ||SRs_2.148|| (amaru. 18)
atha (20) smṛtiḥ-

children.translated_text: Through well-being, reflection, firm practice, seeing something similar, and the like,

children.text:
smṛtiḥ pūrvānubhūtārtha-pratītis tatra vikriyāḥ |
kampanodvahane mūrdhno bhrū-vikṣepādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.149|| 71
children.translated_text:
<s>smṛti</s> is the recollection of previously experienced objects. In it, the expressions are:
trembling, nodding of the head, knitting of brows, and the like. ||2.149||

body.translated_text: Now, (20) <s>Smṛti</s> (Memory) —

body.text:
svāsthyena, yathā-
ramyāṇi vīkṣya madhurāṃś ca niśamya śabdān
paryutsuko bhavati yat sukhito' pi jantuḥ |
tac cetasā smarati nūnam abodha-pūrvaṃ
bhāva-sthirāṇi jananāntara-sauhṛdāni ||SRs_2.150|| (śak. 5.2)
body.translated_text:
From well-being (<s>svāsthya</s>), for example —
That even a happy creature becomes restless
upon seeing beautiful things and hearing sweet sounds —
the heart surely remembers, without prior awareness,
friendships from other lifetimes, stable in feeling. ||2.150|| (<s>Śākuntala</s> 5.2)

body.text:
cintayā, yathā-
līneva pratibimbiteva likhitevotkīrṇarūpeva ca
pratyupteva ca vajra-lepa-ghaṭitevāntar-nikhāteva ca |
sā naś cetasi kīliteva viśikhaiś ceto-bhuvaḥ pañcabhiś
cintā-santati-tantu-jāla-niviḍa-syūteva lagnā priyā ||SRs_2.151|| (mā.mā. 5.10)
body.translated_text:
From reflection (<s>cintā</s>), for example —
As if dissolved, as if reflected, as if painted, as if carved,
as if inlaid, as if cemented with diamond-paste, as if embedded within,
as if nailed into our hearts by the five arrows of the Mind-born one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>),
as if densely stitched by the web of threads of continuous thought — the beloved clings. ||2.151|| (<s>Mālatī-Mādhava</s> 5.10)

body.text:
dṛḍhābhyāsena, yathā-
tad vaktraṃ nayane ca te smita-sudhā-mugdhaṃ ca tad vācikaṃ
sā veṇī sa bhuja-kramo' tisaralo līlālasā sā gatiḥ |
tanvī seti ca seti seti satataṃ tad-dhyāna-baddhātmano
nidrā no na ratir na cāpi viratiḥ śūnyaṃ mano vartate ||SRs_2.152|| (rasa-kalikā, 32)[*12]
[*12] This verse appeared previously after kārikā 2.56a.
body.translated_text:
From firm practice (<s>dṛḍhābhyāsa</s>), for example —
That face, and those eyes, and that speech sweet with the nectar of smiles,
that braid, that sequence of arms so exceedingly graceful, that gait languid with playfulness —
'She is slender' and 'she is thus' and 'she is so' — of one whose mind is bound in constant meditation on her,
there is no sleep, no pleasure, no cessation — the mind moves in emptiness. ||2.152|| (<s>Rasa-kalikā</s>, 32)

body.text:
sadṛśālokanena, yathā-
ārakta-rājibhir iyaṃ kusumair nava-kandalī salila-garbhaiḥ |
kopād antar-bāṣpe smarayati māṃ locane tasyāḥ ||SRs_2.153|| [vikramorvaśīya 4.15]
body.translated_text:
From seeing something similar (<s>sadṛśālokana</s>), for example —
This new <s>kandalī</s> (plantain) plant with its reddish streaks, with flowers full of water,
reminds me of her eyes — inwardly tearful from anger. ||2.153|| [<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.15]

body.text:
atha (21) vitarkaḥ-
ūho vitarkaḥ sandeha-vimarṣa-pratyayādibhiḥ |

children.text: janito nirṇayāntaḥ syād asatyaḥ satya eva vā | 72
children.translated_text: it ends in a conclusion, which may be false or true.
In it, the <s>anubhāvas</s> are: knitting of brows, tossing of the head, and the like. ||2.154||

body.translated_text:
Now, (21) <s>Vitarka</s> (Conjecture) —
Conjecture (<s>ūha</s>) is <s>vitarka</s>, arising from doubt, deliberation, inference, and the like;

body.text: sandeha-pratyayanād, yathā-

children.text: aṅkaṃ ke' pi śaśaṅkire jala-nidheḥ paṅkaṃ pare menire
children.translated_text: Some suspected it to be a mark on the ocean; others thought it mud;

children.text: sāraṅgaṃ katicic ca saṃjagadire bhūmeś ca bimbaṃ pare |
children.translated_text: a few declared it a spotted deer; and others, an image of the earth.
That which appears dark like a fragment of split sapphire in the moon —

children.text: tan manye ravi-bhītam andha-tamasaṃ kukṣi-stham ālakṣyate ||SRs_2.155||
children.translated_text: I think it is the darkness, frightened of the sun, seen dwelling within [the moon's] belly. ||2.155||

body.translated_text: From doubt and inference (<s>sandeha-pratyayana</s>), for example —

body.text: vimarśo vicāraḥ | tena, yathā-

children.text: gamanam alasaṃ śūnyā dṛṣṭiḥ śarīram asauṣṭhavaṃ
children.translated_text: Her gait is languid, her gaze vacant, her body graceless,

children.text: śvasitam adhikaṃ kiṃ nv etat syāt kim anyad ato' tha vā |
children.translated_text: her sighing excessive — what could this be? Or is it something else?

children.text: bhramati bhuvane kandarpājñā vikāri ca yauvanaṃ
children.translated_text: The command of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the God of Love) wanders through the world, and youth is changeful;

children.text: lalita-madhurās te te bhāvāḥ kṣipanti ca dhīratām ||SRs_2.156||
children.translated_text: those various charming and sweet emotions overthrow even steadfastness. ||2.156||

body.translated_text: <s>Vimarśa</s> is deliberation. By that, for example —

body.text: atra mādhava-gatāṃ cintām upalabhya kim atra kāraṇam iti vimṛśatā makarandena manmatha-nibandhana evāyaṃ bhāva iti satya-nirṇayānto vitarkaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Makaranda</s>, perceiving the anxiety directed toward <s>Mādhava</s> and deliberating 'what is the cause of this?', arrives at the true conclusion that this emotion is rooted in love — thus it is a <s>vitarka</s>.

body.text: atha (22) cintā-

children.translated_text: From the non-attainment of a desired object, from loss of sovereignty, and the like,

children.text:
cintā dhyānātmikā tasyām anubhāvā bhavanty amī |
kārśyādhomukhya-santāpa-niḥśvāsocchrvasanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.157|| 74
children.translated_text:
<s>cintā</s> is meditation-like [brooding]. In it, the <s>anubhāvas</s> are:
emaciation, downcast face, burning, sighing, heavy breathing, and the like. ||2.157||

body.translated_text: Now, (22) <s>Cintā</s> (Anxiety) —

children.translated_text: From not obtaining a desired object, for example —
Slightly bent and downcast is her [face]; with half-closed eyelash-fringed pupils, she is motionless;

children.text: diṭṭhī kapola-pālī ṇihiā kara-pallave mano suṇṇaṃ ||SRs_2.158||
children.translated_text: her gaze [is fixed], her cheek resting on her palm, her mind empty. ||2.158||
[Slightly bent and downcast is her face; with half-closed eyelash-fringed pupils, she is motionless;

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ kapola-pālī nihitā kara-pallave manaḥ śūnyam ||]
children.translated_text: her gaze is fixed, her cheek resting on her palm, her mind empty.]

body.text:
aiśvarya-nāśena, yathā-
yamo' pi vilikhan bhūmiṃ daṇḍenāstamita-tviṣā |
kurute' sminn amoghe' pi nirvāṇālāta-lāghavam ||SRs_2.159|| [ku.saṃ. 2.27]
body.translated_text:
From loss of sovereignty, for example —
Even <s>Yama</s>, drawing [lines] on the earth with his staff whose luster has set,
treats this [staff], though infallible, with the lightness of an extinguished firebrand. ||2.159|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 2.27]

body.text:
atha (23) matiḥ-
nānā-śāstrāratha-mathanād artha-nirdhāraṇaṃ matiḥ |

children.translated_text: In it, the gestures are: performing what needs to be done, resolving doubts,
instructing disciples, knitting of brows, reasoning for and against, and the like. ||2.160||

body.translated_text:
Now, (23) <s>Mati</s> (Intellect/Judgment) —
<s>Mati</s> is the determination of meaning through the churning of various <s>śāstras</s> (sciences).

body.text:
yathā-
daśaratha-kule sambhūtaṃ mām avāpya dhanurdharaṃ
dinakara-kulāskandī ko' yaṃ kalaṅka-navāṅkuraḥ |
iti na vanitām etāṃ hantuṃ mano vicikitsate
yad adhikaraṇaṃ dharma-sthīyaṃ tavaiva vacāṃsi naḥ ||SRs_2.161|| (a.rā. 2.62)
body.translated_text:
For example —
'Born in the lineage of <s>Daśaratha</s>, having obtained me, a bowman —
who is this new sprout of disgrace, assailing the Solar dynasty?'
Thus my mind does not hesitate to slay this woman;
but the words that form the judicial tribunal of <s>dharma</s> are yours alone. ||2.161|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 2.62)

body.text: atha (24) dhṛtiḥ-

children.translated_text: Through knowledge, wisdom, devotion to the teacher and the like, and the attainment of various purposes,

children.text: lajjādibhiś ca cittasya naispṛhyaṃ dhṛtir ucyate ||SRs_2.162||
children.translated_text: and through shame and similar [emotions], the desirelessness of the mind is called <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness). ||2.162||

body.translated_text: Now, (24) <s>Dhṛti</s> (Steadfastness) —

body.text: atrānubhāvā vijñeyāḥ prāptārthānubhavas tathā | 77
body.translated_text: In it, the <s>anubhāvas</s> to be known are: the experience of objects obtained,

body.text: aprāptātīta-naṣṭārthān abhisaṅkṣobhaṇādayaḥ ||SRs_2.163||
body.translated_text: and not being agitated by objects unobtained, past, or lost, and the like. ||2.163||

body.text:
jñānāt, yathā-
aśnīmahi vayaṃ bhikṣām āśāvāso vasīmahi |
śayīmahi mahī-pṛṣṭhe kurvīmahi kim īśvaraiḥ ||SRs_2.164|| (vai.śa. 55)
body.translated_text:
From knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), for example —
We shall eat alms, we shall wear the garment of the directions [i.e., go naked],
we shall sleep on the surface of the earth — what have we to do with lords? ||2.164|| (<s>Vairāgya-śataka</s> 55)

body.text: vijñānād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Even today there exists the surface of the earth, bounded by the moat of four oceans;

children.text: vartante' pi ca tatra tatra rasikā goṣṭhīṣu saktā nṛpāḥ |
children.translated_text: and there too, here and there, connoisseur-kings engaged in assemblies continue;

children.text: ekas tatra nirādaro bhavati ced anyo bhavet sādaro
children.translated_text: if one of them is indifferent, another would be respectful —

children.text: vāg-devī vadanāmbuje vasati cet ko nāma dīno janaḥ ||SRs_2.165||
children.translated_text: if the goddess of speech (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) dwells in one's lotus-mouth, who then is a wretched person? ||2.165||

body.translated_text: From wisdom (<s>vijñāna</s>), for example —

body.text: guru-bhaktyā, yathā-

children.text: tiṣṭhan bhāti pituḥ puro bhuvi yathā siṃhāsane kiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: 'Standing before one's father on the ground — does the same joy come from a throne?

children.text: yat saṃvāhayataḥ sukhaṃ hi caraṇau tātasya kiṃ rājyataḥ |
children.translated_text: What happiness from kingship equals the pleasure of pressing father's feet?

children.text: kiṃ bhukte bhuvana-traye dhṛtir asau bhuktojjhite yā guror
children.translated_text: What is the value of eating in the three worlds compared to the composure that comes from serving one's preceptor after eating?

children.text: āyāsaḥ khalu rājyam ujjhita-guros tatrāsti kaścid guṇaḥ ||SRs_2.166||
children.translated_text: Kingship is but toil for one who has abandoned his guru — what merit is there in that?' ||2.166||

body.translated_text: From devotion to one's teacher, as for example —

body.text: (nāgānanda 1.7)
body.translated_text: (from <s>Nāgānanda</s> 1.7)

body.text: nānārtha-siddhyā, yathā-

children.text: krodhāndhaiḥ sakalaṃ hataṃ ripu-kulaṃ pañcākṣatās te vayaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The entire enemy clan has been slain by those blinded with rage; the five of us are unscathed;
the ocean of insult, brought about by the wrongful conduct toward <s>Pāñcālī</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>), has been crossed;

children.text: tvaṃ devaḥ puruṣottamaḥ sukṛtinaṃ mām ādṛto bhāṣase
children.translated_text: You are the Supreme Lord, the <s>Puruṣottama</s>, and you honor me as one of merit —

children.text: kiṃ nāmānyad ataḥ paraṃ bhagavato yāce prasannād aham ||SRs_2.167||
children.translated_text: what more indeed could I ask of the gracious <s>Bhagavān</s>?' ||2.167||

body.translated_text: From the accomplishment of various aims, as for example —

body.text: (veṇī-saṃhāraḥ 6.45)
body.translated_text: (from <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 6.45)

body.text: atha (25) harṣaḥ-

children.translated_text: Joy is produced by the attainment of a heart's desire, by the achievement of a worthy object, 78
by meeting with friends, by the grace of gods, and the like. ||2.168||

body.translated_text: Now, (25) <s>Harṣa</s> (joy) —

body.text: manaḥ-prasādo harṣaḥ syād atra netrāsya-phullatā | 79
body.translated_text: Joy is the gladness of the mind; its [expressions] are: beaming of eyes and face, 79

body.text:
priyābhāṣaṇam āśleṣaḥ pulakānāṃ prarohaṇam |
svedodgamaś ca hastena hasta-sampīḍanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.169|| 80
body.translated_text: speaking lovingly, embracing, rising of horripilation, breaking out of perspiration, pressing hand with hand, and the like. ||2.169|| 80

body.text:
manorathasya lābhena, yathā-
nivāta-padma-stimitena cakṣuṣā
nṛpasya kāntaṃ pibataḥ sutānanam |
mahodadheḥ pūra ivendu-darśanād
guruḥ praharṣaḥ prababhūva nātmani ||SRs_2.170|| (ra.vaṃ. 3.17)
body.translated_text: From the attainment of a heart's desire, as for example — 'With an eye steady as a lotus in still air, as the king drank in the beautiful face of his son, a great joy, like the swelling of the ocean at the sight of the moon, arose, uncontainable within himself.' ||2.170|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 3.17)

body.text: yogya-vastu-siddhyā, yathā-

children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>), passionate, with his red-palmed hand
as if [colored] with the lac-dye from the soles of <s>Pulomajā</s>'s (<s>Śacī</s>'s) feet,
wiped <s>Hari</s> (the horse <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>), neighing deep as thunder,
on the mouth, hard and fleshless. ||2.171||

body.translated_text: From the achievement of a worthy object, as for example —

body.text: atra uccaiḥśravaso lābhena devendrasya harṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the joy of <s>Devendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) is from obtaining <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>.

body.text:
mitra-saṅgamād, yathā-
ibha-kumbha-tuṅga-kaṭhinetaretara- stana-bhāra-dūra-vinivāritodarāḥ |
pariphulla-gaṇḍa-phalakāḥ parasparaṃ parirebhire kukura-kaurava-striyaḥ ||SRs_2.172|| (māghe 13.16)
body.translated_text: From meeting with friends, as for example — 'With breasts heavy and firm as elephant-frontal-globes, kept far from each other's bellies by their burden, with cheek-surfaces in full bloom, the women of the <s>Kukuras</s> and <s>Kauravas</s> embraced one another.' ||2.172|| (from <s>Māgha</s> 13.16)

body.text: mitra-saṅgamaḥ pūjyādi-saṅgamādīnām apy upalakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: 'Meeting with friends' is also a general term for meeting with venerable persons and the like.

body.text:
pūjya-saṅgamena, yathā-
yugānta-kāla-pratisaṃhṛtātmano
jaganti yasyāṃ savikāsam āsata |
tanau mamus tatra na kaṭabha-dviṣas
tapadhanābhyāgama-sambhavā mudaḥ ||SRs_2.173|| (śi.va. 1.23)
body.translated_text: From meeting with a venerable person, as for example — 'In that body of the enemy of <s>Kaṭabha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), in whom the worlds, which had been withdrawn at the time of the cosmic dissolution, now blossomed forth — the joys born of the arrival of the lord of austerities (<s>Bhṛgu</s>) could not be contained.' ||2.173|| (from <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 1.23)

body.text:
deva-prasādād, yathā-
tasyāḥ prasannendu-mukhaḥ prasādaṃ
gurur nṛpāṇāṃ gurave nivedya |
praharṣa-cihnānumitaṃ priyāyai
śaśaṃsa vācā punaruktayeva ||SRs_2.174|| (ra.vaṃ. 2.68)
body.translated_text: From the grace of a deity, as for example — 'He, with a face bright as the propitious moon, having conveyed the grace of the king of kings to his preceptor, reported to his beloved, with words that seemed redundant, what had been already inferred from the signs of joy.' ||2.174|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 2.68)

body.text:
ādi-śabdād guru-rāja-prasādādayaḥ | guru-prasādād, yathā-
asmad-gotra-mahattaraḥ kratu-bhujām adyāyam ādyo ravir
yajvāno vayam adya te bhagavatī bhūr adya rājanvatī |
adya svaṃ bahu manyate sahacarair asmābhir ākhaṇḍalo
yenaitāvad arundhatī-patir api svenānugṛhṇāti naḥ ||SRs_2.175|| (a.rā. 1.18)
body.translated_text: The word 'and the like' includes the grace of a teacher, a king, and so forth. From the grace of a teacher, as for example — 'Today this sun is the foremost of our lineage, the first among those who partake of sacrificial offerings; today we are sacrificers; today, O Blessed One, the earth has a king; today <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> (<s>Indra</s>) regards himself as great together with our companions — because to this extent even the husband of <s>Arundhatī</s> (<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>) favors us with his own grace.' ||2.175|| (from <s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.18)

body.text:
rāja-prasādād, yathā-
prītir asya dadato' bhavat tathā
yena tat-priya-cikīrṣavo nṛpāḥ |
sparśitair adhikam āgaman mudaṃ
nādhiveśma-nihitair upāyanaiḥ ||SRs_2.176|| (śi.va. 14.47)
body.translated_text: From the grace of a king, as for example — 'His delight in giving was such that the kings who wished to please him gained more joy from gifts offered [to him] than from those placed in their own residences.' ||2.176|| (from <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 14.47)

body.text:
atha (26) autsukyam-
kālākṣamatvam autsukyam iṣṭa-vastu-viyogataḥ |
tad-darśanād ramya-vastu-didṛkṣādeś ca tat-kriyāḥ ||SRs_2.177|| 81
tvarānavasthitiḥ śayyā-sthitir uttāna-cintane |
śarīra-gauravaṃ nidrā-tandrā-niḥśvasitādayaḥ ||SRs_2.178|| 82
body.translated_text: Now, (26) <s>Autsukya</s> (eagerness/longing) — The inability to endure [the passage of] time due to separation from a desired object, or from seeing it, or from the wish to see a beautiful thing, and the like — is <s>Autsukya</s>. ||2.177|| 81 Its actions are: haste, restlessness, sitting on the bed in supine contemplation, heaviness of the body, drowsiness, sleep, sighing, and the like. ||2.178|| 82

body.text:
tatra iṣṭa-vastu-viyogāt-
saṃkṣipyante kṣana iva kathaṃ dīrgha-yāmā triyāmā
sarvāvasthāsv ahar api kathaṃ manda-mandātapaṃ syāt |
itthaṃ cetaś caṭula-nayane durlabha-prārthanaṃ me
gāḍhoṣmābhiḥ kṛtam aśaraṇaṃ tvad-viyoga-vyathābhiḥ ||SRs_2.179|| [me.dū. 2.48]
body.translated_text: Of these, from separation from a desired object — 'How can the three-watched night, with its long watches, be condensed to a mere instant? How can the day, in all its states, have its heat diminished to gentleness? Thus, O restless-eyed one, my mind, craving for what is difficult to obtain, has been rendered shelterless by the deep-burning pangs of separation from you.' ||2.179|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 2.48]

body.text:
tatra iṣṭa-vastu-darśanāt-
āyāte dayite manoratha-śatair nītvā kathañcid dinaṃ gatvā vāsa-gṛhaṃ jaḍe parijane dīrghāṃ kathāṃ kurvati |
daṣṭāsmīty abhidhāya satvara-padaṃ vyādhūya cīnāṃśukaṃ tanvaṅgyā rati-kātareṇa manasā nītaḥ pradīpaḥ śamam ||179|| [amaru 77]
body.translated_text: From seeing a desired object — 'When the beloved arrived, having somehow passed the day with a hundred fantasies, entering the inner chamber while the dull-witted attendant carries on a long tale — saying "A snake has bitten me!" with hasty steps, shaking off her Chinese silk garment, with a mind eager for love, the slender-limbed woman extinguished the lamp.' ||179|| [<s>Amaru</s> 77]

body.text: ramya-didṛkṣayā, yathā-

children.translated_text: With a toilette that was completed leaving the rest undone, agitated,
opened up and overflowing onto the road,
for the sake of seeing <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>/<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
the city-women thronged to the latticed windows. ||2.180||

body.translated_text: From the desire to see something beautiful, as for example —

body.text:
atha (27) augryam-
aparādhāvamānābhyāṃ cauryāābhigrahaṇādibhiḥ |
asat-pralāpanādyaiś ca kṛtaṃ caṇḍatvam ugratā ||SRs_2.181|| 83
kriyās tatrāsya-nayana-rāgo bandhana-tāḍane |
śirasaḥ kampanaṃ kheda-vadha-nirbhartsanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.182|| 84
body.translated_text: Now, (27) <s>Augrya</s> (ferocity) — Fierceness produced by offences, insults, seizure of a thief, baseless accusations, and the like — is <s>Augrya</s>. ||2.181|| 83 Its actions are: reddening of face and eyes, binding and beating, shaking of the head, vexation, killing, harsh rebuke, and the like. ||2.182|| 84

body.text:
aparādhād, yathā-
praṇayi-sakhī-salīla-parihāsa-rasādhigatair
lalita-śirīṣa-puṣpa-hananair api tāmyati yat |
vapuṣi vadhāya tatra tava śastram upakṣipataḥ
patatu śarasy akāṇḍayam adaṇḍaṃ ivaiṣa bhujaḥ ||SRs_2.183|| (mā.mā. 5.31)
body.translated_text: From an offence, as for example — 'Since she who is your beloved friend suffers even from playful, sporting blows with the delicate <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers — as you hurl your weapon at her body for the purpose of slaying — may this arm of yours, which falls upon the arrow as if it were a staff without cause, itself fall [in punishment]!' ||2.183|| (from <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 5.31)

body.text: atra mālatī-nikāra-rūpāparādhād mādhavasyaugryam |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Mādhava</s>'s ferocity arises from the offence of the mistreatment of <s>Mālatī</s>.

body.text: avamānāḍ, yathā-

children.translated_text: Never having previously known contempt from enemies,
with a mind enraged against the one conveying [their] disregard,
he of deeds condemned by the wise, the enemy of sacrifice (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>),
struck the order-bearer with his mace. ||2.184||

body.translated_text: From insult, as for example —

body.text:
cauryābhigrahaṇād, yathā-
bhuja-viṭapa-madena vyartham andhambhaviṣṇur
dhig apasarasi cauraṃkāram ākruśyamānaḥ |
tvad-urasi vidadhātu svām avaskāra-keliṃ
kuṭila-karaja-koṭi-krūra-karmā jaṭāyuḥ ||SRs_2.185|| (a.rā. 5.11)
body.translated_text: From seizure of a thief, as for example — 'Blinded in vain by the intoxication of arm-strength, shame! You run away, being called a thief — may <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, fierce in the action of his crooked talon-tips, perform his sport of reviling upon your chest!' ||2.185|| (from <s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 5.11)

body.text:
asat-pralāpād, yathā-
katham api na niṣiddho duḥkhinā bhīruṇā vā drupada-tanaya-pāṇis tena pitrā mamādya |
tava bhuja-bala-darpādhyāyamānasya vāmaḥ śirasi caraṇa eṣa nyasyate vārayainam ||SRs_2.186|| (veṇī-saṃhāra 3.40)
body.translated_text: From baseless accusations, as for example — 'Somehow not prevented by that father of mine, wretched and timid, the hand of <s>Drupada</s>'s daughter [was given away] today — this foot of the enemy, who meditates upon the pride of your arm-strength, is being placed on our head — prevent it!' ||2.186|| (from <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 3.40)

body.text:
atha (28) amarṣaḥ-
adhikṣepāvamānādyaiḥ krodho' marṣa itīryate |

children.translated_text: Its [manifestations] are: perspiration, shaking of the head, downcast face, brooding, 85
searching for a remedy, enthusiasm, resolution, and the like. ||2.187||

body.translated_text: Now, (28) <s>Amarṣa</s> (indignation) — The anger arising from censure, insult, and the like is called <s>Amarṣa</s>.

body.text:
tatra adhikṣepād, yathā-
iti bhīṣma-bhāṣita-vaco' rtham
adhigatavatām iva kṣaṇāt |
kṣobham agamad atimātram
atho śiśupāla-pakṣa-pṛthivī-bhṛtāṃ gaṇaḥ ||SRs_2.188|| (śi.va. 15.47)
body.translated_text: From censure, as for example — 'Upon grasping the meaning of the words spoken by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, as it were in an instant, the group of kings in <s>Śiśupāla</s>'s faction was exceedingly agitated.' ||2.188|| (from <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 15.47)

body.text:
avamānād, yathā-
dhvaṃsena hṛdayaṃ sadyaḥ paribhūtasya me paraiḥ |
yady amarṣaḥ pratīkāraṃ bhujālambaṃ na lambhayet ||SRs_2.189|| (ki.a. 11.57)
body.translated_text: From insult, as for example — 'If the indignation in the heart of me, who am humiliated by enemies through destruction, should not find a counteraction resting on the arm...' ||2.189|| (from <s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 11.57)

body.text: atha (29) asūyā-

children.translated_text: Caused by another's good fortune, wealth, learning, valor, and the like, 86

children.text:
guṇe' pi doṣāropaḥ syād asūyā tatra vikriyāḥ |
mukhāpavartanaṃ garhā bhrū-bhedānādarādayaḥ ||SRs_2.190|| 87
children.translated_text: the imputation of fault even in merit is <s>Asūyā</s>. Its manifestations are: turning the face away, reproach, frowning, disrespect, and the like. ||2.190|| 87

body.translated_text: Now, (29) <s>Asūyā</s> (envy) —

body.text: para-saubhāgyena, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Do not bear pride [saying] "on the surface of my cheek shines
a spray-design drawn by the beloved's own hand" —

children.text: anyāpi kiṃ na sakhi bhājanam īdṛśīnāṃ
children.translated_text: is not any other woman also a receptacle of such [favors],

children.text: vairī na ced bhavati vepathur antarāyaḥ ||SRs_2.191||
children.translated_text: friend, unless the intervening obstacle of trembling should become an enemy?' ||2.191||

body.translated_text: From another's good fortune, as for example —

body.text: (keśaṭasyeti subhāṣita-ratna-kośe)
body.translated_text: (attributed to <s>Keśaṭa</s> in the <s>Subhāṣita-ratna-kośa</s>)

children.translated_text: From another's wealth, as for example —
'The prosperity that benefits the world belongs to the good, whose minds are pure;
yet, even upon merely seeing it, the evil-minded are consumed with jealousy.' ||2.192||

body.text:
para-vidyayā, yathā-
pratyakṣādi-prabhā-siddha-viruddhārthābhidhāyinaḥ |
vedāntā yadi śāstrāṇi bauddhaiḥ kim aparāddhyate ||SRs_2.193|| (pra.ca. 2.4)
body.translated_text: From another's learning, as for example — 'If the <s>Vedāntas</s> are texts that declare meanings contradicted by truths established through perception and the like, what offence is committed by the <s>Bauddhas</s> (Buddhists)?' ||2.193|| (from <s>Prabodhacandrodaya</s> 2.4)

body.text: yathā vā-

children.translated_text: 'While your glory, O <s>Siṃha-kṣitipati</s>, a receptacle of virtues, shines in its fullness,
and your splendor burns enemies,
that most deluded-minded sage <s>Kaṇāda</s> said "there are only nine substances" — alas!

children.text: caturdhā tejo' pi vyabhajata kaṇādo munir api ||SRs_2.194||
children.translated_text: He even divided <s>tejas</s> (brilliance) into four [kinds]!' ||2.194||

body.translated_text: Or as —

body.text: atra prauḍha-kavi-samaya-prasiddha-mārgānusāriṇo vaktuḥ parimita-dravya-vādini kaṇāde mahaty asūyā mūḍhatama-dhīr iti vāg-ārambheṇa vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the speaker — following the path well-known in the convention of accomplished poets — expresses great envy toward <s>Kaṇāda</s>, the proponent of a limited number of substances, by the opening words 'most deluded-minded.'

body.text: para-śauryeṇa, yathā-

children.text: strī-mātraṃ nanu tāṭakā bhṛgu-suto rāmas tu vipraḥ śucir
children.translated_text: '<s>Tāṭakā</s> was merely a woman; <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s son (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) — well, <s>Rāma</s> is a pure <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: mārīco mṛga eva bhīti-bhavanaṃ vālī punar vānaraḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Mārīca</s> was merely a deer, an abode of fear; <s>Vālin</s>, again, was merely a monkey —

children.text: bhoḥ kākutstha vikatthase kim atha vā vīro jitaḥ kas tvayā
children.translated_text: O <s>Kākutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), what do you boast of? Indeed, what hero has been conquered by you?

children.text: dor-darpas tu tathāpi te yadi samaṃ ko-daṇḍam āropaya ||SRs_2.195||
children.translated_text: Yet if your arm's pride persists, then string your bow against an equal!' ||2.195||

body.translated_text: From another's valor, as for example —

body.text: (hanuman-nāṭaka 14.21)
body.translated_text: (from <s>Hanumān-nāṭaka</s> 14.21)

body.text:
atha (30) cāpalyam-
rāga-dveṣādibhiś citta-lāghavaṃ cāpalaṃ bhavet |

children.translated_text: Its actions are: without deliberation, embracing and clinging, 88
utterance of expulsion, harshness, beating, commanding, and the like. ||2.196||

body.translated_text: Now, (30) <s>Cāpalya</s> (fickleness) — The lightness of mind arising from passion, hatred, and the like is <s>Cāpalya</s>.

body.text:
rāgeṇa, yathā-
vijanam iti balād amuṃ gṛhītvā
kṣaṇam atha vīkṣya vipakṣam antike' nyā |
abhipatitu-manā laghutva-bhīter
abhavad amuñcati vallabhe' tigurvī ||SRs_2.197|| (śi.va., 7.57)
body.translated_text: From passion, as for example — 'Having seized him forcefully in a deserted place, and then momentarily spotting a rival nearby, another woman — intent on pouncing — out of fear of [appearing] fickle, became instead exceedingly heavy [in embrace], not releasing her beloved.' ||2.197|| (from <s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 7.57)

body.text:
dveṣeṇa, yathā-
pādāghātaiḥ surabhir abhitaḥ satvaraṃ tāḍanīyo
gāḍhāmodaṃ malaya-marutaḥ śṛṅkhalādāma datta |
kārāgāre kṣipata tarasā pañcamaṃ rāga-rājaṃ
candraṃ cūrṇīkuruta ca śilāpaṭṭake piṣṭa-bimbam ||SRs_2.198|| (bāla-rāmāyaṇa 5.49)
body.translated_text: From hatred, as for example — 'The bull [of spring] should be immediately struck with kicks on all sides! A tight chain should be given to the <s>Malaya</s> breeze with its dense fragrance! Throw the fifth [note], the king of <s>rāgas</s>, swiftly into prison! And crush the moon to powder on the stone slab — a paste-image!' ||2.198|| (from <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 5.49)

body.text: atra sītā-viraheṇa rāvaṇasya vasantādi-viṣaya-dveṣeṇa tat-tad-adhidevatānāṃ tāḍanā-jñāpanādibhir anubhāvaiś cāpalyaṃ dyotyate |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s fickleness is expressed through the <s>anubhāvas</s> of beating, commanding, and the like toward the presiding deities of spring and other [pleasant] objects, out of hatred for them due to separation from <s>Sītā</s>.

body.text: atha (31) nidrā-

children.translated_text: From intoxication, natural disposition, exercise, freedom from anxiety, fatigue, and the like, 89
the closing down of the mind is <s>nidrā</s> (sleep). Its actions are: heaviness of the face, ||2.199||

body.translated_text: Now, (31) <s>Nidrā</s> (sleep) —

body.text: āghūrṇamāna-netratvam aṅgānāṃ parimardanam | 90
body.translated_text: rolling of the eyes, rubbing of the limbs, 90

body.text:
niḥśvāsocchvāsane sanna-gātratvaṃ netra-mīlanam |
śarīrasya ca saṅkoco jāḍyaṃ cety evam ādayaḥ ||SRs_2.200|| 91
body.translated_text: sighing and inhaling, slackening of the body, closing of the eyes, contraction of the body, and sluggishness — these and similar [responses]. ||2.200|| 91

body.text:
madād, yathā-
yasmin mahīṃ śaṃsati vāṇinīnāṃ
nidrāṃ vihārārdha-pathe gatānām |
vāto' pi nāsraṃsayad aṃśukāni
ko lambayed āharaṇāya hastam ||SRs_2.201|| (ra.vaṃ. 6.75)
body.translated_text: From intoxication, as for example — 'In that [reign] which proclaimed that the earth had [become peaceful enough for] sleep for the merchant-women who had gone half-way on their journey — even the wind did not cause their garments to slip; who then would extend a hand to seize them?' ||2.201|| (from <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 6.75)

body.text: svabhāvād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Extending one creeper-like arm upward as a [support] near her sidelong glance,

children.text: anyām apy alasāṃ nidhāya vipulābhoge nitamba-sthale |
children.translated_text: placing the other, languid, upon the broad expanse of the hip,

children.text: nīvīṃ kiñcid iva ślathāṃ vidadhatī niḥśvāsam unmuñcatī
children.translated_text: her waist-cord slightly loosened, releasing sighs,
with breasts raised crosswise by the pressure of the bed — the slender-waisted one sleeps. ||2.202||

body.translated_text: From natural disposition, as for example —

body.text:
vyāyāmād, yathā-
alasa-lulita-mugdhānyadhva-sañjāta-khedād
aśithila-parirambhair datta-saṃvāhanāni |
parimṛdita-mṛṇālī-durbalāny aṅgakāni
tvam urasi mama kṛtvā yatra nidrām avāptā ||SRs_2.203|| (u.rā.ca. 1.24)
body.translated_text: From exercise, as for example — 'With limbs delicate as crushed lotus-stalks, given massage through tight embraces, languid and innocent, wearied from the journey of the other [lovemaking] — placing your body on my chest, you found sleep there.' ||2.203|| (from <s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 1.24)

body.text:
naiścintyād, yathā-
dattendrābhaya-vibhramādbhuta-bhujāsambhāra-gambhīrayā
tvad-vṛttyā śithilīkṛtas tribhuvana-trāṇāya nārāyaṇaḥ |
antas toṣa-tuṣāra-saurabha-maya-śvāsānilāpūraṇa-
prāṇottuṅga-bhujaṅga-talpam adhunā bhadreṇa nidrāyate ||SRs_2.204|| (a.rā. 1.27)
body.translated_text: From absence of anxiety, for example — 'By your conduct, which has given <s>Indra</s> fearlessness and [left him in] amazement at your magnificent arms, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> has been relieved of the duty of protecting the three worlds. Now he sleeps happily on his serpent-bed, whose coils are raised high by the breathing winds infused with the coolness and fragrance of inner satisfaction.' ||SRs_2.204|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.27)

body.text:
śramād, yathā-
kevalaṃ priyatamā-dayālunā
jyotiṣām avanatāsu paṅktiṣu |
tena tat-parigṛhīta-vakṣasā
netra-mīlana-kutūhalaṃ kṛtam ||SRs_2.205|| (ku.saṃ. 8.84)
body.translated_text: From fatigue, for example — 'Only by the compassionate beloved, when the rows of stars had descended [i.e., at dawn], by him who held her to his chest — the curiosity of closing the eyes was accomplished.' ||SRs_2.205|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.84)

body.text:
atha (32) suptiḥ-
udreka eva nidrāyāḥ suptiḥ syāt tatra vikriyāḥ |

children.translated_text: cessation of the senses, closing of the eyes, limpness of the limbs,
dream-manifestations, motionlessness, and [sounds of] breathing and exhalation, and so forth. ||SRs_2.206||

body.translated_text: Now (32) <s>Supti</s> (deep sleep) — <s>Supti</s> is the intensification of <s>nidrā</s> (sleep); its disturbances therein are:

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: The breath-winds of the sleeping <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), moistened within by the <s>rasa</s> (sentiment) of compassion,
naturally fragrant with the scent of the <s>Vedānta</s>,
the remnants of which have been drunk by the serpent-king who serves as his bed —
may those [breath-winds] protect you! ||SRs_2.207||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atha (33) bodhaḥ-

children.translated_text: From dreams, from touch, from sounds, from the completion of sleep, and the like,
<s>prabodha</s> (awakening) is the recovery of consciousness; its actions therein are: rubbing the eyes, ||SRs_2.208||

body.translated_text: Now (33) <s>Bodha</s> (awakening) —

body.text: śayyāyā mokṣaṇaṃ bāhu-vikṣepo' ṅguli-moṭanam | 94
body.translated_text: releasing oneself from the bed, stretching the arms, cracking the fingers,

body.text: śiraḥ-kaṇḍūyanaṃ cāṅga-valanaṃ caivam ādayaḥ ||SRs_2.209||
body.translated_text: scratching the head, turning the body, and so forth. ||SRs_2.209||

body.text:
svapnād, yathā-
tribhāga-śeṣāsu niśāsu ca kṣaṇaṃ
nimīlya netre sahasā vyabudhyata |
kva nīlakaṇṭha vrajasīty alakṣya-vāg
asatya-kaṇṭhārpita-bāhu-bandhanā ||SRs_2.210|| (ku.saṃ. 5.57)
body.translated_text: From a dream, for example — In the nights, with only a third remaining, having closed her eyes for a moment, she suddenly awoke, and with an imperceptible voice saying 'Where are you going, O <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (Blue-throated one, i.e. Śiva)?' — she who had placed the clasp of her arms on a neck that was not truly [there]. ||SRs_2.210|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 5.57)

body.text: sparśanād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Having smelled the face of the lotus-eyed one lying above him,
asleep then from the fatigue of hurried love-play —
'This morning wind, fragrant with lotuses,
arriving through the jeweled window, has awakened me.' ||SRs_2.211||

body.translated_text: From touch, for example —

body.text:
śabdād, yathā-
uṣasi sa gaja-yūtha-karṇa-tālaiḥ
paṭu-paṭaha-dhvnaibhir vinīta-nidraḥ |
aramata madhurāṇi tatra śṛṇvan
vihaga-vikūjita-vandi-maṅgalāni ||SRs_2.212|| (ra.vaṃ. 9.71)
body.translated_text: From sound, for example — At dawn, his sleep dispelled by the loud sounds of drums and the flapping of elephant-herds' ears, he delighted in hearing there the sweet morning benedictions of birds and bards. ||SRs_2.212|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 9.71)

body.text:
nidrā-sampūrtyā, yathā-
te ca prāpur udanvantaṃ bubudhe cādi-pūruṣaḥ |
avyākṣepo bhaviṣyantyāḥ kārya-siddher hi lakṣaṇam ||SRs_2.213|| (ra.vaṃ. 10.6)
body.translated_text: From the completion of sleep, for example — They reached the ocean, and the primordial Person (<s>Ādi-puruṣa</s>) awoke. Absence of disturbance is indeed the mark of an undertaking that will succeed. ||SRs_2.213|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 10.6)

body.text: uttamādhama-madhyeṣu sāttvikā vyabhicāriṇaḥ | 95
body.translated_text: The <s>sāttvika</s> and <s>vyabhicārin</s> [states] in superior, inferior, and middling [characters]

body.text: vibhāvair anubhāvaiś ca varṇanīyā yathocitam ||SRs_2.214|| [*13]

children.translated_text: Mental states such as agitation (<s>udvega</s>), affection (<s>sneha</s>), hypocrisy (<s>dambha</s>), jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), and the like
are subsumed within those already stated, and hence are not shown separately. ||SRs_2.215||

body.translated_text: should be described appropriately through <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions). ||SRs_2.214||
Editor's note: The inclusion of unstated mental states within those stated.

body.text: Ed. adds: anukta-citta-vṛttīnām uktāntarbhāvaḥ |

tathā hi-para-pratāraṇa-rūpa-dambhasya jihmatāvahitthāyām antar-bhāvaḥ | citta-dravatā-lakṣaṇasya snehasya harṣe' ntarbhāvaḥ | sva-viṣaya-dāna-mānādy-amarṣaṇa-rūpāyā īrṣyāyā amarṣe' ntarbhāvaḥ | para-viṣayāyās tv asūyāyām | udvegasya tu nirveda-viṣādādiṣu yathocitam antarbhāva ity ādi draṣṭavyam | tathā ca bhāva-prakāśikā-kāraḥ-
anye' pi yadi bhāvāḥ syuś citta-vṛtti-viśeṣataḥ |
antarbhāvas tu sarveṣāṃ draṣṭavyo vyabhicāriṣu ||SRs_2.216|| iti |
body.translated_text: Thus: hypocrisy (<s>dambha</s>), whose nature is the deception of others, is subsumed under crookedness and dissimulation (<s>avahitthā</s>). Affection (<s>sneha</s>), characterized by the melting of the heart, is subsumed under joy (<s>harṣa</s>). Jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>), whose nature is the intolerance of honor given to a rival in one's own domain, is subsumed under indignation (<s>amarṣa</s>); but when directed at another's domain, it is subsumed under envy (<s>asūyā</s>). Agitation (<s>udvega</s>) should be seen as subsumed appropriately under <s>nirveda</s>, <s>viṣāda</s>, and so forth. And thus the author of the <s>Bhāva-prakāśikā</s> [states]: 'If there be other states also, arising from particular mental conditions, their subsumption within the <s>vyabhicārins</s> should be recognized.' ||SRs_2.216||

body.text: vibhāvāś cānubhāvāś ca te bhavanti parasparam | 97
body.translated_text: <s>Vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions) can be reciprocal to each other.

body.text: kārya-kāraṇa-bhāvas tu jñeyaḥ prāyeṇa lokataḥ ||SRs_2.217||
body.translated_text: Their cause-and-effect relationship should be understood generally from worldly experience. ||SRs_2.217||

body.text: tathā hi-santāpasya dainyaṃ prati vibhāvatvaṃ glāniṃ pratyanubhāvatvaṃ ca | prahārasya pralaya-mohau prati vibhāvatvam augryaṃ pratyanubhāvatvaṃ ca | viṣādasya utpātāvegaṃ pratyanubhāvatṃ stambhaṃ prati vibhāvatvam | vyādher glāni-stambha-pralayādīn prati vibhāvatvam |
body.translated_text: Thus: torment has the character of a <s>vibhāva</s> toward wretchedness (<s>dainya</s>) and the character of an <s>anubhāva</s> toward debility (<s>glāni</s>). A blow has the character of a <s>vibhāva</s> toward death (<s>pralaya</s>) and stupor (<s>moha</s>), and the character of an <s>anubhāva</s> toward ferocity (<s>augrya</s>). Despondency (<s>viṣāda</s>) has the character of an <s>anubhāva</s> toward portent-caused agitation (<s>utpātāvega</s>), and the character of a <s>vibhāva</s> toward paralysis (<s>stambha</s>). Disease (<s>vyādhi</s>) has the character of a <s>vibhāva</s> toward debility (<s>glāni</s>), paralysis (<s>stambha</s>), death (<s>pralaya</s>), and the like.

body.text: svātantryāt pāratantryāc ca te dvidhā vyabhicāriṇaḥ | 98
body.translated_text: The <s>vyabhicārins</s> are of two kinds: independent (<s>svatantra</s>) and dependent (<s>paratantra</s>).

body.text:
para-poṣakatāṃ prāptāḥ paratantrā itīritāḥ |
tad-abhāve svatantrāḥ syur bhāvā iti ca te smṛtāḥ ||SRs_2.218|| 99
body.translated_text: Those that have attained the role of nourishing another [state] are called dependent; in the absence of that [subordination], they are independent — thus they are regarded as [free-standing] <s>bhāvas</s>. ||SRs_2.218||

body.text:
tatra pāratantryeṇa nirvedo, yathā-
kuryuḥ śastra-kathām amī yadi manor vaṃśe manuṣyāṅkurāḥ
syāc ced brahma-gaṇo' yam ākṛti-gaṇas tatreṣyate ced bhavān |
samrājāṃ samidhāṃ ca sādhakatamaṃ dhatte chidākāraṇaṃ
dhiṅ maurvī-kuśa-karṣaṇolbaṇa-kiṇa-granthir mamāyaṃ karaḥ ||SRs_2.219|| (a.rā. 4.44)
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>nirveda</s> in its dependent form, for example — [The verse about Paraśurāma's self-deprecation, beginning] 'If these scions of Manu's lineage were to speak of the science of weapons...' [already quoted] ||SRs_2.219|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 4.44)

body.text: ity atra nirvedasya krodhāṅgatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>nirveda</s> serves as a subordinate element of the wrathful sentiment (<s>krodha</s>).

body.text:
nirvedasya svatantratvaṃ, yathā-
prāptāḥ śriyaḥ sakala-kāma-dudhās tataḥ kiṃ
nyastaṃ padaṃ śirasi vidviṣatāṃ tataḥ kim |
sampāditāḥ praṇayino vibhavais tataḥ kiṃ
kalpaṃ sthitās tanubhṛtāṃ tanavas tataḥ kim ||SRs_2.220|| [vai.śa. 67]
body.translated_text: The independent form of <s>nirveda</s>, for example — [The verse beginning] 'Wealth that fulfills all desires has been obtained — so what?...' [already quoted] ||SRs_2.220|| (<s>Vairāgya-śataka</s> 67)

body.text: ityādi | atra nirvedasyānanyāṅgatvāt svatantratvam |
body.translated_text: And so forth. Here, since <s>nirveda</s> is not subordinate to any other [sentiment], it is independent.

body.text: nanu nirvedasya śānta-rasa-sthāyitvaṃ kaiścid uktam | tat katham asya anya-rasopakaraṇatvam iti ced, ucyate | sati khalu grāme sīmā-sambhāvanā | sthāyitvaṃ nāma saṃskāra-pāṭavena bhāvasya (vāsanā-rūpeṇa sthitasya kāraṇa-vaśād udbodhitasya) muhur muhur navībhāvaḥ | tena nirveda-vāsanā-vāsitaṃ bhāvaka-cetasi naiṣphalyābhimateṣu vibhāvādiṣu (bhāvakānāṃ prathamaṃ pravṛtter evāsambhavāt) tat-sāmagrī-phala-bhūtasya nirvedasyotpattir eva na saṅgacchate | kiṃ punaḥ sthāyitvam | kiṃ ca asati nirveda-sthāyini śānta-rūpo bhāvakānām āsvādaś citra-gata-kadalī-phala-rasāsvāda-lampaṭānāṃ rāja-śukānāṃ viveka-sahodaro bhaved iti kṛtaṃ saṃrambheṇa |
body.translated_text: Now, some have stated that <s>nirveda</s> has the status of a permanent state (<s>sthāyin</s>) of the <s>Śānta-rasa</s> (tranquil sentiment). How then can it serve as an accessory to another <s>rasa</s>? To this we reply: When a village exists, boundary-demarcation is possible. The status of <s>sthāyin</s> means: through the efficacy of habitual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), the repeated renewal of a <s>bhāva</s> that abides in the form of a latent disposition (<s>vāsanā</s>), awakened by its cause. Now, in the minds of audience-members infused with the latent disposition of <s>nirveda</s>, concerning <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like that are regarded as futile — since the initial engagement of the audience is itself impossible [in such cases] — the arising of <s>nirveda</s>, which would be the fruit of that aggregate [of causes], is simply not consistent. How much less its status as a <s>sthāyin</s>! Moreover, without <s>nirveda</s> as a <s>sthāyin</s>, the aesthetic relish in the form of <s>Śānta</s> by the audience-members would be akin to the discernment of those royal parrots who desire to taste the juice of banana fruits [painted] in a picture — so enough with this controversy.

body.text:
viṣādasya paratantratvaṃ, yathā-
vāraṃ vāraṃ tirayati dṛ;cām udgato bāṣpa-pūras
tat-saṅkalpopahita-jaḍima-stambham abhyeti gātram |
sadyaḥ svidyann ayam aviratotkampa-lolāṅgulīkaḥ
pāṇir lekhā-vidhiṣu nitarāṃ vartate kiṃ karomi ||SRs_2.221|| (mā.mā. 1.38)
body.translated_text: The dependent form of <s>viṣāda</s>, for example — [The verse about Mādhava's inability to paint, beginning] 'The flood of tears that has risen again and again blurs both my eyes...' [already quoted] ||SRs_2.221|| (<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 1.38)

body.text: atra viṣādasya śṛṅgārāṅgatvam | svatantratvaṃ, yathā-
body.translated_text: Here, <s>viṣāda</s> is a subordinate element of the erotic sentiment (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>). Its independent form, for example —

body.text:
sañcāriṇī dīpa-śikheva rātrau
yaṃ yaṃ vyatīyāya patiṃvarā sā |
narendra-mārgāṭṭa iva prapede
vivarṇa-bhāvaṃ sa sa bhūmi-pālaḥ ||SRs_2.222|| (ra.vaṃ. 6.67)
body.translated_text: As the maiden choosing a husband passed by each one, like a moving lamp-flame in the night, each king she passed was reduced to paleness, like a waterwheel [left behind]. ||SRs_2.222|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 6.67)

body.text: ity atra viṣādasyānanyāṅgatvam | evam anyeṣām api svatantratva-paratantratve tatra tatrohanīye |
body.translated_text: Here, since <s>viṣāda</s> is not subordinate to any other [sentiment], it is independent. In the same way, the independent and dependent natures of the other [vyabhicārins] should be understood in their respective contexts.

body.text: ābhāsatā bhaved eṣām anaucitya-pravartitām |

children.translated_text: Impropriety is twofold: from unreality (<s>asatyatva</s>) and from unworthiness (<s>ayogyatva</s>).

children.text: asatyatva-kṛtaṃ tat syād acetana-gataṃ tu yat ||SRs_2.223||
children.translated_text: That which is attributed to an insentient being (<s>acetana</s>) — that is caused by unreality. ||SRs_2.223||

body.translated_text: The semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of these [vyabhicārins] occurs when they are set in motion by impropriety (<s>anaucitya</s>).

children.translated_text: For example —

children.text: kas tvaṃ bhoḥ, kathayāmi daiva-hatakaṃ māṃ viddhi śākhoṭakaṃ vairāgyād iva vakṣi, sādhu viditaṃ, kasmād idaṃ, kathyate |
children.translated_text: 'Who are you, sir?' — 'Know me, the fate-stricken one, to be a <s>śākhoṭaka</s> tree.' — 'You speak as if from detachment!' — 'Well understood.' — 'Why this?' — 'Let me tell you:' —

children.text: vāmenātra vaṭas tam adhvaga-janaḥ sarvātmanā sevate na cchāyāpi paropakāra-karaṇe mārga-sthitasyāpi me ||SRs_2.224||
children.translated_text: 'Here to the left stands a banyan tree; travelers serve it with their whole being — but not even my shade [is sought], though I stand on the roadside, for rendering service to others.' ||SRs_2.224||

body.text: atra vṛkṣa-viśeṣatvād acetane śākhoṭake citta-vikārasyāsambhavānucito nirvedo' yam ābhāsatvam āpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, since the <s>śākhoṭaka</s> is a particular species of tree and therefore insentient, the impossibility of mental states in it renders this <s>nirveda</s> improper — thus it becomes a semblance (<s>ābhāsa</s>).

body.text: ayogyatva-kṛtaṃ proktaṃ nīca-tiryaṅ-narāśrayam ||SRs_2.225|| 101
body.translated_text: That which is caused by unworthiness is said to pertain to base characters, animals, or low persons. ||SRs_2.225||

children.translated_text: Of these, [ābhāsa] pertaining to a base animal, for example —
'Lay your eggs at the shore of the tide — be not anxious in mind!

children.text: māṃ jānāti samudro' yaṃ ṭiṭṭibhaṃ sāhasa-priyam ||SRs_2.226||
children.translated_text: This ocean knows me — the <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s> (sandpiper), lover of daring deeds!' ||SRs_2.226||

body.text: atra yadi samudra-velāyāṃ prasūye tarhi udvela-kallola-mālābhir mamāpatyāni hṛtāni bhaveyur iti śaṅkitāyāṃ nija-gṛhiṇyāṃ kaścit ṭiṭṭibhaḥ pakṣi-viśeṣo garvāyate | tad ayaṃ garvo nīca-tiryag-gatatvād ābhāso nātīva svadate |
body.translated_text: Here, a certain <s>ṭiṭṭibha</s>, a particular kind of bird, boasts to his wife who is anxious that if she lays her eggs at the ocean's shore, the waves might carry away her offspring. This pride, being attributed to a base animal, becomes a semblance and is not fully relished.

body.text: nīca-narāśrayo, yathā-

children.translated_text: Lying flat on his back, with the splendor of both palms serving as a pillow,
at the foot of a <s>gandhūra</s> tree, with sounds of grunts and snorts
tracking [his sleep], with long, heavy breaths, with hundreds of puffs, and lips smacked together —
thus, fatigued from agricultural labor, the lowly one sleeps. ||SRs_2.227||

body.translated_text: Pertaining to a base human, for example —

body.text:
utpatti-sandhi-śāvalya-śāntayo vyabhicāriṇām |
daśāś catasras tatra utpattir bhāva-sambhavaḥ ||SRs_2.228|| 102
body.translated_text: The four phases of the <s>vyabhicārins</s> are: arising (<s>utpatti</s>), junction (<s>sandhi</s>), complexity (<s>śāvalya</s>), and cessation (<s>śānti</s>). Of these, arising is the birth of a <s>bhāva</s>. ||SRs_2.228||

body.text:
yathā-
evaṃ vādini devarṣau pārśve pitur adhomukhī |
līlā-kamala-patrāṇi gaṇayāmāsa pārvatī ||SRs_2.229|| (ku.saṃ. 6.84)
body.translated_text: For example — While the divine sage (<s>Devarṣi</s>, <s>Nārada</s>) was thus speaking, <s>Pārvatī</s>, face lowered, at her father's side, counted the petals of a lotus held in play. ||SRs_2.229|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 6.84)

body.text: atra lajjāyāḥ harṣasya vā samutpattiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here is the arising of shame or of joy.

body.text:
sarūpam asarūpaṃ vā bhinna-kāraṇa-kalpitam |
bhāva-dvayaṃ milati cet sa sandhir iti gīyate ||SRs_2.230|| 103
body.translated_text: When two <s>bhāvas</s>, whether of the same or different kind, produced by different causes, meet together — that is called junction (<s>sandhi</s>). ||SRs_2.230||

body.text: svarūpayoḥ sandhir, yathā-

children.translated_text: When the hosts of enemies, having fallen to the ground from the sword-blows
of <s>Anapota-siṃha</s>,
have their limbs dispatched to the laps of their beloveds,
the closings of their eye-corners occur. ||SRs_2.231||

body.translated_text: Junction of two [bhāvas] of the same kind, for example —

body.text: atra nāyaka-khaḍga-prahāra-priyā-janāṅga-sparśābhyāṃ kalpitayoḥ pratināyakeṣu mohayoḥ sandhir netrānta-nimīlanena vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the junction of the two delusions (<s>moha</s>) in the antagonists — one produced by the hero's sword-blow and the other by the touch of their beloveds' bodies — is manifested through the closing of the eye-corners.

body.text: asarūpayoḥ sandhir, yathā-

children.translated_text: The bodies of the antagonists of the illustrious King <s>Siṃha-bhūpa</s>
perspire and tremble exceedingly —
when thundering sounds concordant with war-drums [are heard],
[the bodies] of those whose necks are embraced by their beloveds. ||SRs_2.232||

body.translated_text: Junction of two [bhāvas] of different kinds, for example —

body.text: atra garjiteṣu nāyaka-saṃnāha-niḥsāṇa-śaṅkayāṅkuritasya pratināyakānāṃ trāsasya priyāliṅgana-taraṅgitasya ca harṣasya sveda-vepathu-sādṛśya-kalpita-saṃśleṣaḥ sandhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, when thunder sounds, the terror (<s>trāsa</s>) of the antagonists, sprung from the suspicion that it is the sound of the hero's war-preparations, and the joy (<s>harṣa</s>) rippling from the embrace of their beloveds — the junction is the blending [of these two different bhāvas] contrived through the resemblance of their consequent expressions (perspiration and trembling).

body.text: atyārūḍhasya bhāvasya vilayaḥ śāntir ucyate ||SRs_2.233|| 104ab
body.translated_text: The dissolution of a <s>bhāva</s> that has reached its peak — that is called cessation (<s>śānti</s>). ||SRs_2.233||

body.text: yathā-

children.text: śuddhāntasya nivārito' py anunayair niḥśaṅkam aṅkūrito
children.translated_text: Though restrained by the entreaties of the inner chambers, boldly sprouted,
though checked by the counsels of aged ministers, grown further still —
the tree of excessive pride in the hostile kings is uprooted from the very root
merely by the sight of the army of King <s>Anapota-siṃha</s>. ||SRs_2.234||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra hitopadeśānādarādhirūḍhasya pratināyaka-gatasya garvasya śāntir āmūlam unmūlyata iti vāg-ārambheṇa vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the cessation of the antagonists' pride, which had mounted despite disregard of good counsel, is manifested through the verbal expression 'is uprooted from the very root.'

body.text: śavalatvaṃ tu bhāvānāṃ saṃmardaḥ syāt parasparam ||SRs_2.235|| 104
body.translated_text: The complexity (<s>śāvalya</s>) of <s>bhāvas</s> is their mutual conflict (<s>saṃmarda</s>). ||SRs_2.235||

body.text: yathā-

children.text: ko vā jeṣyati soma-vaṃśa-tilakān asmān raṇa-prāṅgaṇe
children.translated_text: 'Who shall conquer us, the ornaments of the Lunar dynasty, on the field of battle?'

children.text: hantāsmāsu parāṅmukho hata-vidhiḥ kiṃ durgam adhyāsmahe |
children.translated_text: 'Alas, fate is hostile and has turned against us! Shall we retreat to a fortress?'

children.text: asmat-pūrva-nṛpān asau nihatavān dīrghān dhig asmad-bhujān
children.translated_text: 'He has slain our former kings — fie upon our long arms!'

children.text: kiṃ vākyair anapota-siṃha-nṛpateḥ sevaiva kṛtyaṃ param ||SRs_2.236||
children.translated_text: 'What use are words? — service to King <s>Anapota-siṃha</s> is the only course!' ||SRs_2.236||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra garva-viṣādāsūyā-cintā-smṛty-amarṣa-nirveda-matīnāṃ saṃmardo bhāva-śāvalyam ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the mutual conflict of pride, despondency, envy, anxiety, recollection, indignation, self-deprecation, and resolve — that is called <s>bhāva-śāvalya</s> (complexity of states).

body.text:
dig-antarāla-sañcāra-kīrtinā siṃha-bhūbhujā |
evaṃ sañcāriṇaḥ sarve sa-prapañcaṃ nirūpitāḥ ||SRs_2.237|| 105
body.translated_text: By King <s>Siṃha-bhūbhuj</s>, whose fame traverses the quarters of space, all the <s>sañcārins</s> (transitory states) have thus been expounded in full detail. ||SRs_2.237||

body.text:
iti sañcāri-bhāvāḥ |
atha sthāyinaḥ-
body.translated_text: Thus [ends the section on] the transitory states (<s>sañcāri-bhāvas</s>). Now the permanent states (<s>sthāyins</s>) —

body.text:
sajātīyair vijātīyair bhāvair ye tv atiraskṛtāḥ |
kṣrābdhivan nayanty anyān svātmatvaṃ sthāyino hi te ||SRs_2.238|| 106
bharatena ca te kathitā rati-hāsotsāha-vismaya-krodhāḥ |
śoko' tha jugupsā bhayam ity aṣṭau lakṣma vakṣyate teṣām ||SRs_2.239|| 107
body.translated_text: The <s>Sthāyī-bhāvas</s> (permanent sentiments) are those which, though overshadowed by emotions of the same or different kind, like the milk-ocean, lead all others to [merge into] their own nature. ||SRs_2.238|| And <s>Bharata</s> has enumerated them: <s>Rati</s> (love), <s>Hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>Utsāha</s> (heroic energy), <s>Vismaya</s> (wonder), <s>Krodha</s> (anger), <s>Śoka</s> (sorrow), <s>Jugupsā</s> (disgust), and <s>Bhaya</s> (fear) — eight in total. Their characteristics will now be stated. ||SRs_2.239||

body.text:
tatra ratiḥ-
yūnor anyonya-viṣayā sthāyinīcchā ratir bhavet |
nisargeṇābhiyogena saṃsargeṇābhimānataḥ ||SRs_2.240|| 108
upamādhyātma-viṣayair eṣā syāt tatra vikriyāḥ |
kaṭākṣa-pāta-bhrū-kṣepa-priya-vāg-ādayo matāḥ ||SRs_2.241|| 109
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Rati</s> (love) — <s>Rati</s> is the permanent desire of a young couple directed toward each other. It arises from innate disposition (<s>nisarga</s>), from ardent devotion (<s>abhiyoga</s>), from association (<s>saṃsarga</s>), from self-regard (<s>abhimāna</s>), ||SRs_2.240|| from analogy (<s>upamā</s>), from inner conviction (<s>adhyātma</s>), and from sense-objects (<s>viṣaya</s>). Among these, the reactions are: casting sidelong glances, raising the eyebrows, speaking sweet words, and the like. ||SRs_2.241||

body.text: tatra nisargeṇa ratir, yathā-
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Rati</s> arising from innate disposition, for example —

body.text:
alaṃ vivādena yathā śrutas tvayā
tathāvidhas tāvad aśeṣam astu saḥ |
mamātra bhāvaika-rasaṃ manaḥ sthitaṃ
na kāma-vṛttir vacanīyam īkṣate ||SRs_2.242|| (ku.saṃ. 5.82)
body.translated_text: 'Enough of dispute! Let him be entirely as you have heard. My mind here is fixed on the sole essence of emotion — it does not regard what is dictated by desire as [worthy of] censure.' ||SRs_2.242|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 5.82)

body.text: atra rūpādi-dṛṣṭa-kāraṇa-nirapekṣā pārvatyāḥ ratir janmāntara-vāsanā-rūpā nisargād eva bhavati | abhiyogo' bhiniveśaḥ | tad-eka-paratvam iti yāvat |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Pārvatī</s>'s love, independent of any perceived cause such as beauty, is in the form of latent impressions from a previous birth — arising from innate disposition (<s>nisarga</s>) alone. <s>Abhiyoga</s> means passionate devotion — i.e., single-minded attachment.

body.text:
tena, yathā-
tan me manaḥ kṣipati yat sarasa-prahāram
ālokya mām agaṇita-skhalad-uttarīyā |
trastaika-hāyana-kuraṅga-vilola-dṛṣṭiḥ
sāśliṣṭavaty amṛta-saṃvalitair ivāṅgaiḥ ||SRs_2.243|| (mā.mā. 4.8)
body.translated_text: Through that [devotion], for example — 'That [sight] captivates my mind — seeing me [dealing] a vigorous blow, she, her upper garment slipping unheeded, with a glance restless like a startled one-year-old deer, embraced [me] with limbs as if suffused with nectar.' ||SRs_2.243|| (<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 4.8)

body.text: atrottarīya-skhalanādi-sūcitena madayantikā-premābhiyogena makarandasya tatra ratir utpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Makaranda</s>'s love arises through <s>Madayantikā</s>'s passionate devotion indicated by the slipping of her upper garment and such signs.

body.text:
saṃsargeṇa, yathā-
utpattir deva-yajanād brahma-vādī nṛpaḥ pitā |
suprasannojjvalā mūrtir asyāṃ snehaṃ karoti me ||SRs_2.244|| (ma.vī.ca. 1.21)
body.translated_text: From association, for example — 'Born of a divine sacrifice, her father is a Vedic sage and king. Her form is resplendent and serene — she inspires affection in me.' ||SRs_2.244|| (<s>Mahāvīra-carita</s> 1.21)

body.text: atra deva-yajana-janakādi-sambandha-gauraveṇa sītāyāṃ rāmasya ratiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Rāma</s>'s love for <s>Sītā</s> arises through the prestige of her association with a divine sacrifice, <s>Janaka</s>, and such connections.

body.text:
atha abhimāṇaḥ | idam eva mama priyaṃ nānyad ity abhiprāyo' bhimānaḥ | tena, yathā-
jagati jayinas te te bhāvā navendu-kalādayaḥ
prakṛti-madhurāḥ santy evānye mano madayanti ye | mama tu yad iyaṃ yātā loke vilocana-candrikā
nayana-viṣayaṃ janmany ekaḥ sa eva mahotsavaḥ ||SRs_2.245|| (mā.mā. 1.39)
body.translated_text: Now <s>Abhimāna</s> (self-regard) — the conviction that 'this alone is my beloved, none other' is <s>abhimāna</s>. Through that, for example — 'In this world, victorious are those new-moon-crescent-like sentiments and other such things; and there exist other naturally charming things that intoxicate the mind. But for me, since she — the moonlight of the eyes — has appeared in this world, that alone is the one great festival for my eyes in this birth.' ||SRs_2.245|| (<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 1.39)

body.text: atra mādhavasya vilcana-candrikā-nayana-mahotsavādy-abhimānena itara-ramaṇīya-vastu-naiḥspṛhyeṇa ca mālatyāṃ ratiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Mādhava</s>'s love for <s>Mālatī</s> arises through the self-regard of calling her 'the moonlight of the eyes' and 'the festival of vision,' and through indifference to all other charming objects.

body.text:
upamayā, yathā-
api turaga-samīpād utpatantaṃ mayūraṃ
na sa rucira-kalāpaṃ bāṇa-lakṣyīcakāra |
sapadi gata-manaskaś citra-mālyānukīrṇe
rati-vigalita-bandhe keśa-pāśe priyāyāḥ ||SRs_2.246|| (ra.vaṃ. 9.67)
body.translated_text: Through analogy, for example — 'He did not even aim his arrow at the peacock, with its beautiful plumage, flying up from near the horse; his mind having at once gone to the tresses of his beloved — their bond loosened by love-play — scattered with colorful flower-garlands, [which resembled the peacock's tail].' ||SRs_2.246|| (<s>Raghu-vaṃśa</s> 9.67)

body.text: atra mṛgayāntaritāpi daśarathasya priyā-viṣayā ratis tadīya-keśa-kalāpa-sadṛśa-keki-kalāpa-darśanenotpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, even while engaged in hunting, <s>Daśaratha</s>'s love directed toward his beloved arises upon seeing the peacock's plumage, which resembles the tresses of his beloved.

body.text:
adhyātmaṃ svātma-prāmāṇya-mātram | tena, yathā-
kāmaṃ pratyādiṣṭāṃ smarāmi na parigrahaṃ munes tanayān |
balavat tu dūyamānaṃ pratyāyayatīva me hṛdayam ||SRs_2.247|| (śaku. 5.31)
body.translated_text: <s>Adhyātma</s> (inner conviction) means merely the authority of one's own heart. Through that, for example — 'I certainly do not remember having married the daughter of the sage, [though she was] repudiated. But my heart, burning intensely, seems to persuade me [otherwise].' ||SRs_2.247|| (<s>Śakuntalā</s> 5.31)

body.text: atra duṣyantasya nija-citta-santāpa-pratyayena śāpa-vismṛtāyām api śakuntalāyāṃ ratiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Duṣyanta</s>'s love for <s>Śakuntalā</s>, even though forgotten through a curse, is [established] through the evidence of his own heart's anguish.

body.text: viṣayāḥ śabdādayaḥ | tatra śabdena, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: 'O friend, for me, struck down by fate,
let the sight of him be or not be —
if only that sound of the flute
were to fall again upon the pathway of my ears, that alone would suffice.' ||SRs_2.248||

body.translated_text: <s>Viṣayas</s> (sense-objects) are sound and the like. Among these, through sound, as [composed] by me —
