body.text: atra prāg-adṛṣṭe' pi kṛṣṇe veṇu-nādena kāmavallyā ratiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Kāmavallī</s>'s love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, even though not previously seen, arises through the sound of his flute.

body.text:
sparśena, yathā-
yad ayaṃ ratha-saṅkṣobhād aṃsenāṃso rathāṅga-suśroṇyāḥ |
spṛṣṭaḥ saroma-vikriyam aṅkuritaṃ manobhaveneva ||SRs_2.249|| (vi.u. 1.11)
body.translated_text: Through touch, for example — 'When, from the jostling of the chariot, his shoulder touched the shoulder of the one with chariot-wheel-round hips — [her body] sprouted a change of horripilation, as if from the God of Love himself.' ||SRs_2.249|| (<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 1.11)

body.text: rūpeṇa, yathā-

children.text: ayaṃ rāmo nāyaṃ sa tu janaka-dharmaṃ dalitavān
children.translated_text: 'Is this <s>Rāma</s>? No, not he — for he broke the bow of <s>Janaka</s>'s lineage.

children.text: ayaṃ kāmo nāyaṃ sa tu madhumadāmodita-manāḥ |
children.translated_text: Is this <s>Kāma</s> (the God of Love)? No — for his mind is intoxicated by the fragrance of honey.
O friend, I know — he is the very fruit of the creation of the eyes of young women,
the origin of good fortune — the illustrious <s>Siṃha-kṣitipati</s> is indeed victorious!' ||SRs_2.250||

body.translated_text: Through form, for example —

body.text: atra rāmādi-smaraṇa-hetunā nāyaka-rūpātiśayena kasyāścid ratiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, a certain woman's love arises through the surpassing beauty of the hero, which causes the remembrance of <s>Rāma</s> and others.

body.text:
rasena, yathā-
haras tu kiñcit parilupta-dhairyaś
candrodayārambha ivāmburāśiḥ |
umā-mukhe bimba-phalādharoṣṭhe
vyāpārayāmāsa vilocanāni ||SRs_2.251|| (ku.saṃ. 3.67)
body.translated_text: Through taste, for example — '<s>Hara</s> (Śiva), his composure somewhat diminished, like the ocean at the commencement of moonrise, fixed his eyes upon the <s>bimba</s>-fruit-red lower lip of <s>Umā</s>'s face.' ||SRs_2.251|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.67)

body.text: atra yadyapi sambhogāt prāg-ajñātasyādhara-rasasya rasaṃ prati vibhāvatā na saṅgacchate, tathāpi prasiddehḥ sambhāvitasya rasasyaiva vibhāvatvaṃ bimba-phalādharoṣṭha iti padena vyajyate | athavā samāsvādita-dākṣāyaṇī-bimbādharasya parameśvarasya tad-rasenaiva jananāntara-saṅgatāyām api tasyāṃ ratiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, although the taste of her lower lip was unknown before union, the <s>vibhāva</s> status of the well-known, expected taste is suggested by the word '<s>bimba</s>-fruit-lipped.' Alternatively, for <s>Parameśvara</s> (Śiva), who had previously tasted the <s>bimba</s> lip of <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> (his former wife), love for her — even [now] met in another birth — arises through that very taste.

body.text: gandhena, yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: 'Attended at every step, with hopeful expectation, by swarms of restless bees
who have taken a vow of putting to shame the fragrance of freshly blooming <s>mālatī</s> flowers,
the natural fragrance emanating from the <s>campaka</s>-radiant limbs of this fawn-eyed one —

children.text: nāmodo' yam adṛṣṭa-pūrva-mahimā badhnāti me mānasam ||SRs_2.252||
children.translated_text: this fragrance of unprecedented power captivates my mind.' ||SRs_2.252||

body.translated_text: Through scent, as [composed] by me —

body.text: atra parāśara-muni-prasādena labdhena divyena satyavatī-śarīra-saurabheṇa śantanos tasyāṃ ratiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Śantanu</s>'s love for <s>Satyavatī</s> arises through the divine bodily fragrance obtained by the grace of the sage <s>Parāśara</s>.

body.text: bhojas tu samprayogeṇa ratim anyām udāharat ||SRs_2.253|| 110a
body.translated_text: <s>Bhoja</s>, however, has cited union (<s>samprayoga</s>) as another [source] of love. ||SRs_2.253||

body.text:
yathā-
unnamayya sakaca-graham oṣṭhaṃ
cumbati priyatame haṭha-vṛttyā |
huṃ huṃ muñca ma ma meti ca mandaṃ
jalpitaṃ jayati bāla-vadhūnām ||SRs_2.254|| (vijjikāyā idam iti subhāṣitāvaliḥ)
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'When the most beloved one lifts [her] lip by pulling her hair and kisses forcefully, the slow murmuring of young brides — "Humph, humph! Let go! Don't! Don't!" — is victorious!' ||SRs_2.254|| (This is attributed to <s>Vijjikā</s> in <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s>.)

body.text: vākṛtaṃ ca tenaiva | atra tarjanārthamokṣaṇārtha-vāraṇārthāṇāṃ mandaṃ maṇdaṃ prayogān mānavatyāḥ samprayoge raty-utpattiḥ pratīyata iti |
body.translated_text: This [position] was also rejected by him [<s>Siṃhabhūpāla</s>]. Here, through the gradual, slow use of words for threatening, releasing, and forbidding, the arising of love during union of the sulking woman is understood, thus —

body.text: samprayogasya śabdādiṣv antarbhāvān na tan-matam ||SRs_2.255|| 110
body.translated_text: Since union (<s>samprayoga</s>) is subsumed under sound and the other [sense-objects], that view is not [separately] accepted. ||SRs_2.255||

body.text: tathā hi-uktodāharaṇe mānavatī-jalpitasya śabda-rūpatvam eva | tathā ca-
body.translated_text: For indeed, in the cited example, the murmuring of the sulking woman is itself of the nature of sound. And likewise —

body.text:
āarapasārioṭṭhaṃ aghaḍiaṇāsaṃ acuṃbiaṇiḍākaṃ |
baṇṇaghialippamuhie tīe paricumbaṇaṃ bharimo ||SRs_2.256|| (gāthā 1.22)
body.translated_text: 'With lips extended in eagerness, with unfitting nose, with unkissed forehead,

children.translated_text: [Chāyā translation:] With lips extended in eagerness, with nose not [properly] joined, with forehead unkissed,
we remember the kissing of that one whose face was smeared with turmeric-paste.' ||SRs_2.256|| (<s>Gāthā</s> 1.22)

body.text: ity ādiṣu cumbanādīnām api sparśeṣv antar-bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: In these and similar [examples], even kissing and the like are subsumed under touch among the sense-objects.

body.text: atha raty-avasthāḥ
body.translated_text: Now the states of <s>Rati</s> (love)

body.text:
aṅkura-pallava-kalikā-praspunaphalabhoga-bhāg iyaṃ kramaśaḥ |
premā mānaḥ praṇayaḥ sneho rāgo' nurāgaś ca ||SRs_2.257|| 111
body.translated_text: — This [<s>Rati</s>] partakes successively of the stages of sprout, leaf, bud, blossom, fruit, and enjoyment: [namely] <s>Premā</s> (affection), <s>Māna</s> (pride), <s>Praṇaya</s> (tender regard), <s>Sneha</s> (attachment), <s>Rāga</s> (passion), and <s>Anurāga</s> (deep passion). ||SRs_2.257||

body.text:
atha premā-
sa premā bheda-rahitaṃ yūnor yad bhāva-bandhanaṃ ||SRs_2.258|| 112a
body.translated_text: Now <s>Premā</s> (affection) — <s>Premā</s> is the undivided emotional bond between a young couple. ||SRs_2.258||

body.text:
yathā-
rathāṅga-nāmnor iva bhāva-bandhanaṃ
babhūva yat prema parasparāśrayam |
vibhaktam apy eka-sutena tat tayoḥ
parasparasyopari paryacīyata ||SRs_2.259|| (raghu. 3.24)
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'The mutual love of those two, like that of a pair of <s>Cakravāka</s> birds, was an emotional bond dependent on each other. Though divided by the birth of one son, each one's [love] accumulated even more upon the other.' ||SRs_2.259|| (<s>Raghu-vaṃśa</s> 3.24)

body.text: atra bheda-kāraṇe suta-snehe saty api sudakṣiṇā-dilīpayo rater aparihāṇena bheda-rahitatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, even though the son's affection could be a cause for division, the love of <s>Sudakṣiṇā</s> and <s>Dilīpa</s> remains undivided — this demonstrates its indivisible nature.

body.text: [keṣucit lipiṣu idam udāharaṇam atra dṛśyate-
body.translated_text: [In some manuscripts, this example appears here —

children.translated_text: 'For the two long separated, whose bodies have grown limp from the agony of longing,

children.text: navam iva jagaj jātaṃ bhūyaś cirād abhinandatoḥ |
children.translated_text: meeting again after so long, the world seemed born anew, as they rejoiced once more;

children.text: katham api dine dīrghe yāte niśām adhirūḍhayoḥ
children.translated_text: when somehow the long day had passed and the night was entered,

children.text: prasarati kathā bahvī yūnor yathā na tathā ratiḥ || (amaru. 39)]
children.translated_text: much conversation flowed between the young couple, but not so much love-making.' ||(<s>Amaru</s> 39)]

body.text: atha mānaḥ-

children.translated_text: That which, through an emotional bond of love, from a sense of independence, [becomes] heart-touching

children.text: bahnāti bhāva-kauṭilyaṃ so' yaṃ māna itīryate ||SRs_2.260||
children.translated_text: and exhibits crookedness of emotion — that is called <s>Māna</s> (love-pride). ||SRs_2.260||

body.translated_text: Now <s>Māna</s> (love-pride) —

body.text:
yathā-
vyapohituṃ locanato mukhānilair
apārayantaṃ kila puṣpajaṃ rajaḥ |
payodhareṇorasi kācid unmanāḥ
priyaṃ jaghānonnata-pīvara-stanī ||SRs_2.261|| (kirāṭa 8.19)
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'Unable to dispel the pollen of love-born [flowers] from her eyes with the breezes of her face, a certain woman with full, upraised breasts, transported in mind, struck her beloved with her breast upon his chest.' ||SRs_2.261|| (<s>Kirātārjunīya</s> 8.19)

body.text: atrāparādha-sambhāvanāyām api prema-kalpita-svātantryeṇa avajñā-rūpaṃ citta-kauṭilyam |
body.translated_text: Here, even though an offense is suspected, there is the crookedness of heart in the form of contempt, arising from the independence produced by love.

body.text: [keṣucit lipiṣu idam udāharaṇam atra dṛśyate-
body.translated_text: [In some manuscripts, this example appears here —

children.translated_text: 'Abandon your anger, O [woman] of causeless [jealous] eyes!
I have bowed before the twilight, nothing more.
Do you not know your own husband, who follows the same <s>dharma</s>,
to be of the same conduct as a <s>Cakravāka</s> bird?' ||(<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.57)]

body.text: atha praṇayaḥ-

children.translated_text: That which, through outward and inner courtesies devised by love and pride,

children.text: badhnāti bhāva-viśrambhaṃ so' yaṃ praṇaya ucyate ||SRs_2.262||
children.translated_text: produces an intimate trust (<s>viśrambha</s>) of emotion — that is called <s>Praṇaya</s>. ||SRs_2.262||

body.translated_text: Now <s>Praṇaya</s> (tender regard) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'When the beloved is about to declare the gambling-wager promised to her companions,
with furrowed brows,
she clasps his neck with both hands
and covers his mouth with her own cheek.' ||SRs_2.263||

body.translated_text: As [illustrated] —

body.text: atra bhāva-bandhanāparādha-kauṭilyayor anuvṛttau kaṇṭhālambanādinopacāreṇa visrambhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, while the emotional bond and the crookedness of offense continue, through courtesies such as clasping the neck, intimate trust is [produced].

body.text: [keṣucit lipiṣu idam udāharaṇam atra dṛśyate-
body.translated_text: [In some manuscripts, this example appears here —

children.translated_text: 'Why is her garment-hem tightly fastened by her girdle?' —

children.text: mugdhākṣī svapitīti tat-parijanaṃ svairaṃ priye pṛcchati |
children.translated_text: [he] casually asks her attendants, 'Is the innocent-eyed one asleep?'

children.text: mātaḥ svaptum apīha vārayati mām ity āhita-krodhayā
children.translated_text: 'Mother, she won't even let me sleep here!' — [the wife, pretending] anger,

children.text: paryasya svapana-cchalena śayane datto' vakāśas tayā || (amaru. 18)]
children.translated_text: turning over under the pretext of sleep on the bed, gave him entry.' ||(<s>Amaru</s> 18)]

body.text: atha snehaḥ-

children.translated_text: When trust has reached its utmost limit, and from seeing [the beloved] and such,

children.text: yatra dravaty antaraṅgaṃ sa sneha iti kathyate ||SRs_2.264||
children.translated_text: the inner heart melts — that is called <s>Sneha</s> (attachment). ||SRs_2.264||

body.translated_text: Now <s>Sneha</s> (attachment) —

body.text: darśanena, yathā kandarpa-sambhave-
body.translated_text: Through seeing, as in <s>Kandarpa-sambhava</s> —

children.translated_text: 'Then the hearts of both [of them],
traversed by warm sighs,
were led to a state of melting by the craftsman of passion (<s>Anurāga</s>),
by the very heat of their mutual love, as if making them one.' ||SRs_2.265||

body.text: atra lakṣmī-nārāyaṇayor anyonya-darśanenāntaḥ-karaṇa-dravībhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, through the mutual seeing of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, there is a melting of the inner heart.

body.text:
sparśanena, yathā-
gāḍhāliṅgana-vāmanīkṛta-kuca-prodbhinna-romodgamā
sāndra-sneha-rasātireka-vigalat-śrīman-nitambāmbarā |
mā mā mānada māti mām alam iti kṣāmākṣarollāpinī
suptā kiṃ nu mṛtā nu kiṃ manasi me līnā vilīnā nu kim ||SRs_2.266|| (amaru 36)
body.translated_text: Through touch, for example — 'With horripilation sprouting from breasts compressed by tight embrace, with the garment on her splendid hips slipping from the excess of dense affection, murmuring with languid eyes "Don't, don't, O honorable one, don't embrace me so, enough!" — is she asleep, or dead, or absorbed in my mind, or dissolved?' ||SRs_2.266|| (<s>Amaru</s> 36)

body.text: sa tredhā kathyate prauḍha-madhya-manda-vibhedataḥ | 115
body.translated_text: This [<s>Sneha</s>] is said to be of three kinds, distinguished as intense (<s>prauḍha</s>), moderate (<s>madhya</s>), and mild (<s>manda</s>).

body.text:
pravāsādibhir ajñāta-citta-vṛttau priye jane |
itara-kleśa-kārī yaḥ sa prauḍhaḥ sneha ucyate ||SRs_2.267|| 116
body.translated_text: When the beloved's mental state is unknown due to travel and the like, the [attachment] that causes suffering to the other — that is called intense <s>Sneha</s> (attachment). ||SRs_2.267||

body.text:
yathā-
etasmān māṃ kuśalinam abhijñāna-dānād viditvā
mā kaulīnād asita-nayane mayy aviśvāsinī bhūḥ |
snehān āhuḥ kim api virahe dhvaṃsinas te tv abhogād
iṣṭe vastuny upacita-rasāḥ prema-rāśī bhavanti ||SRs_2.268|| [me.dū. 2.52]
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'Having recognized me as well from this token of recognition, O dark-eyed one, do not from nobility of birth be distrustful of me. They say that in separation, affections are somehow destroyed — but toward a cherished object, [affections] accumulated with feeling become heaps of love.' ||SRs_2.268|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 2.52]

body.text: atra proṣite yakṣe sneha-janitayā tad-anyāsaṅga-śaṅkayā janitaḥ priyā-kleśaḥ mayy aviśvāsinī mā bhūr iti pratyāśvāsanena vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, while the <s>Yakṣa</s> is away, the suffering of his beloved caused by the suspicion of his attachment to another, born of affection, is revealed through the reassurance 'do not be distrustful of me.'

body.text:
atha madhyamaḥ-
itarānubhavāpekṣāṃ sahate yaḥ sa madhyamaḥ ||SRs_2.269|| 117a
body.translated_text: Now the moderate [<s>Sneha</s>] — that which tolerates the expectation of another's experience is the moderate [attachment]. ||SRs_2.269||

body.text:
yathā-
kiṃ devyāḥ kṛta-dīrgha-roṣa-muṣita-snigdha-smitaṃ tan-mukhaṃ
kiṃ vā sāgarikāṃ kramoddhata-ruṣā santarjyamānāṃ tathā |
baddhvā nītam ito vasantakam ahaṃ kiṃ cintayāmy adya bhoḥ
sarvākāra-kṛta-vyathaḥ kṣaṇam api prāpnomi no nirvṛtim ||SRs_2.270|| (ratnā. 3.19)
body.translated_text: As [illustrated] — 'What [do I think of]? The Queen's face, its tender smile stolen by prolonged anger? Or <s>Sāgarikā</s>, being threatened by her anger rising in sequence? <s>Vasantaka</s>, who was seized and brought away? What am I to think of today, alas — afflicted in every way, I do not attain peace even for a moment!' ||SRs_2.270|| (<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 3.19)

body.text: atra sāgarikānubhavāpekṣayā rāja-sneho vāsavadattāyāṃ madhyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, in comparison with <s>Sāgarikā</s>'s experience, the king's affection toward <s>Vāsavadattā</s> is middling.

body.text: atha mandaḥ-

children.text: dvayor ekasya mānādau tad anyasya karoti yaḥ | 117
children.translated_text: When, during the pride or such [behavior] of one of two [beloved ones], he who

children.text: naivopekṣāṃ na cāpekṣāṃ sa sneho manda ucyate ||270||
children.translated_text: shows neither neglect nor attention to the other — that affection is called mild (<s>manda</s>). ||2.270||

body.translated_text: Now, the mild [affection] —

body.text:
yathā-
manye priyāhṛtamanās tasyāḥ praṇipāta-laṅghanaṃ sevām |
evaṃ hi praṇayavatī sā śakyam upekṣituṃ kupitā ||SRs_2.271|| (mā.a.mi. 3.23)
body.translated_text: For example — 'I think [he], whose mind is captivated by his beloved, regards her prostrations as [mere] service; for thus the affectionate one [can] be disregarded only when she is angry.' ||2.271|| (<s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 3.23)

body.text: atra kupitāyām irāvatyām upekṣāpekṣābhāvasya kathanena rājñaḥ snehas tad-viṣayo mandaḥ | ādi-śabdād atiparicayādayaḥ | yathā-
body.translated_text: Here, by the statement of the absence of both neglect and attention toward the angered <s>Irāvatī</s>, the king's affection toward her is [shown as] mild. The word 'and so forth' [implies] excessive familiarity, etc. For example —

body.text: yaḥ kaumāra-haraḥ sa eva hi varas tā eva caitra-kṣapās

children.translated_text: those are the very same breezes heavy with the fragrance of blossoming <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), laden with <s>kadamba</s>;
and I am the very same [woman] — yet, in the matter of love-play's artful sport,
my heart yearns for the bank of the <s>Revā</s>, beneath the reed-cane tree. ||2.272||

body.translated_text: He who stole my virginity is indeed the very same bridegroom; those are the very same moonlit nights of <s>Caitra</s>;

body.text: atra kasyāścit svairiṇyā gṛhiṇītva-paricayena pati-daśāṃ prāpte' pi jāre upekṣāpekṣayor abhāva-kathanān mandaḥ snehaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, a certain self-willed woman (<s>svairiṇī</s>), though her paramour has attained the status of husband through the familiarity of married life, expresses neither neglect nor attention — hence this is mild affection.

body.text: atha rāgaḥ-

children.text: duḥkham apy adhikaṃ citte sukhatvenaiva rajyate | 118
children.translated_text: That which, through the intensity of affection, causes even excess suffering

children.text: yena sneha-prakarṣeṇa sa rāga iti gīyate ||SRs_2.273||
children.translated_text: to appear as pleasure in the mind — that is celebrated as <s>Rāga</s> (passion). ||2.273||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Rāga</s> (passion) —

body.text: kusumbha-nīlī-mañjiṣṭha-rāga-bhedena sa tridhā | 119
body.translated_text: It is threefold, by the distinction of <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower), <s>nīlī</s> (indigo), and <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder) [dyes].

body.text:
kusumbha-rāgaḥ sa jñeyo yaś citte rajyati kṣaṇāt |
atiprakāśamāno' pi kṣaṇād eva vinaśyati ||SRs_2.274|| 120
body.translated_text: <s>Kusumbha-rāga</s> is that which colors the mind instantly, and though exceedingly bright, perishes in an instant. ||2.274||

body.text:
yathā-
bahu-ballahassa jā hoi ballahā kahabi pañjadi ahāiṃ |
sā kiṃ chaṭṭhaṃ maggaī katto miṭṭhaṃ a bahuaṃ a ||SRs_2.275|| (gāthā 1.72)
body.translated_text: [Prakrit:] She who becomes the beloved of one who has many beloveds — for barely five days — does she seek a sixth [day]? Whence [can one have] both sweetness and abundance? ||2.275|| (<s>Gāthā-saptaśatī</s> 1.72)

children.text: [bahu-vallabhasya yā bhavati vallabhā katham api pañca-divasāni |
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] She who becomes the beloved of one who has many beloveds — for barely five days —

children.text: sā kiṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ mṛgayate kuto mṛṣṭaṃ ca bahukaṃ ca ||]
children.translated_text: does she seek a sixth? Whence both sweetness and abundance?

body.text: nīlī-rāgas tu yaḥ sakto nāpaiti na ca dīpyate ||SRs_2.276|| 121a
body.translated_text: <s>Nīlī-rāga</s> is that which, once attached, neither departs nor shines forth. ||2.276||

body.text:
yathā-
yadaiva pūrve janane śarīraṃ
sā dakṣa-roṣāt sudatī sasarja |
tadā-prabhṛty eva vimukta-saṅgaḥ
patiḥ paśūnām aparigraho' bhūt ||SRs_2.277|| (ku.saṃ. 3.53)
body.translated_text: For example — 'From the very moment when in a former birth that beautiful-toothed one (<s>Satī</s>) cast off her body out of anger at <s>Dakṣa</s>, from that time onward, the Lord of Creatures (<s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Śiva</s>), free from attachment, remained without a consort.' ||2.277|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.53)

body.text: atra paśupati-citta-rāgaḥ satī-saṅgamābhāva-niścayenāpi nāpaiti | viṣayābhāvān na prakāśate ca |
body.translated_text: Here, the passion in <s>Paśupati</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) mind does not depart even from the certainty of the impossibility of union with <s>Satī</s>; and due to the absence of its object, it does not manifest either.

body.text: acireṇaiva saṃsaktaś cirād api na naśyati | 121
body.translated_text: That which, once attached even briefly, does not perish even after a long time,

body.text: atīva śobhate yo' sau māñjiṣṭho rāga ucyate ||SRs_2.278||
body.translated_text: and which shines forth exceedingly — that is called <s>mañjiṣṭha-rāga</s> (madder-passion). ||2.278||

body.text:
yathā-
advaitaṃ sukha-duḥkhayor anugataṃ sarvāsv avasthāsu yad
viśrāmo hṛdayasya yatra jarasā yasminn ahāryo rasaḥ |
kālenāvaraṇātyayāt pariṇate yat sneha-sāre sthitaṃ
bhadraṃ tasya sumānuṣasya katham apy ekaṃ hi tat prāpyate ||SRs_2.279|| (u.rā.ca. 1.38)
body.translated_text: For example — 'That which is the identity of joy and sorrow followed [through all circumstances], that which is the repose of the heart in all states, that in which the relish is not stolen away by old age, that which remains when the essence of affection has matured through time and the removal of veils — that blessed state of the truly human — somehow, that one thing alone is attained.' ||2.279|| (<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 1.38)

body.text: rāga eva svayaṃ vedya-daśā-prāptyā prakāśitaḥ | 122
body.translated_text: When <s>Rāga</s> (passion) itself, having reached the stage of being self-experienced, is manifested,

body.text: yāvad-āśraya-vṛttiś ced anurāga itīritaḥ ||279||
body.translated_text: and when it operates as long as the substrate [body] exists — then it is called <s>Anurāga</s> (deep love). ||2.279||

children.translated_text: For example, by me [the author] —
'With unceasing horripilation, incessant perspiration, unbroken trembling,
with perpetually half-closed eye-corners — I behold that inseparable couple.' ||2.280||

body.text: atra pārvatī-parameśvarayo ratiḥ śarīraikya-sambandhena yāvad-āśraya-vṛttiḥ anubhūta-sarva-rāgopaplavatayā sva-saṃvedya-daśā-prakāśita-nitya-bhoga-rūpā aśrānta-romāñcādibhir anubhāvair vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the love (<s>rati</s>) of <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), operating as long as their substrate exists by virtue of their bodily unity, manifested in the self-experienced state through the subsidence of all forms of passion, is expressed through the <s>anubhāvas</s> of unceasing horripilation and the like, as eternal enjoyment.

body.text: anye prītiṃ rater bhedm āmananti na tan-matam | 123
body.translated_text: Others consider <s>Prīti</s> (affection) as a subdivision of <s>Rati</s> (love); that is not our view.

body.text: asamprayoga-viṣayā seyaṃ harṣān na bhidyate ||280||
body.translated_text: This [<s>Prīti</s>], having as its object non-sexual union, is not different from <s>Harṣa</s> (joy). ||2.280||

body.text: atha hāsaḥ-

children.translated_text: From the distortion of speech, appearance, dress,

children.text: laulyādeś ca parasthānām eṣām anukṛter api ||SRs_2.281||
children.translated_text: and action, as well as from the fickleness and the like of others, and from the imitation of these, ||2.281||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Hāsa</s> (laughter) —

body.text: vikāraś cetaso hāsas tatra ceṣṭāḥ samīritāḥ | 125
body.translated_text: the transformation of the mind is <s>Hāsa</s> (laughter). The actions therein are stated to be:

body.text: dṛṣṭer vikāro nāmauṣṭha-kapola-spandanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.282||
body.translated_text: distortion of the glance, quivering of the nose, lips, and cheeks, and the like. ||2.282||

body.text: bhāṣā-vikāro bhāṣaṇāsambaddhatvādiḥ | ākṛti-vikṛtir ativāmana-danturatvādiḥ | veṣa-vikāro viruddhālaṅkāra-kalpanā | kriyā-vikāro vikaṭa-gatitvādiḥ | eṣām udāharaṇāni kaiśikyāṃ śuddha-hāsyaje narmaṇi nirūpitāni draṣṭavyāni |
body.translated_text: Distortion of speech means incoherence and such. Distortion of appearance means extreme dwarfishness, protruding teeth, and such. Distortion of dress means incongruous ornamentation. Distortion of action means grotesque gait, etc. Examples of these are to be seen in the section on <s>Narma</s> (humor) born of pure comedy in the <s>Kaiśikī</s> [mode].

body.text:
laulyād, yathā-
bāleya-taṇḍula-vilopa-kadarthitābhir
etābhir agni-śaraṇeṣu sadharmiṇībhiḥ |
utrāsahetum api daṇḍam udasyamānam
āghrātum icchati mṛge munayo hasanti ||SRs_2.283|| (a.rā. 2.20)
body.translated_text: From fickleness, for example — 'The sages laugh at the deer who, tormented by these [children] who pilfer rice-balls mixed with <s>bāleya</s> (banana?), their fellow-dwellers at the fire-sanctuaries, wish to sniff the very staff raised to frighten them.' ||2.283|| (<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 2.20)

body.text: atra mṛgāṇāṃ santrāsana-yaṣṭi-samāghrāṇa-laulyena munīnāṃ hāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the sages laugh at the fickleness of the deer in sniffing the rod meant to frighten them.

body.text:
purānukaraṇena, yathā-
pi pi priya sa sa svayaṃ mu mu mukhāsavaṃ dehi me
ta ta tyaja du du drutaṃ bha bha bha bhājanaṃ kāñcanam |
iti skhalita-jalpitaṃ mada-vaśāt kuraṅgīdṛśaḥ
prage hasita-hetave sahacarībhir adhyaiyata ||SRs_2.284|| (sa.ka.ā.)
body.translated_text: From imitation, for example — '"Pi pi, dear one, yo you your-self, gi gi give me the nectar of your lips, le le leave, qui qui quickly, ta ta take the go go golden vessel!" — thus her stammering speech, caused by intoxication, the doe-eyed woman's [words], at dawn were studied by her companions as a source of laughter.' ||2.284|| (<s>Sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇa</s>)

body.text: atha utsāhaḥ-

children.translated_text: The mental activity that is a readiness for praiseworthy deeds,

children.text: satvarā mānasī vṛttir utsāhas tatra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.285||
children.translated_text: aided by power, composure, allies, and such — that is <s>Utsāha</s> (enthusiasm). The actions therein are: ||2.285||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) —

body.text: kālādyavekṣaṇaṃ dhairyaṃ vāg-ārambhādayo' pi ca | 127
body.translated_text: consideration of time and such [factors], composure, speech-modes, and the like.

body.text: sahajāhārya-bhedena sa dvidhā paribhāṣyate ||SRs_2.286||
body.translated_text: It is declared to be twofold by the distinction of innate (<s>sahaja</s>) and acquired (<s>āhārya</s>). ||2.286||

body.text: śaktyā sahajotsāho, yathā-

children.translated_text: Then <s>Hanumān</s> ascended the great mountain <s>Mahendra</s>
in order to leap across the ocean,
knowing from the throbbing of his auspicious right eye
that the accomplishment of <s>Rāghava</s>'s mission was already in hand. ||2.287||

body.translated_text: Innate enthusiasm from [natural] power, for example —

body.text: sa eva dhairyeṇa, yathā-

children.text: śaktyā vakṣasi magnayā saha mayā mūḍhe plavaṅgādhipe
children.translated_text: 'O foolish lord of monkeys! When the <s>Śakti</s> (spear) was lodged in my chest, along with me,

children.text: nidrāṇeṣu ca vidravatsu kapiṣu prāptāvakāśe dviṣi |
children.translated_text: when the monkeys were asleep and others had fled, when the enemy had seized the opportunity —
did you not hear the words uttered on the battlefield by the son of <s>Sumitrā</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>),

children.text: saumitrer adhiyuddha-bhūmi gaditā vācas tvayā na śrutāḥ ||SRs_2.288||
children.translated_text: of mighty and firm self-composure, who restrained the monkey-warriors [saying] "Fear not!"?' ||2.288||

body.translated_text: The same [innate enthusiasm] with composure, for example —

body.text: atra rāvaṇa-śakti-prahāreṇa kṣīṇa-śakter api lakṣmaṇasya dhairya-janitotsāhaḥ kapi-bhaṭāśvāsanādibhir vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, though <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s power was depleted by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s spear-blow, his enthusiasm born of composure is conveyed through the reassuring of the monkey-warriors and the like.

body.text:
sahāyena sahajotsāho, yathā-
sa gupta-mūla-prayatnaḥ śuddha-pārṣṇir ayānvitaḥ |
ṣaḍ-vidhaṃ balam ādāya pratasthe vijigīṣayā ||SRs_2.289|| (ra.vaṃ. 4.26)
body.translated_text: Innate enthusiasm from allies, for example — He, whose efforts were from protected foundations, whose rear was secured, who was furnished with [proper] march, taking the sixfold army, set forth with the desire for conquest. ||2.289|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 4.26)

body.text: śaktyāhāryotsāho, yathā-
body.translated_text: Acquired enthusiasm from power, for example —

body.text:
hastālambitam akṣa-sūtra-valayaṃ karṇāvataṃsīkṛtaṃ
srastaṃ bhrū-yugam unnamayya racitaṃ yajñopavītena ca |
saṃnaddhā jaghane ca valkala-paṭī pāṇiś ca dhatte dhanur
dṛṣṭaṃ bho janakasya yogina idaṃ dāntaṃ viraktaṃ manaḥ ||SRs_2.290|| (bā.rā. 1.53)
body.translated_text: 'The rosary-bracelet held in the hand, the lotus placed as an ear-ornament, the drooping brows raised upward, rearranged with the sacred thread, the bark-garment girded at the waist, and the hand now holds a bow — behold, O people! Is this the tamed, renounced mind of a <s>Yogin</s> of <s>Janaka</s>'s [lineage]?' ||2.290|| (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 1.53)

body.text: dhairya-sahāyābhyām āhāryo, yathā-
body.translated_text: Acquired [enthusiasm] from composure and allies, for example —

body.text:
tava prasādāt kusumāyudho' pi
sahāyam ekaṃ madhum eva labdhvā |
kuryāṃ harasyāpi pināka-pāṇer
dhairya-cyutiṃ ke mama dhanvino' nye ||SRs_2.291|| (ku.saṃ. 3.10)
body.translated_text: 'By your grace, even though I am the flower-weaponed one (<s>Kāma</s>), having obtained <s>Madhu</s> (Spring) as my sole ally, I would cause even <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the wielder of <s>Pināka</s>, to lose his composure — who then are other bowmen compared to me?' ||2.291|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.10)

body.text: atra svabhāva-śakti-rahitasya manmathasya indra-protsāhana-janitena dhairyeṇa vasanta-sahāyena cāhṛtotsāho dhairya-cyuti-cikīrṣā-kathanād abhivyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the acquired enthusiasm of <s>Manmatha</s> (<s>Kāma</s>), who lacks natural power, arising from the composure generated by <s>Indra</s>'s encouragement and from his ally <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), is conveyed through the expression of his desire to shatter [<s>Śiva</s>'s] composure.

body.text: atha vismayaḥ-

children.translated_text: The expansion of the mind that occurs from seeing for the first time and such [encounters with]

children.text:
vistāraś cetaso yas tu vismayaḥ sa nigadyate |
kriyās tatrākṣi-vistāra-sādhūkti-pulakādayaḥ ||SRs_2.292|| 129
children.translated_text: extraordinary objects — that is called <s>Vismaya</s> (wonder). The actions therein are: widening of the eyes, exclamations of 'well done!', horripilation, and the like. ||2.292||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vismaya</s> (wonder) —

body.text: yathā-

children.text: śilā kampaṃ dhatte śiva śiva viyuṅkte kaṭhinatām
children.translated_text: 'The rock assumes trembling! <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>! It relinquishes its hardness!
Ah! The semblance of a woman — it attains womanhood!'

children.text: vadaty evaṃ rāme vivalita-mukhī balkalam uraḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus speaking, as <s>Rāma</s> [approached], the sage's wife, her face turned upward,

children.text: sthale kṛtvā baddhvā kaca-bharam udasthād ṛṣi-vadhūḥ ||SRs_2.293||
children.translated_text: placing the bark-garment upon her chest and binding up her hair, stood up. ||2.293||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha krodhaḥ-
vadhāvajñādibhiś citta-jvalanaṃ krodha īritaḥ |
eṣa tridhā bhavet kordha-kopa-roṣa-prabhedataḥ ||SRs_2.294|| 130
vadha-cchedādi-paryantaḥ krodhaḥ krūra-janāśrayaḥ |
abhyarthanāvadhiḥ prāyaḥ kopo vīra-janāśrayaḥ ||SRs_2.295|| 131
śatru-bhṛtya-suhṛt-pūjyāś catvāro viṣayās tayoḥ |
muhur daṣṭoṣṭhatā bhugna-bhrukuṭī-danta-ghaṭṭanam ||SRs_2.296|| 132
hasta-niṣpīḍanaṃ gātra-kampaḥ śastra-pratīkṣaṇam |
sva-bhujāvekṣaṇaṃ kaṇṭha-garjādyāḥ śātrava-krudhi ||SRs_2.297|| 133
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Krodha</s> (anger) — The burning of the mind through killing, contempt, and the like is called <s>Krodha</s> (anger). It is threefold by the distinction of <s>Krodha</s> (wrath), <s>Kopa</s> (indignation), and <s>Roṣa</s> (fury). ||2.294|| <s>Krodha</s> (wrath), extending to killing and dismembering, belongs to cruel persons. <s>Kopa</s> (indignation), extending mostly to entreaty, belongs to heroic persons. ||2.295|| The four objects of both are: enemies, servants, friends, and venerable persons. Repeatedly biting the lips, knitting of the brows, gnashing of teeth, ||2.296|| clenching of the fists, trembling of the body, looking toward weapons, gazing at one's own arms, roaring from the throat — these and the like are [the reactions] in anger directed at enemies. ||2.297||

body.text:
vadhena śatru-viṣaya-krodho, yathā-
kṛtam anumataṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vā yair idaṃ guru-pātakaṃ
manuja-paśubhir nirmaryādair bhavadbhir udāyudhaiḥ |
naraka-ripuṇā sārdhaṃ teṣāṃ sabhīm akirīṭinām
ayam aham asṛṅ-medo-māṃsaiḥ karomi diśāṃ balim ||SRs_2.298|| (ve.saṃ. 3.24)
body.translated_text: Anger at enemies through killing, for example — 'By you human-beasts, devoid of propriety, bearing arms, by whom this great sin was committed, approved, or witnessed — together with the enemy of <s>Naraka</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), of those crownless ones in the assembly, I shall make an oblation to the directions with their blood, fat, and flesh.' ||2.298|| (<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 3.24)

body.text: avajñayā śatru-viṣaya-krodho, yathā-

children.translated_text: 'He whose intellect ventures to despise <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
whose power is praised at the summit of the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) —
I shall bring down my foot upon his head
three times, [a foot] terrible as the staff of the Destroyer at the dissolution of the world.' ||2.299||

body.translated_text: Anger at enemies through contempt, for example —

body.text: atra parameśvarāvajñayā janito dakṣa-viṣayo dadhīci-krodhaḥ paruṣa-vāg-ārambheṇa vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the anger of <s>Dadhīci</s> directed at <s>Dakṣa</s>, generated by the contempt of <s>Parameśvara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), is conveyed through harsh speech-modes.

body.text:
bhṛtya-krodhe tu ceṣṭāḥ syus tarjanaṃ mūrdha-dhananam |
nirbhartsanaṃ ca bahudhā muhur nirvarṇanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.300|| 134
body.translated_text: In anger directed at servants, the actions are: threatening, shaking the head, scolding in many ways, repeated scrutiny, and the like. ||2.300||

body.text: yathā vīrānande-

children.translated_text: 'His ten heads shaking, his fingers trembling,
his eyes fierce, his throat pregnant with harsh roaring —
seeing the faces of the night-wanderers (<s>Rākṣasas</s>), having then descended
from the palace, the Ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) was struck by the fist of the lord of monkeys (<s>Sugrīva</s>).' ||2.301||

body.translated_text: As in <s>Vīrānanda</s> —

body.text: atra sugrīva-sampāte palāyiteṣu bhṛtyeṣu rāvaṇasya krodho mūrdha-dhūnanādibhir anubhāvair vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, when <s>Sugrīva</s> attacked, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s anger at his servants who fled is conveyed through the <s>anubhāvas</s> of shaking the heads and the like.

body.text: mitra-krodhe vikārāḥ syur netrāntaḥ-patad-aśrutā |

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ dhyānaṃ ca naiścalyaṃ śvasitāni muhur muhuḥ | 135
children.translated_text: silent meditation, motionlessness, repeated sighing,
silence, downcast face, bent gaze, and the like. ||2.302||

body.translated_text: In anger directed at friends, the disturbances are: tears falling from the corners of the eyes,

body.text: yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: 'Hearing of the abduction of <s>Subhadrā</s>, carried out by
that son of <s>Kuntī</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) with his (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) consent — their minds agitated, bodies rigid,

children.text: namad-vaktrāḥ svānte kim api vilikhanto' tikuṭilair
children.translated_text: faces bowed, tracing something in their hearts with deeply furrowed [brows],
the <s>Yadu</s> warriors looked at the lord of the <s>Yadus</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) with tear-filled sidelong glances.' ||2.303||

body.translated_text: For example, by me [the author] —

body.text: atra subhadrā-haraṇānumatyā janitaḥ kṛṣṇa-viṣayo yadūnāṃ krodhaḥ kuṭila-vīkṣaṇādibhir vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the anger of the <s>Yadus</s> directed at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, generated by his consent to <s>Subhadrā</s>'s abduction, is conveyed through curved glances and the like.

body.text: pūjya-krodhe tu ceṣṭāḥ syuḥ sva-nindā namra-vaktratā | 136
body.translated_text: In anger directed at venerable persons, the actions are: self-blame, downcast face,

body.text: anuttara-pradānāṅga-sveda-gadgadikādayaḥ ||SRs_2.304||
body.translated_text: failure to reply, perspiration of the limbs, choking of voice, and the like. ||2.304||

body.text: yathā vīrānande-

children.translated_text: 'Seeing the mother — who was the [very] mother of <s>Rāma</s>'s exile —
though wishing to speak harshly, [yet] overcome by stammering,
with face bowed down, with sidelong glance reddening and curved,
the great-souled <s>Bharata</s> burned exceedingly within his heart.' ||2.305||

body.translated_text: As in <s>Vīrānanda</s> —

body.text: śatru-krodhe tu ceṣṭāḥ syur bhāva-garbhita-bhāṣaṇam | 137
body.translated_text: In anger directed at enemies [elsewhere the text reads 'roṣa'], the actions are: speech pregnant with meaning,

body.text: bhrūbheda-niṭila-sveda-kaṭākṣaāruṇimādayaḥ ||SRs_2.306||
body.translated_text: furrowing of the brows, perspiration on the forehead, reddened sidelong glances, and the like. ||2.306||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Locks of hair shaken by anger, trembling born throughout the body,

children.text: kiñcit kokanada-cchadena sadṛśe netre svayaṃ rajyataḥ |
children.translated_text: eyes reddening spontaneously, somewhat resembling red lotus petals —

children.text: dhatte kāntim idaṃ ca vaktram anayor bhaṅgena bhīma-bhruvoś
children.translated_text: this face bears the beauty of the furrowing of both terrible brows,
like a moon with a prominent mark, like a lotus with a restless bee.' ||2.307||

body.translated_text: For example —
(<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 5.36)

body.text: atra lavasya candraketoś ca paraspara-viṣayaḥ kopo bhrū-bhedādibhir vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the mutual anger of <s>Lava</s> and <s>Candraketu</s> toward each other is expressed through the knitting of brows and the like.

body.text: bhṛtyādi-kopa-tritaye tat-tat-krodhāditāḥ kriyāḥ ||SRs_2.308|| 138
body.translated_text: In the three types of anger toward servants and others, the actions appropriate to each respective anger [are to be understood]. ||2.308||

body.text:
atha roṣaḥ-
mithaḥ strī-puṃsayor eva roṣah strī-gocaraḥ punaḥ |

children.translated_text: Its limit is [the restoration of] trust. Here the expressions are: sidelong glances,
quivering of the lip, reddening of the eye-corners, sighing, and the like. ||2.309||

body.translated_text:
Now, <s>Roṣa</s> (Resentment) —
<s>Roṣa</s> is [a form of anger] between a man and a woman only; moreover, it is directed toward the woman.

body.text: yathā vīrānande-

children.translated_text: Broken by the knitting of brows, with reddened corners of the eyes,
with trembling lip, accompanied by excessive sighing —
as the daughter of the Earth (<s>Sītā</s>) beheld the face of her lord,
she thought that even release from prison was something most painful. ||2.310||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Vīrānanda</s> —

body.text: atra rāvaṇa-kārāgāra-śaṅkayā janitaḥ sītā-viṣayo rāmasya roṣo bhrū-bhaṅgādibhir anubhāvair vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Rāma</s>'s resentment directed toward <s>Sītā</s>, produced by suspicion due to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s captivity, is expressed through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as the knitting of brows.

body.text: pratyayāvadhitvaṃ, yathā-
body.translated_text: Its being limited by [the restoration of] trust, for example —

body.text:
diṣṭyārdha-śruta-vipralambha-janita-krodhād ahaṃ no gato
diṣṭyā no paruṣaṃ ruṣārdha-kathite kiñcin mayā vyāhṛtam |
māṃ pratyāyayituṃ vimūḍha-hṛdayaṃ diṣṭyā kathāntaṃ gatā
mithyā-dūṣita-yānayā virahitaṃ diṣṭyā na jātaṃ jagat ||SRs_2.311|| (ve.saṃ. 2.13)
atra svapna-vṛttānta-śravaṇa-bhrānti-janitasya bhānumatī-viṣayakasya suyodhana-roṣasya svapna-śeṣa-śravaṇa-janita-pratyaya-kṛtā śāntiḥ diṣṭyety-ādi-vāg-ārambheṇa vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the resentment of <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) directed toward <s>Bhānumatī</s>, produced by the confusion of hearing the dream-account, is pacified by trust generated from hearing the remainder of the dream — this is expressed through the verbal expression 'fortunately' and the like.

body.text: dvedhā nigaditaḥ strīṇāṃ roṣaḥ puruṣa-gocaraḥ | 140
body.translated_text: Women's resentment, directed toward men, is described as twofold:

body.text: sapatnī-hetur ādyaḥ syād anyaḥ syād anya-hetukaḥ ||SRs_2.312||
body.translated_text: the first is caused by a co-wife, and the other has another cause. ||2.312||

body.text: sapatnī-hetuko roṣo vipralambhe prapañcyate | 141
body.translated_text: Resentment caused by a co-wife is elaborated in the section on <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation).

body.text: anya-hetu-kṛte tv atra kriyāḥ puruṣa-roṣavat ||SRs_2.313||
body.translated_text: But when caused by another reason, the actions are like those of male resentment. ||2.313||

body.text:
yathā-
mayy eva vismaraṇa-dāruṇa-citta-vṛttau
vṛttaṃ rahaḥ-praṇayam apratipadyamāne |
bhedād bhruvoḥ kuṭilayor atilohitākṣyā
bhagnaṃ śarāsanam ivātiruṣā smarasya ||SRs_2.314|| (śaku. 5.23)
body.translated_text:
For example —
Toward me, whose mental activity was cruel with forgetfulness,
who did not recognize the secret love previously experienced —
with her curved brows knit and her eyes deeply reddened,
it was as if the bow of <s>Smara</s> (the God of Love) was broken in extreme anger. ||2.314|| (<s>Śākuntala</s> 5.23)

body.text: atra prāktana-vṛttāntāpahnava-janito duṣyanta-viṣayakaḥ śakuntalā-roṣo bhrū-bhaṅgādibhir anubhāvair vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the resentment of <s>Śakuntalā</s> directed toward <s>Duṣyanta</s>, produced by his denial of past events, is expressed through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as the knitting of brows.

body.text: atha śokaḥ-

children.translated_text: Grief is the burden of mental anguish caused by the calamity of kinsmen, misfortune, loss of wealth, and the like.
In it, the expressions are: pallor, ||2.315||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Śoka</s> (Grief) —

body.text: bāṣpodgamo mukhe śoṣaḥ stambha-niḥśvasitādayaḥ | 143
body.translated_text: shedding of tears, dryness of the mouth, stupor, sighing, and the like.

body.text: uttamānam ayaṃ prauḍho vibhāvair anya-saṃśritaiḥ ||SRs_2.316||
body.translated_text: In the superior [person], this [grief] is mature, [caused] by <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) residing in others. ||2.316||

body.text: ātma-sthair atirūḍho' pi prāyaḥ śauryeṇa śāmyati | 144
body.translated_text: Even when it intensifies from causes within oneself, it is generally pacified by heroism.

body.text: tatra ceṣṭā guṇākhyāna-nigūḍha-ruditādayaḥ ||SRs_2.317||
body.translated_text: In it, the expressions are: narrating [the deceased's] virtues, concealed weeping, and the like. ||2.317||

body.text: para-gata-vibhāvair, yathā-

children.translated_text: May the Lord protect you — [<s>Rati</s>], with her disheveled hair scattered over her face,
falling upon the ashes of her husband, sweeping the ground with her palms,

children.text: hā prāṇeśvara hā smareti rudatīṃ bāspākulākṣīṃ ratiṃ
children.translated_text: crying 'Alas, lord of my life! Alas, remember!' — weeping, with eyes flooded with tears —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yasya lalāṭa-locanam api vyāptāśru nirvāpitam ||SRs_2.318||
children.translated_text: seeing her, even his (<s>Śiva</s>'s) forehead-eye was pervaded with tears and extinguished. ||2.318||

body.translated_text: From <s>vibhāvas</s> residing in others, for example —

body.text: atra rati-gata-śocya-daśā-vilokanena devasya śoko bāṣpodgamena vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the grief of the Lord (<s>Śiva</s>), from witnessing the pitiable state of <s>Rati</s>, is expressed through the shedding of tears.

body.text:
ātma-gatair, yathā-
ayi karṇa karṇa-subhagāṃ prayaccha me
giram udvamann iva mudaṃ mayi sthirām |
satatāviyuktam akṛtāpriyaṃ kathaṃ
vṛṣasena-vatsala vihāya yāsi mām ||SRs_2.319|| (ve.saṃ. 5.14)
body.translated_text:
From causes within oneself, for example —
O <s>Karṇa</s>, give me a word pleasant to the ear, steadfast to me,
as if disgorging joy.
O lover of <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, how can you leave me,
who has been constantly united [with you] and never offended? ||2.319|| (<s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 5.14)

body.text: syād eṣa mṛti-paryantaḥ sva-parasthais tu madhyame | 145
body.translated_text: This [grief] may last until death; but in the middling [person], with causes from self and others,

body.text: anativyakta-rudita-pramukhās tatra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.320||
body.translated_text: the expressions are: not-quite-manifest weeping and such. ||2.320||

body.text: svagatair madhyamasya, yathā karuṇā-kandale-
body.translated_text: Of the middling [person], from causes within oneself, for example, in the <s>Karuṇā-kandala</s> —

children.text: nyāyopādhir ayaṃ yad aśru-kaṇikā muñcanti bandhu-vyaye
children.translated_text: 'This is the condition of propriety, that tear-drops are shed at the loss of kinsmen;

children.text: rāgopādhir ayaṃ tyajanti viṣayān yaj jñātayo dustyajān |
children.translated_text: this is the condition of attachment, that relatives abandon hard-to-relinquish pleasures;

children.text: prāṇānāṃ punar utkramaḥ kim upadhis tat kena vijñāyate
children.translated_text: but as for the departure of the vital breaths — what is its condition? Who can know that
without the Lord <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) and <s>Daśaratha</s> of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> dynasty?' ||2.321||

body.text: atra vasudevasya bandhu-vipattijaḥ śokaḥ prāṇotkramaṇena vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the grief of <s>Vasudeva</s>, born from the calamity of kinsmen, is expressed through the departure of the vital breaths.

body.text:
para-gatair, yathā-
nirbhidyanta ivāṅgakānya-suharair ākranda-saṃstambhanaiḥ
kaṇṭhe garva-niruddha-bāṣpa-vigame vācāṃ gatir gadgadā |
dhāvaty antara-saṃstutān api janān kaṇṭhe grahītuṃ manaḥ
kāṣṭhā tasya mamedṛśī yadukule kulyaḥ kathaṃ jīvati ||SRs_2.322|| [*14]
[*14] karuṇā-kandalād iti bhāti |
atra yadu-kula-dhvaṃsanena nāradasya śokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the grief of <s>Nārada</s> is [caused] by the destruction of the <s>Yadu</s> lineage.

body.text: hetubhiḥ svagatair eva prāyaḥ strī-nīcayor ayam | 146
body.translated_text: This [grief] in women and low persons is mostly from causes within oneself,

body.text:
maraṇa-vyavasāyāntas tatra bhū-pariveṣṭanam |
urastāḍana-nirbheda-pātoccai rodanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.323|| 147
body.translated_text:
ending in the resolve to die. In it, the [expressions are]: rolling on the ground,
beating the breast, tearing [the hair], falling down, loud crying, and the like. ||2.323||

body.text: atha nīca-gato, yathā karuṇā-kandale-
body.translated_text: Now, in a low person, for example, in the <s>Karuṇā-kandala</s> —

children.translated_text: With hair half-torn, with breast-slopes smeared with blood by their own hands,
with cheeks scratched by nails, with foreheads shattered by strikes against stones,
with throats torn open from wailing, with voices broken and stammering —
this condition of the inner-chamber attendants carves at the mind. ||2.324||

body.text:
strī-gato, yathā-
atha sā punar eva vihvalā
vasudhāliṅgana-dhūsara-stanī |
vilalāpa vikīrṇa-mūrdhajā
sama-duḥkhām iva kurvatī sthalīm ||SRs_2.325|| [ku.saṃ. 4.4]
body.translated_text:
In a woman, for example —
Then she, distraught again,
her breasts grey from embracing the earth,
lamented with disheveled hair,
as if making the ground share her sorrow. ||2.325|| [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 4.4]

body.text:
atha jugupsā-
ahṛdyānāṃ padārthānāṃ darśana-śravaṇādibhiḥ |
saṅkocanaṃ yan manasah sā jugupsātra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.326|| 148
nāsāpidhānaṃ tvaritā gatir āsya-vikūṇanam |
sarvāṅga-dhūnanaṃ kutsā muhur niṣṭhīvanādayaḥ ||SRs_2.327|| 149
body.translated_text:
Now, <s>Jugupsā</s> (Disgust) —
The contraction of the mind from seeing, hearing, and the like
of disagreeable objects — that is <s>jugupsā</s>. In it, the expressions are: ||2.326||
covering the nose, hurried gait, contortion of the face,
shaking of the entire body, reproach, repeated spitting, and the like. ||2.327||

body.text: ahṛdya-darśanād, yathā-

children.translated_text: From the corpses with bones sweating from intense heat, with fat reaching the boiling point,
the flesh-eaters (<s>piśācas</s>), dragging [corpses] even from numerous pyres with clinging smoke,
with overcooked flesh drooping, with joints loosened on both sides and marrow freed from the channel —

children.text: ete niścūṣya jaṅghān alakam udayinīr majja-dhārāḥ pibanti ||SRs_2.328||
children.translated_text: these [ghouls], sucking out the shanks, drink streams of marrow as if [drinking from] the river <s>Udayinī</s>. ||2.328||

body.translated_text: From seeing something disagreeable, for example —
(<s>Mālatī-Mādhava</s> 5.17)

body.text: atra jaṅghā-niścūṣaṇa-majja-dhārā-pānādi-janitā piśāca-viṣayā mādhavasya jugupsā garhaṇena ete kuṇapa-bhuja ity anena vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the disgust of <s>Mādhava</s> toward the <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating ghouls), produced by the sucking of shanks and drinking of marrow-streams, is expressed through the reproach: 'these flesh-eaters.'

body.text: śravaṇād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Slimy inside with fat, marrow, and blood,
covered by skin, with joints bound by sinews and bones,
in this body — a house of the <s>caṇḍāla</s> of <s>karma</s> —
what virtuous person would bind his affection, [the body] from which putrid smell rises? ||2.329||

body.translated_text: From hearing, for example —

body.text: atra kasyacid vastu-tattva-vicārāgama-śravaṇa-janitā dehe jugupsā-rūpā nindā vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the disgust in the form of censure toward the body, produced in someone through hearing the investigation of the true nature of things, is expressed.

body.text:
ghṛṇā śuddhā jugupsānyā daśa-rūpe nirūpitā |
sā heya-śravaṇotpanna-jugupsāyā na bhidyate ||SRs_2.330|| 150
body.translated_text:
Pure aversion (<s>ghṛṇā</s>) is [one type of] <s>jugupsā</s>; another is defined in the <s>Daśa-rūpa</s>.
That [latter type], arising from hearing about what is to be rejected, does not differ [essentially] from <s>jugupsā</s>. ||2.330||

body.text:
atha bhayam-
bhayaṃ tu mantunā ghora-darśana-śravaṇādibhiḥ |
cittasyātīva cāñcalyaṃ tat prāyo nīca-madhyayoḥ ||SRs_2.331|| 151
uttamasya tu jāyeta kāraṇair atilaukikaiḥ |
bhaye tu ceṣṭā vaivarṇyaṃ stabdhatvaṃ gātra-kampanam ||SRs_2.332|| 152
palāyanaṃ parāvṛtya vīkṣaṇaṃ svātma-gopanam |
āsya-śoṣaṇam utkrośa-śaraṇānveṣaṇādayaḥ ||SRs_2.333|| 153
body.translated_text:
Now, <s>Bhaya</s> (Fear) —
Fear is the extreme agitation of the mind caused by offense [against a superior], seeing or hearing terrible things, and the like.
It [occurs] mostly in the low and middling [persons]. ||2.331||
But in the superior [person], it would arise from supernatural causes.
In fear, the expressions are: pallor, rigidity, trembling of the limbs, ||2.332||
fleeing, looking back, hiding oneself,
drying of the mouth, outcry, seeking refuge, and the like. ||2.333||

body.text:
mantur aparādhaḥ | tasmād, yathā-
vibhūṣaṇa-pratyupahāra-hastam
upasthitaṃ vīkṣya viśāmpatis tam |
sauparṇam astraṃ pratisañjahāra
prahveṣv anirbandha-ruṣo hi santaḥ ||SRs_2.334|| (ra.vaṃ. 16.80)
ghora-darśanād, yathā-

children.translated_text: The <s>Pāṇḍya</s> king, defeated by fear of the <s>Cola</s>,
fleeing toward the southern direction,
in confusion, plunging into the ocean,
cursed <s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), the destroyer of the bridge. ||2.335||

body.translated_text: From seeing something terrible, for example —

body.text: atra yuddha-saṃrambha-bhīmasya colasya darśanāt pāṇḍyasya bhayaṃ palāyanādibhir vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the fear of the <s>Pāṇḍya</s> [king] from seeing the terrible <s>Cola</s> [king], fierce in the fury of battle, is expressed through fleeing and the like.

body.text: ghora-śravaṇād, yathā-

children.translated_text: Hearing in the battlefield, O lord of the <s>Mādhava</s> kings, the sound of your bowstring,
the rival heroes, reaching the cave of the ancestral mountain, deep in dense darkness,
hiding there, their glory cut down, having lost their courage,

children.text: sraṣṭāraṃ naṣṭa-dhairyāḥ kamala-bhuvam aho hanta nindanti mandam ||SRs_2.336||
children.translated_text: blame — alas! — the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, the creator of the splendor of their army's gem-arrays, and reproach him sluggishly. ||2.336||

body.translated_text: From hearing something terrible, for example —

body.text: atilaukikāt kāraṇād uttamasya, yathā-
body.translated_text: Of the superior [person], from a supernatural cause, for example —

body.text:
aśaknuvan soḍhum adhīra-locanaḥ
sahasra-raśmer iva yasya darśanam |
praviśya hemādri-guhā-gṛhāntaraṃ
nināya bibhyad divasāni kauśikaḥ ||SRs_2.337|| [māgha 1.53]
body.translated_text:
Unable to endure the sight of him [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>],
which was like that of the thousand-rayed sun,
<s>Kauśika</s> (<s>Indra</s>), entering the interior of a cave-dwelling on the golden mountain,
spent his days in fear. ||2.337|| [<s>Māgha</s> 1.53]

body.text: atra varṇanīyatayā uttama-rāvaṇaṃ prati devendrasya (bhītatva-varṇanāt) madhyamatvaṃ (eveti tasya uttamatvaṃ katham iti) nāśaṅkanīyam | yataḥ prakṛtir eva kāraṇaṃ puṃsām uttamatve | na tu varṇanā | varṇanāyāḥ kāraṇatve priyeṇa tasyānaparādha-bādhitāḥ (māghe 1.61) ity ādibhiḥ augryādi-bhāva-kathanam (varṇanīyatayā) uttamasya rāvaṇasya nocitaṃ syāt | tasmād uttama-prakṛter api devendrasya lokātirikta-vara-prabhāva-bhīṣaṇād rāvaṇād bhayam upapadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the middling status should not be suspected [of <s>Indra</s>] merely because the fear of <s>Devendara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) toward the superior <s>Rāvaṇa</s> is described; for it is one's nature that is the cause of a person's superior status, not the description [by a poet]. If description were the cause, then the narration of [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s] ferocity and other states through [verses like] 'by his beloved, those of no offense are afflicted' (<s>Māgha</s> 1.61) and the like would not be appropriate for the superior <s>Rāvaṇa</s> either. Therefore, even for <s>Devendara</s>, who is of superior nature, fear from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who is terrifying due to the power of boons transcending the world, is well-established.

body.text: uttamasyāpi hetuja-bhayānaṅgīkāre-

children.text: vidrāṇe dravya-nāthe savitari tarale jāta-śaṅke śaśāṅke
children.translated_text: When the Lord of Wealth (<s>Kubera</s>) is put to flight, when the Moon is trembling and apprehensive,

children.text: vaikuṇṭhe kuṇṭha-garve dravati maghavati klānta-kāntau kṛtānte |
children.translated_text: when <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>)'s pride is blunted, when <s>Maghavan</s> (<s>Indra</s>) flees, when <s>Kṛtānta</s> (<s>Yama</s>) is fatigued and drained,
when <s>Śatadhrḥtau</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) in the sky, with one hand raised, cries 'sacrilege!' —

children.text: pāyād vaḥ kāla-kūṭaṃ jhaṭiti kavalayan līlayā nīla-kaṇṭhaḥ ||SRs_2.338||
children.translated_text: may the Blue-throated one (<s>Śiva</s>), playfully swallowing the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison in an instant, protect you! ||2.338||

body.translated_text: If one does not accept fear from a cause even in the superior —

body.text: ity atra vidrāva-tāralyādibhir udghoṣitasya dravya-nātha-savitrādi-gata-bhayasya apalāpaḥ katham abhidheyaḥ | tad-apalāpe ca kāla-kūṭa-bhakṣaṇasya sukaratvāt tat-kārya-nirvahaṇaika-prāṇasya nīlakaṇṭha-prabhāvotkarṣasya kathaṃ mastakonnamanaṃ syāt |
body.translated_text: Here, how can one deny the fear of the Lord of Wealth (<s>Kubera</s>), the Sun, and others, which is proclaimed through their flight, trembling, and the like? And if that fear is denied, then since swallowing the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison would be easy [for anyone], how could the supreme excellence of the Blue-throated one (<s>Śiva</s>), who alone is the life-breath for accomplishing that deed, be exalted?

body.text:
hetujād itare prokte bhaye soḍhala-sūnunā |
kṛtrimaṃ tūttama-gataṃ gurv-ādīn pratyavāstavam ||SRs_2.339|| 154
vibhīṣikotthaṃ bālāder vitrāsitakam ity ubhe |
tatrāntyam antarbhūtaṃ syād ghora-śravaṇaje bhaye ||SRs_2.340|| 155
bhikṣu-bhallūka-corādi-sūcanā-kalpitatvataḥ |
ādyaṃ tu yukti-kākṣyāyāṃ bhaya-kakṣyāṃ na gāhate ||SRs_2.341|| 156
gurv-ādi-saṃnidhau yasmān nīcaiḥ sthity-ādi-sūcitam |
bhāvo vinaya eva syād atha syān nāṭake yadi ||SRs_2.342|| 157
avahitthatayā tasya bhayatvaṃ dūrato gatam |
ato hetujam evaikaṃ bhayaṃ syād iti niścayaḥ ||SRs_2.343|| 158
body.translated_text:
Fear other than that caused by a cause is stated by <s>Soḍhala</s>'s son [to be as follows]:
the artificial [fear], which belongs to the superior, is [feigned] before elders and others as deference. ||2.339||
That arising from threats is [fear] of children and others; the startling [fear] — both of these
are included within fear caused by hearing something terrible. ||2.340||
Because [the startling fear] is fabricated by the suggestion of mendicants, bears, thieves, and the like;
while the former [deference] enters the category of propriety but does not enter the category of fear. ||2.341||
Since in the presence of elders and others, [the behavior] indicated by standing quietly and the like
by low persons would be the emotion of modesty (<s>vinaya</s>) itself, if indeed it appears in drama. ||2.342||
As <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), its being fear is far removed.
Therefore, the conclusion is that there is only one type of fear — that caused by a cause. ||2.343||

body.text:
tathā ca bhāratīye-
etat svabhāvajaṃ syāt
sattva-samutthaṃ tathaiva kartavyam |
punar ebhir eva bhāvaiḥ
kṛtakaṃ mṛdu-ceṣṭitaiḥ kāryam ||SRs_2.344|| iti | (nā.śā. 6.71)
body.translated_text:
And thus in the <s>Bhāratīya</s> [section of the Nāṭya-śāstra] —
'This [emotion] would be natural,
arising from <s>sattva</s> (the mind's truth), and similarly it should be enacted;
and again with these very emotions,
the artificial should be performed with gentle gestures.' ||2.344|| Thus. (<s>Nāṭya-śāstra</s> 6.71)

body.text: nanu cātra svabhāvajaṃ kṛtakaṃ ceti dvividhaṃ bhayaṃ pratīyate | tasmāt tad-virodha iti cet, maivam | bharatādy-abhiprāyam ajānatāṃ pelavokti-mātra-tātparyeṇa na śaṅkitavyam | tathā hi-yathā loke mañjiṣṭhādi-dravyaṃ sahajo raktimā gāḍhataraṃ vyāpnoti | evaṃ madhya-nīcayor bhayaṃ svalpa-kāraṇa-mātre' pi sahajavad dṛśyata iti sahajam ity upacaryate | yathā kṛtako lākṣā-rasaḥ prayatna-sajjito' pi kāṣṭhādikam antar na vyāpnoti, evam uttama-gataṃ bhayam iti alaukika-kāraṇa-prakarṣeṇāpi kṛtakavad eva pratīyata iti kṛtakam ity upacaryate | anyathā (tasya vāstavatve) svābhāvikasya bhayasya dāma-darśane' pi samutpatti-prasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: Now, here two types of fear are perceived — natural and artificial. If [one objects] that there is a contradiction in that, not so. One should not raise doubts based merely on the import of superficial statements, without knowing the intention of <s>Bharata</s> and others. For just as in the world a dye-substance like madder pervades its own natural redness all the more deeply, so for the middling and inferior [heroes], fear is perceived as if natural even from a slight cause — hence it is figuratively called 'natural.' Just as an artificial [dye] like lac-juice, even when carefully applied, does not penetrate wood and the like internally, so fear belonging to the superior [hero] is perceived as if artificial even through an extraordinary cause of extreme magnitude — hence it is figuratively called 'artificial.' Otherwise (if it were real), natural fear would arise even at the sight of a rope [mistaken for a snake].

body.text: nanu yadi svābhāvikaṃ bhayaṃ (uttamasya) na vidyate (tarhi)-
body.translated_text: Now, if natural fear does not exist [in the superior hero, then how to explain] —

body.text:
dvāre niyukta-puruṣānumata-praveśaḥ
siṃhāsanāntika-careṇa sahopasarpan |
tejobhir asya vinivārita-dṛṣṭi-pātair
vākyād ṛte punar iva prativārito' smi ||SRs_2.345|| (mā.a.mi. 1.12)
body.translated_text: 'Entering through the gate with the permission of the appointed guards, approaching together with an attendant who moves near the throne — by the splendors of this [king], my gaze being repelled, I was turned back, as it were, even without a word.' ||2.345|| (from <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 1.12)

body.text: ity ādiṣu kathaṃ bhayotpattir iti ced ucyate | bhīṣaṇās trividhāḥ-ākṛti-bhīṣaṇāḥ kriyā-bhīṣaṇāḥ māhātmya-bhīṣaṇāś ceti | tatrākṛti-bhīṣaṇāḥ rakṣaḥ-piśācādayaḥ | kriyā-bhīṣaṇāḥ vīrabhadra-paraśurāma-śārdūla-vṛkādayaḥ | māhātmya-bhīṣaṇā deva-naradevādayaḥ | tato' tra māhātmya-bhīṣaṇa-rāja-darśanād bhayaṃ nāṭyācāryasya (hara-dattasya) jāyate | na punaḥ svabhāvāt | tad etan niḥśaṃśayaṃ kṛtam aho durāsado rāja-mahimā iti pūrva-vākyaṃ grathnatā tenaiva kālidāseneti sarvaṃ kalyāṇam |
body.translated_text: If one asks how fear arises in such cases, the answer is: the frightening ones are of three kinds — frightening by appearance, frightening by action, and frightening by majesty. Of these, those frightening by appearance are <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and the like. Those frightening by action are <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, <s>Paraśurāma</s>, tigers, wolves, and the like. Those frightening by majesty are gods, kings, and the like. Therefore, here the fear of the drama-teacher (<s>Haradatta</s>) arises from seeing the king, who is frightening by majesty — not from his own nature. And this is placed beyond doubt by the connecting sentence 'Ah, what an unapproachable royal majesty!' composed by <s>Kālidāsa</s> himself. Thus all is well.

body.text: bhojenoktāḥ sthāyino' nye garvaḥ sneho dhṛtir matiḥ |

children.translated_text: they are said to be the permanent states of the <s>Uddhata</s> (Insolent), <s>Preyas</s> (Affectionate), <s>Śānta</s> (Tranquil), and <s>Udātta</s> (Sublime) sentiments respectively. 159

children.text: tatra sneho rater bhedas tridhā cecchātma-tat-kṛtaḥ ||SRs_2.346||
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>sneha</s> (affection) is a division of <s>rati</s> (love), being threefold: arising from desire, from the self, and from that [the beloved]. ||2.346||

body.translated_text: Other <s>sthāyins</s> (permanent states) stated by <s>Bhoja</s> are: <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>sneha</s> (affection), <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment), and <s>mati</s> (judgment);

body.text: tathā hi-idaṃ khalu tenaiva preyo-rasa-vādinā mahārājenodāhṛtam-
body.translated_text: For indeed, this was illustrated by that very great king [<s>Bhoja</s>], the proponent of the <s>Preyas</s> sentiment —

body.text:
yad eva rocate mahyaṃ tad eva kurute priyā |
iti vetti na jānāti tat priyaṃ yat karoti sā ||SRs_2.347|| iti |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever pleases me, that very thing my beloved does; she knows this, yet she does not know that what she does is pleasing.' ||2.347|| Thus.

body.text:
tenaiva vyākṛtaṃ ca-vatsala-prakṛter dhīra-lalita-nāyakasya priyālambana-vibhāvād utpannaḥ snehaḥ sthāyi-bhāvo viṣaya-saundaryādibhir uddīpana-vibhāvair uddīpyamānaḥ samupajāyamānair mati-dhṛti-smṛty-ādibhir vyabhicāri-bhāvair anubhāvaiś ca praśaṃsādibhiḥ saṃsṛjyamāno niṣpannaḥ preyo-rasa iti pratīyate | rati-prītyor api cāyam eva mūla-prakṛtir iṣyate |
na tāvad asya snehasya ratiṃ prati mūla-prakṛtitvam | raty-aṅkura-daśāyām asyāsambhavāt | sambhogecchā-mātraṃ hi ratiḥ | saiva prema-māna-praṇayākhyābhis tisṛbhiḥ pūrva-daśābhir utkaṭībhūtā caturtha-daśāyāṃ citta-dravī-bhāva-lakṣaṇa-sneha-rūpatām āpnoti | tathā ca bhāva-prakāśikāyām-
body.translated_text: And he [<s>Bhoja</s>] analyzed it thus: The <s>sneha</s> (affection) that arises as a permanent state from the <s>ālambana-vibhāva</s> (foundational determinant) of the beloved, in a hero of the tender-gallant (<s>dhīra-lalita</s>) type with a nature disposed to affection (<s>vatsala</s>) — being stimulated by <s>uddīpana-vibhāvas</s> (excitant determinants) such as the beauty of the object and the like, conjoined with arising <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory states) such as judgment, contentment, memory, and the like, and with <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions) such as praise and the like — is understood to ripen into the <s>Preyas</s> sentiment. And this [<s>sneha</s>] is held to be the root-nature of both <s>rati</s> (erotic love) and <s>prīti</s> (delight). But this <s>sneha</s> does not truly function as the root-nature of <s>rati</s>, since it cannot exist at the sprout-stage of <s>rati</s>. For <s>rati</s> is merely the desire for union. That very [<s>rati</s>], having intensified through three prior stages called <s>prema</s> (love), <s>māna</s> (wounded pride), and <s>praṇaya</s> (intimacy), attains in its fourth stage the form of <s>sneha</s>, characterized by the melting of the heart. As stated in the <s>Bhāva-prakāśikā</s> —

body.text:
iyam aṅkuritā premṇā mānāt pallavitā bhavet |
sakorakā praṇayataḥ snehāt kusumitā bhavet ||SRs_2.348|| iti |
body.translated_text: 'This [love], having sprouted through <s>prema</s>, would put forth leaves through <s>māna</s>; with buds through <s>praṇaya</s>, it would blossom through <s>sneha</s>.' ||2.348|| Thus.

body.text: ato' sminn udāharaṇe snehasya rati-rūpeṇaivāsvādyatvaṃ na pṛthak sthāyitvena | evaṃ ca snehasya rati-bhedatva-kathanāt preyo-rasasyāpi śṛṅgārād apṛthaktvam artha-siddham |
body.translated_text: Therefore, in this example, <s>sneha</s> is relished only in the form of <s>rati</s>, not as a separate permanent state. And since <s>sneha</s> is thus described as a division of <s>rati</s>, the non-separateness of the <s>Preyas</s> sentiment from <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is established by implication.

body.text: anye poṣā-sahiṣṇutvān naiva sthāyi-padocitāḥ ||SRs_2.349|| 160
body.translated_text: The others [viz. garva, dhṛti, mati], being unable to sustain nourishment, are not fit for the status of permanent states. ||2.349|| 160

body.text: tathāpi garva-sthāyitvam udāhṛtam-
body.translated_text: Nevertheless, the permanent status of <s>garva</s> (pride) was illustrated [by <s>Bhoja</s>] —

children.text: apakartāham asmīti mā te manasi bhūd bhayam |
children.translated_text: '"I am the one who has done harm" — let not this fear be in your mind;

children.text: vimukheṣu na me khaḍgaḥ prahartuṃ jātu vāñchati ||SRs_2.350||
children.translated_text: my sword never desires to strike those who have turned their backs.' ||2.350||

body.text: (sa.ka.ā., kāvyādarśa 2.293)
body.translated_text: (from <s>Sāhitya-kaustubha-āloka</s>; <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> 2.293)

body.text: vyākṛtaṃ ca-atra mayāpakāraḥ kṛta iti yat te cetasi bhayaṃ tan mā bhūt | mama khaḍgaḥ parāṅmukheṣu na kadācid api parahartum utsahata iti sarvathaiva rūḍho' haṅkāraḥ pratīyate | so' yaṃ garva-prakṛtir uddhato nāma raso niṣpadyate iti |
body.translated_text: And it was analyzed thus: Here, what fear there is in your mind that 'I have committed an offence' — let that not be. My sword never wishes to strike those who have turned away — thus a thoroughly established ego-sense is perceived. This, having pride as its nature, is called the <s>Uddhata</s> (Insolent) sentiment, it is said.

body.text: na tāvad atra garvaḥ | kiṃ tu pūrvam apakartāraṃ paścād bhītaṃ dviṣantam avalokya jātayā sama-ravi-mukhaṃ na hanmi mā bhaiṣīr iti vāk-sūcitayā nīce dayayā kasyacid vīra-sārvabhaumasya śobhā nāma pauruṣa-sāttvika-bhāvaḥ pratīyate | yadi vā abhītam api śatruṃ bhīto yadi tarhi palāyasvety adhikṣipatīti garva iti ced astu vā garvaḥ | tathāpy asatyabhītikalpanā-rūpa-cittādhyavasāya-prakāśana-dvāreṇa śatru-gata-krodham eva puṣṇāti | kiṃ ca vimukhāprahāra-rūpātma-sambhāvanā-rūpa-garvasya asatya-bhīti-kalpanopabṛṃhaṇāt poṣo bhāvakānāṃ vairasyāya, na kevalaṃ svādābhāvāyeti nāsminn udāharaṇe garvasya sthāyitvam upapadyate |
body.translated_text: But there is no [independent] <s>garva</s> (pride) here. Rather, upon seeing the enemy who had previously been an aggressor and is now frightened, the nobility (<s>śobhā</s>) — a heroic <s>sāttvika-bhāva</s> of some warrior-sovereign — is perceived, expressed through the words 'I do not kill one facing away, fear not,' indicating compassion toward the lowly. Or, if [one argues that] he insults an enemy who is not really afraid [saying] 'if you are afraid then flee' — then let pride be granted. Even so, through the device of manifesting a mental determination in the form of an imagined false fear [in the enemy], it nourishes only the anger directed at the enemy. Moreover, the nourishment of this pride — in the form of self-regard expressed as not striking those who have turned away — through the supplementation of an imagined false fear, leads to distaste in the spectators, not merely to the absence of relish. Therefore, the permanent status of <s>garva</s> is not established in this example.

body.text: dhṛteḥ sthāyitvam api tenaivodāhṛtam, tathā hi-
body.translated_text: The permanent status of <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment) was also illustrated by him [<s>Bhoja</s>], as follows —

body.text:
sarvāḥ sampattayas tasya santuṣṭaṃ yasya mānasam |
upānad-gūḍha-pādasya nanu carmāstṛtaiva bhūḥ ||SRs_2.351|| (sa.ka.ā.) iti |
body.translated_text: 'All prosperity belongs to him whose mind is content; for one whose foot is covered by a shoe, is not the earth as if covered with leather?' ||2.351|| (from <s>Sāhitya-kaustubha-āloka</s>) Thus.

body.text: vyākṛtaṃ ca | atra kasyacid upaśānta-prakṛter dhīra-śānta-nāyakasya arthopagamana-mano' nukūla-dārādi-sampatter ālambana-vibhāva-bhūtāyāḥ samutpanno dhṛti-sthāyi-bhāvo vastu-tattvālocanādibhir uddīpana-vibhāvair uddīpyamānaḥ samupajāyamāna-smṛti-maty-ādibhir vyabhicāri-bhāvair vāg-ārambhādibhiś cānubhāvair anuṣajyamāno niṣpannaḥ śānto rasa iti gīyate | anye punar asya śamaṃ prakṛtim āmananti | sa tu dhṛter eva viśeṣo bhaviṣyatīti |
body.translated_text: And it was analyzed: Here, for a certain hero of tranquil nature, of the <s>Dhīra-śānta</s> (calm-steadfast) type, the permanent state of <s>dhṛti</s> (contentment), arising from the <s>ālambana-vibhāva</s> (foundational determinant) consisting of the fulfillment of aims, a mind in accord, a good wife, and the like — being stimulated by <s>uddīpana-vibhāvas</s> such as contemplation of the truth of things and the like, conjoined with arising <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> such as memory, judgment, and the like, and with <s>anubhāvas</s> such as verbal expression and the like — is said to ripen into the <s>Śānta</s> (Tranquil) sentiment. Others, however, hold <s>śama</s> (equanimity) to be its [the Śānta sentiment's] nature; but that would merely be a special case of <s>dhṛti</s> itself.

body.text: atra tāvad anukūla-dāra-siddhi-janitāyāḥ dhṛtes tu rati-paratantratvam ābāla-gopāla-prasiddham | nanu, vastutattvālocanādibhir asyāḥ sthāyitvaṃ kalpyate iti cet, na | naiḥspṛhya-vāsanā-vāsite bhāvaka-citte vibhāvādiṣv api naiḥsvpṛhyonmeṣād dhṛter mūla-ccheda-prasaṅgāt | artha-sampatti-janitā dhṛtis tu agṛdhnu-lakṣaṇa-lokottaratva-prāpti-vyavasāya-rūpam utsāham anusarantī vīropakaraṇatām āpnotīti nātra dhṛteḥ sthāyitvam | dhṛti-sthāyitva-nirākaraṇa-saṃrambheṇaiva naṣṭas tad-viṣayaḥ śama-sthāyī kutra vā līno na jñāyate |
body.translated_text: Here, first of all, the dependence of <s>dhṛti</s> born from the fulfillment of a congenial wife upon <s>rati</s> (love) is well-known to everyone from children to cowherds. If [one argues that] its permanent status is established through contemplation of the truth of things and the like — no, because when the spectators' minds are perfumed with the impression of desirelessness, the very emergence of desirelessness even toward the <s>vibhāvas</s> would cut <s>dhṛti</s> at its root. And <s>dhṛti</s> born from the attainment of wealth follows upon <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), which has the form of a resolve to attain the unworldly state characterized by freedom from greed — thus becoming an accessory of the Heroic sentiment. Hence <s>dhṛti</s> has no permanent status here. The <s>śama</s> (equanimity) posited as [Śānta's] permanent state — with the very vigor of the refutation of <s>dhṛti</s>'s permanence — has itself been destroyed; where it has disappeared to, one cannot tell.

body.text: mateḥ sthāyitvaṃ tenaivodāhṛtam | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: The permanent status of <s>mati</s> (judgment) was also illustrated by him [<s>Bhoja</s>], as follows —

body.text:
sādhāraṇyān nirātaṅkaḥ kanyām anyo' pi yācate |
kiṃ punar jagatāṃ jetā prapautraḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ ||SRs_2.352|| [ma.vī.ca. 1.31] iti |
body.translated_text: 'Since she [<s>Sītā</s>] is of common [eligibility], any other suitor may also ask for the maiden without apprehension; how much more so the conqueror of the worlds, the great-grandson of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)!' ||2.352|| [from <s>Mahāvīra-carita</s> 1.31] Thus.

body.text: vyākṛtaṃ ca-rāmasya udātta-prakṛter nisargata eva tattvābhiniveśinī matir nānya-viṣaye pravartate | na ca pravṛttā uparamati | sā ca sīteyaṃ mama svīkāra-yogyety evaṃ-rūpeṇa pravṛttā rāvaṇa-prārthanā-lakṣmaṇa-protsāhanābhyām uddīpyamānā samupajāyamāna-cintā-vitarka-vrīḍāvahittha-smṛty-ādibhiḥ kālocitottarānu-mīyamānair viveka-cāturya-dhairyaudāryādibhiḥ saṃsṛjyamānā udātta-rasa-rūpeṇa niṣpadyate iti |
body.translated_text: And it was analyzed: <s>Rāma</s>, being of sublime nature, has a judgment (<s>mati</s>) that by its very nature is devoted to truth and does not turn toward any other object; nor, once engaged, does it desist. That [<s>mati</s>], having been set in motion in the form of 'This <s>Sītā</s> is worthy of my acceptance,' being stimulated by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s suit and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s encouragement, conjoined with arising [<s>vyabhicārins</s>] such as thought, deliberation, modesty, concealment, memory, and the like, and with discrimination, cleverness, fortitude, magnanimity, and the like — inferred from contextually appropriate responses — ripens into the <s>Udātta</s> (Sublime) sentiment.

body.text: atra tāvat sītā-viṣayā ātma-svīkāra-yogyatva-niścaya-rūpā rāmasya matis tu rater utpatti-mātra-kāraṇam eva | tad-aniścaye rater anaucityāt | atra kanyāyāḥ sādhāraṇya-niścayo matiḥ | tasyāḥ sthāyitvam icchāma iti cet, na | sā hi rāvaṇa-viṣaya-lajjāsūyā-doṣa-nivāraṇa-dvāreṇa kārya-karaṇāparāṅmukhībhāva-lakṣaṇa-lokottara-tat-prāpti-vyavasāya-rūpā rāmotsāhaṃ bhāvakāsvāda-yogyatayā protsāhayati |
body.translated_text: Here, first of all, <s>Rāma</s>'s <s>mati</s> in the form of the determination that <s>Sītā</s> is worthy of his own acceptance is merely the initial cause of the arising of <s>rati</s> (love), since without that determination <s>rati</s> would be improper. Here, the <s>mati</s> consists in the determination that the maiden is of common eligibility. If one says 'we wish this to be the permanent state' — no, for it encourages <s>Rāma</s>'s enthusiasm, which has the form of a resolve to attain the unworldly goal of averting the faults of shame and envy directed toward <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, through the turning away from contrary action — and thus nourishes that enthusiasm in a manner fit for the spectators' relish.

body.text:
tad aṣṭāv eva vijñeyāḥ sthāyino muni-saṃmatāḥ |
sthāyino' ṣṭau trayastriṃśac cāriṇo' ṣṭau ca sāttvikāḥ ||SRs_2.353|| 161
evam ekonapañcāśad bhāvāḥ syur militā ime |
evaṃ hi sthāyino bhāvān siṃha-bhūpatir abhyadhāt ||SRs_2.354|| 162
athaiṣāṃ rasa-rūpatvam ucyate siṃha-bhūbhujā |
vidvan-mānasa-haṃsena rasa-bhāva-vivekinā ||SRs_2.355|| 163
ete ca sthāyinaḥ svaiḥ svair vibhāvair vyabhicāribhiḥ |
sāttvikaiś cānubhāvaiś ca naṭābhinaya-yogataḥ ||SRs_2.356|| 164
sākṣātkāram ivānītāḥ prāpitāḥ svādu-rūpatām |
sāmājikānāṃ manasi prayānti rasa-rūpatām ||SRs_2.357|| 165
dadhyādi-vyañjana-dravyaiś ciñcādibhir athauṣadhaiḥ |
guḍādi-madhura-dravyair yathā-yogaṃ samanvitaiḥ ||SRs_2.358|| 166
yadvat pāka-viśeṣeṇa ṣāḍavākhyo rasaḥ paraḥ |

children.translated_text: so too <s>rasa</s> is produced from <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like through [dramatic] performance. 167
This, which is a fusion of bliss, is experienced by the spectators. ||2.359||

body.translated_text: Therefore, only eight permanent states should be recognized, as approved by the sages. The eight permanent states, the thirty-three transitory states, and the eight <s>sāttvika</s> [states] — ||2.353|| 161 thus these <s>bhāvas</s>, combined together, amount to forty-nine. Thus has King <s>Siṃha-bhūpati</s> expounded the permanent states. ||2.354|| 162 Now, their transformation into <s>rasa</s> is described by <s>Siṃha-bhūbhuj</s>, the royal swan of the lake of the learned, the discerner of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>. ||2.355|| 163 These permanent states, through their respective <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>vyabhicārins</s>, <s>sāttvika</s> [bhāvas], and <s>anubhāvas</s>, by means of the actors' performance, ||2.356|| 164 are brought as it were to direct perception, made to attain the form of relish, and become <s>rasa</s> in the minds of the audience. ||2.357|| 165 Just as through a special cooking process, from curds and other seasoning substances, <s>ciñcā</s> (tamarind) and other spices, and <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) and other sweet substances, combined in proper proportion — ||2.358|| 166 the supreme confection called <s>ṣāḍava</s> is produced,

body.text: nanu nāyaka-niṣṭhasya sthāyi-prakarṣa-lakṣaṇasya rasasya sāmājikānubhava-yogyatā nopapadyate | anya-bhavasya tasyānyānubhavāyogāt iti cet satyam | ko vā nāyaka-gataṃ rasam ācaṣṭe | tathā hi-sa ca nāyako dṛṣṭaḥ śruto' nukṛto vā rasasyāśrayatām ālambate | nādyaḥ | sākṣād dṛṣṭa-nāyaka-ratyāder vrīḍā-jugupsādi-pratīpa-phalatvena svādābhāvāt | na dvitīya-tṛtīyau | tayor avidyamānatvāt | na hy asati āśraye tad-āśritasyāvasthānam upapadyate |
body.translated_text: Now, [one may object:] the fitness for experience by the audience of <s>rasa</s>, which is characterized as the culmination of the permanent state residing in the hero, is not tenable — since what belongs to another person cannot be experienced by someone else. True; but who claims that <s>rasa</s> resides in the hero? For the hero, whether seen, heard of, or imitated, serves as the substrate of <s>rasa</s>. Not the first [directly seen], because the direct perception of the hero's <s>rati</s> and the like, resulting in counter-productive effects such as shame and disgust, would preclude relish. Not the second or third [heard of or imitated], because they [the hero] do not [actually] exist [before the audience]. For it is not tenable that what depends on a substrate can persist when that substrate does not exist.

body.text: nanu bhavatu nāmaivam | tathāpi rasasya naṭa-gatatve na sāmājikānubhavānupapattir iti cet, na | naṭe rasa-sambhavaḥ kim anubhāvādi-sad-bhāvena vibhāvādi-sambhavena vā | nādyaḥ, abhyāsa-pāṭavādināpi tat-siddheḥ | kiṃ ca sāmājikeṣu yathocitam anubhāva-sadbhāve' pi tvayā teṣāṃ rasāśrayatānaṅgīkārāt | yadi vibhāvena tatrāpi kim anukārya-mālavikādinā (uta) anukāriṇā svakāntādinā vā | nādyaḥ, anaucityāt | nāpi dvitīyaḥ, naṭe sākṣād-dṛṣṭa-nāyakavad aślīlatā-pratīteḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, let that be so; still, if <s>rasa</s> resides in the actor, the impossibility of the audience's experience does not follow — if one argues thus, no. Does <s>rasa</s> arise in the actor through the presence of <s>anubhāvas</s> and the like, or through the occurrence of <s>vibhāvas</s>?
