Not the first, since that [the display of anubhāvas] can be achieved even through the skill of practiced rehearsal. Moreover, even though the <s>anubhāvas</s> appropriately exist in the audience members, you [the opponent] do not accept that they [the audience] are the substrates of <s>rasa</s>. If through the <s>vibhāva</s> — then is it through the imitated character such as <s>Mālavikā</s> and the like, or through the imitator's own beloved and the like? Not the first, because of impropriety. Nor the second, because [then] the same objectionable directness as with a hero seen in person would be perceived in the actor.

body.text: nanu, mālāvikādi-vibhāva-viśeṣasyānaucityāt (sva-vi-)bhāvasyāsaṃnihitatvāt (sannihitatve' pi sākṣād-dṛṣṭa-nāyakavad aślīlatā-pratīteḥ) ca sāmājikānām api naṭavad eva rasān āśrayatvaṃ prasajyate iti cet, atra kecana samādadhate-
body.translated_text: Now, if [one argues that] since the specific <s>vibhāva</s> of <s>Mālavikā</s> and the like is improper [for the audience], and since [the audience's] own <s>vibhāva</s> is not present (or even if present, the same objectionable directness as with a directly-seen hero would be perceived), therefore the audience members too, just like the actor, would be substrates of <s>rasa</s> — to this, some [scholars] respond:

body.text: vibhāvādi-bhāvānām anapekṣita-bāhya-sattvānāṃ śabdopadhānād evāsādita-sad-bhāvānām anukāryāpekṣayā niḥsādhāraṇānām api kāvye nāṭye ca abhidhā-paryāyeṇa sādhāraṇīkaraṇātmanā bhāvanā-vyāpāreṇa sva-sambandhitayā vibhāvitānāṃ sākṣād bhāvaka-cetasi viparivartamānānām ālambanatvādy-avirodhād anaucityādi-viplava-rahitaḥ sthāyī nirbharānanda-viśrānti-svabhāvena bhogena bhāvakair bhujyate iti |
body.translated_text: The <s>Vibhāvas</s> and other emotional factors — which do not depend on external realities but whose existence is established solely through the medium of words, which are unique with respect to the characters being imitated — are, in poetry and drama alike, through the process of <s>Bhāvanā</s> (creative contemplation), which is the universalization (<s>sādhāraṇīkaraṇa</s>) effected by the mode of denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), presented as related to oneself, and they directly revolve in the mind of the connoisseur. Since there is no contradiction in their functioning as <s>Ālambanā</s> (foundational causes) and the like, and since there is no violation of propriety (<s>aucitya</s>) or other flaws, the <s>Sthāyī</s> (permanent sentiment) is enjoyed by the connoisseurs through a relishing (<s>bhoga</s>) whose nature is repose in unalloyed bliss.

body.text: anye tv anyathā samādhānam āhuḥ | loke pramadādi-kāraṇādibhiḥ sthāyy-anumāne abhyāsa-pāṭavavatāṃ sahṛdayānāṃ kāvye nāṭye ca vibhāvādi-pada-vyapadeśyaiḥ (mamaivaite śatror evaite taṭasthasyaivaite na mamaivaite na śatror evaite na taṭasthasyaivaite iti sambandha-viśeṣa-svīkāra-parihāra-niyamān adhyavasāyāt) sva-sambandhitvena anya-sambandhitvena ca sādhāraṇyāt pratītair abhivyaktībhūto vāsanātmatayā sthitaḥ sthāyī ratyādiḥ pānaka-rasa-nyāyena carvyamāṇo lokottara-camatkāra-kārī paramānandam iva kandalayan rasa-rūpatām āpnotīti |
body.translated_text: Others, however, offer a different resolution. In worldly experience, for connoisseurs who have attained facility through practice in inferring the <s>Sthāyī</s> (permanent sentiment) from causes such as beautiful women and the like — in poetry and drama, through those designated by the terms <s>Vibhāva</s> and the like (with the definite determination of accepting or rejecting specific relations: 'these belong to me alone,' 'these to the enemy alone,' 'these to the neutral party alone,' 'these do not belong to me,' etc.), through universalization as related to oneself and to others — the <s>Sthāyī</s> such as <s>Rati</s> (love) and others, existing in the form of latent impressions (<s>Vāsanā</s>), manifested [through this process], being savored according to the maxim of the juice of a beverage (<s>pānaka-rasa-nyāya</s>), producing a supramundane aesthetic wonder (<s>lokottara-camatkāra</s>), blossoming as it were into supreme bliss — attain the status of <s>Rasa</s>.

body.text: evaṃ ca bhukti-vyakti-pakṣayor ubhayor api sāmājikānāṃ rasāśrayatvopapatter anyatara-pakṣa-parigrahāgrahād udāsmahe |
body.translated_text: Thus, since the connoisseurs' status as the locus of <s>Rasa</s> is established on both the enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>) and manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) views, we remain neutral, without insisting on adopting either position.

body.text: prāyeṇa bhāratīya-matānusāriṇāṃ prakriyā tu (ittham)-loke kāraṇa-kārya-sahakāritām upagataiḥ kāvye nāṭye vā sarasa-sūkti-sudhā-mādhurī-dhurīṇair yathoktābhinaya-sametair vā padārthatvena vibhāvānubhāva-sañcāri-vyapadeśaṃ prāpitaiḥ nāyikā-nāyaka-candra-candrikā-malayānilādi-bhrū-vikṣepa-kaṭākṣa-pāta-sveda-romāñcādi-nirveda-harṣādi-rūpair vāsanātmakair ātma-sambandhitvenābhi-matair bhāvaiḥ dharma-kīrti-ratānāṃ ṣaḍ-aṅga-nāṭya-samaya-jñānāṃ nānā-deśa-veṣa-bhāṣā-vicakṣaṇānāṃ nikhila-kalā-kalāpa-kovidānāṃ santyakta-matsarāṇāṃ sakala-siddhānta-vedināṃ rasa-bhāva-vivecakānāṃ kāvyārtha-nihita-cetasāṃ sāmājikānāṃ manasi mudrā-muditra-nyāyena viparitvartitāḥ vāsitāś cābhivardhitāḥ sthāyino bhāvāḥ (vākyārtha-sthānīyāḥ) kāvyārthatvenābhimatāḥ bāhyārthāvalambanātmakāḥ santo vikāsa-vistara-kṣobha-vikṣepātmakatayā vibhinnāḥ tat-tad-rūpeṇa (raty-utsāhādi-rūpeṇa sāmājikaiḥ) āsvādyamānāḥ paramānanda-rūpatām āpnuvantīti sakala-sahṛdaya-saṃvedana-siddhasya rasasya pramāṇāntareṇa saṃsādhana-pariśramaḥ śrotṛ-jana-citta-kṣobhāya na kevalaṃ, pratyuta nopayogāyeti prakṛtam anusarāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The procedure generally followed by those adhering to the <s>Bhāratīya</s> (Bharata's) school is thus: the <s>Sthāyī-bhāvas</s> (permanent sentiments) — which are regarded as having the nature of latent impressions (<s>Vāsanā</s>) and as related to oneself — [are awakened] in poetry and drama by entities designated as <s>Vibhāvas</s>, <s>Anubhāvas</s>, and <s>Vyabhicārī-bhāvas</s> (the hero and heroine, moonlight, the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, brow-furrowing, sidelong glances, perspiration, horripilation, world-weariness, joy, etc.) — whether these be the sweetness of poetic nectar or accompanied by appropriate acting — in the minds of qualified connoisseurs (<s>Sāmājikas</s>) who are devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, fame, and aesthetic pleasure, versed in the conventions of the six-limbed drama, skilled in the various regional costumes and dialects, proficient in all the arts, free from envy, knowledgeable in all philosophical doctrines, capable of discerning <s>Rasas</s> and <s>Bhāvas</s>, and whose minds are absorbed in poetic meaning — [these <s>Sthāyī-bhāvas</s>], according to the principle of a stamp and its impression (<s>mudrā-mudrita-nyāya</s>), are revolved, pervaded, and intensified; standing as the equivalents of the composite meaning of sentences; regarded as poetic meaning; having external objects as their foundation; being differentiated as expansion, extension, agitation, and dispersal; being savored in their respective forms (as <s>Rati</s>, <s>Utsāha</s>, etc., by the connoisseurs) — they attain the form of supreme bliss. Therefore, [since] <s>Rasa</s>, which is established through the experience of all sensitive hearts, [needs no further proof,] the labor of establishing it through other means of knowledge would not merely [produce] agitation in the minds of the audience, but would actually be of no use at all. So we follow the main subject.

body.text: aṣṭadhā sa ca śṛṅgāra-hāsya-vīrādbhutā api | 168
body.translated_text: And <s>Rasa</s> is eightfold: <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>Hāsya</s> (comic), <s>Vīra</s> (heroic), <s>Adbhuta</s> (wondrous),

body.text: raudraḥ karuṇa-bībhatsau bhayānaka itīritaḥ ||SRs_2.360||
body.translated_text: <s>Raudra</s> (furious), <s>Karuṇa</s> (compassionate), <s>Bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), and <s>Bhayānaka</s> (terrible) — thus declared. ||SRs_2.360||

body.text: eṣūttaras tu pūrvasmāt sambhūto viṣamāt samaḥ | 169
body.translated_text: Among these, each succeeding one is born from the preceding one, though unequal [in nature], they are [treated as] equal.

body.text: bahu-vaktavyatā-hetoḥ sakalāhlādanād api ||SRs_2.361||
body.translated_text: Because of the need for extensive discussion and because of its power to delight all, ||SRs_2.361||

body.text: raseṣu tatra śṛṅgāraḥ prathamaṃ lakṣyate sphuṭam | 170
body.translated_text: among the <s>Rasas</s>, <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) is clearly examined first.

body.text: vibhāvair anubhāvaiś ca sāttvikair vyabhicāribhiḥ ||SRs_2.362||
body.translated_text: Through <s>Vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>Anubhāvas</s> (consequent reactions), <s>Sāttvika</s> (involuntary psychophysical reactions), and <s>Vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions), ||SRs_2.362||

body.text: nītā sadasya-rasyatvaṃ ratiḥ śṛṅgāra ucyate | 171
body.translated_text: <s>Rati</s> (love), when brought to the state of being relishable by the audience, is called <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>.

body.text: sa vipralambhaḥ sambhoga iti dvedhā nigadyate ||SRs_2.363||
body.translated_text: It is declared to be twofold: <s>Vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) and <s>Sambhoga</s> (love-in-union). ||SRs_2.363||

body.text: ayuktayos taruṇayor yo' nurāgaḥ parasparam | 172
body.translated_text: The mutual love of a young couple who are not [yet] united,

body.text: abhīṣṭāliṅganādīnām anavāptau prakṛṣyate ||SRs_2.364||
body.translated_text: which intensifies when the desired embraces and the like are not attained — ||SRs_2.364||

body.text: sa vipralambho vijñeyaḥ sa caturdhā nigadyate | 173
body.translated_text: that should be known as <s>Vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation); and it is declared to be fourfold:

body.text: pūrvānurāga-mānau ca pravāsa-karuṇāv iti ||SRs_2.365||
body.translated_text: <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> (prior love), <s>Māna</s> (love-pride), <s>Pravāsa</s> (separation by travel), and <s>Karuṇā</s> (pathos of separation). ||SRs_2.365||

body.text: atrāyam arthaḥ-nāyikā-nāyakayoḥ prāg-asaṅgatayoḥ saṅgata-viyuktayor vā (parasparam anuraktayoḥ) svocita-vibhāvair anubhāviś copajāyamānaḥ parasparānurāgo' nyatarānurāgo vā svābhilaṣitāliṅganādīnām anavāptau satyām utpadyamānair vyabhicāribhir anubhāvaiś ca prakṛṣyamāṇo vipralambha-śṛṅgāra ity ākhyāyate | sa ca pūrvānurāgādi-bhedena cāturvidhyam āpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here the meaning is: the mutual love — or the love of one of the two — arising between the hero and heroine who have either not yet met or who have met and been separated, [both being] attached to each other, produced by appropriate <s>Vibhāvas</s> and <s>Anubhāvas</s>, intensified by <s>Vyabhicārī-bhāvas</s> and <s>Anubhāvas</s> arising when the desired embraces and the like are not attained — is called <s>Vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment in separation). And it assumes a fourfold nature through the distinctions of <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> and so forth.

body.text: tatra pūrvānurāgaḥ-

children.translated_text: The affection that [arises] prior to union, through seeing, hearing, and the like —
that should be known as <s>Pūrvānurāga</s>. 'Hearing' means learning of the beloved's qualities. ||SRs_2.366||

body.translated_text: Among these, <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> (prior love) —

body.text:
śravaṇena pūrvānurāgo, yathā-
sādhu tvayā tarkitam etad eva
svenānalaṃ yat kila saṃśrayiṣye |
vināmunā svātmani tu prahartuṃ
mṛṣā-giraṃ tvāṃ nṛpatau na kuryām ||SRs_2.367|| (naiṣadhīye 3.77)
body.translated_text: <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> through hearing, for example — 'You have rightly surmised this very thing — that I shall not take refuge in my own [resources] alone. But to make you, [O swan,] speak falsely about the king in order to strike at my own [pride] — [that I shall not do].' ||SRs_2.367|| (<s>Naiṣadhīya</s> 3.77)

body.text: atra haṃsa-mukhān nala-guṇa-śravaṇena damayantyāḥ pūrvānurāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Damayantī</s>'s <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> arises through hearing of <s>Nala</s>'s virtues from the mouth of the swan.

body.text: pratyakṣa-citra-svapnādau darśanaṃ darśanaṃ matam ||367|| 175
body.translated_text: Seeing means seeing directly, in a painting, in a dream, and the like. ||

body.text:
pratyakṣa-darśanād, yathā-
taṃ vīkṣya sarvāvayavānavadyaṃ
nyavartanānyopagamāt kumārī |
na hi praphullaṃ sahakāram etya
vṛkṣāntaraṃ kāṅkṣati ṣaṭ-padālī ||SRs_2.368|| (ra.vaṃ. 6.69)
body.translated_text: Through direct seeing, for example — 'Having seen him, faultless in every limb, the maiden turned back from approaching any other — for the row of bees, having reached a mango tree in full bloom, does not desire any other tree.' ||SRs_2.368|| (<s>Raghu-vaṃśa</s> 6.69)

body.text:
citra-darśanena, yathā-
līlāvadhūta-kamalā kalayantī pakṣapātam adhikaṃ naḥ |
mānasam upaiti keyaṃ citra-gatā rājahaṃsīva ||SRs_2.369|| (ratnāvalī 2.8)
body.translated_text: Through seeing in a painting, for example — 'Playfully waving aside the lotus, showing greater partiality toward us — who is she that enters the mind, like a royal swan depicted in a painting?' ||SRs_2.369|| (<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.8)

body.text: atra citragata-ratnāvalī-darśanād vatsa-rājasya pūrvānurāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Vatsa-rāja</s>'s <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> arises through seeing <s>Ratnāvalī</s> in a painting.

children.translated_text: Through seeing in a dream, for example —

children.text: svapne dṛṣṭākārā tam api samādāya gatavatī bhavatī |
children.translated_text: 'O lady, you who appeared in my dream have taken away even that [dream-form] and departed!

children.text: anyam upāyaṃ na labhe prasīda rambhoru dāsāya ||SRs_2.370||
children.translated_text: I find no other means — be gracious, O beautiful-thighed one, to your servant!' ||SRs_2.370||

body.text: atra kām api svapne dṛṣṭavataḥ kasyacin nāyakasya pūrvānurāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, a certain hero's <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> arises through having seen some woman in a dream.

body.text:
yataḥ pūrvānurāgo' yaṃ saṅkalpātmā pravartate |
so' yaṃ pūrvānurāgākhyo vipralambha itīritaḥ ||SRs_2.371|| 176
pāratantryād ayaṃ dvedhā daiva-mānuṣa-kalpanāt |
tatra sañcāriṇo glāniḥ śaṅkāsūye śramo bhayam ||SRs_2.372|| 177
nirvedautsukya-dainyāni cintā-nidre prabodhatā |
viṣādo jaḍatonmādo moho maraṇam eva ca ||SRs_2.373|| 178
body.translated_text: Since this <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> proceeds in the form of imagination (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), this love-in-separation called <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> is thus declared. ||SRs_2.371|| It is twofold due to dependence: through the agency of fate (<s>daiva</s>) and of human effort (<s>mānuṣa</s>). Among these, the <s>Vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) are: languor, apprehension, jealousy, fatigue, fear, ||SRs_2.372|| world-weariness, eager longing, pitifulness, anxiety, sleep, wakefulness, despondency, stupefaction, madness, ||SRs_2.373|| disease, torpor, and death — these, in sequence. ||SRs_2.378||

body.text:
tatra daiva-pāratantryeṇa, yathā-
śailātmajāpi pitur ucchiraso' bhilāṣaṃ
vyarthaṃ samarthya lalitaṃ vapur ātmanaś ca |
sakhyoḥ samakṣam iti cādhika-jāta-lajjā
śūnyā jagāma bhavanābhimukhī kathaṃcit ||SRs_2.374|| (ku.saṃ. 3.75)
body.translated_text: Among these, through dependence on fate, for example — 'The daughter of the mountain (<s>Pārvatī</s>), having reflected that her father's lofty desire was in vain, and [considering] also her own graceful person — and being additionally shy before her companions — somehow went homeward, empty [of hope].' ||SRs_2.374|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.75)

body.text: atra janakādy-ānukūlye' pi daiva-pāratantryeṇa pārvatyāḥ pūrvānurāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, even though her father and others are favorable, <s>Pārvatī</s>'s <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> [is characterized by] dependence on fate.

body.text: mānuṣa-pāratantryeṇa, yathā-
body.translated_text: Through dependence on human agency, for example —

body.text:
dullaho pio me tasmiṃ bhava hiaa ṇirāsaṃ
ammo apaṃgo me paripphurai kiṃ bi vāmo |
eso so cira-diṭṭho kahaṃ uṇa dakkhidabbo
ṇāha maṃ parāhīṇaṃ tui parigaṇaa satiṇhaṃ ||SRs_2.375|| (mā.a.mi. 2.4)
body.translated_text: 'My beloved is hard to obtain — in him, O heart, be without hope!

children.translated_text: [Chāyā translation:] My beloved is hard to obtain — in him, O heart, be without hope!

children.text: amho apāṅgo me parisphurati kim api vāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: Ah, my sidelong glance flutters strangely to the left!

children.text: eṣa sa cira-dṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃ punar draṣṭavyaḥ
children.translated_text: He, long-seen — how shall he be seen again?

children.text: nātha māṃ parādhīnāṃ tvayi parigaṇaya satṛṣṇām ||]
children.translated_text: O lord, consider me, dependent on others, thirsting for you!' ||SRs_2.375|| (<s>Mālatī-Ādhūni-Mitram</s> 2.4)

body.text: atra (catuṣpada-vastuke gīte) devayānī-pāratantryeṇa śarmiṣṭhāyāḥ yayāti-viṣayaḥ pūrvānurāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here (in a four-footed song), <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>'s <s>Pūrvānurāga</s> directed toward <s>Yayāti</s>, [arising from] her dependence on <s>Devayānī</s>.

body.text:
etasminn abhilāṣādi maraṇāntam anekadhā |
tat-tat-sañcāri-bhāvānām utkaṭatvād daśā bhavet ||SRs_2.376|| 179
tathāpi prāktanair asyā daśāvasthāḥ samāsataḥ |
proktās tad-anurodhena tāsāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate ||SRs_2.377|| 180
abhilāṣaś cintānusmṛti-guṇa-saṅkīrtanodvegāḥ |
savilāpā unmāda-vyādhī jaḍatā mṛtiś ca tāḥ kramaśaḥ ||SRs_2.378|| 181
body.translated_text: In this [<s>Pūrvānurāga</s>], from longing to death, the stages arise in many forms due to the intensity of the respective <s>Vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s>. ||SRs_2.376|| Nevertheless, the ancients have stated the ten stages of this [<s>Pūrvānurāga</s>] in summary; following them, their characteristics are stated. ||SRs_2.377|| Longing, anxiety, recollection, enumeration of virtues, agitation, lamentation, madness, disease, torpor, and death — these, in order. ||SRs_2.378||

body.text:
tatra abhilāṣaḥ-
saṅgamopāya-racita-prārabdha-vyavasāyataḥ |
saṅkalpecchā-samudbhūtir abhilāṣo' tra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.379|| 182
praveśa-nirgamau tūṣṇīṃ tad-dṛṣṭi-patha-gāminau |

children.translated_text: activities aimed at revealing one's passion, self-adornment,

children.text: vyājoktayaś ca vijane sthitir ity evam ādayaḥ ||SRs_2.380||
children.translated_text: speaking through pretexts, lingering in solitary places, and the like. ||SRs_2.380||

body.translated_text: Among these, longing (<s>abhilāṣa</s>) — The emergence of desire born of imagination, from the undertaking of resolute efforts to devise means for union, is longing. The reactions therein are: ||SRs_2.379|| silent entering and exiting [to place oneself] in the path of the beloved's gaze,

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'With steady, unquivering [glances], their modesty-fragrance shattered by sighs,
overflowing with delight, companioned by startled-doe glances,
intense with eagerness, betraying the secret vital points of the wave of love —
with such sidelong glances, a certain woman gazed upon the lord <s>Siṃha-kṣmā-ramaṇa</s>.' ||SRs_2.381||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra rāga-prakāśana-parair dṛṣṭi-viśeṣair nāyake kasyāścid abhilāṣo vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, through special glances aimed at revealing passion, a certain woman's longing for the hero is expressed.

body.text: atha cintā-

children.translated_text: 'By what means shall success [come]? When shall the meeting with him [occur]?

children.text: dūtī-mukhena kiṃ vācyam ity ādy ūhas tu cintanam ||SRs_2.382||
children.translated_text: What should be said through a messenger's mouth?' — such deliberation is called anxiety. ||SRs_2.382||

body.translated_text: Now anxiety (<s>cintā</s>) —

body.text: atra nīvyādi-saṃsparśaḥ śayyāyāṃ parivartanam | 185
body.translated_text: Herein [the reactions are]: touching the waist-band and such, tossing on the bed,

body.text:
sa-bāṣpākekarā dṛṣṭir mudrikādi-vivartanam |
nirlakṣya-vīkṣaṇaṃ caivam ādyā vikṛtayo matāḥ ||SRs_2.383|| 186
body.translated_text: a tearful one-eyed glance, turning of a ring, aimless gazing — these and similar disturbances are recognized. ||SRs_2.383||

body.text: yathā-

children.text: udyānaṃ kim upāgatāsmi sukṛtī devo na kiṃ darśitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Have I come to the garden for nothing? Has the fortunate lord not been shown [to me]?

children.text: śrī-siṃhaḥ sva-sakhī-mukhena sa kathaṃ neyaḥ sa kiṃ vakṣyati |
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Siṃha</s> — how shall he be led [here] through a companion? What will he say?

children.text: siddhyet tena kadā samāgama iti dhyānena savyākulā
children.translated_text: When shall union with him be achieved?' — thus agitated with meditation,

children.text: śayyāyāṃ parivartane śvasiti ca kṣiptvā kapolaṃ kare ||SRs_2.384||
children.translated_text: she sighs on the bed, tossing and turning, resting her cheek on her hand. ||SRs_2.384||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha anusmṛtiḥ-
arthānām anubhūtānāṃ deśa-kālānuvartinām | sāntatyena parāmarśo mānasaḥ syād anusmṛtiḥ ||SRs_2.385|| 187
tatrānubhāvā niḥśvāso dhyāṇaṃ kṛtya-vihastatā |
śayyāsanādi-vidveṣa ity ādyāḥ smara-kalpitāḥ ||SRs_2.386|| 188
body.translated_text: Now recollection (<s>anusmṛti</s>) — the continuous mental reviewing of things previously experienced, in accordance with their place and time, is called recollection. ||SRs_2.385|| The <s>Anubhāvas</s> therein are: sighing, meditation, helplessness in performing duties, aversion to bed and seat, and the like — these are produced by <s>Smara</s> (the God of Love). ||SRs_2.386||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Remembering again and again that moment when the activities of King <s>Annapota Siṃha</s>
were closely associated with the rites of worshipping the King of Love (<s>Kāma</s>),

children.text: smāraṃ smāram amuṃ kṣaṇaṃ śaśimukhī śvāsair vivarṇādharā
children.translated_text: tracing the threads of his passion — the moon-faced one, her lower lip pale from sighing,

children.text: nānyat kāṅkṣati karma kartum ucitaṃ nāste na śete kvacit ||SRs_2.387||
children.translated_text: desires no other appropriate task to perform, neither sits nor lies down anywhere.' ||SRs_2.387||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atah guṇa-kīrtanam-
saundaryādi-guṇa-ślāghā guṇa-kīrtanam atra tu |

children.translated_text: horripilation, faltering speech, gazing slow with emotion,
thinking of union with him, perspiration on the cheeks in the presence of a companion, and the like. ||SRs_2.388||

body.translated_text: Now the enumeration of virtues (<s>guṇa-kīrtana</s>) — the praising of qualities such as beauty and the like is enumeration of virtues. Herein [the reactions are]:

body.text: yathā-

children.text: kiṃ kāmena kim indunā surabhiṇā kiṃ vā jayantena kiṃ
children.translated_text: 'What is <s>Kāma</s> (the God of Love)? What is the moon? What is the fragrant [spring]? What is <s>Jayanta</s>?
By my good fortune, the beauty of King <s>Annapota Siṃha</s> has been beheld by me!'
'Others [are fit] only for his service' — saying thus with horripilation, the beautiful-eyed one,
her cheek-surface perspiring, her words faltering, praises [him] before her companion. ||SRs_2.389||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atha udvegaḥ-

children.text: manasaḥ kampa udvegaḥ kathitas tatra vikriyāḥ | 190
children.translated_text: The trembling of the mind is called agitation. The disturbances therein are:

children.text:
cintā santāpa-niḥśvāsau dveṣaḥ śayyāsanādiṣu |
stambha-cintāśru-vaivarṇya-dīnatvādaya īritāḥ ||SRs_2.390|| 191
children.translated_text: anxiety, sighing from anguish, aversion to bed and seat, rigidity, anxious tears, pallor, pitifulness, and the like are declared. ||SRs_2.390||

body.translated_text: Now agitation (<s>udvega</s>) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'When the kings have departed for the service of King <s>Annapota Siṃha</s>,
and their wives are delayed, with minds agitated by the shining [memory of their men],
with lower lips wilted from sighing, tears welling up and obstructed,

children.text: kāmaṃ snigdha-sakhī-jane viracitā dīnā dṛśor vṛttayaḥ ||SRs_2.391||
children.translated_text: pitiful movements of the eyes are directed, as one pleases, toward the circle of dear companions.' ||SRs_2.391||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha vilāpaḥ-
iha me dṛk-pathaṃ prāpad ihātiṣṭhad ihāsta ca |
ihālapad ihāvātsīd ihaiva nyavṛtat tathā ||SRs_2.392|| 192
ity ādi-vākya-vinyāso vilāpa iti kīrtitaḥ |

children.text: tatra ceṣṭās tu kutrāpi gamanaṃ kvacid īkṣaṇam | 193
children.translated_text: Its actions therein are: going here and there, looking in various directions,

children.text: kvacit kvacid avasthānaṃ kvacic ca bhramaṇādayaḥ ||SRs_2.393||
children.translated_text: standing in various places, and wandering about, and so forth. ||SRs_2.393||

body.translated_text: Now <s>vilāpa</s> (lamentation) — 'Here my gaze fell upon him, here he stood, here he sat, here he spoke, here he stayed, and here indeed he turned back.' ||SRs_2.392|| Such and similar verbal expressions are celebrated as <s>vilāpa</s> (lamentation).

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Here was King <s>Anapota-siṃha</s>, there was I; in this bower of creepers

children.text: kuñje sādaram īkṣitāham iha mam ānandayan sa smitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: he looked at me with affection; here he gladdened me with smiles' —

children.text: ity ālāpavatī vilokitam api vyālokate sambhramād
children.translated_text: thus speaking, she gazes even at what she has already seen, in her agitation

children.text: yātaṃ yāti ca satvarā taru-talaṃ līlāta ekākinī ||SRs_2.394||
children.translated_text: she goes hastily where he has gone, to the foot of the tree, sporting alone. ||SRs_2.394||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atha unmādaḥ-

children.translated_text: In all conditions, everywhere, being always absorbed in thoughts of him,

children.text: atasmiṃs tad iti bhrāntir unmādo virahodbhavaḥ ||SRs_2.395||
children.translated_text: the delusion of perceiving him where he is not — that is <s>unmāda</s> (delirium), born of separation. ||SRs_2.395||

body.translated_text: Now <s>unmāda</s> (delirium) —

body.text: tatra ceṣṭās tu vijñeyā dveṣaḥ sveṣṭe' pi vastuni | 195
body.translated_text: Its actions therein should be known as: aversion even toward beloved objects,

body.text:
dīrghaṃ muhuś ca niḥśvāso nirnimeṣatayā sthitiḥ |
nirnimitta-smita-dhyāna-gāna-maunādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.396|| 196
body.translated_text: long and frequent sighing, standing with unblinking gaze, causeless smiling, meditation, singing, silence, and so forth. ||SRs_2.396||

children.translated_text: From longing, having drawn the form of King <s>Anapota-siṃha</s>, she

children.text: nirvarṇyāyam asau mama priya iti premābhiyoga-bhramāt |
children.translated_text: gazed at it [saying] 'This is my beloved' — and from the delusion of the force of love,

children.text: āśūtthāya tato' pasṛtya tarasā kiṃcid vivṛttānanā
children.translated_text: rising suddenly, withdrawing hastily, her face slightly turned —
she gazes with jealousy, with gentle smiling, with startlement, and with longing. ||SRs_2.397||

body.text:
atha vyādhiḥ-
abhīṣṭa-saṅgamābhāvād vyādhiḥ santāpa-lakṣaṇaḥ |
atra santāpa-niḥśvāsau śīta-vastu-niṣevaṇam ||SRs_2.398|| 197
jīvitopekṣaṇaṃ moho mumūrṣā dhṛti-varjanam |
yatra kvacic ca patanaṃ srastākṣatvādayo' pi ca ||SRs_2.399|| 198
body.translated_text: Now <s>vyādhi</s> (love-sickness) — From the absence of union with the desired one, the sickness characterized by burning — its [actions] therein are burning and sighing, the seeking of cool substances, ||SRs_2.398|| indifference to life, delusion, desire for death, abandonment of fortitude, falling down here and there, drooping eyes, and so forth. ||SRs_2.399||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: When the mind was attached to longing for union with King <s>Anapota-siṃha</s>,
the limbs of the beautiful-bodied one, ignited by the fire of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the God of Love), were in distress;
her companions anointed them with sandalwood paste mixed with cool sand,
and fanned her palms with leaf-fans, again and again extinguishing [the heat]. ||SRs_2.400||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atha jaḍatā-
idam iṣṭam aniṣṭaṃ tad iti vetti na kiñcana |
nottaraṃ bhāṣate praśne nekṣate na śṛṇoti ca ||SRs_2.401|| 199
yatra dhyāyati niḥsaṃjñaṃ jaḍatā sā prakīrtitā |

children.translated_text: Its [expressions] therein are: insensitivity to touch, pallor, limpness of limbs,
spontaneous sighing, rigidity, breathing, and emaciation, and so forth. ||SRs_2.402||

body.translated_text: Now <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupefaction) — She understands nothing — neither 'this is desired' nor 'that is undesired'; she does not reply to questions, does not look, does not hear, ||SRs_2.401|| and meditates in a state of unconsciousness — that is called <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupefaction).

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Overtaken by resolves concerning King <s>Anapota-siṃha</s>, whose sprouts have taken deep root,

children.text: ākrāntā tanutāṃ gatā smara-śaraiḥ śāteva śātodarī |
children.translated_text: the slender-waisted one, reduced to thinness by the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (the God of Love), as if cut down —

children.text: asman-mūlam idaṃ tanutvam iti kiṃ lajjālase locane
children.translated_text: 'This thinness is caused by us' — as if from shame, her languid eyes
have attained the covering of their eyelid-sheaths; let the banner of <s>Ratipati</s> (the God of Love) unfurl! ||SRs_2.403||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atha maraṇaṃ-

children.text: tais taiḥ kṛtaiḥ pratīkārair yadi na syāt samāgamaḥ | 201
children.translated_text: If, despite various remedies attempted, union does not occur,

children.text: tataḥ syān maraṇodyogah kāmāgnes tatra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.404||
children.translated_text: then the endeavor toward death arises; its disturbances from the fire of desire are: ||SRs_2.404||

body.translated_text: Now <s>maraṇa</s> (death [in the context of love]) —

body.text: līlā-śuka-cakorādi-nyāsaḥ snigdha-sakhī-kare | 202
body.translated_text: entrusting one's pet parrot, <s>cakora</s> bird, and the like to the hand of a dear companion,

body.text:
kala-kaṇṭha-kalālāpa-śrutir mandānilādaraḥ |
jyotsnā-praveśa-mākanda-mañjarī-vīkṣaṇādayaḥ ||SRs_2.405|| 203
body.translated_text: hearing the sweet, melodious song of the <s>kalakaṇṭha</s> (Indian cuckoo), fondness for gentle breezes, gazing at moonlight, at mango blossoms, and so forth. ||SRs_2.405||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: The slender one, bidding farewell to her nurtured <s>latikā</s> (vine) with just a glance,

children.text: nyāsīkṛtya ca śārikāṃ parijane snigdhe samaṃ vīṇayā |
children.translated_text: entrusting her pet <s>śārikā</s> (myna) bird together with the <s>vīṇā</s> to her dear attendant,
was entering the moonlight — [when] her circle of knowledgeable companions

children.text: siktena hy anapota-siṃha-nṛpater nāmnā punar jīvitā ||SRs_2.406||
children.translated_text: revived her by sprinkling in her ear the name of King <s>Anapota-siṃha</s>. ||SRs_2.406||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra kecid abhilāṣāt pūrvam icchotkaṇṭhā-lakṣaṇam avasthā-dvayam aṅgīkṛtya dvādaśāvasthā iti varṇayanti | tatrecchā punar abhilāṣān na bhidyate | tat-prāpti-tvarālakṣaṇā utkaṇṭhā tu cintanān nātiricyate ity udāsitam |
body.translated_text: Here, some scholars accept two additional stages — <s>icchā</s> (desire) and <s>utkaṇṭhā</s> (eager longing) — before <s>abhilāṣa</s> (yearning), and describe twelve stages. But <s>icchā</s> is not different from <s>abhilāṣa</s>, and <s>utkaṇṭhā</s>, characterized by eagerness for attainment, does not exceed <s>cintana</s> (anxious thought) — hence they are disregarded.

body.text:
atha māna-vipralambhaḥ-
muhuḥ-kṛto meti neti pratiṣedhārtha-vīpsayā |
īpsitāliṅganādīnāṃ nirodho māna ucyate ||SRs_2.407|| 204
so' yaṃ sahetu-nirhetu-bhedād dvedhātra hetujaḥ |
īrṣyayā sambhaved īrṣyā tv anyāsaṅgini vallabhe ||SRs_2.408|| 205
asahiṣṇutvam eva syād dṛṣṭer anumiteḥ śruteḥ |

children.translated_text: In the jealousy-born love-quarrel, the transitory states are: <s>nirveda</s> (self-deprecation), <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), <s>glāni</s> (debility), <s>dīnatā</s> (wretchedness),
<s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>cāpalya</s> (fickleness), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupefaction), <s>moha</s> (delusion), and so forth. ||SRs_2.409||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>māna-vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation due to a love-quarrel) — The prohibition of desired embraces and the like, repeatedly expressed through the rejecting words 'no' and 'not so' — that is called <s>māna</s> (the love-quarrel). ||SRs_2.407|| This is twofold: with cause (<s>sahetu</s>) and without cause (<s>nirhetu</s>). Of these, the caused variety arises from jealousy (<s>īrṣyā</s>); and jealousy is the intolerance [that arises] when the beloved is attached to another — from seeing, from inference, or from hearing. ||SRs_2.408||

children.translated_text: Of these, the love-quarrel born of jealousy from seeing, for example —

children.text: paccakkha-maṃtu-kāraa ja{i} cumbasi maha ime hada-kapole |
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'If you kiss these cheeks of mine, the target of [your] manifest love-making —

children.text: tā majjha pia-sahīe bisesao kīsa biṇṇao ||SRs_2.410||
children.translated_text: then how did my dear friend come to know of the distinguishing mark?' ||SRs_2.410||
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'If you kiss these my cheeks, the target of manifest love-making —

children.text: tato mama priya-sakhyā viśeṣakaḥ kasmād vijñātaḥ ||]
children.translated_text: then how did my dear companion come to know of the distinguishing mark?'

body.text: atra nāyikā-kapola-cumbana-vyājena tat-pratibimbitāṃ sakhīṃ cumbati nāyake tad-īrṣyayā janito nāyikā-mānaḥ pratyakṣa-mantukārakety anayā sambuddhyā vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the hero, under the pretext of kissing the heroine's cheek, kisses the friend reflected [in the mirror/cheek]; the heroine's love-quarrel generated by jealousy of that is manifested through the vocative 'O maker of manifest love!'

body.text: bhogāṅka-gotra-skhalanotsvapnair anumitis tridhā ||SRs_2.411|| 207
body.translated_text: Inference is threefold: from love-marks, from slips of names, and from dream-talk. ||SRs_2.411||

body.text: bhogāṅkānumiti-janiterṣyamāno, yathā mamaiva-
body.translated_text: The love-quarrel born of jealousy from inferring love-marks, for example, from my own [work] —

body.text:
ko doṣo maṇi-mālikā yadi bhavet kaṇṭhe na kiṃ śaṅkaro
dhatte bhūṣaṇam ardha-candram amalaṃ candre na kiṃ kālimā |
tat sādhv eva kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaṇitibhir naivāparāddhaṃ tvayā
bhāgyaṃ draṣṭum anīśayaiva bhavataḥ kāntāparāddhaṃ mayā ||SRs_2.412|| [*15]
[*15] This verse appeared previously in 1.125.
body.translated_text: 'What fault is it if there is a jewel-necklace on the neck? Does not <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) wear the pure half-moon as an ornament? Is there not blackness even on the moon? So it is well done indeed — enough with explanations — you have committed no offense; it is I who have offended by my inability to see your good fortune, O Beloved.' ||SRs_2.412||

body.text: atra maṇi-mālikādi-lakṣaṇa-madana-mudrānumiti-priyāparādha-janiterṣyā-sambhūto mānaḥ tat sādhv eva kṛtam ity ādibhir viparīta-lakṣaṇoktibhir vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the love-quarrel born of the jealousy generated by the beloved's offense inferred from love-marks such as the jewel-necklace and the like is manifested through contrary expressions such as 'it is well done indeed.'

body.text: gotra-skhalanena yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: With her sidelong glance reddened from anger caused by the transgression of [my] name,
as she strikes me,
'Don't touch me, don't touch me!' — with harsh syllables charmingly spoken —
I think that very lotus-face of the long-eyed one [is most beautiful]. ||SRs_2.413||

body.translated_text: From a slip of names, for example, from my own [work] —

body.text:
utsvapnerṣyayā, yathā-
svapna-kīrtita-vipakṣam aṅganāḥ
pratyabhitsur avadantya eva tam |
pracchadānta-galitāśru-bindubhiḥ
krodha-bhinna-valayair vivartanaiḥ ||SRs_2.414|| (ra.vaṃ. 19.22)
body.translated_text: From jealousy based on dream-talk, for example — Women wished to strike their [husbands] who had uttered a rival's name in their sleep, but without actually speaking [their reproach]; [instead they showed their anger] by tear-drops falling from behind the covers, by the snapping of bangles, and by turning away. ||SRs_2.414|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 19.22)

body.text: śrutiḥ priyāparādhasya śrutir āpta-sakhī-mukhāt ||SRs_2.415|| 208ab
body.translated_text: Hearing (<s>śruti</s>) is the hearing of the beloved's offense from the mouth of a trusted companion. ||SRs_2.415||

body.text: śruti-janiterṣyayā māno, yathā-
body.translated_text: The love-quarrel born of jealousy from hearing, for example —

body.text:
aṅguly-agra-nakhena bāṣya-salilaṃ vikṣipya vikṣipya
kiṃ tūṣṇīṃ rodiṣi kopane bahutaraṃ phūtkṛtya rodiṣyasi |
yasyāste piśunopadeśa-vacanair māne' tibhūmiṃ gate
nirviṇṇo' nunayaṃ prati priyatamo madhyasthatām eṣyati ||SRs_2.416|| (amaru. 5)
body.translated_text: 'Flicking away tear-drops with the tip of her fingernail — why do you weep silently? In your anger you will weep all the more, with many a puff!' — She whose love-quarrel has reached an extreme pitch through the words of a meddlesome informer's counsel — her beloved, wearied of entreaties, will resort to indifference. ||SRs_2.416|| (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 5)

body.text: atra piśuna-sakhī-janopadeśa-janito māno bāṣpādibhir vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the love-quarrel generated by the counsel of a meddlesome friend is manifested through tears and the like.

body.text: kāraṇābhāsa-sambhūto nirhetuḥ syād dvayor api | 208
body.translated_text: That which arises from a mere semblance of a cause — that is the causeless [love-quarrel], which belongs to both [hero and heroine].

body.text: avahitthādayas tatra vijñeyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ ||SRs_2.417||
body.translated_text: The transitory states therein should be known as <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation) and the like. ||SRs_2.417||

body.text:
tatra puruṣasya, yathā-
likhann āste bhūmiṃ bahir avanataḥ prāṇa-dayito
nirāhārāḥ sakhyaḥ satata-ruditocchūṇa-nayanāḥ |
parityaktaṃ sarvaṃ hasita-paṭhitaṃ pañjara-śukais
tavāvasthā ceyaṃ visṛja kaṭhine mānam adhunā ||SRs_2.418|| (amaru. 7)
body.translated_text: Of these, of the man, for example — 'Your life-beloved sits outside, head bowed, drawing on the ground; your companions, having given up food, with eyes swollen from constant weeping; all laughing and talking by the cage-parrots has been abandoned — and this is your condition [too] — O hard-hearted one, relinquish your love-quarrel now!' ||SRs_2.418|| (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 7)

body.text:
yathā vā-
alia-pasuttaa viṇimīliaccha dehi suhaa majjha oāsaṃ |
gaṇḍa-paricuṃbaṇāpulaiaṅga ṇa puṇo cirāissaṃ ||SRs_2.419|| (gā.sa. 1.20)
body.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'O falsely sleeping one, with closed eyes — give me room, O handsome one!

children.translated_text: O one whose body thrills at the kissing of the cheeks — I will not delay again!' ||SRs_2.419|| (<s>Gāthā-saptaśatī</s> 1.20)
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'O falsely sleeping one, with closed eyes — give me room, O handsome one! O one whose body thrills at the kissing of the cheeks — I will not delay again!'

body.text: atrālīka-svāpākṣi-nimīlanādi-sūcita-puruṣa-māna-kāraṇasya prasādhana-gṛha-vyāpāra-nimittaṃ vilambanasyābhāsatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, the cause of the man's love-quarrel — indicated by the pretense of sleep and the closing of eyes — has only a semblance of a cause, namely the delay occasioned by activities in the dressing room.

body.text:
striyā, yathā-
muñca kopam animitta-locane
sandhyayā praṇamito' smi nānyathā |
kiṃ na vetsi sahadharma-cāriṇaṃ
cakravāka-sama-vṛttim ātmanaḥ ||SRs_2.420|| (ku.saṃ. 8.57)
body.translated_text: Of the woman, for example — 'Release your anger, O one with causeless eyes [i.e., angry without cause]! I bowed to the twilight [Sandhyā, personified as a woman], not otherwise. Do you not know your own husband, who behaves like a <s>cakravāka</s> (the bird that is faithful to its mate)?' ||SRs_2.420|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.57)

body.text: atra pārvatī-māna-kāraṇasya parameśvara-kṛta-sandhyā-praṇāmasyābhāsatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, the cause of <s>Pārvatī</s>'s love-quarrel — <s>Parameśvara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) prostration to the evening twilight (<s>Sandhyā</s>) — has only a semblance of a cause [since Sandhyā is a ritual, not a rival].

body.text: nanu aliapasuttety atra gaṇḍa-paricumbanasya niṣedho nāsti | evaṃ muñca kopam ity atra ca niṣedho na śrūyate | tat katham asya nirhetukasya (meti vā neti vā niṣedhābhāve' pi) mānatvam iti cet | meti neti vācika-niṣedhasya upalaksaṇatvāt (aliapasutteti) pūrvasminn udāharaṇe apratikriyayā cumbanānaṅgīkāra-lakṣaṇo niṣedho vidyata eva | aparatra (muñca kopam ity atra) punar anuttara-dānādinā anaṅgīkāra-lakṣaṇo niṣedho vaktavya eva |
body.translated_text: Now, [an objection:] in the verse 'O falsely sleeping one,' there is no prohibition of kissing the cheek; likewise in 'release your anger,' no prohibition is heard. How then can this be a love-quarrel [which is defined as prohibition] even without the verbal refusal 'no' or 'not so'? To this we say: because the verbal refusal is merely illustrative — in the first example ('O falsely sleeping one'), the refusal in the form of non-acceptance of the kiss through non-response is indeed present; in the second ('release your anger'), the refusal in the form of non-acceptance through withholding a reply and such must be understood.

body.text: nanu nirhetukasya mānasya bhāva-kauṭilya-rūpa-mānasya ca ko bheda iti ced ucyate | nirhetuka-māne tu kopa-vyājena cumbanādi-vilambanāt prema-parīkṣaṇaṃ phalam | bhāva-kauṭilya-māne tu cumbanādy-avilambaḥ phalam iti spaṣṭa eva tayor bhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, [another objection:] what is the difference between the causeless love-quarrel and the love-quarrel arising from crooked disposition (<s>bhāva-kauṭilya</s>)? We reply: In the causeless love-quarrel, the fruit is the testing of love through delaying kisses and such under the pretext of anger. In the love-quarrel of crooked disposition, the fruit is the non-delay of kisses and such — thus the distinction between them is clear.

body.text: nirhetukaḥ svayaṃ śāmyet svayaṃ grāhasmitādibhiḥ ||SRs_2.421|| 209
body.translated_text: The causeless [love-quarrel] subsides of its own accord, spontaneously, through seizing [her], smiling, and the like. ||SRs_2.421||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'What is this you have done to my body, noble sir?'
'What is this you have fashioned, O innocent one?'
At the conclusion of their acts, through the signs of enjoyment [on each other's bodies],
the pretended quarrel ended in smiles. ||SRs_2.422||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra lakṣmī-nārāyaṇayor anyonya-mānasya paraspara-kṛta-bhoga-cihna-lakṣaṇa-kāraṇābhāsa-janitasya smitottaratayā svayaṃ śāntir avagamyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the mutual causeless love-quarrel of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, generated by mere semblances of causes in the form of signs of enjoyment made by each other, is understood to subside of its own accord through the ending in smiles.

body.text: hetujas tu śamaṃ yāti yathāyogyaṃ prakalpitaiḥ |

children.translated_text: conciliation (<s>sāman</s>), dissension (<s>bheda</s>), gifts (<s>dāna</s>), prostration (<s>nati</s>), disregard (<s>upekṣā</s>), and change of sentiment (<s>rasāntara</s>).

children.text: tatra priyokti-kathanaṃ yat tu tat sāma gīyate ||SRs_2.423||
children.translated_text: Of these, the utterance of sweet words — that is called conciliation (<s>sāman</s>). ||SRs_2.423||

body.translated_text: The caused [love-quarrel], however, is pacified through appropriately devised means:

body.text: tatra yathā mamaiva-

children.translated_text: 'This servant is exclusively yours, not shared with another —
why do you suspect otherwise in your heart?'
When the beloved speaks thus, through someone who is listened to with respect,
neither the love-quarrel nor the group of companions was perceived [anymore]. ||SRs_2.424||

body.translated_text: An example of that, from my own [work] —

body.text: atra priya-sāmokti-janitā kasyāścid māna-śāntiḥ sakhī-jana-mānādy-ajñāna-sūcitair āliṅganādibhir vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the pacification of someone's love-quarrel through the beloved's conciliatory words is manifested through embraces and the like, indicated by the non-perception of the companion-group and the love-quarrel.

body.text: sakhyādibhir upālambha-prayogo bheda ucyate ||SRs_2.425|| 211
body.translated_text: The employment of reproach by companions and the like — that is called dissension (<s>bheda</s>). ||SRs_2.425||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Abandoning this vice of the love-quarrel, O slender one, place your beloved

children.text: vidheyas te preyān yadi vayam anullaṅghya-vacasaḥ |
children.translated_text: between these breasts — if we are [friends] whose words should not be transgressed.'
Hearing this speech from her affectionate companions, the doe-eyed one
offered water-oblations with her eye-tears to the friend that was her love-quarrel. ||SRs_2.426||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: vyājena bhūṣaṇādīnāṃ pradānaṃ dānam ucyate ||SRs_2.427|| 212ab
body.translated_text: The giving of ornaments and the like as a stratagem — that is called gift (<s>dāna</s>). ||SRs_2.427||

body.text:
yathā-
muhur upahasitām ivāli-nādair
vitarasi naḥ kalikāṃ kim-artham enām |
adhirajani gatena dhāmni tasyāḥ
śaṭhaḥ kalir eva mahāṃs tvayādya dattaḥ ||SRs_2.428|| (śi.va. 7.55)
body.translated_text: For example — 'Why do you offer us this flower-bud, as if mocking us with the buzzing of bees? By virtue of its radiance gone in the night, O deceitful one, you have today given us only a great quarrel, not a flower!' ||SRs_2.428|| (<s>Śiśupālavadha</s> 7.55)

body.text: natiḥ pāda-praṇāmaḥ syāt ||SRs_2.429|| 212c
body.translated_text: Prostration (<s>nati</s>) is the bowing at the feet. ||SRs_2.429||

body.text: tayā, yathā-

children.translated_text: With brow slightly furrowed from anger at slanderous words,
when her own lord prostrates at the foot of her seat,
the young woman, [releasing] tear-drops streaming from the corners of her eyes,
brought down to her pair of breasts the necklace-string, now without virtue [i.e., loosened/purposeless]. ||SRs_2.430||

body.translated_text: By that [means], for example —

body.text: tūṣṇīṃ sthitir upekṣaṇam ||SRs_2.431|| 212d
body.translated_text: Remaining silent is disregard (<s>upekṣaṇa</s>). ||2.431||

body.text:
yathā-
caraṇoāsaṇisaṇṇassa tassa bharimo aṇālabantassa |
pāaṅguṭṭhābeṭṭhia kesa-diḍhāaḍḍhaṇa-suhaṃ ||SRs_2.432|| (gāthā 2.8)
body.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Of him seated at the foot-space [of the bed], we recall — [he] not speaking, the pleasure of tightly pulling the hair wound around the big toe. ||2.432|| (<s>Gāthā-saptaśatī</s> 2.8)

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Of him seated at the foot-space [of the bed], we recall — [he] not speaking,
the pleasure of tightly pulling the hair wound around the big toe.

body.text: atra śayyāyāṃ caraṇāvakāśa-sthiti-maunādibhir upekṣā | tayā janitā mānasya śāntiś caraṇāṅguṣṭha-veṣṭita-keśa-dṛḍhākarṣaṇena vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the disregard is [shown] through staying at the foot-space of the bed, silence, and the like. The cessation of pride generated thereby is conveyed through the tight pulling of the hair wound around the big toe.

body.text: ākasmika-bhayādīnāṃ kalpanā syad rasāntaram |

children.translated_text: It is declared to be twofold: accidental (<s>yādṛcchika</s>) and deliberate (<s>buddhi-pūrva</s>).
That which is brought about by favorable fate is the accidental. ||2.433||

body.translated_text: The contrivance of sudden fear and the like constitutes another <s>Rasa</s> (sentiment).

body.text:
tena māna-śāntir, yathā-
mānam asyā nirākartuṃ pādayor me patiṣyataḥ |
upakārāya diṣṭyaitad udīṇaṃ ghana-garjitam ||SRs_2.434|| (kā.ā. 2.290)
body.translated_text: Cessation of pride through that [accidental means], for example — 'As I am about to fall at her feet to remove her pride, fortunately this thundering of clouds has arisen to my advantage.' ||2.434|| (<s>Kāvyālaṅkāra</s> 2.290)

body.text: atra māna-praṇodana-ghana-garjita-santrāsasya priya-prayatnair vinā daiva-vaśena sambhūtatvād yādṛcchikatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, because the terror of the thunder-clap that dispels pride occurs through the power of fate, without any effort by the beloved, it has the character of being accidental.

body.text: pratyutpanna-dhiyā puṃsā kalpitaṃ buddhi-pūrvakam ||SRs_2.435|| 214
body.translated_text: That which is contrived by a man of ready wit is the deliberate (<s>buddhi-pūrvaka</s>). ||2.435||

body.text:
yathā-
līlā-tāmarasāhato' nya-vanitā-niḥśaṅka-daṣṭādharaḥ
kaścit kesara-dūṣitekṣaṇa iva vyāmīlya netre sthitaḥ |
mugdhā kuḍmalitānanena dadatī vāyuṃ sthitā tasya sā
bhrāntyā dhūrtatayātha sā natim ṛte tenāniśaṃ cumbitā ||SRs_2.436|| (amaru 72)
body.translated_text: For example — 'A certain man, struck by [her] playful lotus, his lower lip bitten boldly by another woman, with eyes as if besmeared with [lotus] filaments, stood with both eyes closed. The innocent woman, standing with her face close to his, blew air [on his eyes]; then, through her confusion and his cunning, she was kissed by him ceaselessly, without having bowed.' ||2.436|| (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 72)

body.text: atra mānāpanodanasya priya-trāsasya netra-vyāvṛtti-naṭana-lakṣaṇatayā nāyakasya pratyutpanna-matyā kalpitatvād buddhi-pūrvakatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, the deliberate character lies in the fact that the removal of pride — [through] the beloved's alarm — was contrived by the hero's ready wit in the form of the pretense of closing the eyes.

body.text:
atha pravāsaḥ-
pūrva-saṅgatayor yūnor bhaved deśāntarādibhiḥ |
caraṇa-vyavadhānaṃ yat sa pravāsa itīryate ||SRs_2.437|| 215
taj-janyo vipralambho' pi pravāsatvena saṃmataḥ |
harṣa-garva-mada-vrīḍā varjayitvā samīritāḥ ||SRs_2.438|| 216
śṛṅgāra-yogyāḥ sarve' pi pravāsa-vyabhicāriṇaḥ |
kāryataḥ sambhramāc chāpāt sa tridhā tatra kāryajaḥ ||SRs_2.439|| 217
buddhi-pūrvatayā yūnoḥ saṃvidhāna-vyapekṣayā |
vṛtto vartiṣyamāṇaś ca vartamāna iti tridhā ||SRs_2.440|| 218
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Pravāsa</s> (separation by distance) — When two young lovers who were previously united become separated by [going to] another land, etc. — that intervening distance is called <s>Pravāsa</s> (separation). ||2.437|| The <s>Vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) born thereof is also accepted as belonging to <s>Pravāsa</s>. ||2.438|| Excluding joy, pride, intoxication, and modesty, all the <s>Vyabhicārī-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions) appropriate to <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment) [operate in] <s>Pravāsa</s>. It is threefold: arising from duty, from flurry, and from a curse. Among these, that arising from duty — ||2.439|| being deliberate on the part of the young lovers, with reference to prior arrangement — is of three kinds: past, future, and present. ||2.440||

body.text: dharmārtha-saṅgrahāya buddhi-pūrvo vyāpāraḥ kāryam | tena vṛtto, yathā-
body.translated_text: Duty (<s>kārya</s>) means a deliberate activity for the acquisition of <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Artha</s>. Past [separation] caused by that, for example —

body.text:
kriyā-prabandhād ayam adhvarāṇām
ajasram āhūta-sahasra-netraḥ |
śacyāś ciraṃ pāṇḍu-kapola-lambān
mandāra-śūnyān alakāṃś cakāra ||SRs_2.441|| (ra.vaṃ. 6.23)
body.translated_text: 'By his unbroken sequence of sacrificial rites, he who constantly invited the Thousand-eyed one (<s>Indra</s>), for a long time made the cheeks of <s>Śacī</s> (Indra's wife) pale, her locks hanging [loose], bereft of <s>Mandāra</s> (coral tree) flowers.' ||2.441|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 6.23)

body.text: atra purandarasya pūrvaṃ śacīm āmantrya paścād adhvara-pradeśa-gamanena tayoḥ saṃvidhān avyapekṣayā (kāryato) vipralambhasya bhūta-pūrvatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, the past nature of the <s>Vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) through duty is shown by <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>)'s having first taken leave of <s>Śacī</s> and then traveling to the sacrificial ground, with reference to their prior arrangement.

body.text: vartiṣyamāṇo, yathā-
body.translated_text: Future [separation], for example —

body.text:
bhavatu viditaṃ chadmālāpair alaṃ priya gamyatāṃ
tanur api na te doṣo' smākaṃ vidhis tu parāṅmukhaḥ |
tava yathā tathābhūtaṃ prema prapannam imāṃ daśāṃ
prakṛti-capale kā naḥ pīḍā gate hata-jīvite ||SRs_2.442|| (amaru 30)
body.translated_text: 'Let it be known — enough of deceitful speeches — go, O beloved! Nor is it your fault — it is Fate that is averse to us. Your love, however it may be, has come to this state. What pain is there for us, O fickle one by nature, now that our life is lost?' ||2.442|| (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 30)

children.translated_text: Present [separation], for example —
'As he said "I go" to his beloved, who was nourished by [the word] "beloved" (<s>priya</s>), who was clinging to his neck —
there was a struggle between his words and his life to exit first.' ||2.443||

body.text:
atha sambhramāt-
āvegaḥ sambhramaḥ so' pi naiko divyādibhedataḥ ||SRs_2.444|| 219a
body.translated_text: Now, from flurry (<s>sambhrama</s>) — Agitation is flurry; it too is manifold, by the distinction of divine and other [causes]. ||2.444||

body.text:
tatra divyo, yathā-
tiṣṭhet kopa-vaśāt prabhāva-pihitā dīrghaṃ na sā kupyati
svargāyotpatitā bhaven mayi punar-bhāvārdram asyā manaḥ |
tāṃ hartuṃ vibudha-dviṣo' pi na ca me śaktāḥ puro-vartinīṃ
sā cātyantam agocaraṃ nayanayor yāteti ko' yaṃ vidhiḥ ||SRs_2.445|| (vi.u. 4.9)
body.translated_text: Of these, the divine, for example — 'She would remain [silent] from the power of anger — but she is not angry for long. She has flown up to heaven — but then, her mind would be tender with renewed love toward me. Even the enemies of the gods could not take her from before me. Yet she has gone utterly beyond the range of my eyes — what is this fate?' ||2.445|| (<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.9)

body.text: atra vipralambhasya kāraṇāntara-nirāsena ko' yaṃ vidhir iti vidheḥ kāraṇatvābhiprāyeṇa divya-sambhrama-janitatvaṃ pratīyate |
body.translated_text: Here, by ruling out other causes [of separation] with 'what is this fate?', the divine-flurry-generated nature of the <s>Vipralambha</s> is understood, with the intention that Fate is its cause.

body.text: atha śāpaḥ-

children.translated_text: <s>Śāpa</s> (curse) is twofold: resulting in disfigurement and resulting in transformation into another form.
Separation through the disfigurement of a curse is [seen] in the cases of <s>Ahalyā</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and others. ||2.446||

body.translated_text: Now, the curse (<s>śāpa</s>) —

body.text:
tādrūpyeṇa, yathā-
kaścit kāntā-viraha-guruṇā svādhikārāt pramattaḥ
śāpenāstaṃgamita-mahimā varṣa-bhogyeṇa bhartuḥ |
yakṣaś cakre janaka-tanayā-snāna-puṇyodakeṣu
snigdha-cchāyā-taruṣu vasatiṃ rāma-giry-āśrameṣu ||SRs_2.447|| [me.dū. 1.1]
body.translated_text: Through transformation into another form, for example — 'A certain <s>Yakṣa</s>, negligent of his duties due to the heavy burden of separation from his beloved, his glory eclipsed by his master's curse requiring a year's endurance, made his dwelling in the hermitages of <s>Rāma-giri</s>, among the trees whose shade was cool, at the waters sanctified by the bathing of <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter (<s>Sītā</s>).' ||2.447|| [<s>Meghadūta</s> 1.1]

body.text: atha karuṇa-vipralambhaḥ-

children.translated_text: When one of the two [lovers] dies, and the limit [of separation] is the revival [of the dead],
the separation of the other is called 'compassionate' (<s>karuṇa</s>), because it follows the hope of reunion. ||2.448||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Karuṇa-vipralambha</s> (compassionate separation) —

body.text: karuṇa-bhrama-kāritvāt so' yaṃ karuṇa ucyate | 221
body.translated_text: Because it causes the bewilderment of compassion, it is called 'compassionate.'

body.text: sañcāriṇo' nubhāvāś ca karuṇe' pi pravāsavat ||SRs_2.449||
body.translated_text: The <s>Sañcārī</s> (transitory emotions) and <s>Anubhāvas</s> (consequents) in the compassionate [separation] are the same as in <s>Pravāsa</s>. ||2.449||

body.text:
yathā-
atha madana-vadhūr upaplavāntaṃ
vyasana-kṛśo pratipālayāṃ babhūva |
śaśina iva divātanasya rekhā
kiraṇa-parikṣaya-dhūsarā pradoṣam ||SRs_2.450|| (ku.saṃ. 4.46)
body.translated_text: For example — 'Then the wife of <s>Madana</s> (<s>Rati</s>), emaciated by misfortune, waited for the end of the calamity — like the crescent of the daytime moon, growing grey from the diminishing of its rays, waiting for dusk.' ||2.450|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 4.46)

body.text: atrākāśa-sarasvatī-pratyayena rater vipralambhaḥ kṛśatvādy-anumitair glāny-ādibhiḥ vyabhicāri-bhāvaiḥ poṣitaḥ samaya-paripālanādibhir anubhāvair vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Vipralambha</s> of <s>Rati</s>, based on the assurance of the celestial voice, is nourished by <s>Vyabhicārī-bhāvas</s> such as languor inferred from emaciation, and is conveyed through <s>Anubhāvas</s> such as observing the [appointed] time.

body.text: atra kecid āhuḥ-karuṇo nāma vipralambha-śṛṅgāro nāsti | ubhayālambanasya tasya ekatraivāsambhavāt | yatra tv ekasyāpāye sati tad-itara-gatāḥ pralāpādayo bhavanti sa śokān na bhidyate iti | tad ayuktam | yatra punar-ujjīvanena sambhogo nāsti, tatra satyaṃ śoka eva | yatra so' sti tatra vipralambha eva | anyathā sambhoga-śiraske anyatarāpāya-lakṣaṇe vairūpya-śāpa-pravāse' pi śoka-rūpatvāpatteḥ |
body.translated_text: Here some say: there is no such thing as <s>Karuṇa-vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s> (compassionate separation in the erotic), since it requires both substrates and cannot exist in one alone. Where, upon the death of one, the lamentations and such directed toward the other occur — that is not different from <s>Śoka</s> (grief). This is not correct. Where there is no reunion through revival, there it is indeed <s>Śoka</s> alone. But where such [revival] exists, there it is <s>Vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). Otherwise, even in separation through the disfigurement or curse-generated journey — which are also characterized by the absence of one of the two — the unwanted consequence of being mere grief would follow.

body.text: nanv evaṃ pravāsa-karuṇayoḥ ko bheda iti ced ucyate-śarīreṇa deśāntara-gamane pravāsaḥ | prāṇair deśāntara-gamane karuṇa iti |
body.translated_text: If asked: 'What then is the difference between <s>Pravāsa</s> and <s>Karuṇa</s>?' — the answer is: when the body goes to another land, it is <s>Pravāsa</s>; when the life-breath goes to another land, it is <s>Karuṇa</s>.

body.text: atra kecid ayoga-śabdasya pūrvānurāga-vācakatvaṃ viprayoga-śabdasya mānādi-vācakatvaṃ cābhipretya ayogo viprayogaś ceti sambhogād anyasya śṛṅgārasya vibhāgam āhuḥ | vipralambha-padasyāprayoge ca kāraṇaṃ bruvate-(saṅketa-sthānam āgamiṣyāmīti) uktvā saṅketam aprāptau tad-vyatikrame (tato) nāyikāntarānusaraṇe ca vipralambha-śabdasya (mukhyaḥ) prayogaḥ | vañcanārthatvāt tasya | (ayoga-viprayoga-viśeṣatvād vipralambhasya tādṛśa-viśeṣābhidhāyakasya vipralambha-śabdasya) tat-sāmānyābhidhāyitve tu vipralambha-śabdasya upacaritatvāpatter iti | tad ayuktam | caturvidhe' pi vipralambhe vañcana-rūpasyārthasya mukhyata eva siddheḥ | tathā ca śrī-bhojaḥ-
body.translated_text: Here some, intending the word <s>ayoga</s> to denote prior love and the word <s>viprayoga</s> to denote pride and such, have proposed the division of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> other than <s>Sambhoga</s> as <s>Ayoga</s> and <s>Viprayoga</s>. And they state the reason for not using the word <s>Vipralambha</s>: the primary usage of the word <s>Vipralambha</s> is in the case of failure to arrive at a tryst after having said 'I will come to the rendezvous,' or in the case of pursuing another heroine [from the tryst] — because the word implies deception. If the word <s>Vipralambha</s> were used to denote these [varieties] in general, it would have a secondary (metaphorical) usage, [they say]. This is incorrect, because in all four types of <s>Vipralambha</s>, the meaning of the character of deception is indeed primary. And thus the illustrious <s>Bhoja</s> [says] —

children.translated_text: 'The word <s>Vipralambha</s>, or that which denotes deception alone,

children.text: vinā samāse caturāś caturo' rthān niyuñjate ||SRs_2.451||
children.translated_text: without qualification, assigns four meanings to four [types].' ||2.451||
'In prior love, the deception is manifold — through modesty and such;

children.text: māne viruddhaṃ tat prāhuḥ punar īrṣyāyitādibhiḥ ||SRs_2.452||
children.translated_text: in pride, they call it 'opposed' — through jealousy and such.' ||2.452||

body.text:
nyāviddhaṃ dīrgha-kālatvāt pravāse tat pratīyate |
viniṣiddhaṃ tu karuṇe karuṇatvena gīyate ||SRs_2.453|| (sa.ka.ā. 5.63,65-6)
body.translated_text: 'In separation, it is understood as "estranged" due to the long duration; in the compassionate, it is called "forbidden" due to its compassionate nature.' ||2.453|| (<s>Sarasvatī-kaṇṭhābharaṇa</s> 5.63, 65-66)

body.text: atha sambhogaḥ-

children.translated_text: Where for the young couple the enjoyment consisting of touching, embracing, and the like

children.text: ghaṭate yatra yūnor yat sa sambhogaś caturvidhaḥ ||SRs_2.454||
children.translated_text: comes to pass in a favorable manner — that <s>Sambhoga</s> (union) is fourfold. ||2.454||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Sambhoga</s> (union) —

body.text: atrāyam arthaḥ-prāg-asaṅgatayoḥ saṅgata-viyuktayor vā nāyikā-nāyakayoḥ paraspara-samāgame prāg-utpannā tadānīntanī vā ratiḥ prepsitāliṅganādīnāṃ prāptau satyāṃ upajāyamānair harṣādibhiḥ saṃsṛjyamānā candrodayādibhir uddīpitā smitādibhir vyajyamānā prāpta-prakarṣā sambhoga-śṛṅgāra ity ākhyāyate | sa ca vakṣyamāṇa-krameṇa caturvidhaḥ |
body.translated_text: The meaning here is: when two lovers — either previously unacquainted, or united and then separated — come together, the <s>Rati</s> (love) that arose previously or arises at that time, being combined with joy and such [emotions] produced by the attainment of the desired embraces and the like, stimulated by the rising of the moon and such [excitants], expressed through smiles and the like, and reaching its fullness — is called <s>Sambhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic sentiment of union). And this is fourfold in the order to be described.

body.text: saṅkṣiptaḥ saṅkīrṇaḥ sampannataraḥ samṛddhimān iti te | 223
body.translated_text: <s>Saṅkṣipta</s> (condensed), <s>Saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed), <s>Sampannatara</s> (accomplished), and <s>Samṛddhimān</s> (resplendent) — these

body.text: pūrvānurāga-māna-pravāsa-karuṇānusambhavāḥ kramataḥ ||SRs_2.455||
body.translated_text: arise respectively from prior love, pride, separation, and compassionate [separation]. ||2.455||

body.text: tatra saṅkṣiptaḥ-

children.translated_text: Where the young lovers enjoy condensed attentions,
[limited] by timidity, bashfulness, and the like — that is called <s>Saṅkṣipta</s> (condensed). ||2.456||

body.translated_text: There, the <s>Saṅkṣipta</s> (condensed) —

body.text: puruṣa-gata-sādhvasena saṅkṣipto, yathā-
body.translated_text: Condensed [union] due to timidity on the man's part, for example —

children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] May the hand of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — trembling with the timidity of the first encounter at the touch of <s>Rādhikā</s>'s breast —
which playfully weighed [like] a mountain — protect you! ||2.457||
[Sanskrit rendering:] May the hand of <s>Hari</s>, trembling with the timidity of the first encounter at the touch of <s>Rādhikā</s>'s breast,
which playfully weighed [like] a mountain, protect you!

body.text:
strī-sādhvasāt saṅkṣipto, yathā-
cumbaneṣv adhara-dāna-varjitaṃ
sanna-hasta-madayopagūhane |
kliṣṭa-manmatham api priyaṃ prabhor
durlabha-pratikṛtaṃ vadhūratam ||SRs_2.458|| (ku.saṃ. 8.8)
body.translated_text: Condensed [union] due to the woman's timidity, for example — 'In kisses, the offering of the lip was withheld; in embrace, the hands drooped, intoxicating [him]; though the love-making of the bride tormented the lord with desire, its reciprocation was difficult to obtain.' ||2.458|| (<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 8.8)

body.text: atha saṅkīrṇaḥ-

children.translated_text: <s>Saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed) is the union that is commingled with dependence on another,
pretended death, and the like, [yet] somewhat refined in the arrows of love. ||2.459||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed) —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Their love-makings, delightful in their friction, full of mutual jealousy,
were divided by those couples —
diversified by wantonness and trust,
made pure by the cessation of pride.' ||2.460||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atha sampannaḥ-

children.translated_text: Attaining its full splendor from the absence of fear, pretense, recollection [of offenses], and the like,
the enjoyment of young lovers reunited after separation is called <s>Sampanna</s> (accomplished). ||2.461||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Sampanna</s> (accomplished) —

children.translated_text: For example —
[Prakrit:] A tooth-mark on the cheek, the coiffure disheveled by the pulling of the hair,
and a gaze that keeps rolling — [these] prove the arrival of the beloved for the bride. ||2.462||
[Sanskrit rendering:] A tooth-mark on the cheek, the coiffure disheveled by the pulling of the hair,

children.text: parighūrṇana-śīlā ca dṛṣṭiḥ priyāgamaṃ sādhayati vadhvāḥ ||)
children.translated_text: and a gaze that keeps rolling — [these] prove the arrival of the beloved for the bride.

body.text: atra aprathama-sambhogatvād bhayābhāvaḥ | danta-kṣatādiṣv aṅgārpaṇānukūlyena vyalīka-smaraṇādy-abhāvaḥ | tābhyām upārūḍha-vaibhavaḥ sampadyate sambhogaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since it is not the first union, there is absence of fear. Through the receptive offering of the body [evidenced] in the tooth-marks and such, there is absence of pretense, recollection [of offenses], and the like. From these two [absences], the enjoyment attains its full splendor.

body.text: atha samṛddhimān-

children.translated_text: 'How much splendor of enjoyment can there be upon being revived?

children.text: śivābhyām eva vijñeyam ity ayaṃ hi samṛddhimān ||SRs_2.463||
children.translated_text: That can be known only by <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Pārvatī</s>' — such is this resplendent [union]. ||2.463||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Samṛddhimān</s> (resplendent) —

body.text:
yathā-
candrāpīḍaṃ sā ca jagrāha kaṇṭhe
kaṇṭha-sthānaṃ jīvitaṃ ca prapede | tenāpūrvā sā samullāsa-lakṣmīm

children.translated_text: like a line of the ocean touched by the moon.' ||2.464||

body.translated_text: 'She embraced <s>Candrāpīḍa</s> by the neck, and life returned to its place in her throat; thereby she attained an unprecedented splendor of delight,

body.text: (abhinandasya kādambarī-kathā-sāre, 8.80)
body.translated_text: (of <s>Abhinanda</s>, in the <s>Kādambarī-kathā-sāra</s> 8.80)

body.text: yathā vā-

children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Embraces without calculation of their confusion,
kisses far beyond the tumult they engender,
dense blows without contrivance —
bow down to the enchantments of the love-sport of <s>Anaṅga</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) and <s>Rati</s>! ||2.465||

body.translated_text: Or for example —

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Embraces without calculation of their confusion,
kisses far beyond the tumult they engender,
dense blows without contrivance —
bow down to the enchantments of the love-sport of <s>Anaṅga</s> and <s>Rati</s>!

body.text: atra punar-ujjīvitenaa kāmena saha ratyā rater bāhyopacārānapekṣayaiva tat-phala-rūpa-sukha-prāpti-kathanāt sambhogaḥ samṛddhyati |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Sambhoga</s> attains its resplendence because, through the revived <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Rati</s>, the attainment of the fruit-like bliss is stated without regard for external attentions.

body.text: atha hāsyaḥ-

children.translated_text: Through <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequent expressions), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) appropriate to it,
laughter (<s>hāsa</s>), when brought to a state of being relishable by the audience, is called <s>Hāsya</s> (the Comic <s>rasa</s>). ||2.466||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Hāsya</s> (the comic sentiment) —

body.text: tatrālasya-glāni-nidrā-vyādhy-ādyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ | 229
body.translated_text: In it, laziness, languor, sleep, illness, and the like are the transitory emotions.

body.text: eṣa dvedhā bhaved ātma-para-sthiti-vibhāgataḥ ||SRs_2.467||
body.translated_text: This is twofold, by the distinction of residing in oneself or in others. ||2.467||

body.text: ātmasthas tu yadā svasya vikārair hasati svayam | 230
body.translated_text: When residing in oneself — when one laughs at oneself through one's own deformities,

body.text: yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe-bhṛṅgiriṭiḥ (ātmānaṃ nirvarṇya sopahāsam)-aho tribhuvanādhipater asya anucarasya mahārha-veṣatā |
body.translated_text: for example, in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> — <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s> (examining himself, with derision) — Ah, what magnificent attire for a servant of the lord of the three worlds!

body.text:
kaupīnācchādane valkam akṣa-sūtraṃ jaṭā-cchaṭāḥ |
rudrāṅkuśas tripuṇḍraṃ ca veṣo bhṛṅgiriṭer ayam ||SRs_2.468|| (bā.rā. 2.2)
body.translated_text:
A bark-garment to cover the loincloth, a rosary of <s>akṣa</s>-beads, matted locks,
<s>Rudrākṣa</s> beads, triple horizontal lines — this is the attire of <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s>! ||2.468|| (<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 2.2)

body.text: atra bhṛṅgiriṭiḥ sva-veṣa-vaikṛtenaiva svayam ātmānaṃ hasati |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s> laughs at himself through the deformity of his own attire.

body.text: parasthas tu para-prāptair etair hasati cet param ||SRs_2.468|| 231a
body.translated_text: When residing in another — if one laughs at another through these [deformities] belonging to another. ||2.468||

body.text:
yathā-
trastaḥ samasta-jana-hāsa-karaḥ kareṇos
tāvat kharaḥ prakharam ullalayāṃcakāra |
yāvac calāsana-vilola-nitamba-bimba-
visrasta-vastram avarodha-vadhūḥ papāta ||SRs_2.469|| (śi.va. 5.7)
body.translated_text:
For example —
The donkey, causing laughter in all people, being frightened of the she-elephant,
brayed vehemently and loudly,
whereupon the <s>avarodha</s> (harem) lady fell, her garment slipping from her round hips swaying on the unsteady seat. ||2.469|| (<s>Śiśupāla-vadha</s> 5.7)

body.text: prakṛti-vaśāt sa ca ṣoḍhā smita-hasite vihasitāvahasite ca | 231
body.translated_text: According to nature, this [laughter] is sixfold: <s>smita</s> (smile), <s>hasita</s> (laughter), <s>vihasita</s> (open laughter), <s>avahasita</s> (derisive laughter), and furthermore

body.text: apahasitātihasitake jyeṣṭhādīnāṃ kramād dve dve ||469||
body.translated_text: <s>apahasita</s> (excessive laughter) and <s>atihasita</s> (uproarious laughter) — two for each of the superior and other [types of persons], in order. ||469||

body.text:
tatra smitam -
smitaṃ cālakṣya-daśanaṃ dṛk-kapola-vikāśa-kṛt ||SRs_2.470|| 232
body.translated_text:
Among these, <s>smita</s> (smile) —
<s>Smita</s> is [a smile] with teeth barely visible, producing a blossoming of the eyes and cheeks. ||2.470||

body.text:
yathā-
utphulla-gaṇḍa-maṇḍalam ullasita-dṛg-anta-sūcitākūtam |
namayantyāpi mukhāmbujam unnamitaṃ rāga-sāmrājyam ||SRs_2.471|| (ku.ā. 2.15)
body.translated_text:
For example —
With cheeks blossoming, with intent hinted by the radiant eye-corners,
even as she lowers her lotus-face, the sovereignty of passion is exalted. ||2.471|| (<s>Kuvalayānanda</s> 2.15)

body.text: atra gaṇḍa-maṇḍala-vikāsa-dṛg-antollāsābhyāṃ nāyikāyāḥ smitaṃ vyajyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the smile of the heroine is expressed through the blossoming of the cheeks and the radiance of the eye-corners.

body.text:
hasitaṃ, yathā-
tad eva lakṣya-daśana-śikharaṃ hasitaṃ bhavet ||SRs_2.472|| 233a
smayamānam āyatākṣyāḥ
kiṃcid abhivyakta-daśana-śobhi mukham |
asamagra-lakṣya-kesaram
ucchvasad iva paṅkajaṃ dṛṣṭam ||SRs_2.473|| (mā.a.mi. 2.11)
body.translated_text:
<s>Hasita</s> (laughter), for example —
That very [expression] with slightly visible teeth-tips is <s>hasita</s>. ||2.472||
The face of the long-eyed woman, smiling,
beautiful with slightly revealed teeth,
appeared like a lotus with incompletely visible filaments,
as if opening. ||2.473|| (<s>Mā.a.mi.</s> 2.11)

body.text: atra kiñcid abhivyakta-daśanatvād idaṃ hasitam |
body.translated_text: Here, because the teeth are slightly revealed, this is <s>hasita</s>.

body.text: vihasitaṃ, yathā-

children.translated_text: That very [laughter], with contracted eye-corners and cheeks, with sweet sound,
timely, with feeling — that is called <s>vihasita</s>. ||2.474||

body.translated_text: <s>Vihasita</s> (open laughter), for example —

children.translated_text: For example —
Even when I was near, [she acted as if] not seeing me, under the pretext of watching the child's play;
I remember her laughter — audible, with contracted eye-corners. ||2.475||

body.text: avahasitam, yathā-

children.translated_text: That which involves expanded nostrils, contracted head and shoulders,
and eyes with a sidelong, crooked glance — that is considered <s>avahasita</s>. ||2.476||

body.translated_text: <s>Avahasita</s> (derisive laughter), for example —

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Upon seeing [the woman's] short, squat mass of hair,
which fell at the mere touch of a hand,
with contracted shoulders, with crooked eye-corners,
with expanded nostrils — the friends laughed. ||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: kampitāṅgaṃ sāśru-netraṃ tac cāpahasitaṃ bhavet ||SRs_2.477|| 235
body.translated_text: <s>Apahasita</s> (excessive laughter) is that which involves trembling of the body and eyes [filled] with tears. ||2.477||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Wishing to kiss both cheeks of his son with parental affection,
when the elephant-faced one (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) was pulled near, their faces closely meeting each other —

children.text: apāyāt pāyād vaḥ pramatha-mithunaṃ vīkṣya tad idaṃ
children.translated_text: may the <s>Pramatha</s> couple (<s>Śiva</s> and <s>Pārvatī</s>), seeing this [scene], protect you —
and that child [<s>Skanda</s>], laughing, with his beak loosely swaying in playful dance. ||2.478||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text:
atihasitam, yathā-
karopagūḍha-pārśvaṃ yad uddhatāyata-niḥsvanam |
bāṣpākulākṣa-yugalaṃ tac cātihasitaṃ bhavet ||SRs_2.479|| 236
body.translated_text:
<s>Atihasita</s> (uproarious laughter), for example —
That which involves the sides embraced by the hands, with loud and prolonged sound,
and eyes brimming with tears — that is <s>atihasita</s>. ||2.479||

body.text:
yathā-
iti vācam uddhatam udīrya
sapadi saha veṇu-dāriṇā |
soḍha-ripu-bala-bharo' sahanaḥ
sa jahāsa datta-kara-tālam uccakaiḥ ||SRs_2.480|| (śi.va. 15.39)
body.translated_text:
For example —
Having uttered these bold words,
together with the reed-splitter [a warrior],
he, the bearer of the enemy army's burden, unable to endure,
laughed loudly, clapping his hands. ||2.480|| (<s>Śiśupāla-vadha</s> 15.39)

body.text:
atha vīraḥ-
vibhāvair anubhāvaiś ca svocitair vyabhicāribhiḥ |
nītaḥ sadasya-rasyatvam utsāho vīra ucyate ||SRs_2.481|| 237
eṣa tridhā samāsena dāna-yuddha-dayodbhavāḥ |
dāna-vīro dhṛtir harṣo matyādyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ ||SRs_2.482|| 238
smita-pūrvābhibhāṣitvaṃ smita-pūrvaṃ ca vīkṣitam |

children.translated_text: giving abundantly when showing favor, and likewise verbal approval,
considering merits and demerits — these are stated as the <s>anubhāvas</s>. ||2.483||

body.translated_text:
Now, <s>Vīra</s> (the Heroic <s>rasa</s>) —
Through <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> appropriate to it,
<s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), when brought to a state of being relishable by the audience, is called <s>Vīra</s>. ||2.481||
This is threefold in brief: arising from generosity (<s>dāna</s>), battle (<s>yuddha</s>), and compassion (<s>dayā</s>).
In the hero of generosity (<s>dāna-vīra</s>), steadfastness, joy, intellect, and the like are the transitory emotions. ||2.482||
Speaking preceded by a smile, looking preceded by a smile,

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: To that thief, who had repelled the fear of death,
the pleased king gave — for the [service of] two upper feet [i.e., a couplet of verse] —
ten <s>koṭis</s> (crores) of gold coins, mountains scratched by the tips of teeth [i.e., tusks],
and eight great elephants as well, with bees humming, intoxicated with rut-juice. ||2.484||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: yuddha-vīre harṣa-garvāmarṣādayā vyabhicāriṇā | 240
body.translated_text: In the hero of battle (<s>yuddha-vīra</s>), joy, pride, indignation, and the like are the transitory emotions.

body.text:
asāhāyye' pi yuddhecchā samarād apalāyanam |
bhītābhaya-pradānādyā vikārās tatra kīrtitāḥ ||SRs_2.485|| 241
body.translated_text:
Desire to fight even without allies, not fleeing from battle,
granting safety to the frightened — these and others are the expressions proclaimed therein. ||2.485||

body.text:
yathā-
rathī niṣaṅgī kavacī dhanuṣmān
dṛptah sa rājanyakam eka-vīraḥ |
vilolayāmāsa mahā-varāhaḥ
kalpa-kṣayodvṛttam ivārṇavāmbhaḥ ||SRs_2.486|| (ra.vaṃ. 7.56)
body.translated_text:
For example —
He, a chariot-warrior with quiver, armor, and bow,
proud, a lone hero [against] the warrior-host,
tossed [them about] like a great boar
[tossing] the ocean waters at the end of an <s>eon</s>. ||2.486|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.56)

body.text: dayā-vīre dhṛti-mati-pramukhā vyabhicāriṇaḥ |

children.translated_text: The disposition of protecting the distressed even at the cost of one's own interests and life,

children.text: āśvāsanoktayaḥ sthairyam ity ādyās tatra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.487||
children.translated_text: words of reassurance, firmness — these and others are the expressions therein. ||2.487||

body.translated_text: In the hero of compassion (<s>dayā-vīra</s>), steadfastness, intellect, and the like are the foremost transitory emotions.

body.text:
yathā-
ārtaṃ kaṇṭha-gata-prāṇaṃ parityaktaṃ sva-bāndhavaiḥ |
trāye nainaṃ yadi tataḥ kaḥ śarīreṇa me guṇaḥ ||SRs_2.488|| (nāgānanda 4.11)
body.translated_text:
For example —
If I do not rescue this afflicted one, whose life hangs in his throat,
abandoned by his own kinsmen,
then what use is my body to me? ||2.488|| (<s>Nāgānanda</s> 4.11)

body.text: atha adbhutaḥ-

children.translated_text: Through <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> appropriate to it,
<s>vismaya</s> (wonder), when brought to a state of being relishable by the audience, attains <s>adbhuta</s> (the state of the wondrous). ||2.489||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Adbhuta</s> (the Wondrous <s>rasa</s>) —

body.text: atra dhṛtyāvega-jāḍya-harṣādyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ | 244
body.translated_text: In it, steadfastness, excitement, stupor, joy, and the like are the transitory emotions.

body.text: ceṣṭās tu netra-vistāra-svedāśru-pulakādayaḥ ||SRs_2.490||
body.translated_text: The expressions are: widening of the eyes, perspiration, tears, goosebumps, and the like. ||2.490||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Salutations, O <s>Soḍhāha</s>!' — through the mouth of a messenger, instructions on another matter [were conveyed];

children.text: tat tādṛk samarāṅgaṇeṣu bhujayor vikrāntam avyāhatam |
