children.translated_text: that such unimpeded prowess of the arms in the battlefields!

children.text: bhītānāṃ parirakṣaṇaṃ punar api sve sve pade sthāpanaṃ
children.translated_text: the protection of the frightened, and the restoration of each to his own station —
remembering again and again, the enemies of the lord <s>Recarla-Siṃha</s> break out in goosebumps. ||2.491||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra nāyaka-guṇātiśaya-janito virodhināṃ vismayaḥ smṛti-harṣādibhiḥ vyabhicāribhir upacitaḥ pulakādibhir anubhāvair vyajyamāno' dbhutatvam āpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the wonder of the adversaries, produced by the excess of the hero's qualities, nourished by transitory emotions such as memory and joy, and expressed through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as goosebumps, attains the state of <s>adbhuta</s>.

body.text: atha raudraḥ-

children.translated_text: Through <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> appropriate to it,
<s>krodha</s> (anger), when brought to a state of being relishable by the audience, is called <s>Raudra</s>. ||2.492||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Raudra</s> (the Furious <s>rasa</s>) —

body.text: āvega-garvaugryāmarṣa-mohādyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ | 246
body.translated_text: Excitement, pride, ferocity, indignation, delusion, and the like are the transitory emotions.

body.text: prasveda-bhrukuṭī-netra-rāgādyās tatra vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.493||
body.translated_text: Perspiration, furrowed brows, reddening of the eyes, and the like are the expressions therein. ||2.493||

body.text: yathā karuṇākandale-

children.translated_text: With lips pressed by [teeth] agitated by self-reproach,
with efforts launched [simultaneously], indivisible by their simultaneity,
with cries of 'Strike! Cut!' — the <s>Bhilla</s> (tribal) bands,
blinded by arrogance, have besieged <s>Āniruddhi</s>. ||2.494||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Karuṇā-kandala</s> —

body.text: atra vajra-viṣayo bhilla-varga-krodhaḥ svātmākṣepādibhir uddīpitā darpāndha-paruṣa-vāg-ārambhādy-anumitair garvāsūyādibhiḥ paripoṣitaḥ svoṣṭha-pīḍana-śatru-nirodhādibhir anubhāvair abhivyakto raudratayā niṣpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the anger of the <s>Bhilla</s> bands directed toward <s>Vajra</s>, kindled by self-reproach and the like, nourished by pride, envy, and other [emotions] inferred from harsh speech beginning with arrogance-blinded [words], and expressed through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as pressing one's own lips and besieging the enemy, is produced as <s>Raudra</s>.

body.text: atha karuṇaḥ-

children.translated_text: Through <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> appropriate to it,
<s>śoka</s> (grief), when brought to a state of being relishable by the audience, is called <s>Karuṇa</s>. ||2.495||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Karuṇa</s> (the Pathetic <s>rasa</s>) —

body.text: atrāṣṭau sāttvikā jāḍya-nirveda-glāni-dīnatāḥ | 248
body.translated_text: In it, the eight <s>sāttvikas</s>, stupor, world-weariness, languor, wretchedness,

body.text: ālasyāpasmṛti-vyādhi-mohādyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ ||SRs_2.496||
body.translated_text: laziness, loss of memory, illness, delusion, and the like are the transitory emotions. ||2.496||

body.text: yathā karuṇākandale-

children.translated_text: His body instantly inflamed a hundredfold by the calamity of the lineage,

children.text: muhur bāṣpaṃ śvāsān malinam api rāgaṃ prakaṭayan |
children.translated_text: repeatedly displaying tears, sighs, and even darkened complexion,

children.text: ślathair aṅgaiḥ śūnyair asakṛd uparuddhaiś ca karaṇair
children.translated_text: with limbs slack, with senses vacant, with faculties repeatedly obstructed —

children.text: yuto dhatte glāniṃ karuṇa iva mūrto yadupatiḥ ||SRs_2.497||
children.translated_text: the lord of the <s>Yadus</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) bears languor, as if he were <s>Karuṇa</s> (<s>rasa</s>) embodied. ||2.497||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Karuṇā-kandala</s> —

body.text: atra bandhu-vyāpatti-janito vasudevasya śoko bandhu-guṇa-smaraṇādibhir uddīpito mlānatvendriya-śūnyatvādi-sūcitair dainya-moha-glānyādi-sañcāribhiḥ prapañcito muhur bāṣpa-śvāsa-malina-mukha-rāgādibhir anubhāvair abhivyaktaḥ karuṇatvam āpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the grief of <s>Vasudeva</s>, produced by the calamity of kinsmen, kindled by remembrance of their virtues and the like, elaborated by transitory emotions such as wretchedness, delusion, and languor indicated by fading and vacant senses, and expressed through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as repeated tears, sighs, and darkened facial color, attains the state of <s>Karuṇa</s>.

body.text: atha bībhatsaḥ-

children.translated_text: Through <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> appropriate to it,
<s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), when nourished, is relished as <s>Bībhatsa</s>. ||2.498||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Bībhatsa</s> (the Disgusting <s>rasa</s>) —

body.text: atra glāni-śramonmāda-mohāpasmāra-dīnatāḥ | 250
body.translated_text: In it, languor, fatigue, madness, delusion, <s>apasmāra</s> (epileptic fit), wretchedness,

body.text:
viṣāda-cāpalāvega-jāḍyādyā vyabhicāriṇaḥ |
sveda-romāñca-nāmāgra-cchādanādyāś ca vikriyāḥ ||SRs_2.499|| 251
body.translated_text:
despondency, agitation, excitement, stupor, and the like are the transitory emotions;
perspiration, goosebumps, covering the tip of the nose, and the like are the expressions. ||2.499||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: Surrounded by clusters of flies as if by the residue of sin,
touching his wound soaked with pus using a scrap of cloth,
the poor man afflicted with skin-disease, quickly moving aside from the chariot-path, contracting his eye-corners,
with nose covered, makes the people [recoil]. ||2.500||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra dardu-rogi-viṣayā rathyā-jana-jugupsā makṣikā-pūyādibhir uddīpitā tvarāpasaraṇānumitair viṣādādibhiḥ poṣitā netra-saṅkocanādibhir abhivyaktā bībhatsatām āpnoti |
body.translated_text: Here, the disgust of the street-people toward the skin-disease sufferer, kindled by flies and pus and the like, nourished by despondency and other [emotions] inferred from the haste of moving aside, and expressed through the contraction of the eyes and the like, attains the state of <s>Bībhatsa</s>.

body.text:
atha bhayānakaḥ-
vibhāvair anubhāvaiś ca svocitair vyabhicāribhiḥ |
bhayaṃ sadasya-rasyatvaṃ nītaṃ proktaṃ bhayānakaḥ ||SRs_2.501|| 252
tatra santrāsa-maraṇa-cāpalāvega-dīnatāḥ |

children.translated_text: despondency, delusion, epileptic fit, apprehension, and the like are the transitory emotions.
The expressions are drying of the mouth and the like; and the <s>sāttvikas</s> [are all] except tears. ||2.502||

body.translated_text:
Now, <s>Bhayānaka</s> (the Fearsome <s>rasa</s>) —
Through <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> appropriate to it,
<s>bhaya</s> (fear), when brought to a state of being relishable by the audience, is declared as <s>Bhayānaka</s>. ||2.501||
In it, terror, [resolve to] die, agitation, excitement, wretchedness,

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: The enemies of King <s>Śrī-Siṃha</s>, agitated upon hearing [the sound of] his march,
with palates drying, with feet stumbling, looking in every direction,

children.text: dhāvitvā katham apy upetya tamasā gāḍhopagūḍhāṃ guhām
children.translated_text: having somehow run and reached a cave deeply embraced by darkness,
search even within it, by the touch of their hands, for another pit [to hide in]. ||2.503||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra nāyaka-pratibhūpatināṃ bhayaṃ tad-dhāṭī-śravaṇādinoddīpitaṃ vyākulatva-tālu-śoṣa-pada-skhalanādy-anumitair āvega-śaṅkātrāsādibhir vyabhicāribhir upacitaṃ palāyana-guhā-praveśa-gartāntarānveṣaṇādibhir anubhāvair anubhūyamānaṃ bhayānakatvena niṣpadyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the fear of the rival kings of the hero, kindled by hearing of his march and the like, nourished by transitory emotions such as excitement, apprehension, and terror inferred from agitation, palate-drying, and stumbling of feet, and experienced through <s>anubhāvas</s> such as fleeing, entering a cave, and searching for another pit, is produced as <s>Bhayānaka</s>.

body.text: kecit samāna-balayo rasayoḥ saṅkaraṃ viduḥ | 254
body.translated_text: Some hold that when two <s>rasas</s> are of equal strength, there is a mixing (<s>saṅkara</s>) of the <s>rasas</s>.

body.text: na parīkṣākṣamam idaṃ mataṃ prekṣāvatāṃ bhavet ||SRs_2.504||
body.translated_text: This view would not withstand the scrutiny of the discerning. ||2.504||

body.text: tuṣyatve pūrva āsvādaḥ katarasyety aniścayāt | 255
body.translated_text: If both are satisfying, there is uncertainty as to which is relished first;

body.text: spardhāparatvād ubhayor anāsvāda-prasaṅgataḥ ||SRs_2.505||
body.translated_text: since both are rivals to each other, there would follow the absurdity of neither being relished. ||2.505||

body.text: tayor anyatarasyaiva prāyeṇāsvādanād api | 256
body.translated_text: Since generally only one of the two is relished,

body.text:
yugapad rasanīyatvaṃ nobhayor upapadyate |
eṣām aṅgāṅgi-bhāvena saṅkaro mama saṃmataḥ ||SRs_2.506|| 257
body.translated_text:
the simultaneous relishability of both is not established.
The mixing of these through the relation of principal and subsidiary (<s>aṅga-aṅgi-bhāva</s>) is my accepted view. ||2.506||

children.translated_text: And thus in the <s>Bhāratīya</s> [section] —

children.text: bhāvo vāpi raso vāpi pravṛttir vṛttir eva vā |
children.translated_text: Whether <s>bhāva</s> or <s>rasa</s> or <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity) or <s>vṛtti</s> (mode),

children.text: sarveṣāṃ samavetānāṃ rūpaṃ yasya bhaved bahu ||
children.translated_text: among all that are combined, that whose form predominates —

body.text: sa mantavyo rasaḥ sthāyī śeṣāḥ sañcāriṇo matāḥ ||SRs_2.507|| (nā.śā. 7.119) iti |
body.translated_text: that should be considered the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyin</s>); the rest are considered transitory (<s>sañcārins</s>). ||2.507|| (<s>Nāṭya-śāstra</s> 7.119) Thus.

body.text:
tulādhṛtatvam anayor na syāt prakaraṇādinā |
kavi-tātparya-viśrānter ekatraivāvalokanāt ||SRs_2.508|| 258
body.translated_text:
The equal balancing of these two would not occur, because of context and the like;
since the repose of the poet's intention is seen in one alone. ||2.508||

body.text:
atha paraspara-viruddha-rasa-pratipādanam-
ubhau śṛṅgāra-bībhatsāv ubhau vīra-bhayānakau |
raudrādbhutāv ubhau hāsya-karuṇau prakṛti-dviṣau ||SRs_2.509|| 259
svabhāva-vairiṇor aṅgāṅgi-bhāvenāpi miśraṇam |
vivekibhyo na svadate gandha-gandhakayor iva ||SRs_2.510|| 260
virodhino' pi sāṃnidhyād atiraskāra-lakṣaṇam |
poṣaṇaṃ prakṛtasyeti ced aṅgatvaṃ na tāvatā ||SRs_2.511|| 261
yat kiñcid upakāritvād aṅgasyāṅgitvam aṅgini |
na tat-saṃnidhi-mātreṇa carvaṇānupakārataḥ ||SRs_2.512|| 262
anyathā pānakādyeṣu śarkarāder ivāpatet |

children.translated_text: even a blade of grass that falls in between would have beneficence;
and the desire for relishing [the drink] would become the consuming-together-with-grass. ||2.513||

body.translated_text:
Now, the exposition of mutually opposed <s>rasas</s> —
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>Bībhatsa</s> are both [opposed]; <s>Vīra</s> and <s>Bhayānaka</s> are both [opposed];
<s>Raudra</s> and <s>Adbhuta</s> are both [opposed]; <s>Hāsya</s> and <s>Karuṇa</s> are natural enemies. ||2.509||
Even the mixing of natural enemies through the relation of principal and subsidiary
is not palatable to the discerning, just as perfume and sulphur [are incompatible]. ||2.510||
If one argues that mere proximity of opposed [rasas], characterized by non-concealment,
nourishes the principal — [we reply:] subsidiary status is not established thereby. ||2.511||
Because something is slightly beneficial, the subsidiary does not become principal in the principal;
not by its mere proximity, since it does not aid in the relishing. ||2.512||
Otherwise, [it would be] like sugar and the like in beverages —

body.text: nisarga-vairiṇor aṅgāṅgi-bhāvāt svādābhāvo, yathā-

children.translated_text: Let saliva-water flow, or let it be full of tooth-bones,
or let the lip be streaked with blood,
or let the eyes be lustrous, mingled with well-moist flesh —
this face of yours is the essence of worldly existence. ||2.514||

body.translated_text: The absence of relish from the principal-subsidiary relation of natural enemies, for example —

body.text: atra śṛṅgāra-rasāṅgatām aṅgīkṛtavatā bībhatsena aṅgino' pi vicchedāya mūle kuṭhāro vyāpāritaḥ | evam anyeṣām api virodhinām aṅgāṅgi-bhāvenāsvādābhāvas tatra tatrodāharaṇe draṣṭavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Bībhatsa</s>, having accepted the subsidiary role to <s>Śṛṅgāra rasa</s>, has wielded an axe at the root even of the principal. Thus, the absence of relish from the principal-subsidiary relation of other opposed [rasas] too should be observed in the respective examples.

body.text: bhṛtyor nāyakasyeva nisarga-dveṣiṇor api | 264
body.translated_text: Like two servants of the hero, [when two <s>rasas</s>] that are natural enemies

body.text: aṅgayor aṅgino vṛddhau bhaved ekatra saṅgatiḥ ||SRs_2.515||
body.translated_text: are both subsidiaries, their co-occurrence in one [composition] promotes the principal. ||2.515||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: When she fashioned <s>makarī</s> (crocodile) marks on both cheeks with musk,
and the inscriptions of your royal titles were quietly composed upon their own breasts out of excessive familiarity,
O hero, King <s>Śrī-Siṃha-bhūpa</s>, the bold women of your rivals' inner chambers,

children.text: ānavyājena lajjāṃ sapadi vidadhate svāvarodhe pragalbhāḥ ||SRs_2.516||
children.translated_text: under the pretext of bowing, at once display shame [as if she were] a co-wife to [their] royal fortune. ||2.516||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra pratināyaka-gatayoḥ śṛṅgāra-bībhatsayoḥ nāyaka-gata-vīra-rasāṅgatvād ekatra samāveśo na doṣāya |
body.translated_text: Here, since the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>Bībhatsa</s> belonging to the antagonists are both subsidiaries of the <s>Vīra rasa</s> belonging to the hero, their co-occurrence in one [verse] is not a fault.

body.text: nanv atra śatrūṇāṃ sva-vakṣasi nāyaka-viruda-vilekhanena jīvitānta-nirmita-sthānīyena janitā nija-jīvita-jugupsā svāvarodha-sāṃnidhyādibhir uddīpitā lajjānumitair nirveda-dainya-viṣādādibhir upacitā tad-anumitair eva mānasika-kutsādibhiḥ abhivyaktā satī nāyaka-gataṃ śaraṇāgata-rakṣā-lakṣaṇaṃ vīraṃ puṣṇātīti pratīyate | na punaḥ pratināyaka-gatasya śṛṅgārasya nāyaka-vīropakaraṇatvam (iti ced), ucyate-nāyaka-kṛpā-kaṭākṣa-sthirīkṛta-rājyānāṃ pratināyakānāṃ tādṛśāḥ (śṛṅgāra-) vinodāḥ sambhaveyuḥ | nānyatheti tasya śṛṅgārasya nāyaka-vīropakaraṇatva-viruda-dhāraṇādi-paricayena rājya-lakṣmī-sapatnī-pada-prayogeṇa cābhivyajyate |
body.translated_text: Now, the self-disgust of the enemies' [wives] produced by [their husbands'] inscribing the hero's royal title upon their own breasts — [a deed] tantamount to an end-of-life creation — kindled by the proximity of the harem women and the like, nourished by world-weariness, wretchedness, despondency, and the like inferred from shame, and expressed by mental reproach and the like inferred from those [emotions], is perceived as nourishing the <s>Vīra</s> [<s>rasa</s>] belonging to the hero, characterized by the protection of those who seek refuge. If one objects that the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> of the antagonists does not serve as an instrument for the hero's <s>Vīra</s> — [we reply:] such <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>-amusements of the antagonists are possible [only because] their kingdoms have been secured by the gracious side-glance of the hero. Not otherwise. And this instrumentality of that <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> for the hero's <s>Vīra</s> is expressed through the familiarity of bearing the [hero's] title and through the use of the expression 'co-wife to royal fortune.'

body.text: atha rasābhāsaḥ-

children.translated_text: A <s>rasa</s>, by a subsidiary growing in self-willed power,
would become a semblance, like a master [overcome] by an unruly minister. ||2.517||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>) —

children.translated_text: And thus in the <s>Bhāva-prakāśikā</s> —
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> predominantly [mixed with] <s>Hāsya</s> is declared a semblance of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>;
<s>Hāsya</s> predominantly [mixed with] <s>Bībhatsa</s> is declared a semblance of <s>Hāsya</s>. ||2.518||
<s>Vīra</s> predominantly [mixed with] <s>Bhayānaka</s> is declared a semblance of <s>Vīra</s>;
<s>Adbhuta</s> by contact with <s>Karuṇa</s> is called a semblance of <s>Adbhuta</s>. ||2.519||
<s>Raudra</s> by contact with grief and fear is declared a semblance of <s>Raudra</s>;
<s>Karuṇa</s> predominantly [mixed with] <s>Hāsya</s> is called a semblance of <s>Karuṇa</s>. ||2.520||

body.text:
bībhatso' dbhuta-śṛṅgārī bībhatsābhāsa ucyate |
sa syād bhayānakābhāso raudra-vīropasaṅgamāt ||SRs_2.521|| iti |
body.translated_text:
<s>Bībhatsa</s> [mixed with] <s>Adbhuta</s> and <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is called a semblance of <s>Bībhatsa</s>.
A semblance of <s>Bhayānaka</s> arises from contact with <s>Raudra</s> and <s>Vīra</s>. ||2.521|| Thus.

body.text:
atra śṛṅgāra-rasasya arāgād aneka-rāgāt tiryag-rāgāt mleccha-rāgāc ceti caturvidham ābhāsa-bhūyastvam | tatra arāgas tv ekatra rāgābhāvaḥ | tena rasasyābhāsatvaṃ, yathā-
sa rāmo naḥ sthātā na yudhi purato lakṣmaṇa-sakho
bhavitrī rambhoru tridaśa-vadana-glānir adhunā |
prayāsyaty evoccair vipadam acirād vānara-camūr
laghiṣṭhedaṃ ṣaṣṭhākṣara-para-vilopāt paṭha punaḥ ||SRs_2.522|| (ha.nā. 10.12)
body.translated_text:
Here, the semblance of <s>Śṛṅgāra rasa</s> is fourfold: from absence of love, from love toward many, from love toward animals, and from love of <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians). Among these, absence of love is the absence of love in one [party]. From that, the semblance of <s>rasa</s>, for example —
'That <s>Rāma</s> will not stand before us in battle, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s companion;
now, O beautiful-thighed one, the gods' faces will wilt.
The monkey army will soon fall into great calamity.
Read [the verse] again lightly, with the deletion of every sixth syllable.' ||2.522|| (<s>Hanumān-nāṭaka</s> 10.12)

body.text: atra sītāyāṃ rāvaṇa-viṣaya-rāgātyantābhāvād ābhāsatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, because of the complete absence of love in <s>Sītā</s> for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, it is a semblance.

body.text: nanv ekatra rāgābhāvād rasasyābhāsatvaṃ na yujyate | prathamam ajātānurāge vatsa-rāje jātānurāgāyāḥ ratnāvalyāḥ-
body.translated_text: Now, the objection that the semblance of <s>rasa</s> due to absence of love in one [party] is not justified — [since] in the case of <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, who has developed love for Prince <s>Vatsa</s> before his love had arisen —

body.text:
dullaha-jaṇāṇurāo lajjā guruī parabbaso appā |
pia-sahi visamaṃ pemmaṃ maraṇaṃ saraṇaṃ nu varam ekkaṃ ||SRs_2.523|| (ra.ā. 2.1)
body.translated_text:
Difficult [to obtain] is the love of people; shame is heavy; the self is under another's control;
O dear friend, love is cruel — death alone is the one best refuge! ||2.523|| (<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.1)

children.translated_text: [Difficult to obtain is the love of people; shame is heavy; the self is under another's control;

children.text: priya-sakhi viṣamaṃ prema maraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ nu varam ekam ||]
children.translated_text: O dear friend, love is cruel — death alone is the one best refuge!]

body.text: ity atra pūrvānurāgasyābhāsatva-prasaṅga iti ced ucyate | abhāvo hi trividhaḥ prāg-abhāvo' tyantābhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvaś ceti | tatra prāg-abhāve darśanādi-kāraṇeṣu sambhāviteṣu rāgotpatti-sambhāvanayā nābhāsatvam | itarayos tu kāraṇa-sad-bhāve' pi rāgānutpatter ābhāsatvam eva | anye tu striyā eva rāgābhāve rasasyābhāsatvaṃ pratijānate | na tad upapadyate | puruṣe' pi rāgābhāve rasasyānāsvādanīyatvāt | yathā-
body.translated_text: — here, the prior love (<s>pūrvānurāga</s>) would be subject to the charge of being a semblance — if [so objected], [we] reply: Absence [of love] is threefold: prior absence (<s>prāg-abhāva</s>), absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>), and destruction-absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>). In the case of prior absence, since the causes such as seeing [the beloved] are anticipated, there is the possibility of the arising of love, hence it is not a semblance. In the other two [types], even when causes exist, since love does not arise, it is indeed a semblance. Others, however, maintain that it is a semblance of <s>rasa</s> only when the woman lacks love. That is not tenable, because when the man too lacks love, the <s>rasa</s> becomes unrelishable. For example —

body.text:
gate premāveśe praṇaya-bahu-māne' pi galite
nivṛtte sad-bhāve jana iva jane gacchati puraḥ |
tad utprekṣyotprekṣya priya-sakhi gatāṃs tāṃś ca divasān
na jāne ko hetur dalati śatadhā yan na hṛdayam ||SRs_2.524|| (amaru 43)
body.translated_text:
When the onset of love has departed, when even the honor of affection has dwindled,
when true feeling has ceased, when he passes before me like a stranger among strangers —
then, imagining and re-imagining those bygone days, dear friend,
I know not what the reason is that my heart does not shatter into a hundred pieces. ||2.524|| (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 43)

body.text: atra hṛdaya-dalanābhāva-pūrva-gata-divasotprekṣādy-anumitair nirveda-smṛty-ādibhir abhivyakto' pi striyā anurāgaḥ premāveśa-ślathanādi-kathitena puruṣa-gata-rāga-dhvaṃsanena cārutāṃ nāpnoti |
body.translated_text: Here, the love of the woman, though expressed through world-weariness, memory, and the like inferred from the imagining of bygone days and the non-shattering of the heart, does not attain beauty because of the destruction of the man's love, described through the loosening of love's onset and the like.

body.text: puruṣa-rāgātyantābhāvena rasābhāsatvaṃ, yathā-
body.translated_text: From absolute absence of love in the man, it is a <s>rasābhāsa</s>, for example —

body.text:
dhyāna-vyājam upetya cintayasi kām unmīlya cakṣuḥ kṣaṇaṃ
paśyānaṅga-śarāturaṃ janam imaṃ trātāpi no rakṣasi |
mithyā-kāruṇiko' si nirghūṇataras tvattaḥ kuto' nyaḥ pumān
serṣyaṃ māra-vadhūbhir ity abhihito buddho jinaḥ pātu vaḥ ||SRs_2.525|| (nāgā. 1.1)
body.translated_text:
'Under the pretense of meditation, whom are you contemplating? Open your eyes for a moment —
behold this person afflicted by <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (<s>Kāmadeva</s>'s) arrows — even as protector, you do not save!
You are falsely compassionate, more merciless [than others] — what other man is [as heartless] as you?'
Thus addressed by <s>Māra</s>'s (the Tempter's) wives with jealousy — may the <s>Buddha</s>, the Conqueror, protect you! ||2.525|| (<s>Nāgānanda</s> 1.1)

body.text: atra jinasya rāgātyantābhāvena rasābhāsatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, because of the absolute absence of love in the Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>), it is a <s>rasābhāsa</s>.

body.text:
anekatra yoṣito rāgābhāsatvaṃ, yathā-
paraspareṇa kṣatayoḥ prahartror
utkrāntavāyvoḥ samakālam eva |
amartya-bhāve' pi kayościd āsīd
ekāpsaraḥ-prārthanayor vivādaḥ ||SRs_2.526|| (ra.vaṃ. 7.53)
body.translated_text:
From the love of a woman toward many [men], it is a semblance, for example —
Of two combatants who struck each other,
whose vital breaths departed at the same moment,
even upon attaining the state of immortals, there arose
a dispute between the two who desired the same <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymph). ||2.526|| (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 7.53)

body.text: atra kasyāścid divya-vanitāyā vīra-dvaye raṇānivṛtti-maraṇa-prāpta-devatābhāve anurāgasya nirupamānaśūra-guṇopādher avaiṣamyeṇa pratibhāsanādābhāsatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, because the love of a certain divine woman for two heroes — who attained divinity through death without retreating from battle — appears without inequality, due to the qualifier of unparalleled heroic virtue [being equal in both], it is a semblance.

body.text: anekatra puṃso rāgād, yathā-
body.translated_text: From the love of a man toward many [women], for example —

children.text: ramyaṃ gāyati menakā kṛta-rucir vīṇā-svanair urvaśī
children.translated_text: <s>Menakā</s> sings charmingly; <s>Urvaśī</s>, with the sounds of the <s>vīṇā</s>, creates delight;
<s>Tilottamā</s> displays wondrous intimacy in the sequence of various bodily gestures;

children.text: āsāṃ rūpam idaṃ tad uttamam iti premānavasthā dviṣā
children.translated_text: 'this is their beauty, that is the finest' — this unsettled state of love, split by rivalry,
was attained by [a hero slain by] the sword-edge of King <s>Śrī-Yanapota-Siṃha</s>. ||2.527||

body.text: atra nāyaka-khaḍga-dhārā-galitātmanaḥ kasyacit svarga-pratināyaka-vīrasya menakādi-svarloka-gaṇikāsu avaiṣamyeṇa rāgād ābhāsatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, because of the love without inequality of a certain heavenly antagonist-hero — whose life slipped away upon the edge of the hero's sword — toward the celestial courtesans <s>Menakā</s> and others of the heavenly world, it is a semblance.

body.text: nanv evaṃ dakṣiṇādīnām api rāgasyābhāsatvam iti cet, na | dakṣiṇasya nāyakasya nāyikāsu anekāsu vṛtti-mātreṇaiva sādhāraṇyam | na rāgeṇa | tad ekasyām eva rāgasya prauḍhatvam | itarāsu tu madhyamatvaṃ mandatvaṃ ceti tad-anurāgasya nābhāsatā | atra tu avaiṣamyeṇa anekatra pravṛtter ābhāsatvam upapadyate |
body.translated_text: If it is objected that by this [reasoning], the love of the gallant (<s>dakṣiṇa</s>) [hero] and others would also be a semblance — no; because the <s>dakṣiṇa</s> hero's commonality among many heroines is by conduct alone, not by love. His love is mature toward one alone; toward the others, it is middling or faint. Hence his love is not a semblance. But here, because of the equal pursuit of many without inequality, the semblance-status is established.

body.text:
tiryag-rāgād, yathā-
madhu dvirephaḥ kusumaika-pātre
papau priyāṃ svām anuvartamānaḥ |
śṛṅgeṇa ca sparśa-nimīlitākṣīṃ
mṛgīm akaṇḍūyata kṛṣṇa-sāraḥ ||SRs_2.528|| (ku.saṃ. 3.36)

mleccha-rāgād, yathā-
ajjaṃ mohaṇa-suhiaṃ muatti mottū palāie halie |
dara-phuḍia-beṇṭa-bhāroṇaāi hasiaṃ ba phalahīe ||SRs_2.529|| (gāthā 4.60)
body.translated_text:
From the love of <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians), for example —
'The noble lady, blissful in the swoon of love, is dead!' — having said this, when the ploughman fled,
the cotton plant, drooping under the barely-split-open weight of its bolls, seemed to laugh. ||2.529|| (<s>Gāthā</s> 4.60)

children.translated_text: [The noble lady, blissful in the swoon of love, is dead! — having said this, when the ploughman fled,
the cotton plant, drooping under the barely-split-open weight of its bolls, seemed to laugh.]

body.text: atra surata-mohana-supti-maraṇa-daśayor vivekābhāvena hālikasya mlecchatvaṃ gamyate |
body.translated_text: Here, the barbarian status of the ploughman is understood from his inability to distinguish between the states of love-swoon death and [actual] death.

body.text: nanu tiryaṅ-mleccha-gatayor ābhāsatvaṃ na yujyate | tayor vibhāvādi-sambhavāt | āsvāda-yogyatā-pratīter iti cet, na | bho mleccha-rasa-vādin ! uktalādhipateḥ śṛṅgāra-rasābhimānino narasiṃhadevasya cittam anuvartamānena vidyādhareṇa kavinā bāḍham abhyantarī-kṛto' si | evaṃ khalu samarthitam ekāvalyām anena-
body.translated_text: Now, the objection that the semblance-status is not justified for those [emotions] belonging to animals and <s>mlecchas</s>, since the <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like do occur in them, and the capacity for relishability is perceived — [we reply:] No, O advocate of <s>mleccha-rasa</s>! You have indeed been taken inside [the position of] <s>Narasiṃhadeva</s>, the lord of <s>Uktala</s>, who claims the <s>Śṛṅgāra rasa</s> for himself, by the poet <s>Vidyādhara</s> who follows his [patron's] mind. For thus he has argued in the <s>Ekāvalī</s> —

body.text: apare tu rasābhāsaṃ tiryakṣu pracakṣate | tan na parīkṣā-kṣamam | teṣv api vibhāvādi-sambhavāt | vibhāvādi-jñāna-śūnyās tiryañco na bhājanaṃ bhavitum arhanti rasasyeti cet, na | manuṣyeṣv api keṣucit tathā-bhūteṣu rasa-viṣaya-bhāvābhāva-prasaṅgāt | vibhāvādi-sambhavo hi rasaṃ prati prayojakaḥ | na vibhāvādi-jñānam | tataś ca tiraścām apy asty eva rasaḥ iti | (ekāvalyām 106)
body.translated_text: 'Others, however, declare a <s>rasābhāsa</s> in animals. That does not withstand scrutiny, since the <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like do occur in them. If [one objects that] animals, being devoid of knowledge of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like, cannot be receptacles of <s>rasa</s> — no; because in certain humans too, who are similarly constituted, there would follow the absurdity of the absence of <s>rasa</s>. For it is the occurrence of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like that is instrumental for <s>rasa</s>, not the knowledge of <s>vibhāvas</s>. Therefore, <s>rasa</s> indeed exists in animals as well.' (<s>Ekāvalī</s> 106)

body.text: na tāvat tiraścāṃ vibhāvatam upapadyate | śṛṅgāre hi samujjvalasya śucino darśanīyasyaiva vastuno muninā vibhāvatvenāmnātam | tiraścam udvartana-majjanākalpa-racanādy-abhāvād ujjvala-śuci-darśanīyatvānām asambhāvanā prasiddhaiva |
body.translated_text: But the <s>vibhāva</s>-status of animals is not established. For in <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, only a thing that is radiant, pure, and beautiful is taught by the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] as having <s>vibhāva</s>-status. Since animals lack anointing, bathing, ornamental arrangement, and the like, the impossibility of their being radiant, pure, and beautiful is well-known indeed.

body.text: atha sva-jāti-yogyair dharmaiḥ kāriṇāṃ kariṇīṃ prati (dadau saraḥ paṅkaja ity ādi (ku.saṃ. 3.37) padye iva) vibhāvatvam iti cen, na | tasyāṃ kakṣyāyāṃ kariṇāṃ kariṇī-rāgaṃ prati kāraṇatvaṃ na punar vibhāvatvam |
body.translated_text: If [one argues that] through qualities appropriate to their own species (as in the verse 'the lake gave the elephant lotuses' and the like [<s>Kumārasambhava</s> 3.37]), there is <s>vibhāva</s>-status — no; in that category, the [features] are causes of elephants' love for she-elephants, but not <s>vibhāvas</s> [in the technical sense].

body.text: kiṃ ca, jāti-yogyair dharmair vastuno na vibhāvatvam | api tu bhāvaka-cittollāsa-hetubhiḥ rati-viśiṣṭair eva |
body.translated_text: Moreover, a thing does not have <s>vibhāva</s>-status through species-appropriate qualities, but only through those that cause delight in the heart of the connoisseur (<s>bhāvaka</s>) and are distinguished by <s>rati</s> (love).

body.text: kiṃ ca, vibhāvādi-jñānaṃ nāma aucitya-vivekaḥ | tena śūnyās tiryañco na vibhāvatām arhanti |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, knowledge of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like is [nothing but] the discernment of propriety (<s>aucitya-viveka</s>). Animals, being devoid of that, do not qualify for <s>vibhāva</s>-status.

body.text: tarhi vibhāvādi-jñāna-rahiteṣu manuṣyeṣu rasābhāsa-prasaṅga iti cet, naiṣa doṣaḥ | viveka-rahita-janopalakṣaṇa-mleccha-gatasya rasasyābhāsatve sveṣṭāvāpteḥ |
body.translated_text: If one objects that in humans too who lack knowledge of <s>vibhāvas</s>, there would follow the charge of <s>rasābhāsa</s> — that is no fault; since our position is achieved by the semblance-status of <s>rasa</s> belonging to <s>mlecchas</s>, who are the designation for people lacking discernment.

body.text: kiṃ ca vibhāvādi-sambhavo hi rasaṃ prati prayojako na vibhāvādi-jñānam ity etan na yujyate | tathā hi-vibhāvāder viśiṣṭasya vastu-mātrasya vā sambhavo rasaṃ prati prayojakaḥ | viśiṣṭa-prayojakatvāṅgīkāre vivekādi-praveśo' ṅgīkṛta iti asmad-anusaraṇam eva śaraṇaṃ gato' si |
body.translated_text: Moreover, the [position that] 'the occurrence of <s>vibhāvas</s> and the like is instrumental for <s>rasa</s>, not the knowledge of <s>vibhāvas</s>' — this is not tenable. For it is the occurrence of the qualified [<s>vibhāva</s>], or of the mere object, that is instrumental for <s>rasa</s>. If one accepts the instrumentality of the qualified [<s>vibhāva</s>], one has accepted the inclusion of discernment and the like — thus you have resorted to following our position alone as refuge.

body.text: atra vivekaṃ vinā tad-itara-viśeṣavattvaṃ vaiśiṣṭyam iti cen, na | viśeṣāṇāṃ dharmiṇi paramotkarṣānusandhāna-tat-parāṇām anyonya-sahiṣṇūnām iyattayā niyamāsambhavāt |
body.translated_text: Here, if [one claims] that the distinction lies in having specificities (<s>viśeṣas</s>) other than those, without discrimination — no, because the specificities, which are intent on ascertaining the supreme excellence in the substrate, being mutually compatible, cannot be limited in number.

body.text: atha yadi vastu-mātrasya tarhi anvāsitam arundhatyā svāhayeva havir bhujam (ra.vaṃ. 1.56) ity ādāv api strī-puṃsa-vyakti-mātra-vibhāva-sad-bhāvād anvāsanālakṣaṇānubhāva-sambhavāc ca śṛṅgāraḥ svadanīyaḥ prasajyeta | kiṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Now, if [one argues it is the case with] the bare object alone, then in passages like 'Attended upon by <s>Arundhatī</s>, like <s>Svāhā</s> [attends upon] the consumer of oblations' (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 1.56), since there exists the <s>vibhāva</s> of mere male-female individuals and since the <s>anubhāva</s> in the form of attendance is possible, the unwanted consequence would follow that <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> should be relished. Moreover —

children.text: ajjaṃ mohaṇa-suhiaṃ muatti mottū palāie halie |
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Today, the pleasant enchantment — let go of it! Let it be released! Leave it, O plow-wielder!
The slightly loosened burden of the girdle — [she] laughed at the fruit-woman.'

body.translated_text: Footnote:

body.text: 529 saṅkhyaka-padyaṃ draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: See verse numbered 529.

body.text: ity ādiṣu strī-puṃsa-vyakti-mātra-vibhāva-sadbhāvaḥ sphuṭa eva | tad-aviveka-janita-hāsya-paṅka-nirmagnaṃ śṛṅgāra-gandha-gajam uddhartuṃ tvaratām ity alaṃ rasābhāsāpalāpa-saṃrambheṇa |
body.translated_text: In passages such as these, the existence of the <s>vibhāva</s> of mere male-female individuals is quite evident. Let him hasten who would rescue the elephant of even the fragrance of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, submerged in the mud of laughter born from such non-discrimination! Enough of the excitement of the discourse on <s>Rasābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>rasa</s>)!

body.text: nanu sītādi-vibhāvair vastu-mātrair eva yoṣin-mātra-pratītau sāmājikānāṃ rasodayaḥ | na punar viśiṣṭaiḥ | tat katham iti ced, ucyate | atra janaka-tanayatva-rāma-parigrahatvādi-viruddha-dharma-parihāreṇa lalitojjvala-śuci-darśanīyatvādi-viśiṣṭa eva śabdataḥ | (pratipadyamāno) sītādi-vibhāvo yoṣit-sāmānyaṃ tādṛśam eva jñāpayati | na punaḥ strī-jāti-mātram iti sakalam api kalyāṇam |
body.translated_text: If one objects: 'It is through bare objects alone, such as <s>Sītā</s> and the like, functioning as <s>vibhāvas</s>, that the <s>rasa</s> arises in the spectators through the perception of [her as] womanhood in general, and not through specificities' — the answer is: here, the <s>vibhāva</s> such as <s>Sītā</s>, presented verbally as specified by qualities such as being graceful, radiant, pure, and beautiful to behold — with the exclusion of contradictory attributes such as being <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter and <s>Rāma</s>'s wife — conveys womanhood in general of precisely that [refined] sort, and not the mere generic category of woman. Thus all is well.

body.text:
hariścandro rakṣākaraṇa-ruci-satyeṣu vacasāṃ
vilāse vāgīśo mahati niyame nīti-nigame |
vijetā gāṅgeyaṃ jana-bharaṇa-saṃmohana-kalā-
vrateṣu śrī-siṃha-kṣitipatir udāro viharate ||SRs_2.530|| 267
body.translated_text: A <s>Hariścandra</s> in the delight of truthful words that accomplish protection, a lord of speech in grand verbal display, [a master] of great discipline in the precepts of statecraft, a conqueror — like <s>Gāṅgeya</s> (<s>Bhīṣma</s>) — in vows of the art of enchanting and nourishing people, the illustrious King <s>Siṃha</s> magnanimously delights. ||2.530||

body.text:
nitya śrīyannapota-kṣitipati-januṣaḥ siṃha-bhūpāla-mauleḥ
saundaryaṃ sundarīṇāṃ hariṇa-vijayināṃ vāgurā locanānām |
dānaṃ mandāra-cintāmaṇi-sura-surabhī-garva-nirvāpaṇāṅkaṃ
vijñānaṃ sarva-vidyā-nidhi-budha-pariṣac-chemuṣī-bhāgya-rekhā ||SRs_2.531|| 268
body.translated_text: Of the eternally glorious <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s>, the crown [jewel], born of King <s>Annapota</s>: the beauty [he inspires] is a snare of the deer-conquering eyes of beautiful women; his generosity bears the mark of quenching the pride of the <s>Mandāra</s> tree, <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> gem, celestial cow, and <s>Kalpa</s>-tree; his learning is the fortune-line of the assemblies of sages who are treasuries of all knowledge. ||2.531||

body.text:
iti śrīmad-āndhra-maṇḍalādhīśvara-pratigaṇḍa-bhairava-śrīmad-anapota-narendra-nandana-bhuja-bala-bhīma-śrī-siṃha-bhūpāla-viracite rasārṇava-sudhākara-nāmni nāṭyālaṅkāra-śāstre rasikollāso nāma
dvitīyo vilāsaḥ
||2||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, named <s>Rasikollāsa</s> (The Delight of the Connoisseur), in the treatise on dramatic aesthetics called <s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s>, of arm-strength [mighty as] <s>Bhīma</s>, son of the illustrious Emperor <s>Anapota</s>, <s>Pratigaṇḍa-Bhairava</s>, lord of the <s>Āndhra</s> realm. ||2||

body.text:
(3)
tṛtīyo vilāsaḥ
bhāvakollāsaḥ
body.translated_text: (3) Third Chapter: <s>Bhāvakollāsa</s> (The Delight of Emotion)

body.text:
sa kṣemadāyī kamalānukūlaḥ
kaṭhora-pārāvata-kaṇṭha-nīlaḥ |
kṛpā-nidhir bhavya-guṇābhirāmaḥ
paraḥ pumān raja-mahīdhra-vāsī ||SRs_3.1|| 1
body.translated_text: May that Supreme Being, giver of welfare, favorable to <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), dark as the throat of a bold pigeon, a treasury of compassion, charming with auspicious qualities, dwelling on the Royal Mountain (<s>Rāja-mahīdhra</s>), [protect us]. ||3.1||

body.text: bhavatv iti sambandhaḥ smaraṇīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'May [He] be [gracious]' — this is the implied construction.

body.text:
tad īdṛśa-rasādhāraṃ nāṭyaṃ rūpakam ity api |
naṭasyātipravīṇasya karmatvān nāṭyam ucyate ||SRs_3.2|| 2
yathā mukhādau padmāder ārope rūpaka-prathā |

children.translated_text: so too, the superimposition of the hero upon the actor is called <s>Rūpaka</s>.
And that <s>Nāṭya</s> is tenfold, consisting of the enactment of the meaning of sentences. ||3.3||

body.translated_text: That <s>Nāṭya</s> (drama), the repository of such <s>rasas</s>, is also called <s>Rūpaka</s> (dramatic composition). Because it is the deed of a highly skilled actor (<s>naṭa</s>), it is called <s>Nāṭya</s>. ||3.2|| Just as the metaphorical convention (<s>rūpaka</s>) [operates] in the superimposition of a lotus, etc. upon a face, etc.,

body.text:
tathā ca bhāratīye (18.2-3)-
nāṭakaṃ saprakaraṇam aṅko vyāyoga eva ca |
bhāṇaḥ samavakāraś ca vīthī prahasanaṃ ḍimaḥ |

children.translated_text: <s>Bhāṇa</s> (monologue), <s>Samavakāra</s> (conflict play), <s>Vīthī</s> (skit), <s>Prahasana</s> (farce), <s>Ḍima</s> (spectacle play),

body.translated_text: And thus in the <s>Bhāratīya</s> [section] (18.2-3) — '<s>Nāṭaka</s> (heroic drama), <s>Prakaraṇa</s> (social play), <s>Aṅka</s> (one-act play), <s>Vyāyoga</s> (military play),

body.text: rasetivṛtta-netāras tat-tad-rūpaka-bhedakāḥ | 4
body.translated_text: and <s>Īhāmṛga</s> (chase play) — thus should be known the tenfold classification of drama.' ||3.4|| <s>Rasa</s>, plot (<s>itivṛtta</s>), and hero (<s>netā</s>) are the distinguishing factors of each type of <s>Rūpaka</s>.

body.text: lakṣitau rasanetārāv itivṛttaṃ tu kathyate ||SRs_3.5||
body.translated_text: When <s>Rasa</s> and the hero have been determined, the plot (<s>itivṛtta</s>) is then described. ||3.5||

body.text: itivṛtta-kathā-vastu-śabdāḥ paryāya-vācinaḥ | 5
body.translated_text: <s>Itivṛtta</s>, <s>Kathā</s>, and <s>Vastu</s> — these words are synonyms.

body.text: itivṛttaṃ prabandhasya śarīraṃ trividhaṃ hi tat ||SRs_3.6||
body.translated_text: The <s>itivṛtta</s> (plot) is the body of the composition; it is of three kinds. ||3.6||

body.text: khyātaṃ kalpyaṃ ca saṅkīrṇaṃ khyātaṃ rāma-kathādikam | 6
body.translated_text: Well-known (<s>khyāta</s>), invented (<s>kalpya</s>), and mixed (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>). Well-known is like the story of <s>Rāma</s> and such.

body.text: kavi-buddhi-kṛtaṃ kalpyaṃ mālatī-mādhavādikam ||SRs_3.7||
body.translated_text: Invented is that created by the poet's imagination, like <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> and such. ||3.7||

body.text: saṅkīrṇam ubhayāyattaṃ lava-rāghava-ceṣṭitam | 7
body.translated_text: Mixed is that dependent on both, like the exploits of <s>Lava</s> [and <s>Kuśa</s>] in [plays about] the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty.

body.text: lakṣyeṣv etat tu bahudhā divya-martyādi-bhedataḥ ||SRs_3.8||
body.translated_text: This [plot], in specific instances, is manifold by the distinction of divine, human, and other [types]. ||3.8||

body.text: tac cetivṛttaṃ vidvadbhiḥ pañcadhā parikīrtitam | 8
body.translated_text: And that <s>itivṛtta</s> (plot) is declared by the learned to be fivefold:

body.text: bījaṃ binduḥ patākā ca prakarī kāryam ity api ||SRs_3.9||
body.translated_text: <s>Bīja</s> (seed), <s>Bindu</s> (drop), <s>Patākā</s> (banner), <s>Prakarī</s> (episode), and <s>Kārya</s> (denouement). ||3.9||

body.text: atha bījaḥ-

children.text: yat tu svalpam upakṣiptaṃ bahudhā vistṛtiṃ gatam | 9
children.translated_text: That which is introduced in a small form and which expands in many ways,

children.text:
kāryasya kāraṇaṃ prājñais tad bījam iti kathyate |
uptaṃ bījaṃ taror yadvad aṅkurādi-prabhedataḥ ||SRs_3.10|| 10
phalāya kalpate tadvan nāyakādi-vibhedataḥ |
phalāyaitad bhaved yasmād bījam ity abhidhīyate ||SRs_3.11|| 11
children.translated_text: the cause of the [dramatic] action — that is called <s>Bīja</s> (seed) by the wise. Just as a seed sown for a tree, through the distinctions of sprout, etc., serves to produce fruit, so too this [dramatic seed], through the distinctions of the hero and others, serves to produce the fruit; hence it is called <s>Bīja</s> (seed). ||3.10-11||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Bīja</s> (seed) —

body.text: yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe prathama-dvitīyāṅkayoḥ kalpite mukha-sandhau svalpo rāmotsāho bījam ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the <s>Mukha-sandhi</s> (opening juncture) constructed in the first and second acts, the small [hint of] <s>Rāma</s>'s enthusiasm is called the <s>Bīja</s> (seed).

body.text:
atha binduḥ-
phale pradhāne bījasya prasaṅgoktaiḥ phalāntaraiḥ |
vicchinne yad aviccheda-kāraṇaṃ bindur ucyate ||SRs_3.12|| 12
jala-bindur yathā siñcaṃs taru-mūlaṃ phalāya hi |
tathaivāyam upakṣipto bindur ity abhidhīyate ||SRs_3.13|| 13
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Bindu</s> (drop) — When the main fruit of the seed is interrupted by incidental fruits introduced in passing, that which serves as the cause of [maintaining] continuity is called <s>Bindu</s> (drop). ||3.12|| Just as a drop of water, watering the root of a tree, serves to produce fruit, so too this [element], when introduced, is called <s>Bindu</s> (drop). ||3.13||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] tṛtīya-caturthāṅkayoḥ kalpite pratimukha-sandhau nikṣipto rāvaṇa-virodha-mūlaṃ sītā-parigraho bindur ucyate |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the <s>Pratimukha-sandhi</s> (progression juncture) constructed in the third and fourth acts, the winning of <s>Sītā</s> as wife, which is the root of the conflict with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, is called the <s>Bindu</s> (drop).

body.text:
atha patākā--
yat pradhānopakaraṇa-prasaṅgāt svārtham ṛcchati |
sā syāt patākā sugrīva-makarandādi-vṛttavat ||SRs_3.14|| 14
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Patākā</s> (banner) — That which, by connection with the main [plot's] accessory, achieves its own purpose — that is the <s>Patākā</s>, like the episode of <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Makaranda</s>, etc. ||3.14||

body.text:
atha prakarī-
yat kevalaṃ parārthasya sādhakaṃ ca pradeśa-bhāk |
prakarī sā samuddiṣṭā nava-vṛndādi-vṛttavat ||SRs_3.15|| 15
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Prakarī</s> (episode) — That which solely accomplishes another's purpose and is limited in scope — that is designated as <s>Prakarī</s>, like the episode of <s>Nava-vṛnda</s>, etc. ||3.15||

body.text: patākā-prakarī-vyapadeśo bhāva-prakāśikā-kāreṇoktaḥ, yathā-
body.translated_text: The designation of <s>Patākā</s> and <s>Prakarī</s> is stated by the author of <s>Bhāva-prakāśikā</s>, as follows —

children.translated_text: 'Just as a banner (<s>patākā</s>) serves as an ornament and a sign for someone,
so the sub-plot of one's own subsidiary hero (<s>upanāyaka</s>) and the like is similarly called.' ||3.16||

body.text:
śobhāyai vedikādīnāṃ yathā puṣpākṣatādayaḥ |
tatha rtu-varṇanādis tu prasaṅge prakarī bhavet ||SRs_3.17|| iti (bhāva-prakāśe) |
body.translated_text: 'Just as flowers and rice-grains serve as ornaments for altars and the like, so the description of seasons and such, introduced in passing, would be a <s>Prakarī</s> (episode).' ||3.17|| — thus in the <s>Bhāva-prakāśa</s>.

body.text:
atha patākā-sthānakāni-
aṅgasya ca pradhānasya bhāvyavasthasya sūcakam |
yad āgantuka-bhāvena patākā-sthānakaṃ hi tat ||SRs_3.18|| 16
etad dvidhā tulya-saṃvidhānaṃ tulya-viśeṣaṇam |

children.text: tatrādyaṃ tri-prakāraṃ syād dvitīyaṃ tv ekam eva hi |17
children.translated_text: Of these, the first is of three kinds, and the second is only one.
Thus, the <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s> should be known by the wise as fourfold. ||3.19||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Patākā-sthānakas</s> (banner-positions) — That which, in an incidental manner, indicates the state of a future affair related to the principal subsidiary [plot] — that is a <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s> (banner-position). ||3.18|| This is twofold: of equal arrangement (<s>tulya-saṃvidhāna</s>) and of equal qualifier (<s>tulya-viśeṣaṇa</s>).

body.text:
tathā ca bharataḥ (19.31)-
sahasaivārtha-sampattir guṇavaty upacārataḥ |
patākā-sthānakam idaṃ prathamaṃ parikīrtitam ||SRs_3.20|| iti |
body.translated_text: And thus <s>Bharata</s> (19.31) — 'The sudden attainment of meaning through a meritorious courtesy — this is declared as the first <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s>.' ||3.20||

body.text:
yathā ratnāvalyām-
vidūṣakaḥ- bhoḥ ! esā kkhu abarā debī bāsabadattā | (bhoḥ ! eṣā khalu aparā devī vāsavadattā |)
body.translated_text: For example, in <s>Ratnāvalī</s> — The <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester): 'Ho! This indeed is the other Queen, <s>Vāsavadattā</s>!' (Prakrit/Sanskrit)

body.text: rājā (saśaṅkaṃ ratnāvalī-hastaṃ visṛjati |)
body.translated_text: The King (anxiously releases <s>Ratnāvalī</s>'s hand).

body.text: ity atra iyaṃ vāsavattety anenopacāra-prayogeṇa bhāvino vāsavadattā-kopasya sūcanāt sahasārtha-sampatti-rūpam idam ekaṃ patākā-sthānakam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the courteous usage 'This is <s>Vāsavadattā</s>', by indicating the future anger of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, this is one <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s> in the form of a sudden attainment of meaning.

body.text:
tathā ca (19.32)-
vacaḥ sātiśayaṃ śliṣṭaṃ kāvya-bandha-samāśrayam |
patākā-sthānakam idaṃ dvitīyaṃ parikīrtitam ||SRs_3.21|| iti |
body.translated_text: And thus (19.32) — 'A verbal arrangement that is superlative, well-connected, dependent on poetic composition — this is declared as the second <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s>.' ||3.21||

body.text: yathā uttara-rāma-carite (1.38)-

children.text: iyaṃ gehe lakṣmīr iyam amṛta-vartir nayanayor
children.translated_text: 'She is the <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) of the house; she is the nectar-wick for the eyes;

children.text: asāv asyāḥ sparśo vapuṣi bahalaś candana-rasaḥ |
children.translated_text: her touch upon the body is like a dense stream of sandalwood;
this arm upon the neck is like a cool, smooth string of pearls —

children.text: kim asyā na preyo yadi param asahyas tu virahaḥ ||SRs_3.22||
children.translated_text: what is there about her that is not dear? Yet separation from her is utterly unbearable.' ||3.22||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> (1.38) —

body.text: (praviśya) pratīhārī-deva upasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Entering) The door-keeper: 'Your Majesty, [a guest] is present.'

body.text: rāmaḥ-aye kaḥ ? ity atra bhaviṣyataḥ sītā-virahasya sūcanād idaṃ śliṣṭaṃ nāma dvitīyaṃ patākā-sthānakam |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>: 'Indeed, who?' — Here, by indicating the future separation from <s>Sītā</s>, this is the second <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s>, called 'well-connected' (<s>śliṣṭa</s>).

children.translated_text: And thus (19.33) —
'Where the introduction of a matter is concealed, respectful,
and accompanied by a well-connected reply — this third [<s>Patākā-sthānaka</s>] is accepted.' ||3.23||

body.text: yathā veṇī-saṃhāre (2.23), rājā-
body.translated_text: For example, in <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> (2.23), the King [says] —

children.translated_text: 'The wind-tossed hem of your flowing garment,
which steals my gaze, the friend of my eyes —
O elephant-thighed one, the pair of your thighs is more than sufficient
for one to sit upon the expanse of your hips for a long time.' ||3.24||

body.text: (praviśya sambhrāntaḥ) kañcukī-deva bhagnam | deva bhagnam !
body.translated_text: (Entering in haste) The chamberlain: 'Your Majesty, it is broken! Your Majesty, it is broken!'

body.text: rājā-kena ?
body.translated_text: The King: 'By whom?'

body.text: kañcukī-deva bhīmena |
body.translated_text: The chamberlain: 'Your Majesty, by <s>Bhīma</s>!'

body.text: rājā-āḥ kiṃ pralapasi ?
body.translated_text: The King: 'Ah! What are you babbling?'

body.text: ity atra śliṣṭa-pratyuttareṇa kañcuki-vākyena bhāvino duryodhanoru-bhaṅgasya sūcanena śliṣṭottaraṃ nāma tṛtīyam idaṃ patākā-sthānakam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the well-connected reply of the chamberlain's speech, by indicating the future breaking of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s thigh, this is the third <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s>, called 'well-connected reply' (<s>śliṣṭottara</s>).

body.text:
tathā ca (19.34) -
dvy-artho vacana-vinyāsaḥ suśliṣṭaḥ kāvya-yojitaḥ |
upanyāsa-suyuktaś ca tac caturtham udāhṛtam ||SRs_3.25|| iti |
body.translated_text: And thus (19.34) — 'A double-meaning verbal arrangement, well-connected, framed in poetic composition, and aptly introduced — that is cited as the fourth [<s>Patākā-sthānaka</s>].' ||3.25||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Displaying an unbounded bud, pale and lacking relish, commencing a yawn, momentarily
extending the weariness of herself through unceasing exhalations —

children.text: adyodyāna-latām imāṃ samadanāṃ nārīm ivānyāṃ dhruvaṃ
children.translated_text: seeing this garden-creeper today, in heat, just like another woman, surely

children.text: paśyan kopa-vipāṭala-dyuti mukhaṃ devyāḥ kariṣyāmy aham ||SRs_3.26||
children.translated_text: I shall make the Queen's face red with the glow of anger.' ||3.26||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: (ratnāvalyāṃ 2.4)
body.translated_text: (in <s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.4)

body.text: ity atra viśeṣaṇa-śleṣeṇa bhāvino ratnāvalī-sandarśanasya sūcanāt tulya-viśeṣaṇaṃ nāma caturthaṃ patākā-sthānakam idam |
body.translated_text: Here, by indicating the future sight of <s>Ratnāvalī</s> through the ambiguity of the qualifiers (<s>viśeṣaṇa-śleṣa</s>), this is the fourth <s>Patākā-sthānaka</s>, called 'equal qualifier' (<s>tulya-viśeṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: atha kāryam-

children.translated_text: The fruit of the entire plot, characterized by <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, or <s>Artha</s>,

children.text: phalaṃ kāryam iti śuddhaṃ miśraṃ vā kalpayet sudhīḥ ||SRs_3.27|| 19a
children.translated_text: is called <s>Kārya</s> (denouement); the wise may conceive it as pure or mixed. ||3.27||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Kārya</s> (denouement) —

body.text: śuddhaṃ, yathā mālatī-mādhave (10.23), kāmandakī-

children.text: yat prāg eva manorathair vṛtam abhūt kalyāṇam āyuṣmatos
children.translated_text: 'That which was previously desired in fond wishes for the welfare of the long-lived one,

children.text: tat puṇyair mad-upakramaiś ca phalitaṃ kleśo' pi mac-chiṣyayoḥ |
children.translated_text: that has borne fruit through merit and through my efforts; the suffering too of my two pupils [has ended].

children.text: niṣṇātaś ca samāgamo' bhivihitas tvat-preyasaḥ kāntayā
children.translated_text: A well-established union has been arranged between your beloved and his sweetheart;

children.text: samprītau nṛpa-nandanau yad aparaṃ preyas tad apy ucyatām ||SRs_3.28||
children.translated_text: the two princes are delighted — whatever further happiness [there may be], let that too be told.' ||3.28||

body.translated_text: Pure, for example in <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> (10.23), <s>Kāmandakī</s> [says] —

body.text: ity atra kāvyopasaṃhāra-ślokena tṛtīya-puruṣārthasyaiva phala-kathanāt śuddhaṃ kāryam idam |
body.translated_text: Here, since the concluding verse of the poem states only the third <s>puruṣārtha</s> (<s>Kāma</s>) as the fruit, this is a pure <s>Kārya</s>.

body.text: miśraṃ, yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe (10.104)-
body.translated_text: Mixed, for example in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> (10.104) —

children.text: rugṇaṃ cājagavaṃ na cātikupito bhargaḥ sura-grāmaṇīḥ
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Ājagava</s> bow is broken, and <s>Bharga</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) is not exceedingly angry; the chief of the gods (<s>Indra</s>)

children.text: setuś ca grathitaḥ prasanna-madhuro dṛṣṭaś ca vārāṃ nidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: — the bridge is constructed, the gracious and sweet ocean has been seen;

children.text: paulastyaś carama-sthitaś ca bhagavān prītaḥ śrutīnāṃ kaviḥ
children.translated_text: the descendant of <s>Paulastya</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) is in his final state; the blessed poet of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>Vālmīki</s>) is pleased;

children.text: prāptaṃ yānam idaṃ ca yācitavate dattaṃ kuberāya ca ||SRs_3.29||
children.translated_text: this vehicle [<s>Puṣpaka</s>] is obtained; and it has also been given to <s>Kubera</s> who had requested it.' ||3.29||

body.text: ity anenopasaṃhāra-ślokena miśrasya trivarga-phalasya kathanān miśram idam |
body.translated_text: Here, since the concluding verse states the mixed fruit of the three goals (<s>trivarga</s>), this is a mixed [<s>Kārya</s>].

body.text: pradhānam aṅgam iti ca tad vastu dvividhaṃ punaḥ | 19
body.translated_text: The plot (<s>vastu</s>) is again of two kinds: principal (<s>pradhāna</s>) and subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>).

body.text: pradhānaṃ netṛ-caritaṃ pradhāna-phala-bandhi ca ||SRs_3.30||
body.translated_text: The principal is the hero's activity, and it is bound to the principal fruit. ||3.30||

body.text: kāvye vyāpi pradhānaṃ tad yathā rāmādi-ceṣṭitam | 20
body.translated_text: The principal pervades the entire poem, such as the exploits of <s>Rāma</s> and others.

body.text: nāyakārtha-kṛd-aṅgaṃ syān nāyaketara-ceṣṭitam ||SRs_3.31||
body.translated_text: The subsidiary serves the hero's purpose and consists of the activities of characters other than the hero. ||3.31||

body.text: nityaṃ patākā prakarī cāṅgaṃ bījādayaḥ kvacit | 21
body.translated_text: The <s>Patākā</s> and <s>Prakarī</s> are always subsidiary; the <s>Bīja</s> and others are sometimes [subsidiary].

body.text: bījatvād bījam ādau syāt phalatvāt kāryam antataḥ ||SRs_3.32||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bīja</s>, being the seed, comes at the beginning; the <s>Kārya</s>, being the fruit, comes at the end. ||3.32||

body.text: tayoḥ sandhān a-hetutvān madhye binduṃ prakalpayet | 22
body.translated_text: Between those two, one should place the <s>Bindu</s> as [maintaining] causality for the junctures.

body.text: yathāyogaṃ patākāyāḥ prakaryāś ca niyojanam ||SRs_3.33||
body.translated_text: The <s>Patākā</s> and <s>Prakarī</s> should be employed as appropriate. ||3.33||

body.text: atha kāryasya pañcāvasthāḥ-

children.translated_text: The <s>Kārya</s> has five stages, dependent on the activities of the hero and others.

The five stages are: beginning (<s>ārambha</s>), effort (<s>yatna</s>), hope of attainment (<s>prāpty-āśā</s>), certainty of attainment (<s>niyatāpti</s>), and fruition (<s>phalāgama</s>). Of these, mere exertion toward the principal fruit — that is considered <s>ārambha</s> (beginning). ||SRs_3.34||

body.translated_text: Now, the five stages of the <s>Kārya</s> (dramatic action) —

body.text: yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe mukha-sandhau rāmasya lokottarotkarṣa-prāptaye vyavasāya-mātram ārambhaḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the opening juncture (<s>mukha-sandhi</s>), the mere resolve of <s>Rāma</s> to attain transcendent glory constitutes the <s>ārambha</s>.

body.text:
atha yatnaḥ-
yatnas tu tat-phala-prāptyām autsukyena tu vartanam ||SRs_3.35|| 25a
body.translated_text: Now <s>yatna</s> (effort) — <s>Yatna</s> is the conduct [of the hero] with eagerness for the attainment of that fruit. ||SRs_3.35||

body.text: yathā tatraiva pratimukha-sandhau tāṭaka-pātana-bhūta-pati-dhanur-dalanādiṣu rāmasya yatnaḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], in the <s>pratimukha-sandhi</s> (progression), <s>Rāma</s>'s effort is [seen] in the slaying of <s>Tāṭakā</s>, the breaking of the bow of the Lord of Beings (<s>Śiva</s>), and the like.

body.text:
atha prāpty-āśā-
prāpty-āśā tu mahārthasya siddhi-sadbhāva-bhāvanā[*17] ||SRs_3.36|| 25b
[*17] siddha-sad-bhāvanā matā.
body.translated_text: Now <s>prāpty-āśā</s> (hope of attainment) — <s>Prāpty-āśā</s> is the conviction that success in the great objective is real. ||SRs_3.36||

body.text: yathā tatraiva garbha-sandhau mālavan māyā-prayoga-vana-pravāsa-sītāpaharaṇādibhir antaritāyāḥ rāmasya paramotkarṣa-prāpter dhanur-bhaṅgādi-sugrīva-sandhi-setu-bandhanādibhiḥ siddhi-sad-bhāva-bhāvanā-kathanāt prāpty-āśā |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], in the <s>garbha-sandhi</s> (development), <s>prāpty-āśā</s> consists in the narration of the conviction that success is real for <s>Rāma</s>'s supreme glory — which had been obstructed by <s>Mālyavān</s>'s employment of illusion, exile to the forest, the abduction of <s>Sītā</s>, and so forth — through the breaking of the bow, the alliance with <s>Sugrīva</s>, the building of the causeway, and the like.

body.text:
atha niyatāptiḥ-
niyatāptir avighnena kārya-saṃsiddhi-niścayaḥ ||SRs_3.37|| 26a
body.translated_text: Now <s>niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment) — <s>Niyatāpti</s> is the conviction that the task will be accomplished without obstacle. ||SRs_3.37||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] vimarśa-sandhau nikhila-rakṣaḥ-kula-nibarhaṇād avighnena rāmasya phala-saṃsiddhi-niścayo niyatāptiḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the <s>vimarśa-sandhi</s> (pause for deliberation), <s>Rāma</s>'s certainty that the fruit will be accomplished without obstacle, through the complete annihilation of the entire <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan, constitutes <s>niyatāpti</s>.

body.text:
atha phalāgamaḥ-
samagreṣṭa-phalāvāptir bhaved eva phalāgamaḥ ||SRs_3.38|| 26b
body.translated_text: Now <s>phalāgama</s> (fruition) — The attainment of the complete desired fruit — that is indeed <s>phalāgama</s>. ||SRs_3.38||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] nirvahaṇa-sandhau rāmasya tātājñā-nirbahaṇa-vaira-praśamana-rājyopabhogair lokottara-trivarga-phalasyāvāptiḥ phalāgamaḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the <s>nirvahaṇa-sandhi</s> (denouement), <s>Rāma</s>'s attainment of the transcendent fruit of the three goals of life (<s>trivarga</s>) through the execution of his father's command, the pacification of enmity, and the enjoyment of sovereignty — that constitutes <s>phalāgama</s>.

body.text:
atha sandhiḥ-
ekaikasyās tv avasthāyāḥ prakṛtyā caikayaikayā |
yogaḥ sandhir iti jñeyo nāṭya-vidyā-viśāradaiḥ ||SRs_3.39|| 27
patākāyās tv avasthānaṃ kvacid asti na vā kvacit |
patākā-virahe bījaṃ binduṃ vā kalpayet sudhīḥ ||SRs_3.40|| 28
mukhya-prayojana-vaśāt kathāṅgānāṃ samanvaye |
avāntarārtha-sambandhaḥ sandhiḥ sandhāna-rūpataḥ ||SRs_3.41|| 29
body.translated_text: Now <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) — The conjunction of each stage with each [successive] nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) — that should be known as <s>sandhi</s> by those learned in dramatic science. ||SRs_3.39|| The presence of a <s>patākā</s> (sub-plot) in a given [juncture] may or may not occur; in the absence of a <s>patākā</s>, the wise should employ the <s>bīja</s> (seed) or the <s>bindu</s> (drop). ||SRs_3.40|| Through the coordination of the subsidiary stories in accordance with the principal purpose, the connection of subsidiary meanings constitutes <s>sandhi</s>, by virtue of its binding nature. ||SRs_3.41||

body.text:
(tatra pañca-sandhayo bhavanti-)
mukha-pratimukhe garbha-vimarśāv upasaṃhṛtiḥ |
pañcaite sandhayaḥ
body.translated_text: (Of these, the five junctures are:) <s>Mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (progression), <s>garbha</s> (development), <s>vimarśa</s> (pause/deliberation), and <s>upasaṃhṛti</s> (denouement) — these are the five junctures.

body.text:
(mukha-sandhis tad-aṅgāni cettham-)
  teṣu yatra bīja-samudbhavaḥ ||SRs_3.42|| 30
nānā-vidhānām arthānāṃ rasānām api kāraṇam |
tan mukhaṃ tatra cāṅgāni bījārambhānurodhataḥ ||SRs_3.43|| 31
upakṣepaḥ parikaraḥ parinyāso vilobhanam |

children.translated_text: <s>yukti</s> (reasoning), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>samādhāna</s> (re-establishment), <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement), <s>paribhāvanā</s> (wonder),
<s>udbheda</s> (disclosure), <s>bheda</s> (incitement), and <s>karaṇa</s> (action) — thus twelve should be arranged. ||SRs_3.44||

body.translated_text: (The opening juncture and its elements are as follows:) That in which the seed (<s>bīja</s>) arises, ||SRs_3.42|| which is the cause of various meanings and <s>rasas</s> — that is <s>mukha</s> (the opening). Its elements, in accordance with the seed and beginning, are: ||SRs_3.43|| <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction), <s>parikara</s> (elaboration), <s>parinyāsa</s> (confirmation), <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement),

body.text:
tatropakṣepaḥ-
upakṣepas tu bījasya sūcanā kathyate budhaiḥ ||SRs_3.45|| 33b
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>upakṣepa</s> (introduction) — The suggestion of the seed (<s>bīja</s>) — that is called <s>upakṣepa</s> by the wise. ||SRs_3.45||

body.text: yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe pratijñāta-paulastya-nāmani prathae' ṅke-
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the first act titled 'The Vow Concerning <s>Paulastya</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>)' —

body.text: (tataḥ praviśati viśvāmitra-śiṣyaḥ) śunaḥśepaḥ-prātaḥsavana eva yajamānaṃ draṣṭum icchāmiity upakramyaà rākṣasa-rakṣauṣadhaṃ rāmam ānetuṃ siddhāśramād ayodhyāṃ gatavatā tāta-viśvāmitreṇa yajñopanimantritasya parama-suhṛdaḥ śrotriya-kṣatriyasya sīradhvajasya sva-pratinidhiḥ preṣito' smi ity antena (1.23 padyāt pūrvam] rāvaṇādi-duṣṭa-rākṣasa-śikṣā-lakṣaṇa-rāmotsāhopabṛṃhaka-viśvāmitrārambha-rūpasya bījasya sūcanād upakṣepaḥ |
body.translated_text: (Then enters a disciple of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>) <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> — [saying] 'I wish to see the sacrificer at the morning pressing itself,' and beginning thus, ending with — 'I have been sent as a personal representative by my master <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, who has gone to <s>Ayodhyā</s> from <s>Siddhāśrama</s> to bring <s>Rāma</s>, the remedy against <s>Rākṣasas</s>, to invite [King <s>Daśaratha</s>] to the sacrifice on behalf of his dearest friend, the learned <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>Sīradhvaja</s>.' — Because this suggests the seed, namely <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s undertaking whose nature is to nourish the enthusiasm of <s>Rāma</s> for chastising wicked <s>Rākṣasas</s> such as <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, this constitutes <s>upakṣepa</s>.

body.text:
atha parikaraḥ-
parikriyā tu bījasya bahulīkaraṇaṃ matam ||SRs_3.46|| 34a
body.translated_text: Now <s>parikara</s> (elaboration) — The multiplication of the seed — that is considered <s>parikara</s>. ||SRs_3.46||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] (praviśya tāpasa-cchamanā) rākṣasaḥ-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> (entering in ascetic guise) a <s>Rākṣasa</s> [says] —

body.text:
sampreṣito mālyavatām aham adya
jñātuṃ pravṛttiṃ kuśikātmajasya |
purīṃ nimīnāṃ mithilāṃ ca gantuṃ
tāṃ cāpy ayodhyāṃ raghu-rājadhānīm ||SRs_3.47|| (1.23)
body.translated_text: 'Dispatched today by <s>Mālyavān</s>, I [have come] to learn the activities of the son of <s>Kuśika</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>), and to go to <s>Mithilā</s>, the city of the <s>Nimis</s>, and also to that <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the capital of the <s>Raghus</s>.' ||SRs_3.47|| (1.23)

body.text: kula-putraketi saprasāmad āśliṣṭo' smi ity upakramyaà sa hi naktaṃ-carāṇāṃ nisargāmitro viśvāmitro vrata-caryayā, vīra-vrata-caryayā samartho daśaratho' pi tathāvidha eva eva (1.25 padyād anantaraṃ] ity antena viśvāmitrārambhasya mālyavadādi-vitarka-gocaratvena bahulīkaraṇāt parikaraḥ |
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'O noble son' — 'I was embraced with graciousness,' and ending with — 'For <s>Viśvāmitra</s> is the natural enemy of the night-wanderers (<s>Rākṣasas</s>) through his austerities, and <s>Daśaratha</s> too, competent through his vow of heroism, is likewise' — because <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s undertaking becomes an object of deliberation for <s>Mālyavān</s> and others, thereby multiplying [the seed], this constitutes <s>parikara</s>.

body.text:
atha parinyāsaḥ-
bīja-niṣpatti-kathanaṃ parinyāsa itīryate ||SRs_3.48|| 34b
body.translated_text: Now <s>parinyāsa</s> (confirmation) — The narration of the seed's maturation — that is called <s>parinyāsa</s>. ||SRs_3.48||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] rākṣasaḥ (puro' valokya)-kathaṃ tāpasaḥ | (pratyabhijñāya) tatrāpi viśvāmitra-dharma-putraḥ śunaḥśepaḥ ity upakramyaà sampraty eva rākṣasa-bhayāt satre dīkṣiṣyamāṇaḥ sa bhagavān goptāraṃ rāmabhadraṃ varītum ayodhyāṃ gataḥ | rākṣasaḥ (sa-trāsaṃ svagatam)-hanta katham etad api niṣpannam | (prakāśam) bhagavan mā kopīḥ ity ādinā (svagatam) kṛtaṃ yat kartavyam | samprati cāra-sañcārasyāyam avasaraḥ (1.27 padyād anantaram] ity antena viśvāmitrānubhāva-kathanāt sarākṣatrāsa-kathanāc ca bīja-niṣpatteḥ parinyāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Rākṣasa</s> (looking ahead) — 'What, an ascetic!' (Recognizing him) — 'And there too is <s>Śunaḥśepa</s>, the adopted son of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>!' — beginning thus and ending with — 'Just now, out of fear of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, that venerable one has gone to <s>Ayodhyā</s> to choose <s>Rāmabhadra</s> as a protector, being about to be initiated for the sacrifice.' The <s>Rākṣasa</s> (with alarm, aside) — 'Alas! How has this too come about!' (Aloud) — 'Venerable sir, do not be angry,' etc. (Aside) — 'What was to be done has been done. Now is the occasion for the movement of spies.' — Because this narrates <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s spiritual power and the terror of the <s>Rākṣasa</s>, confirming the seed's maturation, this constitutes <s>parinyāsa</s>.

body.text:
atha vilobhanam-
nāyakādi-guṇānāṃ yad varṇanaṃ tad vilobhanam ||SRs_3.49|| 35a
body.translated_text: Now <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement) — The description of the qualities of the hero and others — that is <s>vilobhana</s>. ||SRs_3.49||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] rāvaṇaḥ-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> [says] —

body.text: yasyāropaṇa-karmaṇāpi bahavo vīra-vrataṃ tyājitāḥ ||SRs_3.50||
body.translated_text: '[That bow] by whose mere stringing many were made to abandon their vow of heroism...' ||SRs_3.50||

body.text: ity upakramya, rāvaṇaḥ (sapratyāśam)-
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (with hopeful anticipation) —

body.text:
nirmālyaṃ nayana-śriyaḥ kuvalayaṃ vaktrasya dāsaḥ śaśī
kāntiḥ prāvaraṇaṃ tanor madhumuco yasyāś ca vācaḥ kila |
viṃśatyā racitāñjaliḥ kara-puṭais tvāṃ yācate rāvaṇas
tāṃ draṣṭuṃ janakātmajāṃ hṛdaya he netrāṇi mitrīkuru ||SRs_3.51|| (1.40)
body.translated_text: 'The blue lotus is the residual offering of the beauty of her eyes; the moon is the servant of her face; radiance is the outer garment of her body; and bees are [rivaled by] her words, as it were. <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, with palms joined in twenty hands, entreats you — O heart, make your eyes allies, that I may behold her, that daughter of <s>Janaka</s>!' ||SRs_3.51|| (1.40)

body.text: ity antena tad-guṇa-varṇanād vilobhanam |
body.translated_text: Because this describes her qualities, it constitutes <s>vilobhana</s>.

body.text:
atha yuktiḥ-
samyak prayojanānāṃ hi nirṇayo yuktir iṣyate ||SRs_3.52|| 35b
body.translated_text: Now <s>yukti</s> (reasoning) — The proper determination of purposes — that is considered <s>yukti</s>. ||SRs_3.52||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] paraśurāma-rāvaṇīya-nāmani dvitīyāṅke-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the second act titled '<s>Paraśurāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>' —

body.text: (tataḥ praviśati) bhṛṅgiriṭiḥ (parikrāmann ātmānaṃ nirvarṇya)-aye nirūpatāpi kvacin mahate' bhuyadayāya ity upakramya, bhṛṅgiriṭiḥ-ām, nārada yathā samarthayase | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: (Then enters) <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s> (walking about, examining himself) — 'Ah, even one without form can be of great service somewhere!' — beginning thus, <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s> [says] — 'Yes, <s>Nārada</s>, you reason well. For indeed —'

body.text:
ekaṃ kailāsam adriṃ kara-gatam akaroc cicchade krauñcam anyo
laṅkām ekaḥ kuberād ahṛta vasataye koṅkaṇānabdhito' nyaḥ |
ekaḥ śakrasya jetā samiti bhagavataḥ kārtikeyasya cānyas
tat kāmaṃ karma-sāmyāt kim aparam anayor madhyagā vīra-lakṣmīḥ ||SRs_3.53|| (2.15)
body.translated_text: 'One made <s>Kailāsa</s>, the mountain, fit in his hand; another cut through <s>Krauñca</s>; one seized <s>Laṅkā</s> from <s>Kubera</s> as a dwelling; another [seized] <s>Koṅkaṇa</s> from the ocean; one is the conqueror of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), and the other is of the blessed <s>Kārttikeya</s> — so let the glory of heroism freely reside between these two, since their deeds are equal!' ||SRs_3.53|| (2.15)

body.text: ity antena rāghava-pratināyakayor bhārgava-rāvaṇayoḥ karma-sāmya-nirṇaya-kathanād yuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: Because this narrates the determination of the equality of deeds between <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the antagonists of <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), this constitutes <s>yukti</s>.

body.text:
atha prāptiḥ-
prājñaiḥ sukhasya samprāptiḥ prāptir ity abhidhīyate ||SRs_3.54|| 36a
body.translated_text: Now <s>prāpti</s> (attainment) — The attainment of happiness — that is called <s>prāpti</s> by the wise. ||SRs_3.54||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] nāradaḥ (saharṣaṃ hastam udyamya)-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Nārada</s> (joyfully raising his hand) —

body.text:
citraṃ netra-rasāyanaṃ tridaśatāsiddher mahā-maṅgalaṃ
mokṣa-dvāram apāvṛtaṃ mama manaḥ-prahlādanā-bheṣajam |
sākaṃ nāka-purandhirbhir nava-pati-prāpty-utsukābhiḥ surāḥ
sarve paśyata rāma-rāvaṇa-raṇaṃ vakty eṣa vo nāradaḥ ||SRs_3.55|| (2.16)
body.translated_text: 'Wondrous! A tonic for the eyes! A great auspiciousness heralding the attainment of divine status! The gate of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) flung open! A medicine for the delight of my mind! Together with the heavenly women, eager for a new lord — O gods, all of you behold! This <s>Nārada</s> announces to you the battle between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>!' ||SRs_3.55|| (2.16)

body.text: ity atra nāradasya yuddhāvalokana-harṣa-prāpteḥ prāptiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Nārada</s>'s attainment of joy from witnessing the battle constitutes <s>prāpti</s>.

body.text:
atha samādhānaṃ-
bījasya punar ādhānaṃ samādhānam ihocyate ||SRs_3.56|| 36b
body.translated_text: Now <s>samādhāna</s> (re-establishment) — The re-planting of the seed — that is called <s>samādhāna</s>. ||SRs_3.56||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] bhṛṅgiriṭiḥ-yuddha-ruce mā nirbharaṃ saṃrambhasva | ity upakramya | ayodhyāṃ gatvā paraṃ rāma-rāvaṇīyaṃ yojayiṣyāmi (2.16 padyād anantaram] ity antena rāghavotsāha-bījasya nāradena punar ādhānāt samādhānam |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgiriṭi</s> [says] — 'O battle-lover, do not be excessively vehement!' — beginning thus — 'I shall go to <s>Ayodhyā</s> and arrange the great [encounter between] <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.' — Because <s>Nārada</s> re-plants the seed of <s>Rāghava</s>'s enterprise, this constitutes <s>samādhāna</s>.

body.text:
atha vidhānaṃ-
sukha-duḥkha-karaṃ yat tu tad vidhānaṃ budhā viduḥ ||SRs_3.57|| 37a
body.translated_text: Now <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement) — That which causes happiness and sorrow — that the wise know as <s>vidhāna</s>. ||SRs_3.57||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] prathamāṅke, sītā (sa-sādhvasautsukyam)-ammo rakkhaso tti suṇia saccaṃ sajjhasa-kodahalāṇaṃ majjhe baṭṭāmi | (aṃho rākṣasa iti śrutvā satyaṃ sādhvasa-kautūhalayor antare varte |) ity upakramya sītā-tādasadānaṃdamissāṇaṃ antare ubabisissaṃ (tāta-śatānanda-miśrāṇām antare upavekṣyāmi) | (1.42 padyāt pūrvam] ity antena sītāyāḥ adṛṣṭa-pūrva-rākṣasa-darśanena sukha-duḥkha-vyatikarākhyānād vidhānam |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the first act, <s>Sītā</s> (with timid eagerness) — [Prakrit:] 'Hearing the word "<s>Rākṣasa</s>," truly I find myself between alarm and curiosity!' — beginning thus, <s>Sītā</s> [says] — [Prakrit:] 'I shall sit between father <s>Śatānanda</s> and the masters.' — Because this narrates the intermingling of <s>Sītā</s>'s happiness and sorrow from seeing a <s>Rākṣasa</s> never seen before, this constitutes <s>vidhāna</s>.

body.text:
atha paribhāvanā-
ślāghyaiś citta-camatkāro guṇādyaiḥ paribhāvanā ||SRs_3.58|| 37b
body.translated_text: Now <s>paribhāvanā</s> (wonder) — The amazement of the mind produced by praiseworthy qualities and the like — that is <s>paribhāvanā</s>. ||SRs_3.58||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe], rāvaṇaḥ (sautsukyaṃ vilokya svagatam)-aho tribhuvanātiśāyi makaradhvaja-sañjīvanaṃ rāmaṇīyakam asyāḥ | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (gazing with eagerness, aside) — 'Ah! A beauty surpassing the three worlds, the elixir of life for the banner-bearing god of love! For indeed —'

body.text:
indur lipta ivāñjanena jaḍitā dṛṣṭir mṛgīṇām iva
pramlānāruṇimeva vidrumalatā śyāmeva hema-prabhā |
pāruṣyaṃ kalayā ca kokila-vadhū-kaṇṭheṣv iva prastutaṃ
sītāyāḥ purataś ca hanta śikhināṃ barhāḥ sagarhā iva ||SRs_3.59|| (1.42)
body.translated_text: 'The moon seems smeared with collyrium; her gaze is set like that of does; her redness seems the faded hue of coral creepers; her complexion is like dark-gold radiance; harsh notes seem to be rehearsed in the throats of female cuckoos [by comparison with her voice]; and alas, before <s>Sītā</s>, the plumage of peacocks seems blameworthy!' ||SRs_3.59|| (1.42)

body.text: ity upakramya, śatānandaḥ (apavarya)-aho laṅkādhipater apūrva-garva-garimā | yan mamāpi śatānandasya na niścinute cetaḥ | kiṃ bhaviṣyati (1.46 padyād anantaram] ity antena rāvaṇasya sītā-rāmaṇīyaka-darśanena śatānandasya rāvaṇotsāha-darśanena ca tayoś citta-camatkāra-kathanāt paribhāvanā |
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, <s>Śatānanda</s> (aside) — 'Ah, the unprecedented weight of the arrogance of the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>! It unsettles even my mind, <s>Śatānanda</s>'s. What will happen?' — Because this narrates the mental amazement of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> upon seeing <s>Sītā</s>'s beauty and of <s>Śatānanda</s> upon seeing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s audacity, this constitutes <s>paribhāvanā</s>.

body.text:
athodbhedaḥ-
udghātanaṃ yad bījasya sa udbhedaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||SRs_3.60|| 38a
body.translated_text: Now <s>udbheda</s> (disclosure) — The uncovering of the seed — that is celebrated as <s>udbheda</s>. ||SRs_3.60||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] dvitīyāṅke, rāvaṇaḥ-traiyāmbakaḥ paraśur eṣa nisarga-caṇḍa (2.36) ity ādi paṭhati | jāmadagnyaḥ-apakurvatāpi bhavatā param upakṛtam | yad eṣa smārito' smīty upakramya (2.44 padyāt pūrvam]-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the second act, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> recites — 'This axe of <s>Tryambaka</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) is fierce by nature' (2.36) and so forth. <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) [replies] — 'Even in acting against me, you have done me a supreme favor, for I have been reminded [of my mission]' — beginning thus —

body.text:
lokottaraṃ caritam arpayati pratiṣṭhāṃ
puṃsāṃ kulaṃ na hi nimittam udāratāyāḥ |
vātāpitāpana-muneḥ kalaśāt prasūtir
līlāyitaṃ punar amuṣya samudra-pānam ||SRs_3.61|| (2.51)
body.translated_text: 'Extraordinary conduct bestows fame; a man's family is not the cause of his nobility. <s>Agastya</s>, the scourge of <s>Vātāpi</s>, was born from a pot — yet his drinking of the ocean was a mere sport!' ||SRs_3.61|| (2.51)

body.text: ity antena gūḍha-śaṅkara-dhanur adhikṣepodghāṭanād vā lokottara-carita-sāmānya-varṇanena tirohita-rāmacandrotsāhodghāṭanād vā udbhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: Because this discloses [the seed] through the uncovering of the censure of the hidden bow of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), or through the uncovering of the concealed enthusiasm of <s>Rāmacandra</s> by the general description of extraordinary conduct, this constitutes <s>udbheda</s>.

body.text:
atha bhedaḥ-
bījasyottejanaṃ bhedo yad vā saṅghāta-bhedanam ||SRs_3.62|| 38b
body.translated_text: Now <s>bheda</s> (incitement) — The stimulation of the seed, or the breaking of an alliance — that is <s>bheda</s>. ||SRs_3.62||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] rāvaṇaḥ (vilokya)-atha yācita-paraśunā paraśurāmeṇa kim abhihitam āsīt |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (looking) — 'Then what did <s>Paraśurāma</s>, having been asked for his axe, say?'

body.text: māyāmayaḥ-trailokya-māṇikya rāmodantam ākarṇayatu svāmī |
body.translated_text: <s>Māyāmaya</s> [replies] — 'O jewel of the three worlds, may the lord hear the tale of <s>Rāma</s>!'

body.text:
paulastyaḥ praṇayena yācata iti śrtuvā mano modate
deyo naiṣa hara-prasāda-paraśus tenādhikaṃ tāmyati |
tad vācyaḥ sa daśānano mama girā dattā dvijebhyo mahī
tubhyaṃ brūhi rasātala-tridivayor nirjitya kiṃ dīyatām ||SRs_3.63|| (2.20)
body.translated_text: '<s>Paulastya</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) asks with affection' — hearing this, the mind rejoices; 'This axe, <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) gracious gift, should not be given' — at this, it suffers greatly. 'Then let that Ten-faced one be told by my word: the earth has been given to the <s>Brahmins</s>; tell him — having conquered both the netherworld and heaven, what shall be given to you?' ||SRs_3.63|| (2.20)

body.text: rāvaṇaḥ-kadā nu khalu paraśurāmo rasātala-tridivayor jetā dātā ca saṃvṛttaḥ | rāvaṇaḥ punaḥ pratigrahītā ca | tatas tvayā kim asau pratyuktaḥ | ity upakramya
body.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>: 'When indeed did <s>Paraśurāma</s> become the conqueror and giver of both the nether world and heaven? And <s>Rāvaṇa</s> the receiver? Then what reply did you give him?' And so beginning,

body.text: māyāmayaḥ-deva prakṛti-roṣaṇo reṇukāputraḥ | tat tam evāgatam aham utprekṣe |
body.translated_text: <s>Māyāmaya</s>: 'My lord, the son of <s>Reṇukā</s> is quick to anger by nature. So I imagine it is he himself who has come.'

body.text: rāvaṇaḥ-priyaṃ naḥ (2.24 padyāt pūrvam] ity antena pratināyaka-rūpa-bhārgava-rāvaṇayor uttejanād bhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>: 'That is pleasing to us' — (before verse 2.24) — thus ending. Through the incitement of <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, who are in the role of antagonists, this is <s>Bheda</s> (split/divergence).

body.text:
atha karaṇam-
prastutārtha-samārambhaṃ karaṇaṃ paricakṣate ||SRs_3.64|| 39a
