body.translated_text: Now, <s>Karaṇa</s> (commencement) — The undertaking of the main business is called <s>Karaṇa</s>. ||3.64|| 39a

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] (2.25 padyād anantaram] ubhāv api cāpāropaṇaṃ nāṭayataḥ ity upakramya ā aṅka-parisamāpteḥ jāmadagnya-rāvaṇayoḥ prastuta-yuddhārambha-kathanāt karaṇam |
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] (after verse 2.25) — beginning with 'both enact the stringing of the bow' up to the end of the act — since the commencement of the proposed battle between <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> is narrated, this is <s>Karaṇa</s>.

body.text: atha pratimukha-sandhiḥ-

children.translated_text: Where the seed (<s>bīja</s>) becomes manifest through alternating visibility and invisibility, 39
that is the <s>Pratimukha</s>, following the <s>bindu</s> (drop) and endeavor. ||3.65||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Pratimukha-sandhi</s> (the juncture of development) —

body.text: iha trayodaśāṅgāni prayojyāni manīṣibhiḥ | 40
body.translated_text: In this [juncture], thirteen constituent elements are to be employed by the wise. 40

body.text: vilāsa-parisarpau ca vidhutaṃ śama-narmaṇī ||SRs_3.66||
body.translated_text: <s>Vilāsa</s> (display of desire) and <s>Parisarpa</s> (recollection), <s>Vidhuta</s> (discontent), <s>Śama</s> (tranquility), and <s>Narma</s> (jest), ||3.66||

body.text: narma-dyutiḥ pragamanaṃ nirodhaḥ paryupāsanam | 41
body.translated_text: <s>Narma-dyuti</s> (jesting brilliance), <s>Pragamana</s> (confrontation), <s>Nirodha</s> (impediment), <s>Paryupāsana</s> (conciliation), 41

body.text: puṣpaṃ vajram upanyāso varṇa-saṅgrahanaṃ tathā ||SRs_3.67||
body.translated_text: <s>Puṣpa</s> (flower/auspicious indication), <s>Vajra</s> (harsh speech), <s>Upanyāsa</s> (argument), and <s>Varṇa-saṅgrahaṇa</s> (gathering of descriptions). ||3.67||

body.text:
tatra vilāsaḥ-
vilāsaḥ saṅgamārthas tu vyāpāraḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||SRs_3.68|| 42
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>Vilāsa</s> (display of desire) — <s>Vilāsa</s> is said to be the activity directed toward union. ||3.68|| 42

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] vilakṣa-laṅkeśvara-nāmani tṛtīyāṅke (3.21 padyāt pūrvam] rāmaḥ-aye iyam asau sā sītā, yasyāḥ svayaṃ vasumatī mātā yāga-bhūr janma-mandiraṃ indu-śekhara-kārmukāropaṇaṃ ca paṇaḥ | (sa-spṛhaṃ nirvarṇya) ity ārabhya, pratīhāraḥ-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the third act titled 'The Embarrassed Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>' (before verse 3.21) — <s>Rāma</s>: 'Ah, this is she, <s>Sītā</s>, whose mother is the Earth herself, whose birthplace is the sacrificial ground, and whose hand is the wager for stringing the bow of the crescent-crowned one (<s>Śiva</s>).' (Gazing with longing) — beginning thus, the Doorkeeper [says]:

body.text:
etenoccair vihasitam asau kākalī-garbha-kaṇṭho
laulyāc cakṣuḥ prahitam amunā sāṅga-bhaṅgaḥ sthito' yam |
hārasyāgraṃ kalayati kareṇaiṣa harṣāc ca kiṃcit
straiṇaḥ puṃsāṃ nava-parigamaḥ kāmam unmāda-hetuḥ ||SRs_3.69|| (3.26)
body.translated_text: 'He laughed aloud with a voice pregnant with melodious tones; his gaze was sent forth with restlessness, and he stands with limbs breaking [into gesture]; he fingers the front of his necklace, and out of joy somewhat — the first encounter with a woman is indeed a cause of madness in men.' ||3.69|| (3.26)

body.text: ity antena rāmādīnāṃ sītālambanābhilāṣa-kathanād vilāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus ending — since the narration of the desire of <s>Rāma</s> and others [directed] toward <s>Sītā</s> as the foundational object is recounted, this is <s>Vilāsa</s>.

body.text:
atha parisarpaḥ-
pūrva-dṛṣṭasya bījasya tv aṅka-cchedādinā tathā |
naṣṭasyānusmṛtiḥ śaśvat parisarpa iti smṛtaḥ ||SRs_3.70|| 43
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Parisarpa</s> (recollection) — The constant recollection of a previously seen seed that has been lost through the division of acts and the like is known as <s>Parisarpa</s>. ||3.70|| 43

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] pratīhāraḥ (svagatam)-katham ete kṣatriya-jana-samucite' pi cāpāropaṇa-karmaṇi nikhilāḥ kṣatriyāḥ vitatha-sāmarthyāḥ vartante | tad eṣa param anākalita-sāro vikartana-kula-kumāra āste | yad vā, kim anenāpi-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] — the Doorkeeper (aside): 'How is it that all these <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, though the stringing of the bow is a task fit for warrior folk, prove to have futile strength? And this prince of the <s>Vikartana</s> (Solar) dynasty sits here, his mettle unrecognized. Or then, what use even of him —

body.text:
yasya vajra-maṇer bhede bhidyante loha-sūcayaḥ |
karotu tatra kiṃ nāma nārī-nakha-viḍambanam ||SRs_3.71|| (3.66)
body.translated_text: 'When iron needles break in the splitting of an adamantine gem, what can the imitation of a woman's fingernail accomplish there?' ||3.71|| (3.66)

body.text: (vicintya) bhavatu | tathāpi saṅkīrtayāmy enam | anākalita-sāro hi vīra-prakāṇḍa-sambhūtiḥ ity upakramya |
body.translated_text: (Reflecting) 'But still, let me commend him; for one born of the foremost lineage of heroes has his mettle unrecognized' — beginning thus,

body.text: hemaprabhā-saṃpaṇṇaṃ ca pia-sahīe pāṇi-ggahaṇam (3.79 padyād anantaram] (sampannaṃ ca priya-sakhyā pāṇi-grahaṇam) ity antena pūrvaṃ tāṭakādi-vadha-dṛṣṭasya paścān nikhila-kṣatriya-durāropa-dhūrjaṭi-cāpāropaṇa-prabhāva-varṇanād naṣṭasya rāmabhadrotsāhasya tad-dhanur-bhaṅga-kriyā-rūpeṇa smaraṇāt parisarpaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Hemaprabhā</s>: 'And the hand-clasping of the dear friend has been completed' — (after verse 3.79) — thus ending. Since the heroic energy of <s>Rāmabhadra</s> — previously seen in the slaying of <s>Tāṭakā</s> and others, then lost — is recalled in the form of the stringing of <s>Śiva</s>'s bow, which was impossible for all other <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and the description of its power, this is <s>Parisarpa</s>.

body.text:
atha vidhutam-
nāyakāder īpsitānām arthānām anavāptitaḥ |

children.text: aratir yad bhaved tad dhi vidvadbhir vidhutaṃ matam | 44
children.translated_text: of desired objects by the hero and others is what the learned consider <s>Vidhuta</s>; 44

children.text:
athavānunayotkarṣaṃ vidhutaṃ syān nirākṛtiḥ ||SRs_3.72|| 45a
yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] bhārgava-bhaṅga-nāmani caturthe' ṅke, śatānandaḥ-
children.translated_text: alternatively, the rejection of an excess of conciliation is <s>Vidhuta</s>. ||3.72|| 45a As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the fourth act titled 'The Humbling of <s>Bhārgava</s>' — <s>Śatānanda</s>:

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vidhuta</s> (discontent) — The displeasure arising from the non-attainment

body.text: yasyāste jananī svayaṃ kṣitir ayaṃ yogīśvaras te pitā ||SRs_3.73|| (4.42)
body.translated_text: 'She whose mother is the Earth herself, and whose father is the lord of <s>Yogins</s>...' ||3.73|| (4.42)

body.text: ity ārabhya, rāmaḥ (vicintya svagatam)-rudaty api kamanīyā jānakī-ity antena (4.47 padyād anantaraṃ] sītāyāḥ bandhu-viraha-janitārati-kathanād vidhutam | atha vā matāntareṇa tatraiva, rāmaḥ (samupasṛtya)-bhagavan bhārgava sadayaṃ prasīda ity ārabhya, jāmadagnyaḥ-nābhivādana-prasādyo reṇukā-sūnuḥ (4.58 padyāt pūrvam] ity atra rāmānunayasya bhārgaveṇāsvīkārād vidhūtam |
body.translated_text: Beginning thus — <s>Rāma</s> (reflecting, aside): 'Even while weeping, <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) is lovely' — thus ending (after verse 4.47). Since the discontent born of <s>Sītā</s>'s separation from her kinsmen is narrated, this is <s>Vidhuta</s>. Or alternatively, by another interpretation, in the same [play] — <s>Rāma</s> (approaching): 'O reverend <s>Bhārgava</s>, be graciously pleased' — beginning thus, <s>Jāmadagnya</s>: 'The son of <s>Reṇukā</s> is not to be appeased by salutation' (before verse 4.58) — here, since <s>Rāma</s>'s conciliation is not accepted by <s>Bhārgava</s>, this is <s>Vidhuta</s>.

body.text:
atha śamaḥ-
arateḥ śamanaṃ taj-jñāḥ śamam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ||SRs_3.74|| 45b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Śama</s> (tranquility) — The calming of discontent is what the wise experts call <s>Śama</s>. ||3.74|| 45b

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] (4.57 padyāt pūrvaṃ) hemaprabhā-jujjai paphulla-kodūhala-ttaṇaṃ | parasurāma-daṃsaṇeṇa uṇa sasajjha-sattaṇaṃ bhagga-dhana-ddaṇḍa-caṇḍa-caritassa purado rāmacaṃdassa | (yujyate praphulla-kautūhalatvaṃ paraśurāma-daṃśanena punaḥ sa-sādhvasatvaṃ bhagna-dhanur-daṇḍa-caṇḍa-caritasya purato rāmacandrasya) ity atra rāmacandra-parākrama-kathanāt sītāyāḥ arati-śamanāt śamaḥ |
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] (before verse 4.57) — <s>Hemaprabhā</s> [speaks in Prakrit]: 'The joyful curiosity is justified. Through seeing <s>Paraśurāma</s>, there is again apprehension — before <s>Rāmacandra</s>, whose fierce conduct has broken the bow-staff.' Here, since the narration of <s>Rāmacandra</s>'s valor brings about the calming of <s>Sītā</s>'s discontent, this is <s>Śama</s>.

body.text:
atha narma-
parihāsa-pradhānaṃ yad vacanaṃ narma tad viduḥ ||SRs_3.75|| 46
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Narma</s> (jest) — That speech which is predominantly jocular is known by the learned as <s>Narma</s>. ||3.75|| 46

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] tṛtīye' ṅke, rāmaḥ (sakaṇṭha-rodham)-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the third act — <s>Rāma</s> (with choked voice) —

body.text:
vācā kārmukam asya kauśika-pater āropaṇāyārpitaṃ
mad-dor-daṇḍa-haṭhāñcanena tad idaṃ bhagnaṃ kṛta-nyak-kṛti |
no jāne janakas tad atra bhagavān vrīḍā-vaśād uttaraṃ
nikṣeptre nata-kandharo bhagavate rudrāya kiṃ dāsyati ||SRs_3.76|| (3.71)
body.translated_text: 'By the word of the lord of the <s>Kauśikas</s>, this bow was entrusted for stringing; by the force of my arm-staff, this has been broken, bringing humiliation. I do not know, revered sir, what answer <s>Janaka</s>, out of shame, will give to the reverend <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the one who deposited [the bow].' ||3.76|| (3.71)

body.text: ity atra janakādhipāpalāpena hāsa-pradhānaṃ narma |
body.translated_text: Here, since the speech is predominantly humorous through [<s>Rāma</s>'s] mock lamentation about King <s>Janaka</s>, this is <s>Narma</s>.

body.text:
atha narma-dyutiḥ-
kopasyāpahnavārthaṃ yad dhāsyaṃ narma-dyutir matā ||SRs_3.77|| 46
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Narma-dyuti</s> (jesting brilliance) — That humor which serves to conceal anger is considered <s>Narma-dyuti</s>. ||3.77|| 46

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] caturthāṅke viśvāmitro jāmadagnyaṃ prati-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the fourth act — <s>Viśvāmitra</s> [says] to <s>Jāmadagnya</s>:

body.text:
rāmaḥ śiṣyo bhṛgubhava bhavān bhāgineyī-suto me
vāme bāhāv uta tad-itare kāryataḥ ko viśeṣaḥ |
divyāstrāṇāṃ tava paśupater asya lābhas tu mattas
tat tvāṃ yāce virama kalahād āryakarmārabhasva ||SRs_3.78|| (4.69)
body.translated_text: '<s>Rāma</s> is my pupil, O son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>; you are the son of my sister — on the left arm or the right, what practical difference? The divine weapons are your gift from the Lord of Beasts (<s>Śiva</s>), and his from me — so I beseech you, desist from quarrel and undertake noble deeds!' ||3.78|| (4.69)

body.text: jāmadagnyaḥ (vihasya) : mātur mātula na kiṃcid antaraṃ bhavato bhavānīvallabhasya ca | (ity upakramya)
body.translated_text: <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (laughing): 'Maternal uncle! There is no difference between you and the consort of <s>Bhavānī</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)!' — beginning thus,

body.text: rāmaḥ (vihasya) : jāmadagnya ! ekaḥ punar ayaṃ śastra-grahaṇādhikāro yad guruṣv api tiraskāraḥ (tatraiva kiñcit parastāt) ity antena bhārgava-rāghavayoḥ pūjya-viṣaya-krodhāpahnavārthaṃ hāsya-kathanān narma-dyutiḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> (laughing): '<s>Jāmadagnya</s>! This is indeed a singular prerogative of bearing weapons — that one shows disrespect even to preceptors!' — (somewhat further in the same [act]) — thus ending. Since humor is narrated to conceal the anger of <s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Rāghava</s> toward a venerable person, this is <s>Narma-dyuti</s>.

body.text:
atha pragamaṇam-
tat tu pragamanaṃ yat syād uttarottara-bhāṣaṇam ||SRs_3.79|| 47a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Pragamana</s> (confrontation) — That which consists of successive speech and counter-speech is <s>Pragamana</s>. ||3.79|| 47a

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe], rāmaḥ-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] — <s>Rāma</s>:

body.text:
kiṃ punar imāḥ sarvaṅkaṣā roṣa-vācaḥ |
sarvatyāgī pariṇata-vayāḥ saptamaḥ padma-yoneḥ ||SRs_3.80|| (4.71)
body.translated_text: 'Why these all-consuming words of rage? He who renounced all, mature in years, the seventh from <s>Padmayoni</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>)...' ||3.80|| (4.71)

body.text: iti ślokānte jāmadagnyaḥ: tat kim ?
body.translated_text: At the end of this verse — <s>Jāmadagnya</s>: 'What then?'

body.text:
rāmaḥ (sa-khedam) :
yasyācāryakam indu-maulir akarot sa-brahmacārī ciraṃ
jāto yatra guhaś cakāra ca bhuvaṃ yad gīta-vīra-vratām |
tat kodaṇḍa-rahasyam adya bhagavan draṣṭaiṣa rāmaḥ sa te
helojjṛmbhita-jṛmbhakeṇa dhanuṣā kṣatraṃ ca nālaṃ vayam ||SRs_3.81|| (4.72)
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> (with sorrow): 'He whose teacher was the crescent-crowned one (<s>Śiva</s>), who practiced celibacy for long, from whom <s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>) was born and who made the earth famous for heroic vows — that mystery of the bow, O reverend one, this <s>Rāma</s> will now demonstrate to you: with a bow yawned open in sport, neither the warrior class nor we are a match.' ||3.81|| (4.72)

body.text: jāmadagnyaḥ : sādhu re kṣatriya-ḍimbha, sādhu | ity antena bhārgava-rāghavayor ukti-pratyukti-kathanāt pragamanam |
body.translated_text: <s>Jāmadagnya</s>: 'Well done, O young <s>Kṣatriya</s>, well done!' — thus ending. Since the narration of speech and counter-speech between <s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Rāghava</s> is recounted, this is <s>Pragamana</s>.

body.text:
atha nirodhaḥ-
yatra vyasanam āyāti nirodhaḥ sa nigadyate ||SRs_3.82|| 47b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Nirodha</s> (impediment) — Where calamity befalls — that is called <s>Nirodha</s>. ||3.82|| 47b

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] jāmadagnyaḥ-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] — <s>Jāmadagnya</s>:

body.text:
pakva-karpūra-niṣpeṣam ayaṃ nirapiṣat trayam |
mama vrīḍāṃ ca caṇḍīśa-cāpaṃ ca svaṃ ca jīvitam ||SRs_3.83|| (4.65)
body.translated_text: 'This one has ground to a paste of ripe camphor three things: my shame, the bow of <s>Caṇḍīśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and his own life.' ||3.83|| (4.65)

body.text: janakaḥ-kathaṃ sannyasta-śastrasyāpi punar astra-grahaṇa-kṣaṇo vartate ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s>: 'How is it that even one who has renounced weapons faces the moment of seizing arms again?' — beginning thus,

body.text: prahiṇu tad iha bāṇān vārdhakaṃ māṃ dunoti ||SRs_3.84|| (4.67)
body.translated_text: '...send forth arrows then — old age oppresses me!' ||3.84|| (4.67)

body.text: daśarathaḥ-bhoḥ sambandhin kṛtaṃ kārmuka-parigraha-vyasanena-ity antena janakasya bhārgava-nimittasya jarā-nimittasya vā vyasanasya kathanād nirodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Daśaratha</s>: 'O kinsman, enough of this addiction to grasping the bow!' — thus ending. Since the calamity of <s>Janaka</s>, whether caused by <s>Bhārgava</s> or by old age, is narrated, this is <s>Nirodha</s>.

body.text:
atha paryupāsanam-
ruṣṭasyānunayo yaḥ syāt paryupāsanam īritam ||SRs_3.85|| 48a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Paryupāsana</s> (conciliation) — The appeasement of one who is angered is called <s>Paryupāsana</s>. ||3.85|| 48a

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] viśvāmitraḥ (jāmadagnyaṃ prati)-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] — <s>Viśvāmitra</s> (to <s>Jāmadagnya</s>):

body.text: rāmaḥ śiṣyo bhṛgu-suta bhavān bhāgineyī-suto me ||SRs_3.86|| (4.69)
body.translated_text: '<s>Rāma</s> is my pupil, O son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>; you are the son of my sister...' ||3.86|| (4.69)

body.text: ity atra śloke roṣāndhasya bhārgavasyānunayo viśvāmitreṇa kṛta iti paryupāsanam |
body.translated_text: In this verse, since <s>Viśvāmitra</s> conciliates <s>Bhārgava</s>, who is blinded by anger, this is <s>Paryupāsana</s>.

body.text:
atha puṣpam-
sa-viśeṣābhidhānaṃ yat puṣpaṃ tad iti saṃjñitam ||SRs_3.87|| 48b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Puṣpa</s> (auspicious indication) — That which is a statement with a distinctive [qualification] is called <s>Puṣpa</s>. ||3.87|| 48b

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] tṛtīyāṅke (praviśya) kohalaḥ-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the third act — (entering) <s>Kohala</s>:

body.text: karpūra iva dagdho' pi śaktimān yo jane jane ||SRs_3.88|| [bā.rā. 3.11] ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: 'Like camphor, even when burnt he remains powerful in all people...' ||3.88|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 3.11] — beginning thus,

body.text:
prakaṭita-rāmāmbhojaḥ kauśikavā sapadi lakṣmaṇānandī |
sura-cāpa-namana-hetor ayam avatīrṇaḥ śarat-samayaḥ ||SRs_3.89|| [bā.rā. 3.16]
body.translated_text: 'Having manifested the lotus of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kauśika</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>) immediately brought joy to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>; for the sake of bending the divine bow, this autumn season has descended.' ||3.89|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 3.16]

body.text: ity ante rāmacandra-lakṣaṇārtha-viśeṣābhidhānāt puṣpam |
body.translated_text: Thus ending — since a distinctive description of the marks of <s>Rāmacandra</s> is stated, this is <s>Puṣpa</s>.

body.text:
atha vajram-
vajraṃ tad iti vijñeyaṃ sākṣān niṣṭhura-bhāṣaṇam ||SRs_3.90|| 49a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vajra</s> (harsh speech) — <s>Vajra</s> should be understood as directly harsh speech. ||3.90|| 49a

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] caturthāṅke, jāmadagnyaḥ-nidarśita-lāghava rāghava tad ākarṇaya yat te karomi-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the fourth act — <s>Jāmadagnya</s>: 'O <s>Rāghava</s>, you who have displayed [your] contemptible lightness, now hear what I shall do to you —

body.text:
truṭita-niviḍa-nāḍī-cakravāla-praṇālī-
prasṛta-rudhira-dhārā-carcitoccaṇḍa-ruṇḍam |
maḍamaḍita-mṛḍānī-kānta-cāpasya bhaṅktuḥ
paraśur amara-vandyaḥ khaṇḍayaty adya muṇḍam ||SRs_3.91|| [bā.rā. 4.61]
body.translated_text: 'With severed networks of dense veins in torrents, the ferocious trunk smeared with streaming floods of blood — this axe, worshipped by the immortals, shall today sever the head of the one who broke the bow of the beloved of <s>Mṛḍānī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>)!' ||3.91|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 4.61]

body.text: ity upakramya, yaḥ preta-nāthasyātithyam anubhavitu-kāma ity antena vajra-niṣṭhura-bhāṣaṇād vajram |
body.translated_text: Beginning thus — 'He who wishes to experience the hospitality of the Lord of the Dead' — thus ending. Since there is thunderbolt-harsh speech, this is <s>Vajra</s>.

body.text:
athopanyāsaḥ-
yuktibhiḥ sahito yo' rthaḥ upanyāsaḥ sa iṣyate ||SRs_3.92|| 49b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Upanyāsa</s> (argument) — A proposition accompanied by reasoning is accepted as <s>Upanyāsa</s>. ||3.92|| 49b

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] mātaliḥ-ayaṃ hi pitṛ-bhakty-atiśayaḥ paraśurāmasya yad uta reṇukā-śiraś-chedaḥ [4.29 padyād anantaram] ity upakramya-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] — <s>Mātali</s>: 'For this is <s>Paraśurāma</s>'s excess of filial devotion — namely, the beheading of <s>Reṇukā</s>' (after verse 4.29) — beginning thus,

body.text: yad vā te guravo' vicintya-caritās tebhyo' yam astv añjaliḥ ||SRs_3.93|| [bā.rā. 4.33]
body.translated_text: 'Or rather, your preceptors are of unfathomable conduct — let this salutation be to them!' ||3.93|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 4.33]

body.text: ity antena upapattibhiḥ pitur nideśa-karaṇād api mātṛ-vadha-karaṇasyaiva pratipādanād vā gurūṇām avicintya-caritatvopanyāsena sarvopapannatva-pratipādanād vā upanyāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus ending — since by reasoning it is demonstrated that even the slaying of one's mother was done at the father's command; or alternatively, through the proposition that the conduct of preceptors is unfathomable, everything is shown to be justified — this is <s>Upanyāsa</s>.

body.text:
atha varṇa-saṃhāraḥ-
sarva-varṇopagamanaṃ varṇa-saṃhāra ucyate ||SRs_3.94|| 50a
yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] jāmadagnyaḥ (karṇaṃ dattvā ākāśe)-kiṃ brūtha ? kena na varṇitaṃ dāśaratheḥ śaṅkara-kārmukāropaṇam ? ko na vismitas tad-bhaṅgena ? (sākṣepam) (kena na varṇitam ity ādi paṭhati) śṛṇuta bhoḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Varṇa-saṅhāra</s> (gathering of descriptions) — The assembling of all descriptions is called <s>Varṇa-saṅhāra</s>. ||3.94|| 50a As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] — <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (cupping his ear toward the sky): 'What say you? Who has not described the stringing of <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s bow by <s>Dāśarathi</s> (<s>Rāma</s>)? Who is not amazed by its breaking?' (With scorn) (He recites 'who has not described...' etc.) 'Listen, sirs! —

body.text:
yaḥ kartā hara-cāpa-daṇḍa-dalane yaś cānumantā nanu
draṣṭā yaś ca parīkṣitā ca ya iha stotā ca vaktā ca yaḥ ||SRs_3.95|| [bā.rā. 4.56]
body.translated_text: 'He who is the doer of the breaking of <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) bow-staff, and he who is the sanctioner, and he who is the witness, and he who is the examiner, and he who is the praiser, and he who is the narrator...' ||3.95|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 4.56]

body.text:
ity upakramya-
rāmo rāma-mayaṃ svayaṃ guha-sahādhyāyī samanviṣyati ||SRs_3.96|| [bā.rā. 4.57]
body.translated_text: beginning thus — 'Rāma himself, a fellow student of Guha, searches for what is full of Rāma.' ||SRs_3.96|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 4.57]

body.text: ity antena hara-cāpa-dalanasya niṣiddhayā kartṛtayā anumantṛtayā stotṛtayā ca rāghava-viśvāmitra-pīrādi-parāmarśena brāhmaṇa-kṣatriyādi-varṇānāṃ saṅgrahaṇād varṇa-saṃhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: ending thus — through the discussion of Rāghava, Viśvāmitra, the elders, and others, regarding the breaking of Śiva's bow, in its aspects of prohibited agency, permitted agency, and laudatory agency, the gathering together of the Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, and other varṇas constitutes the Varṇa-saṃhāra (synthesis of elements).

body.text: atha garbha-sandhiḥ-

children.text: dṛṣṭādṛṣṭasya bījasya garbhas tv anveṣaṇaṃ muhuḥ | 50b
children.translated_text: The Garbha (development) is the repeated searching for the seed (bīja), whether seen or unseen. ||SRs_3.97||
Here too, one should arrange the limbs in accordance with the sub-plot (upapattākā).

body.translated_text: Now the Garbha-sandhi (the juncture of development) —

body.text: abhūtāharaṇaṃ mārgo rūpodāharaṇe kramaḥ | 51
body.translated_text: Abhūtāharaṇa (fabrication), Mārga (investigation), Rūpa (doubt), Udāharaṇa (illustration), Krama (sequence), ||

body.text:
saṅgrahaś cānumānaṃ ca toṭakādhibale tathā |
udvegaḥ sambhramāksepau dvādaśaiṣāṃ tu lakṣaṇam ||SRs_3.98|| 52
body.translated_text: Saṅgraha (conciliation), Anumāna (inference), Toṭaka (provocation), Adhibala (overpowering), Udvega (alarm), Sambhrama (agitation), and Ākṣepa (objection) — twelve in number; their characteristics [are now stated]. ||SRs_3.98||

body.text:
tatrābhūtāharaṇam-
abhūtāharaṇam tat syād vākyaṃ yat kapaṭāśrayam ||SRs_3.99|| 53a
body.translated_text: Among these, Abhūtāharaṇa (fabrication) — Abhūtāharaṇa is speech that relies on deceit. ||SRs_3.99||

body.text: yayā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] unmatta-daśānana-nāmani pañcamāṅke mālyavān (hasitvā)-vṛddha-buddhir hi prathamaṃ paśyati caramaṃ kāryam | yan mayā dhūrjaṭi-dhanur-adhikṣepataḥ prabhṛti mati-cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭam eva yad uta daśakandharo' nusandhāsyati sītā-haraṇam |
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], in the fifth act named 'The Maddened Daśānana,' Mālyavān (laughing): 'An aged intellect first foresees the final outcome. What I have seen with the eye of my mind — from the very moment of the insult to Dhūrjaṭi's (Śiva's) bow — is that the Ten-necked one (Rāvaṇa) will undertake the abduction of Sītā.'

body.text: māyā-mayaḥ : tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: Māyā-maya: 'Then what?'

body.text: mālyavān: tataś ca mayā mandodarī-pitur māyā-guror mayasya prathama-śiṣyo viśārada-nāmā yantra-kāraḥ sa-bahumānaṃ niyuktaḥ sītā-pratikṛti-karaṇāya | viracitā ca sā rāvaṇopacchandanārtham | abhihitaṃ ca-
body.translated_text: Mālyavān: 'Then I respectfully commissioned Viśārada by name, the first disciple of Maya — Mandodarī's father, the master of illusion — a master of mechanical devices, to create a replica of Sītā. And it was fashioned for the purpose of deceiving Rāvaṇa. And it was declared —'

body.text:
sūtra-dhāra-calad-dāru-gātreyaṃ yantra-jānakī |
vaktrastha-śārikālāpa laṅkendraṃ vañcayiṣyati ||SRs_3.100|| [bā.rā. 5.5]
body.translated_text: 'This mechanical Jānakī, a puppet moved by strings, with a parrot's voice placed in her mouth, shall deceive the lord of Laṅkā.' ||SRs_3.100|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 5.5]

body.text: ity upakramya, rāvaṇaḥ (punar nirūpya śārikādhiṣṭhita-vaktraṃ sītā-pratikṛti-yantraṃ): aho matimān māyāmayaḥ | chālito' si janaka-rāja-putryāḥ pratikṛti-samarpaṇena (5.20 padyād anantaram] ity antena mālyavat kapaṭa-vākya-saṃvidhānād abhūtāharaṇam |
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, Rāvaṇa (examining again the Sītā-replica mechanism with the parrot installed in its mouth): 'Ah, clever is Māyā-maya! You have been deceived by the offering of a replica of King Janaka's daughter.' (after verse 5.20) — ending thus, through Mālyavān's arrangement of deceitful speech, this constitutes Abhūtāharaṇa.

body.text:
atha mārgaḥ-
mārgas tattvārtha-kathanam ||SRs_3.101|| 53b
body.translated_text: Now Mārga (investigation) — Mārga is the statement of actual truth. ||SRs_3.101||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] nirdoṣa-daśaratha-nāmani ṣaṣṭhāṅke māyā-mayaḥ-ārya kim api dviṣatām apy āvarjakam udātta-jana-caritam | paśya-
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], in the sixth act named 'The Blameless Daśaratha,' Māyā-maya: 'Noble one, the conduct of exalted persons is somehow captivating even to enemies. Behold —'

body.text:
krūra-kramā kim api rākṣasa-jātir ekā
tatrāpi kārya-parateti mayi prakarṣaḥ |
rāmeṇa tu pravasatā pitur ājñayaiva
bāṣpāmbhasām aham apīha kṛto rasajñaḥ ||SRs_3.102|| [bā.rā. 6.9]
body.translated_text: 'The Rākṣasa race is somehow cruel in its ways, [yet] in that [race] too, there is excellence in me, devoted to duty. But by Rāma, dwelling in exile at his father's very command, I too have been made here a connoisseur of the waters of tears.' ||SRs_3.102|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 6.9]

body.text: ity upakramya, māyāmayaḥ-tataś ca vāmadeva-prabhṛtibhir mantribhir yathā-vṛttam abhidhāya sapādopagrahaṃ nivārito' pi tad idam abhidhāya prasthitaḥ-
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, Māyā-maya: 'Then, having been informed of the events by the ministers Vāmadeva and others, though restrained with respectful clasping of his feet, he [Rāma], having declared this, set forth —'

body.text:
mayā mūrdhni prahve pitur iti dhṛtaṃ śāsanam idaṃ
sa yakṣo rakṣo vā bhavatu bhagavān vā raghupatiḥ |
nivartiṣye so' haṃ bharata-kṛta-rakṣāṃ raghupurīṃ
samāḥ samyaṅ nītvā vana-bhuvi catasraś ca daśa ca ||SRs_3.103|| [bā.rā. 6.11]
body.translated_text: 'I have accepted this command of my father with bowed head — let him be a Yakṣa, a Rākṣasa, or the blessed Lord Raghupati himself. I shall return, that very I, to the city of the Raghus protected by Bharata, having duly spent fourteen years in the forest.' ||SRs_3.103|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 6.11]

body.text: ity antena rāma-pravāsa-viṣayasya māyamaya-duḥkhasya satyasyaiva vyaktatvād vā māyāmayādeḥ kapaṭatva-jñāne' pi rāmacandreṇa satyatayāṅgīkārād vā mārgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Ending thus — since the grief of Māyā-maya concerning Rāma's exile, being true, is clearly manifested; or because Rāmacandra, even knowing the deceitful nature of Māyā-maya and others, accepts it as true — this constitutes Mārga.

body.text:
atha rūpam-
rūpaṃ sandeha-kṛd vacaḥ ||SRs_3.104|| 53b
body.translated_text: Now Rūpa (doubt) — Rūpa is speech that creates doubt. ||SRs_3.104||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] ṣaṣṭhāṅke kaikeyī (sodvegam)-paṇamāmi bhaavadiṃ saraūṃ jā pubbaṃ dīsamāṇā ṇayaṇa-pīūsa-gaṇḍūsa-kabalaṃ kareṃti asi | sā saṃpadaṃ hālāhala-kabaḍa-paḍirūbā paḍihāadi | kiṃ puṇa me aojjhā-daṃsaṇe bi akāraṇa-pajjāulaṃ hiaaṃ | [praṇamāmi bhagavatīṃ sarayūṃ yā pūrvaṃ dṛśyamānā nayaṇa-pīyūṣa-gaṇḍūṣa-kavalaṃ kurvatī āsīt, sā samprataṃ hālāhala-kavala-pratirūpā pratibhāti | kiṃ punar me ayodhyā-darśane' pi akāraṇa-paryākulaṃ hṛdayam |]
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], in the sixth act, Kaikeyī (with agitation): 'I bow to the blessed Sarayū river, who, when formerly seen, used to make a mouthful of the nectar-draught of the eyes; now she appears like a mouthful of the Hālāhala poison. Moreover, my heart is agitated without cause even at the sight of Ayodhyā.'

body.text: ity upakramya, daśarathaḥ (akarṇitakena)-
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, Daśaratha (in an aside) —

body.text:
etac chrānta-vicitra-catvara-pathaṃ viśrānta-vaitālika-
ślāghā-ślokam aguñji-mañju-murajaṃ vidhvasta-gīta-dhvani |
vyāvṛttādhyayanaṃ nivṛtta-sukavi-krīḍā-samasyaṃ namad-
vidvadvad vāda-kathaṃ kathaṃ puram idaṃ mauna-vrate vartate ||SRs_3.105|| [bā.rā. 6.12]
body.translated_text: 'How is it that this city dwells in a vow of silence — its varied crossroad-courtyards weary, its bards' laudatory verses ceased, its sweet drums unbeaten, its sound of song destroyed, its recitation discontinued, its contests of skilled poets abandoned, its debate-conversations of bowing scholars [gone]?' ||SRs_3.105|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 6.12]

body.text: ity antena kaikeyī-daśarathayor ayodhyā-viṣaya-viṣāda-vitarka-vinyāsād rūpam |
body.translated_text: Ending thus — through the arrangement of despondent reflections of both Kaikeyī and Daśaratha concerning Ayodhyā — this constitutes Rūpa.

body.text:
athodāharaṇam-
sotkarṣa-vacanaṃ yat tu tad udāharaṇaṃ matam ||SRs_3.106|| 54a
body.translated_text: Now Udāharaṇa (illustration) — Speech that involves words of exaltation is considered Udāharaṇa. ||SRs_3.106||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] asama-parākrama-nāmani saptamāṅke vibhīṣaṇaḥ-sakhe sugrīva ! atiśaśāṅka-śekharam idam āceṣṭitaṃ rāmadevasya yad anena-
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], in the seventh act named 'Of Incomparable Valor,' Vibhīṣaṇa: 'Friend Sugrīva! This exploit of Lord Rāma surpasses even the Moon-crested one (Śiva) —'

body.text:
nirvāṇaṃ jala-pāna-pīḍana-balair yasmin yugāntānalair
yasyābhāti kukūla-murmura-mṛduḥ kroḍe śikhī bāḍavaḥ |
tasyāpy asya kṛśānu-saṅkrama-kṛta-jyotiḥ-śikhaṇḍaiḥ śarair
dattaś caṇḍa-davāgni-ambara-vidhir devasya vārāṃ-nidheḥ ||SRs_3.107|| (7.32)
body.translated_text: 'That ocean in which the submarine fire Bāḍava, soft as smoldering embers, subsides through the exertion of water-drinking forces, even of that [ocean's] cosmic conflagration-winds at the end of an age — upon that very ocean, by arrows whose luminous crests were created by the passage of fire, the Lord has imposed the law of a fierce forest-fire upon the sky.' ||SRs_3.107|| (7.32)

body.text: ity upakramya, samudraḥ-tarhi bāla-nārāyaṇaṃ rāmam evopasarpāmaḥ | na hi rākāmṛgāṅkam antareṇa candra-maṇer ānanda-jala-niṣyandaḥ (7.36 padyād pūrvam] ity antena samudra-kṣobhaka-rāmacandrotsāhotkarṣa-kathanād udāharaṇam |
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, the Ocean: 'Then let us approach Rāma himself, the child-Nārāyaṇa. For indeed, without the full-moon disk, there is no flow of bliss-water from the moon-jewel.' (before verse 7.36) — ending thus, through the narration of the exalted enthusiasm of Rāmacandra, who agitated the ocean, this constitutes Udāharaṇa.

body.text:
atha kramaḥ-
bhāva-jñānaṃ kramo yad vā cintyamānārtha-saṅgatiḥ ||SRs_3.108|| 54b
body.translated_text: Now Krama (sequence) — the knowledge of the [true] state of affairs, or the connection of meaning being deliberated — is called Krama. ||SRs_3.108||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] ṣaṣṭhāṅke [6.4 padyād anantaram] mālyavān (smṛti-nāṭikena)-na jāne kiṃ hi vṛttaṃ kaikeyī-daśarathayoḥ |
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], in the sixth act (after verse 6.4), Mālyavān (in a recollection-interlude): 'I do not know what has transpired between Kaikeyī and Daśaratha.'

body.text: (upasarpitakena) māyamayaḥ-jayatv āryaḥ |
body.translated_text: (approaching) Māyā-maya: 'Victory to the noble one!'

body.text: śūrpaṇakhā-jedu jedu kaṇiṭṭhamādām aho | [jayatu jayatu kaniṣṭha-mātāmahaḥ |]
body.translated_text: Śūrpaṇakhā: 'Victory, victory to the younger maternal grandfather!' [Prakrit rendered into Sanskrit]

body.text: mālyavān-atha kiṃ vṛttaṃ tatra ?
body.translated_text: Mālyavān: 'Now what has transpired there?'

body.text: māyamayaḥ-yathādiṣṭam āryeṇa | ity upakramya |
body.translated_text: Māyā-maya: 'As instructed by the noble one.' Beginning thus,

body.text: mālyavān (saharṣam)-tarhi vistarataḥ kathyatām |
body.translated_text: Mālyavān (with joy): 'Then tell it in detail!'

body.text: ity antena mālyavac cintā-samakālam eva śūrpaṇakhā-māyāmayayor upagamanād vā mālyavato vilambāsahābhiprāya-parijñānavatā māyāmayena niṣpannasya kāryasya saṅkṣepa-kathanād vā kramaḥ |
body.translated_text: Ending thus — because Śūrpaṇakhā and Māyā-maya arrive at the very time of Mālyavān's anxious reflection; or because Māyā-maya, understanding Mālyavān's impatient intention, narrates the accomplished task in summary — this constitutes Krama.

body.text:
atha saṅgrahaḥ-
saṅgrahaḥ sāmadānārtha-saṃyogaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||SRs_3.109|| 55a
body.translated_text: Now Saṅgraha (conciliation) — Saṅgraha is declared to be the conjunction of conciliation and gift. ||SRs_3.109||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] saptamāṅke, samudraḥ (sābhyarthanam)-
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], in the seventh act, the Ocean (with supplication) —

body.text:
indur lakṣmīr amṛta-madire kaustubhaḥ pārijātaḥ
svar-mātaṅgaḥ sura-yuvatayo deva dhanvantariś ca |
manthāmreḍaiḥ smarasi tad idaṃ pūrvam eva tvayātta
sampraty abdhiḥ śṛṇu jala-dhanas tvāṃ prapannaḥ praśādhi ||SRs_3.110|| [bā.rā. 7.36]
body.translated_text: 'The Moon, Lakṣmī, the nectar-wine, the Kaustubha gem, the Pārijāta tree, the celestial elephant, the divine maidens, and Dhanvantari — you recall, O Lord, that all these were formerly taken by you through the churning-repetitions. Now hear — the Ocean, the treasure-house of waters, takes refuge in you. Command [me]!' ||SRs_3.110|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 7.36]

body.text: rāmaḥ (sagauravam)-bhagavan ratnākara ! namas te | ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: Rāma (with reverence): 'O Blessed Ratnākara (Ocean)! Salutations to you!' Beginning thus,

body.text: samudraḥ-yathā saptamo vaikuṇṭhāvatāraḥ [7.44 padyāt pūrvam] ity antena samudra-rāmacandrayoḥ paraspara-priya-vacana-saṅgrahaṇāt saṅgrahaḥ |
body.translated_text: The Ocean: 'As [befitting] the seventh incarnation of Vaikuṇṭha...' (before verse 7.44) — ending thus, through the mutual exchange of pleasant words between the Ocean and Rāmacandra — this constitutes Saṅgraha.

body.text:
atha anumānam-
arthasyābhyūhanaṃ liṅgād anumānaṃ pracakṣate ||SRs_3.111|| 55b
body.translated_text: Now Anumāna (inference) — the conjecture of meaning from signs is called Anumāna. ||SRs_3.111||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe, 7.21 padyāt pūrvam] pratīhārī (samantād avalokya)-katham ayam anyādṛśa iva lakṣyate' mburāśiḥ |
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa, before verse 7.21], the door-keeper (looking all around): 'How is it that this ocean appears somehow different?'

body.text: vandī (yathopalakṣita-mārgeṇa sa-camatkāraṃ puro' valokya)-paśya | vilīyamāna-jala-mānuṣa-mithunam atyartha-kadarthyamāna-śaṅkhinī-yūtham ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: The bard (looking ahead with wonder, following the observed signs): 'Look! Pairs of aquatic humans are dissolving, schools of conch-creatures are being excessively tormented...' — beginning thus,

body.text:
pratīhārī-
āṃ jñātaṃ dhāmni vārāṃ raghupatir
viśikhāḥ prajvalantaḥ patanti ||SRs_3.112|| [bā.rā. 7.30]
body.translated_text: The door-keeper: 'Ah, I understand — in the domain of the waters, the blazing arrows of the Lord of the Raghus are falling!' ||SRs_3.112|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 7.30]

body.text: ity antena samudra-kṣobha-liṅgānumita-rāmotsāhārtha-kathanād anumānam |
body.translated_text: Ending thus — through the narration of Rāma's heroic energy inferred from the signs of the ocean's agitation — this constitutes Anumāna.

body.text:
atha toṭakam-
saṃrambhaṃ tu vacanaṃ saṅgirante hi toṭakam ||SRs_3.113|| 56a
body.translated_text: Now Toṭaka (provocation) — speech that [expresses] fury is called Toṭaka. ||SRs_3.113||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] hanumān-yathādiśati svāmī | (sarvato' valokya)-
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], Hanumān: 'As the master commands!' (looking all around) —

body.text:
dṛpyad-vikrama-kelayaḥ kapi-bhaṭāḥ śṛṇvantu sugrīvajām
ājñāṃ mauli-niveśitāñjali-puṭāḥ sator iha vyūhane |
dor-daṇḍa-dvaya-tāḍana-ślatha-dharā-bandhoddhṛtān bhūdharān
ānetuṃ sakalāḥ prayāta kakubhaḥ kiṃ nāma vo duṣkaram ||SRs_3.114|| [bā.rā. 7.46]
body.translated_text: 'Let the monkey warriors, sporting with proud valor, hear the command of Sugrīva, with cupped palms placed on their heads, regarding the army's formation here. Go, all of you, to [every] direction, to bring mountains uprooted from the earth's bond, loosened by the striking of your two arm-clubs. What indeed is difficult for you?' ||SRs_3.114|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 7.46]

body.text: ity upakramyāṅka-parisamāpteḥ kapi-rākṣasādi-saṃrambha-kathanāt toṭakam |
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, until the conclusion of the act — through the narration of the fury of the monkeys, Rākṣasas, and others — this constitutes Toṭaka.

body.text:
atha adhibalam-
budhair adhibalaṃ proktaṃ kapaṭenātivañcanam ||SRs_3.115|| 56b
body.translated_text: Now Adhibala (overpowering) — Adhibala is declared by the wise to be extreme deception through trickery. ||SRs_3.115||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] ṣaṣṭhāṅke [6.5 padyāt pūrvam] māyāmayaḥ-athaikadā dayita-sneha-mayyā kaikeyyā samam asurānīka-vijayāya pūrita-suhṛn-manorathe daśarathe tgirviṣṭapa-tilaka-bhūtaṃ puruhūtaṃ prabhāvavati samupasthitavati tad-rūpa-dhāriṇau kuvalayābhirāmaṃ rāmaṃ saparicchadaṃ chalayituṃ ayodhyāṃ śūrpaṇakhā ahaṃ ca prāptavantau | ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], in the sixth act (before verse 6.5), Māyā-maya: 'Then once, when Daśaratha — whose friends' wishes had been fulfilled — set out for the conquest of the Asura army, together with Kaikeyī, [imbued] with the affection of a beloved wife, and when the powerful Puruhūta (Indra), the ornament of heaven, arrived — then Śūrpaṇakhā and I arrived at Ayodhyā to deceive by trickery the lotus-charming Rāma along with his retinue, assuming his form.' Beginning thus,

body.text: mālyavān-kim asādhyaṃ vaidagdhyasya [6.5 padyād anantaraṃ] ity antena māyāmaya-śūrpaṇakhābhyāṃ kapaṭa-veṣa-dhāraṇena rāma-vāmadeva-vañcanād adhibalam |
body.translated_text: Mālyavān: 'What is impossible for cleverness?' (after verse 6.5) — ending thus, through the deception of Rāma and Vāmadeva by Māyā-maya and Śūrpaṇakhā wearing disguises — this constitutes Adhibala.

body.text:
atha udvegaḥ-
śatru-vairādi-sambhūtaṃ bhayam udvega ucyate ||SRs_3.116|| 57a
body.translated_text: Now Udvega (alarm) — Fear arising from enmity and such is called Udvega. ||SRs_3.116||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [6.56 padyāt pūrvam] (tataḥ praviśati gaganārdhāvataraṇa-nāṭitakena ratna-śikhaṇḍaḥ)-svasti mahārāja-daśarathāya |
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa] (before verse 6.56), (then enters Ratna-śikhaṇḍa, pantomiming descent from the sky): 'Welfare to the great King Daśaratha!'

body.text: daśarathaḥ-api kuśalaṃ vayasyasya jaṭāyoḥ |
body.translated_text: Daśaratha: 'Is all well with my friend Jaṭāyu?'

body.text: ratnaśikhaṇḍaḥ-priya-suhṛd-upayogena | na punaḥ śarīreṇa |
body.translated_text: Ratnaśikhaṇḍa: 'Through the service of a dear friend — but not bodily.'

body.text: daśarathaḥ-bhadra samupaviśya kathyatām | vyākulo' smi ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: Daśaratha: 'Good sir, be seated and speak. I am agitated.' Beginning thus,

body.text: kosalyā-hā debba tue kida-viḍaṃbaṃ samatthiaṃ baṇa-gadaṃ rāhava-kuṭuṃbaṃ | [hā deva tvayā kṛta-viḍambaṃ samarthitaṃ vana-gataṃ rāghava-kuṭumbam | ]
body.translated_text: Kosalyā: 'Alas, my lord, by you was this humiliation accomplished — the family of Rāghava sent to the forest!' [Prakrit rendered into Sanskrit]

body.text: sumitrā-ṇa kebalaṃ baṇa-gadaṃ | bhubaṇa-gadaṃ bi | [na kevalaṃ vana-gataṃ | bhuvana-gatam api |] (6.70 padyād anantaraṃ] ity antena mātṛ-gata-bhīter upanyāsād udvegaḥ |
body.translated_text: Sumitrā: 'Not merely sent to the forest — sent to [another] world also!' (after verse 6.70) — ending thus, through the presentation of fear concerning the mothers — this constitutes Udvega.

body.text:
atha sambhramaḥ-
śatru-vyāghrādi-sambhūtau śaṅkātrāsau ca sambhramaḥ ||SRs_3.117|| 57b
body.translated_text: Now Sambhrama (agitation) — Apprehension and terror arising from enemies, tigers, and the like constitute Sambhrama. ||SRs_3.117||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] vāmadevaḥ (sāsraṃ svagatam)-
body.translated_text: As in that same [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa], Vāmadeva (with tears, to himself) —

body.text:
he mad-vāṇi nijāṃ vimuñca vasati drāg dehi yātrāṃ bahiḥ
(rājānaṃ prati prakāśam)
deva stambhaya cetanāṃ śravaṇayor abhyeti śuṣkāśaniḥ |
(dampatī śaṅkāṃ nāṭayataḥ) vāmadevaḥ-
tvad-rūpād vipināya cīvaradharo dhanvī jaṭī śāsanaṃ
rāmaḥ prāpya gataḥ kutaścana vanaṃ saumitri-sītā-sakhaḥ ||SRs_3.118|| [bā.rā. 6.13]
body.translated_text: 'Ho, my speech! Leave your own dwelling; quickly grant passage outward!' (aloud, to the king) 'O King, steady your consciousness — a dry thunderbolt approaches your ears!' (The royal couple act out alarm.) Vāmadeva: 'One in your very form — wearing bark-garments, bearing a bow, wearing matted locks — Rāma, having received the command, has gone from somewhere to the forest, accompanied by Saumitri (Lakṣmaṇa) and Sītā.' ||SRs_3.118|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 6.13]

body.text: ubhau mūrcchataḥ | vāmadevaḥ-deva samāśvasihi |
body.translated_text: Both faint. Vāmadeva: 'O King, take heart!'

body.text: daśarathaḥ (samāśvāsya)-kena punaḥ kāraṇena ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: <s>Daśaratha</s> (composing himself) — 'For what reason?' — beginning thus,

body.text: daśarathaḥ-vatsa rāmabhadra manye mamaiva malayācala-nivāsinaḥ priya-vayasyasya jaṭāyor api śoka-śaṅkur ayaṃ sarvaṅkaṣo bhaviṣyati | [6.55 padyād anantaram] ity antena kausalyā-daśarathādīnāṃ rakṣas-tarakṣu-haryakṣa-prabhṛti-sañcaraṇa-dāruṇāraṇyādiṣu rāma-pravāsa-viṣaya-śaṅkā-trāsānuvṛtti-kathanāt sambhramaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Daśaratha</s> [says] — 'Dear child <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, I think that even for my dear companion <s>Jaṭāyu</s>, who dwells on <s>Malayācala</s>, this all-pervading apprehension of grief will arise.' [From after verse 6.55] — and ending thus. Because this narrates the continued apprehension and fear of <s>Kausalyā</s>, <s>Daśaratha</s>, and others regarding <s>Rāma</s>'s sojourn in terrible forests where <s>Rākṣasas</s>, hyenas, lions, and the like roam, it constitutes <s>sambhrama</s> (agitation).

body.text:
atha ākṣepaḥ-
garbha-bīja-samākṣepam ākṣepaṃ paricakṣate ||SRs_3.119|| 58a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>ākṣepa</s> (anticipatory hint) —
The anticipatory hint of the seed of the <s>garbha</s> (development) is called <s>ākṣepa</s>. ||3.119||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] pañcamāṅke [5.74 padyād anantaraṃ] (praviśya apaṭīkṣepeṇa chinna-nāmā kṛtāvaguṇṭhanā) śūrpaṇakhā (sākrandaṃ pādayor nipatya)-ajja ekka-mādua pekkha takkhaa-cūḍāmaṇī uppāḍido | baḍavāṇala-jālā-kalāpaaṃ ghuṃtalidaṃ | dasakaṇṭha-kaniṭṭha-bahiṇie accāhidaṃ | [ārya eka-mātṛka prekṣasva takṣaka-cūḍāmaṇir utpāṭitaḥ | baḍavānala-jvālā-kalāpakaṃ cūrṇitam | daśakaṇṭha-kaniṣṭha-bhaginyā atyāhitam |] ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the fifth act [after verse 5.74] (entering, through the removal of the curtain, disfigured, with her veil drawn) — <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> (with a cry, falling at his feet) — 'O noble brother, look! The crown-jewel of <s>Takṣaka</s> (serpent-king) has been uprooted! The mass of submarine fire-flames has been pulverized! An outrage has been committed upon the youngest sister of the Ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>)!' — beginning thus,

body.text: rāvaṇaḥ (prakāśam)-tataḥ kiṃ tasyāḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (aloud) — Then what [happened] to her?

body.text: śūrpaṇakhā-sāpi laṃkessarassa samucidatti abaharaṃtī tehiṃ kābālia-bbada-joggā kidaṃhi | [sāpi laṅkeśvarasya samuciteti vyavaharantī taiḥ kāpālika-vrata-yogyā kṛtāsmi |]
body.translated_text: <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> — She too, claiming to be worthy of the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, was made fit for the <s>Kāpālika</s> vow [i.e., had her nose and ears cut off] by them!

body.text: ity antena aṅkānta-gata-bhāgena sakala-devatā-tejas tiraskaraṇa-rāvaṇātiśaya-varṇanā-garbhīkṛtasya rāmotsāhasya śūrpaṇakhā-karṇa-nāsā-nikṛntana-rūpeṇa samudbhedād ākṣepaḥ |
body.translated_text: — and ending thus. Because the enthusiasm of <s>Rāma</s>, which had been implanted within the narrative of the excellence of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s superiority that eclipses the radiance of all deities — at the end of the act — bursts forth in the form of the cutting of <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>'s ears and nose, it constitutes <s>ākṣepa</s>.

body.text: atha vimarśa-sandhiḥ-

children.translated_text: That in which the seed-purpose, burst forth from the <s>garbha</s> (development),
is deliberated upon through enticement, anger, distress, and the like — that is called <s>vimarśa</s>. ||3.120||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>vimarśa-sandhi</s> (deliberation juncture) —

body.text: prakarī-niyatāptyānuguṇyād atrāṅga-kalpanam | 59
body.translated_text: The elements [of this juncture] are arranged in accordance with <s>prakarī</s>, <s>niyatāpti</s>, and <s>ānuguṇya</s> [i.e., contextual fitness]:

body.text: apavādo' tha sampheṭo vidrava-drava-śaktayaḥ ||SRs_3.121||
body.translated_text: <s>apavāda</s> (censure), <s>sampheṭa</s> (verbal clash), <s>vidrava</s> (rout), <s>drava</s> (transgression), and <s>śakti</s> (power), ||3.121||

body.text: dyuti-prasaṅgau chalana-vyavasāyau nirodhanam | 60
body.translated_text: <s>dyuti</s> (threat), <s>prasaṅga</s> (narration of the relevant), <s>chalana</s> (mutual insult), <s>vyavasāya</s> (declaration of prowess), and <s>nirodhana</s> (obstruction),

body.text: prarocanā vicalanam ādānaṃ syus trayodaśa ||SRs_3.122||
body.translated_text: <s>prarocanā</s> (foreshadowing), <s>vicalana</s> (perturbation), and <s>ādāna</s> (seizure) — thus thirteen. ||3.122||

body.text:
atha apavādaḥ-
tatrāpavādo doṣāṇāṃ prakhyāpanam itīryate ||SRs_3.123|| 61
body.translated_text:
Now <s>apavāda</s> (censure) —
Among these, <s>apavāda</s> is declared to be the proclamation of faults. ||3.123||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] aṣṭamāṅke vīra-vilāsa-nāmani [ādau] (tataḥ praviśato rākṣasau) ekaḥ-sakhe durmukha kim api mahān sattva-bhraṃśo daśakaṇṭhasya yat kumāra-siṃhanāda-vadham apy ākarṇya na śokaṃ kṛto nāpy amarṣaḥ | ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], in the eighth act titled '<s>Vīra-vilāsa</s>' (Heroic Display) [at the beginning] (then two <s>Rākṣasas</s> enter) — the first [says] — 'Friend <s>Durmukha</s>, what a great loss of courage (<s>sattva</s>) on the part of the Ten-necked one, that even upon hearing of the slaying of Prince <s>Siṃhanāda</s>, he has neither grieved nor shown indignation!' — beginning thus,

body.text: trijaṭā-kahaṃ deveṇa diṇṇo lajjā-deīe jalāṃjalī | [kathaṃ devena datto lajjā-devyai jalāñjaliḥ |] [8.10 padyād anantaram] ity antena rāvaṇa-gata-durbuddhi-doṣa-prakhyāpanād apavādaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Trijaṭā</s> — 'How has the lord offered water-oblation to the goddess of Shame?' [After verse 8.10] — and ending thus. Because this proclaims the fault of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s evil counsel, it constitutes <s>apavāda</s>.

body.text:
atha sampheṭaḥ-
doṣa-saṅgrathitaṃ vākyaṃ sampheṭaṃ sampracakṣate ||SRs_3.124|| 62a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>sampheṭa</s> (verbal clash) —
Speech strung with faults is declared to be <s>sampheṭa</s>. ||3.124||

body.text:
yathā tatraiva, sumukhaḥ (janāntikam)-sakhe durmukha ! kim api śauryātireko rāmānujasya yad amunā nikumbhilāṃ prasthitasya kumāra-meghanādasya sandiṣṭam, yad uta-
yāvan naiva nikumbhilāya-janataḥ siddhe havir lehini
prāpta-syandana-bāṇa-cāpa-kavacaḥ svaṃ manyase durjayam |
vaidehī-viraha-vyathā-vidhurite' py ārye vidhāya krudho
vandhyās tāvad ayaṃ sa śakra-vijayiṃs tvāṃ lakṣmaṇo jeṣyati ||SRs_3.125|| [bā.rā. 8.15]
body.translated_text:
For example, in the same [play], <s>Sumukha</s> (aside) — 'Friend <s>Durmukha</s>! What extraordinary excess of valor in <s>Rāma</s>'s younger brother, that he sent this message to Prince <s>Meghanāda</s> as he was setting out for <s>Nikumbhilā</s>, namely —
"As long as the fire-licking oblation at <s>Nikumbhilā</s> is not accomplished,
and you consider yourself invincible with chariot, arrows, bow, and armor —
even though the noble one (<s>Rāma</s>) is shaken by the anguish of separation from <s>Vaidehī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>),
until then, this <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, O conqueror of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), shall conquer you — fruitless [your efforts]!"' ||3.125|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 8.15]

body.text: ity upakramya, nepathye-
body.translated_text: — beginning thus, from behind the stage —

body.text:
sītā-priyaṃ ca daliteśvara-kārmukaṃ ca
bāli-druhaṃ ca racitāmbudhi-bandhanaṃ ca |
rakṣohaṇaṃ ca vijigīṣu-vibhīṣaṇaṃ ca
rāmaṃ nihatya caraṇau tava vanditāhe ||SRs_3.126|| [bā.rā. 8.47]
body.translated_text:
'Having slain <s>Rāma</s> — <s>Sītā</s>'s beloved, the breaker of <s>Īśvara</s>'s bow,
the enemy of <s>Bālin</s>, the builder of the ocean-causeway,
the slayer of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and the [patron] of the victorious <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> —
we shall bow at your feet!' ||3.126|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 8.47]

body.text: ity antena, lakṣmaṇendrajit-kumbhakarṇānāṃ roṣa-vākya-grahaṇāt sampheṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: — and ending thus. Because this captures the wrathful words of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Indrajit</s>, and <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, it constitutes <s>sampheṭa</s>.

body.text:
atha vidravaḥ-
virodha-vadha-dāhādir vidravaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||SRs_3.127|| 62b
body.translated_text:
Now <s>vidrava</s> (rout) —
Conflict, slaughter, conflagration, and the like are declared to be <s>vidrava</s>. ||3.127||

body.text: yathā tatraiva (8.48 padyād anantaraṃ] sumukhaḥ-deva padātilavaḥ sumukhas tu manyate lakṣmaṇa-didhakṣayā kumāra-meghanādena pāvakīyaḥ śaraḥ saṃhita iti upakramya,
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play, after verse 8.48] <s>Sumukha</s> [says] — 'O lord, the foot-soldier <s>Lava</s>... <s>Sumukha</s> thinks that Prince <s>Meghanāda</s> has readied a fiery arrow with the intent of burning <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>' — beginning thus,

body.text: (dakṣiṇataḥ) sumukhaḥ-ayam aparaḥ kṣate kṣārāvasekaḥ |
body.translated_text: (From the right side) <s>Sumukha</s> — 'Here is another sprinkling of salt on a wound!'

body.text:
ākarṇākṛṣṭa-cāponmukha-viśikha-śikhā-śekharaḥ śūla-pāṇir
bibhrāṇo bhairavatvaṃ bahula-kalakalārāva-raudrāṭṭa-hāsaḥ |
dhyātaḥ saumitri-ṇātha prasarad-urutarottāla-vetāla-mālas
tad-vaktrād utpatadbhiḥ samajani śikhibhir bhasmasād indrajic ca ||SRs_3.128|| [8.85]
body.translated_text:
'With banner-staff marked by arrows, with charioteer swooning and bowing,
attended by rows of vulture-birds greedy for the taste of flesh,
with axle-staff shattered by the fall of the great headless trunk of the lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
by horses who neighed and were carried away remembering the stable — the chariot is being taken to <s>Laṅkā</s>.' ||3.128|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 8.85]

body.text: (rāvaṇo mūrcchati sarve yathocitam upacaranti |) rāvaṇaḥ (mūrcchā-viccheda-nāṭitakena) ity antena kapisenāvikṣobha-sugrīva-nirodha-kumbhakarṇa-vadhendrajid-bhasmīkaraṇa-rāvaṇa-mūrcchādi-saṅkathanād vidravaḥ |
body.translated_text: (<s>Rāvaṇa</s> faints; all attend to him as appropriate.) <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (acting out the breaking of the swoon) — and ending thus. Because this narrates the disturbance of the monkey army, the capture of <s>Sugrīva</s>, the slaying of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, the incineration of <s>Indrajit</s>, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s fainting, and the like, it constitutes <s>vidrava</s>.

body.text:
atha dravaḥ-
guru-vyatikramaṃ prāha dravaṃ tu bharato muniḥ ||SRs_3.129|| 63a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>drava</s> (transgression) —
The sage <s>Bharata</s> calls <s>drava</s> a transgression against a superior. ||3.129||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, karaṅkaḥ-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], <s>Karaṅka</s> [says] —

body.text:
dhik śauṇḍīrya-madoddhataṃ bhuja-vanaṃ dhik candrahāsaṃ ca te
dhig vaktrāṇi nikṛtta-kaṇṭha-valaya-prītendu-maulīni ca |
nidrā-lāvatighasmare pratidinaṃ svāpān mahā-medure
pratyāśā cira-vismṛtāyudha-vidhau yat kumbhakarṇe sthitā ||SRs_3.130|| [bā.rā. 8.74]
body.translated_text:
'Shame on the forest of arms, arrogant with pride of prowess! Shame on your <s>Candrahāsa</s> [sword]!
Shame on the faces [of those severed heads] with crescent-moon crowns delighting in the necklaces of severed throats!
In drowsy <s>Lāvatighasmare</s> (?), sleeping daily in the great corpulence [of sloth],
the hope rests in <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, who has long forgotten the practice of arms!' ||3.130|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 8.74]

body.text: ity atra svāminor daśakaṇṭha-kumbhakarṇayor anujīvinā rākṣasena nindā-karaṇād dravaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because a <s>Rākṣasa</s> retainer censures his masters, the Ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) and <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, it constitutes <s>drava</s>.

body.text:
atha śaktiḥ-
utpannasya virodhasya śamanaṃ śaktir iṣyate ||SRs_3.131|| 63
body.translated_text:
Now <s>śakti</s> (power) —
The pacification of the conflict that has arisen is considered <s>śakti</s>. ||3.131||

body.text: yathā tatraiva rāvaṇa-vadha-nāmani navamāṅke [9.49 padyād pūrvam], purandaraḥ-yat kulācala-sandoha-dahana-karmaṇi bhagavān kālāgnirudraḥ ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], in the ninth act titled 'The Slaying of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>' [before verse 9.49], <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) [says] — 'That the blessed <s>Kālāgnirudra</s> [acts] in the matter of burning the mass of family-mountains...' — beginning thus,

body.text:
nepathye-
bāṇair lāñchita-ketu-yaṣṭi-śikharo mūrcchā-namat-sārathir
māsāsvādana-lubdha-gṛdhra-vihaga-śreṇībhir āsevitaḥ |
rakṣo-nātha-mahā-kabandha-patana-kṣuṇṇākṣa-daṇḍo hayair
heṣitvā smṛta-mandurāsthiti-hṛtair laṅkāṃ ratho nīyata ||SRs_3.132|| [bā.rā. 9.56]
body.translated_text:
From behind the stage —
'With banner-staff peaks marked by arrows, with charioteer swooning and bowing,
attended by rows of vulture-birds greedy for the taste of flesh,
with axle-staff shattered by the fall of the great headless trunk of the lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>,
by horses who neighed remembering the stable and were drawn [away] — the chariot is being taken to <s>Laṅkā</s>.' ||3.132|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 9.56]

body.text: ity antena niravaśeṣa-pratināyaka-bhūta-rāvaṇa-kaṇṭhotsādana-kathanena virodha-śamanāt śaktiḥ |
body.translated_text: — and ending thus. Because this narrates the complete cutting of the throat of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the entire antagonist, thereby pacifying the conflict, it constitutes <s>śakti</s>.

body.text:
atha dyutiḥ-
dyutir nāma samuddiṣṭā tarjanodvejane budhaiḥ ||SRs_3.133|| 64a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>dyuti</s> (threat) —
<s>Dyuti</s> is designated by the wise as the threatening and alarming [of others]. ||3.133||

body.text: yathā tatraiva aṣṭamāṅke, rāvaṇaḥ (ūrdhvam avalokya)-kim ayam atisatvaraḥ sura-samājaḥ ? śaṅke katipaya-yātudhāna-vadhān tāpasaṃ prati prīyate | (sa-krodha-tarjanam)
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], in the eighth act, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (looking upward) — 'What, is this divine assembly in such haste? I suspect they are rejoicing at the slaying of a few <s>Rākṣasas</s>, toward the ascetic (<s>Rāma</s>).' (With angry threat) —

body.text:
harṣotkarṣaḥ kim ayam amarāḥ kṣudra-rakṣo-vadhād vas
tan me doṣṇāṃ vijita-jagatāṃ vikramaṃ vistṛtāḥ stha |
kiṃ cādyaiva priya-raṇa-raso bodhyate kumbhakarṇas
tūrṇaṃ jetā sa ca diviṣadāṃ bodhyate meghanādaḥ ||SRs_3.134|| [bā.rā. 8.12]
body.translated_text:
'Is this exuberance of joy, O immortals, [merely] from the slaying of petty <s>Rākṣasas</s>?
Then you are wide [of the mark regarding] the valor of my arms, which have conquered the world!
Moreover, let <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, who delights in the <s>rasa</s> of battle, be awakened today itself;
and quickly let <s>Meghanāda</s> too be awakened — he, the conqueror of the gods!' ||3.134|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 8.12]

body.text: ity upakramya, nepathye-biraeha keli-ākaḍḍhaṇa-pāḍaṇijjaṃ goura-duvāraṃ, boḍheha bibiha-ppaharaṇa-saṇṇāha-daha-sahassāi | (vracayata kelikākarṣaṇa-pātanīyaṃ gopura-dvāram | vahata vividha-praharaṇa-saṃnāha-daśa-sahasrāṇi |) ity antena devatā-tarjana-laṅkā-pura-janodvejana-kathanād dyutiḥ |
body.translated_text: — beginning thus, from behind the stage — [Prakrit:] 'Prepare the gate of the fortress for the sport of pulling down and demolishing! Carry ten thousand sets of various weapons and armor!' — and ending thus. Because this narrates the threatening of the deities and the alarming of the people of <s>Laṅkā</s>-city, it constitutes <s>dyuti</s>.

body.text: atha prasaṅgaḥ-

children.translated_text: The narration of the matter at hand is declared to be <s>prasaṅga</s>.
Others say that <s>prasaṅga</s> is the celebration of elders. ||3.135||

body.translated_text: Now <s>prasaṅga</s> (narration of the relevant) —

body.text: yathā tatraiva navamāṅke [ādau] (praviśya) yama-puruṣaḥ-tatra-bhavato lulāya-lakṣaṇaḥ sakala-prāṇibhṛtāṃ vihita-nāśasya kīnāśasya kim api viśvātiśāyinī prabhaviṣṇutā ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], in the ninth act [at the beginning] (entering) a <s>Yama</s>-attendant [says] — 'The supremely surpassing power of the venerable one, known by the mark <s>Lulāya</s>, the destroyer ordained for all living beings...' — beginning thus,

body.text: daśarathaḥ-bhagavan gīrvāṇa-nātha sa-prasādam ito nidhīyantāṃ dṛṣṭayaḥ | [9.18 padyāt pūrvam] ity antena yama-purandarādi-pūjya-saṅkīrtanād vā prastuta-rākṣasa-vadha-rūpasyārthasya prapañcanād vā prasaṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Daśaratha</s> [says] — 'Blessed lord of the gods, graciously turn your glances hither!' [Before verse 9.18] — and ending thus. Because this celebrates the worshipful <s>Yama</s>, <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), and others, or because it elaborates the matter at hand, namely the slaying of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, it constitutes <s>prasaṅga</s>.

body.text:
atha chalanam[*18]-
avamānādi-karaṇaṃ kāryārthe chalanaṃ viduḥ ||SRs_3.136|| 65
[*18] nātya-śāstre atra chādana iti saṃjñā prāpyate |
body.translated_text:
Now <s>chalana</s> (mutual insult) —
The performance of contempt and the like for the sake of one's purpose is known as <s>chalana</s>. ||3.136||

body.text:
yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] cāraṇaḥ (karṇaṃ dattvā ākāśe)-kim āha rāmabhadraḥ | re re rākṣasa-putra-
yad gaurī-caraṇābjayoḥ prathamatas tyakta-praṇāma-kriyaṃ
premārdreṇa sa-vibhrameṇa ca purā yenekṣitā jānakī |
lūnaṃ te tad idaṃca rākṣasa-śiro jātaṃ ca śāntaṃ manaḥ
śeṣa-ccheda-vidhis tu samprati paraṃ svar-vandin-mokṣāya me ||SRs_3.137|| [bā.rā. 9.10]
body.translated_text:
For example, in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], a <s>Cāraṇa</s> (celestial bard) (lending his ear to the sky) — 'What does <s>Rāmabhadra</s> say? — Ho ho, son of a <s>Rākṣasa</s>!
"That [eye] which, before <s>Gaurī</s>'s (<s>Pārvatī</s>'s) lotus-feet, first abandoned the act of obeisance,
and with which, moist with love and with agitation, <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) was formerly gazed upon —
this head of yours, O <s>Rākṣasa</s>, has been severed, and my mind is at peace;
the procedure for cutting the rest is now [merely] for the liberation of the celestial panegyrists held captive by you!"' ||3.137|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 9.10]

body.text: kim āha rāvaṇaḥ ? re re kṣatriyā-putra sulabha-vibhrama-carma-cakṣur asi ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: 'What does <s>Rāvaṇa</s> say? — Ho ho, son of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman! You are an eye [easily] deluded by cheap enchantment!' — beginning thus,

body.text: rāmaḥ-tad ittham abhidhānam apavitraṃ te vaktram | ito nirviśatu vadha-śuddhim [9.46 padyād anantaram] ity antena rāma-rāvaṇābhyāṃ parasparāvamānana-karaṇāt chalanam |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> [says] — 'So this is your utterance — impure is your mouth! Let it now attain purification by death.' [After verse 9.46] — and ending thus. Because <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> mutually perform contempt, it constitutes <s>chalana</s>.

body.text:
atha vyavasāyaḥ-
vyavasāyaḥ sva-sāmarthya-prakhyāpanam itīryate ||SRs_3.138|| 66a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>vyavasāya</s> (declaration of prowess) —
<s>Vyavasāya</s> is declared to be the proclamation of one's own might. ||3.138||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe]-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>] —

body.text:
bho laṅkeśvara dīyatāṃ janakajā rāmaḥ svayaṃ yācate
ko' yaṃ te mati-vibhramaḥ smara nayaṃ nādyāpi kiṃcid gatam |
naivaṃ cet khara-dūṣaṇa-triśirasāṃ kaṇṭhāsṛjā paṅkilaḥ
patrī naiṣa sahiṣyate mama dhanur jyā-bandha-bandhūkṛtaḥ ||SRs_3.139|| [bā.rā. 9.19]
body.translated_text:
'O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, let <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter be given — <s>Rāma</s> himself asks!
What is this delusion of your mind? Remember statecraft — nothing has yet passed!
If not so, stained with the throat-blood of <s>Khara</s>, <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Triśiras</s>,
this arrow will not be tolerated — [this arrow] from my bow, made red like a <s>bandhūka</s> flower by the bowstring-band!' ||3.139|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 9.19]

body.text: ity upakramya-kim āha rāvaṇaḥ ? re re mānuṣī-putra ! ayam asau akṣatriyo rāvaṇaḥ | kṣatriyo rāmaḥ | tad atra dṛśyatām | kataro vineyaḥ | kataro vinetā iti | kim āha rāmabhadraḥ ? haṃho amānuṣī-putra ! kṣatriyo rāmaḥ | ayam asau akṣatriyo rāvaṇaḥ | tad atra dṛśyatāṃ kataro vineyaḥ, kataro vinetā [9.26 padyād anantaraṃ] ity antena rāma-rāvaṇābhyāṃ sva-sāmarthya-prakhyāpanād vyavasāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: — beginning thus. 'What does <s>Rāvaṇa</s> say? — Ho ho, son of a mortal woman! Here is that non-<s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>Rāvaṇa</s>! And <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>Rāma</s>! Then let it be seen here — who is to be disciplined and who is the discipliner!' 'What does <s>Rāmabhadra</s> say? — Ha ha, son of a non-human woman! <s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>Rāma</s>! Here is that non-<s>Kṣatriya</s> <s>Rāvaṇa</s>! Then let it be seen here — who is to be disciplined and who is the discipliner!' [After verse 9.26] — and ending thus. Because <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> both proclaim their own might, it constitutes <s>vyavasāya</s>.

body.text:
atha virodhanam-
virodhanaṃ nirodhoktiḥ saṃrabdhānāṃ parasparam ||SRs_3.140|| 66
yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe tasminn eva sthāne] cāraṇaḥ-katham amarṣitābhyāṃ rāma-rāvaṇābhyāṃ pratyupakrāntam iṣu-varṣādvaitam ity upakramya, cāraṇaḥ-nanv ayam oṃkāro rāvaṇa-śiro-maṇḍala-cchedana-vidyāyāḥ [9.39 padyād anantaram] ity antena saṃrabdhayo rāma-rāvaṇayoḥ divyāstra-prayoga-rūpa-paraspara-saṃrodha-karaṇād virodhanam |
body.translated_text:
Now <s>virodhana</s> (obstruction) —
<s>Virodhana</s> is the mutual speech of obstruction by those who are furious. ||3.140||
For example, in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, at the same point], a <s>Cāraṇa</s> [says] — 'How have the enraged <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> commenced a veritable non-duality of arrow-showers!' — beginning thus, the <s>Cāraṇa</s> — 'Indeed, this <s>oṃkāra</s> [sound] is [the prelude to] the science of severing the array of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s heads...' [after verse 9.39] — and ending thus. Because the furious <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> mutually obstruct each other through the employment of divine weapons, it constitutes <s>virodhana</s>.

body.text:
atha prarocanā-
siddhavad bhāvino' rthasya sūcanā syāt prarocanā ||SRs_3.141|| 67a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>prarocanā</s> (foreshadowing) —
The indication of a future event as if it were already accomplished — that is <s>prarocanā</s>. ||3.141||

body.text: yathā tatraiva aṣṭamāṅke [8.16 padyād anantaram], karaṅkaḥ (janāntikam)-sakhe kañkāla devaḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ prabodhayati | na punar ātmānam | kiṃ ca prayatnena bodhito' py asau rāmeṇa punaḥ śāyitavya eva |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], in the eighth act, <s>Karaṅka</s> (aside) — 'Friend <s>Kaṅkāla</s>, the Lord is awakening <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> — but not himself! Moreover, even though [<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>] is awakened with effort, he is to be put to sleep again by <s>Rāma</s>!'

body.text: kaṅkālaḥ-maṇṇe bibhīsaṇaṃ bajjia sabbassa bi esā gaī | [manye vibhīṣaṇaṃ varjayitvā sarvasyāpy eṣā gatiḥ |]
body.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkāla</s> [says in Prakrit] — 'I think, except for <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, this is the fate of everyone!'

body.text: karaṅkaḥ-tathaiva | ity atra bhaviṣyataḥ kumbhakarṇādi-rākṣasa-nāśasya kaṅkāla-karaṅkābhyāṃ siddhavat niścitya sūcanāt prarocanā |
body.translated_text: <s>Karaṅka</s> — 'Just so.' — Here, because the future destruction of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> and other <s>Rākṣasas</s> is indicated by <s>Kaṅkāla</s> and <s>Karaṅka</s> as if already accomplished, this constitutes <s>prarocanā</s> (anticipatory delight).

body.text:
atha vicalanam-
ātma-ślāghā vicalanam ||SRs_3.142|| 67c
body.translated_text: Now <s>vicalana</s> (boasting) — Self-praise is <s>vicalana</s>. ||SRs_3.142||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, karaṅkaḥ-kim āha kumbhakarṇaḥ-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], <s>Karaṅka</s> — 'What does <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> say?' —

body.text:
āstāṃ dhanuḥ kim asinā parato bhusuṇḍī-
cakrair alaṃ bhavatu paṭṭiśam udgarādyaiḥ |
dhāvat-plavaṅga-pṛtanā-kabala-krameṇa
yāsyāmy ahaṃ suhitatāṃ ca ripu-kṣayaṃ ca ||SRs_3.143|| [bā.rā. 8.37]
body.translated_text: 'Let the bow be! What need of a sword? Away with the bludgeon! Enough of discus, spear, and throwing-clubs! By the method of swallowing the running monkey-armies in mouthfuls, I shall attain both satisfaction and the destruction of the enemy!' ||SRs_3.143|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 8.37]

body.text: (punaḥ pṛcchati rāvaṇaḥ) sādhu vatsa, sādhu | satyaṃ mad-anujo' si, ity upakramya-
body.translated_text: (<s>Rāvaṇa</s> asks again) — 'Well done, my boy, well done! Truly you are my younger brother!' — beginning thus —

body.text:
anena laṅkā yad akāri mat-purī
hanūmato gātra-gatena bhasmasāt |
nijāparādha-praśamāya tad dhruvaṃ
niṣevituṃ mām upayāti pāvakaḥ ||SRs_3.144|| [bā.rā. 8.48]
body.translated_text: 'That <s>Hanūmat</s>, through the body [of his], reduced my city <s>Laṅkā</s> to ashes; surely the fire now approaches me to expiate my own offense.' ||SRs_3.144|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 8.48]

body.text: ity antena rāvaṇa-kumbhakarṇābhyām ātma-ślāghā kṛteti vicalanam |
body.translated_text: Thus ending — since <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> engage in self-praise, this constitutes <s>vicalana</s>.

body.text:
atha ādānaṃ-
ādānaṃ kārya-saṅgrahaḥ ||SRs_3.145|| 67d
body.translated_text: Now <s>ādāna</s> (gathering up) — <s>Ādāna</s> is the gathering up of the action. ||SRs_3.145||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] navamāṅke purandaraḥ-sakhe daśaratha katham ayam ananya-sadṛśākāro rāmabhadra-puruṣakāraḥ | ataś ca-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the ninth act, <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) [says] — 'Friend <s>Daśaratha</s>, how this heroic exploit of <s>Rāmabhadra</s> is of a form unequaled by any other! And therefore —'

body.text:
nirdagdha-tripurendhano' stu giriśaḥ krauñcācala-cchedane
pāṇḍityaṃ viditaṃ guhasya kim u tāv ajñāta-yuddhotsavau |
lūtvā paṅka-jalāvamānana-vanaṃ vīrasya laṅkā-pater
vīrāṇāṃ caritādbhutasya parame rāmaḥ sthitaḥ sīmani ||SRs_3.146|| [bā.rā. 9.57]
body.translated_text: 'Let <s>Giriśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) be the one who burned the three cities; the skill of <s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>) in splitting Mount <s>Krauñca</s> is well known — but were those two ever acquainted with the festival of battle? Having cut down the jungle-swamp of contempt belonging to the heroic lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> — <s>Rāma</s> stands at the supreme frontier of heroes whose deeds are marvelous!' ||SRs_3.146|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 9.57]

body.text:
ity upakramya-
raṇa-rasika-sura-strī-mukta-mandāra-dāmā
svayam ayam avatīrṇo lakṣmaṇa-nyasta-hastaḥ |
viracita-jaya-śabdo vandibhiḥ syandanāṅgād
dinakara-kula-lakṣmī-vallabho rāmabhadraḥ ||SRs_3.147|| [bā.rā. 9.59]
body.translated_text: Beginning thus — 'Having himself descended, his hand placed on <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, wreathed with <s>mandāra</s> garlands released by the celestial women who relished the battle, with cries of victory uttered by bards, from the chariot-platform — <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, the beloved of the glory of the Solar dynasty!' ||SRs_3.147|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 9.59]

body.text: ity antena nikhila-bhuvana-bādhā-śamana-rūpa-rāvaṇa-vadha-sampādita-dharmādi-lakṣaṇa-kārya-viśeṣa-saṅgrahaṇād ādānam |
body.translated_text: Thus ending — because the particular action characterized by <s>Dharma</s> and the like, accomplished through the slaying of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (which constitutes the removal of the affliction of all the worlds), is gathered up, this constitutes <s>ādāna</s>.

body.text:
atha nirvahaṇa-sandhiḥ-
mukha-sandhyādayo yatra vikīrṇā bīja-saṃyutāḥ |
mahat-prayojanaṃ yānti tan-nirvahaṇam ucyate ||SRs_3.148|| 68
sandhi-virodhau grathanaṃ nirṇayaḥ paribhāṣaṇe prasādaś ca |
ānanda-samaya-kṛtayo bhāṣopagūhane tadvat ||SRs_3.149|| 69
atha pūrva-bhāva-sayujāv upasaṃhāra-praśastī ca |
iti nirvahaṇasyāṅgāny āhur amīṣāṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye ||SRs_3.150|| 70
body.translated_text: Now the <s>nirvahaṇa-sandhi</s> (denouement juncture) — Where the [elements of the] opening juncture and the rest, together with their seeds, are brought to their great purpose — that is called <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (denouement). ||SRs_3.148|| <s>Sandhi</s> (junction), <s>virodha</s> (conflict), <s>grathana</s> (weaving), <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination), <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s> (mutual discourse), <s>prasāda</s> (graciousness); <s>ānanda</s> (joy), <s>samaya</s> (relief), <s>kṛti</s> (confirmation); <s>bhāṣā</s> (discourse), <s>upagūhana</s> (embracing), and likewise ||SRs_3.149|| <s>pūrva-bhāva</s> (prior state), <s>sayuja</s> (union); <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion), <s>praśasti</s> (eulogy) — these are the elements of the denouement; I shall now state their definitions. ||SRs_3.150||

body.text:
tatra sandhiḥ-
bījopagamanaṃ sandhiḥ ||SRs_3.151|| 71a
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>sandhi</s> (junction) — The approach toward the seed — that is <s>sandhi</s>. ||SRs_3.151||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] rāghavānanda-nāmani daśamāṅke [ādau] (tataḥ praviśati saśokā) laṅkā-hā duddhara-taba-visesa-paritosidārabindāsaṇa tihubaṇekkamalla dasa-kaṇṭha hā helā-bandīkida-mahinda mehanāda hā samara-saṃraṃbha-suppasaṇṇa kuṃbha-kaṇṇa kahiṃsi dehi me paḍibaaṇaṃ | [hā durdhara-tapo-viśeṣa-paritoṣitāravindāsana tribhuvanaika-malla daśakaṇṭha ! hā helā-bandīkṛta-mahendra meghanāda ! hā samara-saṃrambha-suprasanna ! kumbhakarṇa kvāsi dehi me prativacanam |] ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, in the tenth act titled '<s>Rāghavānanda</s>' (The Joy of <s>Rāghava</s>) — (then enters, with grief) <s>Laṅkā</s> [personified, speaking in Prakrit] — 'Alas, <s>Daśakaṇṭha</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), who gratified <s>Brahmā</s> (seated on the lotus) by your extraordinary austerities, O sole champion of the three worlds! Alas, <s>Meghanāda</s>, who made great <s>Indra</s> a captive in sport! Alas, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, ever gracious in the fury of battle — where are you? Give me an answer!' — beginning thus,

body.text: (praviśya satvarā) alakā-sakhi dharma-jetari vibhīṣaṇe' pi netari tatrabhavatī sa-śoka-śaṅkur iva |
body.translated_text: (Entering hastily) — 'Friend <s>Alakā</s>, even with the righteous conqueror <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> as lord, she [Laṅkā personified] seems [full of] grief and apprehension.'

body.text: laṅkā-jaṃ tiṇetta-mittassa ṇaarī bhaṇadī | [yat trinetra-mitrasya nagarī bhaṇati |] [10.2 padyāt pūrvam] ity antena duṣṭa-rākṣasa-śikṣā-rūpa-rāmotsāha-bījopagamanāt sandhiḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Laṅkā</s> [in Prakrit] — 'For the city of the friend of the Three-eyed one (<s>Śiva</s>) speaks [thus].' — Thus ending, because this approaches the seed — namely <s>Rāma</s>'s enterprise of chastising the wicked <s>Rākṣasas</s>, this constitutes <s>sandhi</s>.

body.text:
atha virodhaḥ-
kāryānveṣaṇaṃ virodhaḥ syāt ||SRs_3.152|| 71b
body.translated_text: Now <s>virodha</s> (conflict) — The search for the [remaining] action — that is <s>virodha</s>. ||SRs_3.152||

body.text:
yathā tatraiva, nepathye-
rudrāṇi lakṣmi varuṇāni sarasvati dyauḥ
sāvitri dhātri sakalāḥ kula-devatāś ca |
śuddhy-arthinī viśati śuṣmaṇi rāma-kāntā
tat saṃnidhatta sahasā saha loka-pālaiḥ ||SRs_3.153|| [bā.rā. 10.2]
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], [heard] from behind the stage — '<s>Rudrāṇī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Varuṇānī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Dyaus</s>, <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Dhātrī</s>, and all the family deities — <s>Rāma</s>'s beloved (<s>Sītā</s>), seeking purification, enters the fire; therefore, assemble at once together with the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-guardians)!' ||SRs_3.153|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.2]

body.text: ity upakramya, laṅkā-aho devadāṇaṃ bi sīdāpakkha-bādo | adhavā sabbo guṇesu rajjadi | ṇa sarīresu | [aho devatānām api sītā-pakṣapātaḥ | athavā sarvo guṇeṣu rajyati | na śarīreṣu |] [10.8 padyād anantaram] ity antena sītā-śuddhi-rūpa-kāryānveṣaṇād virodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, <s>Laṅkā</s> [in Prakrit] — 'Ah, even the gods are partial to <s>Sītā</s>! Or rather, everyone is attached to virtues, not to bodies.' — Thus ending, because the search for the action of <s>Sītā</s>'s purification is narrated, this constitutes <s>virodha</s>.

body.text:
atha grathanam-
grathanaṃ tad-upekṣepaḥ ||SRs_3.154|| 71c
body.translated_text: Now <s>grathana</s> (weaving) — <s>Grathana</s> is the anticipation of that [final action]. ||SRs_3.154||

body.text:
yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe]-
 baddhaḥ setur lavaṇa-jaladho krodha-vahneḥ samittvaṃ
nītaṃ rakṣaḥ-kulam adhigatāḥ śuddhimantaś ca dārāḥ |
tenedānīṃ vipina-vasatāveṣa pūrṇa-pratijño
diṣṭyāyodhyāṃ vrajati dayitā-prītaye puṣpakeṇa ||SRs_3.155|| [bā.rā. 10.15]
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> — 'The bridge over the salt-ocean has been built; the fire of wrath has been used as fuel; the <s>Rākṣasa</s> clan has been subdued; the wife's chastity has been verified. Therefore now, O [<s>Rāma</s>], whose vow has been fulfilled by the sojourn in the forest, by good fortune he proceeds to <s>Ayodhyā</s> in the <s>Puṣpaka</s> [aerial chariot], for the delight of his beloved!' ||SRs_3.155|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.15]

body.text: tad bhoḥ sakala-plavaṅga-yūtha-patayaḥ ity ārabhya,
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'O all chieftains of the monkey-hosts!' —

body.text:
sampreṣitaś ca hanumān bharatasya pārśvaṃ
laṅkāṅganācakita-netra-nirīkṣita-śrīḥ |
yāty eṣa vārinidhi-laṅghana-dṛṣṭa-sāro
rājyābhiṣeka-samayocita-kārya-siddheḥ ||SRs_3.156|| [bā.rā. 10.16]
body.translated_text: 'And <s>Hanumān</s> has been dispatched to <s>Bharata</s>'s side, his splendor observed by the startled eyes of the women of <s>Laṅkā</s>; he goes, his worth proven in the crossing of the ocean, for the accomplishment of the tasks befitting the occasion of the royal consecration.' ||SRs_3.156|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.16]

body.text: ity antena rāmābhiṣeka-rūpa-parama-kāropekṣād grathanam |
body.translated_text: Thus ending — because of the anticipation of the supreme action in the form of <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration, this constitutes <s>grathana</s>.

body.text:
atha nirṇayaḥ-
syād anubhūtasya nirṇayaḥ kathanam ||SRs_3.157|| 71d
body.translated_text: Now <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination) — The narration of what has been experienced — that is <s>nirṇaya</s>. ||SRs_3.157||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [bāla-rāmāyaṇe] rāmaḥ (apavārya)-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s> (aside [to <s>Sītā</s>]) —

body.text:
ayyasmad-agra-kara-yantra-nipīḍitānāṃ
dhārāmbhasāṃ smarasi majjana-keli-kāle |
subhru tvayā nija-kucābharaṇaika-yogyam
atrābja-valli-dalam āvaraṇāya dattam ||SRs_3.158|| [bā.rā. 10.76]
body.translated_text: 'Do you remember, fair-browed one, during the sport of bathing, the streams of water pressed out by the water-machines at the hands of the elders? By you, a single lotus-petal, fit only to adorn your own breasts, was given as a covering!' ||SRs_3.158|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.76]

body.text:
kiṃ ca-
tad iha kalaha-kelī saikate narmadāyāḥ
smarasi sutanu kiṃcin nau parādhīna-suptam |
uṣasi jala-samīra-preṅkhaṇācārya-kāryaṃ
tad anu madana-mudrāṃ tac ca gāḍhopagūḍham ||SRs_3.159|| [bā.rā. 10.77]
body.translated_text: Moreover — 'Do you remember, slender one, something on the banks of the <s>Narmadā</s>, in the sport of quarreling? Our sleep, dependent on each other; at dawn, the rocking by the water-breezes acting as a teacher; and thereafter the love-mark and that tight embrace?' ||SRs_3.159|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.77]

body.text: ity atra rāmeṇa svānubhūtārtha-kathanān nirṇayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since <s>Rāma</s> narrates personally experienced events, this constitutes <s>nirṇaya</s>.

body.text:
atha paribhāṣā-
paribhāṣā tv anyonyaṃ jalpanam athavā parivādaḥ ||SRs_3.160|| 72a
body.translated_text: Now <s>paribhāṣā</s> (mutual discourse) — <s>Paribhāṣā</s> is mutual conversation, or alternatively, censure. ||SRs_3.160||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [10.92 padyād anantaram] sītā-ajja-utta dasakaṇṭha-ṇisūaṇa vārāṇasī-saṃkittaṇeṇa sumarābidamhi akkhiāṇaddaṃ jaṇaṇī-bhūdaṃ mihilāṃ mahā-ṇāarīṃ | [ārya-putra daśakaṇṭha-nisūdana vārāṇasī-saṅkīrtanena smāritāsmi akṣy-ānandaṃ jananī-bhūtaṃ mithilāṃ mahā-nāgarīm |] ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], <s>Sītā</s> [in Prakrit] — 'Noble lord, destroyer of <s>Daśakaṇṭha</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), by the mention of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, I am reminded of <s>Mithilā</s>, the great city, my motherland, a delight to the eyes!' — beginning thus,

body.text: vibhīṣaṇaḥ-iha hi khalu kṣatriyāntakarasya bhaṅgo bhārgava-muner dattaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> — 'Here indeed the defeat of the Destroyer of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) was given by the sage <s>Bhārgava</s>!'

body.text:
sugrīvaḥ-
apāṃ phenena tṛpto' sau snātaś candrikayā ca saḥ |
yad aprasūta-kauśalyaṃ kṣatraṃ kṣapitavān muniḥ ||SRs_3.161|| [bā.rā. 10.94]
body.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> — 'He was sated with the foam of water and bathed in moonlight — that sage who destroyed the <s>Kṣatriya</s> class, whose valor was born without [true] skill!' ||SRs_3.161|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.94]

body.text: ity antena sītā-rāma-vibhīṣaṇa-sugrīvāṇām anyonya-saṃjalpanena vā sugrīveṇa bhārgava-parīvāda-sūcanād vā paribhāṣaṇam |
