body.translated_text: Thus ending — either through the mutual conversation of <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Sugrīva</s>, or through <s>Sugrīva</s>'s indication of censure of <s>Bhārgava</s>, this constitutes <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s>.

body.text:
atha prasādaḥ-
śuśrūṣādi-prāptaṃ prasādam āhuḥ prasannatvam ||SRs_3.162|| 72b
body.translated_text: Now <s>prasāda</s> (graciousness) — That state of being pleased, attained through service and the like — that the [authorities] call <s>prasāda</s>. ||SRs_3.162||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, rāmaḥ (hastam udyamya)-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], <s>Rāma</s> (raising his hand) —

body.text:
haṃho puṣpaka-vāyu-vega-muninā dhūmaḥ puraḥ pīyate
chāyāṃ mā kuru ko' py ayaṃ dina-maṇāv ekāgra-dṛṣṭiḥ sthitaḥ |
dūrād atra bhava pradakṣiṇa-gatiḥ sthāṇor idaṃ mandiraṃ
kiñcit tiṣṭha tapasvinas tava puro yāvat paryānty adhvanaḥ ||SRs_3.163|| [bā.rā. 10.59]
body.translated_text: 'Ho, the smoke ahead is being swallowed by the speed-wind of <s>Puṣpaka</s>! Do not cast a shadow — someone stands there gazing intently at the sun! Give way from here, proceed in a clockwise path — this is the temple of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); wait a moment — let the travelers' paths [clear] before you, O ascetic!' ||SRs_3.163|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.59]

body.text: ity upakramya, agastyaḥ-
body.translated_text: Beginning thus, <s>Agastya</s> —

body.text:
kā dīyatāṃ tava raghūdvaha samyag-āśīr
niṣkaṇṭakāni vihitāni jaganti yena |
āśāsmahe nanu tathāpi saha sva-vīrair
bhū-kāśyapopama-suta-dvitayā vadhūḥ syāt ||SRs_3.164|| [bā.rā. 10.64]
body.translated_text: 'What proper blessing can be given to you, O scion of <s>Raghu</s>, by whom the worlds have been made free of thorns? Yet we do wish: together with your own heroes, may the bride be [blessed with] a pair of sons equal to <s>Bhū</s> and <s>Kāśyapa</s>!' ||SRs_3.164|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.64]

body.text: rāmaḥ-param anugṛhītaṃ raghu-kulam ity antena agastya-dattāśīrvāda-rūpa-prasāda-kathanāt prasādaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> — 'The <s>Raghu</s> dynasty has been supremely graced.' — Thus ending, because the narration of the graciousness in the form of <s>Agastya</s>'s blessing is given, this constitutes <s>prasāda</s>.

body.text:
atha ānandaḥ-
abhilaṣitārtha-samāgamam ānandaṃ prāhur ācāryāḥ ||SRs_3.165|| 73a
body.translated_text: Now <s>ānanda</s> (joy) — The encounter with the desired object — that the preceptors call <s>ānanda</s>. ||SRs_3.165||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, rāmaḥ-haṃho vimāna-rāja vimucya vasudhā-savidha-vartinī gatiṃ kiñcid uccair bhava | kutūhalinī jānakī divya-loka-darśana-vyatikarasya | (ūrdhva-gati-nāṭikena)
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], <s>Rāma</s> — 'Ho, O king of aerial chariots, abandon the course near the earth and rise somewhat higher! <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) is curious about the spectacle of the divine worlds!' (With the acting of upward flight) —

body.text:
yathā yathārohati baddha-vegaṃ
vyomnaḥ śikhāṃ puṣpakam ānatāṅgi |
mahāmbudhīnāṃ valayair viśālais
tathā tathā saṅkuciteva pṛthvī ||SRs_3.166|| [bā.rā. 10.22]
body.translated_text: 'As the <s>Puṣpaka</s>, ascending with constrained speed, reaches the summit of the sky, O graceful-limbed one, the earth seems to contract with the vast rings of the great oceans.' ||SRs_3.166|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.22]

body.text: sura-cāraṇa-kiṃnara-vidyādhara-kula-saṅkulaṃ gagana-garbham īkṣasva | (praviśya) vidyādharaḥ : ataḥ parama-gamyā asmādṛśāṃ bhuvaḥ | sa ca brahma-loka iti śrūyate |
body.translated_text: 'Behold the expanse of the sky, thronging with the hosts of gods, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Vidyādharas</s>!' (Entering) A <s>Vidyādhara</s>: 'Beyond this, the earth is inaccessible to beings like us. And that [realm] is called the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.'

body.text: ity antena sītādīnām abhilaṣita-divya-loka-darśana-rūpārtha-siddher ānandaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus ending — because <s>Sītā</s> and the others attain the desired sight of the divine worlds, this constitutes <s>ānanda</s>.

body.text:
atha samayaḥ-
samayo duḥkha-saṅkṣayaḥ ||SRs_3.167|| 73b
body.translated_text: Now <s>samaya</s> (relief) — <s>Samaya</s> is the cessation of sorrow. ||SRs_3.167||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, bharataḥ : ārya ! rāvaṇa-vidrāvaṇa bharato' ham abhivādaye | ity upakramya (bharata-sugrīva-vibhīṣaṇāḥ parasparaṃ pariṣvajante |) ity antena bandhūnām anyonyāvalokana-pariṣvaṅgādibhir duḥkhāpagama-kathanāt samayaḥ |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], <s>Bharata</s>: 'Elder brother! I, <s>Bharata</s>, the one who routed <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, pay my respects!' — beginning thus — (<s>Bharata</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> embrace one another.) — Thus ending, because the cessation of sorrow through the mutual seeing and embracing of kinsmen is narrated, this constitutes <s>samaya</s>.

body.text:
atha kṛtiḥ-
kṛtir api labdhārtha-susthirīkaraṇam ||SRs_3.168|| 73c
body.translated_text: Now <s>kṛti</s> (confirmation) — <s>Kṛti</s> is also the firm establishment of what has been obtained. ||SRs_3.168||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, (praviśya) hanumān-deva mattaḥ śruta-vṛttānto vasiṣṭhaḥ samaṃ bharata-śaturghnābhyām anyābhiś ca prakṛtibhir bhavad-abhiṣeka-sajjas tiṣṭhati | ity upakramya, vasiṣṭhaḥ : kā dīyatāṃ tva raghūdvaha samyag āśīr ity ādi paṭhati |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], (entering) <s>Hanumān</s> — 'Lord, having heard the full account from me, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, together with <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s> and the other ministers, stands ready for your consecration.' — Beginning thus, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> recites: 'What proper blessing can be given to you, O scion of <s>Raghu</s>...' and so forth.

body.text: rāmaḥ: ārṣaṃ hi vacanaṃ vibhinna-vaktṛkam api na visaṃvadati yad agastya-vācā vasiṣṭho' pi brūte [10.69 padyād anantaram] ity antena agastya-labdhāśīrvādasya vasiṣṭha-vacana-saṃvādena sthirīkaraṇāt kṛtiḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>: 'For the word of a sage, even when uttered by different speakers, does not contradict itself — since <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> also says what <s>Agastya</s> said.' — Thus ending, because the blessing obtained from <s>Agastya</s> is confirmed by its agreement with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s words, this constitutes <s>kṛti</s>.

body.text:
atha bhāṣaṇam-
mānādyāptiś ca bhāṣaṇam ||SRs_3.169|| 73d
body.translated_text: Now <s>bhāṣaṇa</s> (discourse) — The attainment of honor and the like — that is <s>bhāṣaṇa</s>. ||SRs_3.169||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, vasiṣṭhaḥ-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same [play], <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> —

body.text:
rāmo dānta-daśānanaḥ kim aparaṃ sītā satīṣv agraṇīḥ
saumitriḥ sadṛśo' stu kasya samare yenedrajin nirjitaḥ |
kiṃ brūmo bharataṃ ca rāma-virahe tat-pādukārādhakaṃ
śatrughnaḥ kathito' grajasya ca guṇair vandyaṃ kuṭumbaṃ raghoḥ ||SRs_3.170|| [bā.rā. 10.102]
body.translated_text: '<s>Rāma</s>, tamer of the Ten-faced one — what more [need be said]? <s>Sītā</s>, foremost among chaste women; <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) — who is his equal, who conquered <s>Indrajit</s> in battle? What shall we say of <s>Bharata</s>, who worshipped <s>Rāma</s>'s sandals during his absence? <s>Śatrughna</s> is proclaimed by the virtues of his elder brother — the family of <s>Raghu</s> is worthy of veneration!' ||SRs_3.170|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.102]

body.text: ity atra vasiṣṭhena raghu-kuṭumbasya rāmacandrādi-sat-puruṣotpatti-sthānatayā tallakṣaṇa-bahu-māna-prāpti-kathanād bhāṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: Here, since <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> narrates the attainment of great honor by the family of <s>Raghu</s> as the birthplace of excellent persons like <s>Rāmacandra</s> and his defining qualities, this constitutes <s>bhāṣaṇa</s>.

body.text:
atha upagūhanam-
upagūhanam adbhuta-prāptiḥ ||170|| 74a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Upagūhana</s> (embrace/revelation of wonder) — <s>Upagūhana</s> is the attainment of something wondrous. ||3.170||

body.text:
yatha tatraiva, alakā-aho nu khalu bhoḥ pati-vratā-mayaṃ jyotiḥ anabhibhavanīyaṃ jyotir-antaraiḥ | yataḥ,
praviśantyā citācakraṃ jānakyā pariśuddhaye |
na bhedaḥ ko' pi nirṇītaḥ payasaḥ pāvakasya ca ||SRs_3.171|| [bā.rā. 10.9]
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], <s>Alakā</s> [says]: 'Ah, surely indeed! The light born of a devoted wife is a light that cannot be overpowered by other lights. For: When <s>Jānakī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) entered the funeral pyre for her purification, no distinction whatsoever was discerned between the water and the fire.' ||3.171|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.9]

body.text:
(vicintya) ity upakramya, nepathye-
yogīndraś ca narendraś ca yasyāḥ sa janakaḥ pitā |
viśuddhā rāma-gṛhiṇī babhau daśaratha-snuṣā ||SRs_3.172|| [bā.rā. 10.14]
body.translated_text: (Reflecting) — beginning thus, backstage — 'She whose father is <s>Janaka</s>, who is both a king of <s>Yogins</s> and a king of men — the purified wife of <s>Rāma</s>, the daughter-in-law of <s>Daśaratha</s>, shone forth.' ||3.172|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.14]

body.text: ity antena sītāyāḥ niḥśaṅka-jvalana-praveśa-nirapāya-nirgamana-rūpāścarya-kathanād upagūhanam |
body.translated_text: — thus ending. Since there is the narration of the wonder of <s>Sītā</s>'s fearless entry into the fire and her unharmed emergence, this is <s>Upagūhana</s>.

body.text:
atha pūrva-bhāvaḥ-
dṛṣṭa-krama-kāryasya syād dṛṣṭiḥ pūrva-bhāvas tu ||SRs_3.173|| 74b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Pūrva-bhāva</s> (foreshadowing) — <s>Pūrva-bhāva</s> is the perception of a matter whose sequence has been observed. ||3.173||

body.text: yathā tatraiva [10.102 padyād anantaram]-vatsa rāmabhadra praśasto muhūrto vartate | tad adhyāssva pitryaṃ siṃhāsanam ity upakramya, vasiṣṭhaḥ-rāmabhadra dhanyo' si | yasya te bhagavān kubero' rthī ity antena vasiṣṭhena rāmabhadrasyābhiṣekāṅgīkaraṇa-kubera-vimāna-pratyarpaṇa-rūpayor arthayor darśanāt pūrva-bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>, after verse 10.102] — 'Dear <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, an auspicious moment is at hand. Therefore, ascend the ancestral lion-throne' — beginning thus, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>: '<s>Rāmabhadra</s>, you are blessed. For the blessed <s>Kubera</s> himself seeks a favor from you' — thus ending. Since two matters are perceived — namely, <s>Rāmabhadra</s>'s acceptance of the coronation and the restoration of <s>Kubera</s>'s aerial chariot — this is <s>Pūrva-bhāva</s>.

body.text:
atha upasaṃhāraḥ-
dharmārthādy-upagamanād upasaṃhāraḥ kṛtārthatā-kathanam ||SRs_3.174|| 75a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion) — <s>Upasaṃhāra</s> is the statement of fulfillment through the attainment of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and the like. ||3.174||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, vasiṣṭhaḥ-vatsa rāmabhadra kiṃ te bhūyaḥ priyam upakaromi |
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>: 'Dear <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, what further kindness shall I do for you?'

body.text: rāmaḥ-kim ataḥ priyam asti |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>: 'What happiness could be greater than this?'

body.text:
rugṇaṃ cājagavaṃ na cāpi kupito bhargaḥ sura-grāmaṇīḥ
setuś ca grathitaḥ prasanna-madhuro dṛṣṭaś ca vārāṃ nidhiḥ |
paulastyaś caramaḥ sthitaś ca bhagavān prītaḥ śrutīnāṃ kaviḥ
prāptaṃ yānam idaṃ ca yācitavate dattaṃ kuberāya ca ||SRs_3.175|| [bā.rā. 10.104]
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Ājagava</s> bow is broken, and <s>Bharga</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) is not exceedingly angry; the chief of the gods (<s>Indra</s>) — the bridge is constructed; the gracious and sweet ocean has been seen; the descendant of <s>Paulastya</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) is in his final state; the blessed poet of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>Vālmīki</s>) is pleased; this vehicle [<s>Puṣpaka</s>] is obtained; and it has been given to <s>Kubera</s> who had requested it.' ||3.175|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.104]

body.text: ity atra rugṇaṃ cājagavaṃ ity anena bhūta-pati-dhanur dalanena sītādhigama-rūpakām aprāpteḥ paulasytaś caramaḥ sthitaḥ ity anena śaraṇāgata-rakṣaṇena dharma-prāpteḥ prāptaṃ yānam idaṃ cety atra vimāna-ratna-lābhenārtha-prāpteś ca na cāpi kupito bhargaḥ sura-grāmiṇīr ity ādibhiḥ pādānta-vākyaiḥ rāmacandreṇa sva-kṛtārthatā-kathanād upasaṃhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, 'the <s>Ājagava</s> bow is broken' — by the breaking of <s>Paśupati</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) bow, [stating] the attainment of <s>Kāma</s> in the form of winning <s>Sītā</s>; 'the descendant of <s>Paulastya</s> is in his final state' — by the protection of those who sought refuge, [stating] the attainment of <s>Dharma</s>; 'this vehicle is obtained' — by the acquisition of the jewel-chariot, [stating] the attainment of <s>Artha</s>; and through the remaining half-verse phrases such as 'nor is <s>Bharga</s> exceedingly angry,' the <s>Upasaṃhāra</s> consists of <s>Rāmacandra</s>'s statement of his own fulfillment.

body.text: kiṃ ca, rugṇaṃ cājagavaṃ setuś ca grathita ity ādibhyāṃ yuddhotsāha-siddheḥ paulastyaś caramaḥ sthitaḥ ity atra vibhīṣaṇasya pālanena dayā-vīra-siddheḥ yācitavate dattaṃ kuberāya cety anena dānavīra-siddheś ca rāmabhadreṇa svakṛtārthatā-kathanād vā upasaṃhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Moreover, from 'the <s>Ājagava</s> bow is broken' and 'the bridge is constructed,' the accomplishment of martial valor (<s>yuddhotsāha</s>) is established; from 'the descendant of <s>Paulastya</s> is in his final state,' through the protection of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, the accomplishment of the valor of compassion (<s>dayā-vīra</s>) is established; from 'it has been given to <s>Kubera</s> who had requested it,' the accomplishment of the valor of generosity (<s>dāna-vīra</s>) is established. Alternatively, through <s>Rāmabhadra</s>'s statement of his own fulfillment [in these terms], this is the <s>Upasaṃhāra</s>.

body.text:
atha praśastiḥ-
bharataiś carācarāṇām āśīr āśaṃsanaṃ praśastiḥ syāt ||SRs_3.176|| 75b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Praśasti</s> (benediction) — The blessing — the invocation of welfare upon all beings, moving and still — by the actors (<s>bharatas</s>) constitutes the <s>Praśasti</s>. ||3.176||

body.text: yathā tatraiva, tathā cedam astu bharata-vākyam-
body.translated_text: As in the same [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>], 'And thus let this be the <s>Bharata-vākya</s> (closing benediction)' —

body.text:
samyak saṃskārra-vidyā-viśadam upaniṣad-bhūtam arthādbhutānāṃ
grathnantu grantha-bandhaṃ vacanam anupatat-sūkti-mudrāḥ kavīndrāḥ |
santaḥ santarpitāntaḥ-karaṇam anuguṇaṃ brahmaṇaḥ kāvya-mūrtes
tat tattvaṃ sāttvikaiś ca prathama-piśunitaṃ bhāvayanto' rcayantu ||SRs_3.177|| [bā.rā. 10.105]
body.translated_text: 'May the foremost poets, whose seal is the unfailing felicitous expression, compose their literary works — lucid with properly refined learning, embodying the essence of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, filled with wondrous meanings! And may the virtuous, their inner faculties gratified, consonant with <s>Brahman</s> who is the poetic embodiment, worship and contemplate that very truth, first intimated by the <s>sāttvika</s> [mode]!' ||3.177|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 10.105]

body.text: ity atra kavīndrāṇāṃ nirdoṣa-sūkti-grathanāśaṃsanena bhāvakānāṃ ca tad-grantha-bhāvanāśaṃsanena ca sakala-vyavahāra-pravartaka-vāṅmaya-rūpa-jagan-maṅgala-kathanāt praśastir iti sarvaṃ praśastam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the invocation of the foremost poets' composition of faultless felicitous works, and of the devotees' contemplation of those works, and thus the proclamation of universal welfare through the literary expression that sets in motion all worldly activity, this is the <s>Praśasti</s>. Thus everything is auspicious.

body.text:
rasa-bhāvānurodhena prayojanam apekṣya ca |
sāphalyaṃ kāryam aṅgānām ity ācāryāḥ pracakṣate ||SRs_3.178|| 76
keṣāṃcid eṣām aṅgānāṃ vikalpaṃ kecid ūcire |
mukhādi-sandhiṣv aṅgānāṃ kramo' yaṃ na vivakṣitaḥ ||SRs_3.179|| 77
kramasyānādṛtatvena bharatādibhir ādimaiḥ |
lakṣyeṣu vyutkrameṇāpi kathanena vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||SRs_3.180|| 78
catuḥ-ṣaṣṭhi-kalā-marma-vedinā siṃha-bhūbhujā |
lakṣitā ca catuḥṣaṣṭhir bāla-rāmāyaṇe sphuṭam ||SRs_3.181|| 79
body.translated_text: 'The authorities say that the efficacy of the subsidiary elements [of the junctures] should be determined with regard to <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, and purpose.' ||3.178|| 'Some have spoken of optionality for certain of these subsidiary elements. The order of the subsidiary elements within the <s>Mukha</s> and other junctures is not to be insisted upon.' ||3.179|| 'Because the order has been disregarded by <s>Bharata</s> and other early authorities, and because the discerning have described them even in reversed order in exemplary works.' ||3.180|| 'By the king <s>Siṃha</s>, knower of the secrets of the sixty-four arts, the sixty-four [juncture-elements] have been clearly identified in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>.' ||3.181||

body.text:
atha sandhy-antarāṇi-
mukhādi-sandhiṣv aṅgānām aśaithilya-pratītaye |
sandhy-antarāṇi yojyāni tatra tatraikaviṃśatiḥ ||SRs_3.182|| 80
ācāryāntara-saṃmatyā camatkārodayād api |
vakṣye lakṣaṇam eteṣām udāhṛtim api sphuṭam ||SRs_3.183|| 81
sāma-dāne bheda-daṇḍau pratyutpanna-matir vadhaḥ |
gotra-skhalitam ojaś ca dhīḥ krodhaḥ sāhasaṃ bhayam ||SRs_3.184|| 82
māyā ca saṃvṛtir bhrāntir dūtyaṃ hetv-avadhāraṇam |
svapna-lekhau madaś citram ity etāny ekaviṃśatiḥ ||SRs_3.185|| 83
body.translated_text: Now, the inter-juncture elements (<s>Sandhy-antarāṇi</s>) — 'In the <s>Mukha</s> and other junctures, in order to ensure the tightness of the subsidiary elements, inter-juncture elements should be employed — twenty-one in number, here and there.' ||3.182|| 'With the approval of other authorities, and because they too produce aesthetic wonder, I shall state the definitions and clear illustrations of these.' ||3.183|| '<s>Sāma</s> (conciliation), <s>Dāna</s> (gift), <s>Bheda</s> (dissension), <s>Daṇḍa</s> (punishment), <s>Pratyutpanna-mati</s> (ready wit), <s>Vadha</s> (slaying), <s>Gotra-skhalita</s> (slip of name), <s>Ojas</s> (vigor), <s>Dhī</s> (resolve), <s>Krodha</s> (anger), <s>Sāhasa</s> (daring), <s>Bhaya</s> (fear), ||3.184|| <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), <s>Saṃvṛti</s> (concealment), <s>Bhrānti</s> (delusion), <s>Dūtya</s> (embassy), <s>Hetv-avadhāraṇa</s> (ascertainment of cause), <s>Svapna</s> (dream), <s>Lekha</s> (letter), <s>Mada</s> (intoxication), and <s>Citra</s> (marvel) — these are the twenty-one.' ||3.185||

body.text:
tatra sāma-
tatra sāma priyaṃ vākyaṃ svānuvṛtti-prakāśanam ||SRs_3.186|| 84a
body.translated_text: There, <s>Sāma</s> (conciliation) — <s>Sāma</s> is pleasant speech that reveals one's own compliance. ||3.186||

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre, rājā-aye na bhetavyam |
body.translated_text: As in <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s>, the King: 'Come, there is nothing to fear!'

body.text: mālavikā (sāvaṣṭambham)-jo ṇa bhāadi so mae bhaṭṭiṇī-daṃsaṇe diṭṭha-sāmattho bhaṭṭā | [yo na bibheti sa mayā bhaṭṭinī-darśane dṛṣṭa-sāmarthyo bhartā |]
body.translated_text: <s>Mālavikā</s> (with firm resolve): '[Prakrit:] He who does not fear — he is my master, whose prowess I have witnessed in the presence of the Queen!' [Sanskrit:] 'He who does not fear — he is my master, whose prowess I have witnessed in the Queen's presence!'

body.text:
rājā-
dākṣiṇyaṃ nāma bimboṣṭhi nāyakānāṃ kula-vratam |
tan me dīrghākṣi ye prāṇās te tvad-āśā-nibandhanāḥ ||SRs_3.187|| [mā.a.mi. 4.14]
body.translated_text: The King: 'O bimba-lipped one, graciousness is the hereditary vow of heroes. O long-eyed one, those very life-breaths of mine are bound to the hope of you.' ||3.187|| [<s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 4.14]

body.text: ity atra rājño vacanaṃ nāma |
body.translated_text: Here, the King's speech is the [inter-juncture element called] <s>Sāma</s>.

body.text:
atha dānaṃ-
dānam ātma-pratinidhir bhūṣaṇādi-samarpaṇam ||SRs_3.188|| 84b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Dāna</s> (gift) — <s>Dāna</s> is the offering of ornaments and the like as a proxy for oneself. ||3.188||

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave, mālatī-pia-sahi sabbadā sumaridabbahmi | esā bi māhaba-sahatthaṇimmāṇamaṇoharā baula-mālā māladī-ṇibbisesaṃ pia-sahīe daṭṭabbā | sabbadā hiaeṇa a dhāraṇijjā iti | [priya-sakhi ! sarvadā smartavyāsmi | eṣā ca mādhava-sva-hasta-nirmāṇa-manoharā bakula-mālā mālatī-nirviśeṣaṃ priya-sakhyā draṣṭavyā | sarvadā hṛdayena ca dhāraṇiyā iti |] (iti svakaṇṭhād unmucya mādhavasya kaṇṭhe vinyasyantī sahasāpasṛtya sādhvasotkampaṃ nāṭayati |) [6.11 padyād anantaram] |
body.translated_text: As in <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s>, <s>Mālatī</s> [says in Prakrit]: 'Dear friend, you must always remember me! And this <s>bakula</s>-garland, made beautiful by <s>Mādhava</s>'s own hand, should be regarded by you, my dear friend, as no different from <s>Mālatī</s> herself. It should always be worn close to your heart.' [Sanskrit rendering:] 'Dear friend, you must always remember me! And this <s>bakula</s>-garland, made beautiful by <s>Mādhava</s>'s own hand, should be regarded by you, my dear friend, as no different from <s>Mālatī</s> herself. It should always be worn close to your heart.' (Removing it from her own neck and placing it on <s>Mādhava</s>'s neck, she suddenly withdraws, acting out trembling from alarm.) [After verse 6.11]

body.text: atra mālatyā martukāmāyāḥ pratinidhitayā lavaṅgikāyāṃ bakulamālā-samarpaṇaṃ dānam |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Mālatī</s>, who is about to die, offers the <s>bakula</s>-garland to <s>Lavaṅgikā</s> as her proxy — this is <s>Dāna</s>.

body.text:
atha bhedaḥ-
bhedas tu kapaṭālāpaiḥ suhṛdāṃ bheda-kalpanam ||SRs_3.189|| 85a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Bheda</s> (dissension) — <s>Bheda</s> is the contrivance of a rift among friends through deceitful speech. ||3.189||

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave, kāmandakī-
body.translated_text: As in <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s>, <s>Kāmandakī</s> [says] —

body.text:
rājñaḥ priyāya suhṛde sacivāya kāryād
dattvātmajāṃ bhavatu nirvṛtimānamātyaḥ |
durdarśanena ghaṭatāmiyam apy anena
dhūma-graheṇa vimalā śaśinaḥ kaleva ||SRs_3.190|| [mā.mā. 2.8]
body.translated_text: 'Let the minister attain contentment by giving his own daughter, out of duty, to the king's dear friend and counselor. And let this one too achieve [her aim] through the difficult sight of him — like the stainless crescent of the moon [shining despite] the comet.' ||3.190|| [<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 2.8]

body.text: mālatī (svagatam)-hā tāda tumaṃ bi ṇāma mama ebbaṃ ti sabbahā jidaṃ bhoatihṇāe | [hā tāta tvam api nāma mamaivam iti sarvathā jitaṃ bhoga-tṛṣṇayā |] ity atra kāmandakyā mālatī-taj-janakayor bheda-kalpanaṃ bhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Mālatī</s> (aside): '[Prakrit:] Ah, father! Even you indeed — that this should be so for me — [you are] utterly conquered by the craving for enjoyment!' [Sanskrit:] 'Ah, father! Even you indeed treat me thus — utterly conquered by the craving for enjoyment!' Here, <s>Kāmandakī</s>'s contrivance of a rift between <s>Mālatī</s> and her father is the <s>Bheda</s>.

body.text:
atha daṇḍaḥ-
daṇḍas tv avinayādīnāṃ dṛṣṭyā śrutyātha tarjanam ||SRs_3.191|| 85b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Daṇḍa</s> (punishment) — <s>Daṇḍa</s> is threatening upon seeing or hearing of improper conduct. ||3.191||

body.text: dṛṣṭyā, yathā mālatī-mādhave, mādhavaḥ-re re pāpa !
body.translated_text: By seeing, as in <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s>, <s>Mādhava</s> [cries]: 'Ho, ho, villain!'

body.text:
praṇayi-sakhī-salīla-parihāsa-rasādhigatair
lalita-śirīṣa-puṣpa-hananair api tāmyati yat |
vapuṣi vadhāya tatra tava śastram upakṣipataḥ
patatu śirasy akāṇḍayam adaṇḍa ivaiṣa bhujaḥ ||SRs_3.192|| [mā.mā. 5.31]
body.translated_text: 'She whose body suffers even from the blows of delicate <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers, playfully [thrown] by her affectionate friends — upon that very body, where you would cast a weapon for slaughter, may this arm of mine, like an unprovoked thunderbolt, fall upon your head!' ||3.192|| [<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 5.31]

body.text: atrāghora-ghaṇṭasyāvinaya-darśanena mādhava-kṛta-tarjanaṃ daṇḍaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Mādhava</s>'s threatening upon seeing the improper conduct of <s>Aghoraghaṇṭa</s> is <s>Daṇḍa</s>.

body.text: śrutyā, yathā śākuntale, rājā (sahasopasṛtya)-
body.translated_text: By hearing, as in <s>Śākuntala</s>, the King (rushing forward suddenly) —

body.text:
kaḥ paurave vasumatīṃ śāsati śāsitari durvinītānām |
ayam ācaraty avinayaṃ mugdhāsu taspasvi-kanyāsu ||SRs_3.193|| [a.śa. 1.21]
body.translated_text: 'When the ruler of the <s>Paurava</s> dynasty governs the earth as the chastiser of the ill-mannered — who is it that commits this impropriety against these innocent ascetic maidens?' ||3.193|| [<s>Abhijñāna-śākuntala</s> 1.21]

body.text: atrāvinaya-śrutyā duṣyantena kṛtaṃ tarjanaṃ daṇḍaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Duṣyanta</s>'s threatening upon hearing of improper conduct is <s>Daṇḍa</s>.

body.text:
atha pratyutpanna-matiḥ-
tāt-kālikī ca pratibhā pratyutpanna-matir smṛtā ||SRs_3.194|| 86a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Pratyutpanna-mati</s> (ready wit) — Spontaneous presence of mind at the moment is known as <s>Pratyutpanna-mati</s>. ||3.194||

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre, rājā-na khalu mudrām adhikṛtya bravīmi | etayor baddhayoḥ [mālavikā-bakulāvalikayoḥ] kiṃ-nimitto mokṣaḥ | kiṃ devyāḥ parijanam atikramya bhavān sandiṣṭaḥ ity evam anayā [mādhavikayā] praṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: As in <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s>, the King: 'I am not speaking with reference to the signet ring. What is the reason for releasing these two prisoners [<s>Mālavikā</s> and <s>Bakulāvalikā</s>]? Did you go beyond the Queen's attendants and receive direct orders [from her]?' — thus [<s>Mādhavikā</s>] is to be questioned.

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-ṇaṃ pucchido hmi | puṇo mandassa bi me tasmiṃ pañcuppaṇṇā madī āsi | [nanu pṛṣṭo' smi | punar mandassyāpi me tasmin pratyutpannā matir āsīt |]
body.translated_text: The <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester): '[Prakrit:] Indeed I was questioned! And again, even to a fool like me, ready wit arose on that occasion!' [Sanskrit:] 'Indeed I was questioned! And again, even to a fool like me, ready wit arose on that occasion!'

body.text: rājā-kathyatām |
body.translated_text: The King: 'Let it be told!'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-bhaṇidaṃ mae, debbaciṃtaehiṃ viṇṇāvido rāā | sobasaggaṃ bo ṇakkhattaṃ tā avassaṃ sabba-bandha-mokkho karīadutti | [bhaṇitaṃ mayā, daiva-cintakair vijñāpito rājā | sopasargaṃ vo nakṣatram | tad avaśyaṃ sarva-bandha-mokṣaḥ kriyatām iti |]
body.translated_text: The <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: '[Prakrit:] I said: "The astrologers have informed the King. Your star has a malefic conjunction. Therefore all prisoners must absolutely be released!"' [Sanskrit:] 'I said: "The astrologers have informed the King. Your star has a malefic conjunction. Therefore all prisoners must absolutely be released!"'

body.text: rājā (saharṣaṃ)-tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: The King (joyfully): 'And then? And then?'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-taṃ suṇia devīe irāvadī-cittaṃ rakkhaṃtīe rāā kila moedi tti ahaṃ saṃdiṭṭho tti tado jujjadi tti tāe ibbaṃ saṃpādido attho | [tat śrutvā devyā irāvatī-cittaṃ rakṣantyā rājā kila mocayatīty ahaṃ sandiṣṭa iti | tato yujyate iti tayaiva sampādito' rthaḥ |]
body.translated_text: The <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: '[Prakrit:] Hearing that, the Queen, protecting <s>Irāvatī</s>'s feelings — "The King is releasing [them]," she said — and I was commissioned [to do it]. Thus it was justified, and by her alone the matter was accomplished.' [Sanskrit:] 'Hearing that, the Queen, protecting <s>Irāvatī</s>'s feelings — "The King is releasing them" — I was commissioned. Thus it was justified, and by her alone the matter was accomplished.'

body.text: rājā (vidūṣakaṃ pariṣvajya)-sakhe ! priyo' haṃ khalu tava | [4.5 padyād anantaraṃ]
body.translated_text: The King (embracing the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>): 'Friend, I am indeed dear to you!' [After verse 4.5]

body.text: ity atra vidūṣakasya samucitottara-pratibhā pratyutpanna-matiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>'s appropriate and spontaneous reply is <s>Pratyutpanna-mati</s> (ready wit).

body.text:
atha vadhaḥ-
vadhas tu jīvita-droha-kriyā syād ātatāyinaḥ ||SRs_3.195|| 86b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vadha</s> (slaying) — <s>Vadha</s> is the act of assailing the life of an assailant. ||3.195||

body.text: yathā veṇī-saṃhāre [6.44 padyād anantaram], kṛṣṇaḥ-ahaṃ punaś cārvākeṇa rakṣasā vyākulīkṛtaṃ bhavantam upalabhyārjunena saha tvaritataram āyātaḥ |
body.translated_text: As in <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> [after verse 6.44], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'And I, upon learning that you had been thrown into confusion by the <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Cārvāka</s>, came here in great haste together with <s>Arjuna</s>.'

body.text: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ-kiṃ nāma cārvākeṇa rakṣasā vayam evaṃ vipralabdhāḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>: 'Were we indeed so deceived by the <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Cārvāka</s>?'

body.text: bhīmaḥ (sa-roṣam)-bhagavan kvāsau dhārtarāṣṭra-sakho rākṣasaś cārvāko yenāryasya mahāṃś citta-vibhramaḥ kṛtaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s> (angrily): 'Reverend sir, where is that <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Cārvāka</s>, friend of the son of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, who caused such great mental confusion in the noble one?'

body.text: kṛṣṇaḥ-nigṛhītaḥ sa durātmā nakulena |
body.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'That wicked one has been seized by <s>Nakula</s>.'

body.text: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ-priyaṃ naḥ, priyaṃ naḥ | ity atra cārvāka-nigraho vadhaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>: 'This is pleasing to us, pleasing to us!' — Here, the seizure [and killing] of <s>Cārvāka</s> is <s>Vadha</s>.

body.text:
atha gotra-skhalitam-
tad gotra-skhalitaṃ yat tu nāma-vyatyaya-bhāṣaṇam ||SRs_3.196|| 87a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Gotra-skhalita</s> (slip of name) — <s>Gotra-skhalita</s> is the utterance of a transposed name. ||3.196||

body.text: yathā vikramorvaśīye [tṛtīyāṅke ādau] (tataḥ praviśato bharata-śiṣyau) prathamaḥ-aye sadoṣāvakāśa iva te vākya-śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: As in <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> [at the beginning of the third act] — (Enter two pupils of <s>Bharata</s>) First: 'Indeed, the remainder of your sentence seems to contain a flaw.'

body.text: dvitīyaḥ-ām | tarhi ubbasīe baaṇaṃ pamāda-kkhalidaṃ āsi | [āṃ, tatra urvasyā vacanaṃ pramāda-skhalitam āsīt |]
body.translated_text: Second: '[Prakrit:] Yes, there <s>Urvaśī</s>'s utterance was a slip of inadvertence.' [Sanskrit:] 'Yes, there <s>Urvaśī</s>'s utterance was a slip of inadvertence.'

body.text: prathamaḥ-katham iva ?
body.translated_text: First: 'How so?'

body.text: dvitīyaḥ-lacchī-bhūmiāe baṭṭamāṇā ubbasī vāruṇī-bhūmiāe baṭṭamāṇāe meṇaāe pucchidā | sahi samāadā ede tellokka-purisā sakesavā loa-bālā | kadamassiṃ de bhāvāhiṇibesotti [lakṣmī-bhūmikāyāṃ vartamānā urvaśī vāruṇī-bhūmikāyāṃ vartamānayā menakayā pṛṣṭā | sakhi samāgatā ete trailokya-puruṣāḥ sa-keśavā loka-pālāḥ | katamasmiiṃs te bhāvābhinibeśaḥ ? iti |]
body.translated_text: Second [actor (in the role of <s>Urvaśī</s> on the stage of <s>Lakṣmī</s>)]: '<s>Urvaśī</s>, playing the role of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, was asked by <s>Menakā</s>, who was playing the role of <s>Vāruṇī</s>: "Friend, these lords of the three worlds have assembled — <s>Keśava</s> and the World-Protectors. In which one is your heart's inclination?"'

body.text: prathamaḥ--tatas tataḥ ?
body.translated_text: First [actor]: 'And then?'

body.text: dvitīyaḥ-tado tāe purisottame tti bhaṇidabbe purūravasi tti ṇiggadā bāṇī | [tatas tasyāḥ puruṣottama iti bhaṇitavye purūravasīti nirgatā bāṇī |] ity atra nāma-vyatikramaḥ sphuṭa eva |
body.translated_text: Second: 'Then, when she should have said "<s>Puruṣottama</s>" (the Supreme Person), the word "<s>Purūravas</s>" escaped her lips.' Here the slip of names is plainly evident.

body.text:
atha aujaḥ-
ojas tu vāg-upanyāso nija-śakti-prakāśakaḥ ||SRs_3.197|| 87b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Ojas</s> (vigor) — <s>Ojas</s> is a verbal expression that manifests one's own power. ||3.197|| 87b

body.text: yathā uttara-rāma-carite, kuśaḥ-sakhe daṇḍāyana !
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> — <s>Kuśa</s>: 'Friend <s>Daṇḍāyana</s>!

body.text:
āyuṣmataḥ kila lavasya narendra-sainyair
āyodhanaṃ nanu kim āttha sakhe tatheti |
adyāstam etu bhuvaneṣu sa rāja-śabdaḥ
kṣattrasya śastra-śikhinaḥ śamam adya yāntu ||SRs_3.198|| [u.rā.ca. 6.16]
body.translated_text: 'The blessed <s>Lava</s>, they say, has engaged in battle with the king's armies — friend, do you say it is so? Then let the title "king" set today throughout the worlds; let the fire-weapons of the warrior class come to rest today!' ||3.198|| [<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 6.16]

body.text: ity atra ojaḥ spaṣṭam eva |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Ojas</s> is plainly evident.

body.text:
atha dhīḥ-
iṣṭārtha-siddhi-paryantā cintā dhīr iti kathyate ||SRs_3.199|| 88a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Dhī</s> (deliberation) — The thought directed toward the accomplishment of a desired aim is called <s>Dhī</s>. ||3.199|| 88a

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre caturthāṅke [4.2 padyād anantaram] rājā (niśvasya saparāmarśam)-sakhe kim atra kartavyam ?
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s>, in the fourth act (after verse 4.2) — the King (sighing, with deliberation): 'Friend, what should be done here?'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ (vicintya)-atthi ettha ubāo | [asty atropāyaḥ |]
body.translated_text: The <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (reflecting): 'There is a remedy here.'

body.text: rāja-kim iva ?
body.translated_text: The King: 'What kind?'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ (sa-dṛṣṭi-kṣepam)-ko bi adiṭṭho suṇissad | kaṇṇe de kahemi (ity upaśliṣya karṇe) evaṃ bia | [ko' py adṛṣṭaḥ śroṣyati | karṇe te kathayāmi | evam iva | ] ity āvedayati |
body.translated_text: The <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (with a sidelong glance): 'Some unseen person might hear! Let me tell you in your ear.' (Leaning close to his ear) 'Like this...' — he explains.

body.text: rājā saharṣaṃ-suṣṭhu prayujyatāṃ siddhaye | ity atra vidūṣakeṇa dhāriṇī-hasta-maṇi-mudrikākarṣāṇa-hetu-bhūtasya bhujaga-viṣa-vega-kapaṭasya cintanaṃ dhīḥ |
body.translated_text: The King (joyfully): 'Very well, let it be put into practice for success!' Here, the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>'s devising of the stratagem of feigning a snake-poison attack as a means to seize <s>Dhāriṇī</s>'s hand-seal ring is <s>Dhī</s>.

body.text:
atha krodhaḥ-
krodhas tu cetaso dīptir aparādhādi-darśanāt ||SRs_3.200|| 88b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Krodha</s> (wrath) — <s>Krodha</s> is the flaring of the mind from seeing an offence and the like. ||3.200|| 88b

body.text: yathā ratnāvalyāṃ tṛtīyāṅke [ante 3.19 padyāt pūrvam], vāsavadattā-hañje kaṃcaṇamāle edeṇa ebba ladāpāseṇa bandhia gehaṇa eṇaṃ bahmaṇaṃ | eṇaṃ duṭṭha-kaṇṇaāṃ a aggado karehi | [hañje kañcanamāle etenaiva latā-pāśena baddhvā gṛhāṇainaṃ brāhmaṇam | imāṃ duṣṭa-kanyakāṃ cāgrataḥ kuru |] ity atra vāsavadattāyāḥ roṣaḥ krodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, in the third act (before verse 3.19) — <s>Vāsavadattā</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Girl <s>Kañcanamālā</s>! Bind this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with this very creeper-noose and seize him! And place this wicked girl before [me]!' Here the anger of <s>Vāsavadattā</s> is <s>Krodha</s>.

body.text:
atha sāhasam-
sva-jīvita-nirākāṅkṣo vyāpāraḥ sāhasaṃ bhavet ||SRs_3.201|| 89a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Sāhasa</s> (reckless daring) — An action performed with disregard for one's own life is <s>Sāhasa</s>. ||3.201|| 89a

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> —

body.text: aśastra-pātam avyāja-puruṣāṅgopakalpitam |[*19]
body.translated_text: 'Without the fall of weapons, genuinely prepared from a man's own limbs,

body.text:
vikrīyate mahā-māṃsaṃ gṛhyatāṃ gṛhyatām idam ||SRs_3.202|| [mā.mā. 5.12]
[*19] sva-śastra-pūta-nirvyāja-puruṣāṅgopakalpitam iti mudrita-mālatī-mādhava-pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: great flesh is being sold — take it, take it!' ||3.202|| [<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 5.12]

body.text: atra mādhavasya mahā-māṃsa-vikraya-vyāpāraḥ sāhasam |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Mādhava</s>'s act of selling great flesh [his own body] is <s>Sāhasa</s>.

body.text:
atha bhayam-
bhayaṃ tv ākasmika-trāsaḥ ||SRs_3.203|| 89b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Bhaya</s> (terror) — <s>Bhaya</s> is sudden fright. ||3.203|| 89b

body.text: yathā abhirāma-rāghave dvitīyāṅke, (praviśyāpaṭī-kṣepeṇa sambhrāntaḥ) baṭuḥ-ayya parittāahi parittāahi | accahide paḍido hmi | [ārya paritrāhi paritrāhi | atyāhite patito' smi |] (ity abhidravati) ity ādau baṭu-trāso bhayam |
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s>, in the second act — (entering with a tossing of the curtain, alarmed) the young student: 'Sir, save me, save me! I have fallen into a terrible calamity!' (He runs toward [the other]) — here the fright of the young student is <s>Bhaya</s>.

body.text:
atha māyā-
māyā kaitava-kalpanā ||SRs_3.204|| 89c
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) — <s>Māyā</s> is a deceitful contrivance. ||3.204|| 89c

body.text: yathā ratnāvalyāṃ, rājā (āsanād avatīrya)-devi paśya-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> — the King (descending from his seat): 'My Queen, behold —

body.text:
eṣa brahmā saroje rajanikara-kalā-śekharaḥ śaṅkaro' yaṃ dorbhir daityāntako' sau sa-dhanur-asi-gadā-cakra-cihnaiś caturbhiḥ |
eṣo' py airāvatasthas tridaśapatir amī devi devās tathānye nṛtyanti vyomni caitāś cala-caraṇa-raṇan-nūpurā divya-nāryaḥ ||SRs_3.205|| [ra. 4.11]
body.translated_text: 'Here is <s>Brahmā</s> on his lotus; this is <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) with the crescent-moon crest; that one is the slayer of demons (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) with his four arms bearing the signs of bow, sword, mace, and discus; and this one on <s>Airāvata</s> is the lord of the thirty gods (<s>Indra</s>); these, O Queen, are the other gods; and these divine women dance in the sky with tinkling anklets on their moving feet!' ||3.205|| [<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 4.11]

body.text: ity atra aindrajālika-kalpitaṃ kaitavaṃ māyā |
body.translated_text: Here, the deception contrived by the conjurer is <s>Māyā</s>.

body.text:
atra saṃvṛttiḥ-
saṃvṛttiḥ svayam uktasya svayam pracchādanaṃ bhavet ||SRs_3.206|| 90a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Saṃvṛtti</s> (concealment) — <s>Saṃvṛtti</s> is the self-concealment of what one has oneself uttered. ||3.206|| 90a

body.text: yathā śākuntale, rājā (svagatam)-aticapalo' yaṃ baṭuḥ | kadācid imāṃ kathām antaḥ-purebhyaḥ kathayet | bhavatu | enam eva vakṣye-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Śākuntala</s> — the King (aside): 'This young student is too indiscreet; he might sometime tell this story to the inner chambers. Very well, I shall say this to him —

body.text:
kva vayaṃ kva parokṣa-manmatho
mṛgaśāvaiḥ samam edhito janaḥ |
parihāsa-vijalpitaṃ sakhe
paramārthena na gṛhyatāṃ vacaḥ ||SRs_3.207|| [a.śa. 2.18]
body.translated_text: 'Where am I? Where is a person nurtured among fawns, in whom love is hidden? Friend, do not take my words, which are mere playful chatter, as meant in earnest!' ||3.207|| [<s>Abhijñāna-śākuntala</s> 2.18]

body.text: atra duṣyantena svayam uktasya śakuntalā-prasaṅgasya svayaṃ pracchādanaṃ saṃvṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Duṣyanta</s>'s self-concealment of the topic of <s>Śakuntalā</s> that he himself had raised is <s>Saṃvṛtti</s>.

body.text:
atha bhrāntiḥ-
bhrāntir viparyaya-jñānaṃ prasaṅgasya hy aniścayāt ||SRs_3.208|| 90b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Bhrānti</s> (erroneous perception) — <s>Bhrānti</s> is reversed knowledge arising from the uncertainty of the context. ||3.208|| 90b

body.text: yathā veṇī-saṃhāre dvitīyāṅke [2.10 padyād anantaraṃ], bhānumatī-tado ahaṃ tassa adisaidadibba-rūbiṇo ṇaulassa daṃsaṇeṇa ucchuā jādā hida-hiaā a | tado ujjhia taṃ āsanaṭṭhāṇaṃ ladā-maṇḍapaṃ pabisiduṃ āraddhā | [tato' haṃ tasyātiśayita-divya-rūpiṇo makulasya darśanenotsukā jātā hṛta-hṛdayā ca | tata ujjhitvā tadāsana-sthānaṃ latā-maṇḍapaṃ praveṣṭum ārabdhā |]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s>, in the second act (after verse 2.10) — <s>Bhānumatī</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Then, having become eager and captivated in heart by seeing that <s>Nakula</s> of exceedingly divine beauty, I abandoned my seat and began to enter the bower of creepers.'

body.text: rājā (savailakṣyam)-kiṃ nāmātiśayita-divya-rūpiṇo nakulasya darcānenotsukā jātā | hṛta-hṛdayā ca | tat katham anayā pāpayā mādrī-sutānuraktayā vayam evaṃ vipralabdhāḥ | mūrkha duryodhana kulaṭā-vipralabhyamānam ātmānaṃ bahu manyamāno' dhunā kiṃ vakṣyasi | (kiṃ kaṇṭhe śithilīkṛta [ve.saṃ. 2.9] ity ādi paṭhitvā diśo' valokya) aho etad artham evāsyāḥ prātar eva vivikta-sthānābhilāṣaḥ sakhī-jana-saṅkathāsu ca pakṣa-pātaḥ | duryodhanas tu mohād avijñāta-bandhakī-hṛdaya-sāraḥ kvāpi paribhrāntaḥ | ity atra devī-svapnasya aniścayād duryodhanasya viparīta-jñānaṃ bhrāntiḥ |
body.translated_text: The King (<s>Duryodhana</s>) (with embarrassment): 'What? She became eager to see <s>Nakula</s>, who is of exceedingly divine beauty? And captivated in heart? So how have I been thus deceived by this sinful woman, who is enamored of <s>Mādrī</s>'s son? Fool, <s>Duryodhana</s>! You who think highly of yourself, deceived by a harlot — what will you say now?' (Reciting 'Why has the necklace been loosened at the throat?' etc., and looking in all directions) 'Ah! So that is why she has been desiring secluded places since morning and showing partiality in conversations with her female friends! But <s>Duryodhana</s>, deluded, ignorant of the true nature of a courtesan's heart, has been wandering about somewhere!' — Here, the reversed knowledge of <s>Duryodhana</s> arising from the uncertainty of the Queen's dream is <s>Bhrānti</s>.

body.text:
atha māyā-
māyā kaitava-kalpanā ||SRs_3.209|| 89c
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) — <s>Māyā</s> is a deceitful contrivance. ||3.209|| 89c

body.text: yathā veṇī-saṃhāre dvitīyāṅke [2.10 padyād anantaraṃ], bhānumatī-tado ahaṃ tassa adisaidadibba-rūbiṇo ṇaulassa daṃsaṇeṇa ucchuā jādā hida-hiaā a | tado ujjhia taṃ āsanaṭṭhāṇaṃ ladā-maṇḍapaṃ pabisiduṃ āraddhā | [tato' haṃ tasyātiśayita-divya-rūpiṇo makulasya darśanenotsukā jātā hṛta-hṛdayā ca | tata ujjhitvā tadāsana-sthānaṃ latā-maṇḍapaṃ praveṣṭum ārabdhā |]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s>, in the second act (after verse 2.10) — <s>Bhānumatī</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Then, having become eager and captivated in heart by seeing that <s>Nakula</s> of exceedingly divine beauty, I abandoned my seat and began to enter the bower of creepers.'

body.text: rājā (savailakṣyam)-kiṃ nāmātiśayita-divya-rūpiṇo nakulasya darcānenotsukā jātā | hṛta-hṛdayā ca | tat katham anayā pāpayā mādrī-sutānuraktayā vayam evaṃ vipralabdhāḥ | mūrkha duryodhana kulaṭā-vipralabhyamānam ātmānaṃ bahu manyamāno' dhunā kiṃ vakṣyasi | (kiṃ kaṇṭhe śithilīkṛta [ve.saṃ. 2.9] ity ādi paṭhitvā diśo' valokya) aho etad artham evāsyāḥ prātar eva vivikta-sthānābhilāṣaḥ sakhī-jana-saṅkathāsu ca pakṣa-pātaḥ | duryodhanas tu mohād avijñāta-bandhakī-hṛdaya-sāraḥ kvāpi paribhrāntaḥ | ity atra devī-svapnasya aniścayād duryodhanasya viparīta-jñānaṃ bhrāntiḥ |
body.translated_text: The King (<s>Duryodhana</s>) (with embarrassment): 'What? She became eager to see <s>Nakula</s>, who is of exceedingly divine beauty? And captivated in heart? So how have I been thus deceived by this sinful woman, who is enamored of <s>Mādrī</s>'s son? Fool, <s>Duryodhana</s>! You who think highly of yourself, deceived by a harlot — what will you say now?' (Reciting 'Why has the necklace been loosened at the throat?' etc., and looking in all directions) 'Ah! So that is why she has been desiring secluded places since morning and showing partiality in conversations with her female friends! But <s>Duryodhana</s>, deluded, ignorant of the true nature of a courtesan's heart, has been wandering about somewhere!' — Here, the reversed knowledge of <s>Duryodhana</s> arising from the uncertainty of the Queen's dream is <s>Bhrānti</s>.

body.text:
atha dūtyam-
dūtyaṃ tu sahakāritvaṃ durghaṭe kārya-vastuni ||SRs_3.214|| 91a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Dūtya</s> (assistance) — <s>Dūtya</s> is cooperating in an affair that is difficult to accomplish. ||3.214|| 91a

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre [tṛtīyāṅke] vidūṣakaḥ-alaṃ bhavado dhīradaṃ ujjhia paridebideṇa | diṭṭhā kkhu mae tattahodīe mālabiāe piasahī baulābaliā | suṇābidāa maha jaṃ bhavadā saṃdiṭṭhaṃ | [alaṃ bhavato dhīratāṃ ujjhitvā paridevitena | dṛṣṭā khalu mayā tatra-bhavatyā mālavikāyāḥ priya-sakhī bakulāvalikā | śrāvitā ca mayā yad bhavatā sandiṣṭam] [3.1 padyād anantaram] rājā-tataḥ kim uktavatī |
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> [third act] — the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Enough of lamenting, abandoning your composure, sir! For I have seen <s>Bakulāvalikā</s>, the dear friend of Her Honor <s>Mālavikā</s>. And I have communicated to her what was instructed by you.' (After verse 3.1) The King: 'And then, what did she say?'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-vijñāpaya bhaṭṭārakamà tathāpi ghaṭayiṣyāmi iti | atra ca bakulāvalikayā mālavikāgnimitrayor ghaṭane sahakāritvam aṅgīkṛtam iti dūtyam |
body.translated_text: The <s>Vidūṣaka</s>: 'Inform His Majesty that even so I shall arrange it.' Here, since <s>Bakulāvalikā</s> has accepted the role of cooperating in bringing <s>Mālavikā</s> and <s>Agnimitra</s> together, this is <s>Dūtya</s>.

body.text:
atha hetv-avadhāraṇam-
niścayo hetunārthasya mataṃ hetv-avadhāraṇam ||SRs_3.215|| 91b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Hetvavadhāraṇa</s> (determination by reason) — The ascertainment of a matter by means of a reason is considered <s>Hetvavadhāraṇa</s>. ||3.215|| 91b

body.text: yathā śākuntale, rājā-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Śākuntala</s> — the King:

body.text:
strīṇām aśikṣita-paṭutvam amānuṣīṣu
sandṛśyate kim uta yāḥ pratibodhavatyaḥ |
prāg antarikṣa-gamanāt svam apatya-jātam
anyair dvijaiḥ para-bhṛtāḥ khalu poṣayanti ||SRs_3.216|| [a.śa. 5.22]
body.translated_text: 'Even among non-human women, an untaught cleverness is observed — how much more then in those who are endowed with intelligence! Before flying through the sky, the <s>parabhṛta</s> (cuckoo) birds indeed have their offspring raised by other birds.' ||3.216|| [<s>Abhijñāna-śākuntala</s> 5.22]

body.text: atra para-bhṛtānidarśanopabṛṃhitena strītva-hetunā mṛṣā-bhāṣaṇa-lakṣaṇasyārthasya niścayo hetv-avadhāraṇam |
body.translated_text: Here, the ascertainment of the matter characterized as false speech, supported by the illustration of the cuckoo, through the reason of womanhood, is <s>Hetvavadhāraṇa</s>.

body.text:
atha svapnaḥ-
svapno nidrāntare mantra-bheda-kṛd vacanaṃ matam ||SRs_3.217|| 92a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Svapna</s> (dream-talk) — <s>Svapna</s> is considered to be speech during sleep that betrays a secret. ||3.217|| 92a

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre [4.15 padyād anantaram] vidūṣakaḥ (utsvapnāyate)-bhodi mālabie ! [bhavati mālike !]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> (after verse 4.15) — the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (talking in his sleep): 'O Lady <s>Mālavikā</s>!'

body.text: nipuṇikā-sudaṃ bhaṭṭiṇīe | kassa eso attaṇioa-saṃpādaṇ vissasaṇijjo hadāso | sabba-kālaṃ ido ebba sotthibāaṇa-modaehiṃ kucchiṃ pūria saṃpadaṃ mālabiaṃ ussibiṇābedi | [śrutaṃ bhaṭṭanyā | kasyaiva ātma-niyoga-sampādane viśvasanīyo hatāśaḥ | sarva-kālam ita eva svasti-vācana-modakaiḥ kukṣiṃ pūrayitvā sāmprataṃ mālavikām utsvapnāyate |]
body.translated_text: <s>Nipuṇikā</s> [in Prakrit]: 'The Queen has heard! Who is this hopeless one to be trusted with accomplishing a personal commission? All the time, having stuffed his belly with auspicious-ceremony sweets from right here, he now dreams aloud about <s>Mālavikā</s>!'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-irāvadiṃ adikkamaṃtī hohi | [irāvatīm atikrāmantī bhava |]
body.translated_text: The <s>Vidūṣaka</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Be the one who crosses the <s>Irāvatī</s> river!'

body.text: ity atra vidūṣakasyotsvapnāyitaṃ svapnaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the talking in sleep by the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> is <s>Svapna</s>.

body.text:
atha lekhaḥ-
vivakṣitārtha-kalitā patrikā lekha īritaḥ ||SRs_3.218|| 92b
body.translated_text: Now Lekha (letter) — a missive composed with a desired meaning is called a Lekha. ||SRs_3.218||

body.text: yathā vikramorvaśīye [2.11 padyād anantaram] rājā (vibhāvya)-sakhe ! bhūrja-patra-gato' yam akṣara-vinyāsaḥ | ity ārabhya,
body.translated_text: As in Vikramorvaśīya (after verse 2.11), the King (examining): 'Friend! This is an arrangement of letters inscribed on birch-bark.' Beginning thus,

body.text: rājā-vayasya aṅguli-svedena dūṣyerann akṣarāṇi | dhāryatām ayaṃ priyāyāḥ sva-hasta-lekhaḥ | ity atra urvaśī-prahita-patrikārtho lekhaḥ |
body.translated_text: The King: 'Friend, the letters would be spoiled by the sweat of the fingers. Keep this letter written in the beloved's own hand.' — Here, the content of the missive sent by Urvaśī constitutes Lekha.

body.text:
atha madaḥ-
madas tu madyajaḥ ||SRs_3.219|| 93a
body.translated_text: Now Mada (intoxication) — Mada is that produced by wine. ||SRs_3.219||

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre [3.12 padyād anantaram] (tataḥ praviśati yukta-madā irāvatī ceṭī ca) ity atrerāvatī-madaḥ |
body.translated_text: As in Mālavikāgnimitra (after verse 3.12), (then enters Irāvatī in a state of appropriate intoxication, with her maidservant) — here, the intoxication of Irāvatī [is illustrated].

body.text:
atha citram-
citraṃ cākārsya vilekhanam ||SRs_3.220|| 93b
body.translated_text: Now Citra (painting) — Citra is a drawing made by sketching. ||SRs_3.220||

body.text: yathā śākuntale [6.13, padyād anantaram] rājā : akāraṇa-parityāgānuśaya-tapta-hṛdayas tāvad anukampyatām ayaṃ janaḥ punar darśanena | ity ārabhya, rājā-
body.translated_text: As in Śākuntala (after verse 6.13), the King: 'My heart burns with the remorse of causeless abandonment — let this person be shown compassion through seeing [her] again.' Beginning thus, the King —

children.text: darśana-mukham anubhavataḥ sākṣād iva tan-mayena hṛdayena |
children.translated_text: 'For one who experiences the face-to-face encounter, with a heart as if wholly absorbed [in her],

children.text: smṛti-kāriṇā tvayā me punar api citrīkṛtā kāntā ||SRs_3.221||
children.translated_text: by you, who evoke memory, my beloved has been rendered into a painting once more.' ||SRs_3.221||

body.text: ity antena citraṃ sphuṭam iti kalyāṇam |
body.translated_text: Ending thus — the painting is clearly [illustrated]. Thus says Kalyāṇa.

body.text: bhāga-kalpanayāṅgānāṃ mukha-pramukha-sandhiṣu | 93c
body.translated_text: Through the apportioning of limbs to the junctures beginning with Mukha (opening),

body.text: pratyekaṃ niyatatvena yojyā tatraiva kalpanā ||SRs_3.222||
body.translated_text: with each individually assigned, the arrangement should be applied to that very [juncture]. ||SRs_3.222||

body.text: sandhy-antarāṇāṃ vijñeyaḥ prayogas tv avibhāgataḥ | 94
body.translated_text: But the employment of the Sandhy-antaras (inter-junctural elements) should be understood as without fixed assignment;

body.text: tathaiva darśanād eṣām anaiyatyena sandhiṣu ||SRs_3.223||
body.translated_text: since these are also observed in the junctures without fixity. ||SRs_3.223||

body.text: tad eṣām avicāreṇa kathito daśarūpake | 95
body.translated_text: Therefore, without further examination, it is stated in the Daśarūpaka

body.text: sandhy-antarāṇām aṅgeṣu nāntarbhāvo mato mama ||SRs_3.224||
body.translated_text: that the inclusion of inter-junctural elements within the [main] limbs is not my accepted view. ||SRs_3.224||

body.text: sāmādy-upāya-dakṣeṇa sandhyādi-guṇa-śobhitā | 96
body.translated_text: Skilled in the methods of conciliation and the like, adorned with the qualities of junctures and the like,

body.text: nirvyūḍhaṃ siṃha-bhūpena sandhy-antara-nirūpaṇam ||SRs_3.225||
body.translated_text: the exposition of inter-junctural elements has been thoroughly accomplished by Siṃha-bhūpa. ||SRs_3.225||

body.text: atha ṣaṭ-triṃśad bhūṣaṇāni-

children.text: evam aṅgair upāṅgaiś ca suśliṣṭaṃ rūpaka-śriyaḥ | 97
children.translated_text: Thus, with limbs and sub-limbs well-joined, the body of the splendor of dramatic composition

children.text: śarīraṃ vas tv alaṅkuryāt ṣaṭ-triṃśad bhūṣaṇaiḥ sphuṭam ||SRs_3.226||
children.translated_text: should be clearly adorned with thirty-six ornaments. ||SRs_3.226||

body.translated_text: Now the thirty-six ornaments (Bhūṣaṇas) —

body.text: bhūṣaṇākṣara-saṅghātau hetuḥ prāptir udāhṛtiḥ | 98
body.translated_text: Bhūṣaṇa (ornament), Akṣara-saṅghāta (syllabic combination), Hetu (reason), Prāpti (attainment), Udāhṛti (illustration),

body.text: śobhā saṃśaya-dṛṣṭāntāv abhiprāyo nidarśanam ||SRs_3.227||
body.translated_text: Śobhā (splendor), Saṃśaya (doubt), Dṛṣṭānta (example), Abhiprāya (intention), Nidarśana (demonstration), ||SRs_3.227||

body.text: siddhi-prasiddhī dākṣiṇyam arthāpattir viśeṣaṇam | 99
body.translated_text: Siddhi (unexpected attainment), Prasiddhi (well-known illustration), Dākṣiṇya (tactfulness), Arthāpatti (presumption), Viśeṣaṇa (particularization),

body.text: padoccayas tulya-tarko vicāras tad-viparyayaḥ ||SRs_3.228||
body.translated_text: Padoccaya (accumulation of words), Tulya-tarka (parallel reasoning), Vicāra (deliberation), Tad-viparyaya (its opposite), ||SRs_3.228||

body.text: guṇātipāto' tiśayo niruktaṃ guṇa-kīrtanam | 100
body.translated_text: Guṇātipāta (transgression of virtues), Atiśaya (hyperbole), Nirukta (etymology), Guṇa-kīrtana (praise of virtues),

body.text: garhaṇānunayo bhraṃśo leśa-kṣobhau manorathaḥ ||SRs_3.229||
body.translated_text: Garhaṇa (censure), Anunaya (conciliation), Bhraṃśa (fall), Leśa (hint), Kṣobha (disturbance), Manoratha (desire), ||SRs_3.229||

body.text: anukti-siddhiḥ sārūpyaṃ mālā madhura-bhāṣaṇam | 101
body.translated_text: Anukti-siddhi (accomplishment without words), Sārūpya (resemblance), Mālā (garland), Madhura-bhāṣaṇa (sweet speech),

body.text: pṛcchopadiṣṭa-dṛṣṭāni ṣaṭ-triṃśad-bhūṣaṇāni hi ||SRs_3.230||
body.translated_text: Pṛcchā (question), Upadiṣṭa (instruction), and Dṛṣṭa (observation) — these are indeed the thirty-six ornaments. ||SRs_3.230||

body.text:
tatra bhūṣaṇam-
guṇālaṅkāra-bahulaṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ matam ||SRs_3.231|| 102
body.translated_text: Among these, Bhūṣaṇa (ornament) — speech abounding in poetic qualities and figures of speech is considered Bhūṣaṇa. ||SRs_3.231||

body.text: yathā rāmānande-

children.translated_text: 'The sky wears a garment dark as the throat of the Kalabiṅka bird; the mass of clouds
seems to complete the application of a blanket-like paste; the frog community raises a clamor of frenzy;

children.text: gandhaṃ muñcati sikta-lāja-surabhir varṣeṇa siktā sthalī
children.translated_text: the ground, sprinkled by the rain, releases a fragrance like moistened parched grain;

children.text: durlakṣo' pi vibhāvyate kamalinī-hāsena bhāsāṃ patiḥ ||SRs_3.232||
children.translated_text: and the sun, though hard to discern, is revealed through the laughter of lotuses.' ||SRs_3.232||

body.translated_text: As in Rāmānanda —

body.text: atra śleṣa-prasāda-samādhi-samatādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ upamā-rūpakotprekṣa-hetūnām alaṅkārāṇāṃ ca sambhavād idaṃ bhūṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: Here, because of the occurrence of poetic qualities such as Śleṣa (double meaning), Prasāda (lucidity), Samādhi (concentration), Samatā (balance), and the like, and of figures of speech such as Upamā (simile), Rūpaka (metaphor), and Utprekṣā (poetic fancy), and of logical reasoning (Hetu) — this constitutes Bhūṣaṇa.

body.text: atha akṣara-saṅghātaḥ-

children.translated_text: A sentence that conveys a different meaning through closely joined syllables is Akṣara-saṅghāta. ||SRs_3.233||

body.translated_text: Now Akṣara-saṅghāta (syllabic combination) —

body.text: yathā śākuntale [7.20 padyād anantaram] rājā (svagatam) : iyaṃ khalu kathā mām eva lakṣyīkaroti | yadi tāvad asya śiśor mātaraṃ nāmataḥ pṛcchāmi | athavā anyāyyaḥ para-dāra-vyavahāraḥ | ity upakramya,
body.translated_text: As in Śākuntala (after verse 7.20), the King (to himself): 'This story indeed points to me. Let me then ask the name of this child's mother. But no — it is improper to inquire about another man's wife.' Beginning thus,

body.text: (praviśya mṛn-mayūra-hastā) tāpasī-sabba-damaṇa ! sauṃdalābaṇṇaṃ pekkha [sarva-damana ! śakunta-lāvaṇyaṃ prekṣasva |]
body.translated_text: (entering with a clay peacock in hand) The hermit-woman [in Prakrit]: 'Sarva-damana! Behold the beauty of the bird (śakunta-lāvaṇya)!' [Sanskrit: 'Sarva-damana! Look at the beauty of the bird (śakunta-lāvaṇya)!']

body.text: bālaḥ (sadṛṣṭi-kṣepam)-kahiṃ vā me ajjū | [kutra vā mama mātā |]
body.translated_text: The boy (casting a glance around): [Prakrit] 'Where is my mother?' [Sanskrit: 'Where is my mother?']

body.text: ubhe-ṇāma-sārisseṇa baṃcido māubacchalo | [nāma-sādṛśyena vañcito mātṛ-vatsalaḥ |]
body.translated_text: Both [women]: [Prakrit] 'The mother-loving child has been misled by the similarity of the name!' [Sanskrit: 'Deceived by the resemblance of the name, the one devoted to his mother!']

body.text: dvitīyā-baccha, imassa mittiā-morassa raṃmattaṇaṃ dekkha tti bhaṇido' si | [vatsa, asya mṛttikā-mayūrasya ramyatvaṃ paśyeti bhaṇito' si |]
body.translated_text: The second [woman in Prakrit]: 'Child, you were told to look at the beauty of this clay peacock!' [Sanskrit: 'Child, you were told: "Look at the beauty of this clay peacock!"']

body.text: rājā (ātma-gatam)-kiṃ vā śakuntalety asya mātur ākhyā | ity antam | atra śakunta-lāvaṇyam ity atra śakuntalā-nāmākṣarāṇāṃ pratibhānād ayam akṣara-saṅghātaḥ |
body.translated_text: The King (to himself): 'Could it be that Śakuntalā is his mother's name?' — ending thus. Here, through the recognition of the syllables of the name Śakuntalā in 'śakunta-lāvaṇya' (beauty of a bird), this constitutes Akṣara-saṅghāta.

body.text:
atha hetuḥ-
sa hetur iti nirdiṣṭo yat sādhyārtha-prasādhakaḥ ||SRs_3.234|| 103
body.translated_text: Now Hetu (reason) — that which establishes the desired meaning is called Hetu. ||SRs_3.234||

body.text: yathā ratnāvalyāṃ, rājā (tathā kṛtvā śrutvā ca)-
body.translated_text: As in Ratnāvalī, the King (having done so and listened) —

children.translated_text: 'The syllables are clear through effort, sweet by the nature of a woman,
without resonance because of the small body — I think it is a parrot that speaks.' ||SRs_3.235||

body.text: atra śārikālāpa-sādhanāya yatna-spaṣṭākṣaratvādi-hetūnāṃ kathanād ayaṃ hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, through the statement of reasons such as clarity of syllables due to effort and the like, to establish that a parrot is speaking — this constitutes Hetu.

body.text: atha prāptiḥ-

children.translated_text: Prāpti is the inferring of the whole from the knowledge of a part. ||SRs_3.236||

body.translated_text: Now Prāpti (attainment) —

body.text: yathā vikramorvaśīye, rājā (carcarikayāpasṛtya añjaliṃ baddhvā) :
body.translated_text: As in Vikramorvaśīya, the King (stepping aside through the Carcarikā [dance-movement], with palms joined):

children.text: haṃsa prayaccha me kāntāṃ gatir asyās tvayā hatā |
children.translated_text: 'O Swan, give me my beloved — her movement has been impeded by you.
When a part is clearly established, one may be charged with [delivering] what is due.' ||SRs_3.237||

body.text: atra haṃse priyā-gamana-mātra-vibhāvya-priyā-haraṇābhiyogaḥ prāptiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, through merely perceiving the swan's [role in] the beloved's departure — the accusation of the swan for abducting the beloved — constitutes Prāpti.

body.text: atha udāharaṇam-

children.text: vākyaṃ yad gūḍha-tulyārthaṃ tad udāharaṇaṃ matam ||SRs_3.238||
children.translated_text: A sentence whose meaning is hidden but equivalent is considered Udāharaṇa. ||SRs_3.238||

body.translated_text: Now Udāharaṇa (illustration) —

body.text: yathā śākuntale, rājā (svagatam)-katham ātmāpahāraṃ karomi ? bhavatu, evaṃ tāvad enāṃ vakṣye | (prakāśam) bhavati yaḥ pauraveṇa rājñā dharmādhikāre niyuktaḥ so' ham avighna-kriyopalambhāya dharmāraṇyam idam āyātaḥ | ity ārabhya,
body.translated_text: As in Śākuntala, the King (to himself): 'How shall I conceal myself? Very well, I shall address her thus.' (aloud) 'Lady, I am the one appointed by the Paurava king to the office of Dharma, and I have come to this Dharma-forest to oversee that religious duties are performed without obstruction.' Beginning thus,

body.text: śakuntalā-tumhe avedha | kiṃ bi hiae karia matedha | ṇa bo baaṇaṃ suṇissaṃ | [yuvām apetam | kim api hṛdaye kṛtvā mantrayethe | na yuvayor vacanaṃ śroṣyāmi |] ity antam [1.21 padyād anantaram] | atra sābhiprāya-gūḍhārthatayā tad idam udāharaṇam |
body.translated_text: Śakuntalā [in Prakrit]: 'You two, go away! You are deliberating something in your hearts! I shall not listen to your words.' [Sanskrit: 'Go away, both of you! Having put something in your hearts, you are consulting. I shall not hear your words.'] — ending thus (after verse 1.21). Here, through the hidden purposeful meaning, this constitutes Udāharaṇa.

body.text: atha śobhā-

children.translated_text: Śobhā is said to be the natural revelation [of beauty] of a young couple toward each other. ||SRs_3.239||

body.translated_text: Now Śobhā (splendor) —

body.text: yathā ratnāvalyāṃ, sāgarikā (rājānaṃ dṛṣṭvā saharṣaṃ sa-sādhvasaṃ sa-kampaṃ ca svagatam)-eṇaṃ pekkhia adisaddhaseṇa ṇa sakkaṇomi padādo padaṃ bi gantuṃ | tā kiṃ vā ettha karissaṃ ? [enaṃ prekṣya atisādhvasena na śaknomi padāt padam api gantum | tat kiṃ vā atra kariṣyāmi ?]
body.translated_text: As in Ratnāvalī, Sāgarikā (seeing the King, with joy, trepidation, and trembling, to herself in Prakrit): 'Seeing him, from excessive trepidation, I am unable to move even one step. So what shall I do here?' [Sanskrit rendering follows].

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ (sāgarikāṃ dṛṣṭvā)-aho accariaṃ | īrisaṃ kaṇṇāraaṇaṃ māṇusaloe ṇa dīsadi | bho baassa taha takkemi paāvaiṇobi edaṃ ṇimmābia puṇo puṇo bihmao saṃbutto tti | [aho āścaryam | īdṛśaṃ kanyā-ratnaṃ mānusa-loke na dṛśyate | bho vayasya tasmāt tarkayāmi prajāpater api idaṃ nirmāya punaḥ punar vismayaḥ saṃvṛtta iti |]
body.translated_text: The Vidūṣaka (seeing Sāgarikā, in Prakrit): 'Oh wonder! Such a jewel of a maiden is not seen in the human world. Ho, friend, therefore I think that even Prajāpati (the Creator), having fashioned her, was struck with wonder again and again!' [Sanskrit rendering follows].

body.text: rājā-sakhe mamāpy etad eva manasi vartate [2.15 padyāt pūrvam] ity ādinā sāgarikā-vatsarājayor anyonya-nirvarṇanena rūpātiśaya-prakaṭanaṃ śobhā |
body.translated_text: The King: 'Friend, this very thing occupies my mind too.' (before verse 2.15) — through the mutual gazing of Sāgarikā and Vatsa-rāja and the revelation of surpassing beauty, this constitutes Śobhā.

body.text:
atha saṃśayaḥ-
aniścayāntaṃ yad vākyaṃ saṃśayaḥ sa nigadyate ||SRs_3.240|| 105
body.translated_text: Now Saṃśaya (doubt) — a speech that ends in uncertainty is called Saṃśaya. ||SRs_3.240||

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave, makarandaḥ-
body.translated_text: As in Mālatī-mādhava, Makaranda [says] —

children.translated_text: 'Has our friend gone to the abode of the Bhagavatī (goddess)?

children.text: jīvanty athaiṣyati na vety abhiśaṅkito' smi |
children.translated_text: Is she alive? Will she come or not? — I am filled with apprehension.
For the most part, the happiness of meeting with kinsmen, friends, and dear ones
is as fickle as the flash of lightning.' ||SRs_3.241||

body.text: ity atra mālatī kāmandhakyāḥ gṛhaṃ gatā vā jīvati vā na veti saṃśayena vākya-samāpter ayaṃ saṃśayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, with the speech ending in the doubt of whether Mālatī has gone to Kāmandhakī's house, whether she is alive or not — this constitutes Saṃśaya.

body.text:
atha dṛṣṭāntaḥ-
sva-pakṣe darśanaṃ hetor dṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhya-siddhaye ||SRs_3.242|| 106a
body.translated_text: Now Dṛṣṭānta (example) — the demonstration of a reason in one's own thesis, for the establishment of what is to be proved, is called Dṛṣṭānta. ||SRs_3.242||

body.text: yathā śākuntale, rājā-
body.translated_text: As in Śākuntala, the King —

body.text:
śama-pradhāneṣu tapodhaneṣu
gūḍhaṃ hi dāhātmakam asti tejaḥ |
sparśānukūlā iva sūrya-kāntās
tad anya-tejo' bhibhavād vamanti ||SRs_3.243|| [a.śa. 2.7]
body.translated_text: 'In the sages whose chief quality is tranquility, there is hidden a fiery energy of a burning nature. The sun-stones, pleasant to the touch, emit that [fire] when overshadowed by another's brilliance.' ||SRs_3.243|| [Abhijñāna-Śākuntala 2.7]

body.text: ity atra tapodhaneṣu gūḍha-dāhātmaka-tejaḥ-sadbhāve sādhye tat-sādhakasya anya-tejas tiraskāra-janita-tejaḥ-samudgāra-rūpasya hetoḥ sūrya-kānteṣu darśitatvād dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, for the proposition that sages possess hidden energy of a burning nature, the reason — that their fire bursts forth when eclipsed by another's brilliance — is demonstrated through the example of sun-stones. Hence this is Dṛṣṭānta.

body.text: atha abhiprāyaḥ-

children.text: abhiprāyas tv abhūtārtho hṛdyaḥ sāmyena kalpitaḥ | 106b
children.translated_text: Abhiprāya is a charming content that is not literally true, imagined through analogy.
Others say Abhiprāya is the sense of 'mine-ness' toward a charming object. ||SRs_3.244||

body.translated_text: Now Abhiprāya (intention) —

body.text: yathā ratnāvalyāṃ, rājā-
body.translated_text: As in Ratnāvalī, the King —

body.text:
kiṃ padmasya ruciṃ na hanti nayanānandaṃ vidhatte na kiṃ
vṛddhiṃ vā jhaṣaketanasya kurute nāloka-mātreṇa kim |
vaktrendau tava saty ayaṃ yad aparaḥ śītāṃśur ujjṛmbhate
darpaḥ syād amṛtena ced iha tad apy asty eva bimbādhare ||SRs_3.245|| [ra. 3.13]
body.translated_text: 'Does it not destroy the beauty of the lotus? Does it not provide delight to the eyes? Does it not promote the growth of the Fish-bannered one (Kāma)? Is not mere seeing enough? When your face-moon exists, why does this other cool-rayed moon rise? If it be arrogance from possessing nectar — well, that too exists in your bimba-fruit lips!' ||SRs_3.245|| [Ratnāvalī 3.13]

body.text: ity atra candra-sāmyena mukhe amṛta-kalpanād ayam abhiprāyaḥ | athavā tatraivātihṛdya-bimbādhare rājño mamatvam abhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, through the imagination of nectar in her face by analogy with the moon — this constitutes Abhiprāya. Alternatively, the King's sense of possessiveness toward the supremely charming bimba-fruit lip — that too is Abhiprāya.

body.text: atha nidarśanaṃ-

children.translated_text: When well-known things are proclaimed
for the purpose of removing another's contempt — that is called Nidarśana. ||SRs_3.246||

body.translated_text: Now Nidarśana (demonstration) —

body.text: yathā śākuntale, rājā-upapadyate-
body.translated_text: As in Śākuntala, the King: 'It is fitting —'

body.text:
mānuṣīṣu kathaṃ vā syād asya rūpasya sambhavaḥ |
na prabhā-tarala-jyotir udeti vasudhā-talāt ||SRs_3.247|| [a.śa. 1.22]
body.translated_text: 'How could such beauty have its origin among mortal women? A quivering flame of radiance does not rise from the surface of the earth.' ||SRs_3.247|| [Abhijñāna-Śākuntala 1.22]

body.text: atra prati-vastu-nyāyena sadṛśa-vastu-kīrtanaṃ nidarśanam |
body.translated_text: Here, the mention of an analogous well-known thing according to the method of counter-proposition constitutes Nidarśana.

body.text:
atha siddhiḥ-
atarkitopapannaḥ syāt siddhir iṣṭārtha-saṅgamaḥ ||SRs_3.248|| 108
body.translated_text: Now Siddhi (unexpected attainment) — the unforeseen encounter with a desired object is Siddhi. ||SRs_3.248||

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre, vidūṣakaḥ (dṛṣṭvā)-hī hī baassa edaṃ khu sīhupāṇu-bejjidassa macchaāḍiā ubaṇadā | [āścaryaṃ āścaryaṃ vayasya etat khalu sīdhupānodvejitasya matsyaṇḍikā upanatā |]
body.translated_text: As in Mālavikāgnimitra, the Vidūṣaka (seeing, in Prakrit): 'Wonder of wonders, friend! This is indeed like a fish-cake offered to one nauseated by drinking wine!' [Sanskrit: 'How astonishing! A jewel of a maiden such as this is not seen in the human world. Ho, friend, therefore I think that even Prajāpati, having fashioned her, was struck with wonder again and again!']

body.text: rājā-aye kim etat ?
body.translated_text: The King: 'What is this?'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-esā ṇādiparikkhidabesā ūsuabaaṇā eāiṇī mālabiā adūre baṭṭadi | [eṣā nādipariṣkṛta-veṣā utsuka-vadanā ekākinī mālavikā adūre vartate |]
body.translated_text: The Vidūṣaka [in Prakrit]: 'That Mālavikā, adorned by bathing, with an eager face, stands alone nearby!' [Sanskrit rendering follows].

body.text: rājā (saharṣaṃ)-kathaṃ mālavikā |
body.translated_text: The King (with joy): 'What! Mālavikā?'

body.text: vidūṣakaḥ-aha iṃ | [atha kim |]
body.translated_text: The Vidūṣaka [in Prakrit]: 'Indeed!' [Sanskrit: 'What else?']

body.text: rājā-śakyam idānīṃ jīvitam avalambitam [3.5 padyād anantaram] ity atra irāvatī-saṅketaṃ gacchato rājñaḥ mālavikā-darśana-siddhir acintitā siddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: The King: 'Now life can be sustained.' (after verse 3.5) — Here, when the King is going to Irāvatī's rendezvous, the unexpected seeing of Mālavikā is an unforeseen Siddhi.

body.text:
atha prasiddhiḥ-
prasiddhir loka-vikhyātair vākyair artha-prasādhanam ||SRs_3.249|| 109a
body.translated_text: Now Prasiddhi (well-known illustration) — Prasiddhi is the establishing of meaning through well-known sayings. ||SRs_3.249||

body.text: yathā śākuntale, rājā-
body.translated_text: As in Śākuntala, the King —

children.translated_text: 'The lotus, though pierced by the bee, is lovely;

children.text: malinam api himāṃśor lakṣma lakṣmīṃ tanoti |
children.translated_text: the mark on the moon, though dark, bestows beauty.
Thus, the slender one is even more charming in her bark-garment —

children.text: kim iva hi madhurāṇāṃ maṇḍanaṃ nākṛtīnām ||SRs_3.250||
children.translated_text: for what indeed is not an adornment of beautiful forms?' ||SRs_3.250||

body.text: atra śavalādy-anuvedhe' pi ramaṇīyatayā prasiddhānāṃ sarasijādīnāṃ kathanena śakuntalā-manojñatā-sādhanaṃ prasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, through the mention of well-known things like the lotus and others, which are charming even when pierced by bees and the like — the establishment of Śakuntalā's charm constitutes Prasiddhi.

body.text:
atha dāksiṇyam-
cittānuvartanaṃ yatra tad dākṣiṇyam itīritam ||SRs_3.251|| 109b
body.translated_text: Now Dākṣiṇya (tactfulness) — where one follows the inclination of another's mind — that is called Dākṣiṇya. ||SRs_3.251||

body.text:
yathā śākuntale, senāpatiḥ-jayatu svāmī |
rājā-bhadra senāpate mandotsāhaḥ kṛto' smi mṛgayāpavādinā māḍhavyena |
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Śākuntala</s> — the Commander: 'Victory to the Lord!' The King: 'Good Commander, I have been made half-hearted in enthusiasm by <s>Māṭhavya</s> (<s>Māḍhavya</s>), who decries hunting.'

body.text: senāpatiḥ (vidūṣakaṃ prati, janāntikam)-sakhe sthira-pratibandho bhava | ahaṃ tāvat svāminaś citta-vṛttim anuvartiṣye | (prakāśam) pralapatv eṣa vaidheyaḥ | nanu prabhur eva nidarśanam |
body.translated_text: The Commander (to the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>, privately): 'Friend, hold firm in your resistance. Meanwhile I shall follow the inclination of the Master's mind.' (Aloud) 'Let this obedient servant prattle on! For the Master himself is the example —

body.text:
medaś cheda-kṛśodaraṃ laghu bhavaty utthāna-yogyaṃ vapuḥ
sattvānām api lakṣyate vikṛtimac cittaṃ bhaya-krodhayoḥ |
utkarṣaḥ sa ca dhanvināṃ yad iṣavaḥ sidhyanti lakṣye cale
mithyaiva vyasanaṃ vadanti mṛgayāmīdṛg vinodaḥ kutaḥ ||SRs_3.252|| [a.śa. 2.5]
body.translated_text: 'The body becomes lean-bellied from the reduction of fat, light and fit for rising; in animals too, the mind, altered by fear and anger, is observed — and that is the excellence of archers, that their arrows find their mark on a moving target. It is false that they call hunting a vice — where else is such a diversion?' ||3.252|| [<s>Abhijñāna-śākuntala</s> 2.5]

body.text: ity atra senāpateḥ rāja-cittānuvartanaṃ dākṣiṇyam |
body.translated_text: Here, the Commander's compliance with the King's inclination is <s>Dākṣiṇya</s> (tact/courtesy).

body.text:
atha arthāpattiḥ-
uktārthānupapattyā'nyo yasminn arthaḥ prakalpyate |
vākya-mādhurya-saṃyuktā sārthāpattir udāhṛtā ||SRs_3.253|| 110
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — Where, from the impossibility of a stated meaning, another meaning is posited, combined with sweetness of expression — that is illustrated as <s>Arthāpatti</s>. ||3.253|| 110

body.text: yathā ratnāvalyāṃ, vidūṣakaḥ-bhoḥ esā kkhu tue apubbā sirī samāsādidā | [bho eṣā khalu tvayā apūrvā śrīḥ samāsāditā |]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> — the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Sir! You have indeed obtained an unprecedented <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune/Beauty)!'

body.text: rājā-vayasya, satyam |
body.translated_text: The King: 'Friend, truly!'

body.text:
śrīr eṣā pāṇir apy asyāḥ pārijātasya pallavaḥ |
kuto' nyathā sravaty eṣa sveda-cchadmāmṛta-dravaḥ ||SRs_3.254|| [ra. 2.17]
body.translated_text: 'This is <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune); and her hand too is a sprout of the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree — for how else would this stream of nectar flow under the guise of perspiration?' ||3.254|| [<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 2.17]

body.text: atra sveda-cchadmāmṛta-dravotpatter anyathānupapattyā pāṇeḥ pārijātatva-kalpanād iyam arthāpattiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since from the otherwise-impossible production of a nectar-stream under the guise of perspiration, the hand is imagined to be a <s>Pārijāta</s> [tree] — this is <s>Arthāpatti</s>.

body.text:
atha viśeṣaṇam-
siddhān bahūn pradhānārthān uktvā yatra prayujyate |
viśeṣa-yuktaṃ vacanaṃ vijñeyaṃ tad viśeṣaṇam ||SRs_3.255|| 111
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Viśeṣaṇa</s> (specification) — Where, after stating many established principal meanings, a statement endowed with a distinction is employed — that should be known as <s>Viśeṣaṇa</s>. ||3.255|| 111

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave, mādhavaḥ (abhilikhya pradarśayati)
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> — <s>Mādhava</s> (having composed [the verse], shows it).

body.text: makarandaḥ (sa-kautukam)-katham acireṇaiva nirmāya likhitaḥ ślokaḥ | (vācayati)
body.translated_text: <s>Makaranda</s> (with curiosity): 'What! A verse composed and written in so short a time!' (He reads aloud:)

body.text:
jagati jayinas te te bhāvā navendu-kalādayaḥ
prakṛti-madhurāḥ santy evānye mano madayanti ye |
mama tu yad iyaṃ yātā loke vilocana-candrikā
nayana-viṣayaṃ janmany ekaḥ sa eva mahotsavaḥ ||SRs_3.256|| [mā.mā. 1.39]
body.translated_text: 'In the world, those victorious qualities — the crescent moon and the like — are naturally sweet and exist [already]; there are others too which intoxicate the mind. But for me, since this moonlight of the eyes has appeared in the world, that alone is the one great festival in this birth.' ||3.256|| [<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 1.39]

body.text: ity atra indukalādīn mano-mada-hetutayā prasiddhān uktvā tat-samāna-mādhuryāyām api mālatyāṃ viśeṣa-kathanād idaṃ viśeṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: Here, after stating the crescent moon and the like as well-known causes of mental intoxication, since the distinctiveness of <s>Mālatī</s>, who possesses equal sweetness, is then narrated — this is <s>Viśeṣaṇa</s>.

body.text:
atha padoccayaḥ-
bahūnāṃ tu prayuktānāṃ padānāṃ bahubhiḥ padaiḥ |
uccayaḥ sadṛśārtho yaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ padoccayaḥ ||SRs_3.257|| 112
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Padoccaya</s> (accumulation of words) — Where many words employed are gathered together with many other words conveying similar meanings — that should be known as <s>Padoccaya</s>. ||3.257|| 112

body.text: yathā karpūra-mañjaryām, rājā (vācayati)-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Karpūra-mañjarī</s> — the King (reads aloud) [in Prakrit]:

body.text:
saha divasa-ṇisāhiṃ dīharā sāsa-daṃḍā
saha maṇi-balaehiṃ bāha-dhārā galaṃti |
tuha suhaa bioe tīa ubbeaṇīe
sahaa taṇu-ladāe dubbalā jīvidāsā ||SRs_3.258|| [ka.ma. 2.9]
body.translated_text: 'Together with day and night, the long staves of her sighs [grow];

children.translated_text: together with her gem bangles, streams of tears flow;
[missing line]
in your separation, O handsome one, for that agitated woman,
together with her creeper-like body, the hope of life grows weak.' ||3.258|| [<s>Karpūra-mañjarī</s> 2.9]

body.text: ity atra śvāsa-daṇḍādīnāṃ dīrgha-bhāvādi-kriyāsu divasa-niśādibhiḥ saha samāveśād ayaṃ padoccayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since the sighing-staves and the like are linked together with day-and-night and the like in the actions of growing long and so forth — this is <s>Padoccaya</s>.

body.text:
atha tulyārthakaḥ-
rūpakair upamābhir vā tulyārthābhiḥ prayojitaḥ | apratyakṣārtha-saṃsparśas tulya-tarka itīritaḥ ||SRs_3.259|| 113
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Tulyatarka</s> (analogical reasoning) — That which is employed with metaphors or similes of equal meaning, conveying a meaning not directly perceptible — is called <s>Tulyatarka</s>. ||3.259|| 113

body.text:
yathā mālatī-mādhave, mādhavaḥ (saharṣam)-diṣṭyā lavaṅgikā-dvitīyā mālaty api (parāgatā)-
āścaryam utpala-dṛśo vadanāmalendu- sāṃnidhyato mama muhur jadimānam etya |
jātyena candramaṇineva mahī-dharasya sandhāryate drava-mayo manasā vikāraḥ ||SRs_3.260|| [mā.mā. 3.5]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> — <s>Mādhava</s> (joyfully): 'By good fortune, <s>Mālatī</s> too, accompanied by <s>Lavaṅgikā</s>, has come — A wonder! From the proximity of the full-moon-like face of the lotus-eyed one, my mind repeatedly attains a state of torpor; the transformation that is liquid with affection is held by the mind, as a moonstone [is held] by the moon of a mountain, naturally.' ||3.260|| [<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 3.5]

body.text: ity atra indu-candrakāntādy-upamayā paratyakṣasya sneha-rūpa-vikārasya kathanāt tulya-tarkaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, since the imperceptible transformation in the form of affection is narrated through the simile of the moon and the moonstone — this is <s>Tulyatarka</s>.

body.text:
atha vicāraḥ-
vicāras tv eka-sādhyasya bahu-sādhana-varṇanam ||SRs_3.261|| 114a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vicāra</s> (deliberation) — <s>Vicāra</s> is the description of many means for a single end. ||3.261|| 114a

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave, makarandaḥ-vayasya mādhava sarvathā samāśvasihi-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> — <s>Makaranda</s>: 'Friend <s>Mādhava</s>, take heart in every way —

body.text:
yā kaumudī nayanayor bhavataḥ sujanmā
tasyā bhavān api manoratha-labdha-bandhuḥ |
tat saṅgamaṃ prati sakhe na hi saṃśayo' sti
yasmin vidhiś ca madanaś ca kṛtābhiyogaḥ ||SRs_3.262|| [mā.mā. 1.37]
body.translated_text: 'She who is the moonlight of your eyes is of noble birth, and you too are a kinsman obtained through heart's desire. Therefore, friend, there is no doubt about union — in which both Fate and Love have joined their effort.' ||3.262|| [<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 1.37]

body.text: atra saṅgama-rūpa-sādhyārtha-siddhaye parasparānurāga-siddhi-madana-rūpāṇām upāyānāṃ sad-bhāva-kathanād vicāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since the existence of means — mutual attraction, the power of Fate, and Love — is narrated for the purpose of accomplishing the aim in the form of union, this is <s>Vicāra</s>.

body.text:
atha tad-viparyayaḥ-
vicārasyānyathābhāvo vijñeyas tad-viparyayaḥ ||SRs_3.263|| 114
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Tadviparyaya</s> (the reverse of deliberation) — The opposite state of <s>Vicāra</s> should be known as <s>Tadviparyaya</s>. ||3.263|| 114

body.text: yathā rāmānande-

children.text: vyarthaṃ yatra kapīndra-sakhyam api me vīryaṃ kapīnām api
children.translated_text: 'Futile here is even the friendship of the king of monkeys, futile also the valor of the monkeys,

children.text: prajñā jāmbavato' pi yatra na gatiḥ putrasya vāyor api |
