children.translated_text: futile even the wisdom of <s>Jāmbavān</s>, here the speed of the son of the Wind is of no avail,

children.text: mārgaṃ yatra na viśvakarma-tanayaḥ kartuṃ nalo' pi kṣamaḥ
children.translated_text: here even <s>Nala</s>, the son of <s>Viśvakarman</s>, is unable to make a path —

children.text: saumitrer api patriṇām aviṣayas tatra priyā kvāpi me ||SRs_3.264||
children.translated_text: even the arrows of the son of <s>Sumitrā</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) are beyond reach; where then is my beloved?' ||3.264||

body.translated_text: As in the <s>Rāmānanda</s> —

body.text: atra bahūpāya-sāmarthyābhāva-kathanād vicāra-viparyayaḥ spaṣṭa eva |
body.translated_text: Here, since the absence of the capacity of many means is narrated, the reverse of <s>Vicāra</s> is plainly evident.

body.text:
atha guṇātipātaḥ-
guṇātipāto vyatyasta-guṇākhyānam udāhṛtam ||SRs_3.265|| 115a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Guṇātipāta</s> (perverse attribution of qualities) — <s>Guṇātipāta</s> is defined as the narration of reversed qualities. ||3.265|| 115a

body.text:
yathā veṇī-saṃhāre, (tataḥ praviśato bhīmārjunau) bhīmaḥ-bho bho alam alam āśaṅkayā |
kartā dyūta-cchalānāṃ jatu-maya-śaraṇoddīpanaḥ so' timānī kṛṣṇākeśottarīya-vyapanayana-marut pāṇḍavā yasya dāsāḥ |
rājā duḥśāsanāder gurur anuja-śatasyāṅga-rājasya mitraṃ kvāste duryodhano' sau kathayata na ruṣā draṣṭum abhyāgatau svaḥ ||SRs_3.266|| [ve.saṃ. 5.26]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> — (Then enter <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>.) <s>Bhīma</s>: 'Ho! Enough of apprehension! — He who contrived the fraud of the dice-game, who set ablaze the house of lac, that supremely proud one whose wind was the removal of the upper garment of <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>'s (<s>Draupadī</s>'s) hair, whose <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are servants, the king who is the elder of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and his hundred brothers, the friend of the king of <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>) — where is that <s>Duryodhana</s>? Tell [us] — not in anger have we come to see him!' ||3.266|| [<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 5.26]

body.text: atra adhikṣepa-vākyatvād vyatyasta-guṇākhyānaṃ spaṣṭam eva |
body.translated_text: Here, since it is a statement of censure, the narration of reversed qualities is plainly evident.

body.text: atha atiśayaḥ-

children.text: bahūn guṇān kīrtayitvā sāmānyena ca saṃśrayān | 115
children.translated_text: Where, after celebrating many qualities in common, 115

children.text: viśeṣaḥ kīrtyate yatra jñeyaḥ so' tiśayo budhaiḥ ||SRs_3.267||
children.translated_text: a distinction is then proclaimed — that should be known by the wise as <s>Atiśaya</s>. ||3.267||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Atiśaya</s> (surpassing excellence) —

body.text: yathā vikramorvaśīye, rājā (sa-harṣam ākarṇya)-anena priyopalabdhi-śaṃsinā mandra-kaṇṭha-garjitena samāśvāsito' smi | sādharmyāc ca bhūyasī me tvayi prītiḥ |
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> — the King (listening joyfully): 'I am consoled by this deep-throated rumble that portends the finding of my beloved. And from our similarity, my affection for you is even greater —

body.text:
mām āhuḥ pṛthivī-bhṛtām adhipatiṃ nāgādhirājo bhavān
avyucchinna-pṛthu-pravṛtti bhavato dānaṃ mamāpy arthiṣu |
strī-ratneṣu mamorvaśī priyatamā yūthe taveyaṃ vaśā
sarvaṃ mām anu te priyā-virahajāṃ tvaṃ tu vyathāṃ mānubhūḥ ||SRs_3.268|| [vi.u. 4.47]
body.translated_text: 'They call me the lord of earth-bearers (kings), and you are the king of elephants; your gift to supplicants is uninterrupted and vast, and so is mine; among jewels of women, <s>Urvaśī</s> is dearest to me, and in your herd this female is your beloved — in everything [you are] like me; but the anguish born of separation from the beloved — that you must endure [unlike me]!' ||3.268|| [<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.47]

body.text: ity atra samāna-dharmaṇi gajādhirāje purūravasā priyā-virahābhāva-kathanād atiśayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since the absence of the anguish of separation from the beloved is narrated with respect to the elephant-king, who shares common qualities, this is <s>Atiśaya</s>.

body.text:
atha niruktiḥ[*20]-
niruktir niravadyoktir nāmāny artha-prasiddhaye ||SRs_3.269|| 116
[*20] niruktam in the printed edition.
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Nirukti</s> (etymological explanation) — <s>Nirukti</s> is a faultless utterance [giving] names for the purpose of establishing a meaning. ||3.269|| 116

body.text: yathā śākuntale, priyaṃvadā-halā sauṃdale ! ettha ebba dāva muhuttaaṃ ciṭṭha | jāba tue ubagadāe ladā-saṇāho bia aaṃ kesara-rukkhao paḍibhādi | [halā śakuntale, atraiva tāvan muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha | yāvat tvayopagatayā latā-sanātha ivāyaṃ kesara-vṛkṣakaḥ pratibhāti |]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Śākuntala</s> — <s>Priyaṃvadā</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Friend <s>Śakuntalā</s>! Stand right here for a moment! For with you standing beside it, this <s>kesara</s> (filament) tree appears as if sheltered by a creeper.'

body.text: śakuntalā-ado khu piaṃbadāsi tumaṃ | [ataḥ khalu priyaṃvadāsi tvam |] [1.18 padyāt pūrvam] | atra priyaṃvadāyāḥ priya-bhāṣaṇād idaṃ nāma-dheyam ity uktir niruktiḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Śakuntalā</s> [in Prakrit]: 'That is why you are indeed "<s>Priyaṃvadā</s>" (one who speaks sweetly)!' (Before verse 1.18) Here, the statement that <s>Priyaṃvadā</s>'s name derives from her sweet speech is <s>Nirukti</s>.

body.text:
atha guṇa-kīrtanam-
loke guṇātirikānāṃ bahūnāṃ yatra nāmabhiḥ |
eko' pi śabdyate tat tu vijñeyaṃ guṇa-kīrtanam ||SRs_3.270|| 117
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Guṇa-kīrtana</s> (praise of qualities) — Where, among many who are celebrated in the world as surpassingly endowed with virtues, one alone is addressed by those names — that should be known as <s>Guṇa-kīrtana</s>. ||3.270|| 117

body.text: yathā uttara-rāma-carite, vāsantī-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> — <s>Vāsantī</s>:

body.text:
tvaṃ jīvitaṃ tvam asi me hṛdayaṃ dvitīyaṃ
tvaṃ kaumudī nayanayor amṛtaṃ tvam aṅge |
ity ādibhiḥ priya-śatair anurudhya mugdhāṃ
tām eva śāntam athavā kim ihottareṇa ||SRs_3.271|| [u.rā.ca. 3.26]
body.translated_text: '"You are my life, you are my second heart, you are the moonlight of my eyes, you are the nectar of my body" — having thus fondly addressed the innocent one with hundreds of endearments, then — or rather, what avails more words? — peace.' ||3.271|| [<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 3.26]

body.text: ity atra amṛta-kaumudī-prabhṛtināmabhiḥ sītā-śaṃsanaṃ guṇa-kīrtanam |
body.translated_text: Here, the praising of <s>Sītā</s> with names such as 'nectar,' 'moonlight,' and the like is <s>Guṇa-kīrtana</s>.

body.text:
atha garhaṇam-
yatra saṅkīrtayan doṣān guṇam arthena darśayet | guṇān vā kīrtayan doṣān darśayed garhaṇaṃ tu tat ||SRs_3.272|| 118
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Garhaṇa</s> (censure) — Where, while enumerating faults, one reveals a virtue by implication; or while proclaiming virtues, one reveals faults — that is <s>Garhaṇa</s>. ||3.272|| 118

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave, lavaṅgikā-bhaabadi kisaṇa-cauddasī-raaṇi-mahā-masāṇa-saṃcāra-ṇibbaḍia-bisama-bbabasāo ṇiṭṭhābida-caṇḍa-pāsaṇḍ-uddaṇḍa-bhua-daṇḍa-sāhaso sāhasio kkhu eso | ado kkhu me pia-sahī ukkaṃpidā | [bhagavati kṛṣṇa-caturdaśī-rajani-mahā-śmaśāna-sañcāra-pṛthag-bhūta-viṣama-vyavasāyo niṣṭhāpita-caṇḍa-pāṣaṇḍoddaṇḍa-bhuja-daṇḍa-sāhasaḥ sāhasikaḥ khalu eṣaḥ | ataḥ khalu me priya-sakhī utkampitā |]
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> — <s>Lavaṅgikā</s> [in Prakrit]: 'O Lady! His daring venture of wandering through the great cremation ground on the dark fourteenth night, his desperate resolve, his boldness of arm-staff completing the fierce heretical [rite] — this man is indeed a daredevil! That is why my dear friend is in a flutter!'

body.text: makarandaḥ (svagatam)-sādhu lavaṅgike sādhu | sthāne khalv anurāgopakārayor garīyasor upanyāsaḥ | [6.15 padyād anantaram]
body.translated_text: <s>Makaranda</s> (aside): 'Well done, <s>Lavaṅgikā</s>, well done! Rightly indeed is the presentation of the two weighty [topics] — devotion and service.' (After verse 6.15)

body.text: ity atra mahā-māṃsa-vikraya-sāhasasya doṣa-rūpeṇa kathene' pi mādhavānurāgotpādana-guṇatayā paryavasitam idaṃ pramukha-garhaṇatvād garhaṇam |
body.translated_text: Here, though the daring of selling great flesh is narrated as if a fault, it results in producing love for <s>Mādhava</s> — since on its face it is censure, this is <s>Garhaṇa</s>.

body.text: guṇa-kīrtane doṣa-paryavasānam, yathā mālatī-mādhave, madayantikā (tathā kṛtvā)-dummaṇāadi vā iaṃ vāmasīlā | [durmanāyate vā iyaṃ vāma-śīlā |]
body.translated_text: The praise of virtues resulting in fault — as in the <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s>, <s>Madayantikā</s> (doing so): 'Or perhaps this wayward one is troubled.'

body.text: lavaṅgikā-kahaṃ ṇāma ṇava-vahū-vissaṃbhaṇobāajāṇaaṃ laḍahaṃ biaḍḍha-mahura-bhāsaṇaṃ arosaṇaṃ akādaraṃ de bhādaraṃ bhattāraṃ samāsādia dummaṇāissadi me piasahī | [kathaṃ nāma nava-vadhū-visrambhanopāya-jñaṃ laṭahaṃ vidagdha-madhura-bhāṣaṇam aroṣaṇam akātaraṃ te bhrātaraṃ bhartāraṃ samāsādya durmaṇāyiṣyate me priya-sakhī |]
body.translated_text: <s>Lavaṅgikā</s> [in Prakrit]: 'How could my dear friend be troubled upon obtaining your brother as her husband — one who knows the arts of winning a new bride's confidence, who is playful, skilled in sweet and witty speech, not prone to anger, and not faint-hearted?'

body.text: madayantikā-pekkha buddha-rakkhide ! bippadībaṃ ubālabhīāmo | [paśya buddha-rakṣite ! vipratīpam upālabhyāmahe |] [saptamāṅke upakrame]
body.translated_text: <s>Madayantikā</s> [in Prakrit]: 'Look, <s>Buddharakṣitā</s>! We are being reproached in a contrary manner!' (At the beginning of the seventh act)

body.text: ity atra mukhato guṇa-kīrtanam apy antato doṣāyeti garhaṇam idam |
body.translated_text: Here, though on the surface it is the praise of virtues, in the end it results in fault — hence this is <s>Garhaṇa</s>.

body.text:
atha anunayaḥ-
abhyarthanā-paraṃ vākyaṃ vijñeyo' nunayo budhaiḥ ||SRs_3.273|| 119a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Anunaya</s> (entreaty) — A speech primarily consisting of supplication should be known by the wise as <s>Anunaya</s>. ||3.273|| 119a

body.text: yathā veṇi-saṃhāre, dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ-sañjaya ! mad-vacanād brūhi bhāradvājam aśvatthāmānam-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> — <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>: '<s>Sañjaya</s>! On my behalf tell <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, the son of <s>Bhāradvāja</s> —

body.text:
smarati na bhavān pītaṃ stanyaṃ vibhajya sahāmunā
mama ca mṛditaṃ kṣaumaṃ bālye tvad-aṅga-vivartanaiḥ |
anuja-nidhana-sphītāc chokād atipraṇayāc ca yad
vacana-vikṛtiṣv asya krodho mudhā kriyate tvayā ||SRs_3.274|| [ve.saṃ. 5.47]
body.translated_text: 'Do you not remember the breast-milk drunk together with him? And my silk garment crushed in childhood by the tossing of your body? From the grief swollen by the slaying of kinsmen, and from deep affection, if anger is vainly directed at the vocal outbursts of this one — [let it not be so]!' ||3.274|| [<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 5.47]

body.text: ity atra aśvatthāma-prārthanam anunayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the entreaty directed to <s>Aśvatthāman</s> is <s>Anunaya</s>.

body.text:
atha bhraṃśaḥ-
patanaṃ prakṛtād arthād anyasmin bhraṃśa īritaḥ ||SRs_3.275|| 119b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Bhraṃśa</s> (fall/deviation) — The falling from a present state of affairs to another is called <s>Bhraṃśa</s>. ||3.275|| 119b

body.text: yathā prasanna-rāghave, rāvaṇaḥ (saṃvṛtta-nija-rūpaḥ puruṣa-rūpeṇa praviṣṭaḥ |)-kathaya kva tāvat karṇānta-niveśanīya-guṇaṃ kanyā-ratnaṃ kārmukaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Prasanna-rāghava</s> — <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (having resumed his own form, enters in human guise): 'Tell me, where is that jewel of maidens, whose qualities are fit to fill the ear to its end, and the bow?'

body.text: mañjarīkaḥ-idaṃ tāvat kārmukam | kanyā tu caramaṃ locana-patham avatariṣyati |
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjarīka</s>: 'Here is the bow! As for the maiden, she will shortly descend upon the path of your eye.'

body.text: rāvaṇaḥ (sa-saṃrambham)-dhiṅ mūrkha ! kathaṃ re rāśi-nakṣatra-pāṭhakānāṃ goṣṭhīṃ na dṛṣṭavān asi | te' pi kanyām eva prathamaṃ prakaṭayanti | caramaṃ dhanuḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (with vehemence) — Shame on you, fool! Have you not seen the assemblies of astrologers who recite the zodiac signs and asterisms? They too announce the maiden (<s>kanyā</s>, also the zodiac sign Virgo) first and the bow (<s>dhanus</s>, also Sagittarius) last!

body.text: mañjarīkaḥ (svagatam)-katham ayaṃ vācāṭatām eva prakaṭayati | [1.32 padyād anantaram]
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjarīka</s> (aside) — How he displays nothing but loquacity! [After verse 1.32]

body.text: ity atra rāvaṇena [puruṣa-rūpeṇa praviṣṭena] dhanuḥ-kanyayoḥ prakṛtam arthaṃ parityajya rāśi-lakṣaṇasyārthasya prasañjanād ayaṃ bhraṃśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> [who has entered in human form], abandoning the matter at hand concerning the bow and the maiden, introduces the meaning pertaining to the zodiac — this constitutes <s>bhraṃśa</s> (digression).

body.text:
atha leśaḥ-
leśaḥ syād iṅgita-jñāna-kṛd viśeṣaṇavad vacaḥ ||SRs_3.276|| 120a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>leśa</s> (hint) —
<s>Leśa</s> is speech containing qualifying words that produce knowledge of the implied. ||3.276||

body.text: yathā mālatī-mādhave, kāmandakī-
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Mālatī-Mādhava</s>, <s>Kāmandakī</s> [says] —

body.text:
asau vidyāśābhiḥ śiśur api vinirgatya bhavanād
ihāyātaḥ sampraty avikala-śarac-candra-vadanaḥ |
yadāloka-sthāne bhavati puram unmāda-taralaiḥ
kaṭākṣair nārīṇāṃ kuvalayita-vātāyanam iva ||SRs_3.277|| [mā.mā. 2.11]
body.translated_text:
'Having left his home as a mere child out of desire for learning,
he has now arrived here, with a face like the unblemished autumn moon.
When he comes within the range of sight, the city seems
as if its windows were adorned with blue lotuses, by the glances of women mad with desire.' ||3.277|| [<s>Mālatī-Mādhava</s> 2.11]

body.text: ity atra kāmandakyā mālaty-anurāga-jñāna-nivedanasya unmāda-taralair iti viśeṣaṇasya kathanād ayaṃ leśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because <s>Kāmandakī</s> communicates her knowledge of <s>Mālatī</s>'s love through the qualifying expression 'mad with desire,' this constitutes <s>leśa</s>.

body.text:
atra kṣobhaḥ-
kṣobhas tv anya-gate hetāv anyasmin kārya-kalpanaṃ ||SRs_3.278|| 120
body.translated_text:
Now <s>kṣobha</s> (agitation) —
<s>Kṣobha</s> is the attribution of an effect to oneself [when] the cause resides in another. ||3.278||

body.text:
yathā ratnāvalyāṃ, rājā (upasṛtya udbandhanam apanīya)-devi ! kim idaṃ akāryaṃ kriyate ?
mama kaṇṭha-gatāḥ prāṇāḥ pāśe kaṇṭha-gate tava |
anarthārtha-prayatno' yaṃ tyajyatāṃ sāhasaṃ priye ||SRs_3.279|| [ra. 3.16]
atra pāśe vāsavadattā-kaṇṭha-gate tat-kārya-bhūtasya prāṇānāṃ kaṇṭha-gatatvasya vatsa-rājena svasmin kalpanāt kṣobhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, when the noose has reached <s>Vāsavadattā</s>'s throat, the king attributes to himself the effect of that — namely, the vital breaths reaching the throat — hence it is <s>kṣobha</s>.

body.text:
atha manorathaḥ-
manorathas tu vyājena vivakṣita-nivedanam ||SRs_3.280|| 121a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>manoratha</s> (wish-fulfillment) —
<s>Manoratha</s> is the communication of what one wishes to say under a pretext. ||3.280||

body.text: yathā śākuntale, śakuntalā (padāntaraṃ gatvā parivṛtya prakāśam)-ladā-ballaa saṃdāba-hāraa āmaṃtemi tumaṃ bhūobi pairbhoassa | [latā-valaya santāpa-hāraka āmantraye tvāṃ bhūyo' pi paribhogāya |] [3.21 padyād anantaram]
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Śākuntala</s>, <s>Śakuntalā</s> (taking another step, turning around, aloud) — [Prakrit:] 'O bower of creeper-vines, remover of the heat of separation, I bid you farewell for further enjoyment!' [After verse 3.21]

body.text: atra latā-maṇḍapa-vyājena duṣyantāmantraṇaṃ manorathaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the addressing of <s>Duṣyanta</s> under the pretext of the creeper-bower constitutes <s>manoratha</s>.

body.text: atha anukta-siddhiḥ-

children.text: prastāvanaiva śeṣo' rtho yatrānukto' pi gṛhyate | 121
children.translated_text: Where the remaining meaning, though unstated, is grasped merely from the introduction (<s>prastāvanā</s>),

children.text: anukta-siddhir eṣā syād ity āha bharato muniḥ[*21] ||SRs_3.281||
children.translated_text: that is said to be <s>anukta-siddhi</s> — so says the sage <s>Bharata</s>. ||3.281||

body.translated_text: Now <s>anukta-siddhi</s> (implied accomplishment) —
<s>Nāṭya-śāstra</s> 16.169 = 'Where the remaining meaning is not entirely apprehended — that which is understood without being stated is proclaimed as <s>anukta-siddhi</s>.'

body.text: Nāṭ 16.169 = prastāvenaiva śeṣo' rthaḥ kṛtsno yan na pratīyate | vacanena vinānukta-siddhiḥ sā parikīrtitā ||
atha sārūpyaṃ-

children.translated_text: Where [there arises] similarity with objects seen, heard, or experienced,

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ yatra saṅkṣobhāt tat sārūpyaṃ nirūpyate ||SRs_3.282||
children.translated_text: from agitation of mind — that is defined as <s>sārūpya</s>. ||3.282||

body.translated_text: Now <s>sārūpya</s> (resemblance) —

body.text: yathā veṇi-saṃhāre, (praviśya gadā-pāṇiḥ) bhīmaḥ--tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bhīru ! kvādhunā gamyate ? (iti keśeṣu grahītum icchati)
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s>, (entering, mace in hand) <s>Bhīma</s> — 'Stand, stand, coward! Where are you going now?' (He tries to seize [him] by the hair.)

body.text:
yudhiṣṭhiraḥ (balād bhīmam āliṅgya)-durātman ! bhīmārjuna-śatro duryodhana-hataka !
āśaiśavād anudinaṃ janitāparādhaḥ
kṣībo balena bhujayor hata-rāja-putra |
āsādya me' ntaram idaṃ bhuja-pañjarasaya
jīvan prayāsi na padāt padam adya pāpa ||SRs_3.283|| [ve.saṃ. 6.38]
body.translated_text:
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> (forcibly embracing <s>Bhīma</s>) — 'Wicked one! Enemy of <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>! Vile <s>Duryodhana</s>!
"Committing offenses daily since childhood,
intoxicated with the strength of your arms, O slain prince,
having reached the cage of my arms, this inner [space] —
you shall not go alive, step by step, today, O sinner!"' ||3.283|| [<s>Veṇīsaṃhāra</s> 6.38]

body.text: bhīmaḥ-aye katham āryaḥ suyodhana-śaṅkayā nirdayaṃ mām āliṅgati ?
body.translated_text: <s>Bhīma</s> — 'What! Why does the noble one embrace me mercilessly, suspecting me to be <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>)?'

body.text: ity atra cārvāka-śrāvita-duryodhana-vijaya-saṅkathā-saṅkṣepeṇa yudhiṣṭhirādīnāṃ bhīme suyodhana-buddhi-kathanād idaṃ sārūpyam |
body.translated_text: Here, because of the agitation produced by hearing <s>Cārvāka</s>'s account of <s>Duryodhana</s>'s victory, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and the others mistakenly perceive <s>Bhīma</s> as <s>Suyodhana</s> — this constitutes <s>sārūpya</s>.

body.text: atha mālā-

children.translated_text: Where many reasons are stated by the learned
for the accomplishment of the desired aim — that is called <s>mālā</s>. ||3.284||

body.translated_text: Now <s>mālā</s> (garland) —

body.text: yathā dhanañjaya-vijaye-
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Dhanañjaya-vijaya</s> —

body.text:
go-rakṣaṇaṃ sama-daśātrava-māna-bhaṅgaḥ
prītir virāṭa-nṛpater upakāriṇaś ca |
paryāptam ekam api me samartosavāya
sarvaṃ punar militam atra mamaiva bhāgyaiḥ ||SRs_3.285|| [dha.vi. 16]
body.translated_text:
'Protection of the cows, humiliation of the arrogance of the rival of equal might,
and the gratification of King <s>Virāṭa</s>, the benefactor —
any one of these alone is sufficient cause for my festival of battle,
but all have come together here through my fortune!' ||3.285|| [<s>Dhanañjaya-vijaya</s> 16]

body.text: atha madhura-bhāṣaṇam-

children.text: yat prasannena manasā pūjyaṃ pūjayitur vacaḥ | 124
children.translated_text: The speech of one who honors the honorable with a pleased mind,
being a manifestation of praise — that should be known as <s>madhura-bhāṣaṇa</s>. ||3.286||

body.translated_text: Now <s>madhura-bhāṣaṇa</s> (sweet speech) —

body.text:
yathā anargha-rāghave, daśarathaḥ (sapraśrayam)-bhagavan viśvāmitra !
kaccit kāntāra-bhājāṃ bhavati paribhavaḥ ko' pi śauvāpado vā
pratyūhena kratūnāṃ na khalu makha-bhujo bhuñjate vā havīṃṣi |
kartuṃ vā kaccid antar vasati vasumatī-dakṣiṇaḥ sapta-tantur
yat samprāpto' si kiṃ vā raghu-kula-tapasām īdṛśo' yaṃ vivartaḥ ||SRs_3.287|| [a.rā. 1.25]
body.translated_text:
For example, in the <s>Anargha-rāghava</s>, <s>Daśaratha</s> (respectfully) — 'Blessed <s>Viśvāmitra</s>!
"Is there any insult from wild beasts or the like to those dwelling in the forests?
Do not the fire-gods who eat oblations partake of their offerings without obstruction to the sacrifices?
Or does the seven-threaded [sacrificial fire], skilled in the south-gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), dwell within the earth?
Or why have you come? Is this perhaps the ripening of the austerities of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty?"' ||3.287|| [<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.25]

body.text:
viśvāmitraḥ (vihasya)-
janayati tvayi vīra diśāṃ patīn
api gṛhāṅgaṇa-mātra-kuṭumbinaḥ |
ripur iti śrutir eva na vāstavī
pratibhayonnatir astu kutas tu naḥ ||SRs_3.288|| [a.rā. 1.26]
body.translated_text:
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> (laughing) —
'In you, O hero, who beget even the guardians of the directions
as mere householder-kinsmen of your courtyard,
the word "enemy" is merely hearsay, not real;
how could there be anything dreadfully exalted for us?' ||3.288|| [<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.26]

body.text: ity ādāv anyonyaṃ pūjā-vacanaṃ madhura-bhāṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: Here, the mutual words of honor at the beginning constitute <s>madhura-bhāṣaṇa</s>.

body.text:
atha pṛcchā-
praśnenaivottaraṃ yatra sā pṛcchā parikīrtitā ||SRs_3.289|| 125
body.translated_text:
Now <s>pṛcchā</s> (question-as-answer) —
Where the question itself [contains] the answer — that is proclaimed as <s>pṛcchā</s>. ||3.289||

body.text:
yathā-
sarva-kṣiti-bhṛtāṃ nātha dṛṣṭā sarvāṅga-sundarī |
rāmā ramye vanānte' smin mayā virahitā tvayā ||SRs_3.290|| [vi.u. 4.51]
body.translated_text:
For example —
'O lord of all mountains, was the woman, beautiful in every limb,
seen in this lovely forest-edge, separated from me — by you?' ||3.290|| [<s>Vikramorvaśīya</s> 4.51]

body.text: ity atra parvatānāṃ nātha mayā virahitā priyā tvayā dṛṣṭeti praśne rājñāṃ nātha tvayā virahitā mayā dṛṣṭety uttarasya pratīyamānatvād iyaṃ pṛcchā |
body.translated_text: Here, in the question 'O lord of mountains, was my beloved, separated from me, seen by you?' — the answer 'O lord of kings, [the woman] separated from you was seen by me' is implicitly perceived — hence this is <s>pṛcchā</s>.

body.text:
atha upadiṣṭam-
pratigṛhya tu śāstrārthaṃ yad vākyam abhidhīyate |
vidvan-manoharaṃ svantam upadiṣṭaṃ tad ucyate ||SRs_3.291|| 126
body.translated_text:
Now <s>upadiṣṭa</s> (advice grounded in scripture) —
Speech uttered after accepting the meaning of the <s>śāstras</s>,
charming to the minds of the learned and heartfelt — that is called <s>upadiṣṭa</s>. ||3.291||

body.text: yathā śākuntale, śakuntalā (bhayaṃ nāṭayantī)-paurava rakkha abiṇaaṃ | maaṇa-saṃtattābi ṇa hu attaṇo pahabāmi | [paurava rakṣa avinayam | madana-santaptāpi na khalv ātmanaḥ prabhavāmi |]
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Śākuntala</s>, <s>Śakuntalā</s> (feigning fear) — [Prakrit:] 'O <s>Paurava</s>, protect [my] modesty! Even though tormented by <s>Madana</s> (the God of Love), I am indeed not my own mistress!'

body.text:
rājā-bhīru alaṃ guru-janād bhayena | na te vidita-dharmā hi bhagavān doṣam atra grahīṣyati kulapatiḥ | api ca-
gāndharveṇa vivāhena bahvyo rājarṣi-kanyakāḥ |
śrūyante pariṇītās tāḥ pitṛbhiś cānumoditāḥ ||SRs_3.292|| [a.śa. 3.20]
body.translated_text:
The King — 'O timid one, enough of fear of elders! For the venerable chief of the hermitage, who knows the <s>dharma</s>, will not blame [us] in this matter. Moreover —
"By the <s>Gāndharva</s> (mutual consent) rite of marriage, many daughters of royal sages
are heard to have been wed, and their fathers approved."' ||3.292|| [<s>Abhijñāna-śākuntala</s> 3.20]

body.text: ity atra śāstrānurodhenaiva pravṛttatvād idam upadiṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Here, since [the King] has proceeded in accordance with the <s>śāstra</s>, this is <s>upadiṣṭa</s>.

body.text:
atha dṛṣṭam-
yathādeśaṃ yathā-kālaṃ yathā-rūpaṃ ca varṇyate |
yat pratyakṣaṃ parokṣaṃ vā tad dṛṣṭam dṛṣṭavan matam ||SRs_3.293|| 127
body.translated_text:
Now <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (the seen) —
That which is described as it is — according to place, time, and form —
whether directly perceived or inferred — that is considered <s>dṛṣṭa</s> by those of [good] vision. ||3.293||

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre, rājā-aho sarvāsv avasthāsu cārutā śobhāntaraṃ puṣyati | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s>, the King — 'Ah, in all states, her beauty gains fresh dimensions of splendor! For indeed —

body.text:
vāmaṃ sandhi-stimita-valayaṃ nyasya hastaṃ nitambe
kṛtvā śyāmā-viṭapa-sadṛśaṃ srasta-muktaṃ dvitīyam |
pādāṅguṣṭhālulita-kusume kuṭṭime pātitākṣaṃ
nṛttād asyāḥ sthitam atitarāṃ kāntam ṛjvāyatārdham ||SRs_3.294|| [mā.a.mi. 2.6]
body.translated_text:
'Placing her left hand, with bracelet stilled at the wrist-joint, on her hip,
keeping the other [hand] hanging loose, resembling a <s>śyāmā</s>-vine's branch,
with her gaze cast down upon the flower-strewn floor touched by her big toe —
her standing posture after the dance is exceedingly lovely, half-upright and half-extended.' ||3.294|| [<s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 2.6]

body.text: ity atra itara-samakṣaṃ sthitāyāḥ saṃsthāna-jāti-varṇanād idaṃ pratyakṣa-dṛṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Here, because this describes the form and nature of one standing in the sight of the other, this is directly perceived <s>dṛṣṭa</s>.

body.text: apratyakṣa-dṛṣṭaṃ, yathā padmāvatyāṃ-
body.translated_text: The indirectly perceived <s>dṛṣṭa</s>, for example, in the <s>Padmāvatī</s> —

children.translated_text: With lotus-feet crossed, in the beauty of a triple-bend posture,
with the mass of hair loosened over the shoulders,
wearing a peacock-feather crest, clasping a bamboo flute,
I attain a new and special compassion-inducing enchantment. ||3.295||

body.text: ity atra apratyakṣasyaiva gopāla-sundarasya saṃsthāna-viśeṣa-jāti-varṇanād api dṛṣṭavad ābhāsanād idam apratyakṣa-dṛṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Here, because this describes the specific form and nature of <s>Gopāla-sundara</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) who is not directly present, yet appears as if seen, this is indirectly perceived <s>dṛṣṭa</s>.

body.text:
śrī-siṃha-bhūpena kavīśvarāṇāṃ
viśrāṇitāneka-vibhūṣaṇena |
ṣaṭ-triṃśad uktāni hi bhūṣaṇāni
sa-lakṣma-lakṣyāṇi muner matena ||SRs_3.296|| 128
body.translated_text:
By King <s>Śrī-Siṃha-bhūpa</s>, who bestowed many ornaments upon the lords of poets,
thirty-six ornaments have been stated,
recognizable by their marks, according to the sage's doctrine. ||3.296||

body.text:
sākṣad evopadeśena prāyo dharma-samanvayāt |
aṅgāṅgi-bhāva-sampanna-samasta-rasa-saṃśrayāt ||SRs_3.297|| 129
prakṛty-avasthā-sandhyādi-sampatty-upanibandhanāt |
āhuḥ prakaraṇādīnāṃ nāṭakaṃ prakṛtiṃ budhāḥ ||SRs_3.298|| 130
atideśa-bala-prāpata-nāṭakāṅgopajīvanāt |
anyāni rūpakāṇi syur vikārā nāṭakaṃ prati ||SRs_3.299|| 131
ato hi lakṣaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ nāṭakasyābhidhīyate |
divyena vā mānuṣeṇa dhīrodāttena saṃyutam ||SRs_3.300|| 132
śṛṅgāra-vīrānyatara-pradhāna-rasa-saṃśrayam |
khyāteti vṛtta-sambaddhaṃ sandhi-pañcaka-saṃyutam ||SRs_3.301|| 133
prakṛty-avasthā-sandhy-aṅga-sandhy-antara-vibhūṣaṇaiḥ |
patākā-sthānakair vṛtti-tad-aṅgaiś ca pravṛttibhiḥ ||SRs_3.302|| 134
viṣkambhakādibhir yuktaṃ nāṭakaṃ tat trivargadam |
tad etan nāṭakārambha-prakāro vakṣyate mayā ||SRs_3.303|| 135
vidher yathaiva saṅkalpo mukhatāṃ pratipadyate |
pradhānasya prabandhasya tathā prastāvanā smṛtā ||SRs_3.304|| 136
arthasya pratipādyasya tīrthaṃ prastāvanocyate |
prastāvanāyās tu mukhe nāndī kāryā śubhāvahā ||SRs_3.305|| 137
āśīrnamaskriyā-vastunirdeśānyatamā smṛtā |
candranāmāṅkitā prāyo maṅgalārtha-padojjvalā ||SRs_3.306|| 138
aṣṭābhir daśabhiś ceṣṭā seyaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ padaiḥ |
samair vā viṣamair vāpi prayojyety apare jaguḥ ||SRs_3.307|| 139
body.translated_text:
Because of direct instruction itself, primarily through the connection with <s>dharma</s>,
because of being endowed with the principal-subsidiary relation of all <s>rasas</s>, ||3.297||
because of being grounded in <s>prakṛtis</s> (source-elements), <s>avasthās</s> (stages), <s>sandhis</s> (junctures), and the like,
the learned call <s>Nāṭaka</s> (drama) the original form of <s>prakaraṇa</s> and other [dramatic genres]. ||3.298||
By the force of extension, the other <s>rūpakas</s> (dramatic forms),
which subsist on the elements of <s>Nāṭaka</s>, would be modifications of <s>Nāṭaka</s>. ||3.299||
Therefore, the definition of <s>Nāṭaka</s> is stated first:
endowed with a hero of divine or human [nature], of the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (noble-spirited) type, ||3.300||
having as its support <s>rasa</s> with either <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> or <s>Vīra</s> as predominant,
connected with a well-known (<s>khyāta</s>) story (<s>vṛtta</s>), furnished with the five junctures, ||3.301||
with <s>prakṛtis</s>, <s>avasthās</s>, <s>sandhi</s>-elements, <s>sandhi</s>-interstices, and ornaments,
with <s>patākā</s>-episodes (<s>sub-plots</s>), <s>sthānakas</s> (situations), <s>vṛttis</s> (dramatic modes),
their elements, and <s>pravṛttis</s> (regional usages), ||3.302||
furnished with <s>viṣkambhaka</s> (interlude) and the like — that is <s>Nāṭaka</s>, bestowing the three goals of life.
The manner of commencing a <s>Nāṭaka</s> shall now be described by me: ||3.303||
Just as the creator's intention assumes the function of a beginning,
so the <s>prastāvanā</s> (prologue) is regarded as [the beginning] of the principal composition. ||3.304||
The <s>prastāvanā</s> is called the 'ford' for the subject to be conveyed.
At the opening of the <s>prastāvanā</s>, the <s>Nāndī</s> (benediction), bringing auspiciousness, is to be performed. ||3.305||
It is known as [comprising] any of the following: blessing, salutation, or statement of the subject-matter;
it is mostly marked with the name of the moon (<s>Candra</s>), and resplendent with words signifying auspiciousness. ||3.306||
This should be composed in eight, ten, or twelve <s>padas</s> (metrical feet);
others say it may be in even or odd [number of feet]. ||3.307||

body.text: tatrāśīr-anvitā nāndī yathābhirāma-rāghave-
body.translated_text: Among these, a <s>Nāndī</s> containing a blessing — for example, in the <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s> —

children.translated_text: May the sidelong glances of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), who has arisen from his serpent-couch,
which are waves braided with the <s>rasa</s> of compassion and affection,
which are friends of the beauty of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s playful lotus-petals,
smiling with the essence of nectar, obtainable only through exceptional good conduct, bring you welfare! ||3.308||

body.text: namaskriyāvatī nāndī, yathā uttara-rāma-carite-
body.translated_text: A <s>Nāndī</s> containing salutation — for example, in the <s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> —

body.text:
idaṃ kavibhyaḥ pūrvebhyah namo-vākaṃ praśāsmahe |
vandemahi ca tāṃ vāṇīm amṛtām ātmanaḥ kalām ||SRs_3.309|| [u.rā.ca. 1.1]
body.translated_text:
'To those earlier poets, we offer this word of homage;
and we salute that divine <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>), the nectar-portion of the Self.' ||3.309|| [<s>Uttara-rāma-carita</s> 1.1]

body.text: vastu-nirdeśavatī nāndī, yathā prabodha-candrodaye-
body.translated_text: A <s>Nāndī</s> containing statement of the subject-matter — for example, in the <s>Prabodha-candrodaya</s> —

body.text:
antar-nāḍī-niyamita-marul-laṅghita-brahma-randhraṃ
svānte śānti-praṇayini samunmīlad-ānanda-sāndram |
pratyag-jyotir jayati yaminaḥ spaṣṭa-lālāṭa-netra-
vyāja-vyaktīkṛtam iva jagad-vyāpi candrārdha-mauleḥ ||SRs_3.310|| [pra.ca. 1.2]
body.translated_text:
'Victorious is the inner light of the ascetic — with breath regulated through the inner channels and transcending the <s>brahma-randhra</s>,
dense with delight unfolding in the mind that is devoted to peace,
as if made visible through the semblance of the manifest forehead-eye
of the Half-moon-crested one (<s>Śiva</s>), world-pervading!' ||3.310|| [<s>Prabodha-candrodaya</s> 1.2]

body.text: aṣṭā-padānvitā, yathā mahāvīra-carite-
body.translated_text: One with eight <s>padas</s> — for example, in the <s>Mahāvīra-carita</s> —

body.text:
atha svasthāya devāya nityāya hata-pāpmane |
tyakta-krama-vibhāgāya caitanya-jyotiṣe namaḥ ||SRs_3.311|| [ma.vī.ca. 1.1]
body.translated_text:
'Salutation to the Self-established, divine, eternal, destroyer of sin,
who has transcended the divisions of sequence — the light of consciousness!' ||3.311|| [<s>Mahāvīra-carita</s> 1.1]

body.text: daśa-padānvitā yathā abhirāma-rāghave kriyāsuḥ kalyāṇam ity ādi | dvādaśa-padānvitā, yathā anargha-rāghave-
body.translated_text: One with ten <s>padas</s> — for example, in the <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s> — 'May the sidelong glances bring welfare...' etc. [as above]. One with twelve <s>padas</s> — for example, in the <s>Anargha-rāghava</s> —

body.text:
niṣpratyūham upāsmahe bhagavataḥ kaumodakī-lakṣmaṇaḥ
koka-prīti-cakora-pāraṇa-paṭū jyotiṣmatī locane |
yābhyām ardha-vibodha-mugdha-madhura-śrīr ardha-nidrāyito
nābhī-palvala-puṇḍarīka-mukulaḥ kamboḥ sapatnī-kṛtaḥ ||SRs_3.312|| [a.rā. 1.1]
body.translated_text:
'Without obstruction, may we worship the blessed one — whose marks are the <s>Kaumodakī</s> (mace),
whose luminous eyes are skilled in delighting the <s>cakora</s>-bird love of the <s>cakravāka</s>;
[he] whose beauty, half-awakened and charmingly bewildered, is drowsily
reduced to rivalry with the conch by the bud of the lotus in the pool of his navel.' ||3.312|| [<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.1]

body.text: atraiva maṅgalārtha-pada-prāyatvaṃ candranāmāṅkitatvaṃ ca draṣṭavyam |
body.translated_text: Here, the predominance of words signifying auspiciousness and the presence of the name [of a deity] marked with the word 'moon' (chandra) should be observed.

body.text:
nāndy-ante tu praviṣṭena sūtradhāreṇa dhīmatā |
prasādhanāya raṅgasya vṛttir yojyā hi bhāratī ||SRs_3.313|| 140
aṅgāny asyāś ca catvāri bharatenāvabhāṣire |
prarocanāmukhe caiva vīthī-prahasane iti ||SRs_3.314|| 141
vīthī prahasanaṃ sva-sva-prasaṅge vakṣyate sphuṭam |
prarocanā tu sā proktā prakṛtārtha-praśaṃsayā ||SRs_3.315|| 142
sadasya-citta-vṛttīnāṃ saṃmukhīkaraṇaṃ ca yat |

children.translated_text: Commendation should be known as twofold: pertaining to sentient and insentient [objects].
The insentient [objects] are place and time; and the time [refers to seasons] such as spring and autumn. ||SRs_3.316||

body.translated_text: At the conclusion of the <s>nāndī</s>, the wise <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage-manager), having entered for the preparation of the performance-space, should employ the <s>Bhāratī</s> mode. ||SRs_3.313|| Its four elements were declared by <s>Bharata</s> to be: <s>prarocanā</s> (anticipatory delight), <s>āmukha</s> (prologue), <s>vīthī</s> (lane), and <s>prahasana</s> (farce). ||SRs_3.314|| The <s>vīthī</s> and <s>prahasana</s> will be described clearly in their respective contexts. <s>Prarocanā</s>, however, is defined as: that which, through the commendation of the subject at hand, ||SRs_3.315|| turns the mental dispositions of the audience in its direction.

body.text: tatra vasanta-praśaṃsayā prarocanā, yathā padmāvatyāṃ-
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>prarocanā</s> through the commendation of spring, for example, in <s>Padmāvatī</s> —

children.translated_text: With thorns of sparkling buds, buzzing with the humming of bees,
with swaying clusters for breasts, with constantly shaken young-shoot lips —
the creeper-brides, exceedingly passionate devotees of the mango trees on the neighboring branches,
embrace [them] with their arm-like boughs at the beloved rise of spring. ||SRs_3.317||

body.text: śarat-praśaṃse, yathā veṇī-saṃhāre-
body.translated_text: In the commendation of autumn, for example, in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> —

body.text:
sat-pakṣāṃ madhura-giraḥ prasādhitāśā madoddhatārambhāḥ |
nipatanti dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ kāla-vaśān medinī-pṛṣṭhe ||SRs_3.318|| [ve.saṃ. 1.6]
body.translated_text: Having good wings [allies], sweet-voiced, with hopes adorned, with undertakings impelled by pride — the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, by the power of time, fall upon the surface of the earth. ||SRs_3.318|| [<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 1.6]

body.text: atha deśaḥ
body.translated_text: Now, place —

body.text: deśas tu devatārāja-tīrtha-sthānādir ucyate | 144
body.translated_text: Place is said to refer to deities, kings, sacred sites, and the like.

body.text: tad adya kāla-nāthasya yātretyādiṣu lakṣyatām ||SRs_3.319||
body.translated_text: 'Today, at the festival-procession of the Lord of Time...' — in such [instances] it may be observed. ||SRs_3.319||

body.text: cetanās tu kathā-nātha-kavi-sabhya-naṭāḥ smṛtāḥ | 145
body.translated_text: The sentient [subjects of commendation] are remembered as: the subject of the story, the poet, the audience, and the actors.

body.text: kathā-nāthās tu dharmārtha-rasa-mokṣopayoginaḥ ||SRs_3.320||
body.translated_text: The subjects of stories serve the purposes of <s>Dharma</s> (duty), <s>Artha</s> (wealth), <s>Rasa</s> (aesthetic pleasure), and <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation). ||SRs_3.320||

body.text: dharmopayoginas tatra yudhiṣṭhira-nalādayaḥ | 146
body.translated_text: Of these, those serving <s>Dharma</s> are <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Nala</s>, and the like.

body.text: arthopayogino rudra-narasiṃha-nṛpādayaḥ ||SRs_3.321||
body.translated_text: Those serving <s>Artha</s> are <s>Rudra</s>, King <s>Narasiṃha</s>, and the like. ||SRs_3.321||

body.text: rasopayogino vidyādhara-vatseśvarādayaḥ | 147
body.translated_text: Those serving <s>Rasa</s> are <s>Vidyādharas</s>, the lord of <s>Vatsa</s> (<s>Udayana</s>), and the like.

body.text: mokṣopayogino rāma-vāsudevādayo matāḥ ||SRs_3.322||
body.translated_text: Those serving <s>Mokṣa</s> are considered to be <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), and the like. ||SRs_3.322||

body.text: eke tv abhedam icchanti dharma-mokṣopayoginoḥ ||SRs_3.323|| 148
body.translated_text: Some, however, hold that there is no distinction between those serving <s>Dharma</s> and those serving <s>Mokṣa</s>. ||SRs_3.323||

body.text: caturvidhāḥ kavayaḥ
body.translated_text: The four types of poets

body.text:
kavayas tu prabandhāras te bhaveyuś caturvidhāḥ |
udātta uddhataḥ prauḍho vinīta iti bhedataḥ ||SRs_3.324|| 149
body.translated_text: — Poets are the composers of literary works; they are of four kinds, distinguished as: <s>udātta</s> (the dignified), <s>uddhata</s> (the bold), <s>prauḍha</s> (the mature), and <s>vinīta</s> (the modest). ||SRs_3.324||

body.text:
tatra udāttaḥ-
antar-gūḍhābhimānoktir udātta iti gīyate ||SRs_3.325|| 150a
body.translated_text: Of these, the dignified (<s>udātta</s>) — He whose expression of self-regard is inwardly concealed — that is celebrated as <s>udātta</s>. ||SRs_3.325||

body.text: yathā mālavikāgnimitre-
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> —

body.text:
purāṇam ity eva na sādhu sarvaṃ
na cāpi kāvyaṃ navam ity avadyam |
santaḥ parīkṣyāntarad bhajante
mūḍhaḥ para-pratyayaneya-buddhiḥ ||SRs_3.326|| [mā.a.mi. 1.2]
body.translated_text: 'Not everything is good simply because it is old, nor is a poem contemptible merely because it is new. The wise examine and then adopt [what is worthy]; the fool's judgment depends on the authority of others.' ||SRs_3.326|| [<s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 1.2]

body.text: atra santaḥ parīkṣety anena sva-kṛteḥ parīkṣaṇa-kṣamatva-kalpito nija-garvaḥ kāli-dāsena vivakṣita iti tasyodāttatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the words 'the wise examine,' <s>Kālidāsa</s> intends his own pride, based on the worthiness of his composition for examination — thus his <s>udātta</s> nature.

body.text:
atha uddhataḥ-
parāpavādāt svotkarṣa-vādī tūddhata ucyate ||SRs_3.327|| 150
body.translated_text: Now, the bold (<s>uddhata</s>) — He who asserts his own superiority through the censure of others — that is called <s>uddhata</s>. ||SRs_3.327||

body.text:
yathā mālatī-mādhave-
ye nāma kecid iha naḥ prathayanty avajñāṃ
jānanti te kim api tān prati naiṣa yatnaḥ |
utpatsyate' sti mama ko' pi samāna-dharmā
kālo hy ayaṃ niravadhir vipulā ca pṛthvī ||SRs_3.328|| [mā.mā. 1.8]
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> — 'Those who vaunt their disregard for us here — do they know anything? No effort [of mine] is directed at them. Someone equal to me in qualities will arise [in the future] — for time is infinite and the earth is vast.' ||SRs_3.328|| [<s>Mālatī-mādhava</s> 1.8]

body.text: atra jānanti te kim apīti parāpavādāt mama tu ko' pi samāna-dharmety ātmotkarṣa-kathanāc ca bhavabhūter uddhatatvam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the censure of others with 'do they know anything?' and the assertion of his own superiority with 'someone equal to me,' <s>Bhavabhūti</s>'s nature is <s>uddhata</s>.

body.text:
yathā prauḍhaḥ-
yathocita-nijotkarṣa-vādī prauḍha itīritaḥ ||SRs_3.329|| 151a
body.translated_text: Now, the mature (<s>prauḍha</s>) — He who asserts his own superiority in a fitting manner — that is called <s>prauḍha</s>. ||SRs_3.329||

body.text: yathā karuṇākandale-

children.translated_text: The poet <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, whose own fame is ever awake to the world's end,
a connoisseur who is a veritable provocateur in the handling of the essentials of the series of <s>rasas</s> —
in the art of delighting the hearts of connoisseurs through his words,
the grandeur of his composition matures into an essence of abundant bliss. ||SRs_3.330||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Karuṇā-kandala</s> —

body.text: atra rasa-prauḍhi-sandarbha-prasādayor nāṭaka-nirmāṇocitayor eva kathanāt nijotkarṣaṃ prakaṭayann ayaṃ kaviḥ prauḍha ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: Here, because this poet makes manifest his own superiority by proclaiming only those [qualities] — profundity in <s>rasa</s> and clarity of composition — that are fitting for the creation of a drama, he is called <s>prauḍha</s>.

body.text: yuktyā nijotkarṣa-vādī prauḍha ity aparaiḥ smṛtaḥ ||SRs_3.331|| 151
body.translated_text: He who asserts his own superiority through reasoning is considered <s>prauḍha</s> by others. ||SRs_3.331||

body.text: yathā mamaiva-nedānīntana-dīpikā kim u tamaḥ-saṅghātam unmūlayed ity ādi [rasārṇava-sudhākare 1.55] |
body.translated_text: For example, from my own [work] — 'Would a lamp of the present age uproot the mass of darkness?' and so forth [<s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s> 1.55].

body.text: atra jyotsnādi-dṛṣṭānta-mukhena mādhuryaujaḥ-prasādākhyānāṃ guṇānāṃ sva-sāhityaṃ rasaucityena [sattāṃ] pratipādayann ayaṃ kaviḥ prauḍha ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: Here, because this poet, through the illustrations of moonlight and the like, establishes the existence of the qualities called <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), and <s>prasāda</s> (clarity) in his own literary work with propriety of <s>rasa</s>, he is called <s>prauḍha</s>.

body.text:
atha vinītaḥ-
vinīto vinayotkarṣāt svāpakarṣa-prakāśakaḥ ||SRs_3.332|| 152a
body.translated_text: Now, the modest (<s>vinīta</s>) — The <s>vinīta</s> is he who, through an excess of modesty, reveals his own inferiority. ||SRs_3.332||

body.text: yathā rāmānande-

children.translated_text: 'No quality whatsoever can be found in my verbal composition,
even if searched for with effort;
yet the good, out of affection,
honor this literary work on the story of <s>Rāma</s>.' ||SRs_3.333||

body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Rāmānanda</s> —

body.text: atra vinayotkarṣād apakarṣam ātmany āropayann ayaṃ kavir vinīta ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: Here, because this poet attributes inferiority to himself through an excess of modesty, he is called <s>vinīta</s>.

body.text: atha sabhyāḥ-

children.text: sabhyās tu vibudhair jñeyā ye didṛkṣānivtā janāḥ | 152
children.translated_text: The audience should be understood by the learned as those people who come motivated by the desire to see.

children.text: te' pi dvidhā prārthanīyāḥ prārthak iti ca sphuṭam ||SRs_3.334||
children.translated_text: They too are clearly of two kinds: those who are to be solicited (<s>prārthanīya</s>) and those who solicit (<s>prārthaka</s>). ||SRs_3.334||

body.translated_text: Now, the audience (<s>sabhyāḥ</s>) —

body.text: idaṃ prayokṣye yuṣmābhir anujñā dīyatām iti | 153
body.translated_text: 'I propose to perform this [play]; may your permission be given' —

body.text: samprārthyāḥ sūtradhāreṇa prārthanīyā iti smṛtāḥ ||SRs_3.335||
body.translated_text: those who are thus entreated by the <s>sūtradhāra</s> are regarded as the 'solicited.' ||SRs_3.335||

body.text: tvayā prayogaḥ kriyatām ity utkaṇṭhita-cetasaḥ | 154
body.translated_text: 'Let the performance be given by you!' — those with eager minds

body.text: ye sūtriṇaṃ prārthayante te sabhyāḥ prārthakāḥ smṛtāh ||SRs_3.336||
body.translated_text: who thus entreat the <s>sūtradhāra</s> — those audience members are regarded as the 'solicitors.' ||SRs_3.336||

body.text: atha naṭāḥ-

children.text: raṅgopajīvinaḥ proktā naṭās te' pi tridhā smṛtāḥ | 155
children.translated_text: Those who make their livelihood from the stage are called actors; they too are remembered as threefold by experts:

children.text: vādakā gāyakāś caiva nartakāś ceti kovidaiḥ ||SRs_3.337||
children.translated_text: instrumentalists (<s>vādaka</s>), singers (<s>gāyaka</s>), and dancers (<s>nartaka</s>). ||SRs_3.337||

body.translated_text: Now, the actors (<s>naṭāḥ</s>) —

body.text: vīṇā-veṇu-mṛdaṅgādi-vādakā vādakāḥ smṛtāḥ | 156
body.translated_text: The players of <s>vīṇā</s>, flute, <s>mṛdaṅga</s>, and the like are called instrumentalists.

body.text:
ālāpana-dhruvāgīta-gāyakā gāyakā matāḥ |
nānā-prakārābhinaya-kartāro nartakāḥ smṛtāḥ ||SRs_3.338|| 157
body.translated_text: Those who sing <s>ālāpana</s> (free vocal improvisation), <s>dhruvā</s> (set songs), and other songs are considered singers. Those who perform various kinds of <s>abhinaya</s> (dramatic representation) are called dancers. ||SRs_3.338||

body.text:
tad evam-
vistarād uta saṅkṣepāt prayuñjīta prarocanām ||SRs_3.339|| 158a
body.translated_text: Thus — One should employ the <s>prarocanā</s> either at length or in brief. ||SRs_3.339||

body.text: tatra saṅkṣiptā prarocanā, yathā ratnāvalyām-
body.translated_text: Of these, a brief <s>prarocanā</s>, for example, in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> —

body.text:
śrīharṣo nipuṇaḥ kaviḥ pariṣad apy eṣā guṇa-grāhiṇī
loke hāri ca vatsa-rāja-caritaṃ nāṭye ca dakṣā vayam |
vastv-ekaikam apīha vāñchita-phala-prāpteḥ padaṃ kiṃ punar
mad-bhāgyopacayād ayaṃ samuditaḥ sarvo guṇānāṃ gaṇaḥ ||SRs_3.340|| [ra. 1.6]
body.translated_text: 'The illustrious <s>Harṣa</s> is a skilled poet; this assembly too appreciates merit; the story of <s>Vatsa-rāja</s> is delightful in the world; and we are skilled in dramatic art. Even a single one of these would be a ground for attaining the desired fruit — how much more, then, when by the increase of my good fortune, this entire assemblage of virtues has come together!' ||SRs_3.340|| [<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 1.6]

body.text: atra kathā-nāyaka-kavi-sabhya-naṭānāṃ catūrṇāṃ saṅkṣepeṇa varṇanād iyaṃ saṅkṣipta-prarocanā | vistarāt tu bāla-rāmāyaṇādiṣu draṣṭavyā |
body.translated_text: Here, because the four — the subject of the story, the poet, the audience, and the actors — are described in brief, this is a brief <s>prarocanā</s>. The detailed version should be observed in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> and the like.

body.text: evaṃ prarocayan sabhyān sūtrī kuryād athāmukham | 158
body.translated_text: Thus having delighted the audience, the <s>sūtradhāra</s> should then proceed to the <s>āmukha</s> (prologue).

body.text: sūtra-dhāro naṭīṃ brūte sva-kāryaṃ prati yuktitaḥ ||SRs_3.341||
body.translated_text: The <s>sūtradhāra</s> speaks to the <s>naṭī</s> (actress), skillfully [directing the discourse] toward the matter at hand. ||SRs_3.341||

body.text: prastutākṣepa-citroktyā yat tad āmukham īritam | 159
body.translated_text: That which introduces the subject at hand through striking utterances — that is called <s>āmukha</s>.

body.text: trīṇyāmukhāṅgāny ucyante kathodghātaḥ pravartakaḥ ||SRs_3.342||
body.translated_text: Three elements of the <s>āmukha</s> are stated: <s>kathodghāta</s> (opening of the story), <s>pravartaka</s> (impeller), ||SRs_3.342||

body.text: prayogātiśayaś ceti teṣāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate | 160
body.translated_text: and <s>prayogātiśaya</s> (dramatic transition) — their definitions are now stated.

body.text:
sūtriṇo vākyam arthaṃ vā svetivṛtta-samaṃ yadā |
svīkṛtya praviśet pātraṃ kathodghāto dvidhā mataḥ ||SRs_3.343|| 161
body.translated_text: When a character enters, taking up a sentence or meaning of the <s>sūtradhāra</s>'s that corresponds to the plot — <s>kathodghāta</s> is considered twofold. ||SRs_3.343||

body.text:
tatra vākyena kathodghāto, yathā ratnāvalyāṃ-
dvīpād anyasmād api madhyād api jala-nidher diśo' py antāt |
ānīya jhaṭiti ghaṭayati vidhir abhimatam abhimukhī-bhūtaḥ ||SRs_3.344|| [ra. 1.7]
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>kathodghāta</s> by sentence, for example, in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> — 'Even from another island, even from the midst of the ocean, even from the end of a direction — having swiftly brought it together, Destiny, when favorably inclined, quickly arranges the desired [outcome].' ||SRs_3.344|| [<s>Ratnāvalī</s> 1.7]

body.text: iti sūtradhārasya priyā-samāśvāsana-vākyaṃ svasyānukūlatayā paṭhato yaugandharāyaṇasya praveśāt kathodghātaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s>'s entry while reciting the <s>sūtradhāra</s>'s words of reassurance to his beloved as if favorable to himself constitutes <s>kathodghāta</s>.

body.text: arthena kathodghāto, yathā veṇī-saṃhāraḥ-
body.translated_text: The <s>kathodghāta</s> by meaning, for example, in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> —

body.text:
nirvāṇa-vaira-dahanāḥ praśamādarīṇāṃ
nandantu pāṇḍu-tanayāḥ saha mādhavena |
rakta-prasādhita-bhuvaḥ kṣata-vigrahāś ca
svasthā bhavantu kuru-rāja-sutāḥ sa-bhṛtyāḥ ||SRs_3.345|| [ve.saṃ. 1.7]
body.translated_text: 'May the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, together with <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), whose fire of enmity is extinguished, who delight in the caves of tranquility, rejoice! And may the sons of the <s>Kuru</s> king, together with their retainers, with bodies wounded and the earth adorned with their blood, be at peace!' ||SRs_3.345|| [<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 1.7]

body.text: atrottarārdhe sūtradhāreṇa dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ svarga-sthiti-nirupadrava-lakṣaṇayor arthayor vivakṣitayoḥ satoḥ bhīmena svasthā bhavantu mayi jīvati dhārtarāṣṭrā iti nirupadrava-lakṣaṇasyaivārtha-viśeṣasya grahaṇena praveśaḥ kṛta iti ayam arthena kathodghātaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, in the latter half, while the <s>sūtradhāra</s> intended the two meanings — the heavenly state of the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s> and their freedom from trouble — <s>Bhīma</s> enters by grasping only the specific meaning of 'freedom from trouble,' [interpreting it as] 'let the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s> be free from trouble while I am alive!' — this is <s>kathodghāta</s> by meaning.

body.text:
atha pravartakaḥ-
ākṣiptaṃ kāla-sāmyena pravṛttiḥ syāt pravartakam ||SRs_3.346|| 162a
body.translated_text: Now <s>pravartaka</s> (impeller) — That which introduces [a character] through a correspondence of season — that is <s>pravartaka</s>. ||SRs_3.346||

body.text:
yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe-
prakaṭita-rāmāmbhojaḥ kauśikavān sapadi lakṣmaṇānandī |
śara-cāpa-namana-hetor ayam avatīrṇaḥ śarat-samayaḥ ||SRs_3.347|| [bā.rā. 1.16]
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> — 'Having manifested the lotus of <s>Rāma</s>, accompanied by <s>Kauśika</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>), with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>'s joy, this autumn season has descended — for the bending of the bow with the arrow.' ||SRs_3.347|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 1.16]

body.text: atra viśvāmitra-rāma-lakṣmaṇānāṃ śarat-samaya-varṇana-sāmyena praveśaḥ pravartakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, the entry of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> through the correspondence with the description of the autumn season constitutes <s>pravartaka</s>.

body.text: atha prayogātiśayaḥ --

children.translated_text: Through an introduction of the form 'Here he is' or 'This is he,' from the <s>sūtradhāra</s>'s performance,
where the performance is signaled — that indeed is <s>prayogātiśaya</s>. ||SRs_3.348||

body.translated_text: Now <s>prayogātiśaya</s> (dramatic transition) —

body.text:
yathā mālavikāgnimitre-
śirasā prathama-gṛhītām ājñām icchāmi pariṣadaḥ kartum |
devyā iva dhāriṇyāḥ sevā-dakṣaḥ parijano' yam ||SRs_3.349|| [mā.a.mi. 1.3]
body.translated_text: For example, in the <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> — 'I wish to carry out the command that was first received with bowed head, of the assembly. This attendant (<s>parijana</s>) is skilled in the service of the Queen <s>Dhāriṇī</s>.' ||SRs_3.349|| [<s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s> 1.3]

body.text: atrāyam ity upakṣepeṇākṣiptaḥ parijana-praveśaḥ prayogātiśayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the entry of the attendant introduced by the word 'this' constitutes <s>prayogātiśaya</s>.

body.text:
tathā ca śākuntale-
tavāsmi gīta-rāgeṇa hāriṇā prasabhaṃ hṛtaḥ |
eṣa rājeva duṣyantaḥ sāraṅgeṇātiraṃhasā ||SRs_3.350|| [a.śā. 1.5]
body.translated_text: And similarly in the <s>Śākuntala</s> — 'I have been forcibly captivated by the charming melody of your song. Here, like a swift deer, King <s>Duṣyanta</s> [approaches] at great speed.' ||SRs_3.350|| [<s>Abhijñāna-śākuntala</s> 1.5]

body.text: ity atra eṣa ity upakṣipto duṣyanta-praveśaḥ prayogātiśayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the entry of <s>Duṣyanta</s> introduced by the word 'here' constitutes <s>prayogātiśaya</s>.

body.text: prastāvanā-sthāpaneti dvidhā syād idam āmukham | 163
body.translated_text: This <s>āmukha</s> is of two kinds: <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction) and <s>sthāpanā</s> (establishment).

body.text: vidūṣaka-naṭī-pāripārśvikaiḥ saha saṃlāpan ||SRs_3.351||
body.translated_text: Where the <s>sūtradhāra</s>, conversing with the <s>Vidūṣaka</s>, <s>Naṭī</s> (actress), or <s>Pāripārśvika</s> (assistant), ||SRs_3.351||

body.text: stoka-vīthy-aṅga-sahitāny āmukhāṅgāni sūtra-bhṛt | 164
body.translated_text: employs the <s>āmukha</s> elements accompanied by a few <s>vīthī</s> elements —

body.text: yojayed yatra nāṭya-jñair eṣā prastāvanā smṛtā ||SRs_3.352||
body.translated_text: that, dramatic experts regard as <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction). ||SRs_3.352||

body.text: sarvāmukhāṅga-vīthy-aṅga-sametair vākya-vistaraiḥ | 165
body.translated_text: Where the <s>sūtradhāra</s>, with extended dialogue, accompanied by all <s>āmukha</s> elements and <s>vīthī</s> elements,

body.text: sūtradhāro yatra naṭī-vidūṣaka-naṭādibhiḥ ||SRs_3.353||
body.translated_text: together with the <s>Naṭī</s>, <s>Vidūṣaka</s>, actors, and others, ||SRs_3.353||

body.text: saṃlapana prastutaṃ cārtham ākṣipet sthāpanā hi sā | 166
body.translated_text: conversing, introduces the subject at hand — that is <s>sthāpanā</s> (establishment).

body.text: śṛṅgāra-pracure nāṭye yogyaḥ syād āmukha-kramaḥ ||SRs_3.354||
body.translated_text: In a drama predominantly of the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiment, the <s>āmukha</s> sequence is appropriate. ||SRs_3.354||

body.text: ratnāvalydike prāyo lakṣyatāṃ kovidair ayam | 167
body.translated_text: Experts should observe this mostly in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s> and the like.

body.text: vīrādbhutādi prāye tu prāyaḥ prastāvanocitā ||SRs_3.355||
body.translated_text: But in [dramas] predominantly of the <s>Vīra</s> (heroic), <s>Adbhuta</s> (marvelous), and like sentiments, the <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction) is generally appropriate. ||SRs_3.355||

body.text: anargha-rāghavādyeṣu prāyaśo vīkṣyatām iyam | 168
body.translated_text: This should be mostly observed in the <s>Anargha-rāghava</s> and such [plays].

body.text: hāsya-bībhatsa-raudrādi-prāye tu sthāpanā matā ||SRs_3.356||
body.translated_text: But in [dramas] predominantly of the <s>Hāsya</s> (comic), <s>Bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), <s>Raudra</s> (furious), and like sentiments, the <s>sthāpanā</s> (establishment) is considered [appropriate]. ||SRs_3.356||

body.text: vīra-bhadra-vijṛmbhādau sā prāyeṇa samīkṣyatām | 169
body.translated_text: This should be mostly observed in the <s>Vīrabhadra-vijṛmbha</s> and the like.

body.text: kathitāny āmukhāṅgāni vīthy-aṅgāni pracakṣmahe ||SRs_3.357||
body.translated_text: The elements of the <s>āmukha</s> have been stated; [now] we shall describe the <s>vīthī</s> elements. ||SRs_3.357||

body.text: āmukhe' pi ca vīthyāṃ ca sādhāraṇye' pi saṃmataḥ | 170
body.translated_text: Both in the <s>āmukha</s> and in the <s>vīthī</s>, even in their common [elements], the accepted practice

body.text: vīthy-aṅga-saṃprathā teṣāṃ vīthyām āvaśyakatvataḥ ||SRs_3.358||
body.translated_text: of the <s>vīthī</s> elements being called such is due to their indispensability in the <s>vīthī</s>. ||SRs_3.358||

body.text: udghātyakāvalagita-prapañca-trigate chalam | 171
body.translated_text: <s>Udghātyaka</s> (disclosure), <s>Avalagita</s> (enigmatic speech), <s>Prapañca</s> (elaboration), <s>Trigata</s> (trilogue), <s>Chala</s> (deception),

body.text: vākkely-adhibale gaṇḍam avasyandita-nālike ||SRs_3.359||
body.translated_text: <s>Vākkelī</s> (verbal play), <s>Adhibala</s> (superiority), <s>Gaṇḍa</s> (boast), <s>Avasyandita</s> (overflow), <s>Nālikā</s> (tube),

body.text: asat-pralāpa-vyāhārau mṛdavaṃ ca trayodaśa | 172
body.translated_text: <s>Asat-pralāpa</s> (absurd talk), <s>Vyāhāra</s> (discourse), and <s>Mṛdava</s> (softening) — [these are] the thirteen.

body.text:
tatrodghātyakam anyonyālāpa-mālā dvidhā hi tat |
gūḍhāratha-pada-paryāya-kramāt praśnottara-kramāt ||SRs_3.360|| 173
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>udghātyaka</s> (disclosure) is a chain of mutual dialogue; it is twofold: through the sequence of words with hidden meaning, and through the sequence of question and answer. ||SRs_3.360||

body.text: tatra gūḍhārtha-pada-paryāya-kramād udghātyakaṃ, yathā vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhita-nāmani ḍime-

children.text: sakhe ko' yaṃ raudraḥ kathaya mahitaḥ ko' pi hi raso
children.translated_text: 'Friend, who is this fearsome one? Tell me — some great <s>Rasa</s> (sentiment) is honored!'
'What is this so-called <s>Rasa</s>? A grandeur of savor, fragrant with memory!'
'What is this relish? — the mind, whose awareness of other cognizable objects has gradually dissolved —

children.text: mano' vasthā jñātaṃ nanu vadasi nidrāntaram iti ||SRs_3.361||
children.translated_text: a state of mind? — understood! Surely you speak of the interval of sleep.' ||3.361||

body.translated_text: Of these, <s>udghātyaka</s> through the sequence of words with hidden meaning, for example, in the <s>ḍima</s> (dramatic form) named <s>Vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhita</s> —

body.text: atra raudra-rasa-svarūpa-vivecanāya rasāsvādāvasthā-lakṣaṇair gūḍhārtha-pada-paryāyair naṭa-sūtradhārayoḥ saṃlāpād idam ādimam udghātyakam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the dialogue of the actor and the stage-manager — using words that are synonyms with concealed meanings, characterized by the marks of the state of <s>rasa</s>-relish — for the purpose of discriminating the true nature of <s>Raudra-rasa</s>, this is the first type of <s>Udghātyaka</s> (preludial dialogue).

body.text: praśnottara-kramād, yathā tatraiva ḍime-
body.translated_text: Through the sequence of question and answer, as in the same <s>Ḍima</s> (spectacle play) —

children.text: sevyaṃ kiṃ param uttamasya caritaṃ lokottaraḥ kaḥ pumān
children.translated_text: 'What is the supreme thing worthy of cultivation? The conduct of the best. Who is the extraordinary being?

children.text: śrī-siṃhaḥ sa tu kīdṛśo vada nidhir dharmasya dharmas tu kaḥ |
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Siṃha</s>! And what is he like? Tell — he is a treasure of <s>Dharma</s>. And what is <s>Dharma</s>?

children.text: satyoktir vacanaṃ tu kiṃ kavi-nutaṃ ko nāma tādṛk kavir
children.translated_text: Truthful speech. And what is the speech praised by poets? Who indeed is such a poet?

children.text: viśveśaḥ sa tu kīdṛśo vijayate viśveṣu viśveśavat ||SRs_3.362||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśveśa</s>! And what is he like? — He triumphs among all beings, like a lord of the universe!' ||3.362||

body.text: atra gūḍhārtha-pada-paryāya-rahita-praśnottara-krameṇa naṭa-sūtradhārayoḥ saṃlāpāt prakṛta-kavi-varṇanopayuktam idam udghātyakam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the dialogue of the actor and the stage-manager in the sequence of question and answer — without words that are synonyms with concealed meanings — this is an <s>Udghātyaka</s> that serves for the description of the poet at hand.

body.text:
atha avalagitam-
dvidhāvalagitaṃ proktam arthāvalaganātmakam |
anya-prasaṅgād anyasya saṃsiddhiḥ prakṛtasya va ||SRs_3.363|| 174
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Avalagita</s> (oblique reference) — <s>Avalagita</s> is declared twofold, consisting of the hanging [connection] of meaning: the accomplishment of one thing by means of the context of another, or [the accomplishment] of the matter at hand [through another]. ||3.363||

body.text: anya-prasaṅgād anyasya siddhyā avalagitaṃ, yathā abhirāma-rāghave anapota-nāyakīye-
body.translated_text: The accomplishment of one thing through the context of another, as in the <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s>, of which the hero is <s>Anapota</s> —

children.translated_text: 'Ah! The <s>Sārasvata</s> (divinely inspired) eye of poets, of those who see with visionary sight,
would operate with surpassing [power] upon objects of fixed meaning.' ||3.364||

body.text: atra sūtradhāreṇa kavīnāṃ sārasvataṃ cakṣur iti kavi-sāmānya-varṇanena svābhilaṣita-kavi-viśeṣotkarṣa-sādhana-rūpāt prakṛtāerthāvalaganād avalagitam idam |
body.translated_text: Here, the stage-manager, by the general description of poets with the words 'the <s>Sārasvata</s> eye of poets,' [achieves] the <s>Avalagita</s> through the oblique reference to the matter at hand — namely, establishing the superiority of the particular poet he himself desires [to praise].

body.text: anya-prasaṅgena prakṛtasya siddhir, yathā anargha-rāghave-
body.translated_text: The accomplishment of the matter at hand through the context of another, as in the <s>Anargha-rāghava</s> —

body.text: sūtradhāraḥ-māriṣa, sthāne khalu bhavataḥ kutūhalam | īdṛśam evaitat |
body.translated_text: The stage-manager: 'Sir, your curiosity is indeed well-placed! Such indeed is this [work].'

body.text:
tat tādṛg ujjvalakakutstha-kula-praśasti-
saurabhya-nirbhara-gabhīra-manoharāṇi |
vālmīki-vāg-amṛta-kūpa-nipāna-lakṣmīm
etāni bibhrati murāri-kaver vacāṃsi ||SRs_3.365|| [a.rā. 1.12]
body.translated_text: 'These words of the poet <s>Murāri</s> bear the beauty of a well from which one draws the nectar of <s>Vālmīki</s>'s speech — deeply captivating, overflowing with the fragrance of the glorification of the brilliant <s>Kakutstha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>'s) lineage, resembling that [excellence].' ||3.365|| [<s>Anargha-rāghava</s> 1.12]

body.text: atrāprakṛta-vālmīki-varṇana-prasaṅgena prakṛta-māriṣa-kutūhalotkarṣa-saṃsādhana-rūpāt prakṛta-nāṭyāvalaganād idaṃ dvitīyam avalagitam |
body.translated_text: Here, through the context of the incidental description of <s>Vālmīki</s>, the accomplishment of the matter at hand — namely, the enhancement of Sir [Interlocutor]'s curiosity about the drama — constitutes the second type of <s>Avalagita</s>.

body.text:
atha prapañcaḥ-
prapañcas tu mithaḥ stotram asad-bhūtaṃ ca hāsya-kṛt ||SRs_3.366|| 175a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Prapañca</s> (elaboration/mutual mock-praise) — <s>Prapañca</s> is mutual praise that is untrue and produces laughter. ||3.366||

body.text: yathā vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhaṇe-

children.text: nāṭyācāryas tvam asi suhṛdāṃ tvādṛśānāṃ prasādāt
children.translated_text: 'You are the master of dramatic art! By the grace of friends like you —'

children.text: ko' yaṃ gīta-śrama-vidhir aho bhinna-kaṇṭho' dya jātaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'What is this exertion of singing? Ah, your voice has become hoarse today!'

children.text: jñātaṃ jñātaṃ parihasasi māṃ bhāṣitair bhāva-garbhair
children.translated_text: 'Understood, understood — you jest with me through pregnant speeches!'

children.text: maivaṃ vācyaṃ tvam asi hi gurus tatra ceṣṭiḥ pramāṇam ||SRs_3.367||
children.translated_text: 'Let it not be said thus — you are the master here, and in that [matter] performance is the proof.' ||3.367||

body.translated_text: As in the <s>Vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhaṇa</s> —

body.text: atra naṭa-sūtradhārayor anyathārthasyānyonya-stotrasya hāsyāyaiva pravṛttatvāt prapañcaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the otherwise-meant mutual praise of the actor and stage-manager operates solely for the purpose of humor, this is <s>Prapañca</s>.

body.text:
atha trigatam-
śruti-sāmyād anekārtha-yojanaṃ trigataṃ bhavet ||SRs_3.368|| 175b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Trigata</s> (triple application) — Where, due to homophony, a single expression yields multiple meanings — that is <s>Trigata</s>. ||3.368||

body.text: yathābhirāma-rāghave, pāripārśvikaḥ-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s>, the attendant [says] —

children.translated_text: 'The resonance of the <s>vāṇī</s> (speech/lute) and <s>muraja</s> (drum) — melodious to the ear — is it the rumbling of a rain-cloud?

children.text: jaladasya kim ā jñātaṃ tava madhura-gabhīra-vāg-vilāso' yam ||SRs_3.369||
children.translated_text: Or is it the rain-cloud [itself]? Ah, understood — this is your sweet and profound verbal display!' ||3.369||

body.text: atra sūtradhāra-vāg-vilāse muraja-jalada-dhvani-vitarka-sambhāvanāt trigatam |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Trigata</s> consists in the conjectural comparison of the stage-manager's verbal display to the sounds of a drum and a rain-cloud.

body.text:
atha chalam-
proktaṃ chalaṃ sasotprāsaiḥ priyābhāsair vilobhanam ||SRs_3.370|| 176a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Chala</s> (deception) — <s>Chala</s> is declared to be enticement through [words that sound like] praise but [are actually] taunts, resembling [genuine] affection. ||3.370||

body.text: yathā abhirāma-rāghave-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s> —

children.text: vidvān asau kalāvān api rasiko bahu-vidha-prayogajñaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He is learned, accomplished in the arts, a connoisseur, and knowledgeable in various kinds of presentation.'

children.text: iti ca bhavantaṃ vidmo nirvyūḍhaṃ sādhu tat tvayā sarvam ||SRs_3.371||
children.translated_text: 'And thus we know you — you have accomplished everything splendidly.' ||3.371||

body.text: atra viparīta-lakṣaṇayā prahelikārtham ajānataḥ pāripārśvikasyopālambhanāt chalam |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Chala</s> consists in the upbraiding of the attendant, who does not understand the riddle-meaning, through the figure of inverted description.

body.text:
atha vākkeliḥ-
sākāṅkṣasyaiva vākyasya vākkeliḥ syāt samāptitaḥ ||SRs_3.372|| 176
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vāk-keli</s> (word-play) — <s>Vāk-keli</s> is the completion of a sentence left incomplete and expectant. ||3.372||

body.text: yathā maheśvarānande-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Maheśvarānanda</s> —

children.translated_text: 'The one son, the remover of the family's grief, <s>Kumāra</s> (<s>Skanda</s>),
by his parents, whose mouths were turned toward the nourishment of the feigned <s>Bhairava</s> [form],
was summoned with reverence, and above [all else]
the recitation was commenced: "<s>Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya</s>!"' ||3.373||

body.text: atra vākye sākāṅkṣe viśeṣāṃśam anuktvā namaḥ śivāyeti samāpti-kathanād vāk-keliḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Vāk-keli</s> consists in the completion of the incomplete and expectant sentence with '<s>Namaḥ Śivāya</s>', without stating the specific component.

body.text:
atha adhibalam-
spardhayānyonya-sāmarthya-vyaktis tv adhibalaṃ bhavet ||SRs_3.374|| 177a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Adhibala</s> (mutual display of power) — The manifestation of mutual prowess through rivalry — that is <s>Adhibala</s>. ||3.374||

body.text: yathā vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhaṇe-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhaṇa</s> —

children.text: mā bhūc cintā taveyaṃ mayi sati kuśale duṣkaraḥ kiṃ prayogo
children.translated_text: 'Let this worry of yours not exist — when I, the skilled one, am present, what difficulty can there be in the performance?'

children.text: mānin jānāsi kiṃ tvaṃ kim api na viditā cāturī me tvayā kim |
children.translated_text: 'O proud one, do you know? Is my cleverness at all unknown to you?'

children.text: āstāṃ sva-stotra-kanthā kṛtam iha kathaitair bhūta-pūrvaiḥ prasaṅgaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Enough of this garment of self-praise! Enough here of talk about past precedents!'

children.text: patnyāhaṃ vaśya-karmā sapadi naṭavidhāv eṣa sajjībhavāmi ||SRs_3.375||
children.translated_text: 'Wife! I, the master of [magical] subjugation, now gird myself promptly for the dramatic performance!' ||3.375||

body.text: atra naṭa-sūtradhārayoḥ paraspara-spardhayā sva-sva-prayoga-sāmarthya-prakāśanād adhibalam |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Adhibala</s> consists in the mutual display of their respective performative prowess through the rivalry of the actor and the stage-manager.

body.text:
atha gaṇḍam-
gaṇḍaṃ prastuta-sambandhi bhinnārthaṃ sahasoditam ||SRs_3.376|| 177b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Gaṇḍa</s> (sudden double meaning) — <s>Gaṇḍa</s> is an utterance related to the topic at hand, suddenly spoken with a different meaning. ||3.376||

body.text: yathā veṇī-saṃhāre-

children.translated_text: 'Their fire of enmity extinguished, devoted to tranquility,
may the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, together with <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), rejoice!
And may the sons of the <s>Kuru</s> king, with their bodies cleansed [or: with the earth reddened by blood], their bodily conflicts ceased [or: their bodies wounded],
be at ease, together with their servants!' ||[<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 1.7]

body.translated_text: As in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> —

body.text: tatra sūtradhāreṇa nirupadrava-lakṣaṇe' rthe vivakṣite' pi svarga-sthiti-lakṣaṇārtha-sūcakasya rakta-prasādhitaa-bhuva ity ādi-śliṣṭa-vākyasya sahasā prastuta-sambandhitayā bhāṣitatvād gaṇḍam |
body.translated_text: Here, though the stage-manager intends the meaning of 'free from calamity,' the utterance 'with the earth reddened' and similar well-connected phrases also suggest the meaning of 'dwelling in heaven' — because they are spoken suddenly as related to the topic, this is <s>Gaṇḍa</s>.

body.text:
atha avasyanditam-
pūrvoktasyānyathā vyākhyā yatrāvasyanditaṃ hi tat ||SRs_3.377|| 178a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Avasyanditam</s> (clarifying reinterpretation) — Where there is an alternative explanation of something previously said — that is <s>Avasyanditam</s>. ||3.377||

body.text: yathā veṇī-saṃhāre, sūtradhāraḥ-
body.translated_text: As in the <s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s>, the stage-manager —

body.text:
sat-pakṣā madhura-giraḥ prasādhitāśā madoddhatārambhāḥ |
nipatanti dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ kāla-vaśān medinī-pṛṣṭhe ||SRs_3.378|| [ve.saṃ. 1.6]
body.translated_text: 'Well-winged, sweet-voiced, their hopes fulfilled, their enterprises launched in pride,

body.text: pāripārśvikaḥ (praviśya sambhrāntaḥ)-śāntaṃ pāpam | pratihatam amaṅgalam |
body.translated_text: the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> fall to the earth's surface by the power of time.' ||3.378|| [<s>Veṇī-saṃhāra</s> 1.6]

body.text: sūtradhāraḥ-mā bhaiṣīḥ | nanu śarat-samaya-varṇanāśaṃsayā haṃsān dhārtarāṣṭrā iti vyapadiśāmi |
body.translated_text: The attendant (entering in alarm): 'May evil be averted! May inauspiciousness be repelled!'

body.text: atra pūrvoktasya suyodhanādi-nipātasya haṃsa-pātatvena vyākhyānād idam avasyanditam |
body.translated_text: The stage-manager: 'Fear not! In the expectation of describing the autumn season, I designate them as "<s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s>" — meaning "geese" (a type of swan named after <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>).'

body.text: atha nālikā-

children.translated_text: Now, <s>Nālikā</s> (riddle) —

A riddle (<s>prahelikā</s>) with a hidden meaning, intended for humor, is known as <s>Nālikā</s>. It is declared twofold: inner-speech (<s>antar-lāpā</s>) and outer-speech (<s>bahir-lāpā</s>). ||3.379||

body.translated_text: Here, the reinterpretation of the previously stated fall of <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>) and others as the alighting of geese constitutes this <s>Avasyanditam</s>.

body.text: tatra antar-lāpā, yathā prasanna-rāghave-
body.translated_text: There, inner-speech, as in the <s>Prasanna-rāghava</s> —

body.text:
pratyaṅkam aṅkurita-sarva-navāvatāran-
navyollasat-kusuma-rāji-virāji-bandham |
gharmetarāṃśum iva vakratayātiramyaṃ
nāṭya-prabandham atimañjula-saṃvidhānam ||SRs_3.380|| [pra.rā. 1.7]
body.translated_text: 'With every act sprouting all the new <s>avatāras</s>, the arrangement radiating with rows of fresh blossoming flowers, like the cool-rayed one (moon) exceedingly lovely in its curvature [or: with every act], the dramatic composition of most beautiful arrangement — ||3.380|| [<s>Prasanna-rāghava</s> 1.7]

body.text: atra prasanna-rāghava-nāmety uttarasya saptākṣarāṣṭa-paṅkti-krameṇa likhite' sminn eva śloke mṛgyatvād antar-lāpo nāmeyam |
body.translated_text: Here, because the answer '<s>Prasanna-rāghava</s>' [the name of the play] must be sought within this very verse by the method of the seven-syllabled eight-line sequence written [acrostically], this is called inner-speech <s>Nālikā</s>.

body.text:
bahir-lāpā, yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe-
kama-baḍḍhanta-vilāsaṃ rasāsale kaṃ karei kandappo |
[krama-vardhamāna-vilāsaṃ rasātale kaṃ karoti kandarpaḥ |]
body.translated_text: Outer-speech, as in the <s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> — [Prakrit:] 'With progressively increasing grace, whom does <s>Kandarpa</s> (the God of Love) reduce to the netherworld?' [Sanskrit:] 'With progressively increasing grace, whom does <s>Kandarpa</s> reduce to the netherworld?'

body.text: sūtradhāraḥ-aye praśnottaram | seyam asmat-prītir iti devādeśaḥ | tat svayam eva vācayāmi-
body.translated_text: The stage-manager: 'Ah, a question and answer! This is our joy — a divine directive! I shall recite it myself —'

body.text: nirbhaya-gurur vyadhatta ca vālmīki-kathāṃ kim anusṛtya ||SRs_3.381|| [bā.rā. 1.5]
body.translated_text: 'The fearless preceptor — following the story of <s>Vālmīki</s> — what did he compose?' ||3.381|| [<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s> 1.5]

body.text: ity atra bāla-rāmāyaṇam ity uttarasya bahir eva mṛgyatvād bahir-lāpā nāma nālikeyam |
body.translated_text: Here, because the answer '<s>Bāla-rāmāyaṇa</s>' [the play's name] must be sought externally [outside the verse], this is the outer-speech <s>Nālikā</s>.

body.text:
atha asat-pralāpaḥ-
asambaddha-kathālāpo' sat-pralāpa itīritaḥ ||SRs_3.382|| 179b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Asat-pralāpa</s> (incoherent chatter) — Incoherent and disconnected talk is called <s>Asat-pralāpa</s>. ||3.382||

children.translated_text: As in the <s>Vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhaṇa</s>, the actor [says] —

children.text: patnī parilambi-kucā tanayā mama danturāpi taruṇa-vayāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'My wife has drooping breasts; my daughter, though she has protruding teeth, is of young age;

children.text: krīḍā-kapir asti gṛhe tad ahaṃ nāṭya-prayoga-marmajñaḥ ||SRs_3.383||
children.translated_text: there is a pet monkey in the house — therefore I am an expert in the secrets of dramatic performance!' ||3.383||

body.text: atra naṭena svakīya-nāṭya-prayoga-marmajñatve hetutayā kathitānāṃ krīḍā-kapi-sad-bhāvādīnām asambaddhatvād ayam asat-pralāpaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the existence of a pet monkey and other things mentioned by the actor as reasons for his expertise in dramatic secrets are disconnected [from that claim], this is <s>Asat-pralāpa</s>.

body.text:
atha vyāhāraḥ-
anyārthaṃ vacanaṃ hāsya-karaṃ vyāhāra ucyate ||SRs_3.384|| 180a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vyāhāra</s> (unintended double meaning) — Speech that is intended for one purpose but produces humor through another meaning is called <s>Vyāhāra</s>. ||3.384||

body.text: yathā ānanda-kośa-nāmani prahasane-(praviśya) naṭī-ayya ko ṇioo ? [ārya, ko niyogaḥ ?]
body.translated_text: As in the farce called <s>Ānanda-kośa</s> — (Entering) the Actress: '[Prakrit:] Sir, what is the commission?' [Sanskrit:] 'Sir, what is the commission?'

body.text: sūtradhāraḥ-ārye gargarike nūnam ānanda-kośa-nābhilāṣiṇī pariṣad iyam |
body.translated_text: The stage-manager: 'O Lady <s>Gargarikā</s>, surely this audience desires to see <s>Ānanda-kośa</s> (the Treasury of Bliss)!'

body.text: naṭī-tā daṃsedu ayyo | tado kiṃ bilaṃbeṇa | [tad darśayatu āryaḥ | tataḥ kiṃ vilambena ?]
body.translated_text: The Actress: '[Prakrit:] Then let the master show it! Why the delay?' [Sanskrit:] 'Then let the master show it! Why the delay?'

body.text: sūtradhāraḥ-ayi gāyike gargarike bhavatyā mukha-vyāpāreṇa bījotthāpanānusandhāyinā bhavitavyam |
body.translated_text: The stage-manager: 'O singer <s>Gargarikā</s>, you must attend to the oral activity (<s>mukha-vyāpāra</s>) that investigates the raising of the seed (<s>bījotthāpana</s>).'

body.text: naṭī (sa-harṣam)-kīriso so muha-bābāro | [kīdṛśaḥ sa mukhya-vyāpāraḥ ?]
body.translated_text: The Actress (joyfully): '[Prakrit:] What kind of oral activity is that?' [Sanskrit:] 'What kind of principal activity is that?'

body.text: sūtradhāraḥ-nanv amum eva śiśiram adhikṛtya dhruvā-gāna-rūpaḥ |
body.translated_text: The stage-manager: 'Why, it is in the form of <s>Dhruvā</s> singing, taking this very winter season as its subject.'

body.text: ity atra ānanda-kośa-bījotthāpana-mukha-vyāpārāṇāṃ rūpaka-bījotthāpana-dhruvā-gānārthānām api anyārtha-pratītyā hāsyakaratvād ayaṃ vyāhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because the words <s>Ānanda-kośa</s> (treasury of bliss/the play's name), <s>Bījotthāpana</s> (raising the seed/a dramatic technical term), and <s>Mukha-vyāpāra</s> (oral activity/the opening section) produce humor through the perception of their other [non-technical] meanings, this is <s>Vyāhāra</s>.

body.text:
atha mṛdavam-
doṣā guṇā guṇā doṣā yatra syur mṛdavaṃ hi tat ||SRs_3.385|| 180b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Mṛdava</s> (soft irony) — Where faults are [presented as] virtues and virtues as faults — that is <s>Mṛdava</s>. ||3.385||

body.text: yathā-

children.translated_text: 'The <s>Vedic</s> scholars, who know only the ritual of <s>Veda</s>-recitation, are not worthy — like parrots.
From the practice of the <s>Śāstras</s> (sciences), the mutual clamor of men is like that of dogs.
Poetry is vain, since its subject-matter is untrue, like a dream or magic.
For the determination of all practical affairs, the <s>Smṛti</s> (legal tradition) alone should be studied.' ||3.386||

body.translated_text: For example —

body.text: atra kāvyādiṣu guṇa-bhūteṣv api doṣatva-kathanād mṛdavam idam |
body.translated_text: Here, because faultfulness is stated even in such things as poetry and the like which are in fact virtuous, this is <s>Mṛdava</s>.

body.text:
evam āmukham āyojya sūtradhāre sahānuge |
niṣkrānte' that tad-ākṣiptaiḥ pātrair vastu prapañcayet ||SRs_3.387|| 181
vastu sarvaṃ dvidhā sūcyam asūcyam iti bhedataḥ |
rasa-hīnaṃ bhaved atra vastu tat sūcyam ucyate ||SRs_3.388|| 182
yad vastu nīrasaṃ tat tu sūcayet sūcakās tv amī |
viṣkambha-cūlikāṅkāsyāṅkāvatāra-praveśakāḥ ||SRs_3.389|| 183
