body.translated_text: Having thus devised the prologue (<s>Āmukha</s>), when the stage-manager exits together with his assistant, then with the characters introduced thereby, the plot (<s>vastu</s>) should be elaborated. ||3.387|| The entire plot is of two kinds by the distinction of <s>Sūcya</s> (to be indicated) and <s>Asūcya</s> (not needing indication). That portion of the plot which is devoid of <s>rasa</s> is called <s>Sūcya</s>. ||3.388|| That plot which is without <s>rasa</s> should be indicated through the following indicators (<s>sūcakas</s>): <s>Viṣkambha</s> (interlude), <s>Cūlikā</s> (backstage speech), <s>Aṅkāsya</s> (act-opening), <s>Aṅkāvatāra</s> (act-descent), and <s>Praveśaka</s> (entering scene). ||3.389||

body.text:
tatra viṣkambho bhūta-bhāvi-vastv-aṃśa-sūcakaḥ |
amukhya-pātra-racitaḥ saṅkṣepaika-prayojanaḥ ||SRs_3.390|| 184
sa śuddho miśra ity ukto miśraḥ syān nīca-madhyamaiḥ |
so' yaṃ ceṭī-naṭācārya-saṃlāpa-parikalpitaḥ ||SRs_3.391|| 185
mālavikāgnimitrasya prathamāṅke nirūpyatām |
śuddhaḥ kevala-madhyo' yam ekāneka-kṛto dvidhā ||SRs_3.392|| 186
ratnāvalyām eka-śuddhaḥ prāpta-yaugandharāyaṇaḥ |

children.translated_text: The multiple-[character] pure <s>Viṣkambha</s> is in the sixth act of the <s>Anargha-rāghava</s>.
Let it be examined — [it is] composed by <s>Mālyavān</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>. ||3.393||

body.translated_text: There, <s>Viṣkambha</s> (interlude) indicates a portion of past or future plot-matter; it is composed by non-principal characters and has the sole purpose of condensation. ||3.390|| It is declared as pure (<s>śuddha</s>) or mixed (<s>miśra</s>). The mixed is [composed] by low and middling characters. This [mixed type] is constructed through the dialogue of a maid-servant and a dance-master. ||3.391|| Let it be examined in the first act of <s>Mālavikāgnimitra</s>. The pure is [composed] by middling characters alone and is twofold: with one [character] or with many. ||3.392|| The single-[character] pure [<s>Viṣkambha</s>] is [seen] in <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, where <s>Yaugandharāyaṇa</s> [appears alone].

body.text: atha cūlikā-

children.translated_text: The introduction of a matter by bards, panegyrists, charioteers, and others,

children.text: arthopakṣepaṇaṃ yat tu kriyate sā hi cūlikā ||SRs_3.394||
children.translated_text: positioned behind the curtain — that is <s>Cūlikā</s>. ||3.394||

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Cūlikā</s> (backstage speech) —

body.text: sā dvidhā cūlikā khaṇḍa-cūlikā ceti bhedataḥ | 189
body.translated_text: It is of two kinds: <s>Cūlikā</s> (proper) and <s>Khaṇḍa-cūlikā</s> (partial backstage speech).

body.text: pātrair yavanikāntaḥsthaiḥ kevalaṃ yā tu nirmitā ||SRs_3.395||
body.translated_text: That which is constructed solely by characters behind the curtain, ||3.395||

body.text: ādāv aṅkasya madhye vā cūlikā nāma sā smṛtā | 190
body.translated_text: at the beginning of an act or in the middle — that is known as <s>Cūlikā</s> (proper).

body.text: praveśa-nirgamābhāvād iyam aṅkād bahir gatā ||SRs_3.396||
body.translated_text: Because there is no entrance or exit [of the speaker], it falls outside the act [proper]. ||3.396||

body.text: aṅkādau cūlikā, yathā anargha-rāghave saptamāṅke, nepathye-
body.translated_text: A <s>Cūlikā</s> at the beginning of an act, as in the <s>Anargha-rāghava</s>, seventh act, backstage —

body.text:
tamisrā-mūrcchāla-trijagad-agadṅkāra-kiraṇe
raghūṇāṃ gotrasya prasavitari deve savitari |
puraḥsthe dik-pālaiḥ saha para-gṛhāvāsa-vacanāt
praviṣṭo vaidehī dahanam atha śuddhā ca niragāt ||SRs_3.397|| [a.rā. 7.1]
body.translated_text: 'When the god Savitṛ (the Sun), the rays of whose light are the remedy for the three worlds overwhelmed by the darkness of deep night, the progenitor of the Raghu dynasty, stood before [them], together with the guardians of the quarters — from the utterance of the words "dwelling in another's house," Vaidehī (Sītā) entered the fire and then emerged purified.' ||SRs_3.397|| [Anargha-rāghava 7.1]

body.text: ity ādau nepathya-gatair eva pātraiḥ sītā-jvalana-praveśa-nirgamādīnām arthānāṃ prayogānucitānāṃ sūcanād iyaṃ cūlikā |
body.translated_text: Here, through the indication by characters who remain behind the curtain (nepathya) of events unsuitable for direct staging — Sītā's entering and emerging from the fire and the like — this constitutes Cūlikā (interlude).

body.text: aṅka-madhye, yathā ratnāvalyāṃ dvitīyāṅke, (nepathye kalakalaḥ)-
body.translated_text: In the middle of an act, as in the second act of Ratnāvalī, (a commotion behind the curtain) —

body.text:
kaṇṭhe kṛttāvaśeṣaṃ kanaka-mayam adhaḥ śṛṅkhalā-dāma karṣan krāntvā dvārāṇi helācala-caraṇa-raṇat-kiṅkaṇī-cakravālaḥ |
dattātaṅko' ṅganānām anusṛta-saraṇiḥ sambhramād aśva-pālaiḥ prabhraṣṭo' yaṃ plavaṅgaḥ praviśati nṛpater mandiraṃ mandurāyāḥ ||SRs_3.398|| [ra. 2.2]
body.translated_text: 'With a remnant of a golden chain hanging from its neck below, dragging the chain-string, having crossed the doorways with a ring of ankle-bells jingling on its carelessly moving feet, causing alarm to the women, pursued in haste by the horse-keepers along the path — this escaped monkey enters the royal palace from the stable.' ||SRs_3.398|| [Ratnāvalī 2.2]

body.text: atra nepathya-gataiḥ pātraiḥ prayogānucitasya vānara-viplavādy-arthasya sūcanād iyaṃ madhya-cūlikā |
body.translated_text: Here, through the indication by characters behind the curtain of the monkey-commotion and other events unsuitable for direct staging — this constitutes a Madhya-cūlikā (mid-act interlude).

body.text: atha khaṇḍa-cūlikā-

children.translated_text: Through extended dialogues between characters stationed on the stage and behind the curtain,

children.text:
ādau kevalam aṅkasya kalpitā khaṇḍa-cūlikā |
praveśa-nirgamāprāpter iyam aṅkād bahir-gatā ||SRs_3.399|| 192
children.translated_text: a Khaṇḍa-cūlikā is devised solely at the beginning of an act. Since it does not involve entrance or exit, it falls outside the act [proper]. ||SRs_3.399||

body.translated_text: Now Khaṇḍa-cūlikā (partial interlude) —

body.text: yathā bāla-rāmāyaṇe saptamāṅkasyādau, (tataḥ praviśati vaitālikaḥ karpūra-caṇḍaḥ) vaitālikaḥ-bhadra candana-caṇḍa parityaja nidrā-mudrām | vimuñca nijoṭajābhyantaram |
body.translated_text: As in Bāla-rāmāyaṇa, at the beginning of the seventh act, (then enters the bard Karpūra-caṇḍa): Bard — 'Good Candana-caṇḍa, abandon the seal of sleep! Leave the interior of your own hut!'

body.text: nepathye-ayya kappura-caṃḍa esā miṭṭhā pabhāda-ṇiddā | suvissaṃ dāva | [ārya karpūra-caṇḍa eṣā miṣṭā prabhāta-nidrā | svapsyāmi tāvat |]
body.translated_text: Behind the curtain [in Prakrit]: 'Noble Karpūra-caṇḍa, this morning sleep is sweet! Let me sleep a while!' [Sanskrit rendering follows.]

body.text: karpūra-caṇḍaḥ-aho utsāha-śaktir bhavataḥ | amantra-śīlo mahī-patiḥ apara-prabandha-darśī kaviḥ apāṭha-ruciś ca vadnī na ciraṃ nandati |
body.translated_text: Karpūra-caṇḍa: 'Ah, what industrious energy you have! A king who does not take counsel, a poet who does not foresee the next composition, and a student with no taste for study — none of these enjoy happiness for long.'

body.text: nepathye-tā ettha saṃtthara-tthido ṇimīlida-ṇaaṇo jebba suppabhādaṃ paṭhissaṃ | [tad atra saṃstara-sthito nimīlita-nayana eva suprabhātaṃ paṭhiṣyāmi |]
body.translated_text: Behind the curtain [in Prakrit]: 'Then, lying right here with eyes closed, I shall recite the morning benediction!' [Sanskrit rendering follows.]

body.text: karpūra-caṇḍaḥ-etad api bhavato bhūri | tad upaślokayāvo rāmabhadram | (kiñcid uccaiḥ)
body.translated_text: Karpūra-caṇḍa: 'That too is a great deal from you! Then let us sing a laudatory verse for Rāmabhadra.' (somewhat loudly)

body.text:
mārtaṇḍaika-kula-prakāṇḍa-tilakas trailokya-rakṣā-maṇir
viśvāmitra-mahāmuner nirupadhiḥ śiṣyo raghu-grāmaṇīḥ |
rāmas tāḍita-tāṭakaḥ kim aparaṃ pratyakṣa-nārāyaṇaḥ
kausalyā-nayanotsavo vijayatāṃ bhū-kāśyapasyātmajaḥ ||SRs_3.400|| [bā.rā. 7.3]
body.translated_text: 'The crest-jewel of the foremost lineage of the Sun, the protective gem of the three worlds, the unsurpassed disciple of the great sage Viśvāmitra, the leader of the Raghu clan — Rāma, the slayer of Tāṭakā — what more? The manifest Nārāyaṇa, the delight of Kausalyā's eyes — may the son of Bhū-Kāśyapa (Bhū-Viṣṇu) be victorious!' ||SRs_3.400|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 7.3]

body.text:
nepathye-
kandapp-uddāma-dappa-ppasamaṇa-guruṇo bahmaṇo kāla-daṇḍe
pāṇiṃ deṃtassa gaṃgā-taralida-sasiṇo pabbaī-ballahassa |
cābaṃ caṃḍāhisiṃjāraba-harida-ṇahaṃ karṣaṇāruddha-majjhaṃ
jaṃ bhaggaṃ tassa saddo ṇisuṇiti huaṇe bittharaṃto ṇamāi ||SRs_3.401|| [bā.rā. 7.4]
body.translated_text: Behind the curtain [in Prakrit] — 'The bow — whose sky was filled with the sound of its terrible twanging, whose middle was obstructed by the force of drawing — given to the lord of Parvatī (Śiva), the Moon-bearer shaken by Gaṅgā's flow, the staff of Death of Brahmā, weighty in subduing the unbridled pride of Kandarpa (the God of Love) — the sound of its breaking reverberates throughout the world. Obeisance!' ||SRs_3.401|| [Bāla-rāmāyaṇa 7.4]

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit Chāyā:] 'The bow — of Brahmā, weighty as the staff of Death in subduing the unbridled pride of Kandarpa,
given to the beloved of Parvatī (Śiva), the Moon-bearer shaken by the Gaṅgā,
the bow whose sky was filled with the sound of terrible twanging, whose middle was obstructed by the pulling,

children.text: yat bhagnaṃ tasya śabdo niḥśrūyate bhuvane vistaran na māti ||]
children.translated_text: the sound of its breaking is heard spreading throughout the world. Obeisance!'

body.text: atra praviṣṭena karpūra-caṇḍena yavanikāntargatena candana-caṇḍena ca paryāya-pravṛtta-vāg-vilāsais tāṭakāvadhādi-vibhīṣaṇābhaya-pradānāntasya rāmabhadra-caritasya bāhulyāt prayogānucitasya sūcanād iyaṃ khaṇḍa-cūlikā |
body.translated_text: Here, through the conversational playfulness exchanged alternately between the entering Karpūra-caṇḍa and Candana-caṇḍa behind the curtain, indicating by summary the extensive story of Rāmabhadra from the slaying of Tāṭakā to the granting of fearlessness to Vibhīṣaṇa — which is unsuitable for staging — this constitutes a Khaṇḍa-cūlikā.

body.text: enāṃ viṣkambham evānye prāhur naitan mataṃ mama |

children.text: apraviṣṭasya saṃlāpo viṣkambhe na hi yujyate | 193
children.translated_text: For the dialogue of one who has not entered [the stage] is not appropriate in a Viṣkambha.
Therefore, since it has the characteristics of the head of a Viṣkambha, in my view this is a Khaṇḍa-cūlikā. ||SRs_3.402||

body.translated_text: Others call this a Viṣkambha (introductory scene); but that is not my view.

body.text: atha aṅkāsyam-

children.translated_text: By characters who entered at the end of the preceding act, the indication

children.text: sūcanaṃ tad-avicchityai yat tad aṅkāsyam īritam ||SRs_3.403||
children.translated_text: of the subject matter of the coming act, for the sake of its continuity — that is called Aṅkāsya. ||SRs_3.403||

body.translated_text: Now Aṅkāsya (act-face) —

body.text: yathā hi vīra-carite dvitīyāṅkāvasānake | 195
body.translated_text: As, for instance, at the close of the second act of Vīra-carita,

body.text: praviṣṭena sumantreṇa sūcitaṃ rāma-vigrahe ||SRs_3.404||
body.translated_text: by the entering Sumantra, the indication regarding the combat of Rāma — ||SRs_3.404||

body.text: vasiṣṭha-viśvāmitrādi-samābhāṣaṇa-lakṣaṇam | 196
body.translated_text: characterized by conversations with Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, and others —

body.text: vastūttarāṅke pūrvārthāvicchedenaiva kalpitam ||SRs_3.405||
body.translated_text: the subject matter of the following act is arranged with continuity from the preceding content. ||SRs_3.405||

body.text: athāṅkāvatāraḥ-

children.translated_text: Aṅkāvatāra is the entry into the coming act of all characters
who follow the preceding action, without division. ||SRs_3.406||

body.translated_text: Now Aṅkāvatāra (act-descent) —

body.text: dvitīyāṅke mālavikāgnimitre sa nirūpyatām | 198
body.translated_text: This should be examined in the second act of Mālavikāgnimitra.

body.text:
pātreṇāṅka-praviṣṭena kevalaṃ sūcitatvataḥ |
bhaved aṅkād abāhyatvam aṅkāsyāṅkāvatārayoḥ ||SRs_3.407|| 199
body.translated_text: Since the indication is made solely by a character who has entered the act, Aṅkāsya and Aṅkāvatāra both fall within the act, not outside it. ||SRs_3.407||

body.text:
atha praveśakaḥ-
yan nīcaiḥ kevalaṃ pātrair bhāvi-bhūtārtha-sūcanam |
aṅkayor ubhayor madhye sa vijñeyaḥ praveśakaḥ ||SRs_3.408|| 200
so' yaṃ ceṭi-dvayālāpa-saṃvidhānopakalpitaḥ |
mālatī-mādhave prājñair dvitīyāṅke nirūpyatām ||SRs_3.409|| 201
asūcyaṃ tu śubhodātta-rasa-bhāva-nirantaram |
prārambhe yady asūcyaṃ syād aṅkam evātra kalpayet ||SRs_3.410|| 202
rasālaṅkāra-vastūnām upalālana-kāṅkṣiṇām |
janany-aṅkavadādhāra-bhūtatvād aṅka ucyate ||SRs_3.411|| 203
aṅkas tu pañcaṣair dvitrair aṅgino' ṅgasya vastunaḥ |

children.translated_text: characters who serve as supports for the principal and subsidiary plot matter
or for the rasa, should be a charming special arrangement, and should elaborate what cannot be indicated [in summary]. ||SRs_3.412||

body.translated_text: Now Praveśaka (introductory scene) — that which indicates future or past events through low-ranking characters alone, between two acts, should be known as a Praveśaka. ||SRs_3.408|| This is devised through the arrangement of a dialogue between two maidservants. Let the learned examine it in the second act of Mālatī-mādhava. ||SRs_3.409|| What cannot be indicated must be continuous with auspicious, exalted sentiments and emotions. If what cannot be indicated [occurs] at the beginning, one should devise an act for it. ||SRs_3.410|| Because it is the supporting foundation — like a mother's lap — for subjects of rasa, ornament, and plot that seek nurturing, it is called an Aṅka (act). ||SRs_3.411|| An act, with five or six, or two or three,

body.text: atha asūcyavibhāgaḥ-

children.text: asūcyaṃ tad dvidhā dṛśyaṃ śrāvyaṃ cādyaṃ tu darśayet | 205
children.translated_text: The non-indicable is twofold: Dṛśya (visible, i.e., to be shown on stage) and Śrāvya (audible). The first should be displayed [directly].

children.text: dvedhā dvitīyaṃ svagataṃ prakāśaṃ ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_3.413||
children.translated_text: The second is of two kinds: Svagata (aside) and Prakāśa (public), by distinction. ||SRs_3.413||

body.translated_text: Now the classification of Asūcya (the non-indicable) —

body.text: svagataṃ svaika-vijñeyaṃ prakāśaṃ tad dvidhā bhavet | 206
body.translated_text: Svagata is that known to oneself alone. Prakāśa is of two kinds:

body.text: sarva-prakāśaṃ niyata-prakāśaṃ ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_3.414||
body.translated_text: Sarva-prakāśa (addressed to all) and Niyata-prakāśa (addressed to a specific person), by distinction. ||SRs_3.414||

body.text: sarva-prakāśaṃ sarveṣāṃ sthitānāṃ śravaṇocitam | 207
body.translated_text: Sarva-prakāśa is that appropriate to be heard by all who are present.

body.text: dvitīyaṃ tu sthiteṣv apy eṣv ekasya śravaṇocitam ||SRs_3.415||
body.translated_text: The second is appropriate to be heard by only one among those present. ||SRs_3.415||

body.text: dvidhā vibhāvyate' nyac ca janāntam apavāritam | 208
body.translated_text: Another [distinction] is perceived in two ways: Janāntika (aside to a person) and Apavārita (whispered aside).

body.text: tripatākā-kareṇānyān apavāryāntarā kathām ||SRs_3.416||
body.translated_text: Janāntika is when, having screened others with the Tripatākā hand-gesture, a conversation

body.text: anyenāmantraṇaṃ yat syāt taj janāntikam ucyate | 209
body.translated_text: is addressed to another in between — that is called Janāntika.

body.text: rahasyaṃ kathyate' nyasya parāvṛtyāpavāritam ||SRs_3.417||
body.translated_text: When a secret is told to another by turning away — that is called Apavārita. ||SRs_3.417||

body.text: itthaṃ śrāvyaṃ ca dṛśyaṃ ca prayujya susamāhitaiḥ | 210|
body.translated_text: Thus, having employed both the audible and the visible [modes], with well-composed

body.text: pātrair niṣkramaṇaṃ kāryam aṅkānte samam eva hi ||SRs_3.418||
body.translated_text: characters, the exit should be made simultaneously at the end of the act. ||SRs_3.418||

body.text: aṅka-cchedaś ca kartavyaḥ kālāvasthānurodhataḥ | 211
body.translated_text: And the division of acts should be made in accordance with time and circumstance.

body.text: dinārdha-dinayor yogyam aṅke vastu pravartayet ||SRs_3.419||
body.translated_text: One should set in motion the subject matter appropriate to a half-day or a full day within an act. ||SRs_3.419||

body.text: atha garbhāṅkaḥ-

children.translated_text: In connection with acts, I shall state the characteristics of the Garbhāṅka.
For the great exaltation of the rasa, hero, and subject matter, by the skilled, ||SRs_3.420||

body.translated_text: Now Garbhāṅka (embedded act) —

body.text: aṅkasya madhye yo' ṅkaḥ syād asau garbhāṅka īritaḥ | 213
body.translated_text: an act within an act is called a Garbhāṅka.

body.text: vastu-sūcaka-nāndīko diṅ-mātra-mukha-saṅgataḥ ||SRs_3.421||
body.translated_text: It has a Nāndī that indicates the subject matter, only a brief connection with the Mukha (opening), ||SRs_3.421||

body.text: arthopakṣepakair hīnaś cūlikā-parivarjitaiḥ | 214
body.translated_text: lacks Arthopakṣepakas (introductory devices), devoid of Cūlikās (interludes),

body.text: aneṣyad-vastu-viṣayaḥ pātraiś tri-caturair yutaḥ ||SRs_3.422||
body.translated_text: deals with subject matter not to be brought [into the main act], and has three or four characters. ||SRs_3.422||

body.text: nātiprapañcetivṛttaḥ svādhārāṅkāṅga-śobhitaḥ | 215
body.translated_text: Not overly elaborated in its plot, adorned as a limb of its supporting act,

body.text: prastutārthānubandhī ca pātra-niṣkramaṇāvadhiḥ ||SRs_3.423||
body.translated_text: connected with the main subject matter, and ending with the exit of the characters. ||SRs_3.423||

body.text: prathamāṅke na kartavyaḥ so' yaṃ kāvya-viśāradaiḥ | 216
body.translated_text: It should not be made in the first act — [so say] those skilled in poetry.

body.text: so' yam uttara-rāme tu rasotkarṣāya kathyatām ||SRs_3.424||
body.translated_text: This should be observed in Uttara-rāma-carita for the exaltation of rasa. ||SRs_3.424||

body.text: netur utkarṣako jñeyo bāla-rāmāyaṇe tv ayam | 217
body.translated_text: In Bāla-rāmāyaṇa, this is known to serve the exaltation of the hero.

body.text: amogha-rāghave so' yaṃ vastūtkarṣaika-kāraṇam ||SRs_3.425||
body.translated_text: In Amogha-rāghava, this is the sole cause for the exaltation of the plot. ||SRs_3.425||

body.text: nāṭake aṅka-niyamaḥ-

children.text: nāṭake' ṅkā na kartavyāḥ pañca-nyūnā daśādhikāḥ | 218
children.translated_text: In a Nāṭaka, the acts should not be fewer than five nor more than ten.
A Nāṭaka endowed with such qualities bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. ||SRs_3.426||

body.translated_text: Regarding the number of acts in a Nāṭaka —

body.text:
tathā ca bharataḥ-
dharmārtha-sādhanaṃ nāṭyaṃ sarva-duḥkhāpanoda-kṛt |
āsevadhvaṃ tad ṛṣayas tasyotthānaṃ tu nāṭakam ||SRs_3.427|| iti |
body.translated_text: And thus Bharata [says]: 'Drama is the means of achieving Dharma and Artha, the remover of all sorrow. O sages, partake of it — the Nāṭaka is its [supreme] expression.' ||SRs_3.427|| Thus.

body.text: pūrṇādi-nāṭaka-bhedānaṅgīkāraḥ-

children.translated_text: Some have devised sub-divisions of the Nāṭaka such as Pūrṇa (full) and the like.

children.text:
teṣāṃ nātīva ramyatvād aparīkṣākṣamatvataḥ |
muninānādṛtatvāc ca tān uddeṣṭum udāsmahe ||SRs_3.428|| 220
children.translated_text: Since they are not very charming, since they cannot withstand scrutiny, and since they were not regarded by the Sage [Bharata] — we refrain from enumerating them. ||SRs_3.428||

body.translated_text: Rejection of the sub-divisions of Nāṭaka such as Pūrṇa and the like —

body.text:
atha prakaraṇam-
yatretivṛttam utpādyaṃ dhīra-śāntaś ca nāyakaḥ |
rasaḥ pradhānaṃ śṛṅgāraḥ śeṣaṃ nāṭakavad bhavet ||SRs_3.429|| 221
tad dhi prakaraṇaṃ śuddhaṃ dhūrtaṃ miśraṃ ca tat tridhā |
kula-strī-nāyakaṃ śuddhaṃ mālatī-mādhavādikam ||SRs_3.430|| 222
gaṇikā-nāyikaṃ dhūrtaṃ kāmadattāhvayādikam |
kitava-dhyputakārādi-vyāpāraṃ tv atra kalpayet ||SRs_3.431|| 223
miśraṃ tat kulajā-veśye kalpite yatra nāyike |
dhūrta-śuddha-kramopetaṃ tan mṛcchakaṭikādikam ||SRs_3.432|| 224
body.translated_text: Now the Prakaraṇa (social drama) — where the plot is invented, the hero is of the Dhīra-śānta (steadfast-tranquil) type, the predominant rasa is Śṛṅgāra (erotic), and the rest is as in a Nāṭaka — ||SRs_3.429|| that is a Prakaraṇa. It is of three kinds: Śuddha (pure), Dhūrta (roguish), and Miśra (mixed). The pure type has a woman of noble family as the heroine, like Mālatī-mādhava and the like. ||SRs_3.430|| The roguish type has a courtesan as the heroine, like Kāmadatta and the like. One should devise in it activities of rogues, gamblers, cheaters, and the like. ||SRs_3.431|| The mixed type is where both a woman of noble family and a courtesan are devised as heroines, endowed with roguish and pure elements in sequence — like Mṛcchakaṭika and the like. ||SRs_3.432||

body.text:
nāṭikāyāḥ na pṛthag-rūpatvam-
nāṭikā tv anayor bhedo na pṛthag rūpakaṃ bhavet |
prakhyātaṃ nṛpater vṛttaṃ nāṭakād āhṛtaṃ yataḥ ||SRs_3.433|| 225
buddhi-kalpita-vastutvaṃ tathā prakaraṇād api |
vimarśa-sandhi-rāhityaṃ bhedakaṃ cen na tan matam ||SRs_3.434|| 226
ratnāvalyādike lakṣye tat-sandher api darśanāt |
strī-prāya-caturaṅkādi-bhedakaṃ cen na tan matam ||SRs_3.435|| 227
eka-dvi-try-aṅka-pātrādi-bhedenānantatā yataḥ |
devī-vaśāt saṅgamena bhedaś cet tan na yujyate |
mālavikāgni-mitrādau nāṭikātva-prasaṅgataḥ ||SRs_3.436|| 228
body.translated_text: The Nāṭikā (minor drama) is not a separate form — the Nāṭikā should not be a separate Rūpaka (dramatic form) distinct from these two. Since the plot is a well-known royal story — it is derived from the Nāṭaka; ||SRs_3.433|| since the subject matter is invented by the intellect — it is also [derived] from the Prakaraṇa. If the absence of the Vimarśa-sandhi (deliberation juncture) be cited as the distinguishing factor — that view is not accepted, ||SRs_3.434|| since that juncture is also observed in works like Ratnāvalī and the like. If predominantly female characters and four acts be cited as distinguishing factors — that view is not accepted, ||SRs_3.435|| since there would be infinite [types] through differences of one, two, three acts, characters, and the like. If the distinguishing factor be union through the intervention of a divine woman — that is not appropriate either, since it would entail classifying Mālavikāgnimitra and the like as Nāṭikās. ||SRs_3.436||

body.text:
prakaraṇikā-nāṭikayor anusaraṇīyā hi nāṭikā-saraṇiḥ |
ata eva bharata-muninā nāṭyaṃ daśadhā nirūpitaṃ pūrvam ||SRs_3.437|| 229
body.translated_text: The course to be followed for Prakaraṇikā and Nāṭikā is indeed that of the Nāṭikā. For this very reason, the sage Bharata originally established drama as tenfold only. ||SRs_3.437||

body.text:
atha utṛṣṭikāṅkaḥ-
khyātena vā kalpitena vastunā prākṛtair naraiḥ |
anvitaḥ kaiśikī-hīnaḥ sāttvatyārabhaṭī-mṛduḥ ||SRs_3.438|| 230
strīṇāṃ vilāpa-vyāpārair upetaḥ karuṇāśrayaḥ |
nānā-saṅgrāma-saṃnāha-prahāramaraṇotkaṭaḥ ||SRs_3.439|| 231
mukha-nirvāhavān yaḥ syād eka-dvi-try-aṅka icchayā |
utsṛṣṭikāṅkaḥ sa jñeyaḥ sa-viṣkambha-praveśakaḥ ||SRs_3.440|| 232
asminn amaṅgala-prāye kuryān maṅgalam antataḥ |
prayojyasya vadhaḥ kāryaḥ punar ujjīvanāvadhiḥ ||SRs_3.441|| 233
ujjīvanād apy adhikaṃ manoratha-phalo' pi vā |
vijñeyam asya lakṣyaṃ tu karuṇākandalādikam ||SRs_3.442|| 234
body.translated_text: Now the Utsṛṣṭikāṅka (abandoned-act form) — with subject matter either well-known or invented, accompanied by common (Prākṛta) characters, devoid of the Kaiśikī style, employing the Sāttvatī and Ārabhaṭī styles softly, ||SRs_3.438|| containing the activities of women's lamentations, based on the Karuṇa (pathetic) rasa, abounding in various battles, armings, blows, and deaths, ||SRs_3.439|| having only the Mukha (opening) and Nirvāhana (conclusion) [junctures], with one, two, or three acts as desired — that should be known as the Utsṛṣṭikāṅka, with Viṣkambha and Praveśaka. ||SRs_3.440|| In this [form], which is mostly inauspicious, an auspicious [event] should be placed at the end. The killing of the protagonist should be enacted, up to the point of his revival. ||SRs_3.441|| [There should be] even more than revival, or the fruition of a desire. Its exemplary work should be recognized as Karuṇā-kandala and the like. ||SRs_3.442||

body.text:
atha vyāyogaḥ-
khātetivṛtta-sampanno niḥsahāyaka-nāyakaḥ |
yukto daśāvaraih khyātair uddhataiḥ pratināyakaiḥ ||SRs_3.443|| 235
vimarśa-garbha-rahito bhāraty-ārabhaṭī-sphuṭaḥ |
hāsya-śṛṅgāra-rahita ekāṅko raudra-saṃśrayaḥ ||SRs_3.444|| 236
eka-vāsara-vṛttāntaḥ prāpta-viṣkambha-cūlikaḥ |

children.translated_text: with a battle not occasioned by a woman — that is called Vyāyoga by the learned. ||
Its subject matter should be understood as the victory of <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) and the like. ||3.445||

body.translated_text: Now the Vyāyoga (heroic one-act) — endowed with a well-known plot, with a hero without allies, accompanied by ten or fewer well-known, impetuous antagonists, ||SRs_3.443|| devoid of the Vimarśa and Garbha [junctures], clearly employing the Bhāratī and Ārabhaṭī styles, devoid of humor and erotic sentiment, consisting of one act, based on the Raudra (furious) rasa, ||SRs_3.444|| with action spanning a single day, furnished with Viṣkambha and Cūlikā,

body.text: atha bhāṇaḥ-

children.text: svasya vānyasya vā vṛttaṃ viṭena nipuṇoktinā | 238
children.translated_text: An account of one's own or another's life, narrated by a <s>viṭa</s> (man-about-town) with skillful speech, 238
praiseworthy for valor and good fortune, indicative of the Heroic and Erotic sentiments, ||3.446||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Bhāṇa</s> —

body.text: buddhi-kalpitam ekāṅkaṃ mukha-nirvahaṇānvitam | 239
body.translated_text: composed through imagination, having a single act, comprising the opening and concluding [junctures], 239

body.text: varṇyate bhāratī-vṛttyā yatra taṃ bhāṇam īrate ||SRs_3.447||
body.translated_text: and narrated in the <s>Bhāratī</s> mode — that is called a <s>Bhāṇa</s>. ||3.447||

body.text: eka-pātra-prayojye' smin kuryād ākāśa-bhāṣitam | 240
body.translated_text: In this [genre], to be performed by a single actor, one should employ <s>ākāśa-bhāṣita</s> (speech addressed to the sky/an imaginary interlocutor). 240

body.text: anyenānuktam apy anyo vacaḥ śrutveva yad vadet ||SRs_3.448||
body.translated_text: Where one speaks as if having heard the speech of another, though that other has not actually spoken — ||3.448||

body.text: iti kiṃ bhaṇasīty etad bhaved ākāśa-bhāṣitam | 241
body.translated_text: 'What is it you say?' — such is <s>ākāśa-bhāṣita</s>. 241

body.text: lāsyāṅgāni daśaitasmin saṃyojyānyatra tāni tu ||SRs_3.449||
body.translated_text: In this [genre], the ten <s>lāsya</s> elements should be combined; elsewhere they [are optional]. ||3.449||

body.text: geya-padaṃ sthita-pāṭhyam āsīnaṃ puṣpa-gandhikā | 242
body.translated_text: <s>Geya-pada</s> (sung verse), <s>Sthita-pāṭhya</s> (recitation while standing), <s>Āsīna</s> (recitation while seated), <s>Puṣpa-gandhikā</s> (flower-fragrance dance), 242

body.text:
pracchedakas trimūḍhaṃ ca saindhavākhyaṃ dvimūḍhakam |
uttamottamakaṃ cānyad ukta-pratyuktam eva ca ||SRs_3.450|| 243
body.translated_text: <s>Pracchedaka</s> (love-quarrel), <s>Trimūḍha</s> (triple-bewilderment), <s>Saindhava</s> (Sindhi dance), <s>Dvimūḍhaka</s> (double-bewilderment), <s>Uttamottamaka</s> (supreme-excellence), and <s>Ukta-pratyukta</s> (dialogue in verse). ||3.450|| 243

body.text:
atha geya-padam-
vīṇādi-vādanenaiva sahitaṃ yatra bhāvyate |
lalitaṃ nāyikā-gītaṃ tad geya-padam ucyate ||SRs_3.451|| 244
cañcat-puṭādinā vākyābhinayo nāyikā-kṛtaḥ |
bhūmi-cārī-pracāreṇa sthita-pāṭhyaṃ tad ucyate ||SRs_3.452|| 245
bhrū-netra-pāṇi-caraṇa-vilāsābhinayānvitam |
yojyam āsīnayā pāṭhyam āsīnaṃ tad udāhṛtam ||SRs_3.453|| 246
nānā-vidhena vādyena nānā-tāla-layānvitam |
lāsyaṃ prayujyate yatra sā jñeyā puṣpa-gandhikā ||SRs_3.454|| 247
anyāsaṅgama-śaṅkinyā nāyakasyātiroṣayā |
prema-ccheda-prakaṭanaṃ lāsyaṃ pracchedakaṃ viduḥ ||SRs_3.455|| 248
aniṣṭhura-ślakṣṇa-padaṃ sama-vṛttair alaṅkṛtam |
nāṭyaṃ puruṣa-bhāvāḍhyaṃ trimūḍhakam udāhṛtam ||SRs_3.456|| 249
deśa-bhāṣā-viśeṣeṇa calad-valaya-śṛṅkhalam |
lāsyaṃ prayujyate yatra tat saindhavam iti smṛtam ||SRs_3.457|| 250
cārībhir lalitābhiś ca citrārthābhinayānvitam |
spaṣṭa-bhāva-rasopetaṃ lāsyaṃ yat tad dvimūḍhakam ||SRs_3.458|| 251
aparijñāta-pārśvasthaṃ geya-bhāva-vibhūṣitam |
lāsyaṃ sotkaṇṭha-vākyaṃ tad uttamottamakaṃ bhavet ||SRs_3.459|| 252
kopa-prasāda-janitaṃ sādhikṣepa-padāśrayam |
vākyaṃ tad ukta-pratyuktaṃ yūnoḥ praśnottarātmakam ||SRs_3.460|| 253
śṛṅgāra-mañjarī-mukhyam asyodāharaṇaṃ matam |
lāsyāṅga-daśakaṃ tatra lakṣyaṃ lakṣya-vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||SRs_3.461|| 254
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Geya-pada</s> — Where a graceful song by the heroine is performed accompanied by the playing of the <s>vīṇā</s> and other instruments — that is called <s>Geya-pada</s>. ||3.451|| 244 Where the heroine's verbal acting is performed with opening gestures (<s>cañcat-puṭa</s>) and the like, through the movement of <s>bhūmi-cārī</s> (ground-movements) — that is called <s>Sthita-pāṭhya</s> (recitation while standing). ||3.452|| 245 Recitation to be performed while seated, accompanied by the acting of brow, eye, hand, and foot movements — that is called <s>Āsīna</s> (seated recitation). ||3.453|| 246 Where <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance) is performed with various kinds of instrumental music and various beats and tempos — that is known as <s>Puṣpa-gandhikā</s>. ||3.454|| 247 Where a heroine, suspicious of [her lover's] meeting with another woman, openly displays the cutting of affection through excessive anger at the hero — the learned call that <s>lāsya</s> [element] <s>Pracchedaka</s>. ||3.455|| 248 Drama that is neither harsh nor rough in diction, adorned with even meters, and rich in masculine sentiment — that is called <s>Trimūḍhaka</s>. ||3.456|| 249 Where <s>lāsya</s> is performed in a regional dialect, with swinging bangles in chains — that is known as <s>Saindhava</s>. ||3.457|| 250 <s>Lāsya</s> performed with graceful <s>cārīs</s> (dance-movements), accompanied by acting of varied meanings, endowed with clear <s>bhāva</s> and <s>rasa</s> — that is <s>Dvimūḍhaka</s>. ||3.458|| 251 <s>Lāsya</s> performed without the companion being recognized, adorned with sung emotion, with speech full of longing — that is <s>Uttamottamaka</s>. ||3.459|| 252 Speech born of anger and appeasement, containing words of reproach, consisting of questions and answers between a young couple — that is <s>Ukta-pratyukta</s>. ||3.460|| 253 The <s>Śṛṅgāra-mañjarī</s> and such are considered primary examples of this. The ten <s>lāsya</s> elements therein should be observed by those skilled in examples. ||3.461|| 254

body.text:
atha samavakāraḥ-
prakhyātenetivṛttena nāyakair api tad-vidhaiḥ |
pṛthak-prayojanāsaktair militair deva-dānavaiḥ ||SRs_3.462|| 255
yuktaṃ dvādaśabhir vīra-pradhānaṃ kaiśikī-mṛdu |
try-aṅkaṃ vimarśa-hīnaṃ ca kapaṭa-traya-saṃyutam ||SRs_3.463|| 256
tri-vidravaṃ tri-śṛṅgāraṃ vidyāt samavakārakam |
mohātmako bhramaḥ proktaḥ kapaṭas trividhas tv ayam ||SRs_3.464|| 257
sattvajaḥ śatrujo daiva-janitaś ceti sattvajaḥ |
krūra-prāṇi-samutpannaḥ śatrujas tu raṇādijaḥ ||SRs_3.465|| 258
vātyāvarṣādi-sambhūto daivajaḥ kapaṭaḥ smṛtaḥ |
udāharaṇam eteṣām āvege lakṣyatāṃ budhaiḥ ||SRs_3.466|| 259
jīva-grāho' pi moho vā kapaṭād vidravas tataḥ |

children.translated_text: And this [flight] is considered threefold, being born from the triad of deceptions. 260
The <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is declared to be threefold: connected with <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and <s>Kāma</s>. ||3.467||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Samavakāra</s> — With a well-known plot, with heroes of the same kind, attached to different purposes, who are gods and demons assembled together, ||3.462|| 255 endowed with twelve [character-types], primarily heroic, soft with the <s>Kaiśikī</s> mode, having three acts, devoid of deliberation (<s>vimarśa</s>), and furnished with a triad of deceptions, ||3.463|| 256 having three flights, and three kinds of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> — such should be known as a <s>Samavakāra</s>. Delusion-natured bewilderment is called <s>bhrama</s>; deception (<s>kapaṭa</s>) is of three kinds: ||3.464|| 257 born of <s>sattva</s> (innate), born of the enemy, and born of fate. The <s>sattva</s>-born arises from fierce animals; the enemy-born arises from battle and the like; ||3.465|| 258 that born of storms, rain, and the like is called fate-born deception. Examples of these should be observed by the wise in the [section on] <s>Āvega</s>. ||3.466|| 259 From deception: capture alive or delusion; from that, flight.

body.text: dharma-śṛṅgāraḥ-

children.translated_text: Desire born of vows and the like is called <s>Dharma-śṛṅgāra</s>. 261
The union of <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Śiva</s> is considered its example. ||3.468||

body.translated_text: <s>Dharma-śṛṅgāra</s> —

body.text: artha-śṛṅgāraḥ-

children.translated_text: Where the attainment of happiness through wealth connected with and attendant upon desire 262
[is depicted] — that is called <s>Artha-śṛṅgāra</s>. ||3.469||

body.translated_text: <s>Artha-śṛṅgāra</s> —

body.text: sārvabhauma-phala-prāpti-hetunā vatsa-bhūpateḥ | 263
body.translated_text: The enjoyment of King <s>Vatsa</s> (<s>Udayana</s>) with <s>Ratnāvalī</s>, 263

body.text: ratnāvalyā samaṃ bhogo vijñeyā tad udāhṛtiḥ ||SRs_3.470||
body.translated_text: motivated by the attainment of the fruit of universal sovereignty — that should be known as its example. ||3.470||

body.text: kāma-śṛṅgāraḥ-

children.translated_text: That which arises from sport in forbidden liquor-drinking, 264
other men's wives, and the like, graceful with the relish of each — is called <s>Kāma-śṛṅgāra</s>. ||3.471||

body.translated_text: <s>Kāma-śṛṅgāra</s> —

body.text: tad udāharaṇaṃ prāyo dṛśyaṃ prasanādiṣu | 265
body.translated_text: Its examples are generally to be seen in the <s>Prasanna</s> [plays] and the like. 265

body.text: śṛṅgāra-tritayaṃ tatra nātra bindu-praveśakau ||SRs_3.472||
body.translated_text: The triad of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> is therein; in this [genre] there are no <s>Bindu</s> or <s>Praveśaka</s>. ||3.472||

body.text: mukha-pratimukhe sandhī vastu dvādaśa-nāḍikam | 266
body.translated_text: The <s>Mukha</s> and <s>Pratimukha</s> junctures, and a subject-matter of twelve <s>nāḍikās</s> (time-units) — 266

body.text: prathame kalpayed aṅke nāḍikā ghaṭikā-dvayam ||SRs_3.473||
body.translated_text: should be arranged in the first act, each <s>nāḍikā</s> being two <s>ghaṭikās</s>. ||3.473||

body.text: mukhādi-sandhi-trayavāṃś caturnāḍika-vastukaḥ | 267
body.translated_text: The second act has the three junctures beginning with <s>Mukha</s>, and a subject-matter of four <s>nāḍikās</s>; 267

body.text: dvitīyāṅkas tṛtīyas tu dvi-nāḍika-kathāśrayaḥ ||SRs_3.474||
body.translated_text: the third act has a narrative content of two <s>nāḍikās</s>. ||3.474||

body.text: nirvimarśa-catuḥ-sandhir evam aṅkās trayaḥ smṛtāḥ | 268
body.translated_text: Without <s>Vimarśa</s>, having four junctures — thus three acts are prescribed. 268

body.text: vīthī-prahasanāṅgāni kuryād atra samāsataḥ ||SRs_3.475||
body.translated_text: In this [genre], elements of the <s>Vīthī</s> and <s>Prahasana</s> should be employed in brief. ||3.475||

body.text: prastāvanāyāḥ prastāve prokto vīthy-aṅga-vistaraḥ | 269
body.translated_text: In the <s>Prastāva</s> (prelude) of the <s>Prastāvanā</s> (prologue), the elaboration of <s>Vīthī</s> elements has been stated. 269

body.text:
daśa prahasanāṅgāni tat-prasaṅge pracakṣmahe |
udāharaṇam etasya payodhi-mathanādikam ||SRs_3.476|| 270
body.translated_text: The ten elements of the <s>Prahasana</s> we shall describe in connection with that [genre]. The example of this [<s>Samavakāra</s>] is the Churning of the Ocean and the like. ||3.476|| 270

body.text:
atha vīthī-
sūcya-pradhāna-śṛṅgārā mukha-nirvahaṇānvitā |
eka-yojyā dviyojyā vā kaiśikī-vṛtti-nirmitā ||SRs_3.477|| 271
vīthy-aṅga-sahitaikāṅkā vīthīti kathitā budhaiḥ |
asyāṃ prāyeṇa lāsyāṅga-daśakaṃ yojayen na vā ||SRs_3.478|| 272
sāmānyā parakīyā vā nāyikātrānurāgiṇī |

children.translated_text: a respectable family woman is not suitable, since the [genre's] mode of functioning consists mainly of <s>Vīthī</s> elements. 273
Its illustrative example should be known as the <s>Mādhavī-vīthikā</s> and the like. ||3.479||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Vīthī</s> — Having <s>Sūcya</s> (indication) as its chief [element], with the <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> sentiment, comprising the opening and concluding [junctures], to be performed by one or two [actors], fashioned in the <s>Kaiśikī</s> mode, ||3.477|| 271 having a single act together with <s>Vīthī</s> elements — that is called a <s>Vīthī</s> by the wise. In it, the ten <s>lāsya</s> elements may or may not be employed. ||3.478|| 272 The heroine therein is a common woman or another's wife, who is enamored;

body.text: atha prahasanam-

children.translated_text: Where the subject-matter, junctures, acts, <s>lāsya</s> elements, and modes are as in the <s>Bhāṇa</s>, 274

children.text: raso hāsyaḥ pradhānaṃ syād etat prahasanaṃ matam ||SRs_3.480||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Hāsya</s> (comic) <s>rasa</s> is predominant — that is considered a <s>Prahasana</s>. ||3.480||

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Prahasana</s> (farce) —

body.text: viśeṣeṇa daśāṅgāni kalpayed atra tāni tu | 275
body.translated_text: Specifically, ten elements should be devised therein; they are: 275

body.text:
avagalitāvaskandau vyavahāro vipralambha upapattiḥ |
bhayam anṛtaṃ vibhrāntir gadgada-vāk ca pralāpaś ca ||SRs_3.481|| 276
body.translated_text: <s>Avagalita</s> (lapse), <s>Avaskanda</s> (rival claims), <s>Vyavahāra</s> (dispute), <s>Vipralambha</s> (deception), <s>Upapatti</s> (justification), <s>Bhaya</s> (fear), <s>Anṛta</s> (falsehood), <s>Vibhrānti</s> (confusion), <s>Gadgada-vāk</s> (stammering speech), and <s>Pralāpa</s> (babbling). ||3.481|| 276

body.text:
tatra avagalitam-
pūrvam ātma-gṛhītasya samācārasya mohataḥ |
dūṣaṇaṃ tyajanaṃ cātra dvidhāvagalitaṃ matam ||SRs_3.482|| 277
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>Avagalita</s> (lapse) — The censure of, or the abandoning of, a practice previously adopted by oneself, out of delusion — <s>Avagalita</s> is considered to be of two kinds. ||3.482|| 277

body.text: yathā ānanda-kośa-nāmani prahasane, mithyā-tīrthaḥ-
body.translated_text: As in the farce named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s> — <s>Mithyā-tīrtha</s> (the false pilgrim):

children.text: yāni dyanti galād adhaḥ sukṛtino lomnāṃ ca teṣāṃ sthitiṃ
children.translated_text: 'Those [hairs] which droop down from the neck — of those the maintenance of the meritorious ones [is enjoined],

children.text: yāny ūrdhvaṃ paripoṣayanti puruṣās teṣāṃ muhuḥ khaṇḍanam |
children.translated_text: and those which grow upward, men constantly shave them off —
having acted by a rule contrary to the entire world, for wanderers like me,

children.text: śrī-gītā ca harītakī ca harato hantopabhogyaṃ vayaḥ ||SRs_3.483||
children.translated_text: the <s>Śrī-Gītā</s> and the <s>harītakī</s> (myrobalan) fruit — alas! — consume the enjoyable years of life!' ||3.483||

body.text: atra kenāpi yati-bhraṣṭena sva-gṛhītasya yaty-āśramasya dūṣaṇād idam avagalitam |
body.translated_text: Here, since some fallen ascetic censures the ascetic life he himself adopted, this is <s>Avagalita</s>.

body.text: tyajanād, yathā prabodha-candrodaye, kṣapaṇakaḥ-
body.translated_text: From abandoning, as in the <s>Prabodhacandrodaya</s> — the <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s> (Jain monk) [speaks in Prakrit]:

children.translated_text: 'O beauty of full, firm breasts, with the eyes of a startled fawn —

children.text: jai lamasi kāvāliṇī-bhāvehiṃ sābakā kiṃ kalissaṃdi ||SRs_3.484||
children.translated_text: if you sport with the ways of a <s>Kāpālinī</s> (female Kāpālika ascetic), what will the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (Jain lay-followers) do?'

body.text: aho kāvāliṇīadaṃsaṇaṃ jebba ekkaṃ saukkhamokkha-sāhaṇam | (prakāśam) bho kābālia hagge tuhake saṃpadaṃ dāso saṃbutto | maṃ pi mahābhairavānusāsaṇe dikkhaya |
body.translated_text: 'Ah! The sight of a <s>Kāpālinī</s> is the one means of attaining the bliss of liberation!' (Aloud) 'O <s>Kāpālika</s>! I have now become your servant. Initiate me too into the doctrine of <s>Mahābhairava</s>!'

body.text:
[ayi pīna-ghana-stana-śobhane paritrasta-kuraṅga-vilocane |
yadi ramase kāpālinī-bhāvaiḥ śrāvakāḥ kiṃ kariṣyanti |
body.translated_text: [Sanskrit equivalent of the above Prakrit:] 'O beauty of full, firm breasts, with the eyes of a startled fawn —

body.text: aho kāpālinī-darśanam eva ekaṃ saukhya-mokṣa-sādhanam | (prakāśam) bho kāpālika ahaṃ tava samprataṃ dāsaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | mām api mahā-bhairavānuśāsane dikṣaya |]
body.translated_text: if you sport with the ways of a <s>Kāpālinī</s>, what will the <s>Śrāvakas</s> do?' 'Ah! The sight of a <s>Kāpālinī</s> alone is the means of attaining the bliss of liberation!' (Aloud) 'O <s>Kāpālika</s>! I have now become your servant. Initiate me too into the doctrine of <s>Mahābhairava</s>!'

body.text: ity ādau kṣapaṇakasya sva-mārga-paribhraṃśa avagalitam |
body.translated_text: Here and so forth, the <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s>'s falling from his own path is <s>Avagalita</s>.

body.text:
atha avaskandaḥ-
avaskandas tv anekeṣām ayogyasyaika-vastunaḥ |
sambandhābhāsa-kathanāt sva-sva-yogyatva-yojanā ||SRs_3.485|| 278
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Avaskanda</s> (rival claims) — <s>Avaskanda</s> is the association, through an appearance of connection, of many [claimants] to a single unworthy object, each establishing his own fitness. ||3.485|| 278

body.text: yathā prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani)-
body.translated_text: As in the farce (named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) —

body.text: yatiḥ-sākṣād bhūtaṃ vadati kucayor antaraṃ dvaita-vādaṃ
body.translated_text: The ascetic: 'The space between the breasts directly proclaims the truth — the doctrine of duality!';

body.text: bauddhaḥ-dṛṣṭyor bhedaḥ kṣaṇika-mahimā saugate datta-pādaḥ |
body.translated_text: the Buddhist: 'The distinction of the two eyes — the glory of momentariness — has its footing in the <s>Saugata</s> school!';

body.text: jainaḥ-bāhvor mūle nayati śucitām arhatī kāpi dīkṣā
body.translated_text: the Jain: 'A certain initiation of <s>Arhat</s> brings purity to the base of the arms!';

body.text: sarve-nābher mūlaṃ prathayati phalaṃ sarva-siddhānta-sāram ||SRs_3.486||
body.translated_text: All: 'The root of the navel proclaims the fruit — the essence of all philosophical doctrines!' ||3.486||

body.text: atra yati-bauddha-jainānāṃ gaṇikāyāṃ sva-sva-siddhānta-dharma-sambandha-kathanena sva-sva-pakṣa-parigraha-yogyatva-yojanād avaskandaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, since the ascetic, the Buddhist, and the Jain each narrate the connection of their own philosophical doctrine to the courtesan and thereby establish their own fitness — this is <s>Avaskanda</s>.

body.text:
atha vyavahāraḥ-
vyavahāras tu saṃvādo dvitrāṇāṃ hāsya-kāraṇam ||SRs_3.487|| 279a
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vyavahāra</s> (dispute) — <s>Vyavahāra</s> is the conversation of two or three [persons] that is the cause of laughter. ||3.487|| 279a

body.text: yathā tatraiva prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani) bauddhaḥ (yatiṃ vilokya)-kuto maṇḍa eka-daṇḍī |
body.translated_text: As in the same farce (<s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) — the Buddhist (looking at the ascetic): 'Where from, O shaven, single-staff [ascetic]?'

body.text: mithyā-tīrthaḥ (vilokya dṛṣṭim apakarṣan ātma-gatam)-kṣaṇikavādī na sambhāṣaṇīya eva | tathāpi daṇḍam antardhāya niruttaraṃ karomi | (prakāśam) aye śūnya-vādin ! adaṇḍaḥ amuṇḍo' ham āgalād asmi |
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyā-tīrtha</s> (looking at him, averting his gaze, aside): 'The momentariness-advocate should not be conversed with at all. Still, concealing my staff, I shall render him speechless.' (Aloud) 'O Void-ist! I have come from the beyond, staff-less and unshaven!'

body.text: jainaḥ (ātma-gatam)-nūnam asau māyāvādī | bhavatu | aham api kim apy antardhāya prastutaṃ pṛcchāmi | (prakāśam) aye mahā-pariṇāma-vādin ! bṛhad-bīja lomnāṃ samāna-jātīyatve' pi keṣāñcit saṅkartanam anyeṣāṃ saṃrakṣaṇam iti vyavasthitau kiṃ pramāṇam ?
body.translated_text: The Jain (aside): 'Surely that one is a <s>Māyā-vādin</s> (illusionist). Very well. I too shall conceal something and ask the relevant question.' (Aloud) 'O great transformation-advocate! Though hairs — both big-seeded and small — belong to the same species, what is the authority for the rule that some must be shaved while others are preserved?'

body.text: mithyā-tīrthaḥ-jīvad amedhyaṃ jaṅgama-narako nara-piśāco' yam antardhāyāpi na sambhāṣaṇīyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyā-tīrtha</s>: 'A living piece of filth, a walking hell, a human <s>Piśāca</s> — even concealed, this one is not to be conversed with!'

body.text: niṣkaccha-kīrtiḥ (sādaram)-sakhe ! ārhata-mune vāde tvayā ayam apratipattiṃ nāma nigraha-sthānam āropito māyāvādī |
body.translated_text: <s>Niṣkaccha-kīrti</s> (with respect): 'Friend! O <s>Ārhata</s> sage, in debate you have imposed upon this <s>Māyā-vādin</s> the defeat-ground of incompetence!'

body.text: mithyā-tīrthaḥ (ātma-gatam)-nūnam imāv api mādṛśāv eva liṅga-dhāraṇa-mātreṇa kukṣimbharaī syātām | (iti pippala-mūla-vedikāyāṃ niṣīdati |)
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyā-tīrtha</s> (aside): 'Surely these two are also like me — mere belly-fillers through the wearing of religious marks!' (He sits down on the platform at the foot of a fig tree.)

body.text: ity atra yati-bauddha-jainānāṃ saṃvādo vyavahāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the conversation of the ascetic, the Buddhist, and the Jain is <s>Vyavahāra</s>.

body.text:
atha vipralambhaḥ-
vipralambho vañcanā syād bhūtāveśādi-kaitavāt ||SRs_3.488|| 279b
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Vipralambha</s> (deception) — <s>Vipralambha</s> is swindling through the pretense of spirit-possession and the like. ||3.488|| 279b

body.text: yathā prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani tatraiva)-
body.translated_text: As in the farce (the same <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) —

children.translated_text: 'I shall take my former beloved, named <s>Svacchanda-bhakṣiṇī</s> (she who eats at will);

children.text: gṛhṇāmy enāṃ yadi trātuṃ kṛpā vaḥ śrūyatām idam ||SRs_3.489||
children.translated_text: if you have compassion to save her, hear this: ||3.489||
'With seventy pots of liquor, with twenty fat billy-goats,
and with ten [more] goats, the ritual of the <s>Ciraṇṭī</s>-appeasement is to be performed.' ||3.490||

children.text: adya kartum aśakyaṃ cet tat-paryāptatamaṃ dhanam |
children.translated_text: 'If it cannot be done today, then an equivalent amount of money
should be deposited in the garment-border of this old woman, who is the witness.' ||3.491||

body.text: (iti punar api vyātta-vadanaṃ nṛtyati |)
body.translated_text: (He then dances again with gaping mouth.)

body.text: niṣkaccha-kīrtiḥ-he vratinau ! kim atra vidheyam ?
body.translated_text: <s>Niṣkaccha-kīrti</s>: 'O you two ascetics! What is to be done here?'

body.text: mithyā-tīrthaḥ-bhoḥ ahiṃsā-vādin ! mriyamāṇaḥ prāṇī na rakṣaṇīya iti kiṃ yuṣmad-dharmaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyā-tīrtha</s>: 'O advocate of non-violence! Is it your doctrine that a dying creature should not be saved?'

body.text: arūpāmbaraḥ (sākṣepam)-ekena sukham upādeyam | anyena dhanaṃ pradeyam iti kiṃ yuṣmad-dharmaḥ ?
body.translated_text: <s>Arūpāmbara</s> (with disdain): 'One person enjoys comfort, another must give money — is that your doctrine?'

body.text: niṣkaccha-kīrtiḥ sāntarhāsaṃ sva-dhanaṃ yati-dhanaṃ ca jaraṭhāyāḥ paṭāñcale baddhvā sabalātkāraṃ jainasya kaṭakaṃ tasyāḥ pāda-mūle' rpayati |)
body.translated_text: <s>Niṣkaccha-kīrti</s> (with a hidden laugh) ties his own money and the ascetic's money in the old woman's garment-border, and forcibly places the Jain's bracelet at her feet.)

body.text: madhumallikā (sāṅga-bhaṅgaṃ sasmraṇa-bhayam iva)-ammo devadā vilambeṇa kuppissadi | tā ciraṃṭi-ātappaṇaṃ kāduṃ gacchemi | [amho ! devatā vilambena kopiṣyati | tat ciraṇṭikā-tarpaṇaṃ kartuṃ gacchāmi |] (iti kaṭakam ādāya niṣkrāntā |)
body.translated_text: <s>Madhumallikā</s> (with a feigned body-movement, as if in alarm at remembering) — [Prakrit:] 'Oh! The deity will be angry at the delay! So I shall go to perform the <s>Ciraṇṭikā</s>-worship!' (Taking the bracelet, she exits.)

body.text: ity ādau bhūtāveśa-kaitavena jaina-bauddha-saṃnyāsino vilobhya dhanaṃ kayāpi gaṇikayā gṛhītam ity ayaṃ vipralambhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, at the beginning, some courtesan, having enticed a Jain, a Buddhist, and a <s>Saṃnyāsin</s> through the pretense of spirit-possession, has taken their money — this constitutes <s>vipralambha</s> (deception).

body.text:
atha upapattiḥ-
upapattis tu sā proktā yat prasiddhasya vastunaḥ |
loka-prasiddhayā yuktyā sādhanaṃ hāsya-hetunā ||SRs_3.492|| 280
body.translated_text:
Now <s>upapatti</s> (plausible reasoning) —
<s>Upapatti</s> is declared to be the proving of a well-known fact
by a popularly known reasoning, [employed] as a cause of humor. ||3.492||

body.text: yathā tatraiva prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani) mithyā-tīrthaḥ (puro' valokya)-aye upasarit-tīre pippala-nāmā vanaspatiḥ | yaś ca gītāsu bhagavatā nija-vibhūtitayā nirdiṣṭaḥ | (vicintya) katham asya taror iyatī mahima-sambhāvanā | (vimṛśya) upapadyata eva-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same farce (named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) — <s>Mithyā-tīrtha</s> (looking ahead) — 'Look! On the bank of the tributary stands the <s>Pippala</s>-named sacred tree, which the Blessed One designated in the <s>Gītā</s> as his own divine manifestation!' (Reflecting) 'How can such greatness be attributed to this tree?' (Deliberating) 'It is indeed fitting —

body.text:
tat padaṃ tanu-madhyāyā yenāśvattha-dalopamam |
tad-aśvattho' smi vṛkṣāṇām ity ūce bhagavān hariḥ ||SRs_3.493|| iti |
body.translated_text:
'That abode of the slender-waisted one [a woman's groin], which is like the leaf of the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) —
therefore "I am the <s>Aśvattha</s> among trees" — thus spoke the blessed <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>).' ||3.493|| Thus.

body.text: atra loka-prasiddhena aśvattha-daloru-mūlayoḥ sāmyena hetunā loka-prasiddhasyaiva bhagavad-aśvatthayor aikyasya sādhanaṃ hāsya-kāraṇam upapattiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the proving — by the popularly known reasoning of the similarity between the <s>Aśvattha</s> leaf and the base of the thigh — of the well-known identity of the Blessed One and the <s>Aśvattha</s> tree, as a cause of humor, constitutes <s>upapatti</s>.

body.text:
atha bhayam-
smṛtaṃ bhayaṃ tu nagara-śodhakādi-kṛto daraḥ ||SRs_3.494|| 281a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>bhaya</s> (fear) —
<s>Bhaya</s> is recalled as the alarm caused by city-patrol officers and the like. ||3.494||

body.text: yathā tatraiva prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani) jainaḥ-aho arājako' yaṃ viṣayaḥ yat nagara-parisarāśrita-tapasvināṃ dhanaṃ coryate (ity udvāhur ākrośati) |
body.translated_text: For example, in the same farce (named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) — the Jain [says] — 'Ah, this is a lawless territory, that the wealth of ascetics dwelling in the city's environs is being stolen!' (He shouts in protest.)

body.text: nagara-rakṣakāḥ-aye kim apahṛtaṃ dhanam | kiyat (iti taṃ paritaḥ praviśya parisarpanti |)
body.translated_text: The city guards — 'Hey, what wealth has been stolen? How much?' (They enter and search around him.)

body.text: arūpāmbaraḥ-dhik kaṣṭam | nagara-śīghrakāḥ samāyānti | (ity ūrdhva-bāhur oṣṭha-spandanaṃ karoti | mithyā-tīrtho gaṇikām ākṣipya samādhiṃ nāṭayati | niṣkaccha-kīrtir eka-pādenāvatiṣṭhamānaḥ karāṅgulīr gaṇayati) ity ādau jainādīnāṃ bhaya-kathanād bhayam |
body.translated_text: <s>Arūpāmbara</s> — 'Alas, the calamity! The city patrols are approaching!' (He raises his arms and moves his lips [in silent prayer]. <s>Mithyā-tīrtha</s> throws aside the courtesan and feigns meditation. <s>Niṣkaccha-kīrti</s>, standing on one leg, counts his fingers.) — Here, because this narrates the fear of the Jain and the others, it constitutes <s>bhaya</s>.

body.text: atha anṛtam-

children.translated_text: <s>Anṛta</s> is speech interwoven with vulgar praise.

children.text: tad evānṛtam ity āhur apare sva-mata-stuteḥ ||SRs_3.495||
children.translated_text: Others say that <s>anṛta</s> is [speech that takes the form of] praise of one's own doctrine. ||3.495||

body.translated_text: Now <s>anṛta</s> (indecent speech) —

body.text: yathā tatraiva prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani)-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same farce (named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) —

children.translated_text: Like a lotus touched by the morning sun,
like the parasol of <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the God of Love) with its crimson cloth,
like a lacquer-marked casket of pleasure —

children.text: yūnāṃ mude taruṇi tat padam ārtavaṃ te ||SRs_3.496||
children.translated_text: today, O young woman, that menstrual abode of yours is for the delight of young men! ||3.496||

body.text: atra ārtavāruṇasyoru-mūlasya (asabhyasya) varṇanād idam anṛtam |
body.translated_text: Here, because of the description of the vulgar [subject of] the menstrual region at the base of the thigh, this is <s>anṛta</s>.

body.text: aparaṃ, yathā karpūra-mañjaryām, bhairavānandaḥ-
body.translated_text: Another [example], as in the <s>Karpūra-mañjarī</s>, <s>Bhairavānanda</s> [says] —

body.text:
raṃḍā caṃḍā dikkhadā dhamma-dārā
majjaṃ maṃsaṃ pijjae khajjae a |
bhikkhā bhojjaṃ camma-khaṇḍaṃ ca sejjā
kolo dhammo kassa ṇo bhādi rammo ||SRs_3.497|| [ka.maṃ. 1.23]

children.translated_text: [A widow fierce is the initiated wife of <s>dharma</s>;
liquor and meat are drunk and eaten;
alms are food, a scrap of hide the bed;

children.text: kaulo dharmaḥ kasya no bhāti ramyaḥ ||]
children.translated_text: the <s>Kaula</s> doctrine — to whom does it not appear delightful?]

body.text:
atha vibhrāntiḥ-
vastu-sāmya-kṛto moho vibhrāntir iti gīyate ||SRs_3.498|| 282b
body.translated_text:
Now <s>vibhrānti</s> (bewilderment) —
Delusion caused by the similarity of objects is called <s>vibhrānti</s>. ||3.498||

body.text: yathā tatraiva prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani) bauddhaḥ (puro' valokya)-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same farce (named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) — the Buddhist (looking ahead) —

children.translated_text: 'With golden pinnacles, with lovely arches, with beautiful mirrors —
some <s>Gandharva</s>-city (mirage-city) is seen, walking on the earth!' ||3.499||

body.text: jainaḥ-aye kṣaṇa-bhaṅga-vādin etad utpāta-phalaṃ prathama-darśino bhavata eva pariṇamet | (iti locane nimīlayati |)
body.translated_text: The Jain — 'O advocate of momentariness! May this portent's fruit ripen for you, who first beheld it!' (He closes his eyes.)

body.text: bauddhaḥ (punar nirvarṇya)-hanta kim apade bhrānto' smi |
body.translated_text: The Buddhist (looking again) — 'Ah! I have been deluded without cause!'

children.text: na purīyaṃ viśālākṣī na toraṇam ime bhruvau |
children.translated_text: 'This is not a city — [but] a wide-eyed [woman]; these are not arches — [but] her brows;

children.text: na darpaṇam imau gaṇḍau na ca kumbhāv imau stanau ||SRs_3.500||
children.translated_text: these are not mirrors — [but] her cheeks; and these are not golden pots — [but] her breasts!' ||3.500||

body.text: ity atra bauddhasya moho vibhrāntiḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the delusion of the Buddhist constitutes <s>vibhrānti</s>.

body.text:
atha gadgada-vāk-
asatya-ruditonmiśraṃ vākyaṃ gadgada-vāg bhavet ||SRs_3.501|| 283a
body.translated_text:
Now <s>gadgada-vāk</s> (choked speech) —
Speech mixed with false weeping is <s>gadgada-vāk</s>. ||3.501||

body.text: yathā tatraiva prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani) (bhaginyau parasparam āśliṣya rudita iva) guhyagrāhī (ātmagatam)-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same farce (named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) (the two 'sisters' embrace each other and weep as if [genuinely]) — <s>Guhyagrāhī</s> (aside) —

children.translated_text: 'Without actual tear-drops, mingled with choked sighs, indistinct —
this false weeping of theirs seems to reveal the state at the end of love-making.' ||3.502||

body.text: atra gadgada-vāktvaṃ spaṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>gadgada-vāk</s> quality is evident.

body.text:
atha pralāpaḥ-
pralāpaḥ syād ayogyasya yogyatvenānumodanam ||SRs_3.503|| 283b
body.translated_text:
Now <s>pralāpa</s> (absurd endorsement) —
<s>Pralāpa</s> is the endorsement of something unfit as if it were fit. ||3.503||

body.text: yathā tatraiva prahasane (ānanda-kośa-nāmani) rājā (saudāryodrekam)-aye viḍālākṣa asmadīye nagare viṣaye ca-
body.translated_text: For example, in the same farce (named <s>Ānanda-kośa</s>) — the King (with an excess of magnanimity) — 'O <s>Viḍālākṣa</s>, in our city and territory —

children.text: pati-hīnā ca yā nārī jāyā-hīnaś ca yaḥ pumān |
children.translated_text: 'Let a woman without a husband and a man without a wife

children.text: tau dampatī yathā-kāmaṃ bhavetām iti ghuṣyatām ||SRs_3.504||
children.translated_text: become a couple at will — let this be proclaimed!' ||3.504||

body.text: viḍālākṣaḥ-devaḥ pramāṇam | (iti sānucaro niṣkrāntaḥ |)
body.translated_text: <s>Viḍālākṣa</s> — 'The king's word is authority.' (He exits with his attendant.)

body.text: guhya-grāhī (sa-ślāghā-gauravam)-
body.translated_text: <s>Guhyagrāhī</s> (with mock reverential gravity) —

children.translated_text: 'Demonstrated by the maxim of "the horse is lost, the cart is broken" [i.e., too late],
this proclamation of compassion is fitting for you, O great king!' ||3.505||
Moreover —
'<s>Manu</s> and other kings protected the earth in hundreds;

children.text: na kenāpi kṛto mārga evam āścarya-śaukhyadaḥ ||SRs_3.506||
children.translated_text: by none was a path created that grants such astonishing happiness!' ||3.506||

body.text: atra ayogyasyāpi rājādeśasya dharmādhikāriṇā guhya-grāhiṇā nyāya-parikalpanayā yogyatvenānumodanād ayaṃ pralāpaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, because <s>Guhyagrāhī</s>, the officer of <s>dharma</s>, endorses even the king's unfit decree as fit through the contrivance of reasoning, this constitutes <s>pralāpa</s>.

body.text:
prahasanasya śuddhādi-bhedāḥ-
śuddhaṃ kīrṇaṃ vaikṛtaṃ ca tac ca prahasanaṃ tridhā |
śuddhaṃ śrotriya-śākhāder veṣa-bhāṣādi-saṃyutam ||SRs_3.507|| 284
ceṭa-ceṭī-jana-vyāptaṃ tal lakṣyaṃ tu nirūpyatām |
ānanda-kośa-pramukhaṃ tathā bhagavad-ajjukam ||SRs_3.508|| 285
kīrṇaṃ tu sarvair vīthy-aṅgaiḥ saṅkīrṇaṃ dhūrta-saṅkulam |
tasyodāharaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ bṛhat-saubhadrakādikam ||SRs_3.509|| 286
yac cedaṃ kāmukādīnāṃ veṣa-bhāṣādi-saṅgataiḥ |

children.translated_text: combined with eunuchs, ascetics, old persons, and the like — that is <s>vaikṛta</s> (distorted).
The <s>Kalikeli-prahasana</s> and others are cited as its examples. ||3.510||

body.translated_text:
The varieties of farce — pure (<s>śuddha</s>) and others —
Farce (<s>prahasana</s>) is threefold: pure (<s>śuddha</s>), mixed (<s>kīrṇa</s>), and distorted (<s>vaikṛta</s>).
The pure is endowed with the attire, speech, and the like of <s>Śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholars), religious sectarians, and others. ||3.507||
It is populated by male and female servants. Let its characteristics be examined.
Examples include the <s>Ānanda-kośa</s> and the <s>Bhagavad-ajjuka</s>. ||3.508||
The mixed (<s>kīrṇa</s>) [employs] all the elements of the <s>Vīthī</s>; the miscellaneous (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>) is full of rogues.
Its example should be known as the <s>Bṛhat-saubhadraka</s> and the like. ||3.509||
That which involves the attire, speech, and the like of lovers and others,

body.text: atha ḍimaḥ-

children.translated_text: Connected with a well-known story, devoid of <s>Hāsya</s> and <s>Śṛṅgāra</s>, sealed with <s>Raudra</s>,
sparse in the <s>Sāttvatī</s> mode, prominent in <s>Bhāratī</s> and <s>Ārabhaṭī</s>, ||3.511||

body.translated_text: Now <s>Ḍima</s> —

body.text: nāyakair uddhatair deva-yakṣa-rākṣasa-pannagaiḥ | 289
body.translated_text: with vehement heroes [consisting of] gods, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and serpents,

body.text: gandharva-bhūta-vetāla-siddha-vidyādharādibhiḥ ||SRs_3.512||
body.translated_text: <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Vetālas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and others, ||3.512||

body.text: samanvitaṃ ṣoḍaśabhir nyāya-mārgaṇa-nāyakam | 290
body.translated_text: equipped with sixteen [heroes], with the path-finder as the principal hero,

body.text: caturbhir āṅkair anvītaṃ nirvimarśaka-sandhibhiḥ ||SRs_3.513||
body.translated_text: furnished with four acts, without the <s>vimarśa</s>-juncture, ||3.513||

body.text: nirghātolkoparāgādi-ghora-krūrāji-sambhramam | 291
body.translated_text: with the tumult of meteors, falling stars, eclipses, and the like — terrible, cruel battle-agitation,

body.text:
sa-praveśaka-viṣkambha-cūlikaṃ hi ḍimaṃ viduḥ |
asyodāharaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhitam ||SRs_3.514|| 292
body.translated_text:
with <s>praveśaka</s>, <s>viṣkambha</s>, and <s>cūlikā</s> — that the wise know as <s>Ḍima</s>.
Its example should be known as the <s>Vīrabhadra-vijṛmbhita</s>. ||3.514||

body.text:
atha īhāmṛgaḥ-
yatretivṛttaṃ miśraṃ syāt sa-viṣkambha-praveśakam |
catvāro' ṅkā nirvimarśa-garbhāḥ syuḥ sandhayas trayaḥ ||SRs_3.515|| 293
dhīroddhattaś ca prakhyāto divyo martyo' pi nāyakaḥ |
divya-striyam anicchantīṃ kanyāṃ vāhartum udyataḥ ||SRs_3.516|| 294
strī-nimittāji-saṃrambhaḥ pañcaṣāḥ pratināyakāḥ |
rasā nirbhaya-bībhatsā vṛttayaḥ kaiśikīṃ vinā ||SRs_3.517|| 295
svalpas tasyāḥ praveśo vā so' yam īhāmṛgo mataḥ |
vyājān nivārayed atra saṅgrāmaṃ bhīṣaṇa-kramam ||SRs_3.518|| 296
tasyodāharaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ prājñair māyā-kuraṅgikā |

children.translated_text: Thus by King <s>Śrī-Siṃha-bhūpa</s>, endowed with all characteristics,
the sequence of dramatic forms (<s>rūpakas</s>), complete in all its features, has been delineated. ||3.519||

body.translated_text:
Now <s>Īhāmṛga</s> (the Pursuit) —
Where the story is mixed [divine and human], with <s>viṣkambha</s> and <s>praveśaka</s>,
four acts, without <s>vimarśa</s> and <s>garbha</s> [junctures], three junctures, ||3.515||
the hero being <s>dhīroddhata</s> (vehement-spirited), well-known, divine or mortal,
who undertakes to seize an unwilling divine woman or maiden, ||3.516||
with battle-tumult on account of a woman, five or six antagonists,
all <s>rasas</s> except <s>Bhayānaka</s> and <s>Bībhatsa</s>, all dramatic modes except <s>Kaiśikī</s>, ||3.517||
or with only a small entry of <s>Kaiśikī</s> — that is considered <s>Īhāmṛga</s>.
Here one should by stratagems avert the battle from its terrifying course. ||3.518||
Its example should be known by the wise as <s>Māyā-kuraṅgikā</s>.

body.text: atha nāṭaka-paribhāṣā-

children.translated_text: Now, the conventions useful for understanding the construction of dramatic forms,
are set forth by the lord of the earth, <s>Śrī-Siṃha</s>. ||3.520||

body.translated_text: Now, the conventions of drama (<s>nāṭaka-paribhāṣā</s>) —

body.text: paribhāṣātra maryādā pūrvācāryopakalpitā | 299
body.translated_text: Convention (<s>paribhāṣā</s>) here means the rule established by earlier teachers.

body.text: sā hi naur atigambhīraṃ vivikṣor nāṭya-sāgaram ||SRs_3.521||
body.translated_text: It is indeed a vessel for one who wishes to cross the exceedingly deep ocean of drama. ||3.521||

body.text: eṣā ca bhāṣā-nirdeśa-nāmabhis trividhā matā | 300
body.translated_text: And this [convention] is considered threefold: by language (<s>bhāṣā</s>), indication (<s>nirdeśa</s>), and naming (<s>nāma</s>).

body.text: tatra bhāṣā dvidhā bhāṣā vibhāṣā ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_3.522||
body.translated_text: Among these, language (<s>bhāṣā</s>) is twofold: <s>bhāṣā</s> (proper language) and <s>vibhāṣā</s> (dialect). ||3.522||

body.text: caturdaśa vibhāṣāḥ syuḥ prācyādyā vākya-vṛttayaḥ | 301
body.translated_text: The <s>vibhāṣās</s> (dialects) are fourteen — <s>Prācī</s> (Eastern) and others — [representing] modes of regional speech.

body.text: āsāṃ saṃskāra-rāhityād viniyogo na kathyate ||SRs_3.523||
body.translated_text: Because these lack grammatical refinement, their [specific] employment is not described. ||3.523||

body.text: uttamādiṣu tad-deśa-vyavahārāt pratīyatām | 302
body.translated_text: Let them be understood through the actual usage of the superior and other [character types] in their respective regions.

body.text: bhāṣā dvidhā saṃskṛtā ca prākṛtī ceti bhedataḥ ||SRs_3.524||
body.translated_text: <s>Bhāṣā</s> (proper language) is twofold: <s>Saṃskṛta</s> (Sanskrit) and <s>Prākṛtī</s> (Prakrit). ||3.524||

body.text: kaumāra-pāṇinīyādi-saṃskṛtā saṃskṛtā matā | 303
body.translated_text: That which is refined (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) by the <s>Kaumāra</s>, <s>Pāṇinīya</s>, and other [grammars] is considered <s>Saṃskṛta</s>.

body.text:
iyaṃ tu devatādīnāṃ munīnāṃ nāyakasya ca |
liṅgināṃ ca viṭādīnm anīcānāṃ prayujyate ||SRs_3.525|| 304
body.translated_text:
This is employed for deities and others, for sages, for the hero,
for ascetics, for the <s>viṭa</s> (gallant companion) and others, and for persons who are not of low rank. ||3.525||

body.text: atha prākṛtī-

children.text: prakṛteḥ saṃskṛtāyās tu vikṛtiḥ prākṛtī matā | 305
children.translated_text: The modification (<s>vikṛti</s>) of Sanskrit, [which is] the original (<s>prakṛti</s>), is considered <s>Prākṛtī</s>.

children.text: ṣaḍ-vidhā sā prākṛtaṃ ca śaurasenī ca māgadhī ||SRs_3.526||
children.translated_text: It is sixfold: <s>Prākṛta</s>, <s>Śauraseni</s>, <s>Māgadhī</s>, ||3.526||

body.translated_text: Now <s>Prākṛtī</s> (Prakrit) —

body.text: paiśācī cūlikā paiśācy apabhraṃśa iti kramāt | 306
body.translated_text: <s>Paiśācī</s>, <s>Cūlikā-paiśācī</s>, and <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> — in order.

body.text: atra tu prākṛtaṃ strīṇāṃ sarvāsāṃ niyataṃ bhavet ||SRs_3.527||
body.translated_text: <s>Prākṛta</s> is invariably assigned to all women. ||3.527||

body.text: kvacic ca devī gaṇikā mantrijā ceti yoṣitām | 307
body.translated_text: But sometimes, the queen, the courtesan, and the minister's wife among women,

body.text: yoginy-apsarasoḥ śilpa-kāriṇyā api saṃskṛtam ||SRs_3.528||
body.translated_text: and the <s>Yoginī</s>, the <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymph), and the craftswoman may also [speak] Sanskrit. ||3.528||

body.text: ye nīcāḥ karmaṇā jātyā teṣāṃ prākṛtam ucyate | 308
body.translated_text: Those who are low by deed or birth — for them Prakrit is prescribed.

body.text: chadma-liṅgavatāṃ tadvaj jainānām iti kecana ||SRs_3.529||
body.translated_text: Likewise for those in disguise, and for Jains — so say some. ||3.529||

body.text: adhame madhyame cāpi śaurasenī prayujyate | 309
body.translated_text: <s>Śauraseni</s> is employed for the low and middling [characters].

body.text: dhīvarādy-atinīceṣu māgadhī ca niyujyate ||SRs_3.530||
body.translated_text: And <s>Māgadhī</s> is assigned to fishermen and the most lowly. ||3.530||

body.text: rakṣaḥ-piśāca-nīceṣu paiśācī-dvitayaṃ bhavet | 310
body.translated_text: The two varieties of <s>Paiśācī</s> are for <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and low persons.

body.text: apabhraṃśas tu caṇḍāla-yavanādiṣu yujyate ||SRs_3.531||
body.translated_text: And <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> is employed for <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, <s>Yavanas</s> (foreigners), and the like. ||3.531||

body.text: nāṭakādāv apabhraṃśa-vinyāsasyāsahiṣṇavaḥ | 311
body.translated_text: Others, who cannot tolerate the use of <s>Apabhraṃśa</s> in <s>Nāṭaka</s> and the like,

body.text: anye caṇḍālakādīnāṃ māgadhy-ādīn prayuñjate ||SRs_3.532||
body.translated_text: employ <s>Māgadhī</s> and the like for <s>Caṇḍālas</s> and others. ||3.532||

body.text: sarveṣāṃ kāraṇa-vaśāt kāryo bhāṣā-vyatikramaḥ | 312
body.translated_text: For all, a transgression of language-assignment should be made when there is a [specific] cause.

body.text: māhātmyasya paribhraṃśaṃ madasyātiśayaṃ tathā ||SRs_3.533||
body.translated_text: The causes are declared to be: the fall from one's greatness, the excess of intoxication,

body.text: pracchādanaṃ ca vibhrāntiṃ yathālikhita-vācanam | 313
body.translated_text: concealment, bewilderment, reading what is written as-is,

body.text: kadācid anuvādaṃ ca kāraṇāni pracakṣate ||SRs_3.534||
body.translated_text: and sometimes quotation. ||3.534||

body.text: atha nirdeśa-paribhāṣā-

children.translated_text: The manner of addressing people who should not be called directly by name,
using substituted designations — that is called <s>nirdeśa</s> by those learned in drama. ||3.535||

body.translated_text: Now, the conventions of indication (<s>nirdeśa-paribhāṣā</s>) —

body.text: sa tridhā pūjya-sadṛśa-kaniṣṭha-viṣayatvataḥ | 315
body.translated_text: It is threefold according to whether the [person addressed is] venerable, equal, or junior.

body.text: pūjyās tu devo munayo liṅginas tat-samāstriyaḥ ||SRs_3.536||
body.translated_text: The venerable are: gods, sages, ascetics, and women of their status. ||3.536||

body.text: bahuśrutāś ca bhagavac-chabda-vācyā bhavanti hi | 316
body.translated_text: The very learned should be addressed with the word <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One).

body.text: āryeti brāhmaṇo vācyo vṛddhas tāteti bhāṣyate ||SRs_3.537||
body.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be addressed as <s>Ārya</s> (Noble Sir); an elder as <s>Tāta</s> (Father). ||3.537||

body.text: upādhyāyeti cācāryo gaṇikā tv ajjukākhyayā | 317
body.translated_text: A preceptor as <s>Upādhyāya</s>; a courtesan by the name <s>Ajjukā</s>.

body.text: mahārājeti bhūpālo vidvān bhāva itīryate ||SRs_3.538||
body.translated_text: A king as <s>Mahārāja</s>; a learned man as <s>Bhāva</s> (Sir). ||3.538||

body.text: chandato nāmabhir vācyā brāhmaṇais tu narādhipāḥ | 318
body.translated_text: Kings should be addressed by name, optionally, by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.text: deveti nṛpatir vācyo bhṛtyaiḥ prakṛtibhis tathā ||SRs_3.539||
body.translated_text: A king should be addressed as <s>Deva</s> (Lord) by servants and by ministers. ||3.539||

body.text: sārvabhaumaḥ parijanair bhaṭṭa-bhaṭṭāraketi ca | 319
body.translated_text: An emperor [should be addressed] by attendants as <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> or <s>Bhaṭṭāraka</s>.

body.text: vācyo rājeti munibhir apatya-pratyayena vā ||SRs_3.540||
body.translated_text: [He should be] addressed as <s>Rājan</s> (King) by sages, or with the patronymic suffix. ||3.540||

body.text: vidūṣakeṇa tu prāyaḥ sakhe rājan nitīcchayā | 320
body.translated_text: By the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester), [the king] is usually addressed as 'Friend' or 'O King', according to the desired implication.

body.text: brāhmaṇaiḥ sacivo vācyo hy amātya saciveti ca ||SRs_3.541||
body.translated_text: By <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the minister should be addressed as 'Minister' (<s>amātya</s>) or 'Counselor' (<s>saciva</s>). ||3.541||

body.text: śaiṣāir āryety athāyuṣman iti sārathinā rathī | 321
body.translated_text: By pupils, [their elders are addressed as] 'Noble sir' (<s>ārya</s>) or 'Long-lived one' (<s>āyuṣman</s>). By the charioteer, [the warrior is called] 'Chariot-warrior' (<s>rathī</s>).

body.text: tapasvi-sādhu-śabdābhyāṃ praśāntaḥ paribhāṣyate ||SRs_3.542||
body.translated_text: One who is tranquil (<s>praśānta</s>) is addressed with the words 'Ascetic' (<s>tapasvin</s>) or 'Holy one' (<s>sādhu</s>). ||3.542||

body.text: svāmīti yuva-rājas tu kumāro bhartṛ-dārakaḥ | 322
body.translated_text: The crown prince is [addressed as] 'Master' (<s>svāmī</s>) or 'Prince' (<s>kumāra</s>) or 'Young lord' (<s>bhartṛ-dāraka</s>).

body.text: āvutteti svasur bhartā syāleti pṛtanā-patiḥ ||SRs_3.543||
body.translated_text: The sister's husband is [addressed as] '<s>Āvutta</s>' (brother-in-law); the brother-in-law as '<s>Syāla</s>'; the army commander as '<s>Pṛtanā-pati</s>'. ||3.543||

body.text: bhaṭṭinī svāminī devī tathā bhaṭṭāriketi ca | 323
body.translated_text: '<s>Bhaṭṭinī</s>' (Your Ladyship), '<s>Svāminī</s>' (Mistress), '<s>Devī</s>' (Queen), and also '<s>Bhaṭṭārikā</s>' (Your Honor) —

body.text: paricārajanair vācyā yoṣito rāja-vallabhāḥ ||SRs_3.544||
body.translated_text: thus are the women beloved of the king to be addressed by the attendants. ||3.544||

body.text: rājñā tu mahiṣī vācyā devīty anyāḥ priyā iti | 324
body.translated_text: By the king, the chief queen is to be called '<s>Mahiṣī</s>' (Chief Queen) or '<s>Devī</s>' (Queen); the others as 'Beloved' (<s>priyā</s>).

body.text: sarveṇa patnī tv āryeti pitur nāmnā sutasya vā ||SRs_3.545||
body.translated_text: By everyone, a wife is to be called 'Noble lady' (<s>āryā</s>), [or addressed] by the name of [her] father or son. ||3.545||

body.text: tāta-pādā iti pitā mātāmbeti sutena tu | 325
body.translated_text: The father is [addressed] by the son as 'Venerable Father' (<s>tāta-pādāḥ</s>); the mother as '<s>Ambā</s>' (Mother).

body.text: jyeṣṭhās tv āryā iti bhrātrā tathā syur mātulādayaḥ ||SRs_3.546||
body.translated_text: Elders are [addressed] by a brother as 'Noble ones' (<s>āryāḥ</s>); likewise maternal uncles and others. ||3.546||

body.text: atha sadṛśa-nirdeśaḥ-

children.text: sadṛśaḥ sadṛśo vācyo vayasyety āhvayena vā | 326
children.translated_text: An equal is to be addressed as 'Equal' (<s>sadṛśa</s>) or 'Comrade' (<s>vayasya</s>), or by name.

children.text: haleti sakhyā tu sakhī kathanīyā sakhīti vā ||SRs_3.547||
children.translated_text: By a female friend, a friend is to be addressed as '<s>Hale</s>' (Girlfriend) or '<s>Sakhi</s>' (Friend). ||3.547||

body.translated_text: Now, the mode of addressing an equal —

body.text: atha kaniṣṭha-nirdeśaḥ-

children.translated_text: Sons, pupils, and younger ones are to be addressed by elders
with the appellations 'Dear child' (<s>vatsa</s>), 'Little son' (<s>putraka</s>), 'Long-lived one' (<s>dīrghāyus</s>), 'Son' (<s>tāta</s>), or 'Child' (<s>jāta</s>). ||3.548||

body.translated_text: Now, the mode of addressing an inferior —

body.text: anyaḥ kanīyān āryeṇa janena paribhāṣyate | 328
body.translated_text: Another inferior is addressed by a noble person

body.text: śilpādhikāra-nāmabhyāṃ bhadra bhadra-mukheti ||SRs_3.549||
body.translated_text: by craft-designation, by name, as 'Good fellow' (<s>bhadra</s>), or 'Good-faced one' (<s>bhadra-mukha</s>). ||3.549||

body.text: vācye nīcātinīce tu haṇḍe hañje iti kramāt | 329
body.translated_text: When the addressee is low or very low, [they are called] '<s>Haṇḍe</s>' and '<s>Hañje</s>' respectively.

body.text: bhartrā vācyāḥ sva-sva-nāmnā bhṛtyāḥ śilpocitena vā ||SRs_3.550||
body.translated_text: Servants are to be addressed by their master by their own names or by a title befitting their craft. ||3.550||

body.text: evam ādi prakāreṇa yojyā nirdeśa-yojanā | 330
body.translated_text: In this and similar manner, the scheme of address should be applied,

body.text: loka-śāstrāvirodhena vijñeyā kāvya-kovidaiḥ ||SRs_3.551||
body.translated_text: to be understood by those skilled in poetry, without contradiction to worldly usage and the <s>Śāstras</s>. ||3.551||

body.text: atha nāma-paribhāṣā-

children.translated_text: For one whose name is unmentioned [in the source], in a well-known plot, [even for characters] such as the chamberlain and others —

children.text: itivṛtte kalpite tu nāyakāder api sphuṭam ||SRs_3.552||
children.translated_text: but in an invented plot, clearly [even for] the hero and others, ||3.552||

body.translated_text: Now, the conventions of naming (<s>nāma-paribhāṣā</s>) —

body.text: rasa-vastūpayogīni kavir nāmāni kalpayet | 332
body.translated_text: the poet should devise names that serve the <s>rasa</s> and the plot.

body.text: vinayandhara-bābhravya-jayandhara-jayādikam ||SRs_3.553||
body.translated_text: <s>Vinayandhara</s>, <s>Bābhravya</s>, <s>Jayandhara</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, and so forth — ||3.553||

body.text: kāryaṃ kañcukināṃ nāma prāyo viśvāsa-sūcakam | 333
body.translated_text: should be the names of chamberlains, generally suggesting trustworthiness.

body.text: latālaṅkāra-puṣpādi-vastūnāṃ lalitātmanām ||SRs_3.554||
body.translated_text: With names suggesting ornamental qualities — creepers, ornaments, flowers, and other delicate things — ||3.554||

body.text: nāmabhir guṇa-siddhair ceṭīnāṃ nāma kalpayet | 334
body.translated_text: one should devise the names of maidservants.

body.text: karabhaḥ kalahaṃsaś cety ādi nāmānujīvinām ||SRs_3.555||
body.translated_text: '<s>Karabha</s>' (Young Elephant), '<s>Kalahaṃsa</s>' (Royal Swan), etc. — these are names for attendants. ||3.555||

body.text: karpūra-caṇḍa-kāmpilyety ādikaṃ nāma vandinām | 335
body.translated_text: '<s>Karpūra</s>' (Camphor), '<s>Caṇḍa</s>' (Fierce), '<s>Kāmpilya</s>', etc. — are names for bards.

body.text: subuddhi-vasubhūtyādi-mantriṇāṃ nāma kalpayet ||SRs_3.556||
body.translated_text: '<s>Subuddhi</s>' (Good Intellect), '<s>Vasubhūti</s>' (Blessed with Wealth), etc. — one should devise such names for ministers. ||3.556||

body.text: devarātaḥ somarāta iti nāma purodhasaḥ | 336
body.translated_text: '<s>Devarāta</s>' (God-given), '<s>Somarāta</s>' (Moon-given) — are names for the royal priest.

body.text: śrīvatso gautamaḥ kautso gārgyo maudgalya ity api ||SRs_3.557||
body.translated_text: '<s>Śrīvatsa</s>', '<s>Gautama</s>', '<s>Kautsa</s>', '<s>Gārgya</s>', '<s>Maudgalya</s>' — [are gotra names] as well. ||3.557||

body.text: vasantakaḥ kāpileya ity ākhyeyo vidūṣakaḥ | 337
body.translated_text: '<s>Vasantaka</s>' (Little Spring), '<s>Kāpileya</s>' (Son of Kapila) — thus should the <s>Vidūṣaka</s> (jester) be named.

body.text: pratāpa-vīra-vijaya-māna-vikrama-sāhasaiḥ ||SRs_3.558||
body.translated_text: With words like <s>Pratāpa</s> (Valor), <s>Vīra</s> (Heroic), <s>Vijaya</s> (Victory),

body.text: vasanta-bhūṣaṇottaṃsa-śekharāṅka-padottaraiḥ | 338
body.translated_text: <s>Māna</s> (Honor), <s>Vikrama</s> (Prowess), <s>Sāhasa</s> (Daring), followed by <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring), <s>Bhūṣaṇa</s> (Ornament), <s>Uttaṃsa</s> (Crest),

body.text: dhīrottarāṇāṃ netṝṇāṃ nāma kurvīta kovidaḥ ||SRs_3.559||
body.translated_text: <s>Śekhara</s> (Crown), <s>Aṅka</s> (Mark), <s>Pada</s> (Rank) — the skilled poet should form the names of <s>Dhīrodātta</s> (exalted-steadfast) heroes. ||3.559||

body.text: candrāpīḍaḥ kāmapāla ity ādyaṃ lalitātmanām | 339
body.translated_text: '<s>Candrāpīḍa</s>' (Moon-crested), '<s>Kāmapāla</s>' (Protector of Love), etc. — for those of graceful nature (<s>Dhīra-lalita</s>).

body.text: ugravarmā caṇḍasena ity ādy-uddhata-cetasām ||SRs_3.560||
body.translated_text: '<s>Ugravarmā</s>' (Fierce-armored), '<s>Caṇḍasena</s>' (Fierce-army), etc. — for those of impetuous mind (<s>Dhīroddhata</s>). ||3.560||

body.text: datta-senānta-nāmāni vaiśyānāṃ kalpayet sudhīḥ | 340
body.translated_text: The wise should devise names ending in '<s>Datta</s>' (Given) and '<s>Sena</s>' (Army) for merchants (<s>Vaiśyas</s>).

body.text: karpūra-mañjarī candralekhā rāgataraṅgikā ||SRs_3.561||
body.translated_text: '<s>Karpūra-mañjarī</s>' (Camphor-Blossom), '<s>Candralekhā</s>' (Moon-line), '<s>Rāgataraṅgikā</s>' (Wave of Passion),

body.text: padmāvatīti prāyeṇa nāmnā vācyā hi nāyikā | 341
body.translated_text: '<s>Padmāvatī</s>' (Lotus-possessing) — generally, the heroine should be addressed by such names.

body.text: devyas tu dhāriṇī-lakṣmī-vasumatyādi-nāmabhiḥ ||SRs_3.562||
body.translated_text: Queens, however, [are named] with names like '<s>Dhāriṇī</s>' (Bearer), '<s>Lakṣmī</s>' (Fortune), '<s>Vasumatī</s>' (Earth), etc. ||3.562||

body.text: bhogavatī kāntimatī kamalā kāmavallarī | 342
