body.translated_text: '<s>Bhogavatī</s>' (Endowed with Enjoyment), '<s>Kāntimatī</s>' (Radiant), '<s>Kamalā</s>' (Lotus), '<s>Kāmavallarī</s>' (Creeper of Love),

body.text: irāvatī haṃsapadīty ādi-nāmnā tu bhoginī ||SRs_3.563||
body.translated_text: '<s>Irāvatī</s>', '<s>Haṃsapadī</s>' (Swan-footed), etc. — are names for the courtesan (<s>bhoginī</s>). ||3.563||

body.text: viprakṣatra-viśaḥ śarma-varma-dattānta-nāmabhiḥ | 343
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>Vaiśyas</s> [are named] with names ending in '<s>Śarman</s>', '<s>Varman</s>', and '<s>Datta</s>' respectively.

body.text: śikhaṇḍāṅgada-cūḍānta-nāmnā vidyādharādhipāḥ ||SRs_3.564||
body.translated_text: <s>Vidyādhara</s> (celestial being) lords [are named] with names ending in '<s>Śikhaṇḍa</s>' (Crest), '<s>Aṅgada</s>' (Armlet), or '<s>Cūḍa</s>' (Topknot). ||3.564||

body.text: kuṇḍalānanda-ghaṇṭānta-nāmnā kāpālikā janāḥ | 344
body.translated_text: <s>Kāpālika</s> (skull-bearing ascetic) men [are named] with names ending in '<s>Kuṇḍala</s>' (Earring), '<s>Ānanda</s>' (Bliss), or '<s>Ghaṇṭa</s>' (Bell).

body.text: yogasundarikā vaṃśaprabhā vikaṭamudrikā ||SRs_3.565||
body.translated_text: '<s>Yogasundarikā</s>' (Beauty of Yoga), '<s>Vaṃśaprabhā</s>' (Splendor of Lineage), '<s>Vikaṭamudrikā</s>' (Fierce-ringed) —

body.text: śaṅkha-keyūrikety ādi-nāmnā kāpālika-striyaḥ | 345
body.translated_text: and names ending in '<s>Śaṅkha</s>' (Conch) or '<s>Keyūrikā</s>' (Armlet) — are for <s>Kāpālika</s> women.

body.text: ānandinī siddhimatī śrīmatī sarvamaṅgalā ||SRs_3.566||
body.translated_text: '<s>Ānandinī</s>' (Joyful), '<s>Siddhimatī</s>' (Endowed with Success), '<s>Śrīmatī</s>' (Auspicious), '<s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s>' (All-auspicious),

body.text: yaśovatī putravatīty ādi-nāmnā suvāsinī | 346
body.translated_text: '<s>Yaśovatī</s>' (Glorious), '<s>Putravatī</s>' (Blessed with Sons), etc. — are names for a married auspicious woman (<s>suvāsinī</s>). ||3.566||

body.text: ity ādi sarvam ālocya lakṣaṇaṃ kṛta-buddhinā ||SRs_3.567||
body.translated_text: Having reflected upon all such characteristics, a poet who has made up his mind

body.text: kavinā kalpitaṃ kāvyam ācandrārkaṃ prakāśate | 347
body.translated_text: and composed a poem [accordingly] shines forth as long as the moon and the sun.

body.text: lakṣya-lakṣaṇa-nirmāṇa-vijñāna-kṛta-buddhibhiḥ ||SRs_3.568||
body.translated_text: With minds refined by the knowledge of constructing both exemplary works and their theoretical principles,

body.text: parīkṣyatām ayaṃ grantho vimatsara-manīṣayā | 348
body.translated_text: let this treatise be examined with judgment free from envy.

body.text:
bharatāgama-pārīṇaḥ śrīmān siṃha-mahīpatiḥ |
rasikaḥ kṛtavān evaṃ rasārṇava-sudhākaram ||SRs_3.569|| 349
body.translated_text: The illustrious King <s>Siṃha</s>, thoroughly versed in the <s>Bharata</s> tradition, a true connoisseur, has thus composed the <s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s>. ||3.569||

body.text:
saṃrambhād anapota-siṃha-nṛpater dhāṭī-samāṭīkane
niḥsāṇeṣu dhaṇaṃ dhaṇaṃ dhaṇam iti dhvānānusandhāyiṣu |
modante hi raṇaṃ raṇaṃ raṇam iti prauḍhās tadīyā bhaṭā
bhrāntiṃ yānti tṛṇaṃ tṛṇaṃ tṛṇam iti pratyarthi-pṛthvī-bhujaḥ ||SRs_3.570|| 350
body.translated_text: When King <s>Anapota-Siṃha</s> launches his attacking march in fury, and his war-drums resound in pursuit [crying] '<s>dhaṇaṃ dhaṇaṃ dhaṇam</s>' — his veteran warriors exult [chanting] 'Battle! Battle! Battle!' while his rival kings are thrown into confusion [moaning] 'A straw! A straw! A straw!' ||3.570||

body.text:
matvā dhātrā tulāyāṃ laghur iti dharaṇīṃ siṃha-bhūpāla-candre
sṛṣṭe tatrātigurvyāṃ tad-upanidhitayā sthāpyamānaiḥ krameṇa |
cintāratnaugha-kalpa-druma-tati-surabhī-maṇḍalaiḥ pūritāntāpy
ūrdhvaṃ nītā laghimnā tad-ari-kula-śataiḥ pūryate' dyāpi sā dyauḥ ||SRs_3.571|| 351
body.translated_text: When the Creator, deeming the earth light upon the scales and having created the exceedingly heavy moon-like King <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s> as her counterweight — even when [the other pan] was filled in sequence with hosts of <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> gems, <s>Kalpa</s>-trees, and herds of celestial wish-cows, it was still raised upward by its lightness; even today that heaven is being filled with the hundreds of clans of his enemies. ||3.571||

body.text:
iti śrīmad-āndhra-maṇḍalādhīśvara-pratigaṇḍa-bhairava-śrīmad-anapota-narendra-nandana-bhuja-bala-bhīma-śrī-siṃha-bhūpāla-viracite rasārṇava-sudhākara-nāmni nāṭyālaṅkāra-śāstre bhāvakollāso nāma
tṛtīyo vilāsaḥ
||3||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, named <s>Bhāvakollāsa</s> (The Delight of Emotion), in the treatise on dramatic aesthetics called <s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Siṃha-bhūpāla</s>, of arm-strength [mighty as] <s>Bhīma</s>, son of the illustrious Emperor <s>Anapota</s>, <s>Pratigaṇḍa-Bhairava</s>, lord of the <s>Āndhra</s> realm. ||3||

body.text: samāptaś cāyaṃ rasārṇava-sudhākaraḥ
body.translated_text: And thus the <s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s> is concluded.

children.translated_text: May <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), dark as a <s>tamāla</s> tree, dwelling on the Watery Mountain (<s>Toyaśaila</s>),
the auspicious moon that delights the <s>cakora</s> birds that are the sages, be victorious!
His broad, spotless chest is adorned with the radiance
of saffron-paste from the breast-clusters of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
May the Wind (<s>Māruta</s>), dwelling on the <s>Malaya</s> mountain, grant [us] limbs [of comfort];
the young cool-rayed one (Moon) — a friend of holy fame;

children.text: carati ciram anaṅgaḥ kvāpi kari apy adṛśyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless God of Love), who wanders somewhere unseen even to the performers —
may that Five-arrowed one, saluted by hosts of connoisseurs, be victorious!
May the unbroken succession of blessings from all the twice-born
set in motion auspiciousness and long life for the poets!
